incident_description:
I purchased an Lectric Branded E Trike from a third party.  When we arranged for the test drive and purchase the odometer didn't even register a mile on it because this cute 81 year old man bought it for his dying wife who was unfortunately never able to drive it more than a short distance.  By the time we finished test driving it and agreed to buy it, the odometer registered one mile.  It's a beautiful trike.  I was so excited to be able to take it out on rides with my husband.  Our first couple of journeys we stayed close to home and took shorter rides while I got used to the trike and using the peddle assist feature.  On the third ride we took the trike out on an almost 12 ride on a paved bike path on along a river.  The trike nearly tipped twice on me.  The first time I hit a rock with the front wheel and the second time I tried to drive over an item that I could not navigate around.  I was going slow enough that I was able to slide off the seat and stand to stabilize the trike.  The last trip we were on a different section of the paved bike path and went on a 17 mile journey.  I was using the peddle assist and traveling between 10-11 mph when I came upon a root from a nearby tree that had grown under the asphalt and caused a slight buckle in the path.  I didn't see it in time.  I wasn't able to stop in time to avoid it.  I took a slight turn and the trike ended up toppling over on top of me.  At any rate of speed and a slight turn the trike is unstable.  The end result of that accident was a trip to the Urgent Care facility with a fractured elbow.  I have bone fragments still floating near my elbow and remain in pain nearly a month later.  I love the idea of this trike.  I love that I'm able to ride with my husband.  I just want a stable and reliable ride.  I've tried emailing the manufacturer of the trike multiple times trying to discuss with them ways that I can stabilize the trike so that I can continue to ride it but the only thing they want to tell me is that I voided the warranty when I bought it from a third party.  My point to them remains that by the time I test drove it and took it home it had ONE mile on the odometer.  I'm not asking them to warranty it for a return, I want help in stabilizing it so I can continue to ride it.  They just aren't interested in helping me do that and I am so disappointed at their apparent attempt to avoid liability.

I should interject that I am not new to adult tricycles.  I grew up with an adult tricycle.  I have moderate cerebral palsy which affects my lower extremities and somewhat my mobility.  That being said, I am not unfamiliar with riding, balancing and steering adult tricycles.  I do believe that I have a reasonable expectation that this E Trike would offer me the same stability and reliability that I am accustomed to.
justification: The incident resulted in a fractured elbow with ongoing pain, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The trike's instability has caused multiple near-tipping incidents, suggesting a likelihood of 4 (likely) for future occurrences.

incident_description:
On the evening of Sunday, July 21, around 5:15 PM, I was riding the scooter I purchased from Amazon a few months ago. My destination was the parking lot where my car was parked in [REDACTED]. While riding, the safety locker on the scooter unexpectedly opened, causing me to fall onto the street and sustain injuries to my hands, elbow, arm, and right leg. The wounds were significant, and I was both panicked and bewildered by how it happened. Considering the speed I was traveling at, which was approximately 15 mph, the consequences could have been much worse, so I am thankful for that. Despite the pain and bleeding, I had to drive for four and a half hours following the incident.

It is worth noting that the locker had opened on previous occasions, but I attributed it to my potential failure in properly securing it. However, on this particular instance, I made sure to lock it correctly, and it appeared to be in place. To my surprise, after the incident, I locked it again and gave the scooter a shake, only to find that it opened on its own once more. This poses a significant safety concern, and I strongly believe that a recall is necessary. I contacted the vendor, but their only resolution was to offer a replacement scooter. After reading reviews, I discovered that other people have also experienced similar issues. I kindly request that you thoroughly investigate this matter. The potential consequences were severe, and I do not wish for anyone else to endure a similar situation. Thank you for your attention to this matter.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries to hands, elbow, arm, and leg, and the locker issue has occurred multiple times, indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description:
I have a 2019 Yamaha Wolverine X4.

I took it on a 6 mile trek in the woods.

I returned to my cabin, parked the Wolverine next to my [REDACTED], left it idling and went inside for ~ 3 minutes.

In that time the Wolverine was consumed by fire.

911 was called and I immediately applied water from a garden hose on the fire.

19 minutes later the fire department arrived and applied fire retardant foam to the fire.

29 minutes after the 911 call the fire was contained but both the Wolverine and the [REDACTED] were burned down to the frame.

If this fire had happened 5 minutes earlier the Yamaha would have ignited a giant fire on Idaho State forest land.

No injuries were experienced.

I have pictures and video of the event.

I am having difficulty contacting Yamaha but will continue to do so.

I am leaving the carcass of the Yamaha in place so that hopefully an engineer from Yamaha can come and determine root cause.
justification: The incident involved a fire causing significant property damage but no injuries, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such events are not common but possible with equipment failures.

incident_description: REEBOK 65 CM WEIGHTED STABILITY BALL (sand-filled for added resistance during moves and weighted base) was mere months old when it exploded and sent me down to the floor faster than the KABOOM in the room. The sand was like a powder bomb and left me in the midst of a cloud on the floor. I live alone and am the sole user of this product since buying it. My lower back is already severely deteriorated, with virtually no disc between two vertebrae, so I've been using the "physio" ball to strengthen my core, develop better balance, and gain flexibility through stretching. My body was sitting on top of the ball at the time of this incident, with my feet on the floor and back slightly reclined (thankfully!). Had my back been postured at a 90 degree, I would be paralyzed from the waist down. Because of the reclined altered my center of gravity, the landing was as much sideways and reduced the higher impact of a direct hit on the tailbone. That said, my hip feels severely bruised and the extent of injury is yet TBD. My concern beyond my own health is the welfare of the general public who seeks to improve their overall health and fitness only to be betrayed by the equipment trusted as the training companion. Beyond that, I've enjoyed and benefited from these products for over a dozen years and now my fear of a repeat will prevent me from replacing this item. To be sure, there were NO sharp objects or anything which "poked" the product to make it pop. The ball has about a dozen "rings" around it at various elevations; the ball exploded around the center ring, or the equator.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe hip bruise and potential further injury, but no death or paralysis occurred. The likelihood is unlikely as the product is typically reliable, but the incident did occur.

incident_description:
In March 2022, we purchased a Cannondale kids bike from our local dealer.  This dealer bike shop has since has been sold to Coastal E-bikes,
[REDACTED], Carolina Beach, NC 28428.  The purchase cost was $600.  

There have been numerous problems with this bike, despite very light use by our 6-year old grandson (recreational, street riding only and perhaps 20 rides in total).  

The first issue was a lock-up of the steering column, where it would not turn, causing a crash alongside the road that could have resulted in a serious accident had a car passed at that moment.  The original bike shop fixed that issue and charged us $50.  No talk about warranty.

The second problem was the chain coming off and the gears slipping.  The bike shop had by then changed ownership and, graciously, agreed to look at it.  They tuned up the bike and fixed the chain at a $75 charge.  It's been off twice since then, causing unexpected falls forward over the steering wheel.  The bike is no longer under warranty.

The third problem was again the chain coming off and suddenly, mid ride, losing any gear engagement at all, causing my grandson to crash and, luckily again, he came away with just bumps and bruises.  

This bike isnt functioning and we do not trust it for our grandson to ride it safely.  He is very disappointed, of course, as it was a birthday present and his first real bike.  Selling it is not an option, as we wouldnt get $50 for it, if that, and I do not want another child getting hurt.

Contacted Cannondale, received a claim number, no response for a month.  I called and was told "someone from management would look at it", that was 2 weeks ago.  I called today and they simply did not react while I was explaining the situation, put the call on "hold" until I hung up.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries (bumps and bruises) from multiple crashes caused by mechanical failures, and the likelihood of recurrence is high given the persistent issues.

incident_description:
Dear Sirs,
I am writing to formally report a significant safety concern involving a Pentair Water Pool and Spa, Inc. product. This product, the Max-E-Therm Heater, has caused a fire at my residence, leading to substantial property damage and posing a serious risk to consumer safety.
Incident Details:
	Product: Pentair Max-E-Therm Heater
	Mdel Number: P/N SR400LP
	Serial Number: 44000492100293
	Incident Date: 09/16/2022
	Damage: Fire originating from the heater, leading to property damage and increased insurance premiums.
Independent Expert Findings:
An independent expert's report has concluded that the fire originated in the heater's upper housing area, specifically the combustion chamber. This is notably the same area affected by a recall by Pentair dated April 28, 2021. Despite this, my unit, manufactured slightly later, experienced the same defect leading to ignition.
Manufacturer's Response:
Pentair has acknowledged the potential defect and offered to compensate for the cost of the heater and its installation. However, they have attributed the fire to rodent damage without a physical examination and have only proposed a limited resolution. This speculative attribution raises concerns about the overall safety and design of the heater.
Potential Risk to Consumers:
Given the defect's potential to cause fires, this product poses a serious threat to all users, especially those with units manufactured around the same period as mine. The risk extends beyond financial losses to the safety and well-being of consumers.
Request for Agency Involvement:
In light of these concerns, I urge your agency to:
1.	Investigate the safety and design of the Pentair Max-E-Therm Heater.
2.	Ensure  Pentair extends its recall to cover all units manufactured around the same period as mine.
3.	Supervise the examination of my heater by Pentair to ensure transparency and accuracy. I have requested that experts from relevant consumer protection agencies be present during this examination.
Documentation:
I am in position of all relevant documentation, including the independent expert's report, correspondence with Pentair, and photographic evidence of the damage.
Conclusion:
Your agency must act to prevent further incidents and ensure consumer safety. I look forward to your prompt response and am available to provide any additional information or clarification.
Thank you for your attention to this urgent matter.
justification: The incident involved a fire causing property damage but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: I wear an equestrian safety air vest when competing in horse jumping.  Retailers claim it to be the safest and best choice for protection from falls, with focus on internal injuries and spine.  I wear the FreeJump Air vest that was sold to me as being the best safety option.  From the website this " vest is the first airbag vest made for horseback riding to have been approved by the NF S72-800-2022 standard".  They are all produced in Europe and sold by US retailers.  Twice it has deployed at the wrong time in minor falls, but resulted in the first fall breaking my wrist in 8+ places resulting in surgery and rehab.  The second fall resulted in a completed radial head fracture, multiple contusions, and head trauma.  There is no warning as to peripheral injuries happening while using the vest. Given these are rapidly being sold in the US, and all the companies are from Europe makes it impossible to seek any help from US attorneys - for which I have tried.  Fighting over jurisdiction prior to hearing my cases was not financially feasible.   I would have never worn the airbag vest and would just used a "normal" hard shell vest without all the push from US retailers to purchase.

incident_description: I bought a viribus electric bike from Walmart online marketplace. The bracket holding the front front brake cable failed causing me to lose front brakes. Luckily I was able to stop with rear brake. After pulling the cable tight and securing the bracket the rear brake cable did the same thing. I took it to Walmart to ask the bike mechanic to look at it since I bought the three year warranty with the bike. They told me I had to go through [REDACTED] for repairs. incident_description:
U-Skooter/E-TWow dangerous sudden freeze up of front wheel purchased online from: 
ETWOW.COM
EL PASO, TX 79901 US
Support@USCOOTERS.COM
Shortly before noon on May 22, 2024, [REDACTED] was riding her U-Scooter/E-TWow on [REDACTED]. She was on her way to the [REDACTED] station as part of her daily commute to work. She had been driving this route for over a year without incident.
Suddenly, the front wheel of the scooter locked. Before [REDACTED] could react, she was thrown over the handlebars and onto the road. She sustained a broken orbital bone, a laceration over her right eye, and road rash/soft tissue damage on her hip, her right forearm and both knees.
 Thankfully, she was wearing a helmet, but the damage to her face was severe and paramedics transported her to [REDACTED]. Her pain was so intense that, in the ambulance, paramedics administered two doses of fentanyl.
At the hospital, [REDACTED] underwent a full CT scan and X-Rays, which identified the broken orbital bone in her face. In addition, she was given morphine and oxycodone to deal with her severe pain. She spent seven hours in the trauma ward of the hospital before being released. As a result of the accident, she missed several days of work and continues to experience debilitation and pain from her injuries. It may be months before she is back to normal.
 Upon doing some basic [REDACTED], [REDACTED] discovered that other ETWOW scooter users have experienced the same product flaw that resulted in her crash.  Here is the reference to others experiencing this product flaw:  
[REDACTED]
The scooter has not been turned on since the crash. [REDACTED] has photos of her injuries and documentation from the hospital as well.
The front motor wheel does not behave like a normal wheel.  When the scooter is off there is a lot of resistance to the spin.  So when the battery dies, i walk the scooter instead of riding it manually because of this motor wheel resistance.  It has been this way since i took the scooter out of the box and i believe is a normal part of the design.  I think this design is perhaps why there are problems with the front "wheel locking".  If I'm going 30mph and suddenly a fuse blows (or something), my wheel motor will die and go into its state of resistance.  The resistance at high speed could be creating the sensation of "wheel lock".

Here is [REDACTED] description of the accident:
I was commuting to work on my usual route in the bike lane, alert as always on the lookout for potholes and debris. Suddenly my front motor wheel locked and I was thrown forward onto the pavement. I was going roughly 25mph down an overpass. Though it happened in a manner of seconds, I was aware that this incident was caused by the front wheel locking up. I heard a noise that I am familiar with, a noise made by the regenerative braking system when it is engaged. But I was NOT pushing the brake lever. Then I heard and felt the front motor wheel skid on the pavement. The handlebars were facing perfectly forward throughout this and I was launched head-first over them. The first thing I saw after hitting the pavement was blood dripping from my eye onto the pavement. I could hardly breathe from the pain and shock. A man pulled over and engaged me in concerned questions. He gave me a clean washcloth to apply pressure to my bleeding eye. I was writhing in pain but conscious. A second man walked over and I watched him fetch my scooter that was on its side spinning in circles in the middle of the road. I don't know how it was spinning on its side without an operator pushing the lever, or how it got so far into the road. He asked me how to turn it off.  I felt too pained to answer, but the other man helped him and it was draped over the road barrier near me.  The first man stayed and engaged me until numerous police showed up. The police talked to this man and he may be a witness to the whole event. The ambulance arrived next. 

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in severe injuries including a broken orbital bone and required hospitalization, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) as similar incidents have been reported by other users of the same scooter model.

incident_description: We ordered a diving board for our outdoor, in-ground swimming pool from BackyardPoolSuperstore via Amazon. One of the color choices for the board is grey, and this is the color we ordered.  We ordered this after our pool was closed for the season, so it was not used until the following season which was about a week ago.  Upon installation, we had friends over to swim. This was the first time the new board was in use.  One friend went to use the diving board and immediately yelled out "HOT!!!"  and jumped off quickly.  He said the diving board burned his feet.  I went to investigate, and the board was extremely hot.  I used an infrared thermometer, and on cloudy days the board's temperature ranges anywhere from 130 degrees - 150 degrees F. On sunny days, it registering 200 degrees F.  According to the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC), "Most adults will suffer third-degree burns if exposed to 150 degree water for two seconds. Burns will also occur with a six-second exposure to 140 degree water or with a thirty second exposure to 130 degree water."  Therefore, this product CAN and WILL cause 3rd degree burns.

incident_description: My husband and I purchased two new Seaview 180 V3 Full Face Snorkel masks from Amazon on June 2, 2023.  We used these on a Mexico Vacation in a cove with little to no waves viewing sea turtles June 15, 2023.  Both of us almost passed out and could not make it back to shore.  Luckily the guide noticed and was able to pull us back in where we could barely walk and my lungs hurt.  I contacted the company the next day to explain what happened and see if there was something with the product or how we were using it that caused this.  They insisted it was us or the ocean (ocean was very calm).  Today I read about a study done in July 2020 where snorkels have been known to cause hypoxia by Rapid Onset Pulmonary Edema (ROPE).  This company should have known about the study and it was irresponsible to not mention it as a possibility.  Snorkelers die from this.  I'm very concerned others may have similar issues with the product.  We stopped using them after that one event because it was terrifying to slowly asphyxiate.
justification: The incident involved severe physical distress and potential injury (lung pain, near loss of consciousness), but no death occurred.

Each of the dangerous conditions discussed within this report and complaint

Bombardier Recreational Products Inc. has engaged in a pattern delay, deny and

VI. CONCLUSION.

incident_description:
QingSong Full Face Snorkel Mask for Adults & Kids, Snorkeling Gear with Camera Mount, 180 Degree Panoramic View Snorkel Set Anti-Fog Anti-Leak

Bought this product for 2 children age 9 and 7. Prior to use, product was assembled per instructions and fitted for each child. Both children did a very short test with them (1 minute) in bathtub and no problems were noted. Both children stated good seal and easy to use. Product was taken to trip in Bahamas for snorkeling. Product was again assembled and inspected prior to use. Mask was placed on both children without any noted issues or difficulty breathing. 7 year old began snorkeling with no issues of breathing or talking. In less than 5 minutes, 7 year old began complaining of severe frontal headache. 7 year old taken to shore and mask removed. 7 year old had severe headache for approximately 20 minutes. This headache slowly resolved prior to getting  medical attention. As a healthcare professional, this headache correlates with hypercapnia from CO2 rebreathing. Few minutes after 7 year old taken to shore, 9 year old began complaining of headache and fatigue. 9 year old taken to shore and symptoms resolved approximately 15 minutes after mask removal. This is being reported as safety concern for hypercapnea from rebreathing CO2 which could lead to unresponsiveness and respiratory failure. Concern that CO2 is unable to clear appropriately from mask.
justification: The incident involved two children experiencing severe headaches and fatigue due to CO2 rebreathing, indicating potential hypercapnia, which is a health injury.

incident_description:
I was riding a Rad Power Bikes RadWagon 4, when the bolt holding on the kickstand snapped in half, causing the kickstand to fall off the bike and become lodged under the rear tire. As I was in motion, that cause the back wheel to jam, the bike to stop suddenly and skid sideways, and I narrowly avoided falling into the street along with my two small children who were riding on the back of the bike. We were in an intersection when this happened and could have easily been struck by a vehicle. It is only a combination of the fact that I'm relatively strong, and pure luck that we were not injured or killed.

I did a bit of research and there are multiple reports of this bolt snapping in exactly the same way on [REDACTED] and in the Rad Owners [REDACTED] group, so this is not an isolated incident. I reported it to Rad Power Bikes and they told me to install a new kickstand with the exact same hardware which seems certifiably insane. They need to figure out a recall for the kickstand assembly so it can be attached to the bike with more than a clearly insufficiently strong bolt. If they're not going to do it voluntarily then perhaps you can make them.
justification: The incident caused a dangerous situation but no injury occurred, and there are multiple reports of the same issue indicating it's likely to happen again.

incident_description: On November 14, 2024 I purchased a Queitkat Apex Pro ebike. From day one I have had nothing but problems with the bike and the service of the company. First, after receiving the bike, I noticed the rear wheel sprocket protector wasnt installed on the bike and it is a required safety part that is required to be installed on any bike sold in the USA. It was only after several arguments and an escalation to a manager that it was finally taken care of. Since then I have had many other major issues with the bike including having to replace the shifter which could have caused the exact problem the missing part is meant to prevent. More recently I noticed some loose fasteners that hold the dropouts on the rear frame. Upon inspection I found that there is a major design flaw with using these fasteners as they should never be used for an application like this and their failure is imminent in a very short time. I have only had the bike for 4 months over the winter with few miles on it and something like this should not be wearing out so quickly and actually at all as it is a critical part of the frame and its failure will certainly cause an injury to the rider. Not only is the company refusing to recognize this, they are refusing to honor their lifetime frame warranty and replace these parts when they wear out again. The failure of these fasteners will certainly cause injury in the future and the companies refusal to recognize this honor their warranty needs to be investigated before an injury occurs. I have overwhelming evidence to support my case and would be glad to provide whatever is necessary.
justification: The description indicates potential for injury due to design flaws and imminent failure of critical parts, but no actual injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: On Monday, March 11, 2024 my son came to me and said his headlight did not work on his bike. He also indicated there was a chemical smell coming from the light. I looked at the light charging port and noticed the weather cover was melted. There were not any injuries that happened, but did result in low visibility while riding his bike that night, which could increase the risk of a crash. The battery discharge could have led to a burn. I work in a product safety position for a career, so I went to the device and began to remove the outer cover. I found the lithium battery included in the light to be damaged specifically it was shorted out against the charging port. upon further review, I found the two screws that attached the mounting plate at the bottom of the light were extended and damage the outer case of the lithium battery.  I will be filing a complaint with the manufacturer on Amazon where I purchased this in September 2022.
justification: The incident involved a damaged lithium battery and melted cover, posing a potential burn risk, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
2019 Can-Am Defender Max X Mr HD10, spontaneous fire, incinerated side-by-side minus frame and bumper; I was using utility vehicle ([REDACTED]), no injuries occurred. I drove the machine from my house to end of driveway to pay tractor for pulling my truck out of the ditch (drove 1/2 mile)(heavy snow and ice storm affected Tennessee). Machine was turned off for 10 minutes while I paid the tractor guy. Turned it on to drive home and went 2/5 mile and high temperature gauge came across dash. I turned off machine, took keys out, and walked home 3/5 mile down driveway. As I was walking up to house my wife came out and notice smoke in the distance. We drove our vehicles immediately to side-by-side and it was engulfed in flames, already nearly melted down. Fire department came and put out remaining fire which at that time was mostly burning rubber from the tires ashes. Entire machine other than frame and bumper was incinerated. Conditions - unusual heavy snow in Tennessee. Current recall on 2020/2021 Apache model for snow clogging CVT intake "The stock CVT air intake can become completely obstructed with snow causing the drive belt to overheat and break, posing a fire hazard." Recall on BRP site specifically states other models are not affected and I believe this to be false. They specifically state The heavy snow conditions created similar environment to Apache models posing same risk. Machine was in excellent condition, just over 100 hours. BRP website states that snorkel version does not need update with recall 
"If your vehicle is NOT modified with a track kit
Your vehicle does NOT need to be updated. "

I feel this to be inaccurate as heavy snowfall likely caused obstruction of CVT air intake leading to high engine temperatures and spontaneous fire even after engine was turned off. The safety of my children and anyone riding in the vehicle could have been compromised if I had not immediately stopped, turned off machine, and walked home. I feel Can-am knew about this problem and did not inform owners of possibility. There are recalls dating back to 2013 regarding exhaust clogging with leaves (January 29, 2013). Machine was not being used in any extraordinary manner. 

I can provide pictures when requested.
justification: The incident involved a spontaneous fire that incinerated the vehicle but resulted in no injuries.

incident_description: The inflator on my BCD (scuba vest) malfunctioned while I was on a dive (scuba dive). It got stuck in the on position which caused it to automatically inflate my BCD when I was roughly 100 feet under water. I could not get it to stop inflating. I had to use my emergency dump air valve multiple times in order to safely ascend to the surface to end the dive. This is very dangerous. If a diver goes up too fast, the diver can suffer a stroke, a heart attack, joint damage, irreversible lung damage, and/or a whole host of other bad things, including death in some cases. I was diving long enough at depth that there would have been a very bad result. The BCD is pretty new, has been cleaned thoroughly after every dive, and has been routinely serviced. It had to be manufactured incorrectly or they used materials that degrade too fast when used in the ocean (which is where people dive much of the time) There is no reason the BCD inflator should have malfunctioned in this manner and it was not due to user error. I have contacted the manufacturer (Huish Outdoors - Oceanic) and they now have my BCD in their possession. They are trying to get me to pay to have it fixed. I no longer trust this equipment with my life nor do I trust the manufacturer to fix the problem in a manner that does not place my life at risk in the future. I have spoken with other divers on Scuba discussion boards and there are others who have experienced similar problems. Unfortunately, only those who live to tell can report issues. I want a full refund so I can purchase a good quality BCD but my primary concern and objective is getting an unsafe product off of the market. There was already another recall from this same manufacturer on a weight pocket issue. The handles broke. This is dangerous because the handles are needed so that a diver can dump weights in an emergency situation. It is a drowning hazard to have faulty weight pockets.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous malfunction without injury, and similar issues have been reported by other divers, indicating a possible recurring problem.

incident_description: I'm a professional snowboard equipment reviewer who has done my job for 20 years. In 2019 I saw a 3D rendering for a new snowboard binding that was being touted as the future of snowboarding. In that 3D rendering I noticed some fatal design flaws that only someone as experienced as myself would and expressed my concerns. The designers of the product dismissed my knowledge base immediately. Fast forward to 2022 and they are rolling out their product and I express my concerns for their product and their limited knowledge of how snowboard bindings work. In 2023 after demand from my audience I bought a pair to review and upon getting the product in my hands and inspecting it I noticed catastrophic design and manufacturing faults. I then took the product to Copper Mountain in Colorado to test them. I posted on [REDACTED]  that I was testing them and 3 different employees from 3 different shops reached out to me and informed me that the mounting hardware that they use was not up to industry spec and were sheering off inside the inserts that they screw into and I was advised to swap out the screws. Upon riding the product I noticed that the locking mechanism that they claim has a fail safe failed me on 3 different laps down the slopes I was testing it on. This caused the safety hook and locking mechanism to disengage and allow the foot to release. As I'm a highly experienced snowboard rider with over 3900 days on snow I knew how to safely stop myself from being injured. But, what I've noticed is that this company will not acknowledge publicly to anyone that these have this issue. Upon further inspection after riding them for only 4 hours I noticed severe deterioration of the plastic used in the product, that the screws had shown signs of fatigue, and that the locking mechanism was already starting to wear and fail. In my expert opinion and as someone who has ridden hundreds of snowboard bindings I could see this failing to the general public. After concluding my review of the product I actually released it on [REDACTED]  has I have done with countless other products and there were over 50 comments out of over 750 that said they had a disengagement issue that caused them to release or that it failed to safely and securely lock in. The company will not acknowledge this and is instead hiring influencers to push the product as safe as well as buy fake reviews to bolster their image. You as a commission have recalled a similar product from [REDACTED] bindings in March of 2012. I feel that a recall of this product due to failure in the locking mechanism, release spring, and insert mounting screws is needed.
justification: The incident describes a product with multiple safety failures, including disengagement and deterioration, which could lead to injuries, and reports from users confirm such incidents.

incident_description: I recently purchased a Lectric XP Step-Thru 3.0 White Long-Range eBike. When the bike was delivered, the rear tire/tube was deflated and separated from the bicycle. Upon contacting the company about this issue, I was informed that there was a known defect in the tubes and wheels for the bicycle I purchased. I was told that a batch of the bikes had weak tubes prone to rupture, burrs on the wheel rims that could lead to repeated tube punctures, and/or screws sticking out on the rims that could lead to repeated tube punctures. After I reported the issue, I received what seemed to be a form email about possible fixes for these issues. I had no idea that this was an issue before I purchased this bike, I was not informed about this issues before I received the bike, and I did not find out until I contacted customer service. As far as I know, no widespread notice has been sent out to customers about this issue as I have not received any such public notice even though the product I purchased was affected. I suppose I was lucky, because if my tire had not arrived deflated, I might have thought that the inevitable flat tire was due to user error or environmental hazard. I was never put in harms way because I have been unable to ride the bike even once. However, those customers that are not informed of these defects may repeatedly experience flat tires without understanding that the cause may be a defect with the bicycle wheels and tubes. Lectric offered to pay for me to get the problems repaired, but in the end I could not access a bike shop that would handle the issue. So that I could repair the bike myself, Lectric eventually agreed to send me new front and rear wheels, which are currently on backorder until the end of October. Originally I was told that there would be no point in them sending me new wheels because the new wheels might have the same problem. This indicates that they know there is a problem, but have not fixed it, and are not necessarily checking the products they send out to the public. I recently read about their disc brake caliper recall on the same model bike I purchased (albeit different dates), and this makes me worried about the safety of the product in general.
justification: The incident describes a product defect causing inconvenience and potential safety issues, but no actual injury or harm occurred.

incident_description:
I received a SKLZ Grip Strength Trainer as a Christmas gift in 2022 and have been using it on and off for a year. As I was using it yesterday, the steel spring which regulates the amount of force it takes to squeeze the device, failed catastrophically with one piece of metal shooting off like a rocket (I haven't located this piece yet.) When I went onto their website to register a complaint/post a review, I saw that 7 of the 13 product reviews posted, were about the same problem ([REDACTED] ). My post is still "in moderation" and is pending. The first review reporting a failed spring was posted 4 years ago yet the product is still on the market.

I did not injure myself, nor anyone else, but there is a real possibility someone might have been injured had they been in the same room with me. The spring failed due to metal fatigue and the product is clearly unsafe and should be removed from the market until such time the product is redesigned or a stronger metal is chosen for the spring.

Because of the position of the bars, his head was tightly wedged between the two bars - the bar was pressing against his neck and choking him. I quickly tried to pull his head out but wasnÃÂt able to maneuver his head the way I needed to while he was standing on the bars. Meanwhile his face was turning red from not being able to breathe. I picked him up to try to take the weight off of his neck while my mom pushed his head forward, turned it sideways, and then pulled it out.ÃÂ Afterwards, he was crying and scared, catching his breathe, and had red marks on his neck and collarbone. Otherwise he was ok, thankfully,ÃÂ 

All I can think about now is what would have happened if I hadnÃÂt been standing right in front of him when he did this. What if this took place while I had stepped out of the room to switch loads of laundry or prepare a meal? I imagine what it could have been like him finding him like that a minute too late, and feel an urgent need to inform others. 

It could have ended terribly wrong had I not been right there. We were just spared a potential tragedy, and I donÃÂt want this to happen to any other child (especially if they donÃÂt have a parent close by like I was to help them out of the situation.) After this weekend, I believeÃÂ there needs to be a warning that this is a risk because having him get his head stuck and choking was not something I ever imagined having to worry about with this toy.ÃÂ I am reporting this incident so that something horrific doesnÃÂt happen to another unsuspecting family.

incident_description: My daughter was riding a Mototec 48V electric dirtbike and received a severe laceration on her leg. She was sitting stationary on the bike and then applied the throttle. The bike lurched forward and caused her to fall to the left. Her speed was very low, maybe 2~3 mph. The fall itself caused a small sharp bracket on the outside of the kickstand to puncture her leg. When she rotated her body to get up from the fall, the bracket that had punctured her leg then continued to slice open her leg. Her leg was severely lacerated through all layers of skin, about 5 inches in length. After examining the bike after the incident, the bracket is in a location that will contact the leg during a fall, with the weight of the bike on that bracket. The bracket is also stamped steel and is very sharp on the edge. This is a safety defect. I noticed on Mototec's website that the bracket has been relocated to the inner side of the kickstand on new models shown on their website. CPSC need to investigate Mototec to consider recalling these products and preventing other injuries.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe laceration, indicating an injury (severity level 3). The design flaw and sharp bracket suggest similar injuries are likely under comparable conditions (likelihood 4).

When I let up on the throttle, it went to ÃÂneutralÃÂ for a split second before increasing to full. Due to the electric skateboard having bindings, I was unable to jump off. Based on the data collected, I crashed going roughly 35mph, resulting in a fractured neck, fractured back, serious concussion, and road rash. incident_description:
I am reporting a brake failure (both front and back brakes) that appears to be due to a design flaw in the brakes used for the Schwinn Twinn tandem mountain bike, model S7962AZ.  The brakes failed while my wife and I were riding the bike.  This could have resulted in a serious injury, but only minor injuries resulted; although the brakes failed while riding down a steep hill, I was able to stop the bike by dragging my feet on the pavement.  In doing so, I did sustain a minor back injury, from the difficulty involved in getting the bike to stop.
I examined the brakes closely to see why the failure occurred.  The brake is a cable-pull brake: you pull a brake lever mounted to the handlebar, which pulls a cable, and that cable is connected to lever at the brake.  The lever rotates, and closes the caliper, causing the brake pads to press against the disc rotor to stop the bike.  The design flaw occurs when the brake pads become worn.  Specifically, when the brake pads wear down, the caliper must close more in order for contact to occur.  In order to close the caliper more, the brake lever must be pulled further, causing the lever at the brake to rotate further, which closes the caliper.  When the lever at the brake rotates past a certain amount, it reaches the end of its threads, and "pops" out, completely disengaging the brake.  This happened in both the front and the rear brake, leaving us with no way to stop.
I can reproduce this problem if you need to see it demonstrated, and can send in a video.  This problem only shows up when the bike has been used a lot, as the brake pads need to be worn down.  However, once this happens, the bike is very dangerous, and I'm worried that someone could be seriously injured unless Schwinn addresses the problem.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor back injury due to brake failure, which could have been more severe under different circumstances.

The product in question is a Jetson bicycle. Jetson Light Rider X 20" Wheel Light-Up Bike, Includes Light-Up Frame and Wheels, 3 Different Light Modes, Easily Adjustable Seat Height, 20" Rubber Tires, Blue, JLRX20-BBL

The bicycle was being used for a test run after assembly. Upon bringing the bike back inside the house, I made a sharp right turn to enter the living room, which led to the inadvertent brake activation due to the misplacement of the brake calipers.

How did any injuries occur?

However, I emphasized the potential severity of the defect and insisted on escalating the matter. I returned the bike and requested a replacement, hoping it was an isolated incident. justification: The incident resulted in a concussion, torn rotator cuff, torn biceps tendon, and long-term disability, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) based on the context of a voluntary recall and the described incident.

incident_description:
Peloton Bike+    Post Seat Drops randomly, and Can slip a few levels to completely drops all the way down during a ride.    Have had multiple support calls with Peloton regarding the matter over months, last email to support on 9/12/23, and last calls on  9/18/23.    Over the last 6 or so months this problems has occurred numerous times.   Peloton has replaced the seat post, post sleeve and turn knob multiple times but with same design and problem reoccurs every time.

More details   The seat post level is the height of the bike seat for the rider.   Values range from 0 (1 indicated and is lowest), to 42.   I set my level to 22.5 typically.   Randomly, during a ride, the seat post level can slip gradually from 22.5 to anywhere from 17-20, or completely drops.   Slippage occurs pretty much every ride,    Occasionally the seat post would rapidly fall completely or near completely down, but this appears to be happening more often now.   During my ride on Sept 12, when I filed my last support ticket, the seat dropped quickly all the way down to 0 (below 1 indicated on post).    Luckily all my weight was not on the seat and I was able to catch myself, otherwise I would have gotten injured.    The same issue has occurred when my daughter was on the bike as well.   

This issue can easily cause significant injury, especially to vertebrates in lower back when sitting on seat and it rapidly falls.  Let alone potentially causing the person to fall off the bike.   

Numerous complaints regarding this exact problem exist on various websites on the internet, and multiple sub-threads on each site including Peloton Forum, [REDACTED], and the [REDACTED] site to name a few.   Below are only a few links of other uses reporting the same problem.    One article indicating the Peloton admitting the problem exists on the original Bike (but not the Bike+).    This is false the problem exists on the Bike+ as well, and numerous of the threads/discussions on the internet (some links included below) clearly state by the users they own the Bike+ (as I do) and experienced the exact issue.   

Sample of various threads regarding issue:

[REDACTED]     
         Multiple Complaints about Bike+ Seat Post

[REDACTED]
              This article discusses issue, but claims Peloton only indicates problem with Original Bike not Bike+    (not true)

[REDACTED]
           Thread Doesn't specifically indicate Bike or Bike+  but the problem is the same.    

Note, this appears to be a design flaw.   The turn knob pushes against a piece of V shaped plastic in the post sleeve that pushes against the post and that is how it is supposed to hold the post in place.   I ride multiple of types of spin bikes in the Gym ([REDACTED]), all use notches in the seat post to hold the post and seat in place.   

On a side note, I've been on hold waiting for Peloton support while writing this,   on hold, get connected, then disconnected multiple times.   So far, been on phone for over 2 hrs.                I can Provide before/after pictures as if required.   I asked I could possibly set up a video to record the post during a ride.
justification: The incident involves a recurring seat post slippage issue that has nearly caused injury and poses a significant risk, especially to the lower back, with multiple reports of the same problem.

incident_description:
I used these plates only about 6-10 times over the period of about 6 months. There were times the slide mechanism in one of them would 'jam' and sometimes be hard to disengage. I didn't think anything of it, though. I never dropped the weights, always used the plastic holder that came with them, and never caused impact to the plates in anyway. After this incident, I read the manual to ensure I didn't use them incorrectly. I do use these plates at max weight on most workouts, usually for squats, so I may be an outlier.

Tonight though, I missed closing hours for the gym and decided to use these weights to do a set a normally do with regular dumbbells. One of these exercises are aptly named "skullcrushers" at a full 50lb weight setting - I do a variant though where I put the dumbbell behind just my head, in case it slips or something happens. Thankfully, I did that, because the bolt holding the plates sheared off mid exercise, the sliding mechanism popped out, and 2 or 3 of the plates on that side of the dumbbell whacked me right on the very top of head leaving a nice knot. I was lucky I didnt have the dumbbell above my face at the full extension, as normal skullcrushers call for. 

The bolt holding the sliding mechanism is only about 10mm in diameter, and appears to have sustained shear failure. The length of the moment arm of the sliding mechanism at full extension is about 140mm. I do not believe a single bolt is sufficient for such load.


I'd be glad to ship the dumbbells back for analysis by their engineering team or CPSC for further analysis
justification: The incident resulted in a head injury (a knot on the head) due to equipment failure during exercise, but no death or severe injury occurred.

incident_description:
Bought a Killer Instinct crossbow 22 days ago and fired it for the 3rd time today. 

I was cocking my crossbow. When the metallic click happened to indicate the weapon was cocked and put on safe, I began to unhook the cocking rope. When I did that, the crossbow dry fired. Pieces of the trigger mechanism and the safety mechanism broke off and went flying. Upon inspection after the fact, I discovered the metal hooks that hold the string back actually snapped off and appeared to be made of very low quality, porous looking metal. Had this happened while deer hunting with a bolt in the bow, that could have easily killed someone. Luckily, I had my hands clear, there was no bolt in the bow, and I was alone. Since then, I have spoke to another killer instinct customer who had similar trigger issues, resulting in an accidental discharge. Both I and that person were offered to have the bow ÃÂfixedÃÂ, but not to have the underlying issue of a faulty trigger/safety mechanism redesigned and replaced.

incident_description:
Hi,
Lectric E-Bikes has sold a model (XP 3.0) of bicycle which has defective brakes. They have issued a "service bulletin" silently in a corner of their website informing owners that they must regularly (in my experience, at least every two weeks) adjust the brake cables to compensate. They recommended that owners not comfortable with adjusting their brakes take their bike to a shop, but offer no compensation for any labor that these shops may charge.
The service bulletin is here:
https://help.lectricebikes.com/article/8hgjinfvtg-xp-3-0-brake-service-bulletin
https://files.helpdocs.io/djeddasp2e/other/1684447682318/lectric-safety-bulletin-2.pdf

Additionally, Lectric has started shipping hydraulic brakes on new units of this bicycle, that are not affected by this issue. Owners of existing units were meant to receive an email by "mid-July" with a link to order the brake upgrade kit for free. At the end of July, I had received no such email. I contacted them, and received a link to the form. This form stated on it that in order to get the upgrade for free, one must submit the form by July 31st. Notably, the link to this form is not published on their website, and has not been publicized in any manner that I can locate. Perhaps it was sent in a sales newsletter, but that is not sufficient given the issue at hand.

Lectric once again provides no compensation for labor charged by bicycle repair shops to install this new brake set, which is absurd given the safety-critical nature, and the fact that the original brakes were defective.

In my opinion, a recall should be issued, and Lectric should be forced to provide new brakes swiftly, and pay for all repairs relating to this matter.
justification: The incident involves defective brakes on e-bikes, which could lead to injuries if not properly maintained, but no actual injuries or deaths are reported.

Yesterday these lights were replaced, and upon inspecting them they were flooded with water, which means the pool water was in contact with electrical current posing an electrocucion risk. 

Upon inspection of the lights both lights had a seal on the back that had shrunk and failed.
justification: The incident describes a potential electrocution risk due to water contact with electrical current, but no actual injury or death occurred.

So all of my wheel studs have been over torqued numerous times due to this bad info and have resulted in failures of 4 at this time. This is the Aventon Soltera 7-speed e-bike (https://www.aventon.com/products/soltera-ebike?variant=41304326865091) and the fenders that I believe caused the accident can be found at: https://www.aventon.com/products/aventon-soltera-fender?variant=41697521041603. I was riding the bike as intended and without warning the bike stopped, going from approximately 18-20mph to a full stop immediately when the fender caught onto the wheel. I landed on my head (wearing a helmet) and was unconscious for a period of time before being transported to a local hospital via ambulance.
justification: The incident resulted in a concussion and facial lacerations, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) because the defect could affect other users under similar conditions.

incident_description: I Went to Dick's Sporting Goods in Daly City, California, on January 16, 2021. to purchase a treadmill that did not emit any kind of chemical odors. The store manager recommended the Nordic Track 2450 Commercial Treadmill, and remarked that treadmill did not emit any chemical odors, but that the store did not have any ?oor models available for my inspection of chemical odor emissions. On January 29, 2021, Dick's Sporting Goods Delivery service, delivered and installed the Nordic Track Commercial Treadmill into my rental apartment, while I read the entire instructional manual, and for which there was noting stated in writing warning that the Nordic Track Commercial Treadmill emitted off gassing of chemical odors, and the likely hood of potential harm from exposure of such chemical emissions. Proceeding the completion of the delivery and installation transaction, I turned on the treadmill, and started a brisk walk, and deep breathing exercise session, and within 15 minutes into the aerobic exercise session on the treadmill, a burst of hot, steaming, offensive, chemical odor immediately started to emit from the internal console of the Nordic Track Commercial 2450 Treadmill, and as a result, I inhaled all such chemical fumes, immediately causing me to experience shortness of breath, uncontrollable coughing, itching throat, dizziness, burning eyes, and burning nostrils, all from the exposure to the chemical emissions from the Nordic Track Commercial 2450 Treadmill. I immediately turned the treadmill off, however; within 30 minutes, my apartment was entirely smelled of an offensive, chemical odor, that continued to emit and linger from the Nordic Track Commercial 2450 Treadmill, up until the day I hired a moving company, paying a fee of $500.00, to return the treadmill back to Dick's Sporting Goods, in Daly City, California. As a result exposure of such chemical emission emitting from the Nordic Track Commercial 2450 Treadmill, I have existing respiratory injuries to this present day.
justification: The incident resulted in respiratory injuries from chemical exposure, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is set to 3 (possible) as such incidents are not common but have been reported.

incident_description:
Incident Type: Drowning Hazard
Product: Blu3 Nomad (New)
Purchase Date: 1-July-2023 
User: [REDACTED]
Description of Event: On my second time out with my new Nomad the unit quit on me with full battery in 25 ft of water. This was on the second of two short dives. On the first, the pump changed behavior and breathing became very labored around 20 ft. I surfaced, and the unit performed fine at shallower depth. I assumed that, perhaps, the unit just performs less efficiently the deeper you go, and decided to give it another try. Upon reaching around the same depth (20ft), breathing again became very labored, along with a noticeable change in the behavior of the pump. I continued to the bottom approximately 5 feet deeper (25ft), and as I started to ascend over concerns about the level of breathing difficulty, the unit ceased to pump air all-together. Fortunately, I had a [REDACTED] and ascended using this device. The Nomad began pumping and free-flowing from the regulator when I made it back to about 15 feet.  While I have no apparent injuries, if someone more prone to panic had experienced this catastrophic failure, the outcome could have easily been serious injury or death.

After doing some research, I learned that earlier units had been recalled for a similar issue.  To be clear, this is a new unit purchased on 1-July-2023 and received on 24-July-2023.  I immediately reached out to Blu3 and reported the incident, and sent a second email when they had not responded within 24 hours.  They did respond this morning (two days after the incident) with a very brief email of recognition and a return authorization to facilitate a forensic inspection of the unit.
justification: The incident involved a catastrophic failure of the diving unit, but no actual injury occurred. The potential for serious injury or death was noted, but not realized.

This has happened three times in the past week resulting in several musculoskeletal injuries to my body. I consider myself and advanced board rider, and I believe this product is very dangerous.

incident_description: I bought a super73 s2 ebike in August of 2021. I've put almost 2000 miles on the bike. A couple of days ago I turned the bike on in my garage and I heard a hissing and popping sound. I saw visible sparks shoot from under the seat of the bike and the charger started blinking red. I turned the bike off and have stored it since. I submitted a support ticket to the manufacturer, who has no phone support, and have not heard back in 4 days. The controller appears to have shorted out and there are holes in the device. I store my bike next to a classic car, this could have started a fire and I don't feel safe storing it even with the battery removed. The video was recorded after the sparks and smoke stopped.  The picture was taken one or two days later when I removed the plastic shield from underneath the seat. I believe this could have injured me if I was sitting on the seat when the incident happened.
justification: The incident involved sparks and potential fire risk, but no injury occurred. The likelihood is possible given the visible damage and potential for harm if the user had been seated.

incident_description: My husband received a One Wheel Pint Skateboard for his birthday.  He is an experienced skateboarder, followed the instructions and all appropriate safety precautions.  While riding, the board shut off abruptly and threw him off of the board, resulting in a severely fractured shoulder.  We are concerned that this product is unsafe and are afraid to continue use.  We have contacted the company and they refuse to take back the product.  We have only had it for two weeks.
justification: The incident resulted in a severely fractured shoulder, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The description suggests the issue is not isolated, indicating a likely occurrence (likelihood 4).

incident_description: My treadmills safety locking bar let go in the middle of the night, the treadmill floor ramp came crashing down and broke the treadmill right off its base. My little Yorkie used to sit right under it, thank goodness he was not there ( sadly passed away this March) it wouldÃÂve killed him. Homeowner states that they plugged it in to charge and left the house about 45 minutes ago and were not home when the fire started. A neighbor heard the smoke alarms and came to investigate and saw smoke when he opened the door leading to the calling of 911.

While towing a child and his mother behind a boat, the WOW 2 Coupe, 2-person flotation toy, the towable filled with water spray and did not drain.  The water filling the towable caused the floating toy to sink to a low level in the water.  When going through a mild wave, the towable went under water along with the riders.  Because the cover is loose over the internal air tube and forms a deep gap while being pulled, the child was partially stuck in between the plastic air tube and the nylon cover.  This gap temporarily trapped the childÃÂs legs in the towable while under water but forward motion did release the child by him sliding backwards and out of the towable.  The child and

incident_description:
There appears to be a systematic design flaw that renders the Radio Flyer L885 bike unsafe to use, especially since kickstands have now broken twice in similar ways under the normal conditions of use. In fact, the break occurred in the same location in both cases...It looks like Radio Flyer has attempted to join two hollow pieces of metal by filling them with some kind of a cement or epoxy which clearly is not strong enough to support the weight of the bike.

This is an ~80 pound bike that could seriously injure or kill a child (which it is advertised to carry) if it unexpectedly tipped over on them, which nearly happened to us.

incident_description:
This caller purchased a monkey climbing toy for the backyard May 2022 for their child.

This backyard climbing toy is advertised to hold 170 lbs.

Their child weighs only 40 lbs.

They put this backyard playground toy together according to directions then allowed their child to play on it.

The first time their child climbed on the four-foot-high climbing toy was in May 2022. One of the structureÃÂs bars fell off it, which could have caused their child to fall but did not get injured.

incident_description: This report involves Infinity Boss Three Disc bicycle. While riding the bicycle down a slope (of a ramp), the rear disc brake broke apart unexpectedly. I strongly think this is a safety issue that could risk many riders' lives when riding Infinity Boss Three Disc bicycle , especially when riders are riding their bicycles on the shared lanes where others vehicles like trucks, coaches, or trailers may be present at times. I requested Infinity Cycle Work to consider performing a post mortem investigation on the discs from the same batch and assess if a recall is required. The Infinity Cycle Work took more than one month to finally came back to me and offered a replacement bicycle in exchange for a full and final release to be executed by me.

incident_description:
On May 25, 2023 we were using our 2020 Honda Pioneer 1000-5 to do some yard work. It unexpectedly accelerated, I applied the brake the front wheels locked up trying to stop it but the back wheels continued to push the vehicle.  It ultimately went down our hill and hit a tree. When this happened it slammed my head into the roll bar giving me a concussion and two cuts requiring staples and stitches. We are unsure why the vehicle accelerated and would not stop but upon further research it appears this is a known issue with a current recall for 2016-2019 Honda Pioneer 1000-5.  Ours is a 2020 falling outside of that recall but was purchased in 2019 so I am concerned that some of the early 2020 models should also be included in that recall.

UPDATED ON 9/28/2023: [I have contacted American Honda again after you alerted me they responded and said I had not contacted them.  After giving them the date and time of my previous contact they said they would open an investigation.  

They concluded the investigation recently but their investigation only states "Honda had made a determination on machine" they will not tell me what if any issues they found.]
justification: The incident resulted in a concussion and cuts requiring medical treatment, indicating an injury.

incident_description: I have a CFMOTO CFORCE 800 XC ATV.   I was riding the ATV and the heat coming from the exhaust (not touching the exhaust but the air surrounding) was so hot that it burned the side of my right leg causing red burns, blistering and extreme pain.   I see other comments online indicating this might be a problem with this model.   I had only been riding the ATV for aprox 20 mins.

incident_description: I was riding the Onewheel, well within my abilities when at ten miles an hour it suddenly came to a stop and I was slammed to the ground. I am certain if not for my helmet I would have been killed or at least had an extremely serious TBI. I also hurt my entire right side and at first thought my elbow might have been broken. I am an avid snowboarder (ex-instructor) and skateboarder and know and accept the normal risk associated with board sports. I had had a few pretty bad falls prior while riding Onewheel but fully admit those were due to operator error. The last fall was absolutely a problem with faulty equipment. Future motion ran a remote diagnostic, declared the product fine, and refused to issue a refund.

incident_description: There is a known and ignored safety issue with the batteries on Future Motion's OneWheel Pint X. The battery box that contains the large, dangerous lithium ion battery has sharp edges that crimp the battery wires. This can cause errors, the rider to be thrown off the board, or fires. Every Pint X that has been opened appears to have damaged wires. They are boards that show damage upon opening the box that just after arrival directly from the manufacturer. Future Motion refuses to recall, refund, or repair the root cause of the issue. They are assuring customers there is nothing wrong, but also told me in an email "Our leadership is investigating the production of new battery units to ensure they are built safely and within tolerance". They are clearly aware that there is an issue, but are refusing to take action. This is all being documented at [REDACTED]
justification: The incident involves damaged battery wires that can cause errors, riders being thrown off, or fires, indicating potential for injury or property damage.

The decedent was riding on an ATV around his father's property. When decedent's brother found decedent hutched over on the ground where the ATV was laying on it's side. Decedent explained that while he was riding in the woods, he did not realize that there was a slight drop off in elevation which caused the ATV to tip over. Once decedent was brought back to their father's house he was complaining of a "panic attack", and rib cramps. His sibling noticed that his left arm was not working properly and he had trouble opening a water bottle, and helping himself up out of a chair. Decedent was taken to [REDACTED] Hospital where he was stabilized and then transported to [REDACTED] Hospital in [REDACTED]. When arriving at [REDACTED]it was determined that decedent had sustained a left flail chest w/fractured rib, multiple lung contusions, left hemothorax and pneumothorax, Grade 2 spleen laceration, no perfusion in left kidney, and left shoulder dislocation from the ATV accident. incident_description: I purchased a go kart online that was approximately 80% assembled.  I finished the assembly at home after I received it.  I used the product as intended.  With less than 3 hours of use, the go kart motor started to leak massive amounts of fuel, the frame and the parking brake broke.
justification: The incident involved mechanical failures (fuel leak, broken frame and brake) but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I purchased a Jupiter X-5 electric bike a little over a year ago (2/2022). Recently, while riding the power has suddenly cut off a number of times - while a sufficient electrical charge was showing on the speedometer! In one instance, it was in traffic, but fortunately,  I was able to get safely to the side of the road.
justification: The power cut off while riding in traffic, but no injury occurred as the rider was able to safely move to the side of the road.

incident_description: Bicycle pedal falls off during riding bike.
justification: A bicycle pedal falling off during riding can lead to loss of control and potential injury.

incident_description: One of the steps on a Rhino climbing stick (RTSL-24, hot foot climbing stick) broke at the weld joint, which caused the user to fall a short distance and suffer torso abrasion.  There are 3 intended weld joints attaching the step to the stem, however 2 joints showed no weld penetration which led to the failure.   The weld joint failure occurred while the climbing stick was being first installed.   Fortunately the user was utilizing a linesman belt.  Injury occurred from the user falling due to the step failure and subsequently contacting the steel climbing stick.   Feradyne is the parent company for Rhino stands.

incident_description:
I have had almost countless issues and safety concerns with my NordicTrack Commercial X32i treadmill over the 2+ years I've owned it. Not only has the machine broken and behaved unexpectedly, it has done so in a way that endangers any user of it. From the research I've gathered from other owners of this treadmill, their experiences are largely consistent with mine.

What happened that made you want to report? - Most recently the treadmill just stopped dead and caused me to hurt areas of my ankle, foot, and heel ( I have not seen a doctor yet but feels like a tendon). This was not a "safety stop" where the key was pulled - this was I am running at 8mph and the treadmill COMPLETELY shuts down. The safety key was still in, belt stops, screen is dead. This is not the first time this has happened.
What type of product(s) were being used? - Treadmill (model in description above)
Who was using the product(s)? - Me
How were the product(s) being used? - According to guidelines for a healthy individual using a treadmill and in accordance with safety guidelines (e.g. safety key)

incident_description:
Re:  Safety Latches on Picnic Cooler Lids

Dear Sirs and Madams:

I am a retired engineer who worked for 23 years for the [REDACTED] in Wichita Kansas.  During my time with [REDACTED](1967 through 1989) I was for several years the design engineering manager for thermal products (picnic coolers and jugs).  In the early 1970ÃÂs the CPSC brought to our attention that the latches on all of our larger picnic coolers could be hazardous to small children.  You might remember that at one time old, discarded refrigerators with solid latching doors became deadly traps for kids.  View your publication [REDACTED].

[REDACTED] had a proven, reliable latching system for all of our metal bodied, plastic lined coolers.  We had never had one instance where a kid was injured by a [REDACTED]cooler and I personally did not believe that we posed a risk.  We were building more than a million of this type of product annually.  I traveled to DC to go before the CPSC and was instructed that we must change our designs.  

On returning from the DC meeting I ran a test with smaller children.  We fixed several sizes of coolers so that each one had breathing holes and put these in a room with younger children and, without instructions (to the kids), simply watched.  The kids were young enough that the latches were a mystery but they eventually unlocked the coolers.  The kids soon opened the lids and got in the coolers.  The kids ÃÂhidÃÂ in the coolers.  Eventually kids sat on the lid when another kid was in the cooler.  They would have found a way to lock another kid in the cooler.  I was convinced that we had to change.  [REDACTED] then changed the design of all medium sized and larger coolers so that the lid of the cooler could be pushed open from the inside with minimal force.  We never saw any problems with the use or popularity of the coolers with the safety latch.

All of this happened 50 years ago.  Now it seems that you have either changed your standards or the manufacturers of picnic coolers have forgotten why we changed to safety lids.  There are several brands of picnic coolers (Yeti and others) that offer large capacity picnic coolers with solid rubber latches/straps that could render their coolers death traps for small kids.  I can think of no reason why the underlying principles of the original decision to require safety latches have changed.
justification: The description highlights a potential death risk to small children from being trapped in coolers with unsafe latches, supported by historical context and testing scenarios.

The following summarizes a life-threatening experience that I had that requires action to inform the public of a potentially fatal danger.

My wife and I purchased, at different times from two different vendors (via Amazon), full-face snorkel masks to use on a trip to the Caribbean this past winter (2022-23).  On Wednesday February 15, 2023 we had favorable conditions (sunny, calm seas, good visibility) and went snorkeling from the beach.  Properly wearing the masks, we swam out to a rock pile (artificial reef) that was close to shore and easily accessible from the beach.  We were out about 20 minutes or so, remaining on the surface the entire time per the mask directions.  During the swim back to shore, I unexpectantly began having trouble moving through the water and almost instantly trouble breathing.  I was still on the surface and properly wearing the mask. It took everything I had to remain on the surface and get back to the waterÃÂs edge.  [I had not inhaled or ingested seawater].  I took off the mask, but was unable to stand and continued to have increasing difficulty breathing.  I knew I was in trouble, but didnÃÂt know at the time that my condition was rapidly declining from CO2 poisoning and insufficient oxygen.

Lifeguards and Security from [REDACTED] came to help my wife and provide me with aid.  Staff from the adjacent [REDACTED] Resort came to my aid as well.  An ambulance was called, but my condition continued to decline from the CO2 poisoning.  Shortly after the ambulance arrived, I lost consciousness.  I was informed (after the fact) that my vitals crashed while in the ambulance, and CPR had to be administered to restore vital signs.  After the ambulance arrived at the hospital and I was taken into the emergency treatment room, my vitals crashed again.  CPR was administered a second time and, upon vital signs being restored, I was intubated and placed on a ventilator for a few hours.  Several hours from the initial distress, with the timely assistance on the beach, life-saving medical care and the subsequent ventilation with oxygen and additional medical treatment, my vital signs began returning to normal and I began to recover.

While on the beach, a passer-by had commented to my wife that the issue I was having (un-beknown to us) might be related to the use of the full-face mask, which she still had in her hand.  During the ambulance ride to the ER, my wife began researching online and quickly discovered that my situation, progression and symptomology were all consistent with many (too many) other traumatic events involving the use of full-face snorkel masks.  Unfortunately, for some individuals the outcome was more dire than even my situation.  People have died.  IÃÂnearly died.  

This danger exists, it is real.  The awareness of general knowledge regarding this danger is INSUFFICIENT and UNACCEPTABLE.  ConsumersÃÂpeopleÃÂshould not have to conduct in-depth research to learn about dangers like this.  These products should be pulled from the market.  Until that occurs, all platforms marketing these masks MUST include clear and obvious warnings that their use (even proper use) CAN BE FATAL.

UPDATED ON 6/5/2023: [Per the email below, I have conducted additional research and found the information for the deficiency identified:

Manufacturer or Private Labeler

The additional information for the mask is as follows:

QingSong Full Face Snorkel Mask
Sold by Songxin Products

The mask was purchased through Amazon. Order Date March 7 2022. Order # [REDACTED]

I trust that this information is sufficient for the publishing of my report.  This is a life-threatening situation regarding even the 'proper' use of these products.
FYI, my wife who did not have an incident, was using a mask from a different vendor.  I fear however, that my near-death incident is not isolated to the specific mask maker/model that I was using.  My hypothesis is that the unacceptable number of deaths and other incidents associated with the use of these devices will be attributed to multiple makes and models of the devices.]
