incident_description:
At 4pm, Sunday, April 16, 2023, I drove my ATV out of the garage to hose off some dirt that had accumulated on the snowplow blade.  The ATV was on a trickle charger, stored indoors in a heated garage at all times.  I drove it approx. 50 ft. and parked it on a gravel area adjacent to my concrete driveway.  I hosed off the blade in a minute or so.  I then hosed off the underside of all four fenders.  This whole process took 3-4 minutes.  The engine was cold, the ignition was shut off and the transmission was in park.  The engine was clean--no accumulated oil, grease, or grime and no gasoline leaks or odors.  The gas tank had been filled a couple weeks prior and it was nearly full.  The seats, engine, running boards, and utility boxes were all clean so I did not spray any of those areas.

After cleaning the ATV, I left it in place.  I then backed my truck onto the concrete driveway and gave it a quick rinse with the hose.  This only took 3-4 minutes.  I finished all this about 4:10 pm.  At this point, I looked at my ATV and thought:  "I need to put that in the garage".  My pickup was blocking access to the garage stall where I park my ATV so I decided it could wait until morning.  It had been a warm day and the weather was good.

About 9:20 pm I was in the kitchen reading when I heard a muffled boom that sounded like distant thunder.  It had been a rather warm day so I thought thunder was certainly possible.  I did not give it another thought.  About a minute or two later I heard a second boom. Again, I gave it no thought.  Then another minute or two went by and I heard a third boom.  At this point things weren't sounding quite right so I went out my front door (north side).  It was pitch dark and calm, no wind.  I thought:  "what is going on?".  I then heard a noise on the east side of my house at the lower level in the garage/driveway area.  As I neared the NE corner of my house, I noticed a large orange glow.  When I cleared the corner, I saw that my Polaris ATV was completely engulfed in a massive inferno! Everything was on fire.  The seats, gas tank, fenders, utility box, running boards, dash were all gone.  All I saw was a burning frame and 4 tires on fire.  My ATV was completely gone so I ran down to save my pickup truck which was only 10 feet from the burning ATV.  I quickly moved the truck and then grabbed the garden hose, knocking down the fire in a few minutes.

At this point I fully expected fire trucks to come rolling up with lights flashing and sirens blaring.  That never happened, which was puzzling.  There was vehicle traffic on [REDACTED] approximately 1/3 mi. below my house.  My house sits on top of a prominent hill and that fire could been seen clearly in many directions from 2-3 miles away.  Nobody called.  The next day I checked with the police/sheriff's office to review their 911 logs from Sunday night.  They checked from 8:30 pm to 10:30 pm and nobody called in this fire.  I live in the country about 7 1/2 mi. from town so it is very dark and quiet where I live.   A fire of this size could not have been missed, but surprisingly nobody called it in.



In retrospect, the three muffled "booms" I thought was thunder were most likely my tires and gas tank exploding.  I suspect the fire had been kicking up for at least 3-4 min. (5?) before I went outside and discovered the inferno.

After I knocked down the fire, I noticed that the fabric cover on my boat had melted in the bow area.  The boat was only 5 feet from the ATV.   I never observed any open flames on the boat cover.  I stayed up until 11:30 to make sure a new fire didnÃÂt reignite.  Early the following morning, I inspected my [REDACTED] pickup for any fire/heat damage.  I noticed that a small, plastic trim piece on the right front quarter panel had warped and buckled due to the heat.  I took several pictures of the truck, boat, and ATV on my [REDACTED].
justification: The incident involved a significant fire causing property damage (ATV destroyed, minor damage to truck and boat) but no injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
A product that I purchased as an outdoor activity for my children, which is clearly a product marketed and intended for use as a childrens outdoor recreation, actually failed while being used as intended by my three younger sons and resulted in significant injuries being suffered by each of them. The product: NINJA WARRIOR OBSTACLE COURSE KIT  is manufactured by GASKY KIDS and was purchased under my account through Amazon.com in April of 2021 for a total price of $177.70. The kit is designed to be suspended between two anchor points, we used two trees roughly 30ft apart, and once the proper tension is achieved through a large ratchet style piece of hardware affixed to one end of the strap, special clips and hangers can be attached to the line from which various rope and swing style toys can be added down the length of the line. The goal is to attempt to make an obstacle course from one side to the other and cross the obstacles without touching the bottom strap or ground. 
As stated, my three youngest boys, ages 4, 6, and 11 and have a combined weight of 110 lbs total, were playing on the line at the time of the incident and were all spaced apart on different attachments as well, when the 2" main overhead strap experienced complete product failure and was torn apart almost exactly in two equal pieces. As such, the failure caused everything attached to the line, including children, to suddenly, and violently be dropped to the ground from heights ranging from 3ft. to 8.5ft from the ground. Not only was my 4yr old slammed into the closest tree trunk before falling off of the swing he was sitting on, my oldest was climbing the cargo net attachment that was included with the set and had just reached the top when the line broke, resulting in him practically face planting into the ground from the highest possible point of this set up. As for my 6yr old, he was on a trapeze bar at the time and suffered a busted lip thanks to his knee being plunged into his face after hitting the ground unexpectedly. I am thankful that none of them were struck directly by that top strap when it came apart and all of the tension suddenly unleashed in opposite directions.
Fortunately none of the injuries were serious enough to require a trip to the ER and all three boys were bandaged and iced for most of the afternoon. Once I had my babies cared for, my attention turned to figuring out what happened and why this product failed. My husband and I both looked over the entire strap, which was now in two seperate parts, and discovered that the material appeared to be frayed significantly at the point where the failure occured. We also noticed that each place on the strap where the supplied hangers were attached, the strap showed signs of wearing and stress underneath the clips where it could not be seen unless the hanger was moved to a different position on the line. According to the information provided by the seller of this product, the maximum span of the Ninja line was 50ft between anchor points and was rated to hold a working load of 1,320 lbs. Clearly, these paramenters and limits were not even close to being exceded as my configuration was, at most, 30 feet in length between the two trees and the three victims utilizing it were well below the indicated weight limit by a difference of 1,200lbs.
Following my visual assessment of the damaged product, I contacted the customer service department at Amazon.com to report the product failure and to inquire if there was any type of warranty provided by the seller in such instances of a product design failure. I was advised by Amazon support staff that I would need to contact the seller directly to address such concerns and that the time period of 30 days had obviously lapsed between purchase date and product failure, which ultimately cleared Amazon of any responsibilities in this matter. Aditionally, I was also informed that the seller listed for this purchase recently closed its account with Amazon and no longer sells any products through Amazon's platform, and in accordance with their company policy, Amazon no longer lists or stores any contact information for the seller in their system. Frustrated, but determined,  I was able to track down some of the seller's company details, including the new website being used to market their products, including the Ninja kit that I purchased and was almost responsible for severely injuring my family. Amazon did, however, make an attempt to contact the seller, on my behalf, using the account information provided within my Purchase Order for the product. Unfortunately,  I have not received any correspondence from the seller, the manufacturer, nor Amazon upper management, despite my repeated weekly connections to Amazon's Customer Support attempting to receive any updates on what I believe to  be a dangerous and defective product that is obviously still being sold and utilized by children, who are possibly being placed in a dangerous and harmful situation, only made worse by the fact that the company responsible for the product continues to dismiss and refuse to respond or acknowledge any reports indicating such a failure occured.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries to three children, including a busted lip and impacts from falls, but no serious injuries requiring ER visits.

incident_description: I have an older Cannondale bicycle bought used in in 2013 with 2400 miles on it. I stored the bike until 2019 and then began riding it. In 2022 the arm on the carbon crankset broke at the pedal attachment and nearly caused a crash. I replaced the carbon arm with a metal arm and continued using the bike until the other carbon arm on the right hand side broke at the same place. While searching for a replacement part I discovered a safety recall #07-206 for Cannondale "bicycles with carbon cranksets." I took the broken parts and bicycle to Orange Cycle, the local Cannondale dealer for evaluation. I was told that the Cannondale recall was for a heat treat issue on the aluminum tube in the crank arm assembly and not the integrity of the carbon arms. My concern is that the recall hazard: "The bicycle's crankset could break, posing a fall hazard to the user." actually did happen two times and Cannondale is okay with it. The recall requires me to "stop using the recalled product immediately" which I did because it is broken and unusable, but even if I replace the broken parts with exact replacement parts I am afraid of an accident. Have there been other accidents related to this recall? Is the recall only intended to address the heat treated tube or is the more important carbon arm breakage also included? I am concerned about the real probability of riders falling when fatigue causes the pedal to break from the carbon arm after many repetitive cycles.
justification: The incident involved a broken crankset that nearly caused a crash, but no injury was reported.

I engaged the brakes on the scooter, but nothing happened, forcing me to jump off the scooter to avoid the car,  badly injuring my knee and elbow as I landed on the pavement. On further investigation I realized that the scooter's electric regeneration-only braking is fatally flawed -- it doesn't engage immediately when the paddle is pressed, instead taking a critical moment or two to ramp up. This makes it essentially useless for emergency braking, and extremely dangerous. Almost all other scooters on the market have physical brakes -- drum or hydraulic. Note that the Unagi does have a "fender" brake, where you can press the fender into the rear wheel for additional braking, but this is useless in an emergency scenario since you can't shift your foot to the fender mid stop.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (knee and elbow) due to the scooter's braking system failure, and the likelihood is high given the described flaw in the braking mechanism.

incident_description:
In February 2023 during a family bike ride, my 5th grade daughter crashed when her woom 6 bike's Vario stem and handlebars unexpectedly separated from the steerer tube while she was riding up a small hill with a gentle incline on a paved bike trail a few blocks from our home. I was riding directly behind her and witnessed the accident. She was seated, fortunately was going slow (~5 mpg) and wearing a bike helment and wasn't seriously injured, though she had nasty bruises on her leg, hip and elbow. I noted that a single stem bolt attached the stem to the steerer tube, but as nothing seemed out of place with the bolt, threads, stem, or steerer tube, I reinstalled the stem, tightened the single stem bolt firmly, and she was able to ride home.  

My daughter lost control and crashed her bike again on Thursday March 9th, 2023 when the stem and handlebars unexpectedly separated from the steerer tube of her woom 6 bike while she was riding to school (riding on a sidewalk up a different small hill across the street from her elementary school). She scraped her chin and elbow, got a bloody lip, hit her head and cracked her bike helmet visor, and bruised her hip. She had to rely on the crossing guard to help her up, and a passing adult to help drag her bike the remaining distance to school where the nurse helped her. She was not hospitalized, and we picked her and the bike up after school.

I believe there should be a recall of the stem. We purchased our woom 6 in Feb, 2021. While I haven't found a recall notice about woom's Vario stem, I noted a prior recall for the front fork of woom 4, 5 and 6 sold from from August 2018 through March 2019 (recall # 20-728, dated March 19, 2020).  I also observed that the woom 1+ through 6 bikes currently for sale on woom's website all have two stem bolts on the side, as well as an additional retention bolt on the top of the stem that connects to a nut inside the stem, which I assume is a significantly more secure design than the stem on our daughter's woom 6 bike.

To woom's credit, they did ship me a new woom 6 free of charge, reimbursed me for the cost of a replacement helmet, and offered to reimburse for the cost of professional assembly. However, when I asked a member of their Customer Experience team about a recall they were noncommittal and said they'd notify their safety team.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries including bruises, scrapes, a bloody lip, and a cracked helmet visor, but no hospitalization or death.

Personally I believe the cords are way too long and should have never been made long enough to go around someone's neck, I also believe that with the metal cable being removed from the opposite side that the company this machine is placed at was not supposed to have the metal cable on the machine.

incident_description: In 2021, I worked for Bingham Cyclery in Ogden, UT. We carried IZip bikes, a commuter brand held by Alta Cycling Group. We brought in IZIP Alki 1 and Alki 2 commuter bicycles, some of the only bikes available at the time. We sold one to an eight year-old and the next day, her father returned with the bike. She had crashed because the stem, the part that holds the handlebars, had turned relative to the front wheel, causing her to crash. I was worried, because I had torqued the stem to spec in front of the father as part of its final check before leaving the store. I checked a random bike of the same model and it did the same thing. I tried every single bike with the same stem and they all turned with minimal effort despite being torqued to spec. Maxing out the torque setting on our torque wrench did not fix the problem. I brought the problem to the management of both Bingham Cyclery and Alta and they brought in mechanics who confirmed my conclusions. They did not issue a recall, however. They asked me if it was possible that only my bikes were affected. I responded that the odds against that were phenomenal. I was never informed that I should replace the stems. I had pulled all of the bikes with the affected stems from our sales floor. Two weeks later, I was fired, ostensibly for poor sales performance, despite being one of the company's most prolific salespeople in a time when we had no bikes to sell.
justification: The incident involved a crash due to a faulty bike stem, but there was no mention of injury, only the potential for harm.

incident_description: I've owned four models of OneWheel and have ridden them since the v1 came out.  I have lots of experience with pushback and know how to ride my OneWheels.  I can confidently state that the two times I experienced being "dropped" were not my pushing through pushback.  I alerted FutureMotion when it happend and they denied any issue with the board.  It is the only of the 4 boards I've had this issue with and I know it was not my riding.  One time I had just started off, hadn't even made it 10' and wasn't anywhere near the speeds where pushback would occur, I started going and after ~8' it just dropped the nose and I was on the ground.  The other time I was riding along the levy by the river and going under a bridge, there was  no pushback, the board just stopped.  I have let FutureMotion know when seeing class action suits that I strongly believe they should look deeper at a malfunction in their boards and not write off this issue but they continue to deny it.  I love the OneWheels and completely agree it is a risky sport and one should always wear protection.  I am also convinced that some of the boards are defective and can randomly stop.  Mine was a OneWheel+ model, but I'm sure 9x% of the Plus model and all OneWheel models are probably fully functional, but there is a percentage that are not.

I caught my fall with my face and hand, and I now face the next 2 months with my dominant hand in a cast with a fractured scaphoid in my right wrist. 

Because the app does not provide ride diagnostic information about pushbacks that were triggered, IÃÂm unable to determine why the board stopped, although I assume it is because of a reason that should have triggered pushback.

I wanted to report this incident because I don't think the oneWheel provides enough details in app to prevent or diagnose this kind of shutoff. I understand how the board is supposed to work, but if the single safety feature meant to prevent over-exerting the board is not triggered or goes unnoticed, a fall is almost guaranteed. I would consider myself an experienced rider.

I was riding my Onewheel on a walking trail when I was ejected, and was transported via ambulance to the ER as I took major damage to my head including vision loss in my left eye. I was wearing a skateboarding helmet, and being intentionally cautious to not push limits as I was still rather new to the sport with only 87 miles ridden. 

I have no memory of the accident itself. I took a picture of the Onewheel about 20 minutes prior to the accident, and afterwards, had returned to the walking trail I had already traversed on the Onewheel. 

I was riding on a flat, paved path away from car traffic. I didnÃÂt observe any significant terrain issues, bumps, edges, or other obstacles which would have posed a problem for the Onewheel. I was being sure not to push the limits, and was familiar with ÃÂpushbackÃÂ the device generates when it is operating past its limits. 

While I do not believe I would have ignored that feedback, I have amnesia of the accident itself. I remember being on a country road, safely getting off the Onewheel, and taking a picture at 5:05 PM of the Onewheel as I was enjoying my ride. My memory ends after getting back on, and riding back towards the walking trail. Between 5:22 and 5:24, I took 4 photos showing my head damaged and covered in blood. I have zero memory of taking these pictures, and not sure exactly when or where the accident happened. Metadata of those photos shows the exact location of the walking trail where they were taken. 

I was transported by ambulance to the local ER. My memory resumes in the back of the ambulance, informing the paramedics that I couldnÃÂt see out of my left eye. They claim I had lost consciousness at some point, but didnÃÂt know details of how my accident was reported. 
 I donÃÂt know a detailed timeline due to memory loss. 

The ER informed me I had 4 fractures to my left orbital/sinus, and Traumatic Optic Neuropathy (TON). I was transferred to another hospital at about 2 AM to see specialists. Multiple ophthalmologist have confirmed that this damage is likely to be permanent, and I will never regain vision in my left eye. 

The only thing that really makes sense is despite my caution, I somehow experienced a ÃÂnosediveÃÂ, which Onewheel claims only happens after dramatically ignoring pushback functions. There are no other warnings or indicators thar youÃÂre about to nosedive. I weigh 230 pounds which is within the operating limits the manufacturer reports. The app also documents I have never gone above 16 MPH in the 87 miles itÃÂs logged. Its documented speed limit is 18 MPH.
justification: The incident resulted in severe, permanent injury (vision loss and fractures) requiring emergency medical attention, justifying a severity level of 4. The key moving part is a sliding lock on the dumbbell that slides in and out.  The farther the lock slides out, the more weight plates it locks onto the dumbbell.  After about two months of usage, the sliding lock started to get misaligned.  After turning the knob to set it to a desired weight, the sliding lock would move to its position, but the misalignment causes the sliding lock to fail to latch onto the last weight plate.  As a result, after picking up the dumbbell, the last weight plate falls off on its own - sometimes immediately, sometimes after I start to use the dumbbells in an exercise.  The weight plates have fallen onto my body, so far with no serious injury (scratches and bruises), but if the dumbbell were to be positioned above my face or head for an exercise and the weight were to fall off, it could easily break a nose, injure an eye, break a jaw or cause a concussion.  The weight plates have also damaged my floor from falling onto the hardwood.  If the weight plate were to fall off while standing upright, it could easily break a toe as well.  Most recently, the entire sliding lock has come loose from the dumbbell and all the weights have fallen off. 

There is a serious product design and/or manufacturing flaw with this product that ICON customer support has so far failed to acknowledge or resolve, despite repeated attempts to get their attention and escalate (case #:[REDACTED]).  If you go to the [REDACTED] product page, you will see numerous reviews that complain of the same type of issue.  I urge you to please investigate this product immediately before more consumers get injured from this product.

Dear Madam and/or Sir
I wanted to report injuries I sustained from the lid of an exploding filter canister for our in-ground pool. My hope is that you will increase safety requirements on pool filter canisters.
 On Saturday, August 27, 2022 I was cleaning the filter for our pool pump. The Hayward Filter Canister exploded after I turned the water pressure back on and it hit me in the face and knocked me to the ground.  The victim of course can be blamed as I am a 78 year-old woman, the canister is probably at least 10 years old and no professional taught me how to do this.  ÃÂBut, I had been doing it successfully for at least 10 years. This should not have happened.
After reading some articles on-line and talking with others I thought I should let you know the damage done to me as you may want to address this issue in a way to protect others in the future.  The impact of the lid hitting my face and knocking me to the ground scared me, so I yelled for my husband who luckily was home.  He got me a towel to rest my head on and soak up some of the bloodÃÂand he called 911.  The EMTs on the ambulance, of course, took my vitals and started asking all kinds of questions.  Eventually, I was helped to sit up and transferred to a stretcher to take me to the ER.  In the ER I had a CT Scan, stiches above my eye and stiches below my eye on the cheek bone.  The area above my lip and part of my lip was cut all the way through so it was stitched outside and then inside my mouth.  I was given a referral for a plastic surgeon to address my broken nose.  My skull was in-tact.  I did have one upper front tooth knocked out and two others chipped and dislocated which will need to be extracted. In addition, three bottom teeth were chipped.  A few days later I saw the Plastic Surgeon who set my nose with stents up my nostrils and a white plastic ÃÂcasteÃÂ across my nose.  My dentist sent me to an Oral Surgeon who will remove two teeth in addition to the one that was knocked out once the caste and stents have been removed from my nose.
Issues with the Hayward Pool Pump Filter:
1.	 The lid is only held in place by one stainless steel rod onto which the lid is screwed.  As an article called [REDACTED] by [REDACTED] and [REDACTED], March 2017, discusses, there is an explosion risk in the filter tank when the filter is pressurized.  This was also pointed out in 1974 by the U.S. Consumer Products Safety Commission in an article which mentioned ÃÂproblems of exploding filter tanks.ÃÂ  The risk is, of course, exacerbated when there is only one screw holding the lid in place.
2.	The giant screw was made out of Stainless Steel and the ÃÂlug nutÃÂ or nut secured to the lid was made out of brass.  We believe this utilization of two different kinds of metals is not a good design as the threads did not hold.
3.	There was an air-relief valve but it is not automatic ÃÂor failed to release excess pressure. 
4.	Based on the information in the [REDACTED] article, which is attached, it would be best to require that filter canisters have multiple lugs and nuts as those found made by [REDACTED].
IÃÂm glad I am alive.  Please let me know if you are addressing this consumer protection issue. 
Sincerely,
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
Cc: [REDACTED]

incident_description:
Cyrusher XF650, Affordable Mountain Ebike 
I bought two of these online at the end of May 2022. They came partially pre-assembled but had no instructions to complete the assembly. Once the bikes were completely assembled, as I was able to get the proper regs and instructions for the parts that I did need to assemble, I gave them to my two teenage boys. I have been mountain biking since 1995, never pro, but all over the country, and always did a lot of my own work on my bikes. With these two bikes, next to completely stripping the bikes down to check for any malfunctions or defects, I inspected them as they were, pre-assembled. I took my time and carefully adjusted, tightened, and put the right amount of air in tubes, test rides, etc...so that my boys would be as safe as possible with the functioning of the bikes. After a week of making sure the bikes were ready, the boys rode them that whole day and everything still checked out okay. The next day, on June 1st my son, took off on his bike to go to school in the morning. While riding in the bike lane, at around 25 mph, he said he was suddenly thrown from the bike but had no idea why. He ended up with a broken right knee, broken left wrist, and road rash on his right hand left leg, and left shoulder. He luckily was cleared from trauma 2 level and was discharged from ER that night. It took 6 weeks to get out of the cast and he had to miss going to his camp in VT that he had been going to since he was 8.
When I found my son at the site of the incident, I found the wheel completely flat, mind you I had just checked it the night before, and, the wheel was about 200 yards from where his bike was. No glass or any potholes around. No cars were involved. Nothing that would have caused his wheel to separate from the bike that was on the road or around him to go flat, or to cause a blowout. I have never had a quick-release separate like that in a blowout, but it did appear to be a blowout. When I took the tire and tube off the wheel the rim had this separation in the line where it looked like it was supposed to be connected. Like touching, or supposed to be welded. But it was not touching, and not welded. It just looked wrong and like it was different from the other rims. Next, I noticed that there was a pattern of holes in the tube, and on the inside of the rim were matching sharp bent mental pieces sticking up out of the rim. They were about 3 cm tall and exactly matched the tube holes. The quick release had no prior defects that I had previously Inspected, but now I could see it was looking a bit damaged, but still should not have dislodged. I started thinking was this my fault? No way. I made sure that the quick release was perfect and working. I checked the tire's air and all the parts the night before and I felt very secure with my work. The company Cyrusher tricked me into sending the bikes back saying that they would give me a full refund. As soon as they got the bikes they started giving me the runaround. They said I caused the injury to my son because I put the bike together wrong. Which didn't even make sense because how can they prove I did? Besides, I know I did right, and shame on them for even saying that. I think the quick release was just cheap and didn't hold up to the force that it was put under. They were fat tires and fat rims. They are heavy. So now Cyrusher is trying to trick me into "agreeing" that the incident was my fault for not assembling the bike correctly and that is why my son got hurt. They completely ignored the fact that the inside of the rim had these sharp metal pieces sticking up that were bent out of the rim, in a pattern, that perfectly matched the holes in the inside of the innertube. They should have inspected these rims before sending them out to the consumer population. I should have never trusted this company. They refuse to take responsibility. I am so scared that someone is going to lose their life because of this company. Please, please, please do not buy anything from this company.  They do not care about consumers at all. They wont respond and have kept all of my $3177.00 even though I returned them within my return policy rights. They are selfish and sadly part of this throttle-type mountain ebike that should be illegal. Obviously they are dangerous, but clearly a market that is not to be trusted with companies like Cyrusher and others. They are the only ones who make these types of bikes. [REDACTED] , [REDACTED], and other reputable names will not make this "throttle-type" ebike. They believe in participating in the work to peddle and these are called peddle assist mountain ebikes. I am now just learning. Integrity is not for sale and Cyrusher needs to be stopped.
justification: The incident resulted in a broken knee, wrist, and road rash, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is unlikely (2) as the defect appears specific to this bike model.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that the handlebars of the bicycle is unstable and comes apart. She stated that they are put together with a plastic joint that is not durable. She stated that they have tighten the hand each time the 4 year old kids ride the bike for a few mins. She stated that the bike handles is unsafe because they can come while they are riding causing serious injuries.

(8/8/22) The manufacturer was contacted and the customer service rep advised her to use plumber's tape.  Caller feels that these bikes should be taken off the market due to the potential danger it poses.

The handlebar stem slides down into the front of the main bicycle frame.  There is a plastic joint that screws down, to tighten the handlebars onto the frame.  As the bikes are being ridden, the plastic joint works loose.  We retighten that joint several times during a short period of riding.  The handlebars become so loose to the point they could fall apart.  We constantly stop our grandchildren while they are riding, just to tighten the joint.  When the handle bars come loose, it affects the steering, and God forbid if they would fall apart.  Fortunately we discovered the issue quickly and have stayed on top of it, only to realize how dangerous this is.  I called Huffy Company to report the problem only too be told to apply plumbers tape to the threads of the joint.  My husband tried to apply the tape, but because  the design on how its put together, it is difficult, because there is a rivet in the way, that doesn't enough threads to place the tape on.  We wish we could send you a video on how dangerous this design is.  My husband then used plyers to tighten the joint down, and it still loosend up.

Unfortunately, our daughter purchased "2" 12 in bicycles made by Huffy with the same design flaw.  When her children were smaller, we had the same issues with these bikes, but the kids didn't ride them much since they were just learning to ride and had training wheels. We were stupid enough to go out and buy "2" bigger bikes , when the kids no longer needed the training wheels and had out grown them.  Buying more Huffy bikes was stupid on our part because we now know what a very dangerous design flaw these bikes have.  Four (4) Huffy bikes with the same issue is no coincidence.  Huffy's simple solution with applying plumbers tape is a joke.  No more Huffy bikes for this family!

incident_description:
I purchased a Rad Power Bikes RadWagon 4 cargo ebike for ~$2,000 in October 2021.  This bike is marketed by Rad Power Bikes specifically for having special, custom sized tires (22" -- a unique size for bicycles) made only for Rad Power Bikes through Vee Tire. These tires can only be obtained through Rad Power Bikes and these cannot even be obtained through Vee Tire. After riding the bike for less than 1,300 miles, the rear tire had a blowout. On closer inspection of the tire, I discovered that the sidewall had split (approximately 2") right at the bead, resulting in the inner tube bulging through the slit and cutting the inner tube on the sharp edge of the slit. When I searched for this problem on the internet, I was surprised to actually find out this problem is rather commonplace with these specific tires. I contacted Rad Power Bikes support (since the bike was still under warranty), but was told that Rad Power Bikes warranty does not cover tires. I argued that these are very proprietary tires that are obviously defective since it is happening to so many fellow RadWagon 4 bike owners. They never responded back and simply closed the trouble ticket in their system.  When further investigating this split, just pushing it with my finger cause the split to double in size. It was tearing/separating like a zipper being unzipped. Also, on closer inspection of my front wheel, the same problem is starting to happen at the bead of the front tire.  

I have seen recent posts in RadWagon 4 online forums where new 22" Vee tires are of a different design. Clearly Rad Power Bikes and Vee Tire are both aware of this issue or why would they change the tire design (when the tire is only used on this one model of bicycle)? 

Rad Power Bikes needs to accept responsibility for this problem and recall/replace these tires. This bicycle is specifically marketed for its unique tires, as well as specifically marketed for riding with children passengers. This bike is capable of achieving speeds of up to 25mph (even faster going downhill). If those tires were to fail while someone was riding this bike that fast (especially with children passengers), the end results could easily result in injury to include being life-threatening (or worse).  These tires need to be recalled and replaced immediately.
justification: The incident describes a tire blowout and potential for injury due to defective tires, but no actual injury is reported.

incident_description:
Manufacturer: RadPower Bikes, a US-based electrical bicycle maker
Model: 2022 RadRover 6 Step-thru ebike
Product at fault: 48 volt removable battery
Problem: battery short circuit
Cause: user can inadvertently cross the 48 volt contacts of the charging port with a metallic object
Situation: the battery is secured within the bike frame with a lock.  To remove the battery, a key is used to unlock the latch mechanism which is less than three inches from the charging port.  The charging port has a rubber-like flap to weatherproof it but it is still possible to touch both port contacts with the key or any tool or metal object causing a short.  Doing so results, in an alarming and loud spark that is a safety hazard.  This also renders the battery unusable.  At nearly 80 pounds, the bike is difficult to pedal and use without battery assistance, which is the point of ownership - assisting the user with battery power.  The battery retails for $600 on the RadPower website, https://www.radpowerbikes.com/collections/replacement-parts/products/rad-semi-integrated-battery-pack.
Questions:
Why isn't this circuit better protected, perhaps with a quick acting fuse and reset button?
Why is the charge port so close to the lock?
Why isn't the charge port on the opposite side of the battery to prevent this from happening?
Why isn't the charge port's contacts more deeply recessed to lessen the chance of crossing the circuit?
Could the prongs on a woman's ring or other piece of jewelry cause a short to occur?
Could a child mimicking a parent connecting the charger to the bike cause the same occurrence?

------------------------------------------------------------
Below is a warning from RadPower on this issue:
Please make sure to follow proper charging processes whenever you charge your batteries.
Not Following this process has a high chance of damaging the Battery and could void the battery warranty. When you charge your battery, it is very important that you first plug the charger into the battery, then plug the charger into the wall. When done charging, unplug the Outlet first, then the Battery. Not following this order has a very high chance to blow the internal charging fuse. The use of a surge protector though not required, is also highly recommended. Note: Do not put any metal or electrically conductive objects near the charge port other than the proper end of the charger plug. Note: You may receive an email saying that your issue has been resolved but please note that you can reply to this email thread at any time to reopen this inquiry and get help from me or another Product Support Specialist - closing the inquiry is simply a formality
in our system.
--------------------------------------------------------------------

It seems to me that RadPower acknowledges this occurrence.  However, they admit no guilt to their faulty design.  When I filed my claim with RadPower that my battery would no longer charge, they had the above disclaimer all ready  to send to me.  In fact, the service representative I spoke with was very familiar with this issue, proving to me that this is a continuing problem.  My bike is only four months old so it is the latest version.
justification: The incident involves a safety hazard with potential for injury due to a short circuit, but no actual injury is reported. The likelihood is high given the design flaw and user reports.

incident_description:
I am a valued customer at Amazon. I have been for the past 2 1/2 years. It was July of 2020 that I purchased the Vibration Plate Exercise Machine sold by the eHUPOO store. I didn't use it right away because during that time, Covid -19 had plagued the entire Nation.

incident_description:
I recently bought a tent (Avalanche Outdoors Backpack Tent - 2-Person, 3-Season
Item #72YPF) and used it in a rain storm near [REDACTED].  I slept in it most of the night (probably 6 to 7 hours), then woke up anoxic.  I feel I could have died from oxygen starvation.  I sat up in the tent and instantly lost my breath like I had run a few miles.  I couldn't draw a full breath and my son started breathing rapidly.  I reached over him to open the tent door and woke him up.  He told me that he couldn't breathe.  I opened the door and the oxygen filled the tent and we could breathe again.
This tent has no windows.  I doesn't have a rain fly.  It has some sort of waterproof material or treatment that makes the fabric unbreathable.  I put the fabric up to my face and tried to breath in, but it was like plastic.  No air could move through the material.  This is a death trap just waiting for someone to sleep too long in it and never wake up.
We slept the next night with the door open and packed out.  I don't think that we will have any long term damage from this experience.  Perhaps we lost a few brain cells from being anoxic all night.  I just don't want someone else to get hurt.
justification: The incident caused anoxic conditions leading to breathing difficulties, which qualifies as an injury, and the lack of ventilation in the tent makes recurrence likely under similar conditions.

incident_description:
A peloton bike plus model was delivered to my home on March 24 and less than five minutes into my first ride on the morning of March 25, 2022, the right pedal suddenly came off the arm causing me to fall off the bike and hit my knee. I was able to catch myself midfall, but I could have easily hit my head or suffered a more serious injury. The pedal was still attached to my shoe and there were small metal shards on the ground from where the metal screw that is supposed to attach the pedal to the arm stripped. After recovering from the shock of the fall, I attempted to screw the pedal back onto the arm, but the metal was stripped. The left pedal was still attached to the arm, but barely screwed in and when I attempted to tighten it, it would not screw in. I am not an expert, but it seemed as if the wrong pedal or hardware was used. I was shocked that Peloton conducted no inspection or quality control review of its product before delivery. I am thankful that I did not suffer a more serious injury. To have a pedal come off a brand-new bike when going at a fast pace is extremely dangerous and I hope this does not happen to anyone else.
I called Peloton immediately after my injury on the bike on March 25. I spoke to [REDACTED] and was shocked that he brushed off my injury and my request to report the product defect. I requested to speak with someone regarding my safety concern with the product and he said there was no one else I could speak to. He said a new pedal and arm would be shipped to my home and then I would be contacted to set up a service appointment.
I followed up with written communications to Peloton on May 3, 2022, and May 10, 2022 and specifically requested information on their quality control/inspection measures that they have in place before delivering a bike.  On May 16, 2022, [REDACTED] responded and told me ÃÂat this time, I am unable to share what Peloton measures or quality control standards are taken.ÃÂ  Which I find to be very concerning.
justification: The incident resulted in a knee injury from falling off the bike due to a pedal detachment, which could have been more severe.

incident_description:
I was riding a 'muscle' manual kick scooter (Osprey Dirt) model.  I average 14 miles a week and use it  for a specialized exercise routine you can call it.  A kick scooter (also referred to as a push-scooter or scooter) is a human-powered street-ground vehicle with a handlebar, deck, and wheels propelled by a rider pushing off the ground with their feet. NOTICE: It broke on me while jumping and clearing a standard sidewalk ridge at the edge of an asphalt street and I was at a 90 degree angle to the road. Luckily only a quarter sized scrape on my knee was scraped. This model scooter is supposed to be made for hilly and bumping riding so it should be able to take mini jumps that present itself when riding including juts in sidewalks and irregular roads that can be expected to be encountered while traveling. The manufactures site shows a rider up into the air to be landing hard onto the ground. 
@ https://www.ospreyactionsports.co.uk/osprey-dirt-scooter-gun-metal-grey.html?gclid=Cj0KCQjwheyUBhD-ARIsAHJNM-OAGfNdvjzxqBZQdke2YH72idNwuRrhNcySbWG45GEyMhG-_4ZdfJ8aAgZgEALw_wcB    . Luckily I only skinned my one knee about the size of a quarter.

The part that broke was: The downtube cleanly separated in a catastrophic sudden break just below the headtube. The two main parts of the scooter frame separated in two pieces. See picture. This part is not engineered properly to withstand all the operating forces put upon for an all-terrain vehicle, in a push-kick scooter use type-scope.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury (a quarter-sized scrape on the knee) due to the scooter breaking during use, which suggests a possible likelihood of recurrence under similar conditions.

incident_description:
In the twilight, I tripped over some strands of poly from a woven poly tarp. The tarp had torn and, as it was flapping in the wind, the torn edge unraveled into many long and narrow strands of poly which dangled everywhere.

Woven Poly tarps, shred / tear leaving many narrow strips of very strong film. These strips cannot be easily torn and are a serious hazard to safety of human and animals. When used around the water, the strips can ensnare a swimmer and a single strip can restrain a person to the point of drowning. In land-side applications, they can strangle / snare small animals and pets as well as cause falls as persons may trip over them. 

The manufacturers of these woven poly tarps should be required to heat bond / fuse the strands so that the tarps will not fray and generate these life threatening strands. I can forward a photo of the condition if you be so kind as to provide and email address to which a message can be sent with the photo as an attachment.
justification: The description mentions a trip incident and highlights potential for serious injuries or drowning, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is high (4) due to the described common fraying of tarps.

incident_description:
Dear Fitbit:

I am very disappointed in how you are managing the Fitbit Ionic recall. Every step of the
way seems designed to prevent the majority of impacted consumers from being
remedied.

Yes, I purchased an Ionic and yes I loved it until I noticed some strange corrosion on
the back. I scraped it off as best I could but it still came back. It did not burn my skin or
leave any marks but it eventually corroded the prongs and stopped accepting a charge.
I spent weeks searching for answers on the internet and calling your help-line but found
no help or explanation. You see, I'm diabetic and I depended on the Ionic (via Dexcom)
to give me constant read-out of my blood sugars. It worked great until it didn't.

After trying to find a remedy, I eventually gave up and looked to buy a replacement Ionic
(I liked it that much) only to find that the Ionic had been discontinued. Even so, I took a
chance and bought the Versa 3 model which works fine.

Imagine how surprised and happy I was to receive the recall notice only to discover that
you have made it almost impossible to receive compensation. After I purchased the
new Versa 3, I had no reason to hold on to the Ionic and I disposed of it due to the
corrosion and because it no longer worked.

However, you have made the remedy conditional on receiving the Ionic in return. Who
in their right mind is going to keep a non-working corroded smartwatch that could be a
fire hazard in their house?

In addition, your so called exclusive discounts are for CPSC show only. Your prices are
no better than what was available to the public during the holidays and the selections
are even more limited. Your free watch-band looks like a leftover from Halloween!

But all in all, thank goodness I still used the same email address and/or didn't
automatically send the notification to spam or I might have been unaware and missed
out on a 56 in a million chance of receiving compensation.

Come on! You guys are better than that! Do right by your loyal customers. Don't make
doing the right thing so hard just to save yourselves a few bucks.


Consumer Product Safety Commission
https://www.cpsc.gov/Recalls/2022/Fitbit-Recalls-lonic-Smartwatches-Due%20to-BurnHazard-
One-Million-Sold-in-the-U-S

... "This recall was conducted, voluntarily by the company, under CPSC's Fast
Track Recall process. Fast Track recalls are initiated by firms, who commit to
work with CPSC to quickly announce the recall and remedy to protect
consumers."

Remedy? Maybe for your shareholders but not your customers.

Respectfully,

[REDACTED]

The leash was a coiled bungee leash that had a metal swivel at the end.  A simple string connects the metal swivel (and leash) to the boogieboard.  The string connecting the leash (via metal swivel) was insufficient to withstand the force resulting from my child pulling the boogieboard by the leash and apparently failed.  When it failed, the strap sprung back towards his face, and the metal swivel at the end of the leash struck him in the eye at a high velocity.  The product was being used as it was intended to be used at the beach.
The boogieboard and leash were branded "Morey" which we have learned is manufactured by Wham-O Toy Co. We purchased the boogieboard and leash (packaged together) from Costco in South Carolina.
We have since noticed several other boogieboard leash that are not coiled/elastic which would reduce the speed the leash could spring back if it fails.  We have also since noticed leash that do not contain a metal swivel at the end.  The metal swivel essentially acted as a projectile that blinded my child in one eye.
justification: The incident resulted in partial blindness, which is a significant injury, hence severity level 3. The occurrence likelihood is 2 (unlikely) as such injuries are not common but possible with the described product design.

incident_description:
Union Bindings Company - 2022 Explorer Splitboard Bindings

The bindings can be mounted to the splitboard in both "ride" and "touring" position. In ride position, they are mounted to two sets of plastic discs that are mounted to the board via metal plates. The bindings are then put on over the discs and rotated 90 degrees into riding position. A metal pin is then inserted through a hole in the baseplate of the binding, through the channel of the plastic mounting disc and into another hole on the other side of the baseplate to lock the binding down. There is a plastic arm that is attached to the end of the metal pin at 90 degrees. This arm is used to rotate back into a plastic locking mechanism on the outside of the baseplate. At the end of the plastic arm, there is an indentation where it should snap into the locking mechanism, but there is also a hole in this spot which they tie a canvas like string to attach to the rear strap of the binding. If this string is not attached, you risk dropping  and losing the pin in the snow which would render the bindings completely useless. This attached string does not allow the plastic arm to press down enough to click into place in riding mode leaving it susceptible to slipping out while riding. I've attempted to push the pin arm into locking position with my hands wrapped around the unmounted bindings for leverage. With the string attached, it's impossible to get them to lock in place in a warm living room, let alone mounted to a board covered in snow on the mountain with cold hands or gloves on. When unlocked, the pins slip out of the baseplate and discs extremely easily. I have tested them out for 3 days riding resorts to try to get them to work, but they fail almost every single run. This has caused the bindings to rotate 90 degrees mid ride and has even caused them to pop off multiple times. Luckily I stuck to easy runs with no obstacles, so while I fell multiple times I wasn't hurt more than a few bruises or pulled muscles, but the potential for disaster is ever present with these bindings, and I wouldn't be surprised if someone else was not as lucky as I was.

The toe strap is also secured poorly. Each strap attaches to the plastic strap arm by using two pins that press through holes in the arm. The pins are only a few millimeters tall and barely have a lip at the end to keep them locked in. They also sit flush with the plastic arms making it difficult to press back into position when they pop out, especially when snow gets anywhere near them. Union normally uses a screw of some kind for this, but the system used here fails constantly, and combined with the pin locking issue make these massively unsafe.
justification: The bindings' design flaws caused multiple falls, resulting in bruises and pulled muscles, with a high likelihood of recurrence due to frequent failures.

incident_description: My daughter (4 years old) was riding her new Razor A Kick Scooter for the first time, when one of the handlebars suddenly detached, causing her to crash. She was not seriously injured beyond a few scrapes on her knee. Despite being only 4, she was able to explain to me exactly how the product malfunctioned. When I look at the design of the scooter closely, it's not hard to see how it is unsafe. The grips of the handlebars are detachable by depressing a small pin. Once depressed, the entire handle bar easily slides out of the steering post and the rider is almost guaranteed to lose control and crash. The pins are located very close (less than an inch away) from the foam grips and a place where a child or other user is very likely to put their thumb while riding. A much safer design would be to have this handle bar assembly be a single welded piece. Alternatively, the grips should have a secondary locking mechanism that requires a tool to loosen so that they cannot be suddenly detached while riding.
justification: The child suffered scrapes on her knee, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The design flaw makes detachment likely during use (occurrence likelihood 4).

When it failed again today I re-tightened it and observed that the clamp seems to be closing up. In other words it may not be possible to tighten again because the clamp is already closed. Fortunately I was not injured but I could have been seriously injured. The fact that the pin locking mechanism failed, came unlocked, and allowed my foot to disengage from the board could have led to me loose control and crash into a tree or other object. It could also have led to me twisting or breaking part of my leg or knee since now one foot was connected to the board and the other was not. This has happened to me multiple occasions and it is clear the design of the pin locking mechanism is defective and dangerous. After searching online I found numerous other owners of these bindings are experiencing the exact same issue.
justification: The incident describes a binding failure leading to a crash without injury, but with potential for serious harm, and reports indicate it happens frequently to others.

Within a few days, two of the legs had sunk into the ground, causing the swing set to become unstable and the anchors loose. To keep it from sinking, I installed flat pieces of wood on each leg (secured them with lag screws to the leg) and then anchored the wood to the ground. Even with this, it was still not very stable but was usable. After a few more days of use, one of the feet on the leg broke off at the welds, and a second one was ready to break off. incident_description:
I recently was running on the Nordictrack Commercial X32i treadmill (approximately 10 months after purchase) and noticed some wobbling on the front end and some loud squeaking noise.  When I stopped the treadmill to inspect, I noticed that the metal base that is part of the running deck had split in half (literally split through the metal) and a spring and other minor equipment was scattered on the ground.  

I called Nordictrack immediately and sent photos of the split metal frame and the treadmill, noting that this was a significant safety issue.  They indicated that they would have to pick up the machine and send me a new one, but that a Return Specialist would call me within 30 days to do so.  

After thinking about it over night, I called them back the next day to ask them to escalate this issue, since the metal frame of a running deck should not split in half after 10 months of use, and this represented a significant safety hazard.  I also asked how they could investigate this issue thoroughly if it was not flagged and elevated to senior management that a $4,000 treadmill had essentially broken in half on one side.  Where was their quality control and internal reporting process for these types of consumer safety issues?  I did note that it was in their best interests to watch out for the safety of their own customers.  

They only indicated that they could not escalate the significant safety issue to management and that a Return Specialist would contact me within 30 days.  Again, what concerns me is that their response is not indicative of any urgency or the significance of the safety hazard at hand.  The metal seems to be rusted throughout which, for a new machine, calls in to question their supplier and quality control, not to mention my discussions with them calls in to question their reporting process for significant defects or safety hazards.  Thankfully, there were no injuries, but if they take this as lightly as a routine processing, what exactly will prevent someone from getting hurt in a similar situation?  Again, I have photos of the split metal and treadmill.

incident_description:
I have made repeated complaints to the micromobility operator, as well as the appropriate agency at the City of Denver's gov site, but no response/action.
The product is the shared Lyft electric scooters in the City of Denver, Colorado.
I was using the product.
I was using the product to travel, in a legal and appropriate manner, in accordance with local regulations.
No injuries occurred, but there seems to me a high probability of one occuring.

In Denver, we have a pedestrian/shuttle mall, which is a restricted zone for electric scooters. My understanding is that the geofence is supposed to prevent shared scooters from riding DOWN (along) the mall, which runs NW/SE. However, every block there are roadways that cross the mall, including several roads with bike lanes (in Denver, scooters are supposed to use the bike lane if available, otherwise they are legal in the general laneÃÂthey are not permitted on the sidewalk).

On multiple instances, I have had the geofence restriction kick in while CROSSING the 16th St pedestrian/shuttle mall. The most likely scenario is if I'm riding a scooter and am stopped at a red light before crossing the mallÃÂonce I have a green light, the scooter will most likely not operate. Additionally, the wheels will lock, making it difficult to PUSH the scooter out of the geofenced area. This is not the most dangerous scenario, since being stopped at the light, it's easy enough to push the scooter (against the locked wheels) onto the sidewalk. HoweverÃÂ

ÃÂif I have a green light, the geofence restrictions can kick inÃÂat any point along the block after having crossed the mall. The most dangerous scenario that I have experienced (repeatedly) is on Stout St between 16th & 17th, which does not have a bike lane (I take this road because a) [REDACTED], and b) there's a protected bike lane that starts on 18th & Stout). Because Stout St between 16th & 17th has multiple lanes (and a light rail track), and has parking on the right-hand side, if/when the scooter cuts power and LOCK THE WHEELS while I'm riding down a general traffic lane, there's is literally nowhere to go except to dismount and slowly PUSH the scooter (against the locked wheels) down a half-block in the middle of a general traffic lane (frequently in heavy traffic) until I reach the end of the block and can either get to the sidewalk, or the scooter finally unlocks again.

While I understand the need to have areas where shared scooters are restricted from use, the implementation of the geofencing on the 16th St Mall by Lyft in Denver Colorado represents an extreme safety hazard, particularly for those who are unfamiliar with the misguided implementation of this restriction and are unprepared for their scooters to suddenly cut power and LOCK (resulting in a much faster than expected deceleration) while in traffic.
justification: The incident describes a recurring safety hazard with no reported injuries, but a high probability of injury due to sudden scooter lock-ups in traffic.

I did not hit any object in the road nor did I hit a pothole or other road defect. The tire is a Continental GP5000tl 700C X 25mm.  This is the second such tire I have had fail in the last 14 months.  I have photos of the previous tire and I have photos of this tire along with the tire.

Both tires were mounted on the rear of my [REDACTED] bicycle with [REDACTED] wheels. Inspection of the wheels after the second incident showed no sharp spots on the wheels which might have cut a tire.  The rims had been swapped between the two incidents, so it was not the same rim for both incidents.

There were no injuries in either incident.  The previous incident happened at low speed.  This one, not so much.  Because there was no traffic at the time of the event I was able to use the entire roadway while bringing the bicycle to a stop. If there had been oncoming or passing traffic, injuries up to and including death may have occurred.

I have decided to report this because I read a thread on the Bike Forums web site in which several similar failures of this tire are described. See: 
[REDACTED]
justification: No injuries occurred in either incident, but the potential for injury or death exists if traffic conditions were different.

incident_description: I had a chance to inspect FOUR bicycle helmets Lazer G1 Mips, and ALL had faults that are safety concerns. I first purchased the helmet Lazer G1 Mips (size M, black) from an online vendor ( biketiresdirect.com). The received helmet had a safety issue as there was a cut in the foam with no ability to see how deep the cut was. After seeing the pictures, Lazer customer support told me to exchange it. The second helmet that I received had the same cut in the foam. I decided to get a refund from the vendor and order from Lazer directly. The third helmet I received was even more unsafe as the tightening mechanism (on this helmet called the rollsys system) did not work. An inexperienced user would have not known that it is unsafe to wear a helmet that way. Lazer told me to destroy it and sent me another helmet, now the fourth one. This one was even worse in terms of safety because the inner plastic structure that goes around the head was not fully attached to the remaining parts of the helmet. Upon closer inspection it turned out that a plastic triangular actor point that is normally located in the foam was completely missing in one part of the helmet. In other words, 100% construction error. Again, an inexperienced rider would have not noticed and would have worn a very unsafe helmet where the foam and outer shell were not even fully attached to the system that goes around the rider's head. In case of a crash, this helmet would have been barely better than not wearing a helmet at all.
justification: The incident describes multiple safety defects in bicycle helmets that could lead to injury in a crash, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I was driving my  2017 Honda Pioneer 1000 5 Passenger  [REDACTED]  in the desert on Bureau of Land Management land north of Lake Pleasant, Arizona.  I came to a cattle gate so I placed the vehicle into Park and left it running.  I opened the gate, drove through the gate, placed  the vehicle into park and kept it running.  I went to close the cattle gate.  Probably 30 seconds had passed when I heard a clunk, and watched my Pioneer start moving  down the hill.   After rolling about 50-75 feet it came to rest near a tree.  Rocks on the trail had helped to keep it's speed down.  I did not see any damage.  I verified that the shift lever was still in Park.   I used the vehicle for the rest of the day without issue, however for safety, I turned the wheels appropriately and used a rock to block the tire.  This is a major safety issue as I could have had a passenger in the vehicle and this could have been on a shelf road with a 500-1000 foot drop.  There has already been a recall issued for this problem on "2019 and 2020 Honda Pioneer 1000 5 Passenger" vehicles.  "Hazard: The ROV can move or roll when in the park position, posing crash and injury hazards."   Now I am reporting an incident with the 2017 model year.

incident_description: In recent Consumer ReportsÃÂ bike helmet tests, one manufacturerÃÂs helmet failed a crucial part of our safety evaluation, and we are concerned it can allow the helmet to get pushed out of position during an accident so that it no longer offers any protection.  The buckle on the chinstrap of the Dimensions Kids Bike Helmet With Bluetooth Speakers helmet ($25) released in two out of two samples we evaluated during one of our routine bike helmet tests. The Dimensions Kids Bike Helmet With Bluetooth Speakers was the only one helmet that failed out of the 18 helmets that we put through the same test. We are not aware of any injuries related to chinstrap performance on the Dimensions Kids Bike Helmet With Bluetooth Speakers. In response to CR's findings,  Sakar International (the manufacturer) told CR that the helmet "has had no failure points around the retention strap or any other major safety issue in any other previous testing report." The company also said that it did not have "any consumer complaints directly or indirectly about any retention strap issue."
justification: The helmet failed safety tests but no injuries were reported, indicating an incident without injury. The failure was observed in 2 out of 2 samples, but overall occurrence is unlikely as it was the only helmet out of 18 to fail.

incident_description: Our brand new Nautilus Treadmill spontaneously started on its own and was running at top speeds with a dark display. On the night of July 16th, at approximately 8:30 pm,  roughly 4 hours after assembling the treadmill and plugging it in, the treadmill started on its own while my husband, myself and my two young kids were in another room watching a movie. We heard an extremely loud noise coming from the opposite end of the house and when I went to investigate, I found the treadmill running on its own. The display was completely dark and the belt was running very fast. I called the company to report the issue and after some time, they requested a video in order to help us. I am not sure how this company expects me to get a video of a spontaneous event, and I am even more troubled that they might expect me to allow this treadmill to be plugged in and unattended to see if the problem happens again. I have very young children and I am absolutely NOT okay with putting my children in danger AGAIN to try and get a video of the treadmill running on its own with it being on or being turned on. It is completely negligent and I am not even sure how a video of the event would help them troubleshoot. It seems more like they don't believe me that it happened. Therefore, I would like this to serve of public record that this treadmill is unsafe as it spontaneously turns on by itself and could severely injure or kill someone. I take safety seriously and I expect the Bowflex family of companies to do the same.

incident_description: I purchased SELEWARE Silent Ball Bearing Swing Hanger off amazon (https://www.amazon.com/dp/B07YW8V2D3?ref=ppx_pop_mob_ap_share) on 7/10/21 for use with little tike disc swing in the basement of our home.  The hanger was delivered on 7/12/21 and installed per manufacturer instructions on 7/13/21.  On 7/16/21, my two daughters were in our basement taking turns on the rope swing with the new swing hanger.  My 8 year was pushing my 5 year old in a counter clockwise fashion when all of a sudden the hanger detached from the ball bearing.  My daughter fell along with the swing and landed on her foot which resulted in a fracture of her first metatarsal.  Fortunately she did not hit any walls or kids standing around which could have lead to a catastrophic injury. incident_description:
My son and I were mountain biking when my son took a spill. The result was a skinned knee and elbow, a cut across the bridge of his nose (not bleeding), and a bloody nose from the left nostril. I was surprised about the cut & bloody nose since he was wearing a full face Demon Podium helmet with MIPS. I asked him if he hit a bush or rock, and he said no, just the ground. I checked his helmet and there were no dents or major scrapes, but the visor/peak was pushed below the front brim and couldn't be put back in place since it was wedged under the brim. Also, one of the gray visor bolts was ripped out and missing on the right side. After about 15min, he developed a headache, so we went to the ER where a cat scan confirmed a broken nose and mild concussion.  I  was dumbfounded about the broken nose, especially with a full face helmet. While inspecting the helmet, I slid my finger along the inside edge of the foam padding (typically rests against the forehead), and at the midline, I found a small depression. I checked my other son's helmet (never worn) and the forehead pad inner edge was smooth with no depressions. I had my son put his helmet on and the forehead pad depression aligns with the bridge of his nose. After confirming the chin strap was properly secured, I was able to rotate the helmet down resulting in the brim foam pad connecting with the bridge of his nose. It appears as he hit the ground, the visor took most of the force and since it was secured to the helmet, it rotated the helmet into my son's face.
After searching the internet, it seems this type of injury is common.  To improve the design, the helmet visor should be able to break-away during an impact.  This would prevent it from pivoting the helmet out of its proper position.
justification: The incident resulted in a broken nose and mild concussion, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The description suggests this type of injury is common with this helmet design, making occurrence likelihood possible (3).

incident_description:
We have a Weehoo brand child's bike trailer (model "iGo Turbo) that enables a child to be towed and/or pedal behind an adult bike. It was purchased on March 20, 2018 directly from https://rideweehoo.com The wheel of the trailer has been wobbling for about a week so I looked and attempted to tighten the wheel per the video instructions on their website, at which point the entire rear wheel drop out (on the "non drive" side, i.e. the side without the chain) snapped in half. My suspicion is that this frame area was already weakening/fatiguing as I had not really begun to tighten it when it failed with a cracking sound. The trailer has always been stored indoors in an insulated garage and ridden in fair/dry weather with our child. The trailer is rated to 80 lb cargo/child capacity, our child is nowhere close to this limit (currently under 55 lbs). We have used it in good weather to take our son to school and on short rides around town. We do not use it to "mountain bike" or on non-paved trails (i.e. we have only used this trailer as it was intended.) Fortunately no one was on the bike at the time and there were no injuries.

In looking at the frame design, it looks quite flawed/unsafe which is why I am making this report. Maybe by now the new models are better but there must be hundreds or thousands like our still in use as Weehoo is one of the only companies on the market I know of that make this kind of trailer and it is much loved by many parents. (Including us til last week!) On the drive (chain) side, the drop out and chain stay is quite strong and large. One the non-drive side, I have frankly never seen such a thin drop out or chain stay on a bike. Because it is typically covered up by the cargo panniers/bags, you don't normally see the rear stays so it is possible many people like myself never noticed it before. Even if the rear wheel is primarily being held by the drive side drop out and chain stay, typically bikes are made with two strong rear dropouts for a reason, due to the risk of the rear wheel detaching or hitting the frame. The non-drive chain stay is also the rear "cargo rack" on which the bike bags are attached, so this part of the frame is doing "double duty" as both bike frame and rack. Again, this is not a typical bike design because it makes for high loads on the frame. The cargo bikes I am familiar with that use that sort of design typically employ very large diameter, thick, overbuilt tubing to support the high demands placed on the frame in that situation.

I am not a bike builder but am a long time recreational and long distance cyclist with a fair amount of experience with bikes over the years. It could be that this design doesn't create the safety risk that I think it does, but even if the wheel stays in place despite the possibility of a crack/partial crack in the rear drop out, it still creates a risk that the cargo or the "cargo rack" part of the frame would loosen/twist and end up tangled in the rear wheel so again this just seems like a fairly concerning design. Again, I know that bike frames are inherently have a small potential of failure/fatigue, and at the drop outs particularly, but this design just seems unnecessarily risky.
justification: The incident involved a structural failure of the bike trailer, but no injuries occurred as no one was using it at the time.

The large handle is hard plastic rounded edges except for the back of the handle. That section is a 90-degree edge sharp, sharp enough that it cut off the tip of my right pinky approximately 1/4 inch of it also took off my entire fingerprint or pad of the finger! Gone, the fatty tissue is all that is left. This could happen to anyone looking for a place to grab the chest because of its shape and placement. You assume it's a handle. It is not a handle. It's a support to turn the big handle into a tray holder! What a stupid design. They could have done the same thing by having two hinged supports that click in separately. Making something look like a handle in a spot you expect to have a handle is a bad idea and this has or will happen again. incident_description:
Our house is in Las Vegas, Nevada.  Around January 9, 2017, we installed a removable mesh pool fence with a Magna Latch for the gates.  This was to keep our young son and daughter from entering the pool.  In the early evening of June 20, 2017, friends visited.  Their children played in the pool with our children.  After a while, our daughter and her pool buddy left the pool because our daughter said that she was finished swimming.  However, at some point she went back to the pool and was able to open the gate.  She suffered a near drowning, and she passed away on June 29, 2017 from  injuries resulting from brain anoxia.

June 20, 2017, was a record hot day in Las Vegas.  A couple of days later, an investigation by the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department showed that the Magna Latch was not closing correctly.  The aluminum fence poles had bowed, which pulled the parts of the Magna Latch out of alignment.  The Magna Latch looked like it was closed, but it was not.  Subsequent inspections by experts have confirmed that the Magna Latch is not closing correctly.

Our family is completed devastated by the incident and the passing away of our very young daughter.
justification: The incident resulted in the death of a child due to a malfunctioning pool gate latch, which is the highest severity level.

Mr. [REDACTED] brought the Hisun to Moto El Paso and described that he felt the rear suspension fail before the accident. We contacted Hisun and told them of the accident and they declined to repair the vehicle and said they were not responsible.  Mr. [REDACTED] took the Hisun home.  Other customers came to the dealership with complaints about the rear suspension making abnormal noises and working abnormally, Hisun continued to say that no problem existed and the operation was normal.
Some time latter Hisun informed Moto El Paso that all of the 2015 Hisun 1000 side by sides and some of the 2016 Hisun 1000 side by sides had a rear suspension defect that needed to be repaired by the selling dealership. We began repairing these Hisun 1000 side x sides and are still repairing them when they come into our dealership and etc. I do not believe that Hisun made any attempt to notify the customers that purchased these Hisun products about the defect. They did not request that we contact customers although we did.  I am one dealership of Hundreds and I was told that Hisun only told its top five dealers about this defect (I am one of the 5) I believe that Hisun should have made this a recall and sent out notification to purchasers of these vehicles so as to eliminate the potential for more accidents.  I called Mr.[REDACTED] about his unit when I found out that the accident could have been a result of the defect but he had already sold the unit to a different user who I do not believe has been informed of the potential defect.

incident_description:
Hi,

I got my Apple Watch SE6 in Jan 2021. Since it's the latest "SE6" version and specifically designed for "Fitness and Sports", I wear it to track all my physical activities.
Last weekend (March 5, 2021) I was snowboarding with the "snowboarding mode" on. I took a small side hit jump and landed without falling. However, during the landing, my left wrist with the watch was squeezed in-between my chest and thigh, and somehow I felt a little pain on my wrist. I looked at the watch and it was still functioning and intact. Therefore, I did not pay much attention.

However, the pain started to grow so I took off the watch. Surprisingly, I found the back of the watch completely shattered, with glass pieces inside my skin. I was surprised to find that Apple does not use an impact-resistant glass that can withstand accidental force without shattering into pieces, like [REDACTED]. I mean, the watch was under normal usage, the impact was not big, nor did I hit anything hard, the front of the watch was completely intact, and the watch was still functioning fine. There might be a lot of variables which led to this extremely unlucky incident. However, the watch has a snowboarding workout option for a reason, and I was not doing anything way out of the ordinary.

I called Apple customer care but the engineers responded that this is a rare case, and all they could do is to repair it. They said customers should assume risks wearing it. However, even if I get a replacement, this could happen again, not only to me but to anyone. I was hoping Apple can handle this case more seriously, improve the design or change the type of material to protect the users.

My point is, the incident is strange that only the back of the watch shattered, while the watch is still functioning and intact. If the impact was that big, shouldn't the front side be broken/cracked as well? As I mentioned, I did not even fall or hit anything hard. The watch might have a "perfect collision" which buffered the impact in-between my body and broke only the underside?

As attached images / videos.
