I bought an exercise  bike from Amazon (from the Sunny Health and Fitness company based in California. This is the bike (https://www.amazon.com/Sunny-Health-Fitness-SF-B1002-Cycling/dp/B00467H5YW/ref=asc_df_B00467H5YW/?tag=hyprod-20&linkCode=df0&hvadid=167126942833&hvpos=&hvnetw=g&hvrand=6745425051090476001&hvpone=&hvptwo=&hvqmt=&hvdev=c&hvdvcmdl=&hvlocint=&hvlocphy=9032735&hvtargid=pla-307680638110&psc=1) They resistance pad which is listed as "leather" in their advertisements,  began to smell during use so we had it tested. Turns out the leather pad was actually composed primarily (85-90%) of friable Asbestos. 

We contacted Amazon in the hopes that they would refund us and pull the bike down from their store, where it is listed as a "Top Seller" and "Amazon's Choice." They gave us a refund but after almost a year of fighting with them they refused to pull the product from their store and continue to sell it to this day. I have contacted several agencies in California where I live and where the company is located, but they have all claimed they don't have jurisdiction over this type of safety issue. I still have the resistance pad in question as well as the test results from a Sacramento Testing company. I would hope that somehow you all can take action. I don't have the resources to file a lawsuit myself and my wife is incredibly concerned that we would be exposing ourselves to litigation. I am having trouble living with the fact that everyday these INDOOR bikes are exposing people and their families to a known carcinogen. Any help you can offer would be greatly appreciated.
justification: The incident involves exposure to asbestos, a known carcinogen, but no immediate injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
Re: UNREASONABLE RISK OF SERIOUS INJURY OR DEATH CONCERNING
HONDA CRF250R MULTIPLE YEAR MODELS AND OTHER DISPLACEMENT
MOTOCROSS OFF-ROAD HONDA MOTORCYCLES AND DENSO STATORS
DUE TO ELECTRICAL FAILURE AND SUDDEN UNINTENDED ENGINE SHUT
OFF ENGINE FAILURE DURING OPERATION AND WHILE IN MOTION.

I. REPORT AND COMPLAINT SUBMITTED IN ORDER TO PROTECT
CONSUMERS AND OTHER RIDERS FROM FORESEEABLE FUTHER
INJURIES OR DEATH DUE TO KNOWN UNSAFE AND UNREASONABLY
DANGEROUS HONDA AND DENSO DEFECTIVE PRODUCTS.

This Report and Complaint is respectfully submitted to the United State Consumer
Product Safety Commission in order to prevent foreseeable further injuries and
potential deaths due to known defective products put into the stream of
commerce by Honda and Denso and sold to Americans countrywide and affecting
certain motorcycles worldwide.

II. AMERICAN HONDA MOTOR CO., INC., HONDA MOTOR CO., LTD., DENSO
CORPORATION AND THE HONDA CRF250R.
This Report and Complaint and attachment(s) concerns certain model years Honda
CRF250R motocross off-road motorcycles manufactured by Honda Motor Co., LTD in
Japan and sold in the United States by American Honda Motor Co., Inc., with stators
incorporated thereto manufactured by Denso Corporation.
The population of affected Honda off-road motocross motorcycles are unsafe and
unreasonably dangerous to operate and must now be investigated, recalled and
properly remedied.

III. SUPERIOR COURT OF CALIFORNIA COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES
UNLIMITED CIVIL CASE.

In re and subsequent to the [REDACTED] [settled favorably for the Plaintiff]), we present facts that uncontrovertibly
demonstrate the clear existence of product defects that make certain model year Honda
CRF250R motorcycles unsafe and unreasonably dangerous to operate resulting in
unreasonable risk of serious injury or death.

American Honda Motor Co., Inc., Honda Motor Co., LTD., and Denso Corporation have
known for years about the foregoing product defects but have failed to report or recall
their defective unreasonably dangerous products.

IV. SUDDEN UNINTENDED ENGINE SHUT OFF DUE TO PRODUCT DEFECT.

The product defects contained within the 2014 and many other year model Honda
CRF250Rs, because they can result in the motorcycleÃÂs engine suddenly and
unexpectedly turning off during operation and ceasing operation in its entirety while in
motion (unintended engine shut off), which exposes children, retail end users and other
riders to unreasonable risk of serious injury or death because the motorcycleÃÂs engine
can suddenly and unexpectedly stop running and operation without any indication it is
about to fail.

The failure of the engine to continue running when appropriate may cause loss of
control, leading to motorcycle crashes and therefore significantly raises the risk of
serious injury or death.

V. REQUEST FOR INVESTIGATION OF HONDA AND DENSO; REQUEST FOR
INVESTIGATION AND RECALL OF UNREASONABLY DANGEROUS
PRODUCTS.

This Report and Complaint are submitted to formally request investigation of Honda and
Denso and recalls of the affected Honda CRF250R (and Honda CRF450R [and any
other model using similar Denso stators]) off-road motocross motorcycle populations in
the United States in order to reduce the unreasonable risk of serious injury or death to other unsuspecting operators. This Report and Complaint should be forwarded to your
counterparts in Canada and Europe wherein Honda has marketed and sold its defective
CRF250R off-road motocross motorcycles.

This Report and Complaint concerns a 2014 model year Honda CRF250R incident off road motocross motorcycle, a similar brand new 2014 model year Honda CRF250R
exemplar off-road motocross motorcycle, other similar models, and approximately five
or more years-worth of production Honda CRF250R motorcycles.

Multiple model years and multiple displacement off-road motorcycles are affected by the
product defect(s) and should be recalled by the manufacturer.

To our knowledge, Honda and Denso and their various business entities have not
voluntarily recalled these products.

Stator failures have occurred in the United States and Europe. Stator failures have
occurred with racing teams.

The manufacturer has subsequently improperly used or directed to be used, epoxy as a
means to secure defective stator wires. Honda likes gluing together important electrical
connections and Denso does not know whether their stators will be used on
motorcycles with or without 12VDC batteries and the results thereof. Both are
significant failures and embarrassments to Honda and Denso respectively.

The use of epoxy to additionally secure defective stator wires is below the standard of
care and not in accord with industry standards.

Honda and Denso have actual knowledge of the product defects that form the basis of
this Report and Complaint.

Honda and Denso should provide the Consumer Product Safety Commission with all
information, data and documents relevant to the matter in order to facilitate
determination of the scope of the defective statorÃÂs utilization in the population of
motorcycles it has sold to the American public and worldwide. A thorough investigation
by the CPSC will likely uncover the defects are both manufacturing and design defects.

A recall of all affected Honda off-road motorcycles using defective Denso stators will
help ensure no children or adults are seriously injured or killed as a result of HondaÃÂs
knowing and continued use of defective electrical components.
VI. HONDA STATOR FAILURES AND UNINTENDED ENGINE SHUT OFF
RESULTING IN ENGINE FAILURE AND SUBSEQUENT OPERATOR
PARALYSIS.

I was retained in order to look into a 2014 Honda CRF250R off-road motocross
motorcycle, its sudden unintended engine shut off and crash, operated by a licensed
professional rider, during practice, on a motorcycle closed-circuit dirt track.

The facts of the case indicate the incident 2014 Honda CRF250RÃÂs engine suddenly
and unintentionally shut off during normal and foreseeable operation, resulting in a
horrendous crash and subsequent rider paralysis. An objectively tragic outcome directly
caused HondaÃÂs defective product.

As part of the case workup, we determined a copper wire in the motorcycleÃÂs stator
located within the engine of the incident motorcycle had failed, fractured and
disconnected. The stator is made by Denso for Honda is at issue concerning these
defective unreasonably dangerous off-road motocross motorcycles, please see infra.

If a stator copper wire fractures the result is the engine shuts off (extremely fast, no prior
warning) in under 4/10ÃÂs of a second. Stators are not generally considered wear items
and are expected to last the life of most motorcycles.

As general mechanical and operational propositions and industry standards, stator
wires do not just become disconnected absent something more. The stator is internal to
the motorcycleÃÂs engine and it is not a component that can be damaged by merely
operating and riding these machines.

The crash of this 2014 Honda CRF250R off-road motocross motorcycle left the operator
seriously injured resulting in paralysis and he is now permanently handicapped in a
wheelchair for the rest of his life due to a particular defective Honda motorcycle.

As a court qualified motorcycle expert in the field of motorcycles and other vehicles, I
felt it necessary to report these defects and unsafe conditions present within the
population of Honda off-road motocross motorcycles in order to protect other children
and adults from being seriously injured or killed by these objectively defective Honda
and Denso products.

It is important these companies and products are now investigated and subsequently
recalled in order to preclude another serious injury or potential death associated with
these unreasonably dangerous and unsafe motorcycles.
VII. THE 2014 HONDA CRF250R INCIDENT OFF-ROAD MOTOCROSS
MOTORCYCLE.
Image 001 was captured during an early non-destructive visual only inspection of the
incident 2014 Honda CRF250R.

The stator is an electrical component located within the motorcycleÃÂs engine behind a
left side metal engine cover. As the engine rotates, magnets are rotated, on a rotor or
flywheel, around a set of copper windings and generate electrical current which then
goes on to provide ignition and spark to the engine in order for the engine to run and
continue running.

If a stator copper wire becomes an open circuit (a wire breaks), the motorcycleÃÂs stator
will no longer output electricity properly. These off-road machines do not have a 12
VDC battery on board designed in. Therefore, if the statorÃÂs electrical output is mechanically interrupted, the engine will almost immediately stop firing and will
suddenly and unexpectedly stop running and shut off, potentially leading to a crash
likely resulting in serious injury or death.
VIII. THE DEFECTIVE HONDA AND DENSO STATOR.
Image 002 is the actual incident Honda motorcycleÃÂs Denso stator assembly minus its
rotor.

The connection of the copper winding is at issue and the wire that fractured and failed
causing a serious motorcycle crash resulting in the operatorÃÂs paralysis can be seen
above (and below next page with magnification) partially within its connector surrounded
by solder.
Image 003 is with magnification of the solder ball covering the copper wire and its crimp
connector. Please notice the fracture and disconnect area are located around the
outside diameter (and through the wire) of the copper wire in image 003. Obviously,
this wire should not be in this fractured and disconnected improper condition absent a
product defect.

The fracture and disconnection of this wire caused an open circuit of the electrical circuit
powering the ignition to occur.

When power to the ignition is eliminated the motorcycleÃÂs engine almost immediately
shuts off, blink of an eye fast. We have tested exemplar stators and an exemplar 2014
Honda CRF250R off-road motocross motorcycle and produced video in which we
purposefully interrupted the stator electrical output and measured the time in which ittakes for the engine to suddenly shut off during operation. Loss of engine power can
cause a loss of vehicular control.

When a motorcycleÃÂs engine unexpectedly stops running and unintentionally suddenly
shuts off, a motorcycle may become difficult, if not impossible, to control and may cause
a crash resulting in serious injury or death.

The [REDACTED] Ignition Switch Recalls present similar circumstances to the known
defects regarding Honda and Denso products. Although the parts involved are different
from the [REDACTED] automotive ignition key switch recall from 2014, the results are
very similar in that much as if a [REDACTED] ignition fails and shuts off a motor vehicleÃÂs engine
a crash and serious injury or death can occur, the result of a failed Denso stator in a

Honda off-road motocross motorcycle is the same in that sudden unintended engine
shut off while in motion occurs which can cause a loss of vehicular control, a
subsequent crash and result in serious injury or death to children, the retail consumer or
other rider (other parts involved but same unsafe and unreasonably dangerous
conditions and results).

Additionally, the Honda CRF250RÃÂs engine cannot be restarted after stator and
therefore engine failure occurs. Once the stator failure occurs, the left side of the
engine must be disassembled, a new stator added and engine reassembly, then the
Honda CRF250R can be restarted and ridden.

We are submitting attached herewith a metallurgical report from a co-expert concerning
the metallurgical failure mode of the 2014 Honda CRF250R incident stator.

VIII. THE COVER UP RE WHAT DID HONDA AND DENSO KNOW AND WHEN
CONCERNING THE DEFECT WITHIN THE HONDA CRF250R ENGINE.

It is clear both Honda and Denso knew of the problems and defects associated with
their defective products for years but failed to voluntarily recall their defective products.
Honda had actual knowledge of the product defect for a lengthy period of time and thus
far to date has failed to do the right thing and failed to voluntarily recall their product(s).

HondaÃÂs supplier, Denso, failed to appreciate the potential results of wire failure within
the stator assembly and did not properly understand what would happen if a failure
were to occur.
Concerning HondaÃÂs supplier Denso, we do not know whether the defective
manufacture of motorcycle stators has occurred for other brands and applications and
whether defective stator assemblies have been supplied to other motorcycle
manufacturers.

It is conceivable the defective Denso stator issue is not limited to Honda motorcycles.

It would be important for CPSC to determine whether defective Denso stators are in
other brands of motorcycles, because the product defect may not be limited to Honda
off-road motocross motorcycles and may affect other brands of motorcycles as well.

Honda failed to take responsibility for the defect and blamed others for their productÃÂs
failure. Honda continued to market and sell the Honda CRF250R after and while having
actual knowledge of the product defects present within their engines.

The cover up of the product defect and failure to recall shocks the conscious and
intentionally exposes children, retail end user consumers and other riders to
unreasonable risk of serious injury or death.

Please investigate Honda and Denso regarding this Report and Complaint and the

models of Honda off-road motocross motorcycles, pursue recalls and appropriate
remedies for those affected by this unfortunate set of intentional circumstances. LetÃÂs
stop another tragedy before it occurs again. Thank you.

Respectfully submitted.

incident_description: My wife was riding her Pedego Interceptor on Jan 2, 2021 which she purchased in late 2018.  She was stopped at a traffic light and when the light turned green she began peddling when the e-bike accelerated rapidly.  It then came to abrupt stop without warning.  As a result she lost her balance and fell into the traffic lane.  Fortunately, traffic was light and she was not hit by a car.  However, she fell onto her knees and suffered pain and swelling.  She did not seek medical attention and after a few days of [REDACTED] and ice the pain and swelling subsided.  Prior to the accident the e-bike was not functioning smoothly.  The power seemed to lag and was not as responsive as usual.  Normally, she would set the power selector to the 1 or 2 position.  She thought that the battery might be nearly out, so she shifted the power selector to the highest level - 4.  It seemed to work until she came to the stop before the accident.  Additionally, in 2019, my wife experienced a similar problem with the e-bike.  When she would come to a stop, the bike's electronic pedal-assist would kick in and she could not control it.  I thought she might have inadvertently hit the throttle near the handgrip so I got on the bike and tried riding it and it happened to me as well.  We immediately took the bike into the store where we bought it and they "repaired it." I think they "reset" the computer on it and it seemed to work fine thereafter until the incident on Jan 2, 2021.  I would also wish to point out that even though the voluntary recall was posted on Sept 2020, we received no written or electronic notice of the recall.  It was only after the Jan 2, 2021 incident did I do a [REDACTED] search when I discovered the recall notice.  If purchasers of the product do not receive adequate notice of the recall, the recall is worthless.  The manufacture had all of our personal information to notify us and failed to do so.
justification: The rider suffered pain and swelling from the fall, indicating an injury (severity 3). The issue has occurred before and was not fully resolved, making recurrence possible (likelihood 3).

incident_description: In 2016, I purchased a brand new 2016 Honda Pioneer 1000 utility vehicle/side by side.  The bench seat was uncomfortably warm, because the motor is directly below it, and the vehicle did not come with heat shield protection.  Later, approximately one to two years later, during one of several safety recalls, the heat shield protection for the seat was added.  This greatly reduced the bench seat temperature.  However, one day while braking hard, dangerously the front bench seat cushion shifted forward, off of the plastic bench seat frame.  After stopping the vehicle I found that the bench seat cushion released from the frame because the glue that held it down failed, around the entire seat.  I also found the seat was water logged.  I notified Honda USA.  Honda USA referred my concern to the local dealer Southern Powersports, Chattanooga, Tn.  At this time the vehicle was past it's one year warranty so the dealer only offered to glue the seat back into the frame and not replace it.  I chose to glue it myself.  I used a [REDACTED]  brand adhesive.  This held for maybe a year and has since released, making the seat situation dangerous again.  In my personal, mechanically inclined, opinion I believe the high heat the bench seat endured, prior to the heat shield kit for the seat, caused the glue/adhesive to release.  I can't imagine the glue/adhesive manufacturer engineered their product to be used on a seat inches from a combustion engine without proper heat shielding.  In internet searches I found other owners of the same model from the same years that did not come equipped with the later added heat shield, having the same glue/adhesive problems.  I consider this to be a safety issue, just like if your car seat came off the frame, while you were braking.  Please help.

incident_description: I purchased a RadRunner 1 from Rad Power Bikse along with the passenger package for the bike (early Nov, 2020). The bike is marketed as being able to carry up to 300 lbs of rider and  passenger load. With me (150 lbs) and a passenger (120 lbs) the bike went only a short distance before the back tire blew off the rim.  Upon changing the tube, I noticed the stock tire is rated for a maximum load of 198 lbs. The front tire is the same. Since the bike weighs about 70 lbs. a non-engineer may mistakenly believe that leaves 300 lbs for a rider and passenger. But an engineer would understand the load for bike, rider and passenger is not evenly distributed between the wheels. My estimate  is that 2/3 of bike and rider weight is on the back wheel and the entire passenger weight is on the back wheel. So, with a 150 lb rider, that leaved less than 60 lbs available for passenger weight within the load limit for the back tire. This limit is not noted in the marketing for the bike and passenger package, in fact, the marketing shows 2 adults as rider and passenger.
justification: The incident involved a tire blowout due to exceeding the tire's load limit, but no injury was reported.

I purchased the stand in 2018 and the batch number is 1S-2217.  All four straps from these two stands are broken in the manner described in the recall. Two weeks ago, I had climbed down out of the tree and was bundling the stand for transit out of the woods when I noticed that the straps were broken. These straps have two strands of braided cables, and in each of these, one of the braided cables were broken.  I investigated the stand manufacturer and found the existing recall for the two other models. I then contacted Alliance Outdoor Products and was told that even though my cables broke in the same manner as those in the stands under recall, they would not refund the purchase price. I was told that the reason they were breaking is that people were leaving their stands outside in inclement weather! I do not care about the refund, I simply want this company to address the safety issue that they are now aware of. On 9-23-2020 I went to cock the crossbow using the crank cocking device.  I cranks the bow back to about 3/4 cocked, when the crank cocking device string broke. X-rays revealed no broken bones.  I have severe soft tissue damage the size of a baseball to the top of my foot.  Dr [REDACTED], Ankle and Foot Specialist has me wearing a compression sock to reduce the chance of a blood clog.  I have to wear a Support Boot and keep my foot elevated as much as possible.
There are several complaints on the internet of the crank cocking device string breaking while cocking.  One person reported that the hooks missed his foot, but hit and ground and then ricocheted up striking him in the forehead

Again on9-25-2020 I called and waited on hold for over an hour.  Still no answer.  Why are they in hiding?  What other defective products do they have out in the market place?
justification: The incident resulted in severe soft tissue damage from the crossbow's defective crank cocking device, and similar incidents have been reported by others.

incident_description:
In early June of 2020, I purchased a Schwinn bicycle from WalMart.  When I first rode it, the rear wheel became misaligned and the rear gear cassette lost its bearings.   Upon closer inspection, I found out that the rear hub had split at the threads that the gears mount on.  I registered my bicycle with Schwinn and made a warranty claim.  Schwinn sent me a new wheel assembly that I mounted on my bike.  On July 25th, I rode my bike again for the first time after repairing it and the rear wheel misaligned again, but didn't crack the hub threads.  I disassembled the new hub and compared the parts to the old hub.  I found out that the reason for failure is because the axles had bent in both assemblies.  I rode my bike only on paved roads and never jumped it or went over bumps, but I go up steep hills and challenge myself with higher gear settings.  I suspect the failure is occurring because the supporting bearings on the gear half of the hub are deeply recessed.  At the highest gear, the rear cassette is set to the outer-most gear.  This applies the highest amount of stress on the axle and the axle bends under the load because the bearing is not at the outside of the hub, but about 1.5" recessed and the axle appears to be made with very soft steel.  At this point, I don't believe the bicycle design is safe and Schwinn has stopped responding to my emails.  I also can't contact Schwinn on their support phone number because their system simply reports that there are no associates available and then hangs up.  On this page of this form, I don't see a way to attach images, but I have images.  I will attach if possible or provide them if needed.  I also still have all of the parts (except for the bearings from the first wheel assembly).  My bicycle information is:
Manufacturer: Schwinn
Model Number: S8074WMDS, 24 speed "Taff" Mountain Bike, 29"
Serial Number: SNXDS19G23265
justification: The incident involves repeated mechanical failures of the bicycle's rear wheel assembly, posing a risk of injury but no actual injury reported.

When I turned it on it blew the fuse I rechecked all my wirng and it was fine so I moved the lightbar and put it on a battery by itself and it worked fine so I grabbed the lightbar to move it and it shocked me. Thats when i realized that the light bar was shorting and the entire housing of the light was electrified. I checked with my multimeter by putting the positive probe to the lightbar frame and the negative to the UTV Frame and it read a constant 11 volts
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (shock) due to an electrified lightbar, indicating a moderate severity. The likelihood is possible given the described scenario.

So the eyes have to be everywhere. Unfortunately, the rider before he got on left the vehicle in neutral, motor running, and parking brake on. Unaware that the parking brake was on he drove a good 15-20 minutes in the back field and returned with the ATV ENGULFED in smoke, and oil literally boiling all over the differential. No clue did he have as to why the malfunction. He is inexperienced, not rough with it and was just enjoying the trails in my backyard, which is an old cornfield. We had just had the 20 hour break in service, so we really did not know what was going on. 
After investigation by Suzuki ( the repair shop sent pictures  of the damaged parts) it was determined he rode with brakes engaged which created friction , heating up the guts of the differential, and caused damage to the differential from the heat . The ATV was very hot, and melted many parts, including the Fuel tank cover. The damages amounted to $2500.00. 
My point here, and what I sincerely want to advocate is had there been a brake
Light, or alarm this would have never gotten this far. He had absolutely no knowledge of what the problem was. With the amount of damages and the degree of heat and smoke and enough to melt the fuel cover... im thinking he was pretty close to injuring himself and lucky to be alive.
Not all ATV buyers have experience, many riders are very young. There are many obstacles to watch for when riding. The brake pedal is on the foot rest and the foot can easily be bounced on it when going in dips, etc. I do not know the statistics on these type occurrences, but I can share my experiences. 
I would be more than happy to share with you the damaged parts to provide you the extent of damage and support my request for the need, in the name of safety, a requirement for brake warning lights or alarms be mandated when manufacturing ATVÃÂs.
justification: The incident caused significant damage to the ATV but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I was riding a Catrike Expedition recumbent tricycle on the golf course cart pathway in [REDACTED] on August 23, 2017. The rear wheel ejected at approximately 11 mph and the trike flipped causing my  head to hit the concrete and all four appendages to be injured. I attended [REDACTED] Emergency Room and was treated. I suffered permanent damage to the nerves exiting the foramen at Cervical Vertebrae 4 and 5, causing dysphagia, a life-long inability to swallow normally and breathe. The tricycle was examined by a renowned metallurgical engineer, [REDACTED] of the [REDACTED] engineering department. The quick release skewer that holds the wheels in on almost all recumbent tricycles (of which there are tens of thousands in use in America) is subjected to pressure that exceeds the ability of the quick release skewer to retain the wheel in the frame sixty fold greater than design. Every one of these recumbent tricycles that are not manufactured with a thru axle design are categorically unsafe. I am aware of at least 7 (seven) other riders who have been injured by the ejection of the rear wheel on a recumbent tricycle. Big Cat Human Powered Vehicles, LLC is the only manufacturer I am aware of in the United States. The company is located in Orlando, FL. After consultation with their counsel in early 2018 and demanding that Big Cat manufacture their tricycles with thru axles, in October 2019 Big Cat announced that all future trikes would be made with thru axle designs. Yet there are thousands of trikes manufactured before October 2019 made by Big Cat in use.
justification: The incident resulted in permanent nerve damage and lifelong dysphagia, indicating a severe injury (level 3). The occurrence likelihood is high (4) due to the known design flaw affecting thousands of trikes and multiple reported injuries.

She was in our inflatable kiddie pool, pulled the mermaid tail up to her shoulders, and tucked her arms inside. Then she went under the water and couldn't use her arms or legs to get out. FORTUNATELY her older daughter was right there and pulled her out. She spent two days in the hospital but made a complete recovery.

I'm making this report because you can buy mermaid tail swimsuits anywhere online, but there are no warnings about this hazard. I realize that parents are ultimately responsible for their children's safety, and we are still scarred that we did not see this happen with our own eyes. 

I would advocate for a mandatory point-of-purchase warning on any swimsuit that can restrict movement, to make clear that mermaid tails especially simply should not be used in water by children.

incident_description:
Approximately March 1st 2020, when the weather had warmed enough to make biking comfortable, I set out to test the Pedal Assist Function (PAS) capability on my new Ebike. On the lowest setting (1) when I pedaled, the bike accelerated to about 18 mph. This is faster than you can pedal the bike in the highest mechanical gear, meaning you are not in control of the speed. You must hit either brake or stop pedaling to regain control. The brake cuts power immediately, but there is a delay after you cease pedaling. This behavior on a crowded bike path or city streets where there may be obstacles or need for care could easily cause an accident.  The expected behavior would be gentle acceleration to something more like 5-7 mph, where the bicyclist could keep up or at least avoid obstacles, steer around pedestrians etc. The higher levels of Pedal Assist Mode go even faster. 
Other ebikes I've tried have much more reasonable speeds for pedal assistance mode. Fortunately, I was testing the bike on a smooth, level stretch of road with no traffic, so no one was hurt and I simply don't use the pedal assist mode as it's unduly hazardous even where conditions permit the speed. The ebike company has asked for data and explanations over and over, but has done nothing to correct the problem. I have found others who said they have the same problem with this bike. Here are the youtube links for one review.

[REDACTED]

It is a little hard to explain but over a dozen emails should have got the message across to people who _build_ ebikes. Even with a language barrier.

I am a fan of ebikes and hate to do anything to discourage their adoption, but they should undergo some testing and QA.
justification: The incident describes a hazardous bike behavior that could lead to accidents, but no actual injury occurred during testing.

incident_description: This product is a trap hazard for children, especially toddlers or crawling children. When stored in the upright position as advertised and described in the manual, this product is at risk of trapping or otherwise harming a small child. The product is held upright by a single hydrolic piston. When touched, this piston releases and is gravity aided to convert the treadmill belt deck into the downward position for use. There is no locking mechanism to prevent this process and there is no safeguard to stop the descent of the belt deck. If a small child were to go under the belt deck and trigger the piston by simply touching it lightly, the belt deck would descend potentially trapping the child under the full weight of the belt deck (Which takes two people to lift). This could result in harm or even death. This issue may be resolved by employing a single strap around the console and the bottom of the belt deck to hold the belt deck into the upright position and prevent accidental triggering of the piston.
justification: The incident describes a scenario that could result in harm or death to a child, with a clear mechanism for the hazard to occur.

incident_description: Please note that this was not an incident. I am reporting safety issues with a bike that I purchased. I purchased a 20" wheel-sized bike for my child on Amazon.com. It was listed as "Schwinn Elm Girls Bike for Toddlers and Kids". Although it is a Schwinn branded bike, I believe that the manufacturer's name was Pacific Cycles, as I noted from the manual that came with the bike. The bike that I received had numerous flaws. First, the front fork was manufacturer bent, so that one of the forks was essentially pointing straight up/down, while the other fork was pointing outward. This made it difficult to attach the front wheel to the fork, and was what led me to do an examination of the fork prior to completing assembly. Any parent who does not understand bikes might not detect the issue. It's a potentially big concern since the wheel would be very difficult to install, and would not be safe when installed. Secondly, I found that the hubs of both the front and rear wheel had a deep, grinding sound, indicating that the wheel hubs/bearings were defective. Thirdly, I found that the pedal/crank bearings were also flawed, and made a similar grinding noise as the front and rear wheel hubs. Finally, there have been significant negative reviews for this particular bike on Amazon.com left by parents, namely with safety concerns. In addition to some parents experiencing the issues I've described above, other parents noted that the chain broke after day three of riding, the pedals becoming loose, the pedal/crank bearings breaking after short use (sometimes causing the chain to again fail). The percentage of one star reviews on Amazon.com (mostly safety concerns) is at 11%, while a significant proportion of the 2- and 3- star reviews (i.e., 10% combined) also mention safety and quality control issues with this bike. Please note that I no longer have the bike. I returned it back to Amazon.com on the day that I received it, after detecting the serious flaws with the bike.
justification: The bike had multiple safety defects but no actual incident or injury occurred as it was returned immediately.

incident_description: The Hover 1 Rally electric scooter (see https://www.hover-1.com/hover1-l5-specs) has a design flaw regarding the steering of the electric scooter. The metal stem that leads from the front steering tire up into the handles that give the rider steering control is secured using a very thin piece of plastic. Both the wheel stem and handle bar assembly are metal. Once this small plastic bracket breaks from use (my sons scooter broke after just 5 months of use while he was riding on a public sidewalk and was fortunate enough the scooter veered off into grass opposite the moving traffic in the street) the rider completely loses steering of the scooter. This can have very bad consequences for the rider considering these are usually ridden on public sidewalks and roadways sharing space with or in very close proximity to traffic. I have contacted the company with the issue and all they want to do is replace the plastic bracket with a new one. This is a serious design flaw that needs corrected with an appropriately designed metal bracket to ensure riders maintain control of the scooter at all times. The scooter has a folding design which likely leads to the stressing of the plastic bracket and eventual breakage. That and use of the scooter over sidewalks and streets with bumps and expansion joints which transmit energy up through the wheel into the bracket that is clamping the steering column into the wheel stem also stresses the plastic bracket.
justification: The scooter has a design flaw that can lead to loss of steering, which can be dangerous when riding on public sidewalks and roadways.

I removed the front differential once I got the vehicle back to my house and it was completely  broken in half.  The problem looks to be the welds on the pin holding the spider gear in place broke and the pin locked between the gear and the housing, locking up the front end and steering, causing loss of control of the vehicle. This was a very scarey and dangerous situation and Artic Cat needs to expand the recall to include the 2008/2009 side by sides.

incident_description:
My daughter was cut by the pedals on a stationary exercise bike that unexpectedly had an sharp unfinished metal edge.  Note that this is a stationary bike where you sit and pedal, the bike was not moving and she did not fall or tip over, the pedal just slipped off her foot.  She was using the bike and simply slipped off the pedal, which caused it to scrape against her shin.  Normally this would cause a minor scrape/scratch and maybe a small bruise.  Since the pedal had an unfinished edge which looks like it was not smoothed on one side after it was stamped/cut, the metal edge was very sharp.  She had a large irregular shaped portion of skin sliced off her shin down to the fatty tissue underneath.  There was too much skin removed to be able to stitch it shut, an area roughly 1" by 1" had no skin at all, with a 2" long deep cut coming out of one side.  She went to urgent care and has had I believe 5 appointments since then with a plastic surgeon.  She was in a lot of pain and had a hard time walking or doing other activities for almost 2 weeks. 
 Nearly a month later, the skin still hasn't fully scabbed over and the plastic surgeon expects another month or so of initial recovery plus more to deal with the scarring and any subsequent procedures that will be necessary.  The seller admitted the pedals were not properly finished, but it is unclear whether the defect was with all pedals or just ours.  I want to make sure that other users are notified and other people do not use the unsafe pedals.  It is not that the pedals are metal, or have bumps, it is that one edge of the metal is knife-like because it was not finished properly during manufacturing.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe injury requiring multiple medical interventions and prolonged recovery, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) since the defect was specific to an unfinished pedal edge, not a common issue.

incident_description: I have a Hayward Star Clear Plus C900 cartridge filter for my swimming pool.  After cleaning the filter and reassembling the housing, I started the pump.  The filter was filling back up with water and just as the water started to shoot out of the breather cap I leaned over it to check the pressure because the gauge faces up and as I did that, the filter lid exploded off the filter body housing, hitting me in the face.  I sustained a 9cm cut from the bridge of my nose that went all the way through my right eyebrow.  It cracked me all the way to the skull and it took over 50 stitches at the initial surgery to close me back up. It also cracked my front tooth.  I have had 2 plastic surgeries, 3 visits to the dentist to fix my tooth, damage to my optical nerve and ongoing neurological problems.  I have varying degrees of pain and pressure in my head on a daily basis.  When we looked at the filter to try and figure out what happened we noticed that the threads recessed on the inside top of the lid were about 75% worn away.  There was also a greenish blue residue from the corrosion on the threads and on the stainless steel shaft that it screws down on. The owner's manual for this product states the filter is "ÃÂÃÂ.Manufactured from durable, corrosion-proof materials."  This is totally false.  The inside threads corroded to the point they couldn't hold the pressure any longer.    I have had other people contact me with the same filter telling me theirs exploded and sending me pictures of the top inside of their filter lids with the same corrosion.  Every doctor I have seen has told me I am lucky to be alive.  We found out the lid hit the bottom of a concrete window ledge on the way up to my face and took a chunk out of the concrete.  The doctors feel the energy that concrete absorbed is the only reason I am alive. I contacted Hayward who said they plan to do nothing in regards to the entire situation.  Hayward is well aware of this problem, not just from me, but from others if you dig. Every one of these units is a ticking time bomb.

As the cart attempted to start I heard a loud POP from the engine under the seat.  The cart moved backward out of the garage but never really started properly.  I then smelled a burning oder coming from the cart.  At first I thought it was an electrical issue.  I lifted the seat to see if something was melting.  I saw smoke coming from the air intake filter.  I open the clips and removed the cover.  Mores smoke was coming from the air filter.  I lifted the filter out of the box and found that it was smoldering.  I took it over to an outside faucet and ran water on it to put it out.  By the time I got it to the faucet there were actually flames coming from the filter.  The foam filter that sits under the main filter had melted in the filter box.  

I purchased this vehicle new in 2017 and have not had any problems with it to this point.  It has had all regular required service performed by the dealer I purchased it from.   I believe that had I not intervened and removed the smoldering filter the entire vehicle would have been consumed by flames.

I have contacted the dealer and they will be looking into repairing the cart.  I felt like this is a dangerous situation and needed to be reported and looked into further.
justification: The incident involved a smoldering air filter that could have led to a fire, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:

I was cocking the bow, (which involves having your foot through a straddle at the front of the bow and pressed against the ground, and then pulling the bow string upwards with a cocking rope until it engages the trigger) and the bow string had crossed the dry fire safety and almost engaged the trigger when suddenly the right side of the bow assembly let loose. The bow ribs on the right side, both upper and lower ones, had cracked horizontally which had released the pin and then the wheel.The pin and wheel exploded out of the bow striking me just over the knee on the inner thigh. This bow has 185 lbs of pressure when cocked so the force of the wheel and pin striking me was very strong. Luckily I was wearing thick jeans which stopped penetration, but I still received a painful injury and a large bruise (I took a picture of the bruise two weeks after the fact - it was still there although faded. 

I contacted the company to get my money back, which they refused. I explained to them that I no longer had any trust in their product, and my reasons which should be obvious. I explained that if the direction of my pull was slightly different I could have got the pin in my eye, which at 185 lbs pressure would have entered the brain as well and killed me. I told them that while I got lucky somebody else may not. They did not address my concerns at all, which is why I am filing this complaint. I want a clear conscience that I informed the authorities hopefully before someone is seriously injured or killed by this faulty product. My hope is you can take action to prevent this. Sincerely, [REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in a painful injury and a large bruise, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as the incident happened once in a month of use with 30 bolts fired.

incident_description:

The primary cvt clutch is coupled to the output shaft of the engine so when the belt strings wrapped around the primary clutch sheaves  it got wound up so tight that it stopped the shaft from turning dead in its tracks. I was absolutely not expecting this to happen and of course an atv has no seatbelt, the only protection is the helmet i was wearing thank god. As the front and rear axles instantly stopped turning without warning which was something i never new was even possible and surely with just 380 miles on the machine the cvt belt still had another 1500 miles to go before it should need to be replaced. The atv wpuld not respond to my efforts to steer the machine away from the road, instead it headed towards the edge of the road which had a huge lip of about 6-9ÃÂ. When the front left tire first touched the edge of the asphalt it caused the atv to bank to the right real hard and then my front right tire hit a huge washout and i was thrown from the machine and broke my right wrist. 
This is the 3rd time this atv has destroyed a belt because there is something defective with the primary drive cvt wet clutching assembly that causes it to heat up way beyond normal and then the driven cvt sheaves get so hot that the belt disintegrates and no ÃÂBELTÃÂ light came on or anything which is supposed to when it gets too hot. 342 deg F is what the cvt housing reads after just 8 mins of riding at any speed.  Tons of ppl have had this same problem over and over and Textron tells everyone thats past the 6month warranty that theres nothing they will do to resolve the defect. my atv has 384 miles on it! thats nothing for mileage. first time this happened it had 103 miles. Took to dealership and they said they couldnt do anything since textron bought arctic cat out and textron wouldnt help the ceoÃÂs own son if it came down to it. 
Im pissed. i bring my 6 yr old for little rides on that machine and if he was on it he could have been seriously injoured or killed. i could have been thrown off the atv and flown into the road infront of the suv and then my son would have had to live his life without a father. TEXTRON knows this is a problem! they lasted less then a year and sold to tracker but they need to be held accountable. no one should have to die before you pressure/ force them to hold themselves accountable. i have a $6k piece of garbage now that no one will buy from me because they are known for this issue and its extremely dangerous not to mention expensive to fix. Just put the 4th belt on it and at $180+ each and having primary replaced and then blew another belt, then had one way bearing replaced thinking it was the problem and boom blew another, had the primary rebuilt again and boom another belt gone. its not safe. im not spending $700 to have the wet clutches replaced on a brand new machine.

incident_description:
I purchased a new 2015 Trek Emonda SL5 Red with the Sram Red 22 mechanical group set from a Trek retailer.  After approximately 5,000 miles, I noticed that the chain was not maintaining tension.  This led me to discover that the rear derailleur cage was beginning to separate from the rear derailleur body.  If the cage were to separate from the derailleur body, the cage could enter the rear wheel and cause catastrophic damage to the wheel, bicycle frame, and result in serious injury or death.  

Sram does not specify any routine maintenance for Sram Red rear derailleurs.  I decided to disassemble the derailleur cage from the derailleur body to see if it needed lubrication.  Upon disassembling the derailleur, I discovered that the rear derailleur's pivot pin and retention screw had worn into each other, wearing down both (see pictures).  This could cause the derailleur cage to loosen or dislodge causing the rear derailleur to jam or interfere with the wheel, posing a fall hazard.

I did some research and discovered [REDACTED].  My derailleur has the exact same failure as described in the recall, but the serial number, 45T46097328, does not fall within the range specified in the recall.  I suspect this defect may apply to more derailleurs than the ones identified in the recall, and warrants additional investigation.

I called Sram about this issue.  I was notified that they do not have replacement parts available (i.e. no rear derailleur cage assemblies or retention screws), and that the only remedy is to replace the entire derailleur at my expense.  I inquired if there were any financial assistance offered by the company, and I was told no.  The MSRP for a new Sram Red 22 mechanical rear derailleur is $310.
justification: The incident describes a potential mechanical failure that could lead to serious injury or death, but no actual injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description:
2017, 2018 and 2019 Arctic Cat snowmobiles equipped with Team roller bearing primary clutches and the Arctic Cat Ctec2 engine are experiencing drive clutch failures and structural failures.  The drive clutches are failing and pieces of jagged metal are flying off the clutch. The speed of the clutch is 8000rpm. The speed of the departing pieces are 190mph. The jagged pieces of metal can be as big as a baseball. The damage from the incidents are causing major damage to the snowmobiles. It is only a matter of time before there is serious bodily injury. The drive clutch is within 18ÃÂ of the operator. 

The cause of the clutch failures is three fold. 1. The clutch cover is too weak to withstand the internal spring and weight forces. This causes the cast aluminum to flex and weaken. 2. The design is such that the cover contacts the spider nut and causes the tower and cover to flex which in turn weakens the metal. 3. Engine harmonics from the Ctec2 engine. The metal damaging harmonics accelerates the clutch fractures. The clutch eventually flies apart under load at 8000rpm. 

The Ctec2 engine equipped snowmobiles are having major structural component fail as well. The ÃÂAÃÂ frame chassis bolts are coming loose which could cause frame failure. The secondary clutch bolts are coming loose which could cause the secondary clutch to come unbolted at 8000 rpm. The clutch is constructed in such a way that there are essentially two 11ÃÂ discs bolted together. When the bolt backs out from harmonics, the discs are now free to become detached at 8000rpm. The secondary clutch is 8ÃÂ from the operators leg. The tunnels are cracking on major structural stress points where attached to the chain case.  The tunnel could fail and cause the vehicle to be unpredictable.  The bottom aluminum gear is rapidly wearing which could cause an unexpected instant stop. 

The Ctec2 engine has an inherent problem which is called harmonics. Engine harmonics are extremely damaging to metal parts. Especially structural and metal stress points. Damage is not always visible to the naked eye so once a vehicle has experienced harmonics, there is no way to tell how much damage has been done. The only way is to remove the vehicles from service. 

Arctic has attempted to fix the problem in 2017 by issuing a voluntary recall #17-748 for about 2,700 vehicles. The recall did not fix the issues and the problems are still occurring in 2019.  The company has not issued another recall and are in some cases, denying warranty. 

As evidence of trying to fix the harmonics issue, they have redesigned the cylinders, fuel injector placement, a new flywheel and engine torque link to help ÃÂengine vibration damping.ÃÂ Arctic Cat has disguised this vibration fix as a new and improved engine. While this is step in the right direction, it does not address the past model issues. 
The horsepower/torque curve has been substantially altered for model year 2020. 
Even though Arctic Cat has known injury to the operator is possible and likely, another recall has not been issued. The company obviously cannot be trusted to keep the public from injury. For this reason, this issue needs Federal Agency involvement in the form of a mandatory recall.
justification: The description indicates that serious bodily injury is likely due to high-speed metal fragments and structural failures, placing the operator at significant risk.

incident_description:
I ordered a Predator Platform from Tethrd last year. Upon delivery (approximately in September of 2018), I promptly went to set it up on the tree and it broke when camming it over to lock it onto the tree. I reached out to the company, and they sent a new one. 

However, within the same week multiple other hunters had broken the platform in the same manner, prompting Tethrd to release a "gen 2" platform that was reinforced in the area where they were breaking. They DID NOT recall the original predator platforms, but discontinued manufacturing them and replaced originals with the gen 2 design if consumers requested it. They maintained that there was nothing wrong with the original design, but that they wanted to "beef up" the gen 2 to make it "bulletprood." Tethrd and their representatives repeatedly claimed that the platform was safe to use if used in accordance with their instructions.

Yesterday evening, a consumer posted a picture of his original platform broken in the same manner as mine and others. Several other individuals had also broken the platform over the past year, and were unaware that there were two versions of the platform. Tethrd representatives continued to assert that the platforms did not need to be recalled.

I believe that a tree platform that can potentially break 20ft in the air is dangerous, and consumers should be aware of the dangers. I would like the manufacturer to recall the product, and publish the recall information on their web page and social media sites. There are obviously hunters still using them, and breaking them during use.

incident_description:
In summer 2017, I purchased the Little Tikes Tree House Swing Set and installed it according to the manufacturer's instructions.  Unbeknownst to me, the instructions contained an engineering error that resulted in very serious instability of the entire swingset and danger to the children uses. 

Over time, it started shaking and vibrating and became impossible to swing on, because the railing and posts were mostly disconnected an dready to fall apart

Four bolts holding the railing to the posts became loose and unstable because they were not installed with washers on each side.  The swingset was installed according to the manufacturer's instructions, which called only for a plastic "bolt cover."  Four of these are used, and all four broke.   

I only realized the company's error when I was looking for replacement parts and saw the instructions for the "Endless Adventures Swing Set," which has almost identical layout and engineering.  This nearly identical product is shown with washers installed on both sides of the swingset.  

I have communicated with the customer service for Little Tikes and they have not yet taken responsibility.
justification: The swingset became unstable and dangerous, but no injury or death was reported.

We contacted Super Jumper by phone and email on July 29.  We received an email from Super Jumper with a recall form to complete and submit, which we immediately did.

As of the date of this writing, we have called multiple times the number (during listed business hours) and we have re-submitted the recall form to receive the repair kit at least 3 separate times.

To date they have not responded to our calls or email submissions.  We have not received the repair kit.

And now our Trampoline HAS FAILED just as the recall warned.  A weld on the leg separated and broke.  The trampoline is now inoperable and we have so far been unable to contact or resolve this issue with Super Jumper.

If our experience is anything like what others are receiving, then I'd say this company is failing miserably to meet their obligations.

incident_description:
My 8 year old daughter attends a school in [REDACTED]. While playing on the monkey bars she fell and severely broke her arm.  The break required two separate  surgeries, one too implant a steel bar and the other too remove the steel bar.  The doctor bills have exceeded $100,000.00.
I am a licensed structural engineer so I have a background in investigating engineering problems.. 
[REDACTED], my daughter [REDACTED] leaped from the platform 3ft off the ground to the bars shown in the picture. The top bars are not parallel as are typical on monkey bars. Therefore, she jumped to the third bar which is at an angle.  Since the bar is at an angle one of her hands would reach the bar before the other.  On typical monkey bars both hands would reach the rung at the same time thus dividing the load evenly between both hands. The first hand would see most of her weight thus causing her to fall from the rung. It is hard to believe that the codes and standard rules for monkey bars ever considered the existing configuration.
Yesterday a girl named [REDACTED] broke her arm falling off the ladder to the circular rings. Again demonstrating the floor material is simply to hard. I have felt it and barely deflects.
The flooring is a PIP surface and is very hard I don't think it can attenuate much energy.  We know of four other children she knows who have either fractured or broken bones this school year, The school has hundreds of students with about 40 other locations.  There are probably many other students who have also been injured.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe injury (broken arm requiring surgeries) and there are reports of multiple similar injuries, indicating a recurring issue.

incident_description:
This is a basic recap of the safety incident report sent to Polaris.

I was driving a trail with some side hills and turned down a steep 100 yard long hill crawling at 3-5mph with foot on brake in 4 low/AWD. Then my brake pedal goes down an inch. I pump it and get most of pedal back. A few feet later I loose brakes and take a fast ride with brake pedal to the floor and using what engine braking I had. I finally stopped at the bottom after a hard turn on two wheels into a V ditch crossing. The left front fender was damaged from the side of the ditch where it stopped.  Pulled fender screw backer nut through the plastic and some deep body scratches.

I got out and inspected the brake fluid level thinking the master cylinder must have failed or brake line.  The fluid was slightly low.  I looked at the back side of wheels for signs of brake fluid leaks. Nothing on the rig wet. Then I see a mangled brake pad and backing plate laying inside the right rear wheel. First look at the outside of the wheel and I see the hub cap is gone and the wheel/hub are out of the bearing at a bad angle.

At first I thought the castle nut had somehow backed off shearing the cotter key. After getting a ride out for a jack and some larger tools than I normally carry I took it apart on the trail. I was shocked to find the brake caliper was all that was holding the hub and wheel on because the end of the stub axle that is threaded was completely sheared off. The hub chewed up the outer brake pad as it became wedged when the rotor and hub were separating from the axle and bearing. The hub was completely out of the bearing at this point and the axle splines where no longer in the hub. I pulled the hub and wheel off by hand!  Felt lucky I didnÃÂt lose the wheel and roll down the hill end over end.  With help I was able to straighten the brake parts with a hammer and other tools enough to install them best we could.  With another RZR towing me, we stopped every hundred yards to jack up the vehicle and put the hub and wheel back into the bearing.  I rode the brakes in an effort to hold the wheel and hub in the bearings.  Took several hours to reach camp safely.

This ride started out on flat dirt road about 2 miles from camp.  Sunny and dry day in [REDACTED].  Mostly rocks and dirt like all of the [REDACTED] roads/trails.  I drove across a side hill section of trail to a steep downhill.  Some rocks here and there, but nothing challenging I have not accomplished many times in 30 years of off road experience.

I had no issues until brakes went out.  I had just inspected all fluid levels and checked tire pressure before I started out like I always do.  When this happen some CV grease got on the exhaust pipe and put off some heavy smoke, but no fire.  I had basic tool kit with mini air compressor and tire plug kit in the bed inside a plastic tote tied down.  I also had mini jumper cables, tow strap, rain jacket, an MRE, and some other small items along with 4 small bottles of water.  Fire extinguisher is mounted on the rear roll bar.

I recently rebuilt the front diff due to metal cage on pinion bearing failing and eating the pinion seal at 550 mile point.  I sealed the outdrive hub plugs at this time because they started leaking at 200 mile point. Basically a new machine, but I replaced weak front driveshaft u-joints at this time as well.  I service all fluids such as oil in engine and diffs more frequently than needed, 25 hrs or less.  Last service about 225 miles ago.  I drive about 100 miles between a full inspection.  OCD on maintenance in an effort to make my rigs last.  DoesnÃÂt seem to be helping this unit though.

As an ASE certified mechanic since 1986, I do all my own work on every vehicle I have ever owned.  IÃÂm certified by [REDACTED] on A/C, brake systems, fuel systems, diagnostic equipment, wire blueprints, engine and transmission rebuildsÃÂ both manual and automatic.  I have worked for [REDACTED] turning crankshafts, boring engine blocks and re-manufacturing engine heads.  I also worked for 2 years at a professional speed shop building race engines before serving 22 yrs in the military.

I maintain a maintenance record for each of my rigs. All my vehicles get more service than required.  I have never had the rear of this unit apart.  Still had original parts and tires on the rear.  I never had reason to remove hubs until now.

My RZR has a light bar, roof, windshield, enclosure, heater and fan under roof for me.  I have full coverage insurance in place.  Insurance Company: [REDACTED]. No claim filed on my insurance.  This was a manufacturer defective part.

I drive mountain roads and jeep trails.  Most of that has been in [REDACTED] this year.  Some in [REDACTED].  Few days a week around my home on flat forest covered ground.

I was lucky.  The next guy might not be driving slow or be experienced enough to deal with the incident or have help close by.  This is a part of the axle that should never fail.  It appears that the metal in the stub axle was not heat treated properly or insufficient depth of hardness may have caused low subsurface shear strength at the end of the axle.  Basically the metallurgical properties on this part of the stub shaft needs to be redesigned and strengthened.  A better heat treatment process focused on the threaded part of the axle and shoulder would increase shear strength.  However, the metal should be tested for inherent shear strength in this area and consideration of larger diameter material should also be investigated.  First time I have ever seen a failure on any machine at this threaded axle point.  That includes truck and automotive vehicles involved in major accidents.

Something is not right about this axle and actions to prevent this safety issue are needed. I retained the broken axle for investigation or testing if needed.
justification: The incident resulted in vehicle damage but no injuries, and the failure is described as highly unusual by an experienced mechanic.

incident_description: In February I took my BCD to [REDACTED] for my yearly maintenance. I also had a complaint that the inflator was sticking and sometimes it would slowly inflate. The dive shop examined it and agreed it was a problem and sent it back to Aqualung.  A couple of months later the shop called and said it was back. So I went to pick it up. When the shop gave it to me I immediately noticed it wasn't fixed. It was still sticking. The shop technician looked at it and agreed it wasn't fixed. So they called Aqualung repair shop and had me talk to them. They said they didn't open up the valve, they just hooked up the inflator and it was working as designed and weren't interested in doing anything else.  So I took it home and used it as was throughout the summer. October 5th I was diving at lake Harvey. I was ready to surface, but my inflator didn't work. So I kicked to the surface and manually inflated my BCD. I was very winded by the time I was done. The bcd held air for about 3 seconds and then dumped me back under water. By this point I was very winded. I attempted to manually inflate my bcd again, but it wasn't holding air.  I attempted to go back to my regulator, but I was so winded I couldn't breath through it and spit it out. I was able to signal to my fellow divers who I saw 40' away on the shore.  They were able to get to me and get me to the shore. Upon inspection of my bcd we found that the inflator hose became disconected, Hence the inflator not working.  But also the inflator was stuck in the deflate position. Which is the reason the bcd wouldn't hold air. I have e-mailed Aqualung, but haven't heard back from them.
justification: The incident involved equipment failure leading to a dangerous situation, but no injury occurred as fellow divers assisted.

Our Coverstar Eclipse automated pool cover, installed in early 2018 on our outdoor in-ground pool, began to close on its own while my children were in the pool (it had been open for about half an hour prior to this). I was able to get the children out, and stop the cover. 

The pool cover operates using a touchpad, on which users have to enter a numeric access code in order to open or close it. We'd had a problem some months prior to this incident with certain keys occasionally sticking in the "on" position, such that we were unable to enter our access code. The dealer who installed it was unable to reproduce the problem, and so we simply added a new access code, which was the same digit repeated four times. 

After this incident, when I reached the touchpad, I observed it to be "stuck" again (beeping, and with asterisks appearing in the display as if someone was pressing a key or keys). The cover stopped closing as soon as I began to press keys. 

There exists a wifi-enabled version of this touchpad, but to my knowledge, the version we had was not wifi-enabled.

The entire incident was captured by our security cameras, and I have the recording available.

We contacted the manufacturer immediately following the incident and provided them with the video. They sent the installer out to retrieve the old touchpad and replace it with a new one, and later told us that they observed some moisture infiltration and corrosion in the old unit.

I recently spoke with [REDACTED], the Executive Director of [REDACTED], and he agreed that this was a very serious incident that should be reported.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning pool cover that started closing on its own while children were in the pool, but no injuries occurred as they were safely removed.

incident_description:
This spring I purchase a used high performance road bike from a private party seller. The bicycle was equipped with Zipp 101 wheel set which was purchased by the original owner (not an OEM option for the bicycle). The bicycle was in very good condition upon purchase. 

I rode the bike for over 1000 miles to train and then participated in the 2019 Ride the Rockies organized ride. This is a 6-day, 434 mile event, which includes high-speed downhill sections.

Upon my return I cleaned the bike and hung it on my garage wall where it stayed, unused, for a period of 2-3 wks. In the garage one night I heard a bang and a tinkling sound like metal hitting the floor. I investigated but couldn't see anything out of the ordinary. Dismissing this I went about my business. A few days later I was working on another bicycle near where my road bike is hung and noticed a bright, split, aluminum ring on the garage floor. Not to far from it I found another chunk of aluminum with a fracture face. Realizing it had to have dropped from my bike hanging directly above, I inspected it to find three loose spokes and the fractured hub (Zipp 88) on my Zipp 101 front wheel. I have images of the parts and wheel if it would help. 

I, thankfully, was not riding. Pretty scary to think though what my state would be if that happened on the backside of Monarch Pass in Colorado at 50 mph. There is no way that wheel would have stayed together with three spokes from the same side coming off. It would have collapsed instantly. I would either still be in the hospital or my children would be fatherless.
justification: The incident involved a wheel failure that could have caused severe injury or death if it occurred during a ride, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
My wife and I were riding on a smooth trail in our 2015 Kawasaki Teryx4 LE side by side.  While riding the steering assembly failed.  I was making a left hand curve and turned the steering wheel and it popped and would not turn the wheels.  The front wheels locked in a straight forward position and we struck a small tree.  I was able to back up but the wheels would not turn, even manually to try and negotiate the curve.  I had to use our winch to pull the side by side off the trail to allow others by.  A mechanic friend was contacted that was in the area, he came to our location. The top portion of the rack and pinion steering was popped up and out of place.  We were unable to reset the piece and had to pull the piece out the rest of the way so that the tires could be manually turned to get the side by side out to where a trailer could be driven to load it up.  Luckily we were not traveling very fast at all or this could of caused severe injury or death had we been going at any speed and unable to turn the wheels at all.

This seems to be a very big problem for the Teryx4 as I have seen it discussed in numerous forums that I follow and when I tried to research a fix for it.
justification: The incident involved a steering failure leading to a collision with a tree, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
The vehicle is a 2015 Kawasaki Mule Pro off highway vehicle.  I have experienced two fuel pump failures.  When the failures occur, the vehicle engine either dies or will not start.  When the first failure occurred, the dealer replaced the fuel pump under warranty and no attempt was made to determine the cause of the failure.

When the second failure occurred approximately two years later, I removed the fuel pump and determined that the failure was caused by a law voltage (12 volt) plug located inside the fuel tank.  This plug is completely surrounded by vaporized gasoline.  When it failed, the connection got hot enough to char the plastic surrounding the connection.   An electrical failure of  this nature could cause and electrical spark.  Since the plug that failed is located inside the fuel tank and is surrounded by gasoline vapors, the fuel pump failure creates a risk of fire and explosion.

I took the failed fuel pump to my Kawasaki dealer.  He had two other failed fuel pumps from the same model vehicle in his repair shop.  Both of these failed pumps showed over heating of the electrical plug that had failed on my vehicle.

This appears to me to be a design defect that could cause the explosion of the gasoline tank which holds over five gallons so gasoline.  This tank is located immediately under the passenger seat.  An explosion of this tank would cause serious injury or death.
justification: The incident involves a design defect that could lead to a fire or explosion, posing a risk of serious injury or death.

incident_description:
I purchased a Fitbit Versa in May, 2019. Within a week, I began to notice a rash on the inside (pinky side) of my wrist below the band. 

Although Versas can be used while swimming, I remove to shower. I follow the care instructions for the band. I put a bandage over the rash area and it cleared up within a few days. When I removed the bandage, the rash returned within a day. I switched arms and the rash appeared in the same location. several days I have removed and discovered a brown film on the inside of the band, and realized it is my SKIN that has blistered and transferred to the watch band,

I now have a scar below the wristband due to multiple rash/blister/healing incidents.

I found a forum detailing the recall for the same reason in 2014, and my symptoms match those.  Others had found the site recently with the same issue with subsequent models.

The Fitbit website advises removing and thoroughly cleaning after any" strenuous activity" and to allow it to dry thoroughly. (so much for being wearable to track your activity)

To remove it at night to allow your wrist to breathe (so much for tracking your sleep activity)
To go a few days without wearing it (so much for having a Fitbit).

I have owned a much cheaper tracker which did not need to be charged, and wore it constantly for 1 year with no skin irritation. I owned a [REDACTED] watch with a cheap band for literally years only removing periodically and had no irritation.

I have reported this to Fitbit, but so far have only been advised of the same care instructions listed on the website.

incident_description:
Honda Pioneer 700-4  (2015 model)

I had just finished watching fireworks from afar as I sat on a long and undeveloped road when I went to a turnaround area and noticed a flame coming from beneath the seat of the UTV. I had been sitting idle for some timeprior. I owned the UTV.  I shut the engine off and tried to exit the vehicle with great difficulty and finally  l leaped from the vehicle onto the ground injurying my shoulder. I grabbed some dirt to throw down in the engine area to try and put out the fire numerous times but the fire would not go out.  I removed a chainsaw from the back to try and save it. (The fire was not related to the fireworks in anyway as I was more than a half mile from any firework displays.)

In a panic I then went to restart the engine and then the fire became larger when the fuel pump started to run.  I shut it off and tried more dirt.  I tried it a second time and again more flames.  I then proceeded to walk as quick as possible (i cant run well due to type 2 diabetes) to my camp which about 3/4 of a mile away by road. I yelled for my spouse across the cavern while walking to hopefully have her come get me.  She met me at the driveway of our property and I immediately went and got our three fire extinguishers and 6 gallons of water in a container. I had her call 9-1-1.

When we got to the Honda, it was engulfed.  I expended all my fire extinguishers and the water. It had little effect.  My wife then went in our car to the main gate to let the fireman into the community as it is gated.  By the time they got there the fire had dwindled some and they put water on it to put it out.  The unit burned completely down to just its metal pipe frame. My chain saw also melted even though it was  about 10 feet from the fire.

The fireman mentioned a recall on those units to which I never got a notice from the dealer or otherwise.  I need to dig into my files to get the purchase info, VIN etc., but its a total loss and was not insured.  I am fortunate to have escaped serious injury. My shoulder is currently in pain due to bailing out of the unit onto the ground.  I am considering legal recourse, but not for certain at this time.
justification: The incident resulted in a shoulder injury from escaping the vehicle, and the UTV was completely destroyed by fire.

incident_description: My wife, son, & I were visiting brother-in-law's home.  He has a very nice in-ground pool in his backyard. My wife had just purchased an INTEX "Inflatabull" pool toy from TJMaxx for $39.99, so that brother-in-law's son, and our son (they are ages 11 & 12), could use it for additional pool fun. The "Inflatabull" is a 7ft 10in by 6ft 5in by 2ft 8in (2.39m x 1.96m x 81cm) inflatable floatation toy that allows one to simulate "riding a bull."  The large product depiction on the box shows a teenage boy sitting upright while "riding the bull," while a smaller product depiction shows a teenage girl also sitting upright on the bull, with one hand on the built-in handhold and her other hand up in the air, with three other teenagers surrounding the device with their hands placed on the circular tube.  Brother-in-law was with the kids as they were attempting to get onto the toy.  However, they could not even mount it to simply sit on it, as it was very unstable.  I come over to assist.  We tried letting out some air, thinking that it may make it more stable.  That didn't seem to help.  I decided to try it myself.  We were in the shallow end of the pool, which turned out to be a really bad decision.  I was sitting on the bull for maybe all of 30 seconds as brother-in-law was beginning to gently push the bull towards the deeper end, when I promptly tipped over.  I hit my head on the pool steps, and began to bleed.  Six sutures later, and less than 24-hours from the incident, I'm here on SaferProducts.gov to report my experience.
justification: The incident resulted in a head injury requiring six sutures, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as such incidents can happen with unstable pool toys.

As you can imagine, this was traumatic and horrifying for my young son as well as for meÃÂon the verge of tears, I carried him to the car as he could not walk without severe pain, held him the entire way to the hospital where he shook and sobbed into my arms, then I had to hold him forcefully at the emergency room as the doctor continued the attempts to try and cut his swimsuit mesh, and only after receiving the anesthetic were we able to remove his penis from the mesh.
