incident_description: Sustained periodic electrical burns on wrist and forearm from Fitbit versa.  Back of Fitbit versa watch has 4 gold contacts on the back of the watch.  These 4 gold contacts (small circles) align with 4 pins on the charging cable that the fitbit versa is cradled in when it is in the charging dock charging.  Over the course of several months, I had what would start out as a small red blister and then would get larger, swollen, etc.  Blisters would sometimes be warm to the touch and would burn and sting.  Whole forearm became so swollen at one point my styloid process on my right ulna (which is normally visible- I have small wrists) could not be seen.  Never used product in water. Would always take it off to shower.  Would take it off and put it back on throughout the day, probably worn for 80% of a 24 hour period.  Would wear it while exercising.  While exercising I would notice a pulsating sensation deep in my forearm that felt like it would "travel" up forearm to bicep area and spread around wrist.  I can't help but wonder if the combination 4 gold contacts on the back of the fitbit watch along with the voltage of this larger fitbit and my body sweat was enough to conduct small waves of electricity and leave small burns on skin.  Blisters would not heal and became difficult to move wrist for day to day activities.  Removed watch from forearm for 72 straight hours (5/26/19-5/29/19) and started to feel relief from symptoms.  Smaller blisters started to heal and larger blilsters did not get worse and swelling of forearm started to decrease.  Returned watch to third party distributor I purchased it from on 5/29/19.  Employee asked for the reason for my return.  I explained the blisters on my forearm and showed the employee my still healing arm.  The employee wrote down the report in the system, asked to take a picture of my arm to show her supervisor and stated she would send a report to Fitbit about the product's safety.
justification: The description details repeated electrical burns and swelling, indicating injury (severity 3), but the issue appears isolated to the individual's use case (likelihood 2).

incident_description:
I was riding a 2015 Polaris Sportsman 1000 XP on groomed public trails in Wisconsin.  Over some uneven/rough terrain, the entire front grill, voltage regulator, and fuse box completely fell off of the four wheeler.

This was due to poor quality cast aluminum parts that have fatigued to the point of shattering.  I have pictures.  No collision was involved.

Upon further machine inspection, stress cracks at A Arm mounting points were discovered due to inconsistent welds from the factory on the frame.  This requires professional improvements which I will need to pay out of pocket for.  I don't mind doing that because I want to keep my four wheeler safe.  But others may not know as much and a suspension failure at the wrong time could lead to major injuries or death.
justification: The incident involved equipment failure without injury, but potential for future injuries exists due to undetected stress cracks.

incident_description:
I  have a 2018 Polaris Razor S900 with very low hours.   91.5 hours to be exact.   I started the unit one evening  and drove from my shop to my home for dinner.. The   total distance  is approximately 400ft. I  pulled in garage like normal... I always take the key out..The key was  in my pocket.   I ate dinner (roughly 45 minutes).. I  went back in the  garage to return to shop..   When I entered the garage I smelled a strange smell but brushed it off...  I sat in side by side, attempted to start it, nothing, no starter turning, no audible noise from fuel pump like normal  and no headlights either..  I assumed dead battery.  I removed drivers seat (battery location)  once I removed the seat, I was hit in the face with the  pungent  smell of wires, electronic heat damaged or plastic  burning.  It was the same smell as the one I  smelled upon entering the garage just way more intense..  Upon the  removal of  my seat I noticed immediately  the fuse box cover having a burn or bump in the plastic..  When I pulled the lid off, the fuse box was full of smoke and  literally on fire ... in the center of the box..    I immediately  looked for something  to extinguish the fire with  .,.  I found a [REDACTED] bottled water and poured it on the fuse box to extinguish the fire.    the damage had been done..   I looked it over trying to come to a conclusion to what happened.  In my opinion with the amount of damage the unit has.   It  simply had a circuit issue and caught on fire instead of blowing the fuses..    The fuses were all 10 amp red fuses.  , the fire obviously had started  before I reached the unit .. its simply too much damage to have just occurred.. ..  The fuse panel and wire harness  is ruined .  The utv will not run or operate due to the damage from the fire,     
 I  think someone needs to advise others of this potential for fire, serious injury or even death..   I  think owners should know, the key does not have to even be in the ignition for this to happen....  I can only imagine if this had of happened when  I come home to turn in for the evening..  It would have given me and my family enough time to get to bed and fall asleep.      I feel 100% this product has a major design  flaw and is at fault 100%.  I feel  it would have burned my home up  (my family inside  or not)  if I had not extinguished the fire when I did.   The fire wasn't smoldering,  it was just beginning.....  
 I would also like to state the utv has no modifications to the fuse box or wiring...  It does not have any sound system installed.   It is the way it came from the factory.    I would like to say I understand that any electrical product can fail or have internal issues and short, but it's the fuse box and circuit protection  devices responsibility to protect the unit from catching fire and causing major wiring damages.   My concern is the circuit protection device (fuse box, fuses and relays) itself does not  work and has major design flaws..,  It will not protect the circuits or actual unit from major damage or fire like it should have been engineered  to protect.  It  will catch on fire instead of open the circuit protection devices  that polaris designed them to protect...
justification: The incident involved a fire in the fuse box, which could have led to serious injury or death if not promptly addressed, though no actual injury occurred.

As I completed the exercise and was bringing the dumbell down to re-rack it, the largest weight plate (15lbs) fell off and landed on my foot.  The malfunction resulted in the break of my second metatarsal bone in my left foot.

In doing some research, it appears that the product was recalled in 2011 for this specific problem. I purchased the product in August of 2014 via Amazon. It is obvious the recall did not fix the inherent design flaw.

The product design is flawed as the weight plates are 'secured' to the dumbbell bar via a small plastic lip that relies on tension and gravity to keep it from falling off. If the manufacture used a modified design that actually hooked the plate to the bar, the plate would never have fallen off.

This product should be recalled IMMEDIATELY to prevent others from being injured. It should NOT be allow back on the market until the manufacturer changes the design of its securing mechanism to eliminate the possibility of plates falling off of the bar.
justification: The incident resulted in a broken bone, which is a serious injury, but not a death.

My son was using a brand new bat made by Easton in a baseball game (Easton Project 3 ADV model). It was the first time using this bat in a game and had only been used in two practices before this game. The bat is a two-piece bat, meaning it has a handle made of carbon fiber and a barrel made of metal. The connection between the barrel and the handle is covered by a red piece of plastic. 

My son swung the bat at a pitch that hit exactly on the red connecting piece of plastic. This plastic is an odd shape and has an angle that is not seen on other bats. The ball ricocheted off the plastic and into my sons eye, which was permanently damaged. 

The umpire, coach, players and my self with 30 years of experience have never seen a simple foul ball fly into the batter's face before. The fact this ball hit directly on the red attachment suggests strongly that the odd angle of this attachment is a contributor into this awful injury. 

Because of basic physics this bat design is suspect and I am dubious after this accident that this product has been tested for safety or if it was it was likely ignored by the bat company. 

I have the ball mark from the brand new game ball (my son was the second batter) directly on the red plastic connector I mentioned above and I have a video of the incident.

incident_description:
In June of 2017, we purchased over 200 bags (1.25 cu ft) of Groundsmart Playsafe Rubber Mulch for our kids' new play set.  To our surprise, their Playground "Playsafe" Rubber Mulch had embedded metal wire and even valve stems left in it from the shredded tires.  We found this out the hard way whenever we were cut by stepping or kneeling in the mulch.  We contacted Sam's Club and we were told that they would speak with their Groundsmart supplier.  We were placed in contact with Groundsmart and advised to fill out a claim form that was sent to us via email.  We were told to mail the claim form and the then latest piece of  "Playsafe" rubber mulch with the wire in it to them directly.  We showed the wire-embedded rubber mulch to our local Sam's Club manager and then mailed it in to Groundsmart as instructed.  We were told that it could take some time to track down the source of the issue and to be patient.  So we waited, and waited, and waited. 
Nothing at all!  In the interim, we kept our kids busy with summer activities away from the home and had them wear shoes when in the playground area as much as possible (rather defeats the purpose of spending thousands of dollars to create a fun and safe backyard space).  On September 2, 2018, my 6 year old daughter was outside swinging and her shoes came off.  She stepped onto the Groundsmart "Playsafe" mulch and another piece of metal wire embedded in their mulch sliced across two of her toes underneath.  She and her Autistic twin brother are now terrified of their playset area.  I reached out to Groundsmart again on January 15, 2019, and received an email stating that they would check with their office to see if they have a copy of my claim form and get back to me. I have received no further communications from them as of March 1, 2019.  
If a product carries the name "Playsafe" and purports to be a product safe for use at school playgrounds and kids' parks, I expect much more than this from them  When you read the fine print, it says 99.9% wire free, however my experience based on the amount of metal found thus far compared to the number of bags we purchased is more than that.  I am going to follow up with our Sam's Club again.  They have consistently said that they haven't heard anything, but I notice that they are selling the same bags of mulch again.  Since I did show them the piece that I sent to Groundsmart before mailing it off (and the manager was able to identify to me exactly what the metal was), it is my hope that Sam's Club is not complicit in this.  I truly want to believe that they value the safety of not just their members, but of all children, over the profits from selling dangerous bags of shredded tires under the name "Playsafe".
justification: The incident describes injuries caused by metal wire in the mulch, including a child's cut toes, but no death.

Caller stated that the company advertised that if you are not satisfied they will refund your money but they are not willing to do so.  She stated that the product is misrepresented but they say it is not.

incident_description:
On or about February 20, 2019, I was inflating a soccer ball.  It is labeled as being marketed by Franklin Sports Inc., Stoughton MA 02072.  It is a size 3 soccer ball labelled as F-100.  It bears the number 1160937245.  It also bears a smudged number that appears to be 5063-3.

The soccer ball indicates "inflate 4 - 6 LBS."  As I inflated a Franklin size 3 soccer ball, pressure increased towards 2 pounds per inch ("PSI").  At approximately 2 PSI and certainly before 3 PSI, the soccer ball exploded.  

As it exploded, my 9 year old son, who was seated nearby, was impacted by the explosion on his neck.  He experienced redness, pain, and swelling.  The pain and swelling have since subsided.  

This is the second time a Franklin soccer ball has exploded prior to reaching the recommended pressure.  It also occurred years ago.
justification: The incident caused injury (redness, pain, and swelling) to a child, and it has occurred before with the same product.

incident_description:
Lime green and white electric rental scooter. Riding and wheel locked without warning. I was thrown into a street and broke my arm in the fall. Many such reports convinced me to retain an attorney and file a lawsuit against Lime. 

Was my 23rd ride with Lime scooters so im no amateur. This thing malfunctioned period. lime recalled its entire fleet from Switzerland last month due to this same issue.
justification: The rider suffered a broken arm due to the scooter malfunction, indicating an injury (severity 3). The mention of many similar reports and a fleet recall suggests the issue is likely (likelihood 4).

incident_description:
Eastern Jungle Gym Easy 1-2-3 A-Frame Swing Set Brackets were purchased and combined with locally acquired lumber and an unknown tire swing. It was installed, unanchored and over bare earth, at a preschool.

Approximately two weeks after installation, three preschool-age children were playing on the swing when the whole frame fell over. Two children were uninjured, but the third suffered a head injury and died later that day.
justification: A child died from a head injury caused by the swing set collapsing, which constitutes the highest severity level. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such fatal incidents are not common despite improper installation.

incident_description:
I have a 2005 Zeagle Zena Women's BCD. I was coming up from my dive and upon surfacing, I attempted to inflate my BCD for flotation. The inflation hose all of a sudden blew out (separating from the BC).  I immediately began losing flotation and my BCD began filling with water causing me to sink. I immediately swam to my dive partner and hung onto him to keep from drowning, until I could get aboard the boat. 

Most dive related accidents/deaths occur on the surface!  
I was on the surface of the water, in 5ft swells. Had I not been an experienced diver, level headed and my dive buddy not been close by...I could've drowned! If the inflation hose had failed underwater- a more serious type of emergency situation would've occurred...I could've drowned! 

My BCD was serviced and check out in July 2018, by a local dive shop. It only has 50 lifetime dives on it... and only 4 dives after the service, and prior to this incident.  Upon getting to safety and inspecting the BCD, the welded seams that connects the BCD bladder and inflation hose, seem to have separated, leading to the malfunction.  Zeagle has had the same inflator issues in two of their newer [REDACTED and [REDACTED BCD line. I could find nothing about this year model and at the time I bought it the warranties weren't required to be registered online. This is a serious issue!
justification: The incident involved a serious equipment failure that could have led to drowning, but no actual injury or death occurred due to the diver's experience and proximity of the dive buddy.

incident_description:
I purchased a set of brand new Quadboss V-bar snow chains for my ATV (all-Terrain Vehicle)/Side-by-Side(SXS) tires. Part number: 563555. These tire chains were purchased through Amazon.com via a 3rd party vendor.
In receiving the product the chains came in a black plastic storage box, and looked to be brand new. The label on the outside of the box included a picture of the chains mounted to an ATV tire, and showed a yellow assembly in the middle of the chain set on the tire, also known as a tensioner. The tensioner serves the purpose to keep the chain tight to the tire so that it doesn't come off and cause property damage or bodily injury to the operator or bystanders as spinning tires could throw the chain a great distance, or have it flail around like a whip causing grievous injury. 
No mounting/assembly instructions were included in the box with these tire chains, nor was the pictured tensioner on the label of the box included in the box. I found it very odd that a dangerous product as these would not have instructions on how to safely attach them to a tire.
A typo/mis-spelling on the label of the box is what originally caused me to reach out to the manufacturer, as my SXS tire size was not shown. I reached out to the manufacturer Quadboss on the evening of 12/5/2018 via email. At 11:54 AM on 12/6/2018 I received an email from [REDACTED], with Quadboss Technical Support. Below is the content of my email exchange with [REDACTED].
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
From: [REDACTED]
Date: Wed, Dec 5, 2018 at 6:22 PM
Subject: Question on Vbar chain set
To: <QuadBoss@quadboss.com>

Will you (sic) chain set #563555 fit on tire size 25-10-12? 

Your website doesn't list a chain option for that tire size.

From: [REDACTED]
Date: Thu, Dec 6, 2018 at 11:54 AM
Subject: FW: Question on Vbar chain set
To: [REDACTED]

Thank you for contacting QuadBoss Products.
 
Yes, P/N 563555 would be the best option for your tire size.
 
Thank you,

From: [REDACTED]
Date: Thu, Dec 6, 2018 at 2:22 PM
Subject: Re: FW: Question on Vbar chain set
To: [REDACTED]

[REDACTED],

Thank you for the reply and fitment advice.

When I received the box with the 563555 in the mail yesterday there was no tensioner or instructions in the box. Can you advise what should be in the box leaving the factory?

From: [REDACTED]
Date: Thu, Dec 6, 2018 at 2:25 PM
Subject: RE: FW: Question on Vbar chain set
To: [REDACTED]

[REDACTED],
 
In the box is tire chains only x2 pcs.
 
Tensioners are sold separately (P/N 563558).
 
Thanks,

From: [REDACTED]
Date: Thu, Dec 6, 2018 at 2:33 PM
Subject: Re: FW: Question on Vbar chain set
To: [REDACTED]


So you don't even include mounting/installation instructions?


I did not hear back from [REDACTED] in a timely manner about their lack of installation instructions, and I then went to their website to look for the product listing. On the product listing, the tire chain is shown installed on an ATV tire with no tensioner on the chain set, and no reminder or warning near the photo to the potential purchaser is provided to inform them that tensioners are required for safe operation with these chains, and that they have to be purchased separately. Furthermore, there are no links or product literature available on how to safely mount this chain set to an ATV tire. I have saved screenshots of these product pages, and can provide them upon request.

I find this to be negligence to sell such a dangerous product with complete lack of assembly/installation instructions, and to sell such a product without the minimum required accessories like a chain tensioner is proof of further negligence. Especially on ATV/SXS products that are frequently operated by adolescents under the age of 18 who may not understand fully the dangers of a tire chain and how to properly secure it.

I request the Consumer Safety Product Commission take action against this company Quadboss to ensure that no consumer or bystander be injured by this product. The product should at a minimum have mounting/installation instructions on the manufacturerÃÂs recommended method to install the chain set to ensure safe operation.
justification: The product lacks necessary safety instructions and accessories, posing a potential risk of injury if improperly used, but no actual incident or injury has been reported yet.

incident_description:
I have been riding Ninebot One E+ to work everyday on it, also as a main mode of transportation, for the past 3.5 years in the San Francisco Bay Area, and even take it to nearby beaches such as Half Moon Bay, Monterey or Big Sur when it's sunny here in Northern California. Within a few minutes after the device started making a few popping noise when the power was off, it suddenly exploded and burnt in a vicious fire. I was extremely lucky and no one was hurt. This could have been much, much worse. I could have lost my right leg, I could have died or the entire apartment could have burnt down causing even more casualties.

.This is when I realized the sound--and potentially the smell too--was coming from my beloved 3 year long friend. My instinct now as sharp as blade, I knew I needed to do so something.

~11:45AM - I started hearing popping noise. Initially believed to be coming from outside, only to discover nothing outside the front door.
~11:50AM - Noticed repetitiveness in the noise, occurring every 30 seconds to a minute.
~11:55AM - Started smelling something acrid. Starting to be concerned.
~12:00PM - Found the source of the sound (and potentially the smell)
12:01PM - (film shot, of the device making noise)
~12:02PM - Being super safe, I went to the power strip and turned it off
~12:02PM - Then unplugged the cord from the power strip,
~12:03PM - Then unplugged the cord from the unit.
~12:03PM - I raised the handle bar and tried to grab it from the end of the handle bar as usual, but I didn't. Instead, I grabbed the center of the handle and supported with my left hand under the foot pedal so I don't accidentally agitate the unit too much and trigger it to explode. (VERY RISKY)
~12:03PM - I took it outside and leaned it against the immediate exterior wall I was able to get access to.
~12:09PM - I heard a loud explosion with a small fire when I turned. Immediately, one or two more louder and bigger explosions occurred and followed by much bigger fire, creating fizzing sound and burning everything the battery was wrapped in violently. This lasted for a minute.
12:10PM - When the fire was weakening, the property manager luckily was outside and who saw this happening ran towards me to aid and grabbed the fire extinguisher. I knew I had to document this. (photo available)
justification: The incident involved a dangerous explosion and fire, but no injuries occurred due to quick actions.

incident_description:
Whilst skiing in Aspen I sustained a compression fracture of the tibial plateau as a result of a toe pin breaking on a pair of Marker King Pin Bindings.  This caused me to fall resulting in the injury sustained.  This injury has required surgery and will have a 6 month recovery period.

These bindings are subject to a product recall but I had not been notified by either Marker or their dealer of the recall.  The recall is posted on the Marker website.

The Marker website still states, as of 5 March 2019, that no injuries have been sustained as a result of this product fault.  I informed Marker in the USA and several other locations of my injury on 12th January 2019.  No correction has been posted or any other remedial action proposed by Marker.
justification: The incident resulted in a compression fracture requiring surgery and a 6-month recovery period, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description:
On Saturday, February 16th., 2019 at approximately 1557 hours, my wife, two friends and I were inside a 2018 Polaris RZR XP 4 Turbo (RZR).  Within 5 minutes into the ride my wife, who was the front passenger, smelled fuel and then saw flames to her right.  My wife shouted, ÃÂWe are on Fire!ÃÂ I looked back and saw flames around my two friends in the back seat.  I slammed on the brakes and shouted for everyone to get out.  My wife and the rear passenger seated behind me were able to get out first.  I was delayed with the 4-point harness I had on, but all other positions were 3-point (automotive style) belts.  The right rear passenger shouted, ÃÂI canÃÂt get my seat belt off.ÃÂ  As I moved towards her,  I saw flames were all around her, she was able to release the belt and flee to safety.  Within 10 seconds of her freeing herself, the rear seat erupted in flames.  I then moved towards the rear of the RZR.  It was clear the fire was coming from directly to the rear of the back seats.  I looked under the RZR and could see active and intense fire coming from what appeared to be from the front, top area of the engine (closest to the rear seats).  I made a futile attempt to extinguish the fire with sand/dirt.  My actions had no effect on the fire and it quickly engulfed the entire RZR in flames. 

As black smoke filled the sky, people came to our aid.  One man asked what was the machine? Once I told him it was a RZR, he said, "they catch fire all the time...Polaris will give you a new one.ÃÂ

Once the fire crew arrived, I was told about a recent RZR fire in northern [REDACTED] with a fatality involved. 

My wife called a friend for a ride out of the desert.  This friend is also a RZR owner.  My wife told the friend what had occurred, the friend said (something that was shocking), ÃÂOh, they do that.ÃÂ  I could not believe this.  Numerous people told us Polaris had issues with their products catching fire, in addition to several years of recalls pertaining to fire-related problems.

During my initial research of the RZR, I never found anything about RZRÃÂs catching fire.  Once I put ÃÂPolarisÃÂ + ÃÂFireÃÂ into the internet search, I was shocked at the pages and videos I found. I searched other manufacturers and found little to nothing relating to fires, compared to POLARIS!

It seems to me, POLARIS has not done enough to improve their safety from the lawsuit in the 2013-2016 machines.  The problem continues and I canÃÂt believe this company is still allowed to sell them.  Not only are they allowed to sell them, but they are putting profit over human life! Thank God we didn't die.

I had a number of friends tell me to call POLARIS and have them drop a new RZR in my garage.  It appears this is how this company handles its dangerous products instead of FIXING THE PROBLEM. I donÃÂt want a new RZR, I WANT this company to STOP making a death trap.  I came within seconds of seeing my friends get seriously injured or burned to death. ItÃÂs clear the recalls and/or design of the machines have not fixed the issue with them catching fire.
justification: The incident involved a fire that could have resulted in serious injury or death, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
XTERRA TREADMILL 6.6 is an treadmill offered for sale on https://www.xterrafitness.com/.


The incident occurred on 12/30/2018,  I was using the product when the belt slipped, after which I quickly grabbed the handles but unfortunately twisted my right heel. I am an fit and healthy 27 year old male but I feel this treadmill is unsafe compared to other treadmills I used.

incident_description:
This 77 year old consumer is reporting that he purchased a 2016 ATV from a sports bike dealer retailer in Michigan around the middle of August 2018.
He had no problems with the ATV until  October 23rd, 2018 when he was riding near a cabin they were sharing and he began to smell a burning odor.
He pulled to the side of the road and dismounted only to find that the bike had caught fire. Leaves behind seat between seat and engine.
He was able to extinguish the fire, he was not injured and he was able to restart the ATV to get it back to the cabin, loaded onto his trailer and drive it to a repair location.
He said that the repair shop is cooperating with him.
He has not spoken with the manufacturer but he does intend to speak with them.
Spoke said not their fault.

incident_description: 2018- 2019 Arctic Cat ctec2 8000 snowmobiles develop a condition that causes flames to come out of the exhaust and catch the snowmobile on fire under certain conditions. Arctic Cat is aware of the problem and continue to sell their products. We purchased our 2018 zr 8000 limited in november. My son had it in northern [REDACTED] last weekend and the belly pan caught on fire 3 times over the weekend. He notified me about what happened and i called the dealer. The service manager wasn't in, so i started doing research and this is a problem that was identified last year. Still no resolution to the problem. So i called the customer care line at Arctic Cat and talked to a customer service representative and his response was "what would you like us to do" I told him that selling a product that catches on fire while riding should have never been sold to the consumer. The sale of these vehicles should have been stopped until a valid repair had been performed. I feel we and all of the people that bought these machines are at risk of injury if the sale of these vehicles continues. I'm trying to get someone involved that may be able to speed up a valid repair. I feel Arctic Cat has failed to resolve this in a timely manner and they aren't taking this problem seriously. Thank you. Also theres a lot of information online about the others having this same problem you can find it under ctec 2 exhaust fire/ arctic cat 8000 fire etc.
justification: The incident involves snowmobiles catching fire, which is a known issue, but no injuries or deaths are reported in the description.

Just wanted to let other people know not to let their kids ride this machine. There needs to be a recall and to place a heat shield so no more fires occur. ty.

The sidewalk took a sharp turn and the scooter was unable to stop to slow down to take the corner. As a result, she was thrown off the scooter and was knocked unconscious for over 10 minutes. justification: The incident resulted in injury (torn meniscus) and the problem recurred multiple times, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description: This Report is in follow up to that of Report # [REDACTED] from 6/16/2017 and Report # [REDACTED] from 9/14/2017 concerning the merchant in question, Pacific Cycle. In response to these complaints, I was contacted by Pacific Cycle in an effort to resolve the defective and used merchandise that had been shipped to me by Wal-Mart on behalf of Pacific Cycle, only to discover -- upon ceasing my patronage of Pacific Cycle after these efforts failed -- that Pacific Cycle is only able to remain operational by foisting used, defective and/or poorly configured merchandise onto consumers through the country's largest retailers, Wal-Mart, Target & Amazon. Specifically, it turns out that the Mongoose XR Pro bicycle I had purchased on 9/7/2017 from Walmart.com to replace a Mongoose Ledge 3.5 bicycle I had similarly purchased on 5/8/2016 from Walmart.com (that was 5 years old at the time of purchase, as Pacific Cycle itself informed me a little over a year later on 6/2/2017, when the left pedal came off and could not be put back on) was poorly configured to the point where my only viable option at the time was to return it for a refund. When I took the replacement bike (which Pacific Cycle did give me a full refund for) to the only repair shop in town at the time, Bike Tech Macon (www.biketechmacon.com), the day after receiving it, the repair technician on duty was unable to either realign the gears for the bike or correct the damage caused to the bike chain by the misaligned gears that occurred en route to the repair shop. I aligned the gears and straightened out the bike chain as best I could when I returned home (Pacific Cycle offered to pay to have the chain replaced by Bike Tech Macon at the time, which seemed unfeasible to me at the time, given the incompetence shown by Bike Tech Macon, the distance to the store of over four miles and that fact that the bike itself was the only way that I could reach the repair shop -- unless Pacific Cycle were willing to compensate me for transporting the bike by some other means, which Pacific Cycle did not offer to do), only to have the chain come off the bike and break while riding down a steep decline on the way to the local Wal-Mart early in the afternoon of 1/28/2019. Gratefully, the road was strictly a residential one and completely deserted at the time, or my crash could very easily have been a fatal one, although i experienced a serious health setback related to a cardiovascular stent implantation procedure I had undergone on the night of 8/20/2018 (I would have called an ambulance after my crash, if not for the bike).
justification: The incident resulted in a crash due to a broken bike chain, causing a serious health setback related to a prior cardiovascular procedure, indicating an injury.

After riding the scooter for a few minutes, one of the scooter that I rented was not working properly due to malfunction of the brakes. incident_description:
I experienced a premature heel release from both of my new Look SPX 12 bindings on the first ski run with the new bindings. The double premature heel release caused me to fall forward and I dislocated my shoulder and broke my arm.. The fall was witnessed and reported to the [REDACTED] Ski Patrol. justification: The incident resulted in a dislocated shoulder and a broken arm, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is high (4) due to the reported binding recall and the professional skier's confirmation of a malfunction.

incident_description:
The purpose of my letter is to bring to your attention a life-threatening issue involving the 2008
Honda 250TRX EX Quad (four-wheeled), off-road all-terrain vehicle (ATV). I am currently serving as 
an expert witness for[REDACTED] in her design  defect  law  suit  against Honda, the result of a tragic accident on February 29, 2016, that was easily preventable.
[REDACTED],  a  twenty-four  year  old  female  and  her  boyfriend,  [REDACTED],  had  
recently discovered that she was pregnant with his baby and planned a weekend away to discuss future 
plans for marriage and their new life together. Upon arrival in Julian, California they decided to 
purchase Groupon tickets for a day of riding all terrain off-road vehicles. The salesperson at San 
Diego Motorsports suggested that [REDACTED] rent the 250TRX EX which is equipped with a sport clutch, 
which is essentially an automatic clutch, although it still requires left foot shiftting of the 
gear by lifting your left toe, pivoting at the arch for higher gears and stepping down on the foot 
activated shift lever for lower gears.
On their rented ATV's the two rode out into the desert from San Diego Motorsports, enjoying their
day, when the right rear wheel of her vehicle went down into a divot, or small hole in the 
dirt, her right foot bounced off the foot peg and was immediately sucked into, and under, the right 
rear tire and wheel of the ATV. Given the speed she was travelling, 5 to 10 miles per hour, it is 
estimated that it took 1/10th of a second to pull her foot into the right rear tire. Her right shoe 
was literally torn off her foot, thrown 30 feet from the ATV, she was catapulted over the handle 
bars, her head hit an embankment and she landed on her back, forever paralyzed from the neck down.

Today, [REDACTED] is twenty-six years old, living with her mother and her two year old son. She never 
realized her dream of being married and having a family and living a "normal" life. The Honda 
250TRX EX was the cause of this accident because it was not designed to incorporate a "foot guard" 
to protect the foot environment and keep either foot from being sucked into the tire, in case of an 
inadvertent maneuver, causing the foot to come off the foot peg.

[REDACTED], a well-known motorcycle designer, and myself, have designed and built a prototype 
foot guard and floorboard that is safe, attractive and low cost. We would like to see the Consumer 
Product Safety Commission amend the American National Standards Institute (ANSI) and Specialty 
Vehicle Institute of America (SVIA) standards to insist on the incorporation of foot guards on all 
offÃÂ­ road vehicles to help save people from these tragic accidents that are easily preventable.

[REDACTED], Ph.D.
Automotive Expert Witness
and Forensic Examiner
justification: The incident resulted in severe injury (paralysis from the neck down), which falls under severity level 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated 4 (likely) based on the frequency of similar incidents (1968 out of 3915).

incident_description:
I purchased an Arctic Cat Wildcat Trail ATV on July 10.2018. It was delivered on July 14,2018. On July 26, 2018, it caught fire and burned down my 40'x42'all metal and concrete building causing catastrophic property loss.


This machine had been on recall for starting fires. https://www.arcticchat.com/.../wildcat/457010-exhaust-heat-shields-melt-down.html The "fix" did not work! Heat Shields made out of aluminum melted causing fires. https://www.google.com/search?biw=1044&bih=1025&tbm=isch&sa=1&ei=pW8JXOa3CPCN5wKr65nQCg&q=wildcat+sport+heat+shield+recall&oq=wildcat+sport+heat+shield+recall&gs_l=img.3...0.0..407658...0.0..0.0.0.......0......gws-wiz-img.HP7T-O4dkZ4#imgdii=SKdTQ2zqWH4ucM:&imgrc=vJIDrqeQEOAJTM:

Textron, parent company of Arctic Cat, knows about this problem. I find it very strange that Textron modified the recall on September 11, 2018 to the Canadiens but not to the USA after my fire.

There are certain facts to substantiate my claim. There were 444 of these machines that the plastic panels were melted on which initiated the recall. There were 6 fires at that time that totally destroyed the Arctic Cat Wildcat Trail ATV ,,, models 2014-2017. There has been loss of property associated with this machine already ,,, before my fire. The business, B&F INC where I purchased the machine has installed a fire guard on 2013 Models which were not on the recall. That indicates this goes back to the beginning of manufacture. I have now made a complaint to the Consumer Safety Affairs https://applications.sc.gov/DCAComplaintSystem/Login/ConsumerLogin.aspx to alert them to this issue of safety for the owners of those machines.

Recall Details
Transport Canada Recall 2017510
On certain side-by-side UTVs, the splash panels located behind the driver and passenger seats could melt, potentially resulting in a fire. This could increase the risk of injury and/or damage to property. Correction: Dealers will replace the plastic splash panels behind both the operator and passenger seat with revised ones with added heat reflective material, as well as replace the current aluminium exhaust head pipe shield with a new stainless steel head pipe shield equipped with a better insulator material. Additionally, dealers will ensure the spark plug caps are properly and fully inserted into the engine. Note: In the interim, owners are advised to stop riding their UTV until the defect has been repaired.

Textron has refused to make settlement in my property loss case. I have scoured the Internet and found out that these machines are still a threat to people as well as property. I can provide pictures of the incidents along with testimonials from owners if needed.

I have plenty pictures and files of both the issues that still exist with the product and to support my claim. I tried up loading some of these pictures and files but your form would not accept them. If you e-mail me at crawdaddy2008@live.com, I will be able to send them to you.
justification: The incident involved a fire causing catastrophic property loss but no reported injuries or deaths.

I had to stop hunting immediately , control the bleeding and go to an emergency room.

incident_description: I have owned three Fitbit devices (the Charge HR, Blaze, and now Versa). I have experienced severe skin reactions to the standard band included with these devices. For the Charge HR, there was nothing I could do because alternative bands were not an option. For the Blaze and Versa, using alternative bands of different materials (not made by Fitbit) has resolved the problem. My complaint is that after reporting this to Fitbit, their only response was to offer a return/refund of the device. I made it very clear that my issue is not with the device but with the band and had requested an alternate material band (because they do make them). I even sent them a picture of my arm after wearing the Versa with the provided band for a few days. The rash I had was akin to a chemical burn which after a few days of care actually started to peel like a sunburn would. My most severe reaction was to the Blaze for which I have a small scar on my inner forearm from one of the blisters which had developed from the reaction to its band. A quick search of [REDACTED] shows that this has been a wide and persistent problem for many years with the Fitbit devices yet Fitbit refuses to acknowledge it. In a recent correspondence with them, they told me that this is "rare" and tried to buy me off by offering to refund the entire product. That is not what I wanted or asked for and they are clearly trying to just sweep this under the rug. Something really needs to be done about this.
justification: The incident caused severe skin reactions akin to chemical burns, leading to injury and scarring.

incident_description: I was pumping up a tire on my bicycle with a Zefal Sport G air pump when the handle broke. I suffered a severe laceration to the back of my hand. Upon inspection of the broken part I realized the handle was not a solid piece. The handle was designed with cutouts on the top to have padded inserts. This caused a predictable weakness where it broke.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe laceration, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The design flaw suggests a possible but not certain recurrence (likelihood 3).

incident_description:
I rented a Lime scooter on the 16th September.  I was a first-time user and suffered a fall when I transitioned from the street to the apron of a garage driveway.  There was a 1 inch lip between the street and the driveway, which caused the scooter to buck.  I was thrown off the scooter and broke my fall with my right arm (I stiff-armed my fall while holding my palm out to absorb the impact).  The fall tore two ligaments/muscles in my right shoulder, which required surgery, which i had on the  16th of October.   

Scooters have extremely high centers of gravity and are inherently unstable.  they should be banned as a form of commercial transport.
justification: The incident resulted in a serious injury requiring surgery, which falls under severity level 3. The occurrence likelihood is set to 3 (possible) as such injuries are not uncommon with scooter accidents.

incident_description:
2011 Giant Anthem X 29er 2 - inclusion of additional serial numbers, including those beginning with GW, is required due to the manufacturer's correction being inadequate to reduce the risk of serious injury.  As indicated in CPSC Release [REDACTED] (see below), the frame has cracked at the junction of the seat post and top tube.

I contacted the manufacturer, however, I was told that the serial number on my frame indicated that it was among those manufactured after the issue was identified and a correction was made.  The representative told me that the weld at the junction of the seat post and top tube was made stronger.  However, this modification did not prevent the failure.


Name of Product: 2011 Model Year Anthem Giant Bicycles

Hazard: The frame can crack at the junction of the seat post and top tube, posing a fall hazard to riders.

Importer: Giant Bicycle Inc., of Newbury Park, Calif.

Remedy: Consumers should immediately stop riding the recalled bicycles and contact any authorized Giant Bicycle dealer for a free inspection and repair.
justification: The frame cracking poses a fall hazard, indicating potential for injury, but no actual injuries are reported in the description.

incident_description:
I purchased a FitBit Alte HR wristband in May 2018. As it states I have worn the wristband on my left wrist and not too tightly. The wristband is of a rubber type material which I routinely keep clean.  I do not have any history of allergies or am I allergic to anything. Approximately 2 months after wearing the FitBit a red blister looking spot appeared on the top of my wrist and was itchy occasionally. As the weeks have gone by the red blister looking  area has increased in size and remains red and hard. I have had no irritation from the strap itself and the rash area is directly between where the x2 lights flash on the electronic part of the Fitbit. I am concerned that my skin may be getting some form of chemical burn. Please advise if this product needs investigation? Should I receive a replacement which would not damage my skin?
Thanks

I did file a claim with the company after the incident on 6/15/18 and as of today, the company has neglected to follow up with even a simple phone call to help me pay the emergency room bill.   I have tried to contact them and sent multiple emails with no response for 5 months.   I don't believe that this company is responsible and capable to handling this issue with the dangerous product that they are providing.

incident_description: I rented a Bird electric scooter for the first time. I was riding it from campus to an off campus parking lot. I had never rented one before. It started to wobble but I did not think of anything of it. I continued to ride and when I went down a slight incline the bar that holds the handlebar detached from the scooter and I flipped over where the handlebar should be. I ended up going to the ER which it was concluded that I separated my shoulder. I have been in a sling since the incident and will still be in a sling for a few weeks.

incident_description:
Context:  I am  retired military, with many years of use on various fitness equipment.  My weight: 207 pounds
Equipment:  Consumer-grade treadmill (4.2 hp motor, 300 pound max user capacity).  27 hours/103 miles of use.  Purchased 29 August, 2018.

My Proform "Smart Pro 5000"  treadmill (Icon Health and Fitness product) exhibits roller runaway at 12-15 degree inclines, with my 207 pound frame.  Video of the  condition available upon request.  
This is different than belt slippage.  It occurs when the treadmill motor, belt and rollers are not sufficient to counteract the weight of the user.
This is an unacceptable condition that may lead to injuries.  Apparently, this is a very common complaint, according to Universal Technical Services (UTS).  UTS is Icon Health and Fitness'  warranty division (audio of call available upon request).

UTS can only recommend tightening the belt.  That is not an effective solution.  This can damage the belt/motor and/or cause the belt to shift off center.  

I am concerned that some of the most vulnerable consumers (individuals who are promised the opportunity to lose weight) could be seriously injured, if they're unaware of the danger.

My recommendations to Icon health and Fitness are either 

A.  Limit inclines to no more than 10-12 degrees.

B.  Lower the max capacity to approximately 170 pounds, 

C.  Create "Custom" treadmills based upon the weight of the users, built to handle the incline and weight of the user, over 170 pounds, by installing 5 continuous horsepower motors in their products.
justification: The incident describes a treadmill malfunction that could lead to injuries, though no injuries are reported yet. The issue is reportedly common, indicating a higher likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description:
The submitter said he was notified by the firm that his unit was affected by recall # 16-146 and he took the unit to the retailer to have the recall repair. 

The submitter said since the repair he has noticed a gas odor when using the unit. The submitter has found that the rollover vent valve is defective and believes this is the part causing the fires with these units.

The submitter said about two hours after using the unit he notices the gas odor and realized the rollover vent valve shuts, causing the gas tank to expand. The submitter said he has taken the unit three times to the retailer during the past year but since they could not replicate the incident they could not conduct a repair. 

The submitter said he finally decided to take a video of the incident and he made a hole in the gas tank cap which allows him to see the excessive air coming from the gas tank. The submitter said he sent the retailer the video sometime in September 2017 and the retailer forwarded the video to the firm. The submitter was contacted by the firm and asked to take his unit into the retailer but they refused to tell him how they would address the issue so the submitter said he did not feel comfortable taking the unit to the retailer.

The submitter said the incident occurs approximately two hours after using it and during temperatures higher than 70 degrees. He also indicated that he always notices the strong gas odor.

The submitter indicated his frustration with the unit because he has had issues since the recall repair and the firm who does not address the safety issue. The submitter said many of his other friends with similar units have had this issue and he believes the rollover vent valve needs to be addressed to prevent future incidents.
justification: The incident involves a gas odor and a defective rollover vent valve, posing a potential safety hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
On 9/8/2018, I was using my Gold's Gym Five in One Door Gym Trainer, which is a portable pull-up bar. While I was doing about seven pull-ups, the product abruptly broke, fell off the door frame, and caused me to fall at least several feet onto the ground. My feet hit the floor first, and I lost balance and fell backwards, landing on my back on the concrete floor of the garage. Thankfully, with the exception of a slight headache, which resulted from the metal bar hitting my head as I fell, I was uninjured. I did not seek first-aid nor medical attention, and the pain went away after an hour. However, I easily could have suffered serious leg/knee, back and head injuries. 

Upon examination of the broken product, I observed that both ends of the flat rectangular plastic "crossbar" that was placed on top of the door frame, in order to hold the entire pull-up bar in place, were broken. Each end was attached to the main bar's steel frame with a screw. With the ends broken, the plastic portion completely separated from the main bar, and caused the whole product to lose its grip on the door frame and fall.
justification: The incident resulted in a fall and a slight headache, but no serious injury or medical attention was required.

In any case I happened to bounce the ball on a carpeted floor one time, heard something unusual, and sure enough there was a screw on the floor.  It appears that the screw was not at all engaged with the plastic screw boss.

The heat staked code on the back of the display head (basketball net) is C57G101-H.

If it's desired to get that ball and screw back for analysis, I am happy to cooperate.  It's put away now.
justification: The incident involved a loose screw that could pose a hazard if ingested, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
These are PowerTap P1 pedals, a speciality item used by some cyclists to measure power output while riding.

I am a cyclist with 40 years of riding experience (approximate).

The incident was that I pulled my foot out of the right pedal riding on newish smooth asphalt up a slight hill in a sprint at 23mph.  The forces involved caused me to go over the handlebars and hit the pavement.  I had multiple fractures on 9 ribs and a broken collar bone.

The manufacturer could not "recreate" the circumstances under which the pedals released as they had with me and dismissed the incident.  They never responded when I sent them the attached images showing the lack of clearance between the claw holding the shoe on the pedal and the bottom of the shoe.

I was able to recreated the issue easily.  In colder months, cyclists where toe covers or booties over their shoes for warmth.  It has been this way ever since i first started riding.  These covers all have a hole on the bottom corresponding to the approximate size and shape of a "cleat" on the bottom of a cycling shoe.  The edge of this cutout generally has a sewn seam with elastic to maintain shape.  These seams are generally pretty thin, but mine measures nearly 2mm unstretched.  It is a very common design and brand.

The flaw in the PowerTap pedal is that unlike other brands ([REDACTED]) The gap between the top of the cleat on the pedal and the shoe when it is one the pedal properly is less than 1mm.  On my [REDACTED] pedals this gap is 4mm+.

The effect of this lack of clearance is that the elastic and fabric of the toe cover effectively prevented the cleat from fully and securely closing.  The band gets wedged between the top of the claw and the bottom of the shore.  Under normal levels of effort the foot feels secure and the problem is unnoticeable.  However; at high output levels, as in a sprint, the claw opens and releases the foot. At the time of my accident, my data recording device shows 670 watts where I typically average 150 for a ride.

I can recreate the pinching of the fabric between the shoe bottom and the PowerTap pedal at home.  I can also see other designs clearly accommodate the clearances for a toe cover or bootie (or mud?) between the shoe bottom and claw.
justification: The incident resulted in multiple fractures and a broken collar bone, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) as the issue can be recreated under specific conditions involving high output levels and common cycling gear.

incident_description:
I have a Pentair MasterTemp 400 pool heater that was installed approximately 4 1/2 years ago. In the past I used it infrequently since I had a solar heater for the pool. I primarily used the MasterTemp for the spa. I recently removed by thermal heater and replaced it with solar panels (Jan 2018). Since then I started using the MasterTemp more often for my pool. The pool developed some contamination. I went to the local pool supply company ([REDACTED]) to get some suggestions. They also installed the heater. I brought them a water sample and they detected a large amount of copper. When I asked about the source they mentioned the heater as a possibility. I reduced the copper content with some chemicals but I also inspected the heater. I noticed a  hole in the back panel approximately 6 inches in diameter. The panel had melted. The source seemed to be from inside the heater. I contacted Pentair through their web page but got no response. I phoned a few weeks later and spoke to a technician. He had never heard of this issue but he did suggest I take the panel off and do some inspections. He gave me his email.  I inspected it while it was running and when it was off. I took some images and sent them to the technician. The problem is that the heat exchanger which is made from metal developed a hole  around the flange that connects to the air blower which directs the hot air out of the top of the unit. Hot air from this hole was directed internal to the unit and out the back panel which led to the plastic melting. The metal lid of the heat exhanger had failed.. The exchanger should be sealed. The technician from Pentair replied that he would make a case and summit it to management. I gave him the serial number and the proof of installation. I did ask him if I can use the heater since it still works and he recommended not to. I assume because it is not safe. Someone from management left a phone message but mentioned something about this unit being out of warranty. I have not been able to contact him. He does not pick up the phone nor did he return my call.

My concern with this heater is that it continues to work indicating no problem yet Pentair recommends not using it. I would still being using it today if not for the copper issue and I do not know how long I was operating the unit in its present condition. Also  I still do not know if the copper contamination was caused by the heater. Unless one makes a thorough inspection of the unit you will never know it has an issue. You would literally have to take the panel off while it is in operation to determine it the heat exchanger has failed. The failure of the heat exchanger lid is evident by the observed flame through the breach. To me the problem is either a fundamental design flaw or a manufacturing issue. i cannot believe any well designed heater would develop metal fatigue of this magnitude in only 4 years. If the unit is unsafe it should automatically shut down and/or give an error message but this unit will continue to work and could potentially lead to a catastrophic situation. If the air is hot enough to melt plastic it is hot enough to ignite wood or cause some major internal problem (explosion). This might be a one-off or there might be many other units in the field waiting to fail or have already failed.
justification: The incident involves a heater with a potential design flaw causing a hole in the heat exchanger, leading to melted plastic but no reported injuries or deaths.

I have to tighten it every day before I ride. An internet search revealed that I am not the only one with this problem.
When the incident occurred, I almost went down but managed to stay up. Others may not be so lucky.

incident_description:
I'd like to share my experience with Rheem/ Raypak pool heaters. I purchased a Rheem 206 heater for my pool on the Thursday before Memorial Day. It was installed exactly as specified, and worked flawlessly until the Saturday before Fathers Day. That day, the pilot had gone out, so I had to relight it, which was nothing to be concerned about. Fathers Day morning, after just just 3 1/2 weeks of use, I awoke to find the heater burned to a crisp! Happy Fathers Day to me!

Following the warranty instructions, I contacted [REDACTED], the local Rheem service rep. Their tech wrote it up as "beyond repair, burned up badly." He disassembled it enough to conclude the pressure switch failed, allowing it to burn after the pump shut down for the night. He contacted the Rheem regional rep by phone (right in front of me), telling him it was a "good install" and an obvious part failure.

Since that time, I have been completely turned down by Corporate and refused warranty service. They questioned every aspect of the process. They wrongly concluded the gas valve was broken during installation, and the unit was tampered with to get it to work the 3 weeks that it did! The corporate warranty person, sitting at a desk in California, disagrees with the field tech here in Michigan, even after the tech explained his 28 years of experience and sent pictures of the undamaged gas valve, (which is about the only part left intact on the whole thing!) 

Given the complete denial of responsibility for the fire hazard, I believe this product should be thoroughly investigated. As a highly trained firefighter and fire investigator, I can assure you that this thermal event did not originate in, or have any involvement with, the gas valve. It was installed in exactly the condition it was sold. From the included pictures, you will see the fire hazard. A report was filed by the Livonia Fire Department on the day of the event. 

I wonder how many other units have caught fire and have not been investigated by a very arrogant corporation.
justification: The incident involved a pool heater burning up, but there was no mention of injury or death, only property damage.

incident_description:
Using a Saris Bones 3 trunk bike rack on my 2009 [REDACTED] 4dr sedan carrying 2 bikes, each weighting  about 30-32 pounds, 1 bike next to car, 1 bike (girls' model) in straps farthest from car, the rack broke at the girls' bike connection &
this bike fall off the rack.   
This occurred as I was entering 1-205 in Clackamas County, OR, a busy freeway. Luckily, I could pull off the freeway quickly, and the bike was still attached to the car by a bungi cord I used to tie the 2 bikes together so they wouldn't sway. 
The bike has about $200 in damages, Saris has agreed to send replacement parts for the rack, and no one was injured. However, this could have resulted in serious injury and/or property damage if the bike had not been attached by bungi cord. I read the installation instructions carefully and fitted it to my car. I was not told of any weight or number of bike 
limitations when I bought the rack.
When I called Saris yesterday, I was told that on my car, there is a 70-pound, 2 bike limit, and the bikes must be mounted in the two connections closest to the car. 
When I looked Saris' online "vehicle fit guide" yesterday, I did not see this limitation for Bones 3, only 
for Superbones 3-bike rack. I called Saris again today and was given the same information. However, today the 
online guide shows the limitation for the Bones 3 model. At best, even for the unusual consumer such as me who 
actually reads and attempts to follow instructions, this situation is unclear, hence unsafe for those carrying bikes and others on the highways. I called Saris's exclusive dealer here (River City Bikes) yesterday and asked if there
were any weight/bike limits for [REDACTED], was told there are none.
justification: The incident resulted in bike damage but no injuries, and the occurrence likelihood is possible due to unclear instructions and weight limits.

Please also be advised I have received a rma # [REDACTED] from Hatsan; yet I have been unable to send it back because a pellet is in the breach and I can not remove it. The consumer said that this diving mask permits water to get inside of the breathing compartment, which covers the nose and mouth.

If it is secured snuggly around the face and you keep you face in the water and you head tilted up, water may not get inside.  However, as soon as one submerges their head or there is a lot of splashing, water will get in the mask and may get into the 2 tubes connected to the mask.  Water can then get into ones nose or mouth. The water may enter through the snorkel, especially if the ball jams when submerging or the ball may jam in a closed position after surfacing - making one unable to breathe, a life threatening situation.

By the mouth, there is a pressure release where one can blow water out, but water does not completely exit the mask. When expelling water through the pressure release some of the water goes up the breathing tubes and then returns into the nose and mouth compartment - not safe.

(dates unknown) The consumer sent the firm 3 emails about his concern and he received a response to the first two, but not the 3rd one.  

He purchased the product 'open box', so they are not offering a warranty, but the consumer is not concerned about that.

He believes that these masks may present a safety hazard to swimmers.

I went to the Mares Head Company office near my residence, in person, with
product.
I met with [REDACTED]: Phone number [REDACTED], email [REDACTED]

and explained to him how I had been using it. [REDACTED] suggested that I had

[REDACTED] understood the problem and was kind enough to give me a very

Cordially yours, [REDACTED]

incident_description:
This caller is reporting a manufacturing patio swing purchased from Walmart in 1997.

A 2 year old child sustained injuries matching the design of the swing and narrow 5 to 3 inch opening in the front to rear, side leg support bar and back of the swing seat. The child was small enough to hang over the side support bars but unable to get out of the narrow side support bar and sloping heavy steel frame blocking her retreat from the entrapment.

As the child hung her body over the side support bar, the rear corner of the swing set struck her forehead and eyes multiple times causing subdural hematoma and possible brain injury.

In her efforts to stand up in order to free herself from her body entrapment, upper, mid and lower back came into contact with the curved down- sloping upper steel frame behind her, entrapping her body.

In those same moments she tried to stop the returning swing from hitting her, she grabbed under the swing bench seat frame, her wrist trapped between the 30 plus pound, 3 person bench seat and frame. Both to the front and rear of her wrist showed abrasions matching the swing design and sandy coated paint.

As she tried to hold the swing away from hitting her, she continued to try to back out, her head slid further in the frames narrowing side opening trapping her neck, face, eyes and ears leaving matching injuries to the design of the frame. Her neck was hyper flexed as she tried to pull her head out of the 3 to 5 inch side support bar opening.

The boyfriend feed the child by backing her head out of the entrapment as he pushed the swing away or off her head.

The child was not seen by a physician because once the child was freed and once calmed down seemed ok. Four days after the incident she began having seizures and was taken to [REDACTED] by her mother and mother's boyfriend. The diagnosis was child abuse! However, her injuries are from this swing and this accident. The Keysheen Industries, Garden Winds, Royal Deluxe model RUS4113 is the model that hurt this child. I believe this was taken out of production modify into the model RUS 4116, which has only a 5 to 8 inch narrow opening. I believe both are dangerous and should be recalled.

I now have possession of both models for investigators to examine. In April of 2017, I was able to find the RUS116 from a local man who purchased it also in the same time period of 1997 and his swing seat to use for creating photos to demonstrate how she was injured. Signed. [REDACTED]
justification: The child sustained multiple injuries including subdural hematoma and possible brain injury, which warrants a severity level of 3.

I assumed they were improperly, or incompletely assembled by the store person(s). Got the box home, and sorted all the parts, prior to assembly.  I noticed the front wheel felt wobbly.  I assumed it would tighten up after I assembled it.  After it was completely assembled, I was doing the final adjustments/fine tunings, and noticed the front wheel protruding towards the left side. Also, the kickstand scraped against the rear wheel's spokes when in the folded or up position.  I had to bend it outwards by hand to resolve the issue, but, it seems the metal eventually returns to its original shape, causing more scrapes.

Lastly, there were many parts missing from the box, albeit the box was completely sealed when I bought it.  I assume they were omitted at the factory.

I have looked at the same bike models at other stores, and they all seemed to have the same defects.  Even if a consumer assembles this bicycle model, it will still not be safe for a child to ride on.  Also, I read many reviews online by other customers whom complained of the same problems. Unfortunately, she had also told her grandparents that she wanted that bike, and lo and behold when her birthday came here comes Grandpop rolling in a shiny, brand new, turquoise and pink Girl Talk bike w. a pink ribbon on the handlebars. justification: The incident describes a defective product with potential safety hazards, but no actual injury occurred. The widespread nature of the defects suggests the issue is likely to occur with other units.

I had paid for the bicycle and was picking it up in the Walmart, 4101 N Vermilion St, Suite A in Danville, IL.  After testing the two other womenÃÂs 26ÃÂ, 7 speed bicycles, I did chose the Margaritaville for the seat and the positions fit better.

However, when I was riding around the garden section on it, I didnÃÂt turn fast enough and the bike was headed into a display.  When I applied the brakes, the right brake handle broke.  That is the one that stops the rear wheel.  I am not really that strong, but the brake handle broke very easily.  When I looked at it, I could see that it was made from pot metal.

I have had experience with garden shears that are made out of pot metal and them breaking.  That is not very dangerous, but when a bicycle brake handle breaks that is dangerous.  I am very glad that it broke in the store, for the bike assembler took it and put on a new set of handles made out of stronger metal, probably steel.  However, that could have been a different story, IF I had been going down a hill at 20 MPH.  I may have been frightened severely, injured, disabled or killed.

incident_description: I purchased my Can-Am X3 Maverick Max in September of last year. After less than 100 miles, I took it to the dealership because the steering wasn't responsive. The dealer told me it was normal. I took it out again, and the steering was so poor that it stopped working altogether, and locked in a turned position resulting in a near rollover of the vehicle. I took the vehicle in yet again, and the dealer replaced the power steering motor. It has made no difference, and the steering has actually worsened. Parked on concrete, I cannot steer the wheel with one hand. In 4wd, it is impossible to steer unless the vehicle is moving. Can-Am and BRP know this is an issue, and have even updated the steering motor in the 2019 units, but the 2018 owners have no option. The vehicle becomes inoperable and unsafe.
justification: The incident describes a near rollover due to steering failure, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Purchased a Vilano Shadow 3.0 Road Bike from Amazon, upon assembly of the bike discovered what appear to be substandard design related to the construction of the front fork which allows the front disk brake to strike the inside of the fork. In this condition if ridden could have resulted in loss of control of the bike.

It appears that in order to fit the front disk brakes, the manufacturer simply took a standard front fork and beat in one side of the inner portion of the front fork with a hammer and than painted it over. There is no machined recess or re-enforcement of the area to insure that the tube is not weakened by this procedure or damaged in shipping and to maintain the critical alignment of this componet.

 
The manufacturer claims that the bike conforms to CPSC 1512.
justification: The incident describes a substandard design that could lead to loss of control, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Pistol grip blow gun purchased from Harbor Frieght Tools Item # 68259
This is a held air blow gun which connects to any portable air compressor hose. 
Gun has a bass threaded fitting which is attached on the bottom of the hand held pistol handle. 
I installed a [REDACTED] 1/4 in. x 1/4 in. NPT Male Industrial Plug with tephlon tape to the threaded bass fitting. This is commonly done for air hose quick disconnect. Upon hooking up pistol grip blow gun to pressurize air compressor (120psi), and after using blow gun several time. I laid gun on Work bench, minutes laters pistol grip blow gun separated from bass fitting, which under pressures shot blow gun across the room. This was at a very high velocity. Lucky no one got hurt from the blow gun traveling across the room. Upon inspecting blow gun, it is very evident that a manufacturer defect lead to the separation of the pistol grip blow gun plastic handle and the molded brass fitting. 
This is the third pistol grip blow gun we have purchased from Harbor freight tools which has had a similar incident. 
We also have purchased (2) the same type of pistol grip blow from [REDACTED] ([REDACTED] and [REDACTED]) which have had the same exact problem.
All three of these pistol grip blow guns are made almost identical.


I have a picture of the pistol grip blow gun and the bass fitting if needed.
justification: The incident involved a high-velocity projectile but no injuries were reported, and it's a recurring issue with the same product.

incident_description: On June 22, 2018, 14 year old [REDACTED] was killed when a Goalsetter Systems, Inc. backboard detached from a wall in an indoor basketball court in his family's newly built home and fell on [REDACTED].  The Goalsetter "Installation and Owner's Instructions" for this "Wall Mount Series" backboard contained zero instructions on the minimum requirements for safely installing this 260 lbs. backboard into a wall. Even though the consumer hired, as recommended by Goalsetter, a contractor to install the backboard, Goalsetter failed to provide any warnings or instructions for persons installing the backboard system regarding the dynamic load characteristics or minimum anchoring requirements for installing this backboard.  Goalsetter's deliberate and conscious failure to provide information that it possesses regarding the dynamic load and minimum anchoring of this product, makes this product unsafe.  In contrast, other household items, such as flat screen TV mounts provide minimum anchoring requirements and information regarding the maximum weight bearing capacity.  A copy of the  "Installation and Owner's Instructions"  is attached. Also attached is a national news article regarding the death.  The St. Joseph County Police Department and St. Joseph County Prosecutor's Office is investigating the death and has taken possession of the Goalsetter System and other evidence.
justification: The incident resulted in a death due to the backboard falling, which is the highest severity level. The occurrence likelihood is considered rare based on the provided frequency of 76 out of 3915 incidents.

incident_description:
Purchased John Deere Gator model 550 in 2014, a 2013 demo model had about 14 hours on it.  Had the vehicle serviced at one year after purchase (2015) at the John Deere dealer.  In early 2016 we had several problems with brake not working and not holding the vehicle on even slight hill. Took to a local mechanic to check it and look at the brakes. He said the brake cable was significantly damaged and needed to be replaced. He replaced the brake cable with John Deere part.  In mid 2017 the brake was not holding all the time, would take several attempts pushing the brake to get it in Brake mode, with engine on or off, then this month 7/2016, the brake would not hold on slight upgrade in yard. We again took the the Cookeville, TN John Deere dealer for routine service (7/26/2018) and to check the brake. The mechanic said to brake cable broke when he was removing it before he replaced it with a new cable.  When we spoke with the service dept manager we asked about the brake cable failing, that I considered this a major safety issue and definitely a possible recall issue.  He said ÃÂwe have had a few complaints about this issue from a few other customersÃÂ but that was all he said.  
  We live an area and use the Gator on large, steep hills for manure spreading and trail maintenance in our equine development, which has steep hills and ravines.  After we got home I checked on the CPSC and found there have been numerous complaints about this same issue.  To me THIS IS a major safety issue.  In the past we have been on a narrow trail, on the very edge of a cliff, we got stuck, and if the brake had failed at that point the Gator would have gone over the side, down a rock edge about 100 feet to a river.
justification: The brake failure is a recurring issue with potential for serious accidents, but no actual injury or death is reported in the description.

incident_description: I have a mountain bike with a hydraulic brakeset manufactured by SRAM. These SRAM Guide RS brakes appear to have a design flaw that results in a small plastic piston swelling when the ambient temperature exceeds roughly 95 degrees. The result is that the brake then applies pressure to the hydraulic circuit and causes the brake caliper to lock up. I was riding my bike recently in hot summer weather and this defect occurred while I was on a steep descent.  The front brake of the bike locked up and I lost control and was thrown from the bike causing some injuries.  I have since talked with a number of retail bike shops and learned from scouring the Internet that this is a well known problem.  SRAM has agreed to replace the defective brake levers, but I don't think they should be able to continue to sell these dangerous products.  They are well aware of the defect, it has been a problem for at least 2 years and they appear to still be selling levers that suffer from this problem.  A full description of the problem, dating back to 2016, can be found here https://www.pinkbike.com/forum/listcomments/?threadid=189827
justification: The incident resulted in injuries due to a known design flaw causing brake failure in hot weather, and the problem is well-documented and ongoing.

incident_description:
Last fall (Aug/Sept, 2017), I bought a Cross Pointe Sniper Crossbow.  I shot it a few times on my property before taking it to the range.  At the range, the cross bow string nearly cut my thumb off.  Fortunately, the hand specialist/surgeon was able to sew it back on.  Now, i can use my thumb, but have not regained feeling in the area in front of the wound entry point.

It is true that the manufacturer of this bow has warned the operator against getting a finger in front of the string; however, there is an insufficient safety barrier to prevent this from happening.  Since my accident, I have examined cross bows made by other manufacturers and noticed that all others have a longer, wider, and thicker barrier to prevent the operators fingers from wandering into danger.  I would strongly encourage the manufacturer of Cross Point Sniper crossbows as well as Cabelas/Bass Pro Shops to correct this dangerous deficiency in this product.

I hope to find someone to create an acceptable and safety barrier so that I may safely use this cross bow.  If not, I will have to replace it.  It is not safe to take into the field in its original manufactured condition.
justification: The incident resulted in a serious injury to the thumb, requiring surgery, but the thumb was saved, making it a level 3 severity.

I did not know the tube had been recalled at the time of use. Due to the burning, I searched the internet for potential causes of the burning after using the inner tube and found it had been recalled. I then deflated the inner tube so no one else would use it.
justification: The incident resulted in a burning sensation, redness, and additional symptoms like light-headedness and nausea, indicating an injury.

The submitter noticed that another consumer reported a similar issue to Amazon on January 2, 2018 and there were 11 more complaints about a safety concern. The submitter also contacted the U.S. distributor of the replica scooter who is Global eTrade Services and reported his safety concerns. The firm offered the submitter a refund but didn't address any of his concerns about replicating another model or whether they would investigate the faulty parts. 

Here is the Amazon link to the scooter: https://www.amazon.com/Scooter-Adjustable-Height-Flashing-Children/dp/B075GK8Z7F/ref=sr_1_1?s=books&ie=UTF8&qid=1520274799&sr=8-1&keywords=outon+scooter&dpID=41CV--Q0LGL&preST=_SY300_QL70_&dpSrc=srch
