incident_description:
The Polaris RZR 800S is a popular UTV produced and marketed by Polaris. The units in-question seem to span the years of 2008 thru 2015. In those years, the rear-differential utilized an independent axle produced originally by DANA/SPICER. In future models, c. 2013 / 2014, the DANA group was purchased by SCHAFER. Subsequent to this, the differential units are stamped and labeled as SCHAFER.

In the earlier versions, and up into the initial manufacture of the SCHAFER version, the pinion gear is held in-place with a nylok nut, a nut with a nylon insert to act as a lock-nut.

What has been discovered by much of the RZR community, and has been well documented, is the nylok fails, the nut backs off the pinion gear and the pinion gear becomes wedged into the ring gear / differential housing and fails catastrophically.

This results in the differential seizing, and the entire rear-end drive unexpectedly seizing.

The failure occurs while the vehicle is in-motion and can occur without warning and without recourse.

Consequently, with the rear-drive locked-up solid, given the unit is a posi-track (positive traction) unit, there is no free-spin in the rear-end with the pinion gear wedged between the ring gear and a hole in the housing of the differential. Thus, the rider has a sudden and complete loss of control and propulsion on the unit. It is tantamount to slamming on only the rear brakes of the machine with no way to regain controlled forward movement. On wet or otherwise slick surfaces, which is often the case for such riding conditions, the vehicle cannot be steered as the rear drivetrain no longer responds to either throttle or brake.

At an absolute minimum, from a cost perspective, the financial impact of this is in excess of $1,300, not including labor.

While the issue is very well documented, including by this user, Polaris has yet to acknowledge this as a clear safety issue relating to the proper operation of the vehicle.

Without knowing of this potential for incipient and unexpected catastrophic component failure, and without significant disassembly efforts, including dismantling the drivetrain down to component pieces to check for the nylok and proper torque (roughly 250 ft-lb) on the pinion nut, there is no way to know whether or not the user's unit is at-risk.

For any responsible owner of the RZR vehicle, there should be a reasonable expectation that the unit would operate with proper routine maintenance. As such, there is no level of routine maintenance, fluid changes or otherwise, which would stave-off the nylok failure, backing off the pinion gear threads, and subsequent catastrophic failure of the unit.

The issue is very well documented by photo and video of multiple units both on-line and in the possession of this user.
justification: The incident describes a catastrophic failure leading to sudden loss of control, which can result in injury. The issue is well-documented, indicating a high likelihood of occurrence.

I ordered a product called a Ninebot One from an ebay seller called myfunwheel.  The ninebot is made by segway and myfunwheel is a U.S. seller.  

Their contact info is

Dion@myfunwheel
293 Washington Dr
Brentwood CA, 94513
1 925 493 0920

The Ninebot One is a single wheel device similar to a hover board except that it has a single wheel.  

While my son was riding this device, it stopped suddenly causing him to be thrown from the machine.  When I looked at the machine, I found that the battery was incorrectly installed.  The battery had quite a bit of double sided tape to hold it securely in the machine, but the backing was not removed from the tape.  This left the battery free to move around in the machine.  Because the battery was free to move, the power connection was ripped off the battery while he was riding it, causing the sudden stop and injury.  

This was directly the result of improper battery instillation by the supplier.  

Even though the machine was new, the battery also appeared to be an aftermarket battery.  

My concern is that this company sells hundreds of these machines on ebay, and I am certain that it is common for the batteries to be incorrectly installed.  I feel that there is great risk to other riders.  There is risk of injury or death as a result if this shortcut taken by the seller.
justification: The incident resulted in injury due to the sudden stop caused by improper battery installation, and the likelihood is high given the seller's practices.

incident_description:
After 7 years of owning a pair of Teeter EZ-Up Gravity Boots, purchased online along with a [REDACTED] Sport Inversion Table on 10 January 2010, all four fastening ratchet straps on the boots broke on the same day, 3 Feb 2017, as I was trying to tighten them, one after the other. I'm glad I wasn't hanging upside down when this breakage occurred. I sporadically use my Teeter inversion table and boots, far from on a daily basis, and haven't abused the equipment. Over the 7 years of ownership, I've probably used the table no more than 50 or so times. Other than the straps breaking, the boots are in excellent condition and so is the table. No cracked plastic on the boots (other than the straps). No decaying foam liner on the boots. Points where the straps attach appear fine. The straps are easily removed. They simply slide out. I searched online for replacement straps available for purchase but found none. I finally called Teeter customer service on 8 Feb 2017 as a follow-up to an online problem report I filed with Teeter on 5 Feb 2017 about the strap breakage.

The Teeter customer rep I spoke with on 8 Feb 2017 was polite enough, but reminded me of the 5 year warranty and my boots being out of warranty. She told me I would have to send the boots in at my own expense, and the straps would be replaced at no cost. I asked her if straps could be sent to me instead, as I could easily insert them myself at connection point. She said that's against company policy due to potential liability issues if something else is wrong with the boots. I politely declined the send in repair offer as I do not wish to incur the cost of shipping.

If these straps were made out of more durable plastic, perhaps a [synthetic fiber] mix, or were partially constructed of metal, the straps might not have dry rotted/snapped. As is and based on my breakage experience, the strap design material, prone to dry rot and breakage, poses a potential danger to the consumer after x amount of years and/or x amount of boot usage. Alternative, non-Teeter boots exist on the market that appear to be of better construction, at least when it comes to connection/tightening methods, and that's what I will pursue.

Based on other Teeter boot owners who have posted negative online reviews of these boots due to strap breakage (amazon.com is one good source for these particular reviews), sometimes when the owner was hanging upside down on the table (my strap breakage is not a fluke), these boots appear to have a serious design flaw when it comes to the plastic strap fastening method. I suggest either changing the strap material to something more durable, or redesigning and implementing a hardier and more trustworthy connection/tightening system. At very least, Teeter should offer price friendly replacement straps for sale, especially to those of us for whom the warranty has run out, versus the owner having to send the boots to Teeter for strap replacement---something just about any owner of the boots could easily do him or herself. Also, at least based on my research, Teeter does not mention any potential danger of strap breakage in the product's instructions or other information or otherwise recommend the straps be replaced after a given period of service.
justification: The straps broke but no injury occurred, and similar incidents have been reported by other users.

incident_description:
I purchased a Boosted Board powered longboard on 11/19/2014. I regularly used the product on a daily basis until 7/9/2015 in Foster City, CA when it caused me to fall and dislocate my left knee, including a full ACL, PCL, MCL tear in my knee.

This product is usually used in a "last-mile" commute to and from a destination. It has a dual 1500W remote-controlled motor sending power to two rear wheels. I rode my Boosted Board from my front door to reach my car parked a distance away on the morning of 7/9/2015. On this occasion I rode about 20-25 feet away from my apartment front-door when suddenly the board rapidly decelerated and made a loud grinding noise. I had no time to react and jump off. In the fall I injured my knee and I could not get up due to the pain and had to call for help.

I called a nearby building manager for immediate help and called a friend to take me to hospital. The next day I had an MRI which showed the extent of the injuries including a full ACL, PCL, MCL tear, impaction fractures, a grade II sprain of LCL, patellar retinacular tear, etc. (Full MRI report can be provided.)

On 12 January, 2016 I underwent a 9.5 hour orthopedic surgery to begin repairing my knee. On examination it revealed a full knee dislocation, with complete ACL, PCL, MCL, LCL tears. Full surgery report can be provided. I spent approximately 3 months on crutches, while awaiting a follow-up surgery to address the torn ACL.

On 8 December, 2016 I underwent a second surgery to reconstruct the torn ACL. Full surgery report can be provided.

On 13 July 2015, I provided Boosted Boards with an initial report of my injury and a concern that the product may have malfunctioned, I offered to them that I will return the board in an effort to allow them to investigate. After they received my board on 1 September 2015, they failed to contact me for several weeks while I asked for updates. On October 6 they said they haven't been able to figure anything out. On 16 October, the CEO of Boosted Boards contacted me saying no abnormal behavior was found in their logs and offered me a refund. 

I am aware of this happening to at least one other person. On 7/30/2015, another rider was commuting through San Francisco and described the following, "My board stopped suddenly with a screeching noise as if it were thrown into reverse. [...] I was thrown into scaffolding breaking a finger. I had surgery on Monday to set the finger straight. [...] It took some time to get my board and the remote back online with each other which led me to believe that my incident was most likely some of of RF interference." (More details on this incident can be provided however this is a separate incident and this person is not listed on this report.)

This report and its description of how the board malfunctioned correlate with my experience. Given that this has happened at least twice, I would like CPSC to investigate further, given how Boosted Boards has not been either willing or able to find the cause.
justification: The incident resulted in severe injuries including a dislocated knee and multiple ligament tears, requiring multiple surgeries and extended recovery time.

company when my brand new bike did this I was told it was my fault for not checking to make sure they were tight

incident_description:
I've been a climber for nearly 20 years. When climbing, I use many types of equipment, all of which must function flawlessly. One of the pieces of equipment I use are carabiners which act as a conection point/link between pieces of gear, rope, etc.  Carabiners have spring-loaded gates; it is critical that a carabiner's gate close automatically; not closing automatically greatly weakens the carabiners ability to resist dynamic forces, as well as creates an unsafe situation where gear can become detached from the climbing safety system.

I recently replaced the majority of my carabiners with CAMP Nano 22 carabiners. Although these carabiners have seen very little use, I found two last weekend while climbing with open gates (gates that were open while in use). This creates an incredibly unsafe situation that can easily lead to death.
justification: The description states that open gates on carabiners can easily lead to death, which is a severity level 4. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as it happened twice recently with new equipment.

She's had surgery on one knee and can't use it and the other leg is shaking. Granted she got this mechanism 2/6/2015 and asked over and over again to remove this and/or replace it. NOBODY would listen. Back in 2015, she could separate her legs and manage to avoid the metal bracket. Now, it's totally impossible when she's getting in/out of the bathroom, bed, kitchen and anywhere she goes. All we asked was to either remove it, change it or replace it and they want us to pay $600 plus an expense to ship the scooter to CA. First, she cannot go without a scooter, second, she does not have the funds. Why can't this company take responsibility and either remove/replace it? This company should rectify their mistake. We are frustrated at best. Hope you can help us. Much appreciation! [REDACTED] and [REDACTED]
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning scooter bracket causing physical interference and discomfort, indicating a risk of injury due to the patient's condition and repeated issues.

incident_description: I was riding a specialized epic bike up a forest road. The frame part snapped. This is the chain stay part on the bike. The weld failed. The crack is right along the joint. Straight and clean. A total failure of the weld. I realize the fact that a Mountain bike wouldn't be covered however this is a cross country bike. Not what I would consider a mountain bike in that regard.  The issue I have is upon further investigation and searches along the Internet this isn't an isolated incident. In fact the issue is always the same and the weld fails. I believe this is an issue that needs attention. Apparently Specialized has warrantied this part on a case by case basis. Which I also believe is an unfair practice if they are addressing an issue they are aware of. Furthermore the break can cause the rider to lose control of the bike. I believe this is an issue of manufacturing and not abuse or use other than intended.
justification: The incident describes a bike frame failure that could cause loss of control, but no injury is reported. The issue is not isolated, indicating a recurring problem.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that the trampoline she had purchased 3 1/2 years caused injury to her 29 year old daughter while she was using it, the trampoline broke through the center and pad ripped from spring to spring and she fell to ground on her feet.  She was taken to Verde Valley Hospital by an ambulance where she was treated for ankle sprains and bruises.  The victim was released for follow up.  She had follow up visits with physical therapy and orthopedic surgeon

(6/2016) Consumer stated that she contacted the manufacturer and they advised her that the trampoline was no longer under warranty.  She stated that the trampoline is a safety concern and that there is no warning label to indicate that it could cause this incident.

No warning signs were present that pad was deteriorated

Consumer stated that she would like the company to recall this trampoline.

Injury information:  Injury, Emergency Department Treatment received, physical therapy, unable to walk, severe pain
justification: The incident resulted in injury requiring emergency treatment and follow-up care, but no death. The likelihood is possible given the product's age and lack of warning signs.

incident_description: I purchased a Swagway Hoverboard last year from Amazon and have had a couple incidents with it, such as overheating, and the charging light constantly on even when charged. I attempted to reach out to Amazon, even after I received an email about this same exact product being recalled, and they claim they cannot help me. My daughter is 10 years old, and I will not have her use this product ever again because of all the issues and fires they have had with it.
justification: The incident involves overheating and charging issues, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I purchased a Wheeli Hooverboard online through Zulily.  The hooverboard stopped in the middle of riding, I fell off and shattered my wrist.  Surgery cost over $5,000 in out of pocket expenses.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe injury (shattered wrist requiring surgery), but the likelihood is considered possible as such incidents are not uncommon with hoverboards.

incident_description:
On October 6, 2012 my son fell from a Hunter's View treestand which was manufactured by C & S Global Imports. His full-body fall arrest system (harness) broke at the tree strap. The harness was manufactured by C & S Global Imports and had a label with the number CSFAS2009 sewn into the harness and the tree strap. The tree strap was not cut, it tore apart. My son died as a result of this fall.

Please refer to previous recalls of similar harnesses, your file number RP050173. Hunters View harnesses were recalled in 2005 and again in 2007.

The 2009 harnesses should be recalled.
justification: The incident resulted in a fatality due to a harness failure, and there is evidence of prior recalls indicating a recurring issue.

incident_description: My barnett raptor crossbow  took off top of thumb with string there is not enough room  on forearm to put your fingers foerarm should be lower saftey issue
justification: The description indicates a severe injury to the thumb caused by the crossbow string, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: Two people  were in a bad boy buggy xto. One was driving and one riding. There were no seat belts, door nets, or other safety features to keep passengers inside and safe. Upon turning the xto to the left at less than 5 mph the vehicle hit a small clump of dirt and flipped causing my son (the passenger) to be thrown out and the top heavy roof rack fell on his head. He ended up dying a few hours later.
justification: The incident resulted in a death, which is the highest severity level. The likelihood is considered possible given the lack of safety features and the circumstances described.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that the hoverboards when in use shuts off causing the user to fall.  He stated that his children had received injuries from these units, included bruises on knees, elbows and foreheads.  No medical attention was received.  First aid was administered to their wounds. Caller needs the agency to investigate the individual who sold these items.  However, the  contact is no longer available.   These units was purchased online.

The hoverboards have been stored because they are unsafe.

Caller would like these hoverboards to be recalled.
justification: The incident caused injuries (bruises) but no medical attention was required, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is high (4) as the hoverboards consistently shut off during use, leading to falls.

incident_description: Decedent travelling on rural road at approximately 30 miles per hour, not wearing helmet.  Lost control of ATV and rolled it, causing significant head trauma.  Died at the hospital 3 days later of traumatic head injury.
justification: The incident resulted in death due to traumatic head injury, and such severe outcomes are relatively uncommon.

incident_description: Decedent was found pinned under an ATV on a remote hillside trail.
justification: The description states the decedent was found pinned under an ATV, indicating a fatality.

incident_description:
The submitter states that the playground was evaluated on 8/8/16 by [REDACTED]. The submitter indicated that the evaluation determined the playground has many safety hazards, such as improper ground which presents a fall zone hazard and a laceration hazard due to holes in the steel frame. The playground also poses a burn hazard and a height risk hazard.

The submitter indicated that the playground is very old and the manufacturer is Iron Mountain Forge but they are now apart of Little Tikes.

The submitter states that the school and the school district are aware of the issue but have failed to address the matter. The submitter does not believe the playground has been inspected through the district in a long time and they have been neglecting the safety protocol with the playground.

The submitter would like to remain anonymous from the school and avoid repercussions from the school or school district.
justification: The playground has multiple safety hazards that could lead to injuries, but no actual incidents or injuries are reported in the description.

incident_description: My 2015 Polaris 570 Sportsman stopped running while on a trip in July, 2016. To see if I had enough fuel, I removed the gas cap and found the gas was boiling in the tank. I removed a side panel and saw that the exhaust pipe coming out of the engine was directly under the fuel tank, and the tank was too hot to touch. A friend who was riding with me said he had the same problem with his [REDACTED], he removed his gas cap and was sprayed with vaporized fuel under pressure. I looked on line and found numerous complaints about the same problem. In some cases the seat on the machine caught fire because of the proximity of the exhaust pipe. This problem also relates to Polaris UTVs. Polaris has been aware of this unsafe and dangerous condition for at least nine years.
justification: The incident describes a dangerous condition with potential for injury or fire, but no actual injury or death occurred in this specific case.

incident_description: Aqualung BCD (Bouyancy Control Devices) contain a Powerline inflator that can get stuck, causing unchecked inflation and rapid ascent during scuba diving.  This is under a voluntary recall.  Divers Direct in Miami FL is selling these devices without notifying customers of the defect.  They should have had them repaired or replaced as per the manufacturer's website.  By continuing to sell these, they are endangering the life of their customers.
justification: The defect can cause rapid ascent during scuba diving, which is life-threatening, and the devices are being sold without warning, endangering customers' lives.

incident_description:
14 year old Ice Hockey goalie, wearing Bauer NME10 goalie mask with Titanium cage
Playing at practice, took a shot (puck) off the cage which severely dented and broke the titanium cage right at his eye level. He was dazed and suffered an unnecessary and unexpected experience.
It was our understanding that the $900+ Bauer hockey helmet was more than adequate to protect him from an injury due to faulty equipment. We were absolutely unaware of any recall on this helmet that our son has been wearing for over a year. We were not informed of any safety risk, and if we had been informed we would never have let our son continue to wear this helmet which was supposed to be protecting his head.  
I went today to Monkey Sports to get a replacement cage, was unable to find one, with the help of the goalie department manager there ended up buying an entire new mask.  The manager was unable to remove the  broken Bauer titanium cage from original helmet. He had no knowledge whatsoever of any recall, nor did I until I went home and went on the Bauer website to send them pictures of what happened to the titanium cage. Unknown previously to me I stumbled upon the recall information.  I am beyond angry as a parent that my son has worn this helmet with this titanium cage for the past almost 2 years without any information at all regarding a safety issue. Had we been informed we would have rectified the situation immediately.
justification: The goalie was dazed and suffered an unexpected experience due to faulty equipment, indicating a potential injury risk, though no explicit injury was mentioned.

incident_description: Was at NRG Lab in Mansfield MA using a TRX Rip Trainer. I was doing a reverse curl exercise with the devise (metal bar attached to a resistance elastic band) and as I was pulling the bar towards me, it came apart and the force of the resistance band swung the bar back into my face. It hit me on the bridge of my nose. My nose was broken and the metal edge lacerated my eye lid resulting in several stitches to close the gash. I have been diagnosed with a concussion and have been on a protocol for 2 weeks. I have 2 more weeks to go. The gym claims the bar malfunctioned and they have contacted TRX in CA. They have yet to hear back from TRX. I am reporting this in hopes that TRX will notify its buyers of the product to examine it closely for any defects, My guess is I will not hear from TRX but wanted to report this incident regardless. Thank you.
justification: The incident resulted in a broken nose, lacerations requiring stitches, and a concussion, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is unlikely (2) as it appears to be related to a specific product malfunction.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting that her mother purchased a hoverboard from their online site around November 2015 and sent it to her 14 year old son for Christmas 2015.

Her son placed the hoverboard on charge around the second week in January 2016 but after approximately one half hour his mother smelled plastic burning and during investigating the source of the odor went into her son's room.

She saw smoke coming from the hoverboard; she grabbed a towel, threw it over the hoverboard and kicked the plug out of the outlet which caused sparks at the wall/outlet area.

She moved the hoverboard and used the towel to suffocate any source of heat that could cause it to burst into flames.

When she removed the towel she saw that the unit had melted in half with cracks on the halves.

When she tried to pick the hoverboard up after it cooled it broke in half.

She has now found that Swagway has recalled the unit and she is asking for CPSC to assist her with obtaining a refund for this hoverboard because both she and her now 15 year old son are afraid to have another hoverboard in their home.

There are no injuries to report

She has contacted Swagway numerous times attempting to obtain a refund and she has populated information in forms that they have instructed her to enter information.
justification: The hoverboard caught fire and melted, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I was riding my POLARIS RZR TURBO 2016 in a national park, called "china muerta" and suddenly fire starts in the engine area. The UTV was completely burned, its important to say that this UTV has only 200 miles of use. Additional of this, some trees and wood was burned and i suffer a burn in my left leg.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury to the left leg and significant property damage, including the complete burning of the UTV and surrounding trees.

incident_description:
This BCD is dangerous and should be recalled. I just returned from a dive trip to Grand Cayman Island and used this BCD for the second time diving. On a previous trip to Bonaire last summer Aug 2015, I discovered that the BCD absorbs water into the padded areas and has no ability to drain. When you get to the boat to climb the ladder you find that you have and aditional 10lbs of weight from the accumulated water.
I add some drain holes and hoped this would resolve the problem. Not .... I discovered more areas that water could enter and not get out.
Now the bad water absorption issue is a problem but not as serious as the next issue.
On my last trip I discovered that the air tank can pinch off the air bladder making it extremely difficult to achieve buoyancy when critically required. This BCD does not have a upper right shoulder dump valve so if the tank pinches off the bladder it is extremely difficult to quickly get the air out before shooting to the surface beyond your safety stop. the lower right dump valve can not be reached because the pull handle floats up out of reach. I consider this a serious problem ... hopefully no one gets hurt by this.
justification: The BCD's design flaws pose a risk of buoyancy control failure, which could lead to dangerous situations underwater, though no injuries are reported yet.

incident_description: Less than 5 months ago we purchased a Little Tikes Outdoor swing. This past week while my grandson was in the swing the strap over his right shoulder shredded apart and broke. The left strap thankfully stayed intact. The left one also broke when I was taking him out of the swing. If both straps had given way at the same time he could have been severely injured or worse. Obviously Little Tikes know they have a problem with this product and the straps because they sell replacement ones.
justification: The straps broke but no injury occurred, though there was potential for severe injury or death if both straps had failed simultaneously.

incident_description:
This caller is creating this report for a batters helmet manufactured by a popular corporation in Georgia purchased March 18th, 2016 online via order# [REDACTED].

April 1st, 2016, during a junior varsity baseball game at his school the caller's 14 year old son was hit by a baseball in the cutout triangular ear portion causing his earlobe to be cut at the cartilage.  

He was taken to Johnston Memorial Emergency room in Abingdon, Virginia where he required six stitches to close the wound.

When the 14 year old removed his helmet there was a lot of blood and his parents noticed that there was no padding behind the ear and that the cutout was rough and not smooth.

The caller has submitted two letters to the manufacturer with the second being received on June 15t, 2016 with no response which prompted the caller to also file a report with the Georgia Attorney General and plans to file a report with the Attorney General in his state of Virginia.

The helmet has not been used since this incident and will not be used.

The caller is reporting this product as a potentially severed safety hazard involving head and ear injury.
justification: The incident resulted in a cut requiring stitches (injury), but the likelihood of recurrence is unlikely given the specific circumstances and the helmet's discontinuation.

incident_description:
Purchased a CAP BARBELL WEIGHT BENCH SET ON 3/26/16
On 8/22/16 while I was lifting 80lbs on the bar, one of the pins
used to hold the bar together fell out! I had to carefully and slowly lower the bar with the weights onto the floor to avoid the 80lbs toppling onto my feet.

This use of these metal pins to secure this bar together is not stable and is defective. This should have never happened and someone is going to get seriously hurt if use of this bar is continued to be manurfactured as such.

I have contacted CAP BARBELL and they refuse to even look into it.
justification: The incident involved a defective product that could have caused injury, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: My husband was riding his bike with the Sunlite Child Carrier w/Steel Rack on his bike. We followed the instructions and according to them the seat was properly installed and secure. The only thing keeping the seat on is one bolt/screw with a tamper resistant child lock on it. My husband had just stopped at a stop sign and pushed forward on the peddle to start moving and the one screw holding the seat on came loose and the entire seat (with my 2 year old son inside) slid right off the rack flipped over twice before stopping. My son was wearing a helmet and other than a few scratches and being shaken up he was fine. But if my husband was going faster or my son did not have a helmet on, the damage could have been much worse.
justification: The child sustained minor injuries (scratches) and was shaken up, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The incident occurred due to a single point of failure in the seat's attachment mechanism, suggesting a possible likelihood of recurrence (occurrence likelihood 3).

incident_description:
IÃÂm having a huge safety issue where within months, two (2) motor control boards with minimum use on my Sole F60 Treadmill has caught on fire.   The first motor control board caught on fire and there was burnt damage on the motor control circuit board.  This board was simply replaced with a new one.  Within a month and half the new motor control board caught on fire.  This is the second time a motor control board has caught on fire and there was significantly more burnt damage to the circuit board.

I have gotten to the point where I feel the Sole treadmill is no longer safe.  I can keep replacing these motor control boards, however there is a huge fear of my safety of my home and my family that lives in it.  After all there already has been two (2) fire hazards directly caused by the Sole product, with normal use. 

I have contacted Sole and shared pictures with them and they did not want to help with this safety issue.
justification: The incident involves repeated fire hazards with motor control boards, posing a significant safety risk to the home and family, though no injury or death has been reported yet.

incident_description:
(05/2015) The consumer stated that ATV was parked at home. He thought he put it in park. The ATV started moving. The consumer fiddled with the ATV to get it to stop.

The next time that it happened, he parked the ATV in a trailer, put the ATV in park and closed the trailer Sometime later, he had to move the trailer a few feet with the lawn tractor. When he put the brake on the lawn tractor, he heard a crash. He opened the door of the trailer and saw that the ATV had had crashed into the cabinet in the front of the trailer. 

(9/23/2015)The consumer took the product to a dealership, [REDACTED],  to complain about what had happened. There was also a reverse problem with the unit. The consumer was promised that the problems would be repaired.

When he picked it up at the dealership, he asked if the ATV was going to stay in park and go in reverse when it is placed in reversed. He was advised that it would. 

The reverse problem was not taken care off. The consumer went in to complained and was advised to bring the ATV around to the service entrance. When he bought it up on the ramp and placed it in park, the ATV started rolling backwards.

The dealer advised the consumer that they contacted the manufacturer. 

The dealer said that Polaris does not want to take care of the problem.

(10/10/2015) The consumer went to the dealer and asked them to go out on the lot to get an identical machine to see what would happened. The consumer stated the other ATV worked perfectly.

(1/28/2016)The dealer suggested that the consumer take the ATV back to the place of purchase, which he did. He asked to speak to a manager to demonstrate the problem. The same thing happened again. 

The manager contacted Polaris but Polaris did not want to cooperate in any repairs or replacements.

The consumer stated that there are hills and trails in Minnesota. If a person happens to park the ATV at the crest of a hill thinking the vehicle is in park, it could roll down the hill and crash or run into a child.
justification: The incident involved the ATV rolling unexpectedly, causing property damage but no reported injuries. The issue was recurring but not frequent enough to be considered likely or almost certain.

incident_description:
While riding in the Utah Desert on vacation. We returned to our camping site and noticed a burnt hole in the back of our 2011 Polaris Rzr. The hole was burnt plastic located right above the exhaust pipes in the back of the bed. There is no heat shield under the bed and could have killed my dog, my wife and my 10 year old child. The plastic melted onto the exhaust and had a very bad burnt plastic smell. We have not drove it since. I contacted Polaris and spoke to [REDACT]. They stated its not a 2013 so they are not going to fix it. 

I explained the recalls for the 2013-2016 is for this event exactly. The fuel tank vent line (Z-16-01-a), the voltage regulator (z-16-01-c), "THE HEAT SHIELD (z-16-01-D) to replace and install additional heat shielding to decrease the risk of rear bed/box melting, and to channel fuel away from the engine bay in the event of accidental liquid spills.
justification: The incident involved a burnt hole in the vehicle but no injuries or deaths occurred, though there was potential for harm.

incident_description:
My rear tire went flat a week before I went on a 350 mile bike tour.  The second day of the tour, a new inner tube again went flat in the same place with a 3mm slit in the tire, causing rapid air loss.  I saw that the tire strip was wrinkled, and assumed that the wrinkle caused the leak and the patch would prevent another.  On the last day of the tour I rode on the wheel at 35 mph downhill and at 22 mph for 10 miles continuously while following a tandem.  If the tire had gone flat during these periods, there would have been a loss of control of the bicycle.

Two days later, I removed the tire and wheel strip, intending to replace the wheel strip.  Under the wheel strip, the aluminum of the interior of the double walled wheel had cracked, forming sharp edges as the crack propagated from spoke hole to spoke hole.  One of the cracked sections was over 15 inches long.  The cracks could not be seen when under the tire strip, and the exterior wall had no cracks, so that the crack could not be observed until the tire strip was cut.  

When I explained the incident to Trek, the representative said he was glad I made the ride safely.  Trek later said the wheel was out of the 2 years warranty period, but that they would cover half the expense of a new wheel.  They said that cracks of this type were one of the ways this wheel can fail. The representative at the bike shop said that my body weight of 175 pounds and the tire pressure of 50 psi were not out of specification for this wheel.  

I do not believe that this failure mode should be regarded as acceptable because it cannot be observed by the rider (even with the tire off) and can lead to rapid air loss and loss of control at speeds that could cause serious injury.
justification: The incident involved a potential loss of control due to a hidden wheel crack, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
While my boys were in motion on the hoverboard, it instantaneously stops, throwing them off the board... The iMoto Brand hoverboard 360 has many issues including potential to overheat, catch fire, and even explode, none of which ours has done yet... but ours stops when in use throwing the rider off the equipment violently... it is going and simply stops as if the battery went dead.  We have discontinued use as a result... However, through several communications with the company in which we purchased the Hoverboard 360... They refuse to respond to our email communications, we have given them all of the information that they have asked for, yet they simply take no responsibility for their defective dangerous product.

These hoverboards do not comply with the safety standards established by Underwriters Laboratory in UL 2272
justification: The hoverboard stops suddenly, throwing riders off violently, but no injuries are reported.

incident_description:
While riding the ATV trails in [REDACTED] the brakes on my ATV failed forcing me to jump off of the machine.
The rear brake assembly where it attaches to the axle disassembled causing the brakes to completely fail.
I believe the brake cables are an inch too short which keeps the adjusters too close to the end of the cable and with
the pressure of using the brake puts too much pressure on the adjuster causing it to fail. I had the brakes adjusted
shortly after my purchase as the brakes were not performing correctly. I think this problem with the brakes, if not
addressed by Polaris could cause imminent physical harm and possible death via an accident.
justification: The incident involved brake failure forcing the rider to jump off, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
2012 Can-Am 800 Max, Heat is melting fuel tank.

Heat from the exhaust, in particular the muffler has caused the fuel tank which is plastic to melt.  This melting produce has occurred overtime and gradually melted it to the extent that is now leaks fuel, causing an extreme fire hazard.  Had the fuel ignited during my last outing on the ATV it would have no doubt injured myself and caused a forest fire.

There is a heat shield between the muffler and the fuel tank, however this isn't enough protection to ensure the tank doesn't melt.  There needs to be added protection (Helix Barrier) to the fuel tank to ensure the plastic doesn't melt.
justification: The incident describes a fuel tank melting due to heat, creating a fire hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
On December 25th wearing all the proper safety gear (helmet, knee, elbow and wrist pads) I fell and suffered a tibia and fibula fracture using a smart wheel balance hover board. My kids are afraid to use the devices because their unsafe.
I'm still paying bills because of the accident.
I would like a full refund from the company if this item has any recall.
justification: The incident resulted in a tibia and fibula fracture, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the context of the injury occurring despite proper safety gear.

incident_description:
We have a Intex pool with a non-platform ladder. 
The ladder is very unsafe. Our family and friends are constantly falling through the middle of the ladder where a platform should be. 

Intex tells me that they removed the platform to reduce injuries from jumping, however because of the ladders pool design it is almost impossible to get in and out of the pool without jumping from the ladder. 

First the top rung of the ladder is the same height as the pool, however the handles are very low. I am only 5 feet tall and it is nearly impossible for me to hang on to the handles to turn myself around to go down the ladder. I typically will fall if I try so this forces us to go down the ladder facing forward causing people to slip off a rung at some point. This encourages people to jump from the top step of the ladder to avoid slipping down the ladder and injuring themselves. 

Next the big open space and no platform causes people to unknowingly step on the pool frame while trying to turn around to go into or out of the pool. This is a huge hazard because the frame is typically wet from pool water. There are No Warnings on the pool or the ladder telling people they should avoid standing on the pools frame. When people step on the frame they slip through the center of the ladder  and onto the pool frame. 

The ladders are unstable to begin with because they do not attach too the side of the pool. Trying to balance the ladder and ones self while trying to turn around in order to enter or exit the pool is nearly impossible. 

I have video of my 9 year old daughter who climbed up the ladder and turned around only to fall through the ladder while standing at the top. 

[REDACTED]
As you can see in the video, just turning around my daughter fell through the top ladder and even after she righted herself she was forced to jump from the ladder because she couldn't keep her balance because there is no platform to stand on. 

Index told me people shouldn't stand on the top of the ladder - but that is impossible if one is to use the ladder. My children, our friends and myself have fallen through or from the ladder several times.  

The ladder needs to be recalled and replaced with a platform ladder that mounts to the side of the pool.
justification: The description details multiple incidents of falls and injuries due to the unsafe ladder design, including a child falling through the ladder.

incident_description:
2013 side by side ATV 1000 purchased at Retailer in Cave Junction, Oregon July 22nd, 2014.

He began having problems around July 2015 he noticed that the passenger who was riding with him said their seat was extremely hot and when the caller took the seat off and saw that the plastic platform that the seat slid and locked into was melted with a hole burned through the platform leaving little between the passenger and the motor.   He returned it to the place of purchase where it was repaired at their expense.

He had been riding in the woods July 27th, 2016 for approximately one half hour when the ATV burst into flames with both he and his passenger were burned before they were able to jump off. The burns are described as minor with no physician or hospital visits by either.
The caller burned his index finger and his passenger was burned on his left elbow and forearm.

The flames were around 40 to 42 inches high.

Once he and his passenger jumped off the flames went low enough that the caller pulled the engine cover off quickly so that they could begin throwing dirt on it in an effort to extinguish the flames but then the flames began getting higher again.

The fire from the side by side started a forest fire for which the caller is in danger of being charged with fire suppression 

He contacted the manufacturer Monday, August 1st, 2016 and was informed that they want to inspect the unit.

The caller agreed with this offer then contacted the forest service to be sure it wasn't disposed of once they complete their inspection.
justification: The incident resulted in minor burns to both the driver and passenger, but no medical attention was required, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) based on the specific circumstances described.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the product has a retractable telescoping handle that collapsed while the product is being used.

06/2016) The consumer stated that he was trying to roll the cooler down the ramp to his boat. The handle collapsed and the cooler fell over to the left causing the consumer to fall  over.

When the cooler is moved by holding the handle with one hand and the cooler with the other hand, the handle will twist to the side.

The consumer stated that the handle on the product cannot handle the weight of the cooler.

(06/28/2016) The consumer contacted the firm to advise them of the issue. He was advised that they know that there is a problem and that the handle was in for a re-design.
 
The consumer was assigned incident reference number-[REDACTED]

(07/2016) The consumer was advised in July that they were sending him a replacement cooler.
Per the consumer, the replacement cooler is the same as the original cooler with the same problem.


(08/01/2016) The consumer contacted the firm to advised them that he had received the cooler but it had the same problem. The consumer received a reply that the product has a warranty for one year. He was also advised that there is a one time replacement that had already been done.

No injuries.
justification: The handle collapse caused the consumer to fall, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Ultra UV unit tripped circuit break in the ground fault it was plugged into.  The unit leaked water into the chamber that houses the UV Lights and fried them.  Unit no longer works.
justification: The incident involved equipment damage (UV unit fried) but no reported injuries or fatalities.

incident_description: The Sniper STLS41 "The Scout" model tree stand consists of a ladder connecting to a platform raised some 18 feet in the air. The ladder collapsed under his weight as he was climbing the ladder for the first time during the installation process, despite the stand being rated for 500 lbs. capacity for user(s) and gear. He was caused to fall, resulting in a severe leg and ankle injury. Metallurgical testing has shown that the stand was not manufactured in compliance with WW Industrial Corp.'s carbon steel tubing specifications. In fact, the metal alloy contains no detectable level of carbon and is also deficient in manganese composition, these two elements playing the most important roles in strengthening steel. The manufacturing batch at issue is 7W-1 013. A second incident involving the collapse of another STLS41 from this same manufacturing batch has been reported to the company. There were 730 units manufactured in this batch, whereas there have been over 30,000 sold in total. Accordingly, out of 30,000-plus units sold, the only two reported collapses came from the same batch of 730. There is clearly a manufacturing defect in this batch.

incident_description:
On 2 August 2016 I purchased an EVS Sports T5 Vector Motocross Helmet size large from Rocky Mountain ATV/MC.com. I received the helmet on 5 August 2016 and tried the helmet on.  Right away I felt something was not right about the helmet there was something pushing on my neck at the spot where my spine and my skull connect.  I took the helmet off to investigate and found there was a pad made out of two ÃÂ½ inch stiff foam pads attached to the Styrofoam inside of the helmet under the lining. These pads started at the base of the helmet and were about 2 inches high. They were attached at the jaw and went around the back of the helmet and ended at the same spot on the other side. This caused an area about 1 inch deep above the pad where there was noting causing a pivot point right where my neck attaches to my spine which in case or a impact to the head could cause the spine to snap at that point. 

I put the helmet back on and tightened the chin strap down as if I were to go racing with the helmet on. I took the front of the helmet at the chin vent and pushed upward with my hand. Sure enough my head pivoted upward and back while the pad caused my neck to move forward suddenly a sharp pain shot down my neck and back and I let go of the helmet and it stopped. If I had hit something with my head and the head had been driven backwards such as a branch hanging across a trail it could have had enough impact force to go beyond the pain point to the point of snapping my neck resulting in death or serious injury!

At this point I tried to call EVS Sports and was unable to get a hold of any one so I emailed them about this issue and I contacted rocky Mountain ATV/MC by phone. Rocky Mountain had one of their techs go and get one the helmets and he found the same issue with the pad that it hit him in the back of the neck.  That had me return the helmet and exchange it for a different manufacture. I am sorry to say EVS Sports has refused to answer my replay as of now and Rocky Mountain ATV/MC is still selling the helmets.

I have raced armature and professional motorcycles and ATVÃÂs since 1975 and have worn helmets made by most major manufactures. I have used everything from helmets costing less than an hundred dollars to some costing several hundred dollars so I do know something about helmets and I currently own several older T5 helmets manufactured by EVS Sports which are of a different design. None of them have ever had anything on the inside of the helmet as unsafe as this. This need to be investigated before someone gets hurt or killed and then it is too late for that person.

I purchased an electric bicycle back in December from farbike.com. I assembled it as per manufacturer's instructions and took it to a bicycle mechanic to be certain. I took it home and attempted to charge and it started sparking, so I undid it and contacted the manufacturer. They asked for it back, so I sent it. 

Two months later, I finally get a new battery in. The new battery refuses to hold a charge, so I contacted them again, and suggested the charger might have been damaged as well. They sent me a new charger. With a new battery AND new charger, I then went to charge it overnight, as per the instructions. In the morning, I awoke to flashes of light and popping noises; the battery was sparking and jumping from the table I'd set it on. But I could not get close enough to unplug it as the sparks were too powerful. It set my couch, then my walls and entire home on fire and I lost everything. The Alamo Heights Fire Department has a report; they said if I hadn't awoken when I did I probably would not have awoken at all; the smoke and heat rising upstairs to my loft would have choked me.

We contacted the company, who passed us off to various sales reps but refused to answer our questions on liability or compensation, then passed us off to a rep in China who claimed to know nothing and has since ignored us. No refund on bike, no replacements, no compensation for thousands of dollars in damages to mine and my landlord's property. This company needs to be held accountable!

http://www.farbike.com/x-treme-x-cursion-xb-310li-folding-electric-bike
justification: The incident resulted in significant property damage and a near-fatal situation, indicating a high severity level. The repeated battery issues suggest a possible likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: On Mar 26th 2016 myself and my friend [REDACTED] were moving my Big Game Treestand, Guardian XL model ladder stand, to a better ridgetop location on my property in Bedford, VA 24523. [REDACTED] went up to unhook the ratchet strap to the stand like we have both done on multiple occasions over the last 20+ years. The stand had been in place since late Aug 14 (purchased new) when I put the stand up with another friend for my son to take his first hunt out of on VA youth day 2014. When the ratchet strap broke free for [REDACTED] I felt the stand move (I was holding the ladder section below) and I saw my friend falling head first along the tree!! Thank the Lord he rolled at the last second and landed flat on his back instead of his head. It was a miracle that he was not injured more than he was and he is alive today without permanent injuries. We want to inform as many as we can about what caused this accident. It wasn't because [REDACTED]loss his balance and fell or because he stepped off the stand's platform. It wasn't because he was careless or not watching what he was doing and fell. No, he was not wearing a safety harness at the time because the last thing we both would have thought was that the stand's structural integrity would have failed the way it did.A safety harness would have not prevented what occurred with this tree stand, When the ratchet strap broke free the whole upper platform bent inward and to the left towards the tree that it was attached to. [REDACTED] was kneeling on the foot platform leaning to the left as that was the side that the ratchet strap buckle was located. When this occurred it caused him to go upside down as he went with the platform and then he fell head first out of the stand. It all happened in a split second!!! This stand is supposed to be rated for 500 pounds I believe. The stand's structural integrity or the strength of it's metal failed for reasons unknown. I transported [REDACTED] to the Bedford Memorial Hospital ER where he was seen and treated for his injuries. He caught his leg on a small metal shelf when he fell that supports the gun rest resulting in the tearing of his jeans and causing several lacerations on his thigh. He was also having back and neck pain. Again, it was a miracle he wasn't hurt severely. It could have been me loosening that ratchet strap that day and my fall could have ended much differently that his. I'm a much bigger guy than he is. I checked on the internet for any other accidents like this but couldn't find anything. We wanted to notify the manufacturer and let them know of the accident so they could do an investigation, inspect what happened, and decide what kind of action needed to be done so this did not happen to anyone else. For all we know this could have been an isolated freak accident! I then noticed that when I looked on their website at the treestands the new model of the Guardian XL had additional support braces (see picture below taken in [REDACTED] during Apr 2016, Hampton, VA) that connected the upper platform to the ladder section. These new braces would have prevented (in my opinion) the upper platform from ever folding in, collapsing in, failing, etc like my stand did resulting in [REDACTED] fall. I told [REDACTED] while in the hospital maybe that Big Game Treestands was already aware of the issue and that's why they had added the new braces. We were both sure that they would be very interested to hear what happened to us. That same week I sent an email to Big Game Treestands ?#?BGTS? and notified them of the accident and sent pictures as posted below. I didn't hear anything for days until I got a call from a lawyer from Clarke Hill PLC out of MI. I was told that they represented Big Game Treestands, I had to recount the details of the day the accident happened and I was quizzed on my experience with putting up and taking down treestands. I guess they needed to determine my skill level to see if maybe I was at fault for this accident or I knew what the heck I was doing and talking about. I was last asked what I was looking for from Big Game Treestands and I explained that this was not a law suit waiting to happen or a get rich scheme. We ([REDACTED]and I) just wanted them to look into this so no one else got hurt from a similar accident with this model stand. If they needed to make a recall then so be it. This accident could end much differently if it happened to someone else!! I also asked that [REDACTED]'s ER bill be covered and that my treestand be replaced with one of the newer models since it was only 1.5 years old. I thought this was a simple request and really thought that a large & well known company like Big Game Treestands would look into this immediately and make things right. They already had a recall on 3 models of their climbing stands where someone had fell due to a product failure and they sure didn't need anymore bad press. This company also sponsors a lot of celebrity hunters on TV. After telling the attorney what our request was even he sounded happy and agreed it was a simple request and that he would share everything with his client. It wasn't like we were trying to sue them!!! The attorney asked for more pictures and some other information which I cooperated with immediately. I wanted this to move forward as fast as possible. Well....after 2 whole weeks I hadn't heard a word. I contacted the attorney again and he said he would get with his client and get back with me. Another whole week went by and I hadn't heard anything from the attorney or Big Game Treestands. I then emailed the attorney again along with Big Game Treestands expressing my disappointment in their lack of response. This was 3 additional weeks that someone else could have been hurt putting up or taking down one of their stands. A lot of hunters will reposition their stands in the spring before green up so the deer can get used to them and they are set for fall. I felt that it was pure negligence on their part for not responding or doing anything with the stands as more lives could have been put in danger. I expressed if I did not hear something within 48 hours that [REDACTED] and I would go public with the accident and their lack of response for their customers safety and the product liability of this treestand would no longer be a secret. Within 48 hours I received a call from the attorney stating that once again he would get with his client. I'm thinking.....hasn't he already done this or is this some tactic to stall and see if I'm serious or not?? Has he contacted them at all.....he is playing games?? I'm getting fed up!! The following day I get another call stating that Big Game Treestands is going to send a 3rd party person down to my home in VA to examine the treestand in question and possibly examine the accident location as well. This person would fly in to an airport nearest me which I told them would be Lynchburg or Roanoke. I was told I would hear something soon so everyone could coordinate. I was happy to hear this and figured finally they see that we are serious and demand something to be done for the safety of others. Well.....that call was over 2.5 months ago. I have heard nothing from anyone!! Once again I reach out to the attorney as all correspondence is supposed to go through him. I asked him for an update and I get the same old response "I'll check with my client and get back with you". And...guess what the response was?? Nada! No response at all. So...we are done with them and I am officially done with Big Game Treestands! Not once has anyone from Big Game Treestands reached out to either one of us (yes they have our contact info) to ask what happened, say sorry for the accident, let's look into this right away to see if it's a product/material failure/liability, etc!! No questions or sense of care at all for their customer or [REDACTED] who fell 15 feet due to their treestand buckling up like superman went at it. I even took one of my single man ladder stands at the house and tried bending the platform inward like what happened to this one and I could not get it to budge! There's no way this should have happened to this stand like it did and I'm not sure if it a defect in the design, bad metal from China or somewhere, heck maybe it's made in China with recycled metal from beer cans who knows anymore. So people.....please get the word out and share with your friends who hunt out of these ladder stands. Let them know of the danger so it doesn't potentially happen to them. Let them know how Big Game Treestands answers the concerns of their customers and how it cares if you get into an accident with one of their products due to product liability that is not your fault!!! I would not want them as a sponsor that's for sure. The fact is that neither [REDACTED] nor I should have ever been worried that this could have happened to us! Even if he was wearing a safety harness the accident would have still happened and the product is still to blame because it integrity failed!! I have never had a treestand accident or failure until now and I have been hunting since I was a teenager when Baker climbing stands were popular and yes I owned one. People know that I have been hunting for many years and can contest that I know what I am doing and I am very safety conscious. [REDACTED] and I had a sense of trust in these ladder stands because of using them over the years with no issues or concerns. They give you a different sense of safety and trust that you don't get from a climbing stand, a hang on stand, or a fixed stand made from lumber. That trust is gone and my buddy now has a fear of them that he didn't have before. You just don't realize how this affects you mentally, emotionally, physically, or how it affects your family members who love you! We had just moved another ladder stand that same day before the accident occurred and I was the one that went up and unhooked it. It could have been me that fell from this stand....whether that day or the next time I decided to move it. We don't want this to happen to anyone else and since Big Game Treestands nor their attorneys want you to know we are sharing it ourselves now. If you have any questions please reach out to me. Again, I encourage you to share and educate fellow hunters. Doesn't it make you curious why now all of a sudden they have those new support braces?? I wouldn't buy one without them that's for sure. If they knew of this potential issue and didn't alert their customers then shame on them! They should be sued!! I thank God for watching after my friend [REDACTED] that day (the day before Easter too). Because of his mercy we can both share what happened with others.
justification: The incident resulted in lacerations and back/neck pain, indicating an injury but no death.

incident_description:
While riding Polaris Sportsman 500 down a steep descent, the machine suddenly experienced total brake failure.  This ATV is equipped with both a hand actuated brake which operates both front and rear brakes along with a foot actuated brake that operates rear brakes.  This machine was well maintained and both systems were checked and fully functional before vehicle was operated.  This machine is EXTREMELY DANGEROUS due to several design flaws including:

1- The machine has an automatic (CVT) transmission that does not have engine brakes and cannot be shifted or slowed by utilizing the engine or transmission; i.e. the brakes are the only way to stop or even slow this machine.

2- A single point of failure resulted in complete brake loss.  The hand brake has a completely separate brake fluid reservoir from the foot brake and both have separate hydraulic lines feeding the brakes.  However due to design flaws in this system, a single failure resulted in both the hand and foot brakes failing at the same time.

3- ATVs are designed to be ridden off-road in varied and sometimes steep terrain.  The design of this vehicle does not include any system redundancy to prevent catastrophic brake failure.  The failure of a single component resulted in an EXTREMELY DANGEROUS situation and complete inability to stop or even slow a 500 lb.+ ATV.

The design flaws inherent in this machine nearly cost me my life. I hope this information prevents this machine costing others their own.
justification: The incident describes a near-fatal situation due to design flaws leading to total brake failure on a steep descent, indicating high severity and likelihood of recurrence without intervention.

incident_description:
The "Airhead Revolution," by Kwik Tek, Inc., is an inflatable tube intended to be towed by a recreational boat. It is designed for 2 riders to be spinning 360' as it moves along. The spinning action of the Airhead Revolution is made possible because the tow rope anchor point is located at the direct center of the underside of the tube.  
    The inherent problem with this design is that as the riders are spinning 360' revolutions, they can be thrown in any of the 360' directions, including forward toward the back of the boat. When thrown forward toward the back of the boat, the rider can land on the rope while simultaneously hitting the water, and as the body stops upon hitting the water, the boat continues to pull the tube forward. The body part landing on the rope is then caused to be wedged between the rope and underside of the tube as the tube continues to move forward behind the boat.  With another rider on the tube while this happens, the combination of the remaining riders weight causes the ensnared body part to be become ever more wedged as the space between the rope and the underside of the tube narrows toward the anchor point. This results in the rope acting like a band saw, slicing through the flesh of the ensnared body part as this space narrows toward the anchor point. It also causes the ensnared person to be pinned underwater. 
    This very scenario occurred on August 23, 2015, when a 13 year old girl was using the Airhead Revolution. While spinning, she was thrown off the tube forward and toward the back of the boat. Her left leg landed on the rope, while the rest of her body landed in the water. Her body stopped and the tube, with the remaining rider still on it, continued to move forward. As her ensnared leg was wedged and pinched ever more toward the center anchor point, the rope acted like a band saw slicing through the back of her leg, down to the bone.  Now pinned between the underside of the tube and the tow rope, which had physically penetrating her leg, she was ensnared, unable to free herself, and submerged underwater. The boat then stopped and her mother was able to dive to her, bring her head to the surface before she drowned, and hold her until the rope was cut so she could be freed. The 13 year old girl sustained a devastating and permanent leg injury. 
     Another very similar incident to this has occurred and can be found on [REDACTED] "Reviews" of the Airhead Revolution.
justification: The incident resulted in a devastating and permanent leg injury to a 13-year-old girl, and another similar incident was reported.

Product is a Ninebot Model P purchased from Ninebot US.   The Ninebot P electric unicycle was released in November of last year.  Only one shimpment was released in the US as it was immediately pulled from further delivery and US pre-orders were canceled.  This was a national, as well as international product "pull" from the mfg, Ninebot Inc.  

All US distributors were notified that no further shipments would be received.   NO reason was provided but is was so sudden and without warning.  To cancel a product with significant demand and pre-orders and at Christmas time was a red flag to us owners.  

Immediately, upon receipt of the first shipment deliveries, customers begin complaining that the Ninebot Model P was halting unexpectedly and without warning and the motor would lock up or free spin.  This is easily searchable online in electric unicycle forums.   

I received my Ninebot P in November 2015. After hearing about the issues other owners were experiencing,  I rode with caution and sure enough, experienced a motor/mother board failure while riding in a busy city street.  The Ninebot Model P began to stall and I was able to jump off and stumble a bit with no injury.   The Model P was dead in the water. 

This is an incredibly dangerous scenario as the Ninebot P travels at nearly 20 MPH , and in a street scenario, could cause serious injury, including death should the rider be thrown into moving traffic or pedestrian due to a product failure.  

I believe Ninebot Inc is avoiding a recall and any liability due to consumer safety.   I did send in my Ninebot P and requested a refund within the warranty period but it was rejected due to "no mfg recall exit".    It has been repaired with existing model parts so I am certain it will fail again as most owners have experienced.
justification: The incident involved a motor/motherboard failure causing the unicycle to stall, but the rider was able to jump off without injury. However, the potential for serious injury or death is high given the speed and urban riding conditions.

incident_description:
I purchased a Seachoice Products Anchor Lead Chain, model 44101.  This is a 48" x 3/16" galvanized chain with two 1/4" galvanized shackles.  Both shackles are defective, and of such a defective level of quality that I now suspect whether the chain is any good at all.  In any case, I would not trust my life or the life of my family to such shoddy products.

Here's the problem: the "pin", which is much like a bolt, is threaded on one end.  It goes through one "lug" of the horseshoe shaped shackle, and should engage the threads of the other "lug" of the shackle, where it can be tightened securely.  On these shackles, the machining is so poor that the pins merely spin in the threaded lug and do not engage.  These shackles are fit for decoration only-but only if one were to "glue" the pin in place.

This is a MAJOR safety issue, as the intended use of the shackle is to connect an anchor line (usually nylon) to an anchor.  The anchor is one of the primary safety devices on board any vessel.

PLEASE LET THE PUBLIC KNOW ABOUT THIS JUNK.

Thanks.
justification: The defective shackles pose a major safety risk for anchoring, which could lead to incidents, but no injury or death is reported.
