justification: The fire caused $250,000 damage and killed two dogs, which is a significant incident with a high level of damage.

incident_description: I purchased a Barnett Jackal Crossbow in 2012.  On October 1, 2015 the crossbow inadvertently discharge when I was lifting it and the crossbow string amputated my left thumb.  There are no finger guards on this crossbow.  I had to go to medical emergency to have the thumb reattached.
justification: The incident resulted in a serious injury requiring medical emergency, but the likelihood of such an event is unlikely given the specific circumstances described.

incident_description: I have Zipp 303s on my road bike. I purchased them in 2009 or 2010 (not sure). I was riding my bike and I heard a loud crack and then my rear tire just locked up. When I looked down I saw that my rear hub had broken and the spokes were blown out.
justification: The incident involved equipment failure (rear hub breaking and spokes blowing out) but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
I purchased a ForTech Two Wheels Mini Smart Self Balancing Scooter through Amazon seller [REDACTED] for my daughter for Christmas.  On 1/21/16, my daughter plugged the scooter in to charge around 4:15 PM.  At about 5:25 PM, the scooter/battery exploded and caused a fire in our home.  Fortunately, we were home at the time (2 adults and 5 children) and the fire was contained to one room in the house and there were no injuries, however this product needs to be recalled for safety.  We have an estimated $7000 in damages as a result.  
I've reached out to Amazon and have been in email contact with [REDACTED].  I was told that we are the first people to contact them at [REDACTED] stating we had a fire as a result of the scooter.   My insurance company is now working with them directly.  

There were no injuries to anyone as the scooter was in a home office at the time, but the battery explosion was intense.... it blew from the bottom of the scooter and shot out pieces of the battery all over the room - causing damage 10 feet from where it was plugged in.
justification: The scooter exploded causing a fire and significant property damage, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: My father, who is now deceased, purchased a Barnett Quad 400 crossbow on November 10, 2012 at Dunham's.  On September 23, 2014, he took it out to his backyard to shoot at a target.  When he pulled the trigger, the crossbow fired and inadvertently contacted his thumb, partially amputating it.  The string cut through his flesh and bone, with only a small piece of flesh holding the thumb onto his hand.  He was taken to the emergency room, where he waited for a hand surgeon to arrive to perform surgery to reattach his thumb.  He was kept overnight, and released the next day on September 24, 2014.
justification: The incident resulted in a partial amputation of the thumb, requiring surgery and hospitalization, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). Crossbow accidents leading to such injuries are uncommon but possible (likelihood 3).

incident_description: Used a Barnett Crossbow Wildcat C5 and it took my thumb nail off & broke the bone on the end of my thumb. Barnett does not have a hand guard like other bows.
justification: The description indicates an injury involving the loss of a thumb nail and a broken bone, which qualifies as a severity level 3.

incident_description: The exercise equipment is07x broke and the springs inside flew out and smacked me on the face.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (being smacked on the face by flying springs), but such occurrences are unlikely if equipment is properly maintained.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting an Inversion Table purchased through retailer online January 2010.

There were no problems with the table until December 17th, 2015 when her husband was using it and the metal that holds it together to allow inversion or to right oneself back to standing position broke sending the caller's husband to the floor.

He hit his head and shoulder but was saved from more serious injury due to the pillow used being higher and the table hitting the floor first.

She did contact the manufacturer around January 1st, 2016 and they responded with a resolution to provide the caller with money to purchase another inversion table.

The caller's responded that they would accept that offer if there was a recall generated and the public be made aware of the safety hazard with this table.

The caller and his wife have treated his injuries themselves, not physician has been seen.

The submitter added the company did not respond after they requested that they [the mfr] report to CPSC, and no resolution has been reached.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (hit head and shoulder) but no medical attention was sought, and no death occurred.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting his 2009 snow mobile recalled with release# 10-705 for fire hazard.

He purchased this snow mobile in January 2014 from Spicer's Boat City in Michigan and had only one issue when the clutch burned up during the first 200 miles of use.  This was repaired.

January 10th, 2016 the caller had been riding for approximately one hour when while riding in Sugar Springs, Michigan he noticed that he was low on fuel so he went to station and refilled his fuel.

About fifteen minutes after leaving the gas station the snow mobile stalled at approximately 50 mph and he looked down to see flames coming up between his legs which caused him to pull over and began packing the area with snow to extinguish the flames.

A passerby came with a shovel and then a fire extinguisher but they still couldn't put the fire out.

There was some smoke inhalation but caller states that he is fine and that there are no injuries being reported.

He contacted the manufacturer January 11th, 2015 and he was advised that the legal department would be in touch with him.

He is waiting for their call.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard with smoke inhalation but no reported injuries, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) given the recall and past clutch issue.

incident_description:
The consumer said he purchased the ATV used from another person. The ATV had about 2,630 miles. The ATV was recalled (recall # 12-709) and received the recall remedy. 

(1/18/16) The consumer had poured gasoline in the fuel tank. The consumer noticed a gasoline odor and upon inspecting the ATV the consumer noticed the fuel tank had a hole and there was gasoline on the ground. 

The consumer believes the fuel tank has inadequate protection from the exhaust. The consumer believes the hot exhaust melts a hole in the plastic fuel tank. The consumer believes the ATV poses a fire hazard and should be recalled for this safety hazard. 

The consumer has noticed complaints online about this issue with similar ATV's. The consumer plans to contact the firm about assistance with repairs. 

(9/15/15 approximately) The consumer states the last time he used the ATV he noticed a gasoline odor while riding. The consumer thought the odor was due to pressure in the fuel tank.
justification: The incident involved a fuel tank leak and gasoline odor, but no injury or fire occurred. Similar complaints online suggest this issue is possible but not certain.

incident_description: Purchased a IMOTO HK Hooverboard http://www.imotohk.com/ for Christmas present.  Board failed to properly charge and and charger emitted noise.  Company has  failed to answer calls, emails or return correspondence.
justification: The incident involves a product malfunction and poor customer service, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Diver drowned while scuba diving after spring failed in secondary oral inflation device, Air Source 2, manufactured by Aqua Lung America. Spring failure prevented buoyancy compensation device ("BCD") to provide adequate buoyancy for diver resulting in drowning and death of diver.
justification: The incident resulted in the death of a diver due to equipment failure.

incident_description: On December 20, 2015 my 9 year old child injured herself on a backyard toy that I had purchased from HearthSong.com, a Virginia based retailer.  The product is called the Wonder Wave and can be viewed on hearthsong.com and also on amazon.com at http://www.amazon.com/HearthSong%C2%AE-Wonder-Wave/dp/B016N0JSW6. The toy is a large outdoor toy that ÃÂcan be used as a chair, rocker, hammock, balancing walk activityÃÂ and can fit up to four kids.  HearthSong.com.  My daughter was on the Wonder Wave with one other child.  The motion of the toy caused her fall face-first into the metal frame of the toy.  The impact sheered off her two front teeth.  Photos are available. The teeth were her permanent adult teeth. The damage appears similar to when an ice hockey player gets hit in the mouth with a puck.  The teeth shattered.  She has dental repair work done and now has two ÃÂfakeÃÂ teeth. It was traumatic for all involved, and she will face further dental issues as she matures.  The design of the toy is inherently dangerous.  Shortly after the injury, I asked the company to stop selling the product to children because more children will be hurt. Specifically, the metal bar will certainly hit another child in the face.  The bar has no padding.  Since then, on the Amazon.com website, there have been multiple complaints of injury. There have been parents saying the toy has caused ÃÂfour stiches,ÃÂ  ÃÂhands and feet pinched and smashed in this guillotine-teeter totter,ÃÂ itÃÂs an ÃÂaccident waiting to happen,ÃÂ resulted in a ÃÂtrip to the ERÃÂ, and waiting for ÃÂfirst tooth to get knocked out.ÃÂ  Please help me remove this dangerous toy from the market.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe injury (shattered permanent teeth requiring dental repair), which falls under severity level 3. The occurrence likelihood is high (4) due to multiple reported injuries and complaints about the toy's design.

incident_description:
(10/2015) The consumer stated that he was riding the ATV for about 8 hours. He smelled gas. He looked around and saw that the gas tank was soaked with gasoline. He took off the seat and noticed that the exhaust had melted the plastic gas tank. The exhaust pipe and the heat shield is a quarter inch from the gas tank.

The consumer stated that this is design flaw. The consumer stated that he saw on line where others are having the same issue.

(12/9/2015)The consumer contacted the firm to advised them of the issue. He was advised to take the product to a dealership to see if they if the dealership would pay for the repair.

(12/2015) The consumer took the ATV to Gainesville Motorsports. He was advised that the gas tank had been melted by the exhaust. The company opened a case and sent the information to BRP.

BRP advised the dealership that they would not repair the ATV because it was out of warranty.

The consumer advised BRP that he was not trying to get a warranty but was trying to report a safety hazard.

(12/9/2015)The firm took a report but advised the consumer on 12/14/15 that the ATV was out of warranty.

After speaking to the firm multiple times about the issue, the consumer received an email on 12/24 advising him again that the ATV was out of warranty.
justification: The incident involved a design flaw leading to a melted gas tank, posing a safety hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: Purchased two Hoverboards from Swagway.com as Christmas presents for my 13 year old twin boys. They were defective right out of the box shaking violently and throwing one son for a nasty spill. Injuries were minor causing bruising.
justification: The incident resulted in minor injuries (bruising) to one son, warranting a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is set to 4 (likely) as the product was defective right out of the box, indicating a probable issue.

incident_description:
I am 50 years old and have been hunting my entire life.  On 11/19/2012,  I purchased a Barnett Jackal crossbow at Academy Sports.  On 10/16/2015 I returned home from a hunting trip and was in the process of dislodging the arrow into the ground; unknowingly I had my right thumb above the fore end (flight track).  The string nearly severed my thumb and broke the bone in several small pieces at the knuckle.  

I had to have surgery to re-attach my finger at the knuckle.  A pin was put into place to align my finger.  I also had to wear a prothesis to prevent further injury during my recovery period.  I missed 8 weeks of work due to my injury, and my medical bills totalled $23,000.00.

I consider myself to be more safety conscious than most.  Up until 10/16/2015, I have dislodged my arrows numerous times in the past successfully.  I was fully aware of the injury potential if my fingers were above the flight track when an arrow was dislodged.  With that being said, as much as I hunt, dislodging my arrow became routine, whether it was from shooting at a deer, dislodging the arrow into the ground while practicing target shooting or from an unsuccessful hunt.  

The bottom line is this; if Barnett had installed finger guards on the Jackal crossbow, it is 100% certain my injury, nor the injury of many others, would have ever occurred, period.  Barnett left open room for error when they designed the Jackal with no finger guards in place.  I have been told the Jackal Crossbow is NOW being manufactured with finger guards.  The "fix" came a little too late for me.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe injury requiring surgery and prolonged recovery, but the likelihood is possible given the routine nature of the activity and the lack of finger guards.

incident_description:
I purchased CAP BARBELL Weight Bench Combo with 100 lbs of weight from Walmart. The Model No is: FMS-CS100P.  Serial No is : ZJHS2015/08.
There were few parts defective and the customer service sent replacements.   The following part numbers are for assembly of the weight bar which can hold 100 (One Hundred) pounds and the replacements were defective too.
The manual says not to use the product if the pins do not go all the way in or are loose. First time, the pins were loose. 2nd time, one pin went in and one did not.
This is the very last step in the assembly and I  do not have time to disassemble the whole product and return it back.
1) PFMS80-34 :  Roll Pin  ,  Qty 2
2) PFMS80WA-19  : Inner Bar  , Qty 1
3) PFMS80WA-18  : Outer Bar  , Qty 1

The customer service refuses to send any more replacements or correct the situation.

The weight bar should be a solid bar since this is a safety hazard to have a joined rod without proper design.

I urge you to ask CAP BARBELL to recall their weight bar from this set and replace with solid bars to avoid any injuries and assembly hassles.
justification: The defective parts pose a potential safety hazard, but no actual injury or incident has been reported yet.

incident_description:
Product recall was for fork on road bicycle. Fork failed where the steerer tube interfaces with the steel sleeve that is attached to the fork crown. Resulted in facial lacerations, concussion and broken hand (requiring treatment with surgery).

There is an existing recall that I was unaware of; I'm afraid I may not be the only one: 

Recall date: DECEMBER 18, 2012 Recall number: 13-075
justification: The incident resulted in facial lacerations, concussion, and a broken hand requiring surgery, indicating a severity level of 3. The mention of an existing recall suggests the issue is likely to occur again.

incident_description: During a Hockey Game My son was wearing hie Bauer NME10 goalie helmet and he took a hard shot to the protective face cage. To our surprise the cage had a crack through it and my son was in danger of and injury due to the metal cutting his face. Although he did not get hurt i am very disappointed with this manufactures product . After research i come to find others were injured due to this defect. I would hope the manufacture would do a better job of notifying the public about this. I would hope they would test their product better in the future.
justification: The incident involved a cracked helmet cage posing a danger, but no injury occurred. Research indicates others have been injured, suggesting a possible likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: I purchased a Barnett Jackal cross bow for deer hunting. Due to the way the fire stock is built, the shooters thumb rides above the path of the arrow string. While shooting this bow my thumb was caught by the string and cut my thumb half way off requiring medical attention to sew it back on. I have lost feeling in this thumb. I wanted to report to keep other hunters from experiencing what I have had to go through.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe injury requiring medical attention and permanent loss of feeling in the thumb, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is set to 3 (possible) as the description suggests a design flaw that could affect other users under similar conditions.

incident_description: Sat on the swing and within a few minutes it all fell forward, stand and all, pushing me to the ground flat on my stomach, while body flat and  face in the hard ground. The  the hook end of the stand and weight all landed on my left shoulder blade. Extreme pain though out  shoulder blade and down left arm that I was hoping would subside by now. It hasn't and I just had an MRI and X-rays last week.  Still awaiting results. Pain goes from shoulder blade to hand. The only reason I did not go to the ER because I know there is not much that can be done for a cracked shoulder blade. The pain was and still is horrible. I was not even swinging. Just sitting. The base of this is dangerous and had I been shorter I would have hit on my neck lor head. The weight could have caused spinal cord broken neck or brain injury or death. I am lucky it landed piercing my shoulder blade. I'm quite sure this swing has caused severe injury to others and likely death. My pain is constant. It does not subsid
justification: The incident resulted in severe pain and potential injury to the shoulder blade and arm, requiring medical evaluation with MRI and X-rays.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that on 12/24/15 she used the ATV for about 25 minutes. The consumer parked the ATV in her garage after use. The consumer went out and came back into the garage within 15-20 minutes. She noticed gray smoke being emitted from around the headlight area. The consumer also noticed 1-2in high flames coming out of the same area. The consumer also smelled electrical burning odor.

The consumer took out the key from the ATV. She removed the panel from below the headlight area and removed the ECM. The flames went away immediately.

The consumer also took out the battery. The consumer stated that some of the wires around and coming out of the ECM have charred and melted. The receptacle where the ECM unit plugs into is also charred.

In the past, the consumer has had problems with the battery draining quickly. The consumer was replacing batteries at least 4 times per year. They had 6 incidents since owning the ATV where the battery overheated causing the outside plastic of the battery to melt.  They had to replace the batteries.

The consumer contacted the firm regarding this issue. The consumer was notified that her vehicle is not under any recalls. They informed her to take it to a dealer to get the vehicle diagnosed. They did not provide any guarantee of reimbursement for the cost.

The consumer attempted to contact few dealers in her area. The consumer is having difficulty with the shops being closed due to holidays.

The consumer stated that if her vehicle is not under any recalls, then it needs to be considered for a recall because it has the same fire hazard as the ones being recalled.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke from the ATV, but no injury or death occurred. The recurring battery issues and multiple past incidents suggest a likely recurrence.

incident_description: This is a Pro Form Ellipticycle  Model PFEL70909.0, serial number AA930G16922.  This cycle has moveable arms that move in concert with the feet pedals.  There are bolts that connect the arms to the unit.  These bolts are listed as 5/16"x78mm Shoulder Patch Screw and there are four on the unit - two on each arm.  It is identified in the User Manual as Part #71.  The ellipticycle in questions is about 5 years old, and the above referenced bolt sheared off, causing injury to my wife who was using it at the time when the arm collapsed and she fell against the machine.  The bolt is clearly not made of proper material as it was not able to withstand the application.  The ellipticycle is not used more than once or twice a week, and my wife weights only 140 lbs so the issue is not overweight.  These units should be recalled and all four of these bolts should be replaced to avoid potentially serious injury when they fail.
justification: The incident resulted in injury when the bolt sheared off, causing the arm to collapse and the user to fall against the machine.

incident_description:
(10/23/14) The consumer was using the crossbow to hunt. When the consumer was unloading the crossbow, he put his left thumb above the string and when he squeezed the trigger the string cut the tip of his left thumb. The consumer states the cut was near the knuckle and his nail fell off. The consumer was taken to the emergency room at Lehigh Valley Hospital, located at 2545 Schoenersville Rd, Bethlehem, PA 18017. The consumer required stitches. 

The consumer did not contact the firm and does not plan to.

The consumer noticed online other complaints of similar incidents with similar cross bows. The consumer also noticed the newer cross bows that the firm sells have a finger protection safety mechanism. The consumer states his crossbow did not have this safety mechanism. The consumer believes the cross bows without this safety mechanism are unsafe and should be recalled.
justification: The consumer suffered a significant injury requiring emergency room treatment and stitches, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is set to 4 (likely) due to multiple similar complaints and the absence of a safety mechanism in older models.

incident_description:
4mos. after purchase date treadmill shuts down unexpectedly, suddenly loses all power without warning, it has thrown me off, cause my neck and back to jerk really hard, causing pain and swelling. 
The very last time I used it I could smell a burning scent coming from underneath, I have left it unplugged since that date 12-26-15, I notified Landice repeatedly starting 9-30-14 thru 1-21-16, I have asked three times of them to pick up the treadmill and issue me a refund, they have refuse each time.  I told them I had me a refund, they have refused each time.  I told them I had not been able to use this product as intended because it is dangerous as I had neck and back surgery Feb/2007, the treadmill was recommended by my doctor, but it continues to lose power and is a health risk to me and a possible fire hazard. I notified Landice and explain my concern; he told me he would not issue a refund.
justification: The treadmill caused neck and back pain and swelling due to sudden power loss, and the burning scent indicates a recurring hazard.

incident_description: I have a 2014 Polaris ranger 800 crew vin is [REDACTED].  It has power steering that stops working randomly resulting in a near miss accident with a tree.  It is a known problem with other models of Polaris ranger.
justification: Power steering failure led to a near miss accident, indicating an incident with no injury but potential for harm.

incident_description:
was shooting Barnett Ghost 400 crossbow and string hit my left thumb. Thumb was severely injured. Cut almost completely off. Very small amount of skin and tissue holding thumb on. Was
told at the emergency room that they could not repair it. Was given the option to fold skin over it
and call it an amputation. I opted to be taken to a larger hospital system where they found a hand surgeon who said he would attempt to save it. After two surgeries, steel pins etc. they were able to
save my thumb. Since then it has been almost five months of terrible pain and and life changes 
that no one else should have to go through. I had to sell my construction company of thirty years because I could no longer do that type of work. Also I can not work outside and expose my thumb to the cold.
This could all have been prevented with just a simple safety guard on the forearm of the crossbow
preventing anyone from letting their fingers or thumbs from getting into the travel path of the string. Some manufacturers have these guards and some do not. It needs to be a requirement on all crossbows before more people have this same accident. Especially before it happens to a child.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe injury to the thumb, requiring multiple surgeries and leading to significant life changes, but no death occurred.

incident_description: I have a 2013 can am commander that had the steering completely fail while I was driving it, the steering column where it fits into the steering rack is totally stripped out and the steering wheel spins freely with no movement at the steering rack. This seems like a problem that was in a recall for 2011 and 2012 models, but is apparently not covered with my 2013 model. This repair is estimated to be over $650.
justification: Steering failure while driving is a serious incident but no injury was reported, fitting severity level 2. The issue is known from recalls in similar models, indicating a possible occurrence likelihood.

incident_description: Our Swagway Hoverboard stopped working while I was riding on it causing me to fall and hurt my back.  I have already sent this back once right after purchasing it to be repaired.  This product is unsafe to ride and also for its Lithium battery fire issues.
justification: The hoverboard malfunction caused a fall resulting in a back injury, and the product has a history of issues including battery fires.

incident_description: I have a Polaris Sportsman 500 2004.5 and the ECM went bad on it and there is a recall because these can start fires. I looked up the recall on them and my Vin number was just out of range even though the ECM  is the same one that is the problem. Polaris refuses to do anything about it. The ECM is bad and could have started a fire they need to cover any 4wheeler that has this ECM on it not just ones they have picked!
justification: The ECM is known to potentially cause fires, but no actual incident or injury is reported in the description.

incident_description:
Purchased from Airsplat.com a "BOLT BRSS SOPMOD CQB Airsoft Rifle Tan" at the end of September as a Christmas present.  Also purchased a Ni-MH 9.6V battery for the airsoft gun.  Upon opening the gun at Christmas and putting in the charged battery, the gun would not engage (gears turn) and became very hot at the handle area where held.  It was so hot that you could not continue to hold the gun.  

Bolt advised us to purchase a different battery, 11.1V 15C Li-Po battery, and this was charged, and then placed into the gun.  This was tried on 1/30/16.  The gun started to smoke and became very hot, burning slightly the hand when holding the gun.  The malfunction of the gun is causing the batteries to overload and almost catch on fire.

The seller of the gun will not take the gun back nor refund the money since they say it is over their 60 day purchase time.  I have explained that the gun becomes hot and was defective out of the box.  I have also notified Bolt that the gun is defective out of the box.
justification: The gun malfunction caused overheating and slight burns, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description: I put my RZR on the trailer and put it in park got out and walked around front to lower my tilt trailer and it jumped out of park and rolled down hill over railing and almost squashed me against my truck.
justification: The RZR rolled downhill and almost squashed the person, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: While shooting a Barnett Crossbow (Predator), my thumb was struck with the bow cable causing a severe laceration and broken bone which required me to get 11 stitches, miss 6 weeks of work, physical rehab and it is still  and may never be the same. Numbness, tingling and pain persist along with drastically reduced range of motion. All could have been prevented with proper guarding!!!
justification: The incident resulted in a severe laceration, broken bone, and long-term effects, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the context of improper guarding.

incident_description: Hover-board batteries apparently overheated and caught fire.
justification: The incident involved hover-board batteries overheating and catching fire, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: My three year old was riding his [REDACTED].  He had a helmet on and somehow the helmet got pushed off the top of his head and around to the back.  The clasp was still connected and the pressure from the chin strap was choking him.  Luckily my 5 year old recognized the distress and brought him to me as I was in a different area.  My wife is from [REDACTED] and she wanted me to file this report.  In Sweden they are required to have pressure release clasps on children's bike helmets.  She hopes that by filing this report that maybe the US will follow that thinking.
justification: The child was choking due to the helmet strap, which is a serious incident that could have led to injury or worse if not for the quick action of the sibling.

incident_description:
The people at Pier One told me that I didn't need the stand that we could hang the swing without it.
We hung the swing from the patio.  August 11,2014 I sat in the swing and it fell to the patio.  I shattered My L-1 and fractured my L-2.  I had surgery August 22, 2014 In Houston TX.  My doctor had to drill into my hip for bone marrow so he could do a bone graph on my spine.
justification: The incident resulted in severe injuries (shattered L-1 and fractured L-2) requiring surgery, indicating a high severity level.

incident_description: I was target shooting my Barnett Predator crossbow using a sawhorse as support. I was sighting through the red dot scope trying to acquire the target while holding the forearm of the crossbow with my left hand. Unable to hold steady, I rotated my left hand clockwise to where I was holding the forearm in my left fingers. As I rotated my left hand, my left thumb rotated up above the string rail and into the path of the string. I was unaware of this as I was still looking through the red dot scope towards the target. When I pulled the trigger, the string struck the back of my thumb. The impact exploded my thumbnail, cut off about 1/2 inch of my left thumb, and shattered the bone in my thumb. The Barnett Predator was purchased in 2011 and has no handguards in place. A proper handguard would have prevented my thumb from getting above the rail and into the path of the string.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe injury involving the loss of part of the thumb and bone damage, warranting a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the specific circumstances described.

incident_description:
I bought a bike for my grandson at Walmart. It is a Kent Model # 52090 . While trying to brake, the brake handle snapped off.I have notified Kent Company for a replacement handle. My concern is the handle is made of cheap plastic and will break again. There is no pedal brake on this model and only handle brakes. 
There phone number is 1-800-457-5368. And the claim numver is [REDACTED] 
I have a picture of the defective part.
justification: The brake handle snapped off, but there was no injury reported.

incident_description:
The hinge of the Kiddieland Toys Limited Scooter got stuck and when my 5 year old tried to release it he fell over and the front wheel snapped off. I was able to release the hinge but the scooter is not usable.
We would like the replacement part for the wheel.
justification: The child fell but there was no mention of injury, only damage to the scooter.

incident_description:
While on vacation, we took our 5 year old son swimming in the pool.  He was wearing a pair of toddler Superman swim trunks purchased at Old Navy in Colorado in 2015.  When we returned to our hotel room to change, he began screaming in pain.  

The interior front lining of the swimsuit was made of a mesh material with small holes.  When he tried to remove the swim trunks, the skin from his penis became stuck in the small holes, strangulating it.  We tried for an hour to remove the suit by cutting it off with scissors with no success.  The pain he suffered was unbearable.  We finally requested the hotel to call the paramedics.  By the time the paramedics arrived, my son was relaxed enough that his penis somehow became disentangled.  He suffered abrasions as a result and was sore, but was luckily physically ok.  He did not want to swim again; however, we found other swimsuits that had mesh lining with no small holes.
justification: The child suffered abrasions and pain, indicating an injury, but no long-term physical harm occurred.

incident_description: Leadpo 6.5 Smart Drifting Scooter - as person attempted to step off the device it unexpectedly moved causing her to fall
justification: The person fell when the scooter unexpectedly moved, which typically results in injury.

incident_description:
I was riding my new "MaxiZum" electrically motor-driven "scooter" (with 26" wheels, more properly a footbike or kickbike) westbound in a Class II bike lane when I had to merge into the main traffic lane at a point where the road narrowed to allow for reconstruction of a mid-block crosswalk near our main fire station.

It was the Thanksgiving holiday weekend, so no work was in progress. Thee excavation was covered by a smooth steel plate and the transition from the existing pavement to the plate was eased by a gentle, shallow, smooth graded asphalt ramp with no lumps, bumps, gaps or irregularities.

The line of traffic was moving very slowly and I had plenty of time to observe the construction work as I approached.  With nearly 60 years of cautious and safe cycling experience, and the knowledge that the footbike had an advertised ground clearance of 4 inches, I judged that the very minor elevation change was perfectly safe to ride over at a slow speed. I was wrong.

As my front wheel mounted the incline, two tube ends projecting below the floor frame of the footbike grazed and dug into the asphalt, bringing the MaxiZum to a sudden halt and slightly lifting the rear wheel from the ground and causing it to rotate, airborne, to the right, around the axis of the bike's headset.  I was able to quickly step/jump off to the right and prevent myself from falling all the way to the ground, although my right knee did collapse, resulting in a strained/sprained medial collateral ligament, which is still a bit sore.  following traffic, also moving slowly, was able to stop without hitting me, and I dragged myself and the scooter/footbike off to the side of the road. Not a catastrophe, but it certainly would likely have been if I and/or following traffic had been traveling faster.

When I got home, I put the footbike on a bench, removed the footboard, and inspected the (minor) damage to the tubes that had contacted the pavement.  With the footboard removed, I was also able to measure the actual ground clearance of the device.  As can be seen in the photos I took (if I can find a way to share them with you), the tubes that struck the asphalt provides less than 3" of clearance.  Further, a travel-limit tab on the center kickstand measured about 2 5/8 " ground clearance, but it also shows signs of having struck the pavement (perhaps when the airborne rear wheel came bouncing and sliding back to Earth), so it's quite likely that the original clearance there was even less.

The close examination I was able to do on the bench made it clear that it is not only ground clearance per se that makes this motorized (to approx. 20 mph) device unsafe to operate on US streets and paths with the usual bumps, uneven pavement, projections, etc.  The very design and geometry of the frame makes it dangerous, as well.  The near-90-degree junction of the vertical tube cluster with the floor frame, combined with tube ends and other projections *below* that frame, means that almost any contact with an irregularity or projection from the surface will be, effectively, a "head-on" crash.  With no leading curve or angle, and with the afore-mentioned projections below the frame, and with no skid plate, there is almost no chance that the footbike would be able ride/slide over even the slightest obstacle.

When I contacted the manufacturer, he (trying to prevent me from filing this report, no doubt) promised a detailed written response within a few days.  He then said he was going to Israel for a couple of weeks but would try to write when he was there. From Israel (presumably) he told me he had been busy, but would try to write "soon."  When he returned from Israel, he again promised a letter in a few days, which started and email exchange in which he arrogantly assured me that the problem is with my expectations, not with his product.

Full disclosure: While waiting for resolution of this issue, I raised it in an online forum for scooter enthusiasts, without identifying the brand or model of the product (it turns out that some of the members of the forum, including the forum operator, are friends/customers of the manufacturer, so they probably knew which product I was talking about).  Virtually every response I got was, more or less "That's just how kick scooters are; you have to be constantly alert and ready to stop and dismount at the sight of any obstacle."  I tried to explain that is an unreasonable position to take when talking about a 20 mph motorized footbike, as big as a full-sized bicycle, that is advertised for use on the streets and will likely encounter minor obstacles frequently, and often be surrounded by auto traffic.  They just kept repeating themselves.

In the intervening period, I have test-ridden electric footbikes that have none of the inherent defects of the MaxiZum.  They have more than twice the ground clearance.  They have curved/angled junctions between the vertical members and the floor frame.  They have no projections below the floor frame.  They have skid plates.  They would have been ridden safely over the little construction rise that threw me from the MaxiZum without even noticing it.

Today, I contacted the seller.  He told me what the manufacturer and the forum members told me: that's just the way kick scooters are.

But, no matter how often they call it that, the MaxiZum is NOT a "kick scooter" -- it's a motorized, full-sized footbike.

I appear to be the only person who thinks the device is inherently dangerously flawed, so you may be tempted to just let this go.  Or you may simply not be able to investigate such a "minor" matter.  However, I am quite certain of this:

If very many people ride very many MaxiZum powered footbikes over very many miles of ordinary American roads and trails, there will be serious injuries and, probably, deaths.  How many will simply be a matter of how many scooters he manages to sell and how far the customers ride them.
justification: The incident resulted in a strained/sprained medial collateral ligament, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). Given the design flaws and common road conditions, similar incidents are likely to occur frequently (likelihood 4).

incident_description:
The consumer stated that his son was riding around a bike course with his brother, at approximately 10-15 mph. They rode down the hill, and when the hill swept back up again, the downtube and toptube frame on his sonÃÂs bike broke off.

The consumer's son was ejected from the bike and fell on his head. The consumer's son was examined by the paramedic on the scene.

The consumer's son injured his neck and was diagnosed with whiplash. The consumer's son suffered from whiplash until recently (for about month and half). He also had a black eye. 

The consumer' son was wearing a helmet which cracked when he fell on his head.

The consumer contacted the dealer regarding the incident. The dealer took photos of the frame and submitted the information to Felt. The dealer informed the consumer that Felt will offer frame replacement for $500. The consumer informed the dealer that he does not feel that he should have to pay for this. He asked the dealer to contact Felt and have them examine the bike. The consumer sent the bike to Felt and paid $50 for shipping. After examining the bike, Felt offered the consumer frame replacement for $250. The consumer was not informed what happened to the frame. The consumer asked to have the engineers look at the frames closely to find out what caused it to break. After the engineers examined the bike, Felt offered to have the frames replaced for $594. Felts informed the consumer that the engineers looked at the frame and found nothing structurally wrong with it. 

After that, the consumer contacted Felt directly. The consumer was informed that the frame functioned as structurally designed and that there was no flaw in the frame.  The consumer informed Felt that he does not feel comfortable purchasing another frame that can function and break in the same way after a few months of use. The consumer asked for his money back. Felt informed the consumer that they don't issue refunds directly and that he would have to contact the dealer.

The consumer contacted the dealer and asked for a refund. The consumer was informed by the dealer that Felt would not issue a refund through them so they would not be able to provide it.

The consumer stated that they were not at fault for why the frame broke, and they should not have to pay for replacement frames The consumer is apprehensive about purchasing another frame and would rather get a refund.

The consumer has been having a lot of communication issues with the dealer. 

The consumer's son weighs 120 pounds and is about 5'6" tall.
justification: The consumer's son suffered whiplash and a black eye from the bike frame breaking, indicating an injury but no death.

incident_description:
This fire investigator for Medford, Oregon is reporting a fire incident with a hoverboard that was purchased from Amazon.com December 3rd, 2015 using order# [REDACTED].
December 23rd, 2015 the 20 year old owner of the hoverboard was charging the unit, it beeped to indicate completion of charge.
He got up and walked toward the hoverboard when he heard a whistling sound coming from it then it began smoking at which time he turned to yell for his parents and when he turned back the hoverboard exploded sending shrapnel pieces from the unit into the wall, the floor and into the nearby closet.
This is being reported as a severe fire and injury incident due to the potential for the shrapnel pieces to penetrate the human body if directed toward the user or others nearby.
There were no injuries with this specific incident.
The manufacturer has not been contacted due to there being no clear source indicated.
The caller has the remains of the hoverboard, its packaging and pictures.
justification: The incident involved a hoverboard explosion causing property damage but no injuries, as explicitly stated.

incident_description: I brought a Hoverboard to my friends house on Christmas day. Everyone tried it and was having a good time. My friend's mom was there and she got on. As she was coming down the Hoverboard, she had one foot on the ground, one foot on the board, the board rolled from under her. She fell on the side on the pavement. She got knocked unconscious, a pool of blood started forming around her head. She had blood coming out of her nose. We called 911.  The rescued came after after a few minutes. In the meantime she had regained consciousness and was moaning. The whole family was hysterical and her grand-kids were very traumatized and scared. She got transported to RI Hospital. She had a laceration on her elbow, and the CAT Scan unveiled a small bleeding between her skull and her brain. The laceration on her head was about 3 inches long. After 10 hours in the ER, many observations and thousands of dollars we finally got to take her back home. There is no warnings or safety instructions on the box. It came with a DVD to watch but who really takes the time to watch a whole DVD? It was the worst Christmas day ever!
justification: The incident resulted in a serious head injury with bleeding between the skull and brain, requiring hospital treatment, which qualifies as a severe injury.

incident_description: 2008 polaris rzr utv vin [REDACTED] fuel tank leaking gasoline. there was a recall issued on some of these but polaris claims mine is not included. the safety bulletin is  "Safety Bulletin R-07-08". the fuel tank on this unit has leaked for years so we just did not fill it up all the way and it did not leak some one recently informed me of the recall. polaris is being less than helpful and has told me there would be no safety repair done on my unit now I am terrified that one of my kids could be injured or killed by this and will no longer use the unit until some remedy is found

incident_description: I got a pair of cardiff skates for Christmas.  In the box were some discs that could be used to slow down the skates.  I was hesitant to use them, because in order to do so you had to use an Allen wrench and remove the back wheels.  But wanting to allow myself to get used to the skates I decided to put the discs on.  I read and reread the instructions on how to assemble the discs.  Once the discs are on, tension could be applied to the wheels by tightening the hex screw.  I had fairly well put as much pressure as I could put on the disc, but made sure the wheel could still freely spin.  I got up on my skates and went a short distances-maybe five yards at the most, and thought-I can do this!  When all of a sudden I fell.  I fell on my right hand and right knee.  I was shocked I had taken this hard spill when a friend picked up the wheel and said it came off!.  I emailed the company and they told me I was suppose to check the tightness of the wheels periodically.  I mentioned I had only gone a few yards after I had checked the screws and wheel spin.  I took another look at the screws (which are pretty short to begin with) and noticed some blue on the threads.  I looked over their handout and there is a mention of using Lock Tight on the threads-this information should have been on the instructions for assembling the dics!  But it wasn't.   I emailed the company again stating this, but they did not reply to me.  My hand is feeling better, knee not so much.  Waiting for the scab to heal and then heading to dr for some exrays.
justification: The incident resulted in injury to the hand and knee, requiring medical attention, which fits severity level 3. The likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the described circumstances and lack of clear instructions.

incident_description:
Hoverboard was ridden a few days and charged. The hoverboard was in a moving vehicle when the operator heard a crackling sound then noticed the gold color hoverboard changing colors to black. the owner of the vehicle heard a "pop" sound then a piece shot off the board with a small flame. He stopped the car then heard another loud "pop" and saw another part of the board "explode" with heavier flames. HE exited his vehicle and called 911. The vehicle is a total loss.

The Hoverboard was purchased online from AliExpress on 11/27/2015 and was given to his daughter as a Christmas present.

High Quality Smart Balance 2 Wheel Electric Standing Scooter Self Balancing Monorover Hoverboard. he paid 261.20 including shipping.
justification: The hoverboard caught fire and caused the vehicle to be a total loss, but there were no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: We purchased a Baja Motorsports Mini Bike in July of 2015 for our son's 15 birthday. He rides it around our house. The weekend before last, he was riding over some ruts in our yard. At some point the front forks lifted off the tire, which went rolling forward, and by gravity the front forks went down and dug into the ground, impeding his forward motion, causing him to fly up and over the handle bars. He landed on the ground on his stomach and the bike landed on his back and head. Luckily he was wearing a helmet. He is sore mostly to his back and head. I am a Pediatric Nurse Practitioner and I monitored him the rest of the day. He exhibited signs of a mild concussion with persistent headache and fatigue. He now has no further complaints of pain and the headache and fatigue have resolved.
justification: The incident resulted in a mild concussion and soreness, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) given the described riding conditions and the nature of the incident.

incident_description:
On the 7th of December, 2015, I had my first opportunity to ski since my prior ski trip in March of 2014.  As a busy professional and farther of two young children, I do not often use my skis.  For many years, I have owned a pair of Atomic SX-11 skis with Atomic Race 412 bindings.  On this particular day, I found that my boots were not staying in the bindings and tightened the bindings in an attempt to resolve this issue.  As I put my right boot into the binding after a little tightening, the binding literally blew up.  I was rather surprised to see so much load and stress being concentrated on the plastic frame of the binding.  I checked with the ski shop on the mountain, but they had nothing to replace the bindings with and suggested that I might have a hard time finding a replacement that would match my ski.  I ended up renting a pair of skis for the day.

Wanting to repair my skis, I set about searching for a pair of replacement bindings a few days later.  I quickly came upon this recall notice:    http://www.cpsc.gov/en/Recalls/2009/Atomic-Skis-USA-Recalls-Ski-Bindings-Due-to-Unexpected-Release-Fall-Hazard/  .  Of course, this notice appears to describe exactly what occurred to my bindings.  Unfortunately, I had not been previously aware of this notice ÃÂ nor apparently was the shop I had stopped at.  I called my local Sports Authority store and spoke with the ski shop about my skis and the recall and inquired if they were in fact an authorized Atomic dealer.  The technician I spoke with said he would be happy to take care of this issue for me.  Unfortunately, when I arrived, he had spoken to someone at Atomic and had been instructed to have me email Atomic directly.  So, I returned home, having wasted much precious time. I emailed Atomic as requested with attached pictures showing the failed binding and the date code.  I asked that Atomic send replacement bindings and a voucher for professional replacement service ASAP.  

Atomic responded that they are no longer honoring this recall or offering any assistance to their customers who now have defective, worthless equipment due to the bindings having been, "removed from the ski industry wide indemnification list."  Frustrated, I asked Atomic to reconsider and shared with them the following description of a major fall that I suffered during my previous ski trip which I now believe to have been directly caused by this defective equipment:

It is now obvious to me that my Atomic SX-11 skis and Atomic Race 412 bindings have caused me far more trouble than the inconvenience and expense of dealing with failed equipment and necessitated rental on the mountain.  During my immediate prior ski trip, I experienced a terrible fall which could easily have been fatal.  Fortunately, I was wearing a helmet and backpack which absorbed the brunt of the impact of my fall and I was able to ski away OK after coming to and gathering my gear.  This was a very traumatic experience; the worst I have ever experienced in a lifetime of skiing.  At the time, I attributed the fall ÃÂ caused when my ski popped off at the worst possible moment when I was absolutely depending on it, needing to stop at the top of a steep drop-off, to extreme bad luck.  At this point, it appears obvious to me, that defective equipment was much more to blame than simple bad luck.  Stuff happens, IÃÂm just glad to have been able to ski away OK.  IÃÂm still a little shaken reflecting back on this event.

I shared this story with Atomic over three weeks ago.  I asked them again to make the situation right by replacing my defective equipment.  They have yet to respond.  It appears clear to me that they no longer wish to take responsibility for these defective bindings and any injuries, inconvenience, and trouble which may directly result.  I ask the CPSC to review Atomic's actions, responsibilities and obligations under the law and to direct any resolution / assistance to me, and all similar situated / injured consumers, which might be appropriate and in the public interest.
justification: The incident resulted in a traumatic fall that could have been fatal, but the individual was able to ski away with injuries absorbed by protective gear.

incident_description:
HOVERBOARDS are dangerous!!!!

Son received the "most expensive & safest" hoverboard for Christmas (Powerboard brand). I stepped on it while holding onto the kitchen counter. I am an active (ski, run, etc.) physically fit mother of boys. It took off without me under it and I ended ub landing flat on my back after my feet raising another foot off the ground. It propelled me forward. I ended up with a very swollen sacrum, probable concussion and ruptured vessel in my left wrist (now in a splint). I am unable to sit without excruciating pain and spend the better part of Christmas day in the ER of St. Mary's hospital, Richmond, VA. Ambulance was called (cx due to timing). 
These devices should be taken off the market.......end of story. 
I am unable to lie down, sit or use my left hand/wrist (I am left handed).

There is NO safe version of this product. I am now spending my entire Christmas vacation flat on my stomach until my sacrum and wrist heal.

DANGEROUS toys.....
justification: The incident resulted in injuries including a swollen sacrum, probable concussion, and a ruptured vessel in the wrist, requiring medical attention.

I contacted the BouncePro customer service to report this, they sent another set of springs out to me.  The replacement springs have almost all broken in the same manner as the original ones.    They have hit my daughter in the legs, arms, and torso many times, as well as, landed up in the limbs of our trees.  They break with quite a bit of force behind them.  She has had bruises from the springs hitting her.
justification: The incident describes repeated injuries (bruises) caused by broken springs hitting the user, indicating a severity level of 3. The high frequency of spring failures suggests an occurrence likelihood of 4 (likely).

The consumer's ankle turned and the consumer fell down on the pavement on her left side. The bike landed on top of her. The handle bar hit her right breast.

incident_description:
I purchased a Uwheels hover board for my husband in late October - he received it three weeks later even though they charged my credit card the minute I ordered it.  

The product is totally inferior. It started with a simple problem where the plastic covers popped off and could not be replaced.  Soon the problems became much more serious The Battery charger melted and was smoldering nearly starting a fire in my garage.  If you go to their Facebook page you'll see that many people have had the same experience with their inferior battery packs.

Third the product is unsafe.  We have another hover board from a different manufacturer that is not at all like this one.  With the other one when the battery is getting low it beeps and blinks and tells you the battery is getting low. It also simple slows down until it finally stops - a safe approach. The Uwheels on the other hand provides no warning. It simply goes from full speed to STOP! My husband was riding on it and it came to an abrupt halt!  He was thrown off the product and sprained his wrist.  

Fourth, I have been trying to return the product to no avail.  I submitted a ticket and they simply closed it out with no resolution. I have called both of their retail offices and nobody picks up the phone. I also called the VP Sales - no returned call there either.

This company needs to be STOPPED!  They are manufacturing UNSAFE products that will create fires AND hurt riders!
justification: The hoverboard caused a sprained wrist due to abrupt stopping and has a history of battery issues, indicating both injury and likely recurrence.

incident_description: We received a Nordic Track Elliptical Model NTEL71615. In addition, we had delivery and set-up included. The machine was installed the first week of September, 2015. Due to business obligations that had us out of town for extended periods of time, we did not use the machine until November. On November 19th, 2015, I wrote to the consumer service department of Nordic Track, ICON Services, to let them know that my brand new $1500 machine had electrical currents running through the left handle and could be felt at the screw where you hold on to the bar. I mentioned that I had talked to an electrician and he felt it could be a bare wire in the machine. I got an 'automated' reply back stating a representative would contact me shortly. On December 4th, 2015 I wrote to them again. I explained to them that I had not heard from anyone and I did not want to use the machine due to the electrical current. Again, I got the 'automated' reply stating a representative would contact me shortly. Today is December 22nd and I have not heard from anyone. My concern at this point is it catching fire and damaging my home. I have unplugged the machine. No one can use it for fear of an electrical fire or personal injury. This machine does not have an on/off switch. The only way to use the machine is to manually plug it in to an outlet each time you want to use it, which in itself is not a safe practice.
justification: The incident involves an electrical issue with the machine, posing a potential risk of fire or personal injury, but no actual injury or damage has occurred yet.

incident_description:
I purchased a mini indoor over the door basketball hoop from Ross earlier this year.  After installing the screws and over the door brackets, I put it over the door.  Shortly thereafter, the heavy metal ring and backboard fell right off the brackets!  I checked it again to make sure I didn't do anything wrong.  I again installed it as stated, but it was too wobbly and unsafe to use. The screws are not long enough to hold he item into the brackets.  I figured this particular unit was defective, so after a couple months, I bought a new one from Ross.  The same thing happened.

I already lost the first receipt and it has been more than 30 days for the second item purchased.  I want my money back in full.  It is a miracle my kids didn't get their heads busted open from the heavy metal object falling down!  My floor almost cracked!
justification: The incident involved a defective product falling, but no injuries were reported despite the potential for harm.

Had the homeowners not been home at the time their home would have sustained significant fire damage. The Chappaqua Fire Department will make notification to the Consumer Product Safety Commission as well last the NYS Office of Fire Prevention and Control. We also suggest that any electronic devices that require charging only be done while someone is at home so that immediate action can be taken( call 911).
justification: The incident caused considerable smoke damage but no injuries or deaths, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) as the description suggests a common scenario with electronic devices.

I did go to the hospital and have also been referred to a plastic surgeon/ortho Dr who wants to put pin in my thumb as in addition to the nerve and soft tissue damage that my thumb bone is broken in 2 places.

incident_description:
On the morning of November 14, 2015, I was riding the Powerboard by Hoverboard.  This was purchased from Amazon.com.  When I went to step off of the board, the board leapt forward and swept my feet out from under me.  I fell backwards from a standing position onto my outstretched right arm.  Immediately, I felt my right elbow dislocate and experienced severe pain.  My wife immediately drove me to the nearest emergency room where I was diagnosed with a right (dominant hand) elbow dislocation with a fracture of the joint and a ligament injury.
On November 16, 2015, I underwent surgery on the right elbow and was told that recovery would take 3-6 months.  I am a practicing surgeon and will be unable to work during this recovery period.  I feel that the device is unsafe as it caused a severe career threatening injury and disability.
justification: The incident caused a dislocation, fracture, and ligament injury, requiring surgery and a 3-6 month recovery period, which is a serious injury.

justification: The description clearly states an injury to the left thumb caused by the crossbow firing, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The lack of a safety guard suggests this could happen again under similar conditions, making the occurrence likelihood 'possible' (3).

Nearly severed the end of my left thumb off by getting it into the path of the string and weapon did not have proper hand/finger guards.  Required minor surgery but just had them sew it back up due to being a victim of the recession from my job of over 17 years. Thumb is usable and just numb and sensitive now. This incident happen in 2009 on my parents property while hunting.
justification: The incident resulted in a significant injury requiring minor surgery, but no death or permanent disability occurred. The likelihood is unlikely as it involves a specific, avoidable handling error with a crossbow.

incident_description: My 75 year-old father was riding a Swagway "hoverboard" while using his walker for support.  He fell backwards and split open his scalp in the back of his head and bled profusely since he was on warfarin for a heart condition.  He was not wearing his helmet at the time.  He was transported by ambulance to the emergency room and received staples in the scalp.  A head CT showed no bleeding in the brain.  He was discharged from the emergency department to home and he continues to do well.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (split scalp requiring staples) but no long-term harm or death, and the likelihood is unlikely given the specific circumstances (elderly on warfarin riding a hoverboard without a helmet).

incident_description: My son's friend received a Hoverboard from his grandma for his birthday on November 20th, 2015.  He went to her house after school to pick it up.  She had ordered it on Amazon and it came in the mail earlier that day.  On the way home, they stopped by our home.  He ended up staying.  About four hours after he got the board, he plugged it in to charge in my son's room.  We went to his house to get stuff for him to spend the night, within an hour, we received a call from my husband that the house was on fire.  He heard a noise and thought it was my son and his friend rough housing.  He yelled at them to knock it off.  When the noise didn't stop, he got up to investigate.  He saw flames coming from underneath the door.  He kicked the door open and the hoverboard had exploded.  It was shooting fire, later we realized they were the burning batteries.  My husband carried the burning board through the house and threw it outside.  He went back to the room to put out the fire.  He then went outside to check on the hoverboard and it was still on fire.  He used the garden hose to put it out. He called 911.  The fire was out before they got here but we needed them for smoke removal.  The hardwood floor needs to be replaced, the walls fixed from the shooting batteries, the blinds melted and his futon couch was burned.  He also lost clothes and Xbox games that had melted.  My husband was seen in the ER for smoke inhalation.  If my husband wasn't home, the house would have burned down.
justification: The incident caused smoke inhalation and property damage, making it a severity level 3.

The consumer made an appointment with a hand surgeon for next day. The consumer was informed that he needs an operation on the thumb. The consumer was informed that he may have possibly cut the nerve and the doctor would need to inspect to see if Neuroma occurred.

incident_description:
10/15/2011 (Approximate) - The consumer indicates that the tilt steering cylinder lost pressure and would not stay in the upright position. The consumer contacted the manufacturer and explained the problem he was having; because his unit was out of warranty, he was informed by their Customer Service Representative that they could not provide any assistance to him. The consumer ended up paying one hundred dollars to have the tilt steering cylinder replaced.

12/15/2011 (Approximate) - The consumer indicates that he went to the gas station to fill his unit up and when he arrived home and was dismounting the UTV from his pick-up truck, he noticed that gas had spilled from the top of the gas tank. The consumer contacted the manufacturer to report the issue but was informed that his unit is not included in any recalls and so they could not provide any assistance free of charge. The consumer is aware that because his unit was manufactured in 08/09/2007, it is not included in Release Number 08-521.

The consumer indicates that the he went to two authorized dealerships but nobody ever looked at his unit after they verified it fell outside of the recall date-range.

The consumer tried to patch the gas tank but was unsuccessful and hence ceased use of the unit as of December 2011.

The consumer believes this product poses a safety hazard.

Additional Information :

The consumer  purchased  this 2008 Polaris RZR on 08/15/2007 from ATV Motor Sports 1062 County Road P-47 Omaha, NE 68152 Deater #2677700.  Nebraska Purchase Contract (invoice)#[REDACTED].  According to the manufacturing date sticker found on the right side of the frame on front of the vehicle behind wheel and tire the date the unit was made is 08/09/2007.

According to the U.S. Consumer  Product Safety Commission recall alert #08-521dated 12/06/2007, the consumer's Polaris RZR has the exact  model number  R08VH76AD(red) manufactured between 08/21/2007 and 10/03/2007.  This unit was manufactured 8 working days before the date specified in the recall.  The consumer considers this to be too close to the time frame of when Polaris contends the defect appeared. The consumer believes the Polaris RZR he purchased  has one of the defective gas tanks involved with this recall.

The gas tank is made of plastic and is constructed of two pieces, the main tank itself and a "flange" that is "plastic welded" to the top of the tank on which the fuel pump/sending unit mounts to the tank.  The fuel pump/sending unit is mounted to this flange by 6 machine screws.  These are also a problem on this gas tank. The machine screws are held in place by 6 brass inserts that are basically melted into place on the "flange" these brass inserts loosened themselves in the plastic flange as I found out when trying to repair the tank after  being turned  away by Polaris. The tank has an embossed manufacturer's clock(for lack of terminology) with the codes of the date it was made.  There is no name of the manufacturer of the tank.  See gas tank attachment .

The consumer took several  pictures of the top of the gas tank. See attachments. You can see the fuel pump/sending unit, silver color, on top of the tank.  The consumer started by filling the tank: with gas very slowly till just a small amount of fuel started to show under the the fuel pump/sending unit see pic #1.  The consumer added just enough gas to start a small flow of fuel which seeps out between the flange and the tank see pic #2. Picture #3 shows a side view and you can see the area  where the flange is welded to the top of the tank as does pic #4. This is the defect that  Polaris should cover in my case.  The fuel leaks between the flange and the top of the tank.

Just so you know there is a rubber O ring that seals the fuel pump/sending unit to the top of the flange.  The fuel does not leak at that location.  It is clearly leaking between the two plastic parts of the gas tank itself, the welded flange and the tank.

There are 3 other pictures I have attatched.#5 shows a(sorry)blurred pic of the gas tank serial and model  number.  #6 shows the total  number of engine hour run time and #7 shows the total number of miles driven.  As you can see the consumer is very concerned with this defect. The consumer believes Polaris has miscalculated the exact time frame as to when the gas tank defect  was originally discovered. The consumer would greatly appreciate your involvement in resolving this issue and to publish this report.

Thank You

incident_description: I was trail riding my 2013 Can-am Outlander 650 XMR on the "Soo line" coming from Moose Lake Minnesota. It's a old rail road bed that has been turned into a strait and maintained ATV trail laid with rocks and dirt. I was trail riding with a buddy of mine and we were heading back to my cabin further down the "Soo line".  Me and my buddy were cruising at the same speeds as everyone else on the "Soo line", which is about 45-50 MPH (even though my Outlander 650 is capable of speeds over 70 MPH factory), when a deer popped out and stopped in the middle of the trail. I then locked up all my brakes to avoid hitting the deer, which I did manage to avoid. In the time I hit my brakes my rear brakes failed, shooting my rear pads out the back of ATV.  At that point my rear end started to come out from behind me and I thought I was going sideways and going to crash but I was able to let off the brakes right away because the deer moved out of the way. This allowed me to regain control before going too far sideways and crashing. After that scare, and lose of my rear brakes, I limped back to my cabin safely and went home. I started digging into the ATV to see what all had happened and from what I could see the rear brake system was destroyed. The pad material ripped off the pads and was bent up. The rotor was bent really bad and one of two caliper piston's was bent and no longer operational. The caliper slides were bent and no longer operational and the swing arm mounts for the rear brake system was bent and could not be straightened. The whole swing arm that my suspension, wheel, and connection to the main frame  all come together. I knew that I was dealing with a manufacturer structural defect so I called Can-am. Long story sort, after numerous calls and providing them with the facts and the opportunity to correct it, they made it clear that it's not their problem and to have my third party warranty take care of it. So I called my warranty they told me it's a brake issue and it's not covered, even after I explained how it's a structural defect. I have done research and found others that had similar problems on similar Can-am ATV's and that they were told by the manufacturer that its not their problem. I went further yet to find out that Can-am or BRP has had similar issues in the past six years with brake and structural problems. One was recalled on the 2010 Can-am Spyder for complete brake system failure. Another with one of the Can-am Outlander twin machines, the Can-am renegade, that had rear brake failures to the point they redesigned the rear brakes making it a dual rear brake system instead of a single brake on the rear drive shaft. The Can-am Renegade shares many things with the Can-am Outlander like frame, suspension, power and powertrain, but the Can-am Outlander is heavier and has bigger wheels which creates more force on the brakes. Yet they didn't carry over the new dual rear brake system on the Can-am Outlander. The last issue I found that they had was the G1 frame on all of the Can-am ATV's. These failed under normal use to the point that in 2013 Can-am switched all the frames except the Outlander 400cc over to the newer stronger G2 frame. This frame has the same provisions to accept the dual rear brake system as the Can-am renegade, that was kept even after the frame change, and I still have not seen this safety issue fixed on the Can-am Outlanders. Bottom line... this could have injured or killed me and others I have talked to that have the same safety issue. Can-am  needs to take action either through a forced  recall or free will for fear of someone getting injured or worse.
justification: The incident involved a near-crash due to brake failure, but no injury occurred. Similar issues have been reported, indicating a possible recurring problem.

incident_description:
Text of Submitter's e-mail message dated September 29, 2015:

Subject: Formal complaint / recall required MotoTec 1600w Dirt Electric Skateboard DUAL MOTOR

I'm lucky to be alive writing this. Through walmart, I purchased the MotoTec 1600w Dirt Electric Skateboard DUAL MOTOR. After my 10th ride or so, I was riding down the street going 15/18 mph. I accidentally touched the top of the controller and hit the speed button. The wheels instantly locked up. You can imagine what happened next. I barrel rolled down the asphalt about 40ft. I have scrapes and road rash and internal bruises all over. I am an adventurous person and also an engineer. I know that these types of remotes need to have a failsafe in case buttons are accidentally or intentionally pressed. It should absolutely not lock up the wheels if I press ANY button. It needs to disable all buttons while the board is in motion. This is the worst safety oversight I have ever seen in a product. I am 35 years old. I cringe when I think of a kid using this, accidentally (or even intentionally) pressing a button and then possibly getting hit by a car. I very strongly urge you to stop selling and distributing this until this problem is fixed. You also need to notify those that have purchased it of this problem. This needs to happen immediately. Go ahead and test one, but if mine did it, others will do it too.
justification: The incident resulted in scrapes, road rash, and internal bruises, indicating an injury. The likelihood is high as the issue is inherent in the product design.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting his ATV four wheeler after three incidents of his power steering has gone out on three separate occasions. 
The first incident around September 24, 2015 on the caller's property when the caller was riding at approximately 15 mph and almost hit a fence when the steering went out.  He contacted the manufacturer who advised him to take it to the closest dealer that was 100 miles from the caller's residence at [REDACTED].
The manufacturer advised the caller to have this dealer perform a diagnostic test on the ATV.  The diagnostic test showed that the steering tripped due to an overcurrent in the electrical system.
The dealer reset the electrical system, drove it then returned it to the caller.
The second incident was September 29, 2015 on his friends ranch in Three Rivers, Texas when the caller was riding at approximately 9 mph after which the caller contacted the dealer who had reset the electrical system.  The dealer checked the ATV again then aligned the front wheels, reset it again, drove it then returned it to the caller again.
October 1st, 2015 the caller was riding again on his property at around 20 mph when the power steering went out on the caller after only five miles of riding causing the caller to almost go into a ditch.
The caller as of this date has not been injured and states that he has no intention of riding this ATV at this time.  
The caller states that there is a total of just over 50 miles on the ATV and is asking that this ATV become recalled.  His model is recalled with release# 12-709 but only in the red and yellow colors. The manufacturer has advised him that his Cammo color is not recalled.
He is asking that his Cammo color be added to the recall and that a complete repair be extended to him at manufacturer expense.
