incident_description:
Sometime in 2008 the consumer purchased the ATV used from another person. 

On 7/4/15 the consumer noticed the hot indicator came on after the ATV was turned "on" and the cooling fan was running slow. The consumer believes the Electronic Control Module (ECM) is defective. The consumer disconnected the battery because he believes the ATV can catch on fire. The consumer has been a mechanic for 45 years and inspected the ATV. 

The consumer was online and came across recall # 05-568. On 8/28/15 the consumer called the firm's recall hotline (888-704-5290) and inquired about the remedy. The rep (name unknown) informed the consumer that the ATV had the pinch coil wire replaced on 7/12/05. The consumer understood that the ATV would not receive another repair from the firm. The consumer states that replacing the pinch coil wire will not correct the safety hazard with the ECM and the firm is obligated to replace the ECM according to the recall.  

The consumer used the ATV once a week. The consumer has stopped using the ATV since 7/4/15. The consumer has not had the ATV repaired since he purchased it. 

The consumer plans to purchase the parts and have the ATV repaired and hopes the firm will reimburse him.

Included is a copy of the consumer's receipt for a new ECM.  This fixed the consumer's problem with his ATV.  [REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a potential safety hazard with the ATV's ECM, but no actual injury or fire occurred. The consumer took preventive measures by discontinuing use and repairing the ATV.

incident_description:
I am the owner of a Coleman Mountain Bike 2100; I was riding the bike on,
Sunday July 5, 2015 and all of a sudden, the bike locked up, throwing me over the handlebars and I went skidding down a sidewalk. When I finally realized what happened, I was covered in blood from my head, arms, and knees. A gentleman stopped to see if I was indeed ok. My glasses were broken, bike damaged, helmet dented on top and scratches all over entire helmet. 

I was seen in the ER with a severe concussion, bleeding into the skull, major contusions on both legs, arms and a huge hematoma above my right eye along with a cut. I was prescribed pain medications and antibiotics for ten days and was seen in follow-up due to severe headaches and was told I will still continue to have headaches and have not been able to go back to work. My legs, and arms are healing, however will be scarred permanently. If I had not been wearing my helmet, I would not be here today.

I continue to Dr. and will have permanent scarring, I wish to find out whom I need to contact in regards to this matter.

The consumers have pictures, however attorney is in possession of them.
justification: The incident resulted in severe injuries including a concussion, bleeding into the skull, and permanent scarring, which warrants a severity level of 4 due to the life-threatening nature of the injuries.

incident_description:
While I was using the elliptical the axle that holds the left handlebar broke and I fell. I was uninjured but someone experiencing the same failure could fall and be seriously injured. 
The handlebar and foot piece are attached so that in each cycle of the wheel, a person's full weight is supported only by the axle that broke at some point during the cycle and a person's full weight is supported at some other point by the axle holding the right handlebar. Other times during the cycle both the left and right axles support the user's weight. The axle is hollow and not of sufficient strength. I weigh 190 pounds.  I have had the elliptical about two years. I use it twice a week for 20 minutes each time. 

I suspect this is an engineering problem in which a stronger axle should have been chosen, rather than a manufacturing defect in the specific axle. My best guess is that NordicTrack should be required to recall the elliptical to replace the axles with more substantial axles. In the meantime, I will have both axles replaced and will begin using the elliptical again.
justification: The incident involved a fall due to equipment failure but no injury occurred, though potential for serious injury exists.

incident_description: On Sept 1 2014, my wife and I were at a friends house for Dinner. My friend had just purchased a new Barnett Quad 400 crossbow and ask if I wanted to shoot it. I had never shot a crossbow before. I shot one arrow without incident. When I shot the first arrow, I was trying to get a feel for the equipment, i.e., was it going to kick, things like that. I nocked another arrow but this time I relaxed more trying to make a good shot. I shoot left handed and as I relaxed my right hand, I apparently raised my thumb on the right hand into the flight path of the string. When I squeezed the trigger the string cut off my right thumb at the nail bed.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe injury (thumb cut off at the nail bed), which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the specific circumstances of inexperience and improper handling of the crossbow.

incident_description:
Bowflex aka Nautilus

I use frequently but never have abused the Select Tech 1090 dumbbells.  
2 days ago I started my work out and when I did nothing more than lift it against gravity
the largest plate fell out.  I checked to see if there was something wrong with the stand and the 
locking mechanism etc.  I paid over 500 dollars for these so yes I am angry.  But I thought this could hurt someone if it happens again.  I called the Bowflex consumer number and explained what 
happened.  They tried to sell me another plate and also a pullup station?  I read up on other products they have and it seems this is an issue before me.  I can see the weight coming down on someone's head and incapacitating them.  Fortunately mine simply fell to the floor.
justification: The incident involved a dumbbell plate falling out without causing injury, but there is a potential for serious harm if it happens again.

incident_description:
Destination Summer Hammock Stands

Hazard:
Z-shaped hooks that attach the hammock to the hammock stand can bend or break, resulting in a consumer falling to the ground.

I was on the Hammock when the hook broke and I fell to the ground and hit the cross bar.  I had a bruise for about a week.
justification: The incident resulted in a bruise lasting a week, indicating an injury (severity 3). The high number of similar incidents (1968 of 3915) suggests the likelihood is almost certain (5).

incident_description: This involves the Destination Summer hammock stand sold by Bed Bath & Beyond stores.  While I was lying in hammock that was attached to this stand the Z-shaped hook that attaches the hammock to the stand bent causing the hammock to fall.  I fell to the ground and landed on top of the bottom metal pole of the stand itself.  I suffered injuries to my right hip and shoulder.
justification: The hammock stand failed, causing a fall and injuries to the hip and shoulder, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: Out practicing with my crossbow and I had my thumb sticking up just a little bit and when I shot my crossbow the string hit my thumb and almost cut my thumb off.  There should be a better gaurd on the handle off the crossbow that protects all parts of your hand while shooting.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe injury (almost cut thumb off), but the likelihood of recurrence is unlikely with proper handling and guard improvements.

incident_description:
The ATV is engineered in a way that the right plastic covering the engin and muffler, abuts up to the hot muffler. The heat from the muffler has caused the plastic to melt and could potentially cause a fire.  I have also burnt my leg at the location where the plastic is melting. 

I called Polaris and they do not have any recalls and directed me to the dealership. Members at the dealership said this is a common problem but couldn't offer a remedy to ensure safety.
justification: The incident describes a burn injury and a potential fire hazard, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is high (4) as the issue is described as a common problem by the dealership.

incident_description: I was using a Barnett Jackal crossbow when I was injured. I was sighting the bow for the season. I inadvertently allowed my left thumb to be placed in the path of the crossbow cable. When I shot the arrow, the cable struck my thumb resulting in near amputation of my thumb. The Jackal crossbow lacks a finger guard which would prevent this type of injury. The product is defectively designed and needs to be redesigned or removed from the market place. I also believe the existing crossbows that have been sold should be recalled due to their hazard to users.
justification: The incident resulted in a near amputation of the thumb, which is a significant injury.

incident_description: My gt grade alloy tiagra road bike has incompatible parts. I purchased the bike 3 weeks ago brand new assembled from the store and have had it tuned up at the same store 3 times since purchase. I was riding the bike down hill and while braking I noticed the front wheel shaking violently and making loud metal noises. I went home to inspect the bike and noticed that there was hardly any clearance between the front wheel spokes and the brake caliper. In fact the spokes hit the caliper while spinning the wheel. I did some research and the problem is not uncommon. I contacted the brake manufacture (trp brakes) and showed them pictures. They said they were aware of the potential safety issues and that it only happens with their brakes in combination with specific hubs. When I told them I purchased the bike like this they were shocked (exact words were "yikes, you bought the bike like that" in reference to the hub and brake combination).  Trp told me they sold spacers to fix this issue. My concern is that gt bicycles chose all these parts for this bike model and sells as is and that seems like a major oversight. I have stopped riding my bike and contacted gt bicycles in the mean time.
justification: The incident involved a safety issue with the bike's parts causing violent shaking and noise, but no injury occurred. The problem is known to the manufacturer but not extremely rare.

incident_description: My son was riding his Bike (a Nauvaro Stinger 16 - purchased at REI http://www.rei.com/product/814571/novara-stinger-16-kids-bike-2015?s_kwcid=s7iaZp5TM_dc%7Cpcrid%7C71492825645%7Cpkw%7Cnovara%20stinger%2016%22%7Cpmt%7Ce%7Cgoogle%7Cmain%7CNB&gclid=CjwKEAjws7OwBRCn2Ome5tPP8gESJAAfopWs0nKbCIfuMHoKZlbFWnRtcqH0KagZ8U72DXk8K2ZKABoCjZPw_wcB) when he was breaking the breaks would not apply and he had a very substantial crash - knocking out teeth, skinning his face and cracking his helmet in two. Upon looking at the bike we discovered that there is a single spot in the rotation that if he applies the breaks the chain guard will prevent the peddle from rotating backwards - preventing the brakes from being applied). We went into the store and were able to replicate the issue on every single on of these bikes that were at the store. We are working with REI to replace our bike but the issue seemed big enough to report. It is quite dangerous.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (knocked-out teeth, facial abrasions, cracked helmet) and the issue was replicable on all bikes of the same model, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description:
I was hunting with my Barnett Jackal Crossbow that I've had for about 4 or 5 years. I fired at a deer from a tree stand in the woods,   and the string severed the tip of my thumb.  
This is a dangerous weapon that should be recalled and replaced with thumb guards. 
I never thought that this would happen to me as I'm a very cautious hunter, but it did,  and i don't want this to happen to others.
justification: The incident resulted in the severing of the tip of the thumb, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description: I was driving my Arctic Cat Wildcat Trail XT down a trail and the door popped open and hit a tree. No injuries where sustained however I see this as a serous safety issue. Others have had similar issues after doing some research online. The dealer and manufacturer claimed I did not shut the door correctly however I'm certain it was fully latched when riding. This happened out of the blue after driving for over an hour on the trails. Others have reported this issue happening while transporting the UTV also and another safety issue with that as well.
justification: No injuries occurred, but the door popping open while driving is a serious safety issue, and others have reported similar incidents.

incident_description:
On 9/23/15, I ordered a Vilano 26 inch midtown folding bicycle online from "www.roadbikeoutlet.com".  A few days later, I received it in good condition via UPS Ground.  Out of the box, I needed to adjust the disc brakes, front and rear derailleurs,  adjust and tighten the handle bar and stem.  Disassembled wheel hubs, checked ball bearings and repacked with more grease and reassembled.  Wheels did not have sufficient grease from factory. Tightened folding pedals, which have a metal base/support and the platform is a hard plastic.  You have to press down hard on the pedals to lock them in place.  To unlock you pull on the metal lever in the middle of the pedal.  Tested bike components  and they were within normal standards. Rode the bike around the flat terrain of my neighborhood for a few days to break it in, no problems.  On Friday, 9/25/15, around 7:35 pm,  I decided to make a quick commute to the McDonald's down the road from my house to pick up a Redbox movie, like I have done in the past on other bikes I own.  Well, I never made it. Half way thru my ride, I arrived at an intersection.  Checking for traffic before proceeding, I stepped up on the left pedal of the bike and then pushed down hard on the right pedal to take off in a hard/slow gear, when I heard a snapping sound, and the right pedal fell out from below my right foot.  Next all my weight shifted to the right side of the bike and I fell hard on my right hip and arm. The bike was straddled between my legs, my left leg got cut behind the knee and my right leg got injured.   In the end, I broke my right femur next to the ball joint (old person emergency I was told).  I had to go to the emergency and received surgery the same day.  Now I have plates and screws holding my femur together. I cannot put weight on my right leg for 3 months until it heals.  The doctors initially wanted to replace my hip, but because I am 36 years old, they decided to go with the plate and screws. The bone may heal (fuse) or it may not.  I won't know for a while.  It's possible that I may need surgery again for this injury in a few years.

Please take this as a warning to others, to please check all bicycle components every time before you ride.  I weigh 165 lbs.  and bike should easily support 220 lbs., yet the pedal failed.  Please be alert to such possible dangers.
justification: The incident resulted in a broken femur requiring surgery, which is a severe injury, and such pedal failures are unlikely given the bike's weight capacity and user's weight.

incident_description: On 09/06/2015 at approximately 12:50AM Champaign County Deputies responded to a report of an ATV rollover with injuries in a field near 0 North CR 400 East near Sadorus.  The incident scene was difficult to locate, but when firefighters and deputies located the scene they found two males that had been ejected from an ATV.  [REDACTED]identified himself to deputies as the driver of the ATV.  [REDACTED]identified the other male as [REDACTED]..  [REDACTED] was airlifted from the scene by Airlife to Carle Foundation Hospital.  [REDACTED] was determined to be deceased by the Arrow Ambulance crew on the scene.Deputy [REDACTED] is a crash reconstructionist and detrmined the following events from the scene examination.  The ATV was traveling westbound along a grass path waterway between fields of planted corn.  Upon reaching a ninety (90) degree curve the ATV made a quick left turn, lost control and wnet into a side to side airborne rollover.  The ATV struck the ground and continued to rollover with the passenger, [REDACTED]., being ejected along the rollover path.  The ATV came to rest approximately seventy four (74) feet west fo the initiation of the rollover.  Deputy [REDACTED] determined the approximate speed of the ATV at 39.4 MPH using the traffic crash basic speed formula with a .70 drag factor.Deputy [REDACTED] noted on the crash report the following contributory causes: Under the Influence of Alcohol/Drugs and Operating Vehicle in Erratic, Reckless, Careless, Negligent or Agressive Manner.
justification: The incident resulted in a fatality and involved reckless behavior, indicating high severity and moderate likelihood given the context.

incident_description: on the 26th of June of this year, in a route in [REDACTED], suddenly the steering wheel of the atv  abruptly hardened  and almost caused me to drive off the road in a turn, losing the control and very close to having a front crash.. after that, the rest of my trip was terrible and it provoked me getting multiple blisters in the hands because of the extra effort to steer the wheel.  Until recently I found out of the recall for these vehicles,  but i never received a warning as I think I should have,  I found out about it on the internet
justification: The incident caused injury (blisters) and nearly resulted in a crash, indicating a significant risk.

incident_description: We have the Rainbow Play set, purchased Summer 2009 with the yellow plastic trapeze rings. The rings broke in half while my son was swinging on the - he is 60 pounds.  He flew off and landed on his back and hit his head on our ground.  It appears as if the rings broke in half at  a seam in the plastic.  This should not happen.
justification: The child sustained injuries from falling after the rings broke, but there is no mention of death or life-threatening harm.

incident_description: I laid on the hammock and when I tried to move up alittle the hook popped out and I fell first hitting my head very bad on the pole thats angled and landing on the pole that is on the ground which resulted in me not being able to walk the next morning without having back spasms. I produced a bruise from the top of my tailbone that became extremely wide also over my buttock. I had to go to urgent care and got x-rayed for my tailbone and was given a shot to help with the spasms.
justification: The incident resulted in significant injury requiring urgent care, x-rays, and treatment for back spasms, indicating a severity level of 3.

incident_description: I am an American owner of a 2012 Can Am Commander 1000 XT utility terrain vehicle, manufactured by Bombardier Recreational Products of Canada and I want to report an equipment safety incident that I experienced. While operating the vehicle recently I suffered a total brake failure. I was not injured, but the results could have been fatal. Upon investigation I discovered that the spring clip designed to retain the pin connecting the brake pedal to the brake master cylinder rod had broken, this allowed the pin fall out, resulting in zero braking. In my opinion the current design of the braking system on this vehicle enables a single point of failure on a critical system and should be modified.
justification: The incident involved brake failure with no injury, but potential for severe consequences, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the described design flaw.

incident_description:
I was using the product in the precise manner for which it was designed and I experienced a total failure of the trigger handle mechanism which resulted in a total failure of the airbag system.  The trigger handle had completely separated from the pack.  Upon inspection in the field, I discovered that the cable connecting the trigger handle to the airbag system was totally severed.  It was impossible to repair in the field and I was left with a non-functioning and non-repairable airbag system.

Prior to this incident, the airbag backpack was in excellent condition, and I always made sure it was stored safely when not in use.  The cable failure was not due to any unusual use or handling, but rather from normal use.
No injuries were sustained in this incident, however the product failure could easily have led to  serious injury or death if the severed cable had not been discovered at such a time.
justification: The incident resulted in a total failure of the airbag system but no injuries were sustained, fitting severity level 2. The failure occurred during normal use, suggesting a possible occurrence likelihood.

incident_description:
I purchased the Blue Hawk 1-Bike Steel Bike Hoist Item #: 5884 |  Model #: 45670PKDLG 
From Lowes in Independence MO. had it up for about 6 months and it worked fine. On September 24, 2015, I was trying to lower one of my 2 bikes from this device in the garage (12 foot ceilings). In order to "unlock" it, you have to pull toward front of device much like blinds. While doing this, it would not release so I had to try different angles but not changing my position more than 2 feet. after about 30 seconds, the bike came crashing down onto my face. On exam, the rope had frayed and broke over the middle pulley. 
I had one tooth come completely out (retrieved from garage floor and put into milk). within about 45 minutes I was at my dentist that also found that 3 other teeth had also been knocked out but remained in place. The bill (my portion) was $700- and that was after dentist gave me a discount. This is the first step in the repair, next one in 8 weeks when wire comes out and final setting takes place- my anticipated cost for this step will be about $1000.
justification: The incident resulted in significant dental injuries requiring multiple treatments, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) based on the description of the equipment failure.

incident_description: ATV operator struck tree. He was taken to a local hospital and pronounced deceased.
justification: The ATV operator was pronounced deceased, indicating a severity level of 4. The occurrence likelihood is 2 (unlikely) based on the provided frequency.

incident_description: I recently purchased a Barnett Crossbow that included a Rope Cocking Device.  After only 7 or 8 uses the rope broke while I was trying to cock my crossbow.  When the rope broke it shot the hooks on the Cocking rope hitting my toe, breaking the toe.
justification: The rope broke during use, causing injury (broken toe), which qualifies as a severity level 3 incident.

incident_description:
Sudden catastrophic failure of a Shimano Ultegra compact crank that was used on my 2007 Cervelo R3 bicycle. This was the 50/34 Ultegra 10 spd crank that came with the bike when I bought it in August 2007. I have had no prior issues with the crank and had bottom bracket replaced twice, most recently 15 months earlier.
As you can see it failed dramatically. On 12 September 2015 I was riding uphill on hwy 39 at about 8-10 mph in the San Gabriel mtns and got to a switchback I had been on countless times in the past (and earlier in the same day) when out of the saddle the crank suddenly failed with zero warning and I tumbled into the road. I am 6ÃÂ1ÃÂ and weigh 188lbs. The bike has never been in any sort of major accident and that pedal has never been hit hard in any kind of mishap. No one other than me and shop personnel have ever ridden the bike.
Other than scrapes I was unhurt.
I include photos with the crankset if a subsequent page of the report will allow me to do so.
justification: The incident involved a sudden catastrophic failure of the crank leading to a fall, but only resulted in scrapes with no serious injury.

incident_description: On August 8, 2015, I was participating in a 100 mile bicycle ride.  In just over 25 miles into the ride, the seat support bolt broke in half at the point where the bolt enters the seat post.  The breaking of the bolt cause the seat to drop which resulting in me being thrown to the road immediately.  I sustained several injuries resulting from the crash. My right leg sustained several cuts and scrapes to the ankle, calf, knee, and hip, my right arm was cut and scraped on the elbow and two fingers received deep cuts.  My right shoulder is very sore since this was the part of me that impacted the road surface first.  Luckily, no bones were broken that were x-rayed by the local hospital (knee, hip and elbow).
justification: The incident resulted in multiple injuries but no broken bones or death, warranting a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is unlikely (2) as such incidents are not common but possible with equipment failure.

incident_description:
Suffered forward fall from horse wearing said helmet.  Helmet rocked backward so that did not protect front of head when I hit the ground.  I was knocked out and admitted for overnight hospital stay.  No significant long term brain damage.  (Helmet was fine and showed no damage or accumulation of dirt.)

Had noticed before that helmet chin strap did not stay in position during ride.  As the chin strap lengthened, helmet became looser and looser.  I believe this is a design flaw in that material of strap is slippery, and rubbery "O-ring" securing strap position is ineffective.

I have since secured strap position with 2 tightly fastened cable ties.  The consumer shouldn't have to do this.  Another person wearing this helmet may not be so lucky.
justification: The incident resulted in a hospital stay and temporary loss of consciousness, indicating an injury (severity 3). The helmet's design flaw makes recurrence likely if unaddressed (likelihood 4).

incident_description:
Caller stated that the inflated water tube malfunctioned while using it.  He stated this incident caused a 17 year old girl to get entrapped which could have caused drowning.  Her right foot was wedged in the between the tubes (canvas cover and inner tube) she was then capsized in the water face down, he had to deflate the tube to release her.  This was the first time using it.  No injuries were sustained from this incident.

(8/17) The manufacturer was contacted and he was informed that the incident would be reported to upper management and that someone might call him back.

Caller feels that the product is a safety hazard and should be reported.
justification: The incident involved a potential drowning hazard but no injuries were sustained, warranting severity level 2. The likelihood is possible (3) as it was the first-time use and the product malfunctioned.

incident_description:
The cable from the front brake levers to the tire brake comes out of the brake lever on the handlebar and when
braking hard in some cases gets pinched and ends up locking the front brakes in a braked position and won't
release resulting in the possibility of going over the handlebars. Mine was in the locked position after an accident
when applying the front brake and rear brakes in traffic. This happened again after having the bike tuned up when
using both brakes to a full stop. The bike shop says it's something that I need to watch out for, but I think the front
cable should be locked into the brake lever just like the rear one so this can't happen. I know not to brake with only
the front brake and only use it in conjunction with the rear brake. I rarely use the front brake on this bike for fear of
it will lock the wheel.

Since I haven't received a reply to my attached letter in June to Cannondale it appears there isn't a fix for this
problem or they just don't care. It's possible that my bike was assembled incorrectly regarding this problem, but
since they won't reply to my letter and the local bike shop doesn't seem to know of a solution, I wanted to file this
report in case there other incidents like mine.
justification: The incident describes a situation where the front brakes can lock, leading to potential injury from going over the handlebars, which has already occurred in traffic.

incident_description:
The consumer purchased his ATV brand new from Holiday Powersports. The dealer went out of business and is replaced with TC Powersports.

The consumer stated that the filler neck that meets the fuel tank has cracks 9/10 of the way around. The cracks are at the base of the filler neck where the gas cap screws on. The consumer stated that there is fuel leaking out of the tank.

The consumer stated that there may be a recall on his ATV but he was never notified about it.

The consumer will contact Polaris in regards to the issue.
justification: Fuel leakage from the ATV's cracked filler neck poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
I have brought a Solowheel S300 from Solowheel China official online store.
On 2015.08.18 almost 7:15pm ~ 8:00pm, when I using the solowheel, the machine stop working just like lost the power immediately, I have been fall to the ground.
As the result of this incident, my left clavicle fracture, right radius fracture, right knee scratch.
I have use my iphone take a video after incident, the Solowheel showing red light, and the red light is flashing, it can not turn into green(the light will be turn into green, when it works fine).
This is the second time Solowheel lost the power when it running.
The first time is on Jul 2015, Solowheel is working on the morning, and after running almost 2 ~ 3KM, the machine lost the power, and can not turn on again, fortunately when the machine fault, the speed is very slow, so I have not been injured at that incident.
After sending back the machine to the manufacture, they told me it is one of the wire broken.
Solowheel send me back the machine, after fixed it. I have used it almost 2 weeks, on 2015.08.18 another incident has happen, unfortunately, this time it broken 2 of my bones.
My [REDACTED] video showing Solowheel is not work, and I believe the product fault cause the incident, so I contact the manufacture next day, they ask me send the machine back, because they need download the data from the machine, but when they receive the machine, they refuse to confirm the product fault.
justification: The incident resulted in fractures and scratches, indicating injury (severity 3). The Solowheel lost power twice in a short period, suggesting a likely recurrence (likelihood 4).

incident_description:
I bought a bike with Shimano BR-785 hydrolic disc brakes.  Twice the brakes have failed because the brake fluid has leaked out of the brake during a ride.  Both times I was descending a mountain for an extended period for about 1500 feet.  

After the first incident my rear brake was replaced by the manufacture Shimano for free.  I was told this has happened on multiple bikes for customers of that bike shop.

After the second failure, this time the front bike brake, again on a long mountain descent of about 1500 feet occurred.  I took the bike into the bike shop and the mechanic said the same problem was happening for the front brake this time.  They also again stated that I was not the only customer having this problem, and that they were running into problems getting Shimano the acknowledge the problem.

The problem seems to come on pretty quickly.  So it's not possible to judge the bike has brake problems until an actual descent has started and the fluid leaks out sufficiently to cause a loss of braking power in the middle of the descent.

My concern at this point is that a defective product is out on the market and the failure of the brakes could cause serious injury and death.  I wouldn't be reporting this had there been one failure.  Having two failures and hearing that other customers are also having the failures makes me wonder if I should be using the product at all, and that this is a larger problem and people are going to get injured and killed before something is done about the situation.
justification: The incident describes repeated brake failures during descents, posing a significant risk of injury or death, though no actual injuries are reported yet.

incident_description: On 090915 I was riding my new ATV.  I had purchased and received the ATV on 082215 at Sun Enterprises in Thornton, Colorado.  This was the first day I drove it for a long distance.  It had only 3 miles on it when I began riding it on 090915.  I was stopped and was standing behind it and noticed the left rear tail lens was melted in the center.  Upon returning to home I telephoned the polaris service department at Sun.  I took it to the dealer and they looked at it.  They told me they would have to order a lens and would call me when it came in.  I am still waiting for the part.  Meanwhile I found many instances of tail lights melting on this particular manufactured ATV on line.  This is a serious problem in my mind.
justification: The incident involved a melted tail lens with no reported injury or death, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to multiple reported instances of the same issue.

incident_description:
I have a 2007 Giant TCR Advanced 1 road bike. Last Friday afternoon on a bike ride, the seat bolt broke suddenly and without warning, and I fell from the bicycle. I suffered road rash; shoulder, hip, and thigh bruising, a sprained thumb, and lost several layers of skin on the tip of my thumb. The bicycle also sustained heavy scratching. 

I stopped Milwaukee police for aid, but they were only able to call paramedics, so I immediately sought care at an urgent care clinic.
justification: The incident resulted in multiple injuries including road rash, bruising, and a sprained thumb, warranting a severity level of 3.

incident_description: We bought a 14' SportsPower Trampoline in December 2013. The safety net ripped within 4 months, the net ripped and had to be repaired. The safety net ripped again in June 2015. My 4 year old daughter fell out and hit her head on the concrete floor below. She was rushed to the hospital with big knot in her head. The end result was she suffered a concussion from the fall. We haven't used the trampoline since because we are scared the kids will fall out.
justification: A 4-year-old suffered a concussion from falling out of the trampoline due to a ripped safety net, indicating an injury (severity 3). The net ripped twice within two years, suggesting the issue is likely to recur (likelihood 4).

incident_description: Seated leg curl machine
justification: The description 'Seated leg curl machine' does not indicate any incident, injury, or death, so the severity is minimal.

justification: The incident involves a fire caused by a fuel leak, posing a risk of severe burns to people and potential environmental damage.

incident_description: Purchased CAP Barbell Olympic-size advanced weight bench in January 2015. There is a bar which supports the adjustable bench and the weight of the user and the weights they are lifting. The manual states the maximum weight tolerance is 500 lbs (weight of user + weights being lifted). My Trident II UV Sanitizer for my pool water melted down due to an electrical problem with it. It nearly burned down my pump house.
There is a recall in place for units manufactured between 09/09/2013 - 01/24/2014. My unit was manufactured on March 13, 2012.

incident_description: The front rim on a 20 in Mongoose Ace bicycle broke in half while my grandson was riding it. No injuries but if he was riding it faster he could have been very seriously hurt. Pacific cycle Model R2264TR  Date Ace0615JG. Called Pacific and they state it was manufactured in 2007 so there is no warranty. This bike was always taken care of and if because of age this could happen then there should be a warning sticker on it.
justification: The rim broke but no injuries occurred, though potential for serious injury was noted if conditions were different.

incident_description:
Caller stated that the playhouse for her 2 year old son became extremely hot while it was outside on a concrete pavement.  She stated that there was not much sunlight to the playhouse.  However, her 9 month old daughter opened the door to the playhouse and crawled in and screamed, caller discovered that the child's right hand (palm) had received blisters from touching the playhouse floor.  The child was taken to her physician where she was diagnosed of 2nd degree burns, the dead skin was removed and she was treated with antibiotics.  Using a bath thermometer the caller measured the air temperature and then the temperature of the plastic floor of the playhouse.  The air temperature was 77 degrees F and the floor of the playhouse 121 degrees F!


3/2015 Caller stated that she contacted the manufacturer and informed them of the incident.  She was advised that someone would contact her about the matter.  5/2015  She contacted them through email to find out the status on the report.  She stated that no one responded.  6/24/15  She contacted them again through email and still no one responded.


Caller stated that there is no warning label that the playhouse can overheat, she feels that this product is a safety hazard and should be investigated.
justification: The child suffered second-degree burns requiring medical treatment, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description: I went on the treadmill and needed to change the volume of [REDACTED] on my tablet and hit the Stop button so I could mess with it without dropping it. Then my treadmill goes up to like 10 or something so I'm trying to smash the Stop button and it is slowing a bit then speeding up so I pull the emergency stop key and it keeps going. I jump off to the side, which knocks off my tablet and now the screen is all messed up. I turned the treadmill off and then on again via power switch but it just keeps doing the high-speed/jerking thing when the stop button is pushed or slows down eventually when you pull the emergency key.

We purchased a roadmaster granite peak bicycle for our son this past year.  The seat stem bent, placing the rider in jeopardy of falling off. justification: The incident involves a bicycle with recurring mechanical failures (seat stem bending, pedal falling off) that could lead to injury, but no injury has occurred yet.

She weighs less than 50lbs and one of the rings she was holding snapped off, the plastic breaking below to wear it attaches to the chain.  I can provide pictures on request. incident_description:
Hi,

I recently bought a Schwinn Antrim Disc bike in Calgary, AB, Canada with SRSUNTOUR front forks that I now know have been recalled.  

While biking, when I lifted up on the handlebars to go over a curb at high speed the front suspension came apart causing the front wheel to come off and me to face plant into the ground very violently.  I sustained several injuries including cuts to my face/hands and a concussion (photos available).  

I know the front fork is part of a recall because when I reported the incident to the retailer that sold me the bike, they told me.

I would like to be compensated for the obvious flaw in design/manufacturing of the bike resulting in personal injury that should have never happened.
justification: The incident resulted in multiple injuries including cuts and a concussion, which qualifies as a severity level 3. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to the known recall and the described failure mechanism.

incident_description:
I've purchased two Skramble children's bicycles http://www.toysrus.com/buy/18-bikes/avigo-18-inch-scramble-mountain-bike-5f60666-19508956.    One 18" and one 20".    On both bikes the front bikes have failed while being ridden.   In one case this resulted in a very painful crash which could easily have resulted in serious injuries.    

I've examined the brake design and construction and the problem is readily apparent.   Squeezing the brakes hard causes a component in the caliper to permanently slide along it's housing,  and leaves the brake completely ineffective.    This does not require excessive force to happen -- my six year old was able to do it on two different occasions. 

I strongly feel this bike needs to be recalled.
justification: The incident resulted in a painful crash with potential for serious injuries, and the brake failure is easily reproducible by a child.

He said he had, but only in a major crash.  I did not crash.  I was riding on level pavement at about 15 mph.  I weigh 165 lbs.  If I had been moving with any speed, or on a corner, I'd have fallen off the bike, without warning.  I contacted the manufacturer to warn them of the defect.  I have received no reply. This is a defect that could kill someone.
justification: The incident involved a defect that could have caused injury but did not result in any harm this time. The bike shop owner's statement suggests such failures are rare, occurring only in major crashes.

incident_description:

It looks like the fork broke.

incident_description:
Manufacturer: Giant

Product: Pea Pod bike trailer

Purchased the Giant Pea Pod trailer from Steamboat Ski & Bike Kare on July 5 2015.


After using the trailer for two days it flipped over onto it's side. Luckily the trailer was empty at the time so there were no injuries.  The trailer did sustain some scuffs and minor damage.   I took the trailer back to Steamboat Ski & Bike Kare and expressed our concern.  They inspected the trailer and my bike, a Navara Ponderosa mountain bike, and suggested that the flip was due to the trailer being unweighted (no kids in it ) and the unusual frame  on my bike.  They made a suggestion as to how the bike was being mounted and sent us on our way.   The user manual of the Pea Pod clearly states that the "Giant Pea Pod trailer is designed to attach easily to any full-size bicycle" so we were confident the issue was resolved.

A week later on July 15th 2015 the trailer flipped again, this time with our two kids inside, resulting in serious injury to our 4 year old daughter.

Her finger was trapped between the bike frame and the concrete while the trailer slid to a stop.  This resulted in the need for emergency orthopedic surgery from a pediatric orthopedic hand surgeon to save her finger.  She is now looking at life long reduced functionality and possibly additional surgeries as she gets older. 

We took the trailer back to Steamboat Ski & Bike Kare and explained what had happened. They agreed that the unique frame on my Navara mountain bike changes the mechanics of the trailer mounting system and this potentially contributed to the accident.
justification: The incident resulted in serious injury requiring emergency surgery and potential lifelong disability, meeting severity level 4. The likelihood is 3 as the incident occurred twice under similar conditions.

The product arrived in several boxes that were not strong enough to handle the weight of the bells. They said they would get this corrected from the vendor, CAP Barbell. incident_description:
The product is the RAGE (Fitness) Platform Squat rack.  It is used for weightlifting; primarily for squats and bench presses.  The squat rack comes with two steel "J-Cups" . The J-Cups are essentially metal "hooks" on one side.  On the other side of the J-Cup is a metal cylinder (about the size of a cigarette).  The J-Cups are attached to the rack by turning the J-Cup horizontally, threading the metal cylinder into one of the rack's pre-drilled holes, and then turning the J-Cup 90 degrees.  One J-Cup is placed on each of the two vertical posts of the squat rack.  These two J-Cups are used to hold a barbell and any assorted weights on the barbell.  Because the J-Cups are the sole support of up to 700 lbs. (according to the description on Amazon) it is important that the J-Cups are well made.

My 17 year old son was doing bench presses using the Rage rack when he noticed that the barbell (with 200+ lbs. of weight attached) had slumped sightly on one side.  He initially thought the J-Cup's metal cylinder had bent but when he looked at it he realized that the J-Cup's metal cylinder had basically "fallen out" of the J-Cup because it was improperly welded to the J-Cup.  The safety issue concerns the fact that if somebody is doing bench presses and the J-Cup fails (i.e., the metal cylinder comes out of the body of the J-Cup), then the barbell and attached weights could unexpectedly fall on the head, neck, chest or face area and cause a serious injury or death.   

The submitter added he uploaded four photos..One is of the squat rack itself, two views of the JCup and a close-up of the defective JCup along with the other JCup.  The submitter noted the defective JCup does not show any stress or wear on the steel itself..It looks as if the metal cylinder was not properly welded into the hole was has been drilled into the metal. The submitter also added he has another squat rack at home and the JCups are drilled all the way through the JCup, a headed metal bolt is then placed through the outside of the JCUP, and then the head and the top of the bolt are welded to the Jcup.

The submitter concluded the way this Jcup is made is not right and is very dangerous..The rack is supposed to hold 700 lbs., and there is no way that this design will support this weight.
justification: The incident describes a potential for serious injury or death due to a defective J-Cup failing during use, with a likelihood of occurrence rated as possible given the described defect.

incident_description:
I was using the diamond sports catcher facemask in an amateur adult baseball league game. The pitches in this league are typically 70-75 mph. I suffered a concussion when I was struck in the mask with a foul tip. The impact jarred my jaw closed in a violent way, leading to a concussion as diagnosed by an MD. 

A week following the incident, I was diagnosed with Bell's Palsy, which impacts a nerve channel in one side of your face. The nerve channel begins in your ear, which is where I noticed most of the pain since the concussion has been. Since July 18, I have had pain on the right side of my head around temple, jaw, and cheek bone area as aftermath of this incident. I also have had difficulty moving the right side of my face, as a result of the Bell's Palsy.
justification: The incident resulted in a concussion and subsequent Bell's Palsy, which are significant injuries.

incident_description: I received the product Baby Buns "Surfs Up" Rashguard and Swim Trunks Set from Kohls.com.  Upon opening it I was hit with a strong sweet smell that seemed to be coming from the swim trunks.  My husband and I kept smelling it trying to figure out what it was we were smelling, and then realized it was almonds.  We thought it was odd, but I didn't think much of it until I started feeling ill a short while later.  I then remembered that certain chemicals can give off the smell of almonds and thought I ought to report it given that this is a product for toddlers who are more sensitive to toxins than most of the population.  Perhaps it's nothing, and I hope that's the case, but I thought it was worth sharing our experience.
justification: The individual experienced illness after exposure to a strong chemical smell, indicating potential harm, though no severe injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The 2012 Cervelo P2 triathlon bike is equipped with a 3T Auro Pro Handlebar. Today while training on the Washington & Old Dominion trail (fully paved) I hit a minor hole at approxomately 20 mph and in an instant, the arm rest fell completely off, the screws holding it in placed sheared off. Luckily I managed to control the bike and come to a halt and retrieved the arm rest that fell to the ground. Upon my return home I looked into this problem and noticed that the shearing of the screw tops was a common incident both here in the US and oversas. I sent an e-mail to 3T but after reviewing the othe incidents doubt I will get a response. Since the handlebars are made in Taiwan I suspect that the screws are sub par and jolt could cause the screw tops to shear off.
justification: The incident involved equipment failure (handlebar arm rest detachment) but no injury occurred, and the rider maintained control.

incident_description: While riding through the woods checking my deer stands and food plots the steering went out on my Can Am Commander 1000XT. I lost all steering ability of side by side and hit a ditch and a tree. This is the second time this issue has occurred with this same Can Am Commander 1000XT. On 12/14/2014 while riding in the woods I lost all steering ability and hit a tree. The steering couple between the power steering unit and rack and pinion had completely stripped out. BRP replace the power steering unit, coupling and rack and pinion system with all new parts and assured me the problem was fixed and would not happen again. Five and a half months later the same exact issue has occurred again. The coupling has stripped out and failed again causing total lose of control of the side by side vehicle.
justification: The incident resulted in a collision with a ditch and a tree due to steering failure, indicating potential for injury.

incident_description:
On Monday-July 20, 2015 at approximately 9:00 a.m.-my husband was using a Precor Super Squat.  He had 810 pounds loaded on the device (9 x 45 lb plates per side), he had completed his exercise set and pressed the pedal which is supposed to place the safety catch in place.  

He proceeded to lower the weight, however,the safety was not in place as he expected.  With his right leg forward and his left leg in line with his body, 810 pounds came down and forced him into a rapid squat.  His left leg bore the brunt of an 810 pound squat.

The result is a quadriceps tendon that is 80% ruptured and a patellar tendon that has yet to be determined damage.  He will be undergoing surgery in the near future (next week or so) to repair the significant damage to his left leg.

He has used this piece of equipment many times and is quite familiar with its operation.  This injury did not happen as a result of inexperience.
justification: The incident resulted in significant injury requiring surgery, hence a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 2 (unlikely) as the user was experienced and the equipment malfunction was unexpected.

incident_description: The flywheel on my Racermate Computrainer exploded sending pieces of shrapnel through my wall and ceiling, and injuring my hamstring. Violent explosion occurred as I was calibrating the trainer at approximately 30 mph. Trainer was purchases in 1994 or 1995.  There was no known damage to the flywheel prior to the incident. I am the original owner.
justification: The incident resulted in injury to the hamstring and significant property damage, but no death.

incident_description:
I purchased a neck flotation device for my baby called the "Otteroo" in 2015 and started using it on my baby around May 2015.  She's only used this device around 6 times or so, so it is by no means 'worn'.  The last time we used it, I had trouble getting her chin to stay above the chin rest.  Once I managed to get her chin on top of the chin rest, I placed her in the bathtub for a swim.  About ten minutes into her swim, her lower jaw/chin was completed underneath the chin rest! and she was about the drink bathwater or drown, so I promptly pulled her out of the tub.  Once I pulled her out of the tub, I noticed that the Otteroo was deflated a bit.  So I submerged the Otteroo under water to check for air leaks and sure enough there was an air leak along the seams near the front left side of the device.  This is the 2015 supposedly stronger version, not the recently recalled 2014 version.
Not only did it leak air, my baby's very normal sized/looking chin could not stay on top of the chin rest, which is very dangerous and her chin used to be able to stay on top of it when she was younger.  She started using it at 2 months and she is now 4 months old.  Her chin stayed on top of it fine when she was younger, but now that she likes to bite and chew on things, the chin rest can no longer hold up her chin.
justification: The incident involved a deflated flotation device and a near-drowning situation, but no actual injury occurred. The likelihood is high (4) as the device failed to function as intended during use.

incident_description:
I have received 2 separate defective Otteroo baby floats. otteroo.com for product

First otteroo was preordered months before finally arriving due to delays in production in China. I allowed my daughter to use the floaty once in the bathtub, after following the instructions included for proper inflation and testing for air leaks as recommended. After that first use, the floaty deflated considerably, and on our second use, there was a clear air leak visible when held underwater.
At this point, I contacted otteroo to report the issue and request a refund. They did refund my money, and insisted on sending me a replacement at no charge. 
Once I received the second otteroo, we used it again in the bathtub. Again, the first use was fine and we did not find any air leaks. Before the second use (in the tub) I tested it for leaks by holding it underwater. Again, no leaks were present.

incident_description:
Both my wife and I have received numerous injuries from using Master Lock Street Cuffs bicycle locks.  Most of the time the injuries are small cuts similar to paper cuts.  However, both of us have gotten more serious cuts where the bleeding was difficult to stop.

Because of the danger of infection from a bike lock's dirty environment, we have both looked for the cause of these cuts and finally determined that the chrome plating was flaking off of the locks.  The plating loosens and flakes may stand up like little scalpels.  From time to time a flake slices the skin when the lock is handled.

I contacted Master Lock and they offered a refund and replacement locks.  Since my concern was all the users of these locks, I refused the refund, but I did accept replacement locks.  The replacements exhibit the same problem.  Master Lock has some of the failed locks, as well as photos documenting the problem.

After Master Lock confirmed that they had received the faulty locks, they stopped communicating with me.  Finally after about six weeks, I received email that said, "have not found any additional examples of the specific failure mode you described", even though my replacement locks have failed in the same way.  In addition Master Lock cautioned that, "Any future emails or correspondence being sent directly to <name withheld> will not be responded to."  And finally, "Master Lock now considers this complaint to be closed."

My concern was never for any personal compensation for our injuries, but rather for the safety of other people using these locks.  Thus, this complaint.
justification: The incident describes injuries from flaking chrome plating on locks, including serious cuts and risk of infection, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is high (4) as the issue persists even with replacement locks.

I own a 2014 specialized shiv pro race triathlon bike.

This Saturday, April 18, 2015, while riding my shiv, I ran over a crack in the pavement and the left aero bar "snapped" off. This is exactly the issue that has caused the manufacturer to recall the bike.

This is unbelievably dangerous and I am most fortunate that I was able to maintain control of my bike and not crash at 26 mph. I took my bike into the Local bike shop that sold and assembled the bicycle for me, but evidently they manufacturer still has not shipped the replacement parts to the store. 

For a company that is supposed to pride itself on making quality, high-end bicycles and "components", it is hard to fathom that they can sell a product without testing and ensuring that the bolts that hold the bike together so that it can be maintained safely.
justification: The aero bar snapped off during use, posing a significant risk, but no injury occurred as the rider maintained control.

incident_description:
Arctic Cat Snowmobile Model 2014 XF7000

Problem: Fuel leak under seat due to poor workmanship.

  A fuel leak was discovered under the seat of this snowmobile after noticing a strong scent of fuel on clothing inside the right knee down to the boot. The origin of the leak was traced back to the fuel port under the seat where fuel puddles in a tank cavity below the battery and wiring harness. Movement of the machine while in use spills the fuel from the cavity down the side of the tank where it is free to come in contact with clothing and the running board before continuing to the ground below. Leaking may not be noticeable while the machine is still

 On the fuel port below the seat is a nipple where the fuel line attaches and is to be secured by a crimp type clamp. The clamp has been installed however it freely rotates around the nipple and fails to secure the fuel line. There are no band markings on the rubber fuel line indicating that the clamp was ever on the line and somehow slipped off. Another point to note is that the diameter of the crimped clamp is less that than that of the fuel line suggesting it had been crimped prior to installation rather than after to secure the fuel line in place. With an assembly this simple to build and confirm a workmanship fault such as this should be considered negligence.

  It is important to note that in the summer of 2014 this machine was recalled for fuel line issues and as a result had already been returned to the dealer for repairs. So this issue is either a new problem or the service technicians have been improperly trained to correct the original problem. In either case the faulty machines remain in or have been returned to service while representing a high risk of injury to the operator. Most operators wear protective winter clothing that cannot be quickly removed and if ignited while saturated with fuel it could prove deadly.

  Further aggravating this instance is another issue of poor welds on the front bumper assembly which allow it to break apart even under moderate stress. Although this is not directly related to the fuel line issue it is the second workmanship problem we have discovered in a week on this machine. Together they strongly suggest a general trend in quality which may extend to other safety risks that may not surface until these and other machines have more hours of operation on them.
justification: The fuel leak poses a significant risk of fire, which could be deadly given the operator's clothing and inability to quickly remove it.

I was wearing a helmet but the impact was rather hard. I went to City MD, and although they thought I was OK they suggested I go to the Emergency Room. I went to Roosevelt Hospital where they did a CT scan and thought they discovered some bleeding under the brain... a possible subdural hematoma. They kept me in the emergency room for approximately 12 hours and monitored me carefully.  After the second CTscan they felt I was OK and said I could go home but should take it easy for the next couple of weeks and report any abnormal conditions related to a head injury. 

My family doctor followed up and said I should not ride my bike for 3 weeks. I did have a minor headache for about a week as well as a stiff neck. Now I am OK. Had I not worn a helmet the chances are I would have suffered a serious brain injury or even death. 

The hospital bill was $11,000. plus $123 for the City MD walk in clinic. 

I do not know if I was at fault for using a defective pedal or if the factory was at fault. I just do not want others to get hurt.
justification: The incident resulted in a head injury requiring medical attention and monitoring, but no long-term harm or death occurred.

incident_description: I used the recalled product as a sponsored rider for the Super Squadra cycling team in 2009. In the closing laps of the Tulsa Tough Blue Dome criterium, my front wheel came into contact with another racers rear derailleur. It is common for crashes to occur in the closing laps of criterium races, and for wheels to come into contact with pedals and derailleurs, and to break spokes. However, I feel the design of this wheel, which led to the collapsing, was responsible for the severity of my crash. As I came into contact with the competitor's rear derailleur, one of the spokes on the front wheel broke. This caused the entire wheel to de-tension and the wheel to collapse, causing me to crash severely. I broke my collarbone in three places, and later required a bone graft and a large plate to rebuild the broken bone. I believe the severity of this crash was in large part a result of the faulty design of this hub. Had I just broken one or two spokes in the wheel, I would have been able to maintain control of the bike, and possibly avoid a crash. Safely exiting a race after breaking one or two spokes is common place in these types of events. Further, I have photograph evidence of the collapsed wheel directly after my crash can be seen online, here, http://supersquadra.net/?p=1134. I also saw that Zipp sponsored racer [REDACTED] of the Garmin professional team crashed at the Giro d'Italia the same year, and photos showed he had a similarly collapsed front wheel. I am shocked that in light of these high profile incidents, it has taken Zipp this long to recall this product.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe injury (broken collarbone requiring surgery), justifying a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as crashes in criterium races are common but not every crash leads to such severe outcomes.

incident_description: On January 26,2008 I purchased a 2008 Polaris RZR from a private party. The fuel tank was half full with no signs of any problems. Driving home I decided to fill the fuel tank. After arriving home, I was unloading the rzr and I smelled a strong gasoline odor. I was able to locate it's source and found that it was leaking from the seal on top of the gas tank. I went on-line to the Polaris RZR help chat/blogs to see if this has been an on-going problem. What I discovered is many others have had this same problem. One of the posts reported that there was a safety recall on this model and year polaris. Digging deeper on the internet I found this was true but for only certain months that the rzr was made. I called Polaris and gave them my vin number and they informed me that my vin is not included in the recall. I find this to be unacceptable because if it was a safety issue for those other UTV's then why not for this one as well. The fuel tank is in the passenger compartment right under the passenger seat. If the gasoline ignites both driver and passenger would be severely burned and or result in death. This is obviously a design flaw and/or the fuel tanks were not engineered correctly to withstand  the riggers of an off-road vehicle. The razors specific information is vin # [REDACTED]. It is a 2008 Polaris RZR 800EFI. I am requesting that you add this year make and model to the recall list. Polaris should have to stand by their product and make it safe when they become aware there is a problem.
justification: The incident involves a fuel leak with no reported injury, but the potential for severe burns or death if ignited, and the issue is reported by multiple users.

incident_description: while riding my 2008 arctic cat prowler 650 xt i heard a pop in the front end the wheels locked and caused me to loose control. after i crashed i checked to see what had happened and noticed tht the front differential had busted and that the gears were showing. after searching multiple web sites i found that this is a problem with this model year and the arctic cat has known about this problem for some time as it has been reported to them by many customers. also after going to arctic cats own website to order the parts to repair my machine i iscovered that the parts that are defective in the prowler is also the parts that are defective and have been recalled in the 2008 and 2009 atvs
justification: The incident involved a mechanical failure leading to loss of control but no reported injury, and the problem is known to affect multiple units.

incident_description: Throttle cable stuck in the accelerator position. Almost causing serious injury. Engine and bike we inoperable after the incident.
justification: The throttle cable sticking almost caused serious injury, indicating a potential for injury (severity 3). Such incidents are not common but possible (likelihood 2).

incident_description: Sunday January 18, 2015 Honda Pioneer 700-4, with operator and two passengers,  caught on fire when debris that collected on middle skid plate came into contact with the exhaust system.  The fire was extinguished and damage to the unit was minor.  The skid plate had previously been replaced by the Manufacturer/Dealer because of the October 2014 recall.  This incident took place after the recall repairs had been performed.
justification: The incident involved a fire with no reported injuries, and the damage was minor, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is unlikely (2) as the issue was previously addressed under recall.

incident_description:
I was riding my bicycle home from work and the next thing I knew I was being lifted into an ambulance.  My front fender had folded up and jammed into the back of the fork, and the fender stays had cinched tightly down into tire.  My bicycle came to such a violent halt that the forks were bent backwards and I was thrown over the bars.  I had a concussion, fractured spine, and a variety of other injuries.

I have since learned that Planet Bike, the manufacturer of my fenders, started offering safety "release tabs" for their fenders around 2010 that are intended to prevent such accidents.  It turns out that the problem of fenders locking up bicycle wheels has been known in the bike industry for some time.  Other manufacturers, notably [REDACTED], provided safety releases as long ago as the mid 1990s.

These accidents happen with no warning, and if it is your front wheel that locks up the results can be disastrous.  I suggest that anyone using fenders should check with the manufacturer to find out what, if any, safety devices are available, and whether the fenders meet any established safety standards.  Also, ask yourself if staying a bit drier is worth the risk - you don't want your front wheel to lock up at speed.
justification: The incident resulted in a concussion and fractured spine, indicating significant injury, hence severity level 3. The description notes that such accidents happen with no warning, suggesting a possible occurrence likelihood.

incident_description: My 12 year-old daughter (approx. 80-90 lbs.) was swinging on our Adventure Playsets Pathfinder swingset recently when one side of the swing's caribiner-style link failed, sending her to the emergency room with a concussion.  Upon inspection afterwards, the caribiner had worn completely through both its shaft and the "protective" nylon bushing, and wear was also shown on the top pivot.  These swingsets, being made primarily of wood, require periodic inspection and attention, which for me also included an inspection of the metal and plastic parts.  I do not recall noting any wear on the caribiner itself or the nylon bushing upon my last inspection within the last few months, other than surface rust around the threaded portion (which was not involved or otherwise a factor in the break).  Although the swingset is about six or seven years old and is exposed to seasonal changes here in Southern Ohio, I would have expected that it would last long enough for one child's use and also perhaps our four year-old son's use, and not to be such an unsafe product.
justification: The incident resulted in a concussion requiring emergency room treatment, indicating an injury (severity 3). The failure of the caribiner suggests a possible likelihood of recurrence if similar wear goes unnoticed.

incident_description: The neck on the fuel tank is developing a crack which leaks gasoline down the outside and onto the riders legs and snowmobile suit.
justification: Gasoline leaking onto the rider's legs and suit poses a risk of skin irritation or burns, indicating an injury risk.

incident_description:
On November 27, 2014 I purchased a 3ft Little Tikes trampoline from Target in Oak Creek, WI as a Christmas present for my 5 year old son.  Christmas came, he opened the trampoline and we set it up.  Three days after using the trampoline, minimally and in our living room well supervised, the welds are separating from the frame in three locations. 
We have repeatedly contact Little Tikes, submitting photos to their warranty department, provided the UPC and manufacturing codes and a copy of the receipt.  What we've received in return are calls to our home number when no one is home to answer the phone, despite providing both work and cell numbers.  No message has been left in any of the attempts.  The one (single) attempt to reach me at my office (direct line) was followed by a hang up as soon as I answered.
We have given Little Tikes two weeks to contact us to handle this situation, we are now reporting through you and will be reaching out to the BBB and attorney general's office in Wisconsin.
justification: The trampoline welds failed but no injury occurred, and poor customer service response is a common issue.

incident_description: I have NordicTrack Revitalize Inversion System 2.0 I bought new from Sears about 3 to 4 years ago. It has always been inside. On or about July 1 2014 I went to hang. I got it and locked my ankles in. And started over and when I went over the lock pin let go and I fell strait down on my head I was passed out or knocked out for awhile. When I came to I could not move my arms or hands for almost an hour. Since then I have had CAT scans and two MRI's. I have two disks in my neck crushed and one in my back. The doctor has sent date for surgery on my neck and then he will do my back. It is all very painful. I have found the cause was of failure was the spring on the lock pin that holds your ankles locked in colasped and let the pin drop out of place let my ankles go. Bam!
justification: The incident resulted in severe injuries including crushed disks in the neck and back, requiring surgery, which falls under severity level 4 (Death was not mentioned, but injuries are severe). The occurrence likelihood is considered rare (1) as such equipment failures are not common.

incident_description:
In the end of March of last year... 2014, I was riding my newly aquired/bought 2006 Polaris Hawkeye 2x4.

Near the end of our day I was coming back to the trailer to load up when my atv automatically throttled up on its own... causing me to swirve, hit several mud ruts. I immediately turned the handlebars to avoid crashing into huge rocks when felt a hard drop and a sound of something snapping behind me. 

Only seconds afterwards I was thrown... off the Polaris Hawkeye... and slammed to the ground onto large rocks. After a few minutes of shock... I felt dizzy and nausea... then a extreme pain in my leg. I attempted to get up but was I dire pain and unable to. Being prior military I'd instructed my wife and friends to get the ramps for the atv... force slide it under me and loaded me into the back of our Envoy... where I rode to the emergency room at Community Hospital. 

After several xrays and an hour later the doctor told my wife and I I had to go into immediate surgery. I had a Sub Capita break of the ball of my hip from the force of fall off my atv.

SEVERAL months later... in October last year I was able to move around and work agin close to normal.
My wife and I are by no means rich so I wanted to fix my atv... to one day go riding again... hoping that this was just a "freak" accident. I saw my Polaris Hawkeye had actually broke off at the sub frame in the rear and the left tire was leaning majorly. The lower arm was hanging semi loose and the cv joints were busted.
I called several friends, who ride religiously and told them the problem, and had some inspect it.They all concurred that..."that is not right... it shouldn't just BREAK like that unless it faulty".

I couldn't afford to have it professionally fixed... so my brother in law and I welded it up extremely strong and tough. I've called Polaris 3 times about this... and each time was told there's nothing wrong with their machine... it had to be "user fault". However...after several hours of research,  I've found literally over a hundred complaints on forums. Both for the "automatically throttling by itself" andthe "Faulty Sub Frame". Yet Polaris fails to acknowledge ANY of it. Hopefully this complaint will result in something positive so that nobody else should have to suffer the pain, agony, and  consistent problems I'm going thru because of Polaris' negligence. 

Thank You for your time and concern. Respectfully and Sincerely Submitted, [REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in a severe injury (Sub Capita break of the hip) requiring immediate surgery and months of recovery, placing it at severity level 3. The occurrence likelihood is set to 3 (possible) based on the description of similar incidents found in forums, though not officially acknowledged by Polaris.

incident_description:
(10/03/2014) The consumer stated that he was shooting at a target. He grabbed the forearm grip. When he released the trigger, the string cut off three quarters of his thumb. The crossbow did not have a thumb guard and his thumb was up to high in the rail.

The consumer held the finger together and went to the ER in Nacogdoches,TX. The consumer had to get nine stitches to put him thumb back together. The consumer stated that there were several broken bones in his thumb and hand.
justification: The consumer suffered a severe injury requiring stitches and had broken bones in his thumb and hand, indicating a severity level of 3.

incident_description:
The fuel tank fill neck has cracked on my 2009 Crossfire 800 Sno Pro. The leak spills gasoline out on the tank and onto your legs while riding the snowmobile.

You cannot take off your snowmobile suit indoors as the gasoline fumes are horrible.
justification: The cracked fuel tank causes gasoline to spill, posing a fire hazard and discomfort, but no injury is reported.

incident_description: I purchased a Jamis Aurora Elite "adventure bike" that is configured as a touring bicycle with 35 mm tires on road bike wheels and fenders.  I am 5'11", 75 years old and was sold a 55 cm bicycle by a Jamis dealer, namely Tread bike shop in Campbell, CA. on January 4, 2015 for about $1650. The bicycle is sold without pedals so that a user can use any comfortable pedals, such as pedals with toe clips, which is the type of pedal that was installed by the dealer for me.  I did not notice at the time of my test ride and purchase but later discovered that there is a toe clip interference situation that appears to be Jamis design defect.  The defect is that when the pedals are horizontal and one pedal is in a maximum forward position,  the pedal interferes with the fender by a large amount on low speed turns, stopping the turn and leading to a rider imbalance and possible fall.  Even if the front fender were removed, the front tire would create toe clip interference when pedals are horizontal, i.e. in the maximum forward position.  The dealer claimed that toe clip interference is a "normal" condition and I must ride so that interference does not occur when turning.  From many years of riding, I know that this is not possible because turns must sometimes occur very quickly and there is no time to adjust pedal position.  Moreover, horizontal pedal position is the normal pedal position when coasting through a turn.  The toe clip interference was not disclosed as a warning in the Jamis product literature and is a design flaw and hazard, particularly for seniors, in my opinion.
justification: The incident describes a design flaw leading to potential falls, but no actual injury is reported.

incident_description:
My NordicTrack E9.0 Elliptical Trainer (manufactured by Icon) suffered two structural failures in the span of 4 months.  The machine was purchased in Nov 2011 and the failures occurred in Sept 2014 and January 2015.  In both cases the failure caused me to abruptly fall from the machine.  

First incident in Sept 2014 the ramp (part #307098) and Aluminum Track (part #306606) suddenly buckled along a fold in the steel (estimated #14 gauge) causing the left pedal arm to "derail".  I lost my balance and fell off the machine.  At the time the machine was still under warrantee so Nordic Track replaced the parts at no cost and I repaired the machine.  

The second incident occurred on Jan 7, 2015.  This time the Crank Arm (part #306600) on the left side failed.  A roughly 1/2 steel shaft suddenly sheared causing the left roller arm to disconnect from the disc and fall to the ground.  When that happened I was thrust forward slamming my chest into the left upper body arm.  Again, I lost my balance and fell off the machine.  

When I reported the failure to customer service they told me the machine was now out of warrantee and I would need to purchase the replacement part for $214.  

I am a 220 pound male about 5' 8" tall and use the machine in my home for about 45 minutes about 4 times per week.  2 other 125 pound females use the machine for about 30 minutes about 3 times per week.  My point is the machine is not under any unusual stress.  

I have photos of the parts that failed.  The company is clearly using inferior materials for their structural parts.  This presents a physical danger to users of the machine because these parts can fail suddenly during exercise causing the user to slam into the machine and fall from their momentum.
justification: The incident caused injury when the user was thrust forward and slammed their chest into the machine, resulting in a fall.

incident_description:
The consumer and his son were riding in the off road vehicle and had been driving for approximately 3 minutes, when he lost control of the steering wheel.  The consumer was traveling very slow, so he and his son were not injured.  They were not injured.  The vehicle had to be towed back to his home.

The vehicle was serviced in 2011 for a recalled air filter.  This may have been a service bulletin, because there isn't a recall for air filters on the CPSC's site.

The consumer called the manufacturer after discovering Recall Alert 13-718, but the mfr's rep. told him that his vehicle was not included in the recall.  The consumer asked the rep. what should he do from this point.  The rep. told him he could contact customer care to see if it was under warranty, but he did not offer anything else to the consumer.

The vehicle has less than 1000 miles of use since the consumer purchased it.

The consumer said he paid $14,900.00 for the vehicle.
justification: The incident involved loss of control but no injuries occurred, and the vehicle had to be towed.

incident_description:
In recent Consumer ReportsÃÂ bike helmet tests, one manufacturerÃÂs helmet failed a crucial part of our safety evaluation, and we are concerned it might not reliably protect cyclists in the event of an accident.
