incident_description:
Re:  Can-Am Commander Steering Failures

Product Safety Administration:

I purchased a 2013 Can-Am 800R Commander in November, 2012 from Four Seasons Motor Sports in Rye, Arizona. On the 11th of this month I was helping a friend on his elk hunt and shortly after coming down a very steep hill, the steering on my machine went out like snapping you fingers. Fortunately, I was going slow enough that I was able to stop before hitting a tree.

Since then I have discovered that you issued a recall on the 2011 and 2012 Can-Am Commanders for this very problem. I have also been able to ascertain that the same coupler that failed on these recalled models is the same coupler on the 2013 models.

I phoned your corporate office and after explaining my circumstances, I was informed that my machine was not included in your recall.  I was told that if I took it to a Can-Am dealer for repairs that the dealer could open a case or claim for me and I might be reimbursed.  I have done just that and my machine is now at Four Seasons Motor Sports in Rye, Arizona.

My real issue here is that it is obvious that BRP is aware of the danger with these faulty couplers. The coupler that has failed on 2011-2013 Commanders has been modified on the 2014-2015 models. It now has more bolts holding it in place and one that is supposed to stop the unit from sliding down and uncoupling.

If you look on the "Can-Am Commander Forum" you will see that my problem is not an isolated issue. Steering loss on Can-Am Commanders is happening all over the country. If you do not step up and correct this faulty coupler, someone is gong to be seriously injured or KILLED. I have been in several places with my machine that would have proved fatal if the failure had occurred.

I thought I was purchasing the best UTV available when I purchased your machine. I now have serious doubts and have safety fears if I keep the machine after it is repaired. I implore you to take the necessary steps to correct this issue before you are involved in a class action lawsuit because someone has been permanently disabled or killed.

Seriously Concerned,
justification: The incident involved a steering failure but no injury occurred, and the likelihood is high given the reported widespread issue.

incident_description:

The consumer stated that this is the same issue as the Teryx4 that was recalled in Rel #14-741.


(12/01/2014) The consumer called the company. H advised them of the problem. The consumer stated that the company did not seem interested.
justification: The incident involved a tree limb coming through the floorboards but no injury occurred, and it was noted as a known issue from a previous recall.

incident_description:
Product: Bicycle Handlebar Grips:
MFG: PDW (Portland Design Works)
Model: Whiskey Grips: I used these grips in good faith on my mountain bike for a few months. They caused some
minor pain and soreness at first and during use that I disregarded thinking they needed to break in, it was subtle.
Then came the Incident, nothing out of the ordinary, no crash, just hanging on to the bars and riding normally.
It was after a typical downhill section on a favorite local mountain bike ride. Both hands became bruised and sore,
the term "jackhammer" comes to mind to describe the feeling I had experienced).
I found later that I had injured both my thumb joints, my wrists & hands were very sore and swollen for days.
I contacted the mfg at the time, had a couple e-mail exchanges, but let it go to recover.
However, more than 6 months later, I am still feeling the affects of the injury's incurred from this incident.
These grips are very nicely made and presumably beneficial based on the claimed resemblance to an ergonomic
shape, however they are too hard and slippery to use for mountain or other biking where impacts forces occur
readily. They take extra effort to hang on due to being slippery, don't have any padding or cushioning at all, and I
doubt the Ergonomic shape is right compared to similar products, "Ergonomic" is not regulated as far as I can tell.
The execution is a product a failure - a wolf in sheep's clothing. It should be recalled along with other PDW grip
products. They simply shouldn't be making grips for biking that are so hard and slippery, it defeats the purpose.
justification: The user sustained injuries to both thumb joints, wrists, and hands, with effects lasting over 6 months, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as the incident happened during normal use but may not affect all users.

incident_description:
On Sunday, December 14th, 2014, my 4 year old son was riding his recently purchased MXR16 Raleigh bicycle with training wheels in Long Beach, California, at relatively slow speed under the supervision of his mother, a registered nurse, and father, an epidemiologist, on a relatively clean and fenced in paved recreation area at a local middle school.  The child was wearing a Bell helmet as well as Bell kneepads and elbow pads.  At approximately 1:00 pm under clear weather, my son slowly tipped over, just out of the reach of his father, and fell to his right onto the pavement while gripping the handles and remaining in a seated position.  He immediately let out a scream and began intensely crying.  As his father picked him up, he noticed a significant amount of blood emanating from the childÃÂs right pinky finger, which was amputated cross-sectionally from the left to the right side and was dangling from a sliver of skin.  The pinky finger of the right hand had become caught between the right handle of the handlebar and the pavement and the cylinder of the metal handlebar, under the weight of the bicycle and the 35 pound pre-schooler, had protruded from the rubberized handle.

The child was taken immediately to the closest ER at Long Beach Memorial Hospital, where the ED diagnosis was ÃÂright hand fifth finger tip of the finger with near complete amputation approximately 3 mm segment no involvement of the MCP, PIP, DIP.  With tuft fracture.ÃÂ  The patientÃÂs finger was cleaned, stabilized, x-rayed, immobilized with xeroform dressing, the patient given pain management mediation, and the patient was referred for a next day visit with a local hand and wrist specialist.

The next day, the hand and wrist specialist physician informed the patientÃÂs mother that the amputation was not amenable to surgical intervention, prescribed antibiotics and analgesic medication, and advised to follow up with Kaiser Permanente, the patientÃÂs health care system.  The patient is currently (12/27/14) being monitored by Kaiser Permanente as the fingertip tissue dies, dries, and falls off.
justification: The child suffered a near complete amputation of the right pinky finger, which constitutes a significant injury.

incident_description: Crossbow cut off 1/3 to 1/2 of my thumb while I was attempting to sight it in.
justification: The incident resulted in a significant injury to the thumb, which qualifies as a severity level 3. Crossbow accidents are uncommon but possible during sighting activities.

incident_description: The product is a Trident Series 2 Ultraviolet Water Treatment System.  After being away from our home for a few days, I walked around back to check the pool equipment and found this product had caught on fire.  It is completely destroyed and has damaged the adjacent DE filter as well.  Upon doing a web search of the product, I noticed your office had directed a recall of the product in May 2014.  We did not receive this recall notice for some reason.
justification: The product caught fire and was destroyed, causing damage to adjacent equipment, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: I own a NordicTrack E7.1 Elliptical machine.  While exercising on this equipment, the metal pedal arm broke at the wheel connection causing me to fall.
justification: The incident involved a broken pedal arm causing a fall, which indicates potential for injury but the description does not confirm injury occurred.

incident_description: We have had a swing set made by Flexible Flyer for about three years. This past Sunday (November 30, 2014), my 6 year old daughter was swinging on one of the swings. A few minutes later, she came screaming to me holding her hands up in the air. I asked her what happened and she told me that she had fallen off the swing. I asked how she fell off and she said that the swing broke. I looked at the swing and the seat was broken in half. Luckily, when the seat broke, my daughter was holding on to the chains and when she fell, she landed on her butt. She did have cuts, scrapes, and pinch marks on her fingers, hands, and wrists. I am still horrified at what could have happened had she not been holding on so well or if it had been my 4 year old son swinging since he only knows how to swing laying over the swing on his stomach. I contacted Flexible Flyer about this incident and all they did was say they were sorry and offered to sell me two replacement swings. I would hate to hear of another kid getting hurt or worse from these swings breaking in half. I would think they could find a material that doesn't break in half after only 3 years of sporadic use. Thank you.
justification: The child sustained cuts, scrapes, and pinch marks, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The incident occurred after 3 years of sporadic use, suggesting the likelihood is possible (3).

incident_description: While riding my Can Am Commander 1000 in the woods I lost all steering ability and hit a tree.
justification: The incident involved a loss of steering leading to a collision with a tree, which implies a potential for injury.

incident_description: On November 15,2014 I was riding my Honda 2014 Rancher 4x4 on a straight dirt road about 30-35mph in 4th gear when the front right suddenly dropped to the ground and pulled to the right. I was sent flying in the air about 20 ft. in front of the ATV the 4 wheeler flipped over forward. When I got my bearing the ATV was upside down. I was trying to figure out what happened there was no debris  or anything that would have cause this. I did not collide with another person or anything else. When I looked at the ATV I noticed that the front right lower knuckle had broken away from the ball joint and the upper control arm had broken off the frame. There was damage to the front right brush guard, handle bars and the rear rack. I also had sustained injuries I had injury to my low abdomen ,left thigh muscle tear ,post-concussive syndrome, and right leg injury.  There is also a witness to this incident.I then took the ATV to the dealership where I purchased it , on 11/17/2014 and they said this was not covered underneath the warrantee because they said I hit something mind you I also purchased additional warrantee for $700.00 but it is still covered under the initial manufacture warranty. Yes it was in a collision because the front right lower knuckle broke in half and that caused the ATV to hit front first into the ground and then flip over .  They also told us that we should get insurance and file a claim through my insurance company isn't that fraud. This was not cause by me hitting or jumping or anything like that it happened out of the blue. The ATV has 111 hours and 686 miles it is a 2014 this should not have happened and it could have killed me. It seems Honda would want to fix this problem and find out why this happened because someone out there could be killed or hurt so bad they might have injuries that are not reversible. Now I have a brand new ATV that I can't use, can't fix because it will cost 6,500 and I can't do it myself because they said it will void the warranty they won't do anything with it. Please look in to this it could seriously save someone's life and not allow these businesses to get away with fraud or say they guarantee something and then don't when something happens.
justification: The incident resulted in multiple injuries including a muscle tear and post-concussive syndrome, warranting a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) given the specific mechanical failure described.

incident_description:
Skywalker Trampolines 48 In. Round Zoo Adventure Bouncer with Enclosure
Bought this for my 2 year old and 4 year old. Today my 4 year old showed me how the metal retaining ring in the center had breached the foam and has sticking out significantly. This can pose a high risk of injury if a child hits or falls into the protruding metal bar. I have since contacted Amazon.com and they issued a full refund and had me send it back to them (they paid the UPS cost). 

I took pictures of the protruding metal bars and posted them on my 1 star review and can send them to you as well if you need them. In my opinion after review of the design the bars on the center ring pose a immediate and significant probability of injury to a child and this product should be pulled for corrective engineering.
justification: The metal retaining ring protruding poses a high risk of injury, though no injury was reported in this incident.

incident_description:
Bauer Equipment sells the Bauer 7500 Hockey Helmet, which uses an adhesive to secure  padding inside the helmet. The helmet is certified by the Hockey Equipment Certification Council (HECC) for 6 1/2 years.  The problem is that after an initial period the adhesive begins to fail and the inside padding falls out, eventually making the product unsafe.

 1. ) A little over a year ago the side padding on my son's helmet began coming unglued, and detached  from the helmet. Several months later the pad on the crown of the helmet began falling off as well. At the time the helmet was just over 1 year old and in excellent condition other than the adhesive. During this period we contacted 3 Bauer retailers but were told there was nothing they could do.
2.) This October, the padding on the brow fell off, and rather than reattach as we had with the other padding, we stopped using the helmet as we considered it unsafe.

Given that ice hockey is the number 2 sport for rate of concussion, and that the 7500 is a top selling helmet, this would seem an issue that Bauer would want to address. However, this is not the case.  Bauer does not offer any repair training for its retailers, and simply suggests they not offer a repair for helmets that are older than 365 days  (even if the helmet is one week beyond the warranty period and in excellent condition). When contacted directly, Bauer corporate  said it could offer no repair solution. Bauer abdicates any responsibility for materials or workmanship beyond 365 days, and to cover itself against liability recommends that any helmet with this issue, regardless of overall condition, be disposed and replaced.
justification: The helmet's adhesive fails, making the product unsafe, but no injury has been reported.

incident_description:
The consumer reported safety hazard with the way the steering is designed on the ATV.

The consumer stated that the tie rods hit the lower shock bolt when the steering wheel is turned all the way to the right or all the way to the left.

The consumer stated that in 18 mile ride, he wore out half of the bolt. The consumer believes that if he would have continued riding the ATV, the blot would have completely been worn out and come apart.

The consumer was riding this on a national forest area, flat-wooded land.

The consumer stated that he contacted the manf and spoke to [REDACTED](legal team). She informed him that he is the only one who has complained about this issue. She advised him to take a class on riding side by side vehicle. She informed him that he was probably driving too fast or improperly for the vehicle. 

The consumer stated that he was driving 3-5 mph when turning. The consumer stated that no where in the owner's manual does it state that you cannot turn the steering all the way to the left or right. The consumer stated that he was riding this vehicle properly.

The consumer stated that he verified at the dealer that all of the Wild Cat Trail 700 ATVs by this manf has this issue, even the 2015 models.

The dealership informed him there is nothing else they can do since the manf is not doing anything about it.

The consumer stated that the ATV has 180 miles on it (75 miles from dealership, rest used by him).

The consumer stated that the motor has been replaced because of dirt ingestion from an unknown location. The manf informed him that it is normal for the engine to ingest dirt.
justification: The incident involves a safety hazard with potential for mechanical failure, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I am the owner of a 2014 Polaris 570 Sportsman ATV which on 2 occasions(6/14/14) and (9/6/14) caught fire and melted the seat. Other electrical and mechanical components of the unit were melted and damaged during the second fire. On both occasions the unit was being driven by my son at 3-4 miles per hour.Polaris replaced the seat after the first incident, but did not make any other repairs. After 6 weeks in the dealer's shop the unit was released to me and I was advised it was safe to drive..We were not given any information about the cause of the first fire nor were we advised to take any precautions in operating the unit. After the second fire we contacted Polaris and were advised to take it to a dealer of our choice. It has been at that dealers for 7 weeks and to date no repairs have been made. I have contacted a number of Polaris dealers, talked to several 570 owners and done a great deal of research on the Internet. Polaris has had a substantial number of problems with this unit overheating and melting seats and other mechanical problems. There have also been a number of reports of gasoline in the fuel tank "boiling" to such an extent that gas or gas fumes have apparently been forced out of the fuel tank vent tube and migrating into the instrument cluster and/or light assembly. Since there are no other flammable materials on the unit I believe gas leaked or was forced out of the fuel tank and was ignited by the exhaust or an electrical spark. Polaris has not given us any hint of the cause of either fire nor have they given our dealer any instructions on testing for the cause of the fire or repairing our unit.The dealer who has the unit in his shop is very reluctant to free lance on repairs. We need a resolution and a recall may force Polaris to pay more attention to the problem.
justification: The ATV caught fire twice, causing damage but no reported injuries, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to multiple reports of similar incidents with this model.

incident_description: lost top part of left thumb.while sighting in my crossbow at the range ,I was there for a few hours with my wife n son .A lawyer trying to make crossbows safer for people to use prompted me to fill this out (glad he Did).Crossbows need thumb n finger guards guards(should be mandatory).
justification: The incident resulted in the loss of the top part of the left thumb, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: I purchased about 10-12 of these tubes from Walmart for various use for the kids at our lake house in the summer. After using some of them on the lake on several different occasions some of the kids broke out in a rash. It was never anything life threatening just a huge inconvenience and made for not so happy kids. I assumed the kids were just allergic to them, although it seemed odd because it was a few different kids from different families. Either way, I ended up throwing all of them out. A waste of about $300. I didn't think much of it and my wife was looking stuff up online and she came across the recall. I am not really looking to get anything out of it, I mean what's done is done and we instead just purchased different tubes, but I thought I should report on it as well so others would know. I don't blame the company, these things happen and I don't really understand how this happens with a product like this, but that is life. Thank you for listening to me share my thoughts and experience.
justification: Several kids developed a non-life-threatening rash from using the tubes, indicating a minor health impact but no serious injury.

incident_description:
Riding my 2012 Salsa Vaya about 10 mph, I hit a relatively small pothole and ended up flying over the handlebars. Upon inspection, I found that the front fork had bent just above the brake bracket. When this fork bent, it caused the wheel to cock in it's securing brackets which in turn applied full front brake. My bike sustained several broken parts in the incident: broken front fender, broken chain, bent fork. Also, I had soft tissue damage to my right shoulder causing one day lost work.

I was researching a replacement fork and ran across a recall for forks manufactured by CWI. So I disassemble my fork to find it was not part of this recall. This fork had different manufacturing codes: 2012 06 18.
justification: The incident resulted in soft tissue injury causing one day lost work, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is unlikely (2) as such incidents are not common but possible under certain conditions.

incident_description: On December 5, 2013 I was using my inversion table made by Paradigm. I had went back twice and hung 2 minute each time. On the 3rd time when I went the piece that holds my feet in shot off and dropped me on my head, breaking a vertebrae in my neck and a blood clot.
justification: The incident resulted in a broken vertebrae and a blood clot, which constitutes a severe injury.

incident_description: While wearing the pedometer it caught fire and burnt me.
justification: The pedometer caught fire and caused a burn injury.

incident_description: I was driving a 2014 Arctic Cat prowler 500 HDX XT vin #[REDACTED] on 11/27. While going up a hill it skipped a few times so I turned around and headed home it skipped a couple more times then ran fine. After I got turned around I smelled gas I looked over to see a small puff of smoke come out from under the seat on the passengers side. I shut the machine off as soon as it was off I heard a poof and flames were coming from under the seat I attempted to use snow to put it out but it went up too fast. Before the fire department could arrive it was a total loss
justification: The incident resulted in a total loss of the vehicle due to fire, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
This Bike Friday folding recumbent bicycle has light use, but had multiple failures that led to 3 accidents. The first failure involved a breakage of a seat support. This support was made out of unprotected aluminum that had been hand drilled. The aluminum had oxidized and the metal broke when I hit a bump. The second accident occurred when a quick release failed and the bicycle collapsed. The final accident occurred when the bicycle broke in half.

The bicycle was manufactured 8 years ago, but has been stored in a dry place and was not used very much. It had 800 miles on it. I personally know 2 other people with this bicycle and one had similar problems with the seat and with the quick release. I also asked an engineer friend who looked at it and concluded that it was not a good design. There should be a lock on the quick release. There should also be some sort of coating on the aluminum so that it does not oxidize.
justification: The description mentions multiple accidents due to design flaws, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence and potential for injury.

incident_description:
I purchased a bike rack to carry bags on the back of my mountain bike. The rack came with two tubes that are
connected to the sides of the bike frame with a caliper mechanism that has a latch to open and close. The inside
latch or the left leg latch catches the heel of the foot/shoe when your pedal is up and causes you to be stuck on the
latch. I could not pedal while stuck on this latch and was almost jettisoned off of my bike while pedaling. I was
quite a distance from my home when I discovered this design flaw and had to pedal on my toes and consciously
twist my left foot outwards so that my foot would not catch on the pedal again. This same mechanism is sold by the
thousands to other consumers on the internet and is a real danger to those using the product.
justification: The incident describes a near-accident due to a design flaw, which could lead to injury if not addressed.

incident_description:
I ordered a Black Mountain Products AntiBurst Exercise Ball Weight Limit 2000 Lbs from Amazon.com.  I brought it to my office, where I used it off and on as my desk chair for approximately 2 weeks before it exploded while I was sitting on it.  No, I'm not 2000+ lbs; I'm about a tenth of that.  

The force of the explosion knocked me down and backwards, into my regular desk chair.  I bashed my head against the bottom of my desk chair (on one of the "spokes" that hold the wheels), and was in some pretty intense pain for a few minutes.  5 days later, the goose egg on the back of my head has subsided somewhat, but it's still incredibly sore and I still have a headache.

My coworkers heard the explosion of the ball, and came running.  Thankfully, we have in our building (the California state capitol) an RN who is always on duty.  I asked them to call her down to our office so she could check me out.

The RN did a concussion check, put an ice pack on me, and told me to visit the ER if things got worse; i.e., if I got dizzy or disoriented.

I went to put a product review on [REDACTED]today, and much to my surprise, there are several DOZEN reports like mine on that product.  Several folks have had to go the ER, and several babies who were being held in their parents' arms also had injuries.  

This manufacturer is making defective products, and should be warned/stopped.
justification: The incident resulted in a head injury with ongoing pain and a potential concussion, warranting a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to multiple similar reports of injuries from the same product.

incident_description:
The consumer purchased the used ATV from an online seller.

The consumer stated that the elbow that carry fuel to the engine broke. The fuel drained onto the hot engine and caused a fire. This happened while the consumer's son was riding the ATV on a trail in Canada. The consumer stated that he was able to extinguish the fire with soda. 

The consumer stated that his son was able to get out of the ATV without any injuries.

The consumer stated that the fire damaged the engine and melted the plastic around the engine. The consumer also stated that the seat belt release was only couple inches away from the fire. 

The consumer spoke to an authorize dealer for the manf ([REDACTED]- Franklin, OH). The dealer asked the consumer to bring the ATV down to him. The consumer is taking the ATV down today (10/15/14). The consumer stated that the dealer will examine the ATV and get a hold of the manf in regards to the incident.

Not included in any recalls.
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injuries were reported, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated 3 as such mechanical failures are possible but not frequent.

Item  Xootr.com mg kick scooter with rear fender brake

incident_description:
The consumer would like to file a report against his unit because he feels it poses both a safety and fire hazard.

10/01/2014 The consumer noticed that his unit was leaking gas. Christmas 2013 was the first time the consumer noticed that the six-gallon fuel tank, located under the passengerÃÂs seat, leaked gas. At the time, he attributed the leakage to spillage or possibly when he pumped gas The unit only has 716 miles. It is only ridden during the winter time by the consumerÃÂs daughter and wife. The consumer reports that as long the fuel tank is full, it will leak gas. He is only able to fill it half way to temporarily avoid the problem.

10/09/2014 The consumer contacted the retailer and explained to them that his unit was having the same issue as the ones he saw that were included in a recall (Alert #08-521). He was informed that his unit was not recalled. He was advised that it was out of their hands to fix the problem he was having. They told him that a new fuel tank would cost six hundred dollars. The consumer asked if they would adjust the price given the circumstance. He was told that he would have to pay the full price.

The consumer does not report any injuries to him or his family during this incident.

incident_description: The quad jumped to the right while being ridden on a trail. It threw the rider and rolled down a hill. The rider didn't think he hit anything.

incident_description: My son was putting his air rifle away and it was broken down and as he closed the barrel, it misfired and shot a pellet. justification: The pellet caused an injury requiring emergency room treatment and follow-up medical care, but no death occurred.

incident_description:
A Volton electric bicycle had randomly-dangerous acceleration problems;

1) while holding the bike from a complete stop; the bicycle rips out of ones hands 
2) while riding the bike randomly accelerated from low speed up to 20mph unexpectedly
3) while waiting at stop at a traffic intersection, the bicycle randomly accelerated without notice

These are the types of accelerations that could cause serious or fatal injury.  

I just became aware that you are the regulatory agency for this product.     Record needs to be made of this incident. 

------ Original message ------ To the company by Email
From: 
Date: 9/9/2014 9:41 AM
To: volton;
Subject:Severe Safety Issue and Concern, too dangerous to ride.

[REDACTED]

Today I had several instances in traffic which were highly dangerous both relating to random-maximum accelerations without the throttle during a coast or from an at stop position.    I walked the bicycle home because it has computer-electrical concerns and is unsafe to ride.    

 
These accelerations required me to emergency brake but could have easily resulted in a major accident whereby;

1) The bike would accelerate from stop into traffic
2) The bike would accelerate from a controlled speed to an uncontrolled maximum speed randomly and without notice
 
Neither of these cases pertained to a pedal assist as the bike engaged itself at maximum power for an extended time even when the throttle was in the off position, with the pedals being stationary.      

I would suggest that you notify your insurance carrier and supplier of the aforementioned issues and concerns, and you need to determine whether or not these issues are pervasive.    I am departing Florida the 12th and therefore we need to arrange a return of this device.

Regards [REDACTED]
justification: The incident describes dangerous, unexpected accelerations that could lead to serious injury or death, though no actual injury is reported.

incident_description: While riding a trail a stick came through the floor board of our Teryx 4 Kawasaki 2012 model. The passengers side floor board was in pieces after the stick came through. I Heard there was a recall on this model and years floor board but hadn't received a notice yet. Our friends with same make model and year got a recall notice but we did not, when I called Kawasaki they said our vin did not have a recall but would stand behind it
justification: The incident caused damage to the vehicle but no injuries were reported, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as recalls are not universal and depend on specific VINs.

incident_description: I was riding my bicycle to work when the fork broke/sheared in half, separating the front end of my bike from the frame. I was thrown off my bike and sustained facial injuries requiring emergency medical attention, including abrasions, upper jaw fracture and lacerations to my upper lip that required stitches.
justification: The incident resulted in facial injuries requiring emergency medical attention, including fractures and lacerations, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
(07/02/2014) The consumer stated that the inner tub was inflated to be used as a floating device. The tube was placed in the water. The consumer was floating down the river on the tube. After about 15 minutes, all of her skin that was in contact with the inner tube started burning. It was a burning sensation. The burning sensation continued as long as she was floating down the river . After about an hour, the daughter tried the same inner tube and got the same burning sensation. 

After forty minutes, the consumer got back on the inner tube. She is still getting the burning sensation. 

The consumer did not require medical attention at the time, but did use ice and a cream to alleviate the pain.

(7/07/2014) The consumer went to Trios Health Urgent Care in Kennewick, WA. It was determined that she got a chemical burn from the inner tube.

The daughter did not have the same pain and discomfort and did not require medical attention.
justification: The consumer suffered a chemical burn requiring medical attention, indicating an injury, while the daughter experienced discomfort without needing medical care.

incident_description:

He was riding the bike for a few mins at a speed of 20 mph.  He fell downwards to the pavement with a force, the handle bars were squeezed toward his chest.  This incident caused his prior surgical wound to open in his abdomen about 4-5 inches.  He drove to the Grand Haven Hospital in Michigan where he was treated and sent home for follow up.

The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.


Consumer feels that this bike is a safety hazard and should be investigated.
justification: The incident caused a prior surgical wound to reopen, requiring hospital treatment, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the description of the bike's failure.

incident_description: We got a sportspower tramplonine from walmart 2012 and we set up up an moved for about 8 months.  When we came home the boys started to finally get to use the trampoline it ripped all along the bottom of the trampoline and my child fell out.  Then there was two more rips along witht he big one.
justification: The trampoline ripped, causing a child to fall out, but there is no mention of injury.

incident_description:
Caller stated that her 3 year old son's bicycle helmet was placed outside the garage and she noticed that the plastic covering was melting.  This incident occurred 20 mins after the helmet was sitting in 80 degrees temperature.

5/8/14 She contacted the retailer and she was informed that they would replace the helmet and to contact the agency to file a report.

Caller feels that this helmet is a safety hazard for children.
justification: The helmet melted but no injury occurred, indicating an incident without harm. The likelihood is possible as it happened under specific conditions.

incident_description:
I was riding my electric bike down a paved street when the folding frame cracked at the weld 
connecting the front part of the frame to the hinge that was still attached to the rear part of the frame. While I was able to coast onto the sidewalk, the bike split in half before I could stop so I was still moving about 8mph. I suffered cuts and bruises on my right arm, stomach and ankle. This bike 
was well maintained and had about 2300 miles on it, mainly street riding and paved bike paths.
I contacted the company on 7/28/14 and sent a customer service representative [REDACTED] the 
photos of my bike, but not of my injuries. The company response was to send my an upgraded 
full frame, not folding and  I would have to transfer the existing parts to the new frame. I did
not get the name of the witness who saw my crash, so I have not pursued legal action.  At this
time I am trying to warn riders of this bike of the potential danger, since the company has not sent
any warnings so far to registered owners like myself. They posted an updated manual on their
website noting that the frame could crack on this bike, but they do not notify registered owners
of this, for obvious reasons.
justification: The incident resulted in cuts and bruises, indicating an injury, and the description suggests that the frame cracking is a known issue with the bike model.

incident_description: My husband was jumping on the trampoline and did a flip and the safety net tore. We tried to fix it but it just keep going every time one of the kids fell into it.
justification: The safety net tearing when kids fall into it poses a risk of injury, though no injury was reported in this instance.

incident_description: Installed Bell Universal Bicycle pedal. Everything appeared to be fine. Noticed wobbling today on the left pedal. When I stopped to look at the pedal it came out. The threading in the crank arm had been completely stripped by the pedal
justification: The pedal came out due to stripped threading, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I purchases a Coleman 40-quart Thermoelectric cooler, Model 5645, less tahn 90 days ago.  After a a short time of use, the plug that connects into the car outlet melted.  I am in the process of trying to return the item to WalMart (or via Coleman, if necessary); I don't know yet if they will give me a problem about the return.  I have read several similar stories on-line of this happening
justification: The incident involved a melted plug but no injury was reported, and similar incidents have been reported online indicating a possible recurring issue.

incident_description:
We have an Adventure Playsets The Sherwood Wooden Playcenter, model 1-AP049-07. The monkey bar beams have already been replaced professionally under recall, and these are the beams that failed.

My 6-year-old son was swinging on one of the swings, and we heard a loud crack. Fortunately, we were able to get him off the play set before an emergency situation occurred. The crack is visible, right at the screw attaching the beam to the slide/playhouse.
justification: The monkey bar beams cracked but no injury occurred as the child was safely removed.

incident_description: Rapid Exhaust deflation failure while on surface of water prior to scuba diving. We own two tusa's both have failed. Been diving 25 years - approximately 3500 dives. These are the fifth set of BCDs that we have owned, never had prior failure. One failed 11-2013 contacted tusa usa. Mine failed 9-2014. purchased both on 1-4-2011. tusa bc platina evolution and tusa bcd liberator sigma. Failure while diving could cause an out of control ascent with injury or death. Cable end in mechanism fails due to crimp failure.

incident_description:
On 9/17/2014, the consumer went hunting in the woods. When he was about to use his cross-bow, his right thumb got stuck in the unit and was almost completely detached from his hand. He states his thumb was only held ÃÂby the skin.ÃÂ The consumer is left handed.

The consumer sought immediate medical attention from the nearest ER. The severed thumb was reattached with screws and received fifteen stitches. 

On 9/22/2014, the consumer contacted the manufacturer.  The consumer was told they would send a box so that he may ship the cross-bow back to them in order for them to determine if it is a defective item. The consumer agreed to this and was then asked if he wanted a replacement. The consumer refused the option to receive a replacement and specified to the representative that he was seeking compensation for his medical bills.

On 9/22/2014, the consumer contacted the Better Business Bureau and was told to contact CPSC. They informed him there had been thirteen similar incidents with this firmÃÂs cross-bows.

The consumer reports no other incidents/injuries sustained from this product since it was purchased last year.
justification: The consumer suffered a severe injury (thumb almost completely detached) requiring medical intervention, placing the severity at level 3. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to the mention of thirteen similar incidents with the same product.

incident_description:
Giro bicycle helmet, number 202-3201, serial number Y7095198.
I have written the following letter to Giro Sport Design in Santa Cruz, California (I have shipped this problem helmet to that company):
On July 2, 2014, I was wearing that helmet while riding my bicycle. I fell from the bicycle, on my right side. On August 24, 2014, my son, who is a physician, noticed signs of a possible subdural hematoma, and he took me to a hospital where I was administered a CT scan which confirmed his suspicion. He and I were then taken by helicopter to a hospital where the subdural hematoma was drained by the neurosurgical team. This was a significant injury which, as I say, required hospitalization (five days, with attendant complications).

	I am sending you this helmet, not for the purpose of initiating litigation, but so that your research department can examine the helmet with the goal of improving the safety of your product.
justification: The incident resulted in a significant injury requiring hospitalization and neurosurgical intervention, but no death was reported.

incident_description: Rainbow play systems rusted ladder.  Kids cut hands. Only 3 years old. Company states they have only seem this one other time. Manufacturers defect. Lifetime warranty but they are asking for an additional $300 to fix the problem.
justification: Kids cut hands on a rusted ladder, indicating an injury (severity 3). The company states this has only happened once before, suggesting it's unlikely (likelihood 2).

incident_description: On September 14,2014,I got in a bicycle crash resulting in a broken arm due to unsafe and dangerous make and model of the bicycle tire which were in use that day---The make of the bike tire is from Continental Tire, Ultra Sport 700X25C stock#25-622. The tires have a smooth tread texture which appear to be slippery and the crash is the result of the tire design.the tire is on the rear of the bike and when I've made a left turn,the back wheel fishtailed out and the crash ensued--tires are DANGEROUS!!!
justification: The incident resulted in a broken arm, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
125 cc Coolster atv gas tank leaking fuel on hot engine. I have a 2013 model, which has a shutoff valve screwed into the bottom of the tank.  The threads have Teflon tape wrapped around them to keep valve tight but gasoline eats up tape and gas leaks out. This valve is right above head on engine. You can shut the valve off but gas keeps leaking because it is threaded into gas tank. This is a fire hazard.  Also, when you leave atv in garage it keeps leaking. This is very dangerous for kids to be operating.  This company should do a recall immediately on this problem. I called my dealer where I bought the atv. He said he had problems with others that leaked. He said I need to buy a new tank with a valve, he also said they changed the design with a welded tube to tank and a valve that was mounted away from engine. So I bought a new tank with valve, but the new one I got was just like old tank that leaked. I thought it might be ok, valve seemed to be tight so I installed this new tank and I didn't leak right away, but after it sat for an hour, guess what it started leaking again. I called my dealer and he would talk to his supplier about this problem. He called me back and said they would send a updated tank. Waited a couple of weeks, never received a tank, called dealer again was surprise that I didn't receive tank. He said he will call his supplier again. I have not heard anything since. This design on this old tank will cause a fire in a building and cause injury on a child operating this atv. I have looked at new design on a newer 125cc coolster , it is a lot better design. Hopefully this will be taken care of.

[REDACTED]
justification: Gasoline leaking onto a hot engine poses a significant fire hazard, which could lead to injury or death, especially for children operating the ATV.

incident_description: Using exercise resistance bands from GNC, one band broke under normal usage, snapped back and resulted in a near miss.
justification: The resistance band broke under normal usage, resulting in a near miss, indicating potential for injury but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: I purchased a Michelin City tire, 26 x 1.85 (47-559) size, from Bike Nashbar on Aug 7, 2014. I installed the tire on Aug 22 and inflated to a pressure within the recommended range as stated on the tire (min 36 psi, max 87 psi (6 bar)), using a new floor pump, with a gage, purchased at the same time from Bike Nashbar. The rim was manufactured by Mavic and is rated for the size tire installed. Within minutes, while I was standing next to the bicycle with the newly inflated tire, the tire burst, due to the tire bead popping off the rim. As a result of the burst, which caused a very loud sound, I lost significant hearing in both ears, but especially the right ear which was closer to the source of the sound. I also developed an earache in the right ear. My bicycle rim was warped significantly by the force of the burst. I believe there is a design flaw in the tire with respect to the recommended maximum pressure printed on the tire. As evidence that Michelin knows the max safe pressure is lower than that stated on the tire, the Michelin website (which I checked only after the incident) currently states a max pressure of only 65 psi (4.5 bar) for the  47-559 tire.
justification: The incident resulted in significant hearing loss and an earache, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) since such tire bursts are not common but have been documented.

incident_description: I bought a Vivere 2 person hammock.  When the hammock was hooked up and sat in, the ropes on one side snapped and the person fell to the ground hitting her head.  The ropes were tied together in a knot and the hammock was tried again.  the other side of the hammock ropes started to crackle and also ripped apart, making the person fall to the ground a second time, this time hitting their legs and rear end on the ground.
justification: The person fell twice and hit their head and legs, indicating injury but no death.

incident_description: Driving the cart and the steering assembly broke causing me to crash. There were four people on cart.Two people had minor injuries . There is already a recall on the 2009 models. They need to look into earlier models as well. I was denied the free steering assembly when I asked a authorized dealer because of the year model. justification: Two people had minor injuries from the crash, and there is a known recall on similar models indicating a potential defect.

incident_description:
Hello,

I just wanted to check to see if there was a recall, and wanted to bring the issue to your attention. I hope you understand my concern. Thank you,

incident_description:
I just purchased a stability ball, 75cm, made by GoFit.com from Big 5 Sporting Goods in El Cerrito, CA.  It is rated to 1000 lbs.  I brought the ball home and inflated to 75 cm, determined using the measuring tape that came with the ball.  When I went to remove the measuring tape from around the ball it burst.  This is clearly a defective product an should it be burst during use it could result in a serious injury given that this type of equipment is recommended by physical therapists for individuals with back injuries (which is exactly why I purchased this product).

This product should be recalled and refunds offered to consumers in my opinion.

I contacted the company, Wild Sports, via phone and told the customer service rep what happened. incident_description:
I am writing to report that my 11 week old, 11lb, infant slipped through the otteroo the first time we used it last week. The packaging does not give nearly enough information regarding usage safety. I followed the instructions to the "t" and this accident still occurred. Luckily my baby was only under water for 2-3 seconds, but this could have been so much worse. We were so frightened and she wasn't breathing for at least 5-6 seconds after I rescued her. I called our pediatrician who urged us to take her to the ER for a chest X-ray. They told us to never use the otteroo again... They don't believe it is safe.

After the accident occurred and my baby was declared 'okay', I decided to look on otteroo's web site for further info regarding this product I received as a gift. I was very surprised to see many more safety usage instructions that were not listed on the product nor the product's packaging. One thing I learned online is the fill height of the tub, which instructs to fill tub with at least 2feet of water, and to fill so the baby's feet touch and baby is vertical. This is imperative information!!! Most tubs will overflow at 2 feet of water. I never fill my children's bath water with more than 10-12 inches of water and would only do so if stated on instructions.

This is very concerning to me and there should be a booklet/pamphlet with all instructions, FAQs, and safety precautions included in the package with the product. Everything that is online needs to be included in this package. I will never recommend this product as it could have killed my infant had I not been right there responding as quickly as I did. We spent an evening in the ER, spent $100, and spent at least two days worrying  that she may have inhaled water into her lungs, watching for signs of pneumonia. This is not okay. No product for infants should ever result in this sort of scare. I don't know if she slipped through because she was only floating in 12 inches of water or because you have a defective product or that usage should be based on head circumference??

incident_description:
I own a 2006 Polaris Hawkeye Magnum ATV, which I purchased new . It has approximately 2200 miles on it.  While out for a ride with my husband and grandson on the 4th of July we noticed the rear tires were towed out, angled inward at the top. We were riding up a steep canyon road  with a 2000 foot drop off when we noticed the right axle was actually pulling out of the drive train.  We immediately stopped the ride, got the trailer and did not use the ATV for the rest of our camping trip.   We brought the ATV home and my husband jacked it up and looked to see if he could see a problem.  We had recently put new tires on and wanted to make sure that something wasnÃÂt messed up because of that.  My husband greased the  A-Arms and when he took the quad off the jack the tire and axle had returned to their normal position.
We then went for a ride on July 13, but after only going a mile the tires were again towed out and the axle was coming out of the drivetrain. We again stopped the ride and trailered the quad. 
I began to research on line possible causes for the problem I was experiencing. I found that several people have experienced the same problem and it is because the subframe breaks.  We checked my quad and mine was also broken on the right side. The subframe is made out of very thin metal that is only tacked welded to the undercarriage.  Others who have blogged about this problem state the metal is so thin I cannot be reinforced or welded. The part must be replaced.  The part alone costs on average $300. I also discovered that Polaris developed a beefed up subframe for subsequent models, so it seems as though they knew there was a problem.  Had the axle completely pulled loose and the tire would have come off while I was riding in that canyon, I and my grandson who was riding with me, could have been severely injured  or killed. 
I called a Polaris dealer to see if there was a recall since I saw several people who had had the same problem.  He stated there were no recalls for the subframe.  
I might understand this part breaking if I was jumping and riding like a crazy person, but the fact is I am an over 50 woman who uses this quad for enjoying our mountains, wildlife and  mushrooming, on leisurely rides not exceeding  15-20 MPH.  My husband is very strict about how fast we ride and where we ride.
Polaris needs to take responsibility for a poorly designed part, before someone who isnÃÂt as observant as we and others were  to something that just didnÃÂt look right,  is injured or killed.
justification: The incident involved a mechanical failure that could have led to severe injury or death, but no actual injury occurred as the issue was detected and addressed in time.

incident_description:
I purchased a new Emotion Neo Cross EN703 bike from a local dealer a few days before the accident.  I was traveling downhill on a paved road a short distance from my house, going about 25 mph.  I travel this road nearly every day by bike, so I am quite familiar with it.  The road has a series of speed bumps, and I had traversed the first two of them without difficulty.   The last I remember of the accident was approaching the third.  I woke up being loaded into an ambulance.  The EMT's said the front wheel had separated from the bike.  I was admitted to the hospital with a concussion, multiple abrasions, a damaged mouth, and a nose that will require plastic surgery.

On examining the bike wreckage I determined that one of the dropouts on the front fork had fractured, allowing the wheel to separate.  The fork is an SR Suntour NEX 012 Series Model #4610.  I note that this same model fork has been recently recalled by Trek and Scott bikes for the same kind of failure.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries requiring hospitalization, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is unlikely (2) as the fork failure is a known issue but not common.

These safety stops are used by users to help the user restrict the range of motion, depending on the exercise they are doing.  With the addition of the black spacer bars, the lowest safety pegs cannot be used & in this case when the user needed the lowest range of motion for a decline, the safety stops rested on top of the black spacer bar & the added weight hit one of the unlatched safety stops causing an unbalanced bar.  I brought this to the attention of Matrix & was told to have the users use the safety stop, located above the black spacer bar.  I asked them for instructions for this & was told that this would be outside the range of support.  They would not provide safety instructions. incident_description:
We were riding in a 2012 Kawasaki Teryx4 ATV when the floor directly under the front passenger's foot rests was damaged. We were traveling at only 5 mph over rugged terrain on a four-wheel drive trail in the Arapaho National Forest near Allenspark, CO. This section of the floor is just behind the front wheels of the vehicle and is constructed of thin plastic. Rocks, sticks, and other debris that are thrown from the front wheels often make contact with this plastic, which is the only material protecting the rider's lower body. This was the third incident in the past year where the foot rests have been smashed in on our vehicle. Both the driver and passenger sides are vulnerable to damage and is potentially a dangerous defect that could result in severe bodily injury. 

The dealer we bought the vehicle from has repaired the floor twice before but now they are refusing to do so because we are no longer covered under the warranty. They also are acting as if we are the only customers to ever experience this problem but that certainly is not the case. Here is a link to a thread on Teryx Forums where numerous customers are having the same problem. On page 17 there is a picture of one injury resulting from this defect: 

http://www.teryxforums.net/teryx4/17883-weak-floor-17.html

Kawasaki has addressed this issue in newer models of this ATV by attaching a thin piece of metal to the affected area. We had this piece installed by our dealer but only on the passenger side of the vehicle, yet the floor has broken through yet again. There have been no recalls from Kawasaki for this problem. The only options at this point are to fabricate reinforced parts yourself or purchase a very limited number of aftermarket accessories.
justification: The incident describes repeated damage to the ATV's floor with potential for injury, and references a documented injury case, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to multiple incidents reported by the user and others.

incident_description:
My wife's 2009 Arctic Cat Z1 Turbo sled (Snowmobile) burst into flames while trail riding in Vermont on 3/6/14. I reported the incident with the Arctic Cat, Inc Legal Department and Customer Care Center on 3/7/14.

We purchased two brand new 2009 Z1 Turbo identical sleds off the showroom floor from the Manager, at PJÃÂs Power Sports, in Rangeley ME on 3/12/09. The dealer informed us that they needed to prep the sleds for delivery. We stopped in the shop the day before delivery, to find that one of the engines and odometer were completely removed from the sled. I asked the four mechanics in the shop what was going on, and they all were silent. I insisted they answer my question, and they said to speak to the Manager. I did speak to the Manager, and he informed me that they removed it to put it into another sled for a different customer. Needless to say, I was not happy as the sleds were brand new. This is evidenced by the incorrect engine serial #B11-402985 (non-matching) in my wifeÃÂs sled that caught fire. The correct engine serial # is B11-402279 according to the Manufacturer.

Upon delivery of the new sleds, they overheated, leaked coolant, and needed to be serviced. In addition, the used odometer replacement they put on my wifeÃÂs sled had over 1,500 miles on it. They serviced the sleds to repair the overheating and replaced the second odometer with a new one. However, the overheating on my wifeÃÂs sled was a chronic problem. We had them serviced at Hudson Cycle Center, NH for continued overheating and recall updates at a later date.

Currently, my wifeÃÂs burnt sled VIN serial #[REDACTED] was in pristine showroom condition with roughly 1,100 miles on it and my sled VIN serial #[REDACTED] is in pristine showroom condition with only 1,303 miles on it. They both were purchased, maintained and the recalls were completed in a timely manner by an Authorized Arctic Cat, Inc dealer.

The details of the incident are as follows: 

My wife and I were trail riding in Vermont on 3/6/14. I stopped on the trail because I feared my sled was on fire when gray smoke started pouring out of my sledÃÂs engine compartment. I took the side engine cover off and the smoke subsided. My wife pulled up with her sled, about two feet behind my sled, and stopped. Coincidentally, her engine compartment immediately exploded and burst into flames.  Fortunately, she was able to jump off her sled in time before the gas tank exploded, and I moved my sled a safe distance. Within a minute, her entire sled was engulfed in a 15 foot high wall of flames. I canÃÂt imagine what could have happened if she was still cruising along the trail when the fire erupted. 

The sled is a complete loss. I have documented photos and video of before the fire and during the fire. I paid a recovery team to retrieve the charred remains of my wifeÃÂs sled which is in my possession at my home.

I researched afterwards that Arctic Cat, Inc did a Recall on that specific sled, a 2009 Z1 Turbo on 10/26/09 due to FIRE HAZARD resulting from a DEFECTIVE PRODUCT, according to the U.S Consumer Product Safety Commission, due to 33 reported incidents including 8 vehicle fires.  Arctic Cat, Inc denies any responsibility and declines to investigate our incident.
At this point, we have two sleds, one charred remains and the other a potential danger to my life, which I will no longer feel safe riding. Given the fraudulent nature of the engine swapping, the inexplicable nature of the fire, and the product recall, I feel compelled to report this product to the Consumer Product Safety Commission for investigation.
justification: The incident involved a snowmobile bursting into flames, but no injuries or deaths were reported, aligning with severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is unlikely (2) given the specific circumstances and recall context.

This caller is reporting because he is positive that someone is going to be injured if these are not recalled, the company is not forced to repair with a different scheme of connection or a reinvention of nuts and washers used.

I am in receipt of the report dated 04ÃÂ01ÃÂ14 regarding the failure of the main pulley to remain attached to the axil assembly on an Icon Health & Fitness I ProForm lllOE Eliptical exercise unit.

A defective Icon Health & Fitness I ProForm 1110E Elliptical exercise unit was shipped to and received by the customer as referred to in the report. Icon Health & Fitness I ProForm had previously dispatched a contract
technician; who,stripped two exterior screws {one on each side of the unit) preventing disassembly,inadvertently broke a plastic housing component while inspecting and diagnosing,retrieved a single main pulley screw from the bottom of the unit, disabled the elliptical, failed to repair the unit and indicated follow-up contact would be forthcoming. Arter an extended period of time waiting for follow-through by the company with a repair or replacement,the customer filed complaint with the TN Department of Consumer Affairs seeking remediation in the form of compensated straight-line loss of use,time and repair or replacement. When the company failed to respond by 03ÃÂ28-14,access to the unit was obtained by extraction of two failed exterior screws. The fault was diagnosed and videotaped.The nature of the defect posed a clear public safety hazard. The CPSC was immediately contacted,the public welfare demanding it.

The crank pulley is attached by 4 screws which were not secured in place by means of a split-ring locking washer, internal nor external locking washer, nylon-locking nut, top-locking nut, the use of a through-bolt and nut,jambÃÂ­ nut,wicking thread-locking compound,polymer-patched fastener or any observed means inclusive if sufficient torque to prevent the screws from "backing-out" in normaloperation. In fact,The sole user first observed the defect within 30 minutes of operation with what he is on record as characterizing as "what sounded like a screw falling out." In fact,of the four pulley screws,two had fallen completely out of the pulley.As previously mentioned,one of which had been removed by the contract technician the day of the in-home service call by prying into the plastic shell.Another was recovered from the bottom of the frame and is visible in the first raw footage segment enclosed on the DVO. The second raw footage segment enclosed on the DVD contains some explicit language as the nature of the manufacturing defect,relative threat of bodily injury,and ease of mitigation was made apparent to the owner.The video segment compiled 03-29-14 shows the untouched/untampered position of the third screw which has virtually no remaining thread engagement (i.e. it has nearly backed completely out/unscrewed itself}.

It is my considered opinion,that Icon Health & Fitness I ProForm ModellllOE should be investigated for product recall of all units manufactured.  Made most apparent with the two contributing factors of the speed of failure was observed and the risk of bodily injury being likely when the main pulley, not being adequately secured in place, comes unexpectedly and violently unfixed from the crank-axil.
justification: The incident describes a defective product with a clear risk of bodily injury due to mechanical failure, though no injury has been reported yet.

incident_description:
I was riding my bicycle on a country road at about 18mph and hit a small seam in the road as it transitioned onto a bridge.  The stem on the bicycle broke and caused me to lose control of the bicycle.  However, I did manage to avoid a crash.  After the incident, I took the bicycle to a repair shop and replaced the carbon fiber stem with an aluminum one.  The bicycle mechanic told me that he had heard several reports of Thompson carbon fiber stems breaking.  I called Thompson and was told to send the stem back for analysis, which I did in late August of 2013.  I have heard nothing from Thompson to date concerning the analysis which it was to perform.  Reproduced below is my letter to the manufacturer, which was enclosed with the stem I returned for analysis.

[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]

Thomson
7800 NE Industrial Boulevard
Macon, Ga 31216

Gentlemen:

Enclosed is a Thomson Elite X2 bicycle stem which broke on a recent ride.  Fortunately, I was able to avoid a serious wreck as one side of the stem remained attached.  This stem was installed on a [REDACTED] bike I purchased a little over 3 years ago.  The stem that came on it was too long and I had this one installed instead when I had the bike fitted at a bicycle shop.  The shop provided me with the following torque settings in case I needed to adjust the stem in the future:  Steerer Tube-40 inch pounds; bar clamp--45 inch pounds.  I purchased a torque wrench at the time, but have not had occasion to adjust the stem.  

I do almost all of my training rides on an older steel [REDACTED].  The odometer on the [REDACTED], which I installed after the bike was fitted, reads just over 2,000 miles.  I have not replaced the tires on the [REDACTED] since buying it.  They appear to have a good deal of wear left in them, although I have bought new tires to install before going to Colorado next month to ride in the mountains.  
  
I replaced the stem with an aluminum one at a cost of $48.70.  Having had this experience with a carbon fiber stem, I do not want to take any chance of a recurrance, especially as I will be riding in the mountains in Colorado and New Mexico in late August and early September.  

Please advise me of what you believe caused the failure of the enclosed stem.  At a minimum, I hope that any problems with these stems will be corrected so that others will not have the same experience.  

When I called to report this problem, I was offered a replacement stem.  As I said then, I do not want a replacement stem.  I will not be using another carbon fiber stem from any manufacturer.  I would like a refund of the $48.70 expense incurred solely because of the untimely failure of this stem.  I can be contacted at [REDACTED].
justification: The incident involved a bicycle stem failure but no injury occurred, and the rider managed to avoid a crash. The occurrence likelihood is rated as possible (3) due to multiple reports of similar stem failures.

incident_description: On February 2, 2014, I was riding my 2014 Polaris Pro RMK 800 with my husband and two other friends. After riding for a few hours, we had stopped to take a break for a few minutes. After resting for a few minutes, I started my sled. After allowing it to idle while I put my helmet on, I went to push the throttle down to move off and continue riding. At this point, the throttle stuck wide open and the sled took off straight ahead without me. I was fortunately thrown off the back of the sled, landing flat on my back. The sled continued full speed ahead about 200 feet until it ran head on into a tree. The sled was still operating at full throttle even after hitting the tree, as the track remained spinning at high speed until I was able to get to it and hit the kill switch. I have extensive pictures of my sled right after the accident, including one showing the throttle cable still stuck wide open. I also have multiple witnesses as to this fact. This was an extremely shocking and frightening experience--very thankful that I was not injured or worse.

[REDACTED] has custody of the parts shown in the pictures.
Please let me know what comes next.

Mahalo and Aloha,

[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]

There are no injuries being reported

It is a collapsible scooter for easy carrying and storing. It collapses at the base of the scooter (where you put your feet) bringing the handle bar towards the ground. The  locking bolt (pin) that is supposed to lock the handle in the upright position does not lock. It slides out of place and strips the paint from the scooter. Sp while the child is riding the scooter the handle bars begin to collapse which then makes the nose of the scooter ram into the ground send the kid flying to the concrete (scrapped hands and knees and also smashed the child foot and toes (eventually losing a toenail) between the concrete and the base of the scooter. The locking pin has also inched fingers and hands while trying to get it to lock. 

You can go to the walmart website and see the reviews where several people have complained about the same thing.

incident_description:
SAFETY CONCERN:  Four of the Ovation helmets were tested. Each was subjected to the ASTM F1163-04a Standard Specification for Protective Headgear Used in Horse Sports and Horseback Riding. The drop rig and drop height for each drop was as specified in this standard for testing the helmet. With each helmet dropped onto the visor area of the helmet, each sample tested the break pattern was the same. 
As indicated in the photo with the young lady wearing the #4 sample this broken visor poses a serious danger for the rider with possible contact with the wearers eye and face. 
Testing was conducted in a controlled maner at a SEI Certified lab, Southern Impact Research Lab in Knoxville Tennessee. The current ASTM standard does not have a specific visor test protocol. But the Equestrian Helmet standard committee is currently working on the creation of a test method for helmet visors to stop this type of failure which can cause serious injury to the rider if the visor is impacted during a fall. 
There have been some incidents to date where these visors have broken in the field. This hazardous condition can and should be eliminated by replacing the plastic visor with a rubber, flexible visor. At present this product posses a serious risk of injury to anyone wearing this helmet. A specific warning regarding this breakage is not sufficient. Corrective action should be taken to eliminate this risk. A notification should be sent out to retailers and consumers regarding the risk of serious injury to the wearer if an impact was occur to the visor .
justification: The incident describes a serious risk of injury due to helmet visor breakage, with potential for eye and face contact, indicating a high severity level. The occurrence likelihood is rated based on reported incidents and the potential for future occurrences.

This incident occurred while [REDACTED], in the presence of friends, was riding the Trek 820 Mountain Sport bicycle over a bump on a park-maintained trail. The ejected cap and steel spring struck [REDACTED] in the face and neck area.  [REDACTED] did not lose control of the bike, crash or fall. The sharp force of the impact lacerated the right side of [REDACTED]'s jaw and he sustained a large abrasion to his right sub-mandibular neck area.  [REDACTED]'s incident required medical attention at the Huron Valley - Sinai Hospital Emergency Department and follow up dental work due to a broken tooth.
justification: The incident resulted in a laceration, abrasion, and a broken tooth requiring medical attention, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is unlikely (2) as such mechanical failures are not common.

incident_description:
The Avid Elixir CR Mag (and other similar products) brake lever has a service setting that extends the reach of the  lever beyond its normal range and affords improved access the  reach adjustment set screw.  The service setting is realized by  pulling the lever away from the handlebar until it pops.  The amount of force required to engage the service setting has decreased over time, to the point where the service setting is periodically engaged during the normal action of riding.  This creates a dangerous situation  - since when the lever is outside the normal operating range it is not immediately accessible to the biker and requires the rider to release the handlebar to re-position the lever in the normal operating range.  This situations occurs on both two sets of brakes on separate bikes.  

This is especially dangerous for adverse event braking on downhills, in situations with cars, pedestrians or other moving obstacles.  The frequency of these occurrences is increasing.
justification: The brake lever issue can lead to dangerous situations, especially during adverse events, increasing the risk of injury.

incident_description:
My son bought on-line a Dan Wesson replica 6 inch revolver from AirRattle.com. The gun is manufactured by ActionSportGames. The gun is intended to be as lifelike as possible. It is all metal, except for a black plastic handle. We did not authorize this purchase.

The gun was fitted with an orange muzzle tip that is about 1/2 inch long and 1/2 inch in diameter.

When we found the gun, the orange muzzle tip was missing.  We found it in his room, and it seems that it was not permanently attached to the muzzle of the gun, as required by 15 CFR 1150.

This gun is intended by the manufacturer to be very lifelike. In fact, the manufacturer has received a license from Dan Wesson Firearms to replicate the real gun in this BB gun. 

Without this orange tip, it could easily be mistaken for a real gun and result in the accidental shooting of children or others by law enforcement members or armed members of the public who feel threatened by a child with this BB gun.

This product is defective, inherently unsafe, and not in compliance with 15 CFR 1150.
justification: The missing orange muzzle tip could lead to the BB gun being mistaken for a real firearm, posing a significant risk of accidental shooting, though no injury has occurred yet.
