incident_description:
I visited the Cumming County Fair and Festival on October 5, 2013. The rides at the fair were owned and managed by James H. Drew Exposition. Around 8:30 p.m. I rode the Pirate Ship ride. This is a swinging ship style ride. After tickets for myself and my girlfriend, we were told to get on the platform and get in line up the stairs. There were people beside us the length of the platform as well as tightly behind us. Several guests were on the stairs with the people in front being about 12 inches from the swinging ride. Behind them, several more people were lined up in multiple rows while the ride swung one foot from our face. My concern was that someone could easily trip and get killed as the ride swings back down. I figured this was a simple case of poor training for the workers.

After the ride, I went to a ticket stand and asked to speak to a supervisor. I was directed toward a white trailer for their office. Outside of it, I found a lady worker who I again asked to speak to a supervisor. I was told to speak to a man who introduced himself as [REDACTED]. I told him my concern, and he said "that is the way we do it." I again expressed that it was unsafe. He didn't care. Finally, I said I think it needed to be reported. He said do whatever you want to do.

The management did not listen to my safety concern and I am worried that somebody could be critically hurt or killed.
justification: The description indicates a clear safety hazard with potential for injury or death, but no actual incident occurred during the event.

incident_description:
My wife and I were out traveling on dirt roads through the Eldorado National Forest on Aug. 17 2013 when I started to here a clunking sound from the front end of the Polaris 550 . { We had just purchased the quad a few weeks before and already have had the quad out on a previous trip a week before without any problems. When I bought the quad I noticed that the quad had a few A arm bushings that were [worn] and needed to be replaced but were not bad enough to be replaced as of yet.) When I heard the sound I thought that maybe it was a bushing starting to make noise. Is we got closer to our staging point back at the truck when the noise started getting louder and louder. We made it to the truck OK and loaded the quads on the trailer. The first chance I got I inspected the front end for a bad bushing but found out instead that it was the front left hand Ball joint had completely come loose from the steering knuckle and almost came apart which if it would have happened on the trail would have left me injured, stranded or dead. I found out about the Recall {alert #1 Q-713) and contacted the Polaris dealer they did research and found that the recall had already been done to this quad. I took the quad to the Polaris dealer and they contacted Polaris to see if they would replace it again and the said NO. This is a part that should NEVER come apart period. End of Story It looks like there fix was not a fix but a Band-Aid and someone is going to get injured, stranded or killed if this part isn't made so it will never come apart. Lucky I did not crash.

We purchased a Polaris Sportsman XP 550 quad from a private party with 1100 miles on it several weeks ago. When we bought the quad I noticed that it had a few A arm bushings that were [worn] but not bad enough to be replaced as of yet. Also, the clutch wouldnÃÂt kick in until 2500 rpm which would make the quad lunge on takeoff. On our first trip we had no problems with the steering or the front end. 

To learn more about the Polaris Sportsman XP 550, I went to the Polaris Forum on the Internet. According to the contributors, the clutch is that way new from the factory and someone figured out a fix for it. Also I read a lot of complaints of bushings wearing out in 200 miles or so. It seems that from what I have read that Polaris doesnÃÂt have original replacement parts that will last so all the people give advice on what to do and where to get aftermarket parts that are better. I wish I had seen this before I bought this quad. Always learning something the hard way, I guess.

My wife and I were out traveling on our quads on dirt roads through the Eldorado National Forest on August 17, 2013 when I started to here a clunking sound from the front end of the Polaris XP 550 I was riding. When I heard the sound I thought that maybe it was a bushing starting to make noise. As we got closer to our staging point, the noise started getting louder and louder and maybe sounding like a shock absorber getting loose. We made it to the truck okay and loaded the quads on the trailer. The first chance I got I inspected the front end for a bad bushing but found out instead that it was the front left hand Ball joint stem that had completely come loose from the steering knuckle, and almost came apart. Had this happened while riding on the trail, I would have been injured or died.

Polaris had a Recall of the concerned parts on the Consumer Product Safety Commission website (alert #10-713) so I contacted my local Polaris dealer, Placerville Polaris. They did a research and found that the recall repair work had already been done to this quad. [REDACTED] at the Placerville Polaris talked with me and we decided for me to call Polaris at customer Contact. They in turn told me that the work had already been done and they were not going to have it fixed again. They said that I could to take the quad to the Placerville Polaris so they could call their Polaris Rep because they didnÃÂt have the authority to make the call. So I called [REDACTED] at Placerville Polaris and he asked me to bring the quad down for an inspection and to take pictures to develop a case. When I got there, they gave me a cost estimate of $90.00. The report I got from Placerville Polaris was that the recalled part had FAILED AGAIN and that they spoke to [REDACTED], a Polaris representative (Case # C-2779857-P9B2R7) who denied payment of a repeat repair. This ended up costing me $67.50.

The Service Manager at Placerville Polaris seemed to think that the previous owner didnÃÂt have proper maintenance services done to the quad and that was to fault. He said that the part moves and wears and should have maintenance. 

My thought is that the Ball Joint moves but the ball joint stem where it is connected into the Steering knuckle should not, and that is where the problem lies.

I have three 2007 [REDACTED]and one 2007 [REDACTED]. All trouble - free and the SuzukiÃÂs have a total of approximately 12000 miles all together. My Yamaha and SuzukiÃÂs ball joints are put together like a car with the ball joint stem being a threaded bolt with a castle nut with a cotter pin holding into the steering knuckle that will never come apart. The Polaris has it mounted like a battery cable to a battery. The stem of the ball joint is just pinched in place by the steering knuckle with 1 bolt, and if it pulls loose youÃÂre in trouble. Have you ever had a battery cable come loose on your battery? Yes. And it doesnÃÂt have an A ÃÂARM yanking back and forth on it either. 

There is no excuse. This is a part that should NEVER COME APART, PERIOD! End of story. It is a portion of the part that when put together should never move, wear or need any maintenance whatsoever, no more than the ball joints ends on your car.

It looks like PolarisÃÂs engineers fix was just a brain fart and not a fix at all. And if not recalled and changed someone is going to get injured or killed if this part isnÃÂt made so it will never come apart.

BUT THE PEOPLE AT POLARIS DO NOT SEEM TO CARE.
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a critical mechanical failure that could have resulted in injury or death, but no actual harm occurred this time.

incident_description: I purchased a 2012 Polaris Ranger RZR4 on 12/22/2012. This vehicle was used a total of four times with less than 500 miles on it when the rear bed was melted by the exhaust pipe below it. At the time of the incident we were carrying fuel cans and ammunition in the cargo bed, both receiving damage from the heat generated. This could have easily resulted in a death or serious injury had it not been discovered during one of our stops. Polaris agreed to provide a replacement bed as "good will" but would not pay the $90.00 / Hr labor charge because it was outside the 6 month warranty period. this "Good Will" gesture was recanted after Polaris contacted the dealer to discuss the design flaw and the dealer refused to service the vehicle. When asked what would stop this from happening again they advised they put a heat shield over the exhaust pipe to keep this from happening. Upon inspecting the vehicle, I actually found that the heat shield was placed between the exhaust pipe and the motor. this provided no protection to the plastic bed above it. a search was also conducted online and found multiple other RZR owners experienced the same problem. Polaris has yet to provide any kind of fix to ensure that the vehicle is safe.
justification: The incident involved damage to the vehicle and cargo but no injury or death occurred, though the potential for serious harm was present.

incident_description:
While bicycle riding with a Senior Citizens group, one of the riders dropped off the shoulder of the road and fell from her bicycle. Although contact with the ground resulted in minimal injuries to the ride, her entanglement with the bicycle itself resulted in a severe injury to her right leg.

The chain guard on the bicycle had an extremely sharp circumferential edge - like a meat cutter blade - that rotated into the back of the rider's leg and left two very deep gashes.

The rider received first aid treatment at the site and subsequently had several stitches applied by a medical professional.

The sharp edge on the bicycle chain guard is an extreme safety hazard that can and should be eliminated.
justification: The rider suffered severe injuries requiring medical treatment, but there was no death.

incident_description:
While removing a two man ladder tree stand from a tree the ladder stabilizer bar slipped allowing the ladder to bend causing a fall, which ended in a broken foot.

There were three of us moving the stand.  Two on the ground and one unfastening the straps at the top.  The ladder stabilizer bar is a two piece square tube bar to stiffen the ladder.  Unlike other brands that use tractor pins, Hunter's View uses a set screw with a plastic handle.  We were moving the ladder stand in the morning and overnight there was a heavy dew.  The set screw slipped (slid) causing a jerk inward in the middle of the ladder.  This caused the top to bend out away from the tree.

All factory instructions for set and removal were followed.

Recommend that the set screw be replaced with a tractor pin to avoid further falls and injuries.  The stand itself is solid.
justification: The incident resulted in a broken foot, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the described conditions and equipment failure.

incident_description:
[REDACTED] is an experienced archer and a Coast Guard Petty Officer.  He has been active in the sport of archery for 15 years.

In approximately 2010, [REDACTED] purchased six (6) Eastman Outdoor Wolverine 6070 carbon arrows from Walmart, located at 5741 Buffalo Road, Harborcreek, Pennsylvania 16421.

On Monday, October 8, 2012, [REDACTED] went to a friend's home on [REDACTED] to shoot the arrows for target practice.  He used a Diamond Stud bow by Bowtech that was purchased new in 2010 and that was in perfectly good working order.

[REDACTED] prepared to shoot at his target from a distance of approximately 30 to 50 yards.  He had shot these particular Eastman carbon arrows before.  Prior to firing any of the arrows, he performed a visual inspection and flex testing.  After shooting 3 or 4 arrows, about 12 times totalÃÂthe final distance at the time of the incident being 50 yardsÃÂthe arrow unexpectedly shattered and exploded into his left hand and thumb.

[REDACTED] went to St. John Medical Center's in Cleveland, Ohio, where they performed a debridement.  He had to return to the hospital on October 10, 2012, for further surgical intervention.  The medical records reflect that [REDACTED] underwent exploration of the stab wound of the left thumb with complicated excision of over 100 splintered foreign bodies, primary repair of the ligament of the joint of the left thumb, primary repair of the extensor & distal tendons of the left thumb, DIP joint arthrotomy, and removal of multiple splintered aero shaft foreign bodies of the left thumb.  [REDACTED] was fitted with an appropriate protective dressing and immobilizing splint.

The arrow incident caused [REDACTED] to sustain significant personal injuries.  Medical reports indicate that he suffered severe injury and damage, pain and suffering, and required surgery, treatment, rehabilitation, and has resulted in permanent injury and loss of use.  [REDACTED]'s injury caused him to have trouble in his performance of daily personal activities and at work.  Since the surgical intervention and completing home exercises and home therapy treatment, [REDACTED]ÃÂs injury has improved; however, he still experiences pain and discomfort in his left thumb and hand.
justification: The incident resulted in severe injury requiring multiple surgeries and causing permanent damage, fitting severity level 3. Given the detailed precautions taken, such occurrences are rare.

incident_description:
Yesterday I went out hunting with my son and cousin. We were on a mountain with our 2013 Polaris Ranger 6x6. As per Polaris suggestion for using the parking break without blocking the wheels, I was careful to find a spot to park with very little incline and was sure to set my parking break. I would also note that there was very little if any wind at all. We were spotting animals for nearly 2 hours when the Ranger began to roll. By the time my cousin and I noticed that the vehicle was moving it was picking up speed and was headed directly for my son who was sitting above a 200 foot cliff. Luckily we were within shouting distance and were able to alert him and no one was injured but my nearly new Ranger was destroyed as it went over the cliff. We are thankful that we were not further away from him as this could have been more tragic than just being out thousands of dollars. We have been unable to recover the wreckage at this time. 

We have since done a web search and noticed a fair amount of consumer dissatisfaction with the Polaris Ranger parking break. I was sure to inspect the parking break tension after 25 hours of run time along with the recommended oil change. Our question is whether we have any recourse with Polaris to help recoup the cost incurred to us over their faulty parking break design? We followed the manufacturer's recommendations for safely parking the vehicle and would not expect such an incident such as this. I would like to see if there were more reports whether there should be a recall on these parking breaks and that some aftermarket repairs to these breaks aren't warranted by Polaris for these ATVs cost more than some small cars. This can be very dangerous especially for hunters who typically have loaded firearms and additional fuel. This is a disaster waiting to happen.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and the description suggests dissatisfaction with the parking brake design, indicating a possible recurring issue.

incident_description:
The dealer stated that the driver came home and parked the ATV on his driveway. The driver turned off the engine and about 10 minutes later, he noticed smoke and flames coming from the rear of the ATV. The dealer stated that within 45 seconds, the ATV had engulfed in flames.

The driver had driven the ATV on the day of the incident for 30 miles. 

The dealer and the driver believe that the incident occurred due to the unshielded exhaust. The dealer stated that the unshielded exhaust caused the rear floor panels to melt, lower down, and ignite. 

The dealer stated that he spoke to the manf regarding this incident. The manf informed the dealer that they were aware of the problem and that all of the newer models were being sent out with a repair kit. The dealer was also sent a repair kit for another model he has in hsi shop. The dealer stated that the kit includes a whole new exhaust system that is shielded. 

The dealer stated that he has the leftover metal frame of the ATV that ignited.

There are no recalls on this vehicle.
justification: The incident involved an ATV catching fire, but there was no mention of injury or death. The manufacturer is aware of the issue and has provided a repair kit, indicating a possible but not certain recurrence.

incident_description:
Caller purchased an Aqualung Axiom I3 Buoyancy Compensation Device (BCD), Serial number BB314183 on 01/13/2013. The BCD uses a weight packet retention system called ÃÂSurelock IIÃÂ. The system attaches the packets to the BCD through the use of plastic tension clips. There is no redundant retention system such as a buckled strap of Velcro flap.
During two recent dives he experienced a failure of this system. The weight packet self-detached and fell to the sea bottom.
The complaint is that by not designing the system with a redundant retention system, Aqualung has provided a product that can cause an unexpected hazardous situation for a diver. When the diver loses a weight packet three things can happen:
1. The diver will suffer a rapid increase in buoyancy which can result in an unintended rapid descent from depth without allowing for a decompression and or safety stop as advocated by the Professional Association of Diving Instructors (PADI).
2. The diver will experience a shift of equipment on their body since they will have too much weight on one side of their body.
3. The diver will lose the ability to control their body attitude in the water.
I have contacted the manufacturer. Their position is that the problem may have been due to improper installation by the user. While this is possible the underlying issue is that the product design would allow this to occur in the first place. 
Just as a vehicle provides redundancy to an occupant that they may not have properly fastened their seat belt (in the form of an audible and visual warning), so should this system have some type of back-up in case the retention system fails. The expectation of a vehicle occupant is that their seat belt will stay buckled during its intended use and so should the Surelock II system keep the weight attached to the BCD during its intended use.
Attached are images of the product tag and purchase invoice:
justification: The incident involves a failure of the weight packet retention system, which can lead to a hazardous situation for the diver, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
I believe the Tektro R540 brakeset is an unsafe product in design and/or manufacture.  It should not have been placed on Trek 2011 model Madone 4.5 bicycles.  The Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) and Tektro need to work with the Trek Corporation immediately to recall all bicycles of this model to fix these defective brakes.

I believe that the Tektro R540 brakeset led to an accident on my Trek 2011 model Madone 4.5 bicycle on Sunday, October 21, 2012 in Dublin, California.  The brakes on that bicycle were insufficient to "scrub speed" on a slight downhill on the Iron Horse Trail in that city.  The weather was clear and dry.

I ended up crashing into a curb and chain link fence, causing minor personal injury and significant damage to my then three-month old bicycle.

Numerous comments can be found on internet comment boards about consumers' negative experiences with the Tektro R540 brakeset on this very bicycle model, Trek 2011 Madone 4.5.

See, for example, this website:
http://www.roadbikereview.com/cat/brakes/brake-calipers/tektro/r540/prd_454498_2480crx.aspx

See the comment submitted by "[REDACTED]" on April 24, 2012.  He gave this product an "Overall Rating" of 2 of 6 stars and a "Value Rating" of 2 of 6 stars.

Here is his review of the Tektro R540 brakeset on my very same bicycle model, Trek 2011 Madone 4.5:
"Strengths:    Weight, not much else
Weaknesses:    Lack of power, durability, quick release mech.
Bottom Line:   
These brakes came stock on my 2011 Trek Madone 4.5, never would I choose to buy them individually. After about seven months of using the brakes under normal conditions, the bushings in the main brake bolt wore out and caused an incredibly annoying creaking sound to come from the front caliper in the middle of every lever pull. I will soon be upgrading to a set of [REDACTED] calipers because I'm simply fed up with the lack of stopping power and the creaking noises. The [REDACTED] calipers are a little heavier, but I'd much rather save myself on a steep hill than save some weight. I also don't like that the quick release mechanism is all or nothing, I like a notched quick release for easier dialed-in adjustment."

Other complaints about "brakes", "braking" and "the brake lottery" on internet comment boards for the Trek 2011 Madone 4.5 are additional evidence that numerous consumers across the nation have had problems with brakes on this bicycle.

I call upon Tektro to do the right thing and start a voluntary recall of the Tektro R540 brakeset on all Trek 2011 Madone 4.5 models. Otherwise the CPSC should require this recall.  This product is a significant risk to the lives, limbs and personal property of consumers.

The fact that the Trek Corporation used the Tektro R540 brakeset on its Madone 4.5 model apparently for just one year (2011) suggests that Tektro and/or the Trek Corporation already has notice and/or knowledge that the Tektro R540 brakeset is defective.

I have given Tektro hereby notice of these concerns and requested it to take immediate remedial action by my e-mail of Sept. 22, 2013.
justification: The incident resulted in minor personal injury and significant damage to the bicycle, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to multiple consumer complaints about the brakeset's performance.

This report is about the IST Sports Corp. ProEar scuba diving mask.

The mask has 2 ear cups and 2 plastic tubes attached to the ear cups and to the top of the scuba mask.  The tubes are attached to the mask via a screw and screw-nut mechanism.

I was snorkeling when one of the tubes became detached and the mask flooded with sea water.  After inspecting the mask I realized one of the tube's screw-nut had become unscrewed allowing the tube to detach.  The mask flooded through the hole through which the tube is inserted into the mask.  In a scuba diving situation at a deep depth this could be very dangerous and could lead to fatal consequences.

Upon contacting the seller of the mask they stated that they've had several costumers have the same problem with the mask.   That they've notified IST Corp, but that IST Corp is only advising customers not to move the tubes on the mask too much.

Back last fall, we bought 5 of the Slime Smart Tubes in 26 inch/1.90 with Schrader valves and started using them in May of 2013. 

In just over 3 months, nearly every tube failed in the same way, with the entire tube slowly rotating in the tire so the stem eventually gets stressed against the metal tire opening and then gets ripped away from the tube while riding. The loss of air is very sudden and it easily results in a crash.

I just lost #4 today while riding next to traffic, losing control of my front wheel and crashing hard against the pavement. I came away with bruised ribs and road rash. I was going 20mph. My wife crashed once on this tube and lost air a second time without a crash and my daughter lost tire pressure once while riding as well. In each case, the valve stem separated from the tube and the tube lost in less than a few seconds. 

I would seriously suggest that you pull these from the market. They are too smooth, causing them to rotate in the tire, and too prone to failure. These are not safe to ride on.

incident_description:
We bought the Sportspower 14' Trampoline and Safety Enclosure from Walmart.com in July 2012, though it was not assembled until August 2012.  Because it was purchased online, with in-store pick-up, they had all my contact information.  

I just learned today that the trampoline was recalled in January.  I am very upset that I was not contacted to tell me that the trampoline was recalled.  If Sportspower and Walmart would have worked together it would have been easy for them to contact me.

Today my 11-year old son and 2 neighbors were playing on the trampoline.  My son fell against the net and it tore - a huge tear (30 inches high and 6 feet wide).  My son fell out and hit his head and shoulder on the fence before falling to the ground.

We are very lucky that he was not severely injured.  He is fine, though possibly bruised.

There was NO sign that the net was weakening in any way prior to the tear.
justification: The incident resulted in injury to the child, but there was no death or severe injury.

incident_description:
I was working out on my approx 4 month old treadmill (NordicTrack model C1550) and had the track moving to an 8 incline at a 4.8 speed when the machine completely stalled. I had done a 3 min warm up at 4.8 speed/2 incline prior to increasing the incline to 8. Within 60 seconds of increasing the incline, the machine came to an abrupt halt. I jolted forward, with my upper torso falling into the control panel and my toe box on my right foot riding up slightly on the plastic piece covering the front of the track (which extends at least 3-4" farther than the control panel). Approximately 1-020 seconds after it abruptly stopped, the treadmill started up again at the 4.8 speed it was at prior to stalling and I fell to the track, literally coming within 2ÃÂ of my face/front teeth going into the control panel. The track drug my feet back twisting my right ankle underneath my leg, with the top of my right foot sustaining an abrasion from the tread and my knee getting torn up and bruised prior to the machine emergency stopping when the red switch finally pulled out. My right knee and top of my right ankle were bleeding and my right ankle became very swollen. I also experienced significant bruising on my right knee, and whip-lash like symptoms with midback and neck pain.

My doctor diagnosed me with an ankle sprain, mid and upper back sprain and right knee abrasion and contusion.

As a side note, this treadmill is kept on a surge protector on it's own circuit. I also came across 5+ recent online NordicTrack treadmill reviews where users had similar experiences to what happen to me on 8/4, where the treadmill had abruptly stopped without warning.
justification: The incident resulted in multiple injuries including an ankle sprain, back sprain, and knee abrasion, as diagnosed by a doctor.

incident_description:
Product: "Learn-To-Swim" children's flotation jacket by "PoolMaster".

Product Description: Nylon flotation vest for children, worn over head with flotation sections on belly and back. 2 bright yellow nylon straps secure vest to body by wrapping around chest, and under legs. 

Incident: My 5 year old daughter was wearing this flotation vest during a family outing to the San Marcos river, near Austin yesterday. As she is not yet a good swimmer, she was required to wear this vest at all times. Further, I accompanied her in the water and had her physically held by the jacket strap or her arm the entire time we were in the water. She and I accidentally stepped into deep water and were floated by the current in a way we did not anticipate. I had her in my grip, by the bright yellow jacket strap and we floated for a brief time until we reached a ladder which was provided by the local park for climbing out of the river.

As she climbed out above me, I released the strap and followed her up the ladder. During the ascent, I noticed that her safety belt (which held her in the flotation jacket, and which I had been holding on to) was torn, and no longer attached as designed. After safely exiting the water we inspected the flotation jacket and discovered that the nylon straps on the jacket were entirely compromised - torn and with disintegrating. The straps tear with as little as 5 lbs of shearing pressure applied to them - comparable to paper in its physical strength.

The product itself was purchased from a local pool supply company about 3 months ago, and has been used less than 10 times. 

Complaint: This product is unsafe. The physical integrity of the straps on this device is completely inadequate to satisfy the purpose of its design.
justification: The incident involved a safety-critical product failure (compromised straps) but no injury occurred due to parental supervision.

incident_description:
Smooth Fitness Agile DMT, purchased in January 2009, has been lightly used.  During the moderate workout, the Left Pedal bolt has failed for the second time.  Both times serious injury was averted by chance.  

  It was originally assembled by Smooth Fitness contractor under the purchase agreement.  It was used for less than 50 hours when the bolt failed for the first time.  The bolt completed snapped while a 125lbs female was getting off the machine.  Following the first broken bolt, in April 2009, it was repaired under warranty by a Smooth Fitness Contractor.  It has been very lightly used (less than 100 hours) since the repair, and it has failed again in a very similar manner.

  There appears to be a basic design flaw of the joint.  The shoulder of the threaded bolt is at the interface between Pedal Arm and Pedal Swing Arm.  This location is affected by maximum moment, reduced diameter, and Kt from thread at the same time.  The poor design is destined to keep failing.  If the joint fails while in normal use, it can cause severe injury.  Please review the product, and initiate a recall or redesign of the Pedal Swing Arm and the bolt.  Thank you.
justification: The incident describes a recurring failure of the Left Pedal bolt, with serious injury averted by chance both times, indicating a potential for injury but no actual injury reported.

A branch caught in the metal rack that is on the back of the seat. Her daughter was not injured or hurt.

(06/13/2013) The consumer stated that her son and daughter were on the atv at the same time. Her four year old son was driving. He was going straight and turned to the left. When she turned to the left, the battery cut out again. The atv started to roll backwards. The consumer instructed him to push the pedal. The atv kept rolling backwards. Her daughter jumped off of the atv. Her son stayed on the atv which went down the hill into the woods. The atv flipped over on top of him. The consumer stated that he got a couple of bruises. 

The consumer stated that she flipped the atv over to get it off of her son. When she pushed the gas to get the atv up the hill, the atv started spinning. The back right tire caught her left toe and ripped off her toenail. The consumer did not get medical treatment.

The consumer stated that there is an indicator on the atv that shows the power of the battery. The indicator was on green. When the battery is low, it shows red.
justification: The incident resulted in bruises for the son and a toenail injury for the mother, but no medical treatment was required.

incident_description:

There were no injuries

Manufacturer has been contacted but they are accepting no responsibility.

model# XUV550 with serial# [REDACTED]

incident_description:
Purchased two sets of kids "water wings" at Gap, PA, Weis grocery store.  They had boys' and girls' versions - blue with superheroes and pink with princesses or other characters.  

My son was wearing a pair while swimming and the seal holding the two sides together came apart on one of them.  I assumed it was because he was jumping in the pool and was rough with it.

My daughter was swimming a few days later wearing them and just floating in the water when one of the ones she was wearing separated in exactly the same way.  I was on the opposite side of the pool and by the time I ran around to her side and grabbed her hand her face had gone under several times and she was terrified.  She was ok but if this happens to someone else and they're not right there it could be dangerous.

I called the store on 7/2/13 at around 8 pm (right after the second incident) and asked them to remove the items from the shelf.  Reporting it here as well because I am sure lots of Weis's have these and probably other stores also.
justification: The incident involved a product failure that led to a child's face going underwater multiple times, causing terror but no physical injury.

incident_description: On June 8, 2013, I took my 4 1/2 year-old son to a school/community playground where we met two of his friends.  He and his friends proceeded to play on the GameTime PowerScape Plus play structure.  Eventually they gravitated toward one of the slides, and they climbed, slid, and repeated this sequence on the slide.  During the course of one of these "cycles," I and the two other accompanying adults watched as my son fell from the 90 inch high platform at the top of the slide and landed flat on his back on the wood-chip covered surface,  An additional adult witness told us that he saw my son trip on his way to the slide, try to hang on, and then fall.  The paramedics came and recommended that I take him to the ER for a more thorough evaluation, where he checked out without head, back, or spinal cord trauma; while he had the wind knocked out of him and exhibited some signs of shock, he escaped this incident with hardly a bruise (likely thanks to a recently replenished wood-chip base, according to a contact at the school).  I went back to the scene of his fall the very next day and took photos.  I then discovered a diagonal step across the platform at the top of the slide, inches from the opening that leads to a 7 1/2 foot drop-off.  There is an opportunity for crowding at the top of the slide, and the close proximity of these two features (slide and spiral climber) increases the risk of a fall.  After witnessing my son's accident first-hand, I am very concerned that this tripping hazard near an unprotected opening from an elevated platform is in violation of the safety regulations that this manufacturer claims to follow and poses a hazard for children of all ages.
justification: The child fell from a 90 inch high platform and landed flat on his back, but was not seriously injured.

incident_description: Consumer is suffering Pain in their Wrist, shoulder, and elbow along with tendonitis after using a hollow tennis racket which now require cortisone injections.
justification: The consumer is suffering from pain and tendonitis requiring medical treatment, indicating an injury.

incident_description: I bought my grand children your flexible flyer swing set model number 42124-0212. The first time they tried to use the see saw it broke, rite in the area your company has called for a recall. I need the part/parts in order to b able to fix it or a full refund from your company. they won't even play on it hardly anymore cause they are afraid something else will happen to them. Thank u for taking the time to read this.

incident_description:
My son was involved in a serious accident today with "Gold's Gym Multi-Purpose Training Door Gym.  It was assembled per instructions and came crashing down on him resulting in a fractured jaw and two teeth blown out. He received 5 hours of emergency dental work and won't be back to full health for at least 1-2 months.  This device doesn't have an "Anti-Slip" measures that do not allow it to shift latterally to the right or left of the door frame.  This isn't the only time this is going to happen.  This is a poorly designed device that's dangerous.

UPDATE 7/2/13 FROM SUBMITTER:
Upon further review, it appears my daughter did not read the instructions that came with this equipment and put this on a larger doorframe than is recommended by the manufacturer. This accident could have been avoided if she read the instructions.
justification: The incident resulted in a fractured jaw and dental injuries, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as the accident was due to improper use but highlights potential design flaws.

incident_description:
The consumer says that when he first purchased the ATV he noticed a lot of electrical problems. He says the dash constantly blinked on and off and also an EMC error code would appear.  The dealer told him the electrical system was not strong enough.  The dealer replaced the stator, which is an electrical regulator.  This did little to resolve his issues. 

He then called the manufacturer for assistance, they referred back to the dealer.  After six months of going back and forth he was told by both parties that it was the best they can do.  Last weekend he had an electrical fire and the entire unit was burned to the ground.  He was driving down the road when the dash blinked on and off.  

The ATV stopped running on its own as it has done before.  He walked away for five minutes, and came back to see his ATV on fire from the back portion.  The ATV burned to the ground in ten minutes, burning the aluminum to liquid.  

He then contacted manufacturer yesterday who in turn went back to the dealer and is waiting to fill out an incident report.  The dealer has record of his several complaints and visits over the years.  There is also a complaint on file with the manufacturer from 2008.
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire that destroyed the ATV but no injuries or deaths were reported.

Around noon, consumer said that her daughter, 2 years and 9 months old, was in her little pool in the back yards for 30 minutes.

Consumer said that her daughter started complain that her bottom hurts.  When consumer took her bathing suit out her found out that her daughter had developed unusual rash, hives and redness in her behind and between her legs, and her daughter was very itchy.  She cried.

Consumer said that the bathing suit dye is coming off and she believes that the dye that came out the bathing suit caused that unusual rash.

incident_description: On April27, 2013, I bought a new 2012 KTM SX 150 {VIN No. [REDACTED]) for my son. This was not his first dirt bike and he is an experienced rider. After about five hours or riding time on the dirt bike, my son told me the throttle had stuck wide open on him. I checked it for dirt or damage and made sure the cable was not getting caught on something when he turned the handle bars to the left or right. I found nothing out of place or any damage to the dirt bike and the throttle was working fine. On Saturday, May 18, 2013, he was riding at a dirt bike track in Seaford, Delaware and had no problems with the throttle. The next day, on Sunday, May 19, 2013, while in a race at the same dirt bike track, the throttle got stuck on him again and threw him off the back of the dirt bike and he was sent by ambulance to the hospital. A father of one of the boys my son was racing with retrieved my son's dirt bike from the track. He told me the throttle was stuck wide open and when he turned the throttle it "clicked" and sprung back to zero. I contacted Mike's KTM, a dealer for KTM motor bikes, and inquired if he had heard of any problems with the throttles sticking on this model. He informed me that there is a recall on the throttle on 2013 models; therefore, I bought a new throttle assembly {same part and part number) and installed it on the dirt bike. Test driving in our back yard, once again the new throttle stuck and he was thrown from the dirt bike before the dirt bike crashed, hurting his shoulder. Obviously there is a problem with the 2012 KTM SX 150 model as well.
justification: The incident resulted in injury when the throttle stuck, causing the rider to be thrown off the bike and hurt his shoulder.

incident_description: This product is dangerous. I emailed the manufacturer one week ago about my concerns. I have received no response, therefore, I feel obligated to alert the public. My daughter (8years old) planned a big birthday party for herself in the backyard. Our backyard zip line was one of the major attractions, and, as a present I bought a yellow hornet trolley. It looks great, appears to be very well-made...only there is one problem. The release pin that allows the device to be detached from the cable. It releases spontaneously and causes the riders to fall to the ground. It happened once, and I thought that the child (kids were 8-12 years old) had probably touched the release pin. I warned everyone NOT TO TOUCH THE BLUE BUTTON, and I personally followed and watched two more riders to be sure that they didn't touch it; they didn't touch it but it still released spontaneously, the trolley came apart and they fell to the ground. Fortunately, the distance to ground was only a couple feet and nobody was injured. The problem could probably be fixed by a pin that locks tight, but the manufacturer needs to get onto this before someone is seriously hurt or killed!
justification: The incident involved multiple spontaneous releases of the trolley, causing falls, but no injuries were reported.

The padding them began to fall apart.  After storing our trampoline for almost a year, the padding has completely fallen to pieces, and the netting tore as I was putting the enclosure back up causing me to fall off the trampoline.  No injuries were sustained at that time.
justification: Children sustained injuries from exposed trampoline poles, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to the repeated issues with the trampoline padding and netting.

My DUI bcd (wing type) for scuba diving had the overpressure valve stuck open when diving. Luckily I wore a drysuit so I could get out of the water safely. incident_description: I was on a scuba diving trip to St. Croix and was using a brand new dive regulator, the Oceanic Delta 4.2 with FDX10 1st stage.  I noticed a honking noise as I did a shore dive to 25 feet.  On subsequent dives that were deeper the noise was louder and became painful due to vibrations when descending to 70 feet.  It was very difficult to breath from the regulator and I required assistance from another diver to use their air supply.  I will gladly go into further detail if needed.  This is probably just a defective regulator, but such defects can cause a diver to drown and I wanted it reported.  Feel free to contact me for further information.
justification: The incident involved a defective regulator causing breathing difficulties, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: We purchased our first trampoline with enclosure from Wal-Mart in December 2010. Within 6 months our 11-year-old daughter fell through the net enclosure as described in the recall. When I called and explained that we had owned the product for only 6 months we were told that the netting could have torn due to weathering, but the company would replace it this one time. Afterwards we were sent another enclosure exactly like the first one. Within 8 months of receiving that one the same thing happened and my daughter fell through the netting again and hit the ground along with a visiting friend that was on the trampoline with her. I have since tried to find the netting to purchase another one because I have a three-year-old that requires an enclosure. I visited Wal-Mart to get the name brand of the trampoline we had purchased to find a poster hanging in its place warning people of the recall and the product's hazard. Apparently, there is a little more than weathering to be considered and more like poor quality. Now, my question is, what do I do about an enclosure for the trampoline that I am stuck with?
justification: The incident describes injuries from falling through the netting, indicating a severity level of 3. The recurrence of the issue suggests a high likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description:
Until now, the  two most common soccer injuries are:ankle sprains and Achilles   tendon rupture or tear. During   five years  period of practice soccer,  i injury my self between seven to nine times with  different soccer shoes brands . My most common injury  it was achilles tendon and calf tear. This injuries it has never been associate directly with the soccer shoes design malfunction because to the simple eye view for many of us it's difficult to see how athlete  move  the foot on the grass field.  Thanks to biometric  data analysis equipment  on the marked and it's applicability  on sports we can see what simple eye view can not. 
The grass terrain is an uneven surface no matter what,to the athlete that wear  cleats because  it's faulty design in combination  with the soft ground create  a hazard  for lower leg,bone,muscle,tendons, etc.
How this happened ? 
There is a principal that mostly all sport  shoes designers fallow. Due to the calcaneus or heel fall on mostly all body mass, designers  increase cushions  in the area for more comfortable  impact when we walk,run, jump etc. This principal  has negative effects with cleated sport shoes on a grass terrain.
Cleated shoes  with or without cushion on grass terrain it's acting  like a dagger(on heel area)a holding force and it go deeper according the weight index we apply. The deeper it goes down,the  difficult to pull out. 
Cleats, created bigger problems on grass terrain broke the anatomic alignment  between heel to toes  and for that,  change the  weight and balance center making more difficult  no only departure but turning to the sites, jumping, running, kicking the ball, etc. 
In conclusion ,Cleats,on a grass terrain  created more drag to the player foot to point of over stretching legs muscle and taking the tendons to the limit of  it elasticity  to the limit where injury start.
justification: The description details frequent injuries (ankle sprains, Achilles tendon tears) related to soccer cleats on grass, indicating a clear injury risk.

incident_description:
Our 10,000+ gallon soft sided pool suddenly ripped, evacuating all 80,000 pounds of water in less than a minute.  Due to the setting (atop a hillside), the water channeled itself into 10-12 foot wide river cascading 100 feet onto the adjoining property, and continued downhill.  Fortunately no one was hurt or injured this time, but it's very easy to visualize a different outcome.

The "explosion" happened at approximately 9:30 PM, while still under its "winterized' cover.  The air temperature at the time was about 72 degrees.

After contacting the manufacturer, I was told "Any actions by any individual or entity that attempt to tarnish our company name or products, or to do harm to us financially will be vigorously pursued to the fullest extent of the law." 

My concern is that, toward the end of the lifespan of the pool liner, catastrophic failure could happen.  Had a child been in the pool at the time, who knows how far downhill they would have tumbled.  Had someone been standing next to pool, they would have been flattened.  Had there been a home directly below the pool, with a child playing outside...

Photos available.
justification: No one was hurt or injured this time, but the potential for severe injury or death is high if the incident were to occur under different circumstances.

incident_description:
(04/09/2013) The consumer stated that the received the resistance bands as a gift. This is his first time using the resistance bands. He stated that he started to do curls. He stated that he had been exercising for about two minutes when the band pulled out of the cloth loop. He stated that he did not get injured. 

The resistance bands are the same ones listed in the recall-Rel #13-100.
justification: The resistance band failed during use but no injury occurred, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
On May 7, 2013, I was riding my 2013 CervÃÂ©lo P3 Ultegra Bicycle.  As I was riding, I heard a snapping noise and my hands violently flew up as both handlebars broke away from the base bar.  My bike veered out of control and I flung forward, dragging the bike with me and sliding down the road on the right side of my body.  I slid a number of feet down the road and ended on the other side of the road.  I was unable to move much and was bleeding heavily. I searched for product information on the internet the following morning, which is when I first learned of the recall on the 3T Aura Pro Handlebars on my 2013 CervÃÂ©lo P3 Ultegra Bicycle. I then reported my accident to the bicycle retailer.  The retailer indicated they were in contact with the bicycle and handle bar manufacturers.

incident_description:
The consumer says the seat assembly dropped to the ground while children were playing.  None of the children were injured.  

She contacted the manufacturer who says the unit falls outside of the range of the recall (Release #08-305) and there is nothing they can do.  

They advised her to go on Ebay or Craigslist to find the part that they no longer carry.  She is having the same issue as listed in the recall.
justification: The seat assembly dropped but no injuries occurred, indicating an incident without injury. The issue is recurring as per the recall, suggesting possible likelihood.

incident_description:
My wife owns a home daycare and we purchased this swing set for the business. The problem started in 9/2012 and has continued into 4/2013 to present date 5/2013. Swing Set was purchased on 4/19/2012 but was shipped to us approximately 7/19/2012. Swing Set Model is 46604T (we purchased it online from Walmart. Their model # is WM46604-0412.

The issue is the 4-person Lawn Swing platform which is attached to four steel bars by four bolts (called screws in the owners manual) and four NyLock nuts. Two of these nuts have fallen off the swing three times. In mid-April of this year, I emailed and spoke to customer service about the problem and they sent me out a set of four replacement screws and nuts from Flexible-Flyer customer service. Presently a 3rd nut located on the left front underside of the platform continues to loosen and would fall off if I didn't tighten it weekly. Just yesterday that nut had fallen off the swing completely and I found it in the pea gravel beneath the swing. Kids had been riding on the swing at the time I found it. Once again I replaced and tightened it as firmly as I could. 

On 4/26/2013 I left a voice mail message on the customer service line telling them the Nylock nuts were still falling off the lawn swing platform, that I thought the screws were too short, and they were putting the daycare kids at risk since these nuts were falling off with kids on the swing. No one returned my call. On 4/29/2013 I followed up with an email to customer service stating my call hadn't been returned, and repeating I thought the screws were too short and the company was putting the daycare kids at risk with the lawn swing. I asked them to contact me so that they could also advise me if I was doing something wrong if there wasn't a problem with the design of the swing. Again, there has been no response. I think the company is intentionally avoiding responding to me because I said they were putting the daycare kids at risk and they see a potential liability issue. The platform could conceivably fall off the swing while the children are riding in it which could cause serious physical injuries. 

This lawn swing is potentially unsafe and I have a right to talk to the company about this safety issue when my goal is to avoid having any children injured while riding in the swing.
justification: The swing's nuts repeatedly fall off while children are using it, posing a clear risk of injury if the platform detaches.

incident_description: My son fell  through the enclosure and landed on his head resulting in a depressed skull fracture.
justification: The incident resulted in a depressed skull fracture, which is a serious injury.

incident_description:
Dangerous/Injury situation with a new Defender Metal Pony-Tail Strap Face Protection Shield Model#
DSS12DMS002 Size S/M White UPC 94922 82515 that we purchased for our daughter on March 14, 2013. It is a face shield designed for facial injury protection while playing Softball or Baseball.
So the situation is this, we remove the tags from the new face shield and she started putting the shield on, but the chin cushion pops off resulting in the metal chin guard striking her in the front teeth. She was in terrible pain and we had to place ice in a compress on her from teeth for a long time.
Next I inspected the face shield and reattached the chin cushion onto the face shield. I attempted to put the face mask on thinking a demonstration would help her. The chin cushion popped off and the metal struck me in the 2 front teeth, and it was very painful. I inspected and found that the [hook and loop fastener] on the metal side was the hook side of the [hook and loop fastener], but the chin cushion did not have the proper loop side to properly secure the chin cushion, hence the cushion pops off from the mask when attempting to put the mask on. I went back to the store and found all stock of this brand to either be missing the chin cushion, or with a cushion missing the [hook and loop fastener] loop.
justification: The incident resulted in painful injuries to both the daughter and the parent due to the defective face shield, but no death occurred.

incident_description: I purchased a Horizon T6 treadmill Jan. 7, 2011.  While I was on it one day, it suddenly accelerated to a high speed and shut itself off within a second or so.  I managed to stay on the treadmill so did not sustain an injury.  This happened within less than a year of the purchase date.  The sporting goods store I bought it through repaired it by installing a new computer component (could have been the whole motherboard).  I have been using it since without any problem until yesterday 4/30/13 when it suddenly accelerated again.  I don't think it shut itself off this time.  I managed to jump to the sides and I think I may have hit the stop.  Not sure since it happened so fast.  Thankfully I had been holding on to the rails while walking so again did not get hurt.  I am feeling MORE than leary about getting on a treadmill again!  Have there been any problems reported with this treadmill.  I looked for recalls but only saw one for 2000-2002 models.
justification: The treadmill malfunctioned twice without causing injury, indicating an incident with no harm but a possible likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: I would like to report 3 separate incident/safety concerns regarding the Flexible Flyer Fantastic metal swing set. The swing was purchased as a Christmas gift for my  two nephews who at the time were 2 and 5. They are now 3 and 6. The swing for purchased on 11/30/2012 as a Christmas gift. On Christmas Day, my 5 year old nephew sat on the see saw seat and it broke. He sustained no injuries at this time. The seat was replaced with the provided replacement parts and within three weeks, he sat on it again and the seat sheared off at the base. Once again, no injuries were sustained but he was clearly upset over the incident. At this point, myself and my brother, decided that we would not replace the seats for a third time and the boys were no longer to play around the see saw area. One month later, my 3 year old nephew went to sit in the middle swing. When he did, the swing seat broke away from the chain. He fell to the ground and sustained only a cut to his arm with a few scratches. Since there are two other swings on the set, we decided to not replace the middle swing. At this point, I began obtaining images of the damaged areas of the swing for my own records. Well, today was the final straw. My 5 year old nephew was swinging on the glider by himself under the supervision of myself, his mother and grandmother, when the glider arm broke from the bolt that held it in place. Upon inspection, the bolt was broken in half. My nephew fell to the ground sustaining scrapes to his hands and elbows. It is a miracle he did not break any bones or obtain a head injury. After this, the swing is officially off limits to everyone. I have contacted the company with images sent as well. I have decided to fnally file a report, because according to their website, the only recall on that particular swing, is the see saw seat. At this point, the see saw seat is the least of their worries. The broken glider and broken swing seat could cause far worse injuries. From day one, no one has been allowed on the swing without supervision. My nephews are of normal size and height for their age with no abuse of the equipment made by them. The point that I am trying to make, is that they are only allowed to sit there behinds in the swing seats and the glider. They have never been allowed to hang from the swing or use it in any other way besides the way it was intended.
justification: The incident resulted in minor injuries (cuts and scrapes) from multiple failures of the swing set components, indicating a recurring safety issue.

incident_description:
SCUBA BCD
Power inflator failure Sherwood Avid BCD (SN = 91210067)

The power inflator stuck in an inflate position and caused an unsafe accent.  I could not disconnect the inflator hose in time and shot up to the surface from 70 feet.

System should be designed to release easier and or fail in a no-inflate mode requiring the diver to manually inflate the BCD.
justification: The incident involved an unsafe ascent from 70 feet due to a power inflator failure, which could have caused injury but did not result in death.

incident_description:
The consumer says that on March 2nd 2013 she was driving the snowmobile at about 15 mph on a snowmobile trail in Oquossoc, Maine.  When the snowmobile exploded and immediately shot flames up 2 to 3 feet behind the handle bars and the flames quickly spread to the driver's left side of the sled.  The consumer says the fire dept responded within five minutes.  The consumer says this incident was not a back fire.  The fireman says that the explosion shook the fire station.    

Due to the fact that the fire happened right beside the fire station.  A firemen on duty heard the explosion and came out and saw the snowmobile in flames.  He called 911 which summoned the other firemen.  
The consumer contacted the manufacturer who said the unit is not under warranty.  They also said they have not seen any reports with this product. The product is under recall (Release # 10-705).   The snowmobile was taken to an authorized dealer for repair back in January of 2009 .

It was also taken for service updates in February 2013.  The unit is currently at an authorized dealer, she says they possibly could consider it totaled.  
The consumer says that the manufacturer still has not fixed the problem with the newer models.  The consumer says the 2010, 2011, 2012, and 2013 models all have had the same issue.
justification: The incident involved a snowmobile explosion and fire, but there was no mention of injury or death, only property damage.

incident_description:
Two years ago my dad was using the ameristep plastic tree steps.  One ended up breaking.  Lucky for him it was the bottom one.  He had just put his weight on it and it snapped.  Later i found out they were recalled.  It had the recall date on it.  We went through all 8 we had and 6 were recalled.  Sent them in and got a check back.  We didnt return the other 2 because they were not recalled.  This passed bow season he was using the other two.  Needless to say one broke again.  He fell with his arm around his tree stand.  He had a huge bruse, was very sore, and couldnt pull back his bow for a while.  Ive tryed emailing them about this and can not get a reply.  I still have the step.  The date code on this step is 2/08.  It broke just as the one with the recall did.  Were not very happy with the customer support with them.  

[CPSC NOTE]: Recall was expanded Oct. 27, 2010 to include this date code - see CPSC release #11-024
justification: The incident resulted in injury (bruising and soreness) but no death, and the recurrence of the issue with the same product suggests a likely occurrence.

incident_description:
On 2013-04-07, I suffered an injury as the result of using the "Power Gym Door Mounted Exerciser" (that I will also refer to as the "Power Gym Pullup Bar", or "pullup bar"), which is a sports and recreation product designed for use in the home. The product is designed to be temporarily mounted to an interior doorframe for the duration of an exercise session, then dismounted after the completion of the session.

Prior to use and assembly of the product, I measured my doorframe to ensure that it fit the tolerances mentioned on the Power Gym product's packaging. Then I assembled the pullup bar, following the instruction sheet included with the product.

Then I mounted the pullup bar on my doorframe, and commenced an exercise session of pullups. Midway through my second pullup, the Power Gym pullup bar came loose from the doorframe, and I fell down to the floor, hitting my toe and ankle, and then rolling back on the floor and banging the back of my skull against the corner of a wall.

I suffered bleeding--there is a laceration and bump now on the back of my skull. I received first aid, but have not gone to seek further medical attention. 

I think the Power Gym Pullup Bar severely lacks: 1) proper information on the required tolerances for doorframes as the product was intended for; and, 2) proper anchoring for temporary mounting to an existing doorframe. I think this product is too dangerous for consumers.
justification: The incident resulted in a laceration and bump on the skull, indicating an injury, but no death. The likelihood is possible as the product's failure led to the injury, but it's not a frequent occurrence.

incident_description:

She noticed that the loops that is hooked to the mat that holds the spring are breaking. This would cause the spring to come off. One of the kids slid through the hole that was created by the breakage. The consumer stated that about four of the loops broke. No one was hurt.


(04/09/2013) The consumer contacted the manufacturer. The consumer was told that there was a ninety day warranty. She was told that she could send them receipt but there were no guarantee that they were going to do anything.

incident_description: Around the end of January 2013, I purchased a Bicycle from the Walmart Store on Rosedale Highway in Bakersfield, California. The Bicycle is manufactured by J.T. Kent International in N.J. I was riding the Bike home just east of the Intersection of [REDACTED], the right foot pedal rotated out from the drive wheel and fell off, I became unbalanced and I fell off the Bike onto the pavement striking my right side of my ribcage and the whole of my back. After I got off the ground, I walked the Bike to a nearbye Garage where a Mechanic used a wrench in reattaching the pedal. During this time period he told me that whomever assembled the Bike cross threaded the pedal to the drive wheel. I returned the Bike to the Store and received a refund. Later an Inspector for Walmart examined the Bike and informed me that the problem occured in manufacturing and directed me to the Manufacturer J.T. Kent in N.J. They claim that they want to "Do the right thing" to help me but they haven't been very helpful!
justification: The incident resulted in injury (falling and striking the ribcage and back), but the occurrence likelihood is unlikely as it was caused by a specific manufacturing defect.

incident_description:

incident_description:
The caller stated that the while he was snowboarding down a slope the bindings cracked, his left foot slipped off the board and became stuck in the snow causing his ankle to dislocate.  He was taken to the hospital in Big Bear Ca. where he was treated and transported to Loma linda hospital for further treatment.

The binding broke apart during normal wear and tear. Consumer spoke with mfr and they wanted him to send them the product, and they would replace it as a "get well soon" gift. I had modified the binding color on the cloth on top of the foot latch only, and the part that failed on me was the hard plastic base.  This should never have happened.

UPDATE:
I have over 15 years of snowboarding experience and what happened to me on
March 18th 2013 was the frrst time I have seen or heard of this type of equipment failure.
I was out with my stepson and his friend celebrating his birthday on a beautiful spring
session. The weather and snow surfaces were ideal that day so I feel there were no factors
that could have contributed to the reason my binding disintegrated while I was boarding
down a black diamond run.
I was traveling down a run that I have visited on several occasions while at Snow
Summit ski resort in Big Bear CA. I was traveling a speed that I am very comfortable
with while maneuvering to a trail crossing I started to slow up as I turned to the left
everything was fine and then I started to tum to the right to head down another trail when
my front foot began to wobble and then became dislodged from my snowboard. My foot
planted into the soft snow and the momentum caused my left foot to become dislocated
and break my fibula while I violently crashed to the ground. This was the worst pain I
have felt in my life as well as the sight of my foot being turned the wrong direction was
very difficult to deal with. In the paper work sent to me I stated that this was related to
hazard #05-087. This was a completely separate area of the binding and that portion had
functioned properly.
I was transported to Big Bear hospital by my stepson and the moved to Lorna
Linda medical center for further treatment. I have since required surgery to correct the
damage from my fall. I contacted the manufacture and let them know about my fall and
what the cause of the incident was. I was truthful and honest about the binding including
that I was not happy with the fabric color and how I dyed it from white to black. This did
not in any way affect the integrity of the bindirtg and it wasn't even in the area that failed.
The response from Flow was that there warranty states not to modify or alter there
product, but they were to happy to send me a "get well soon" gift in the form of a new set
of bindings if I sent them my damaged product. This did not sit well for me or my wife
especially since they just seemed that they only wanted to secure the damaged equipment.
In this declaration I have enclosed several photos for your database and for your
documentation.
Thank you
justification: The incident resulted in a dislocated ankle and broken fibula requiring hospital treatment and surgery, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is unlikely (2) as the user has extensive experience and this was the first such failure in 15 years.

incident_description:
I have a 2008 Arctic Cat ATV 700 H1 SE.  While the driver was operating the ATV, the front axle locked up throwing the driver over the handlebars causing days of discomfort, but luckily no serious injury.  I have since read online that hundreds of Arctic Cat customers who purchased 2008 Arctic Cat ATV's have experienced this same dangerous situation and it is due to the fact that during this 2008 model run, the pin in the axle was not welded properly. It received a small tack weld on the pin and was never bead welded all the way around the pin as they had been done previously and since this model run.  Arctic Cat denies any obligation  to recall this known issue and someone is going to get killed over it.  Please refer to the following thread. 
http://www.arcticchat.com/forum/pinned-topics/249118-arctic-cat-front-differentials-locking-up.html
Arctic Cat is now wanting over $3000 to fix this problem on my quad.
justification: The driver experienced discomfort but no serious injury, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is high (4) due to multiple reports of the same issue.

I'm reporting this because I consider this trapeze handle to be a safety risk for children.  If a child is upside down while hanging on these trapeze handles and it breaks, they could fall to the ground on their head and break their neck.
justification: The child fell but was not injured, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood of recurrence is possible given the equipment failure.

incident_description:
[REDACTED] is an experienced archer, an archery instructor and a registered nurse (as well as
an Emergency Medical Technician). He has been active in the sport of archery for
approximately 20 years. By the date of the injury described in greater detail below, he had shot
tens of thousands of arrows without incident.
On Thursday, August 23, 2012, [REDACTED] purchased six Easton FlatLine D.O.A. carbon fiber arrows
(model 6.5gpi 500) from a sporting goods store in Bridgeport, Alabama. As it had in the past,
the store cut the arrow shafts to the appropriate length and installed target shooting points.
On Saturday, August 25, 2012, [REDACTED] went to a friendÃÂs farm on Weiss Lake in Leesburg,
Alabama, to shoot the arrows at a Morrell Yellow Jacket Fieldpoint Target. He used a [REDACTED] 
single cam compound bow that was purchased new in 2010 and that was in perfectly good
working order.
Around 5:00 pm that day, he prepared to shoot at his target from a distance of approximately 65
yards. He had never shot these particular Easton carbon fiber arrows before. Prior to firing any
of the arrows, he performed a visual inspection and flex testing. During that first run through,
and specifically on his fifth shot of the afternoon of an arrow that had never been fired before,
the arrow unexpectedly broke/splintered upon release and punctured his left arm/wrist area.
[REDACTED] went to the Riverview Hospital emergency room in Gadsden, Alabama, where they
performed a debridement. He had to return to the hospital on August 31, 2012 for the first of
two surgeries. The ER records reflect a wound repair of a linear shaped subcutaneous laceration
of approximately 3cm (1.2 inches) to the left wrist. His surgeon remarked that the wound was a
3.5cm incision over the radial aspect of his wrist, near the first dorsal compartment and may have
been slightly dorsal to that. He also suffered a rupture of his extensor pollicis longus (EPL)
tendon.
As a result of the shattered arrow shaft, he suffered extreme nerve damage to his arm, wrist and
hand. He has undergone considerable physical therapy and has been unable to return to work
since this incident.
[REDACTED]
M&A THE LAW OFFICES OF
Mastando & Artrip LLC
justification: The incident resulted in a significant injury requiring multiple surgeries and physical therapy, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) given the archer's extensive experience and the rarity of such incidents despite high arrow usage.

The scooter crashed and daughter fell to ground with minor injuries.  Chain came loose after fall but throttle system remained engaged; turning switch off did not disengage battery.

incident_description:
The Razor E100 scooter must be "kick started" to at least 3MPH before the motor will engage.  Step on the scooter, twist the throttle, and kick to get up to speed.  When the unit was new, letting go of the throttle caused the motor to disengage, allowing the scooter to slow down and even coast to a stop.  (Pressing the brake lever also disengages the motor.)

The throttle is now sticking.  That is, simply letting go the throttle does not cause the motor to disengage.  The rider must now press the brake lever to disengage the motor.

The E100 scooter is designed for kids (weight limit 120 pounds).  This problem with the throttle first occurred when my 11 year old grandson was riding the scooter.

The unit is just over a year and has had very little use.  There are no visible signs of damage, and as far as I know, the unit has never been wrecked or misused.

I called Razor and they are going to send an "electrical repair kit."  However, I'm not sure that I will trust the unit even after the kit is installed.
justification: The throttle sticking is an incident that could lead to loss of control, but no injury was reported. The likelihood is possible as it occurred during use but can be mitigated by pressing the brake.

The fork had developed a crack along the steer tube which would have resulted in a sever crash if the product had continued to be used.

incident_description:
2007 Arctic Cat F5 LXR gas tank leak at fuel sending unit collar after refueling... leaks directly onto top of cylinder and near exhaust components.

Incident occurred after refueling... once unknown as we refueled at home and trailered to a drop off point.  Gas tank had unknowingly leaked in trailer.  Smelled fuel when unloading but thought it was just because we had refueled. Now knowing what do the gas gauge was down a bar when we left on the ride.

Rode 80 miles to Prentice WI where we refueled... used 6.6 gallons ... more than usual when getting 14-15 mpg typically.  Began riding to lunch destination 3 miles away.  Smelled gas while riding.  Upon stopping took off side panel, saw gas running down side of tank in engine compartment.  Quickly pulled console off and saw gas running out of top collar where fuel sending unit is. Gas was dripping directly on top of engine and running along belly pan near exhaust.

Fuel continued to leak until for 15 - 20 minutes until fuel level dropped.

This is an extremely dangerous situation and Arctic Cat needs to RECALL this and other snowmobiles that have this fuel tank.  I am glad we had stopped rather than continuing down the railroad grade at 55 mph... it could have resulted in more than a very disappointed rider.

I will be requesting that Arctic Cat cover all costs and issue an immediate recall.  I will also be informing all other F series Arctic Cat Owners of the problem through our snowmobile club and County/State Association AWSC. 

The internet also has reports of this happening to the [REDACTED] of which I am also an owner.
justification: The incident involves a gas tank leak, which is dangerous but did not cause any injury or death.

incident_description: Consumer reports that he was using a tennis racket and eventually developed permanent and serious injury to his shoulder. He underwent necessary surgery.
justification: The consumer developed a permanent and serious injury requiring surgery, which qualifies as a severity level 3.

justification: The net ripped but no injury occurred as the other boy prevented a fall.

incident_description:
I was driving a 1996 Polaris Magnum 6 x 6 ATV making a turn when the throttle cable would not go  back into normal operation in throttle mode after pressing the throttle half way open. Basically I  released the gas in a turn
and the unit did not release back to throttle mode.  With both hands locked on the brakes the  unit was still moving
quickly.  I was within 10 feet of going over a 15 - 20 foot embankment into a rocky area at the  lake. I reached over, took a chance and turned the key off.  The unit stopped. I purchased the unit  new in 1997; it has 775 miles on it. I filed a complaint with Polaris in  1998 about a carburetor issue that it would not idle properly; the  problem was not corrected.
It is interesting after reviewing your site Polaris did a recall in August 2000 about the sticking  throttle cable issues on
other units.   It would be interesting to see if these units they recalled had the same "Polaris  Electronic Throttle
Control (ETC)" systems  as my 1996 unit.

My paths crossed with a Polaris employee, as I described what happened to me,the person was not 
surprised and stated that early year machines were basically a piece of "Junk" until later years in  2000.

I was fortunate my teenage son was not on the unit because he would not have known to turn the key  off.
justification: The incident involved a stuck throttle cable that nearly caused a dangerous situation, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Sportcraft Tredex 6.0 Treadmill
Walking at 2.8 speed when it suddenly accelerated to an out of control speed. I fell off hitting the treadmill belt on my leg and arms. I had severe burns and bruises. The treadmill continues to run at this out of control speed that the control panel can not even display.
justification: The incident resulted in severe burns and bruises, indicating injury (severity 3). The sudden acceleration of the treadmill is an uncommon but not impossible occurrence (likelihood 2).

incident_description: I bought your Tyke Toter to ride with my 4 year old son on an [REDACTED] bike. Up to last week the seat has been a joy to use with my son on our family bike rides. On Saturday February 23 I took my son [REDACTED] out for our usual paved trail ride. While on our fourth mile of the ride at approximately 10 miles per hour my son's foot slid off the Tyke foot pegs and into the spokes of the bicycle's front wheel.
