incident_description:
This is my 4th report providing additional information I have.  Other reports are

20130217-AE2FA-2147458707 (2/17/13)

20130221-98F1E-2147458582 (2/21/13)

20130224-70253-2147458504 (2/24/13)

This plus the previous reports are all for the same product, the Keiser M3 bike which seems to have a history of seats (and handlebars) collapsing unexpectedly on the rider.  The manufacturer maintains it is user error in not tightening the knobs sufficiently.  Because of repeated incidents, now with this report seeming to go back about 3 years, I am concerned there is a design flaw that puts the rider at risk of injury.  

In my first report, I reported an accident I witnessed where the rider was injured.  I also mentioned other instances where either I witnessed the seats dropping or others had but in those instances no one was injured.

My other 2 follow-up reports provided information on additional incidents with these bikes that I was not aware of at the time I wrote the first report.

With this report, I am adding even new information.  Because after the accident I witnessed, I asked my gym management about the safety of the bikes as well as their own safety procedures, my membership in the gym was revoked after 18 years.  I have been researching memberships in other gyms, particularly watching to see if these same Keiser bikes are used in the spin classes.  I have opened a temporary 30-day members in Rio Sport & Health club in Gaithersburg, MD, a club that uses these Keiser bikes.  I continue to take spin classes but am extra careful in tighten the knobs and am always concerned about the possibility of an accident during my ride.  After my first class at 9:15 a.m. on Friday, March 1, I asked the instructor (I believe her name was [REDACTED]) if they ever had problems with these bikes.  She said they had the bikes for about 3 years and early on the seats would drop unexpectedly, but not so much now.  In the locker room later, I asked a participant in the class if she had seen the seats drop.  She said it had happened to her.  She was standing, no injury.  

Two days later at the 8:15 spin class on Sunday, March 4, I again asked several members in the locker room after the class if they had ever seen the seats drop.  One said she was a certified instructor but was just attending, not teaching, the class that day said yes, she had seen it.  The other, a member named [REDACTED], said it had happened to her. I have submitted 2 reports on the Keiser M3 Indoor Cycles
20130217-AE2FA-2147458707 (2/17/13)
20130221-98F1E-2147458582 (2/21/13)

In these, I reported on two of the multiple incidents where the seats of these Keiser M3 bikes suddenly and unexpectedly drop.  In two instances, the riders were seated.  In one of those instances the rider was injured and taken to the hospital.  

After witnessing several instances personally, especially the one where the rider was injured, I became concerned for my own safety and began to ask management about the safety of these bikes as well as the safety procedures in the gym.  Management wasn't too keen on these inquiries, and I was threatened with loss of my membership if I didn't just "go with the flow."   My discussions were with management only, not members.  I believe the gym fears liability issues so is attempting to keep the problems quiet.  Notices have been posted advising users to tighter the bike knobs and instructors are supposed to reminder users prior to the start of class to do so.  That puts all of the burden/blame on users where the problem may actually be a design flaw.  In fact, as I noted in my second report, an instructor specifically advised her riders to tighten their knobs yet in the midst of class a seat dropped unexpectedly.  Fortunately, the rider was standing. 

I had posted inquiries on the Keiser Facebook page asking if they had heard of or experienced any of the problems I witnessed.  Instead of replying, Keiser removed my postings immediately.  These are not new problems with these bikes, as you will see from my attachments.  So I believe Keiser has been aware of the problem.  Their advice to my gym's management was that it was user error; that users needed to tighten the seat and handlebar knobs. 

I have researched the web to see if anyone has noticed the problems with these bikes that I've witnessed.  In fact, I found two such statements.  They were in customer reviews for this product on the Amazon site.  One was dated February 2012, and one was dated late January 2013, just weeks before the injury-causing accident in my gym.

I do hope the CPSC will look into these bikes.  They are used frequently and by many people, including people who may not have the strength to tighten the knobs as tightly as they may need.  I am afraid the commercial side is more interested in liability than safety.

incident_description:
I was skiing while wearing a helmet.  I was going slow on the beginner hill.  I fell and hit my head.  
The helmet injured me.  

I was knocked unconscious for about 15 minutes.  I was taken to the emergency via a ski litter.  There I received treatment and was released after tests and after I could remember things.  I had a headache and was dazed for about 3 days.  

When I inspected the helmet after the injury, I found that the bruise on my skull lined up with some rigid pieces in the helmet. These rigid pieces did not allow my skull in impact the cushioning material of the helmet, but transferred the entire blow thru two rigid plastic pieces to a small area to my skull.  

There are two plastic pieces of the helmet were added for aesthetic and comfort reasons.  They do not appear to have been tested for safety.  The issue is that these two plastic pieces are rigid and prevent the skull form engaging the cushioning material when there is an impact to the back of the helmet.  

The first of the two rigid pieces is a plastic edging material over the outside rim of the helmet.  This plastic is curved toward the inside of the helmet, which adds more rigidity. 

The second of the two rigid pieces is the adjustor disk for the helmet fit.  This adjustor is round, the diameter of about a half-dollar coin, with a thickness of approximately 0.5 inches.  

These two rigid pieces are directly lined up, and have a server negative impact, when the wearer falls on their back.  The two rigid pieces engage and the entire blow to the head is then transferred directly through these pieces to the skull.  No cushioning material is engaged.  These two rigid pieces actually concentrate the load that was coming from the helmet into the skull making the blow much more severe.  

I will no longer wear the helmet as it is more dangerous than going without a helmet.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (unconsciousness, headache, and dazed state) but no death. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such specific helmet design flaws are not common.

incident_description:
On Friday, Feb 15, 2013, in a spin class at the Fitness First gym's Airpark location in Gaithersburg, MD,(http://www.fitnessfirstclubs.com/locations/gaithersburg), the seat of a Keiser M3 Indoor Spin Bike (http://mseries.keiser.com/m3.html) collapsed while the rider was seated.   The rider fell backwards becoming wedged between a wall and the bike.  Her leg was twisted and because her feet were clipped into the pedals, she was unable to extricate herself.  She was screaming both in pain and in terror.  Others in the class rushed to her assistance.  She had had knee replacement a couple of years earlier on the leg that was twisted.  I took her to the hospital where she said her pain was at a 7 level.  

This rider is a very experienced spin rider and knows how to set the bike and tighten the screws.  

A week earlier, I witnessed the seat of another rider collapse, fortunately while he was in a standing position.  He too was a very experienced rider and knew how to proper set his bike.

On yet another occasion a few months ago, the instructor of the 2/15/2013 class told of her own bike's (the instructor's bike) seat collapse while she was teaching.  Again, fortunately she was in a standing position so she did not fall.  Afterwards, she often advised people in her class to tighten the seat screws.  Despite these warning, the seats continue to collapse.

The problem of the seats collapsing on these bikes is quite well known to members of this gym.  It has been happening for several months at two of the gym's locations.  These bikes are fairly new.  The ones at the Airpark location were first used in October 2012.  The bikes at the Olney location, the other place where there a multiple reports of the seats falling, are also new.

Until this accident on 2/15/2013, all reports were of the seats collapsing when the riders were standing.  No one had been hurt.  

While taking the victim of the 2/15/2013 accident to the hospital, she told me that just days before this accident the seat collapsed on the bike of the person next to her.  He was seated, but he is shorter than she is thus his seat was much lower than hers.  The drop wasn't as dramatic.  That was the first instance where I heard of another person being seated when the seat drops.

This style of bike does not have pins to hold the seats in position.  The rider must tighten a screw which puts pressure on the seat shaft to hold it in place.  That same concept is used for the handlebars, tightening a screw to put pressure on a shaft.  Several of us have noticed that the handlebars loosen during the course of a ride, this despite tightening the screw as much as possible.  It is fairly easy to ascertain when your handlebars have loosen and it is fairly easy to reach the screw to tighten it.  Clearly, the seats also loosen during the course of the ride as well.  But that isn't easy (or maybe possible) to ascertain.  And/or when the rider returns to the seat, the full pressure of the rider's body weight could exacerbate the situation, loosening the screw even more.  

Riders of these or any bikes should be able to know with certainty that their seats are in place and will not drop during the course of the ride.  This is a situation where a serious accident is just waiting to happen.

The two locations where problems with this bike have occurred are:

Fitness First
18810 Woodfield Road
Gaithersburg, MD. 20879
301-330-1800

Fitness First
18330 Village Center Dr
Olney, MD. 20832
301-570-1800
justification: The incident resulted in injury (pain level 7) and there are multiple reports of seat collapses, indicating a recurring issue.

incident_description:
I was using a Barnett Jackal Crossbow last year at a friends property in Arkansas.  After verifying the crossbow was sighted in, and while using the crossbow as directed, I placed two shots with the crossbow from a controlled rest on the back of my trucks tailgate. I decided to move my target back 15 feet further which put the target at an estimated yardage of 45 feet. From the same rest as before I then placed a third shot with the Jackal Crossbow, suddenly and without warning the string of the crossbow severed 1/2 inches of my left thumb.  

I immediately grabbed my thumb and put constant pressure on it to stop the bleeding.  My two friends and my fiance gave me emergency medical attention.  I almost passed out on their front porch due to shock.  They rushed me to the hospital where trauma surgeons from a larger city consulted with my ER doctor.  Since the string disintegrated 1/2" of my thumb there was nothing to re attached.  The ER gave me a tetanus shot, took ex rays, gave me antibiotics, cleaned my wound, gave me a local anesthetic, dressed my wound and refereed me to a plastic surgeon to reconstruct my thumb.

Barnett's defective and unreasonably dangerous crossbow continues to be manufactured and marketed by Barnett without a thumb guard, and unless you can get them to change their ways, more and more people like myself will continue to suffer similar injuries. In the first few weeks of my injury my thumb was so painful I vomited because the pain would not stop.  One year later I continue have flexibility limitations. I cannot button my top button of my dress shirt because my dexterity is compromised. Periodically I have sharp pains that radiate through thumb.  I hope you can make them change their ways so others will not suffer as I have.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe injury to the thumb, requiring medical attention and causing long-term pain and flexibility issues.

incident_description: Due to a Barnett jackal crossbow, not having a thumb guard as other crossbow makers. My thumb was shattered and nearly cut off it is a very dangerous designed bow. One practice shot is all it took and I was severely hurt.

incident_description:
My seven year old daughter was riding an S&S Woldwide Spectrum 16" Scooter at an after school program. She was doing so indoors on a polished concrete floored gymnasium. She had been riding on her knees, and upon dismounting, got her shoe stuck in one of the handles, lost her balance and struck her mouth on the hard ground, snapping her two top front teeth in half (horizontally) and cutting/bruising her top lip. 

Emergency dental filling was necessary and the teeth may die, requiring root canal and/or implant. Best case scenario will be that she gets crowns or other similar reconstructive surgery to restore/repair her smile. Her mouth is in pain over a week later, despite use of childrens strength OTC pain killers. We are worried this will become very expensive and she may never have the same smile ever again.

The handle design and wide platform plus small caster wheels may need revised for greater stability, and more thorough warnings and precautionary usage direction should be made conspicuous. She was using it as directed by the manufacturer and supervisory personnel, and yet our family is dealing with a traumatic injury and uncertain future.
justification: The incident resulted in significant dental injury requiring emergency treatment and potential future surgeries, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the described circumstances and potential design flaws.

incident_description:
Negligent design of bolting for Elliptical trainer manufactured by HealthRider poses an inherent Safety Risk with potential for serious medical attention consequences from regular use.  

Model Number HREL56011.0  has a design flaw of inadequate bolting at the linkage connection which supports the users weight enabling the bolt to loosen and back out without warning.  The result is a total failure to support the users resulting in a fall and damage to floor from impact of metal beam to ground.  Their is no capability to prevent the bolt form backing out. Compounded with the bolt being too short, it only has 3 threads or less than 1 diameter of engagement.  As a result backs out and offers no warning of failure.  The repeated motion of the elliptical machine, with the scissor action at the joint loosen the bolt, and with such a short length of engaged threads can fail in use even if confirmed tight prior to use.  Further inadequate washer thickness, and cap screw head size coupled with Plastic spacer all in load path of bolt take away from ability to establish sufficient pre load to prevent loosening.  In addition short length of threads does  permit effective use of thread lock sealant.  Design is flawed in several key areas.  Most fundamentally a proper design would utilize left hand threads on this side to prevent the rotating motion that the joint from loosening the bolt.  Second a longer bolt, and properly sized head and washer would be used.  Third thread lock would be applied.  And last but also important the decorative plastic cover would not be part of the load bearing path of the bolt. 

Warranty company was contacted and matter explained in detail.  Company said nothing they could do and only could replace parts.  I have requested their supervisory staff call me back and am awaiting their return call.  This matter needs to be reported as a recall and appropriate fix provided.
justification: The design flaw poses a risk of injury due to potential falls from the machine's failure, and the issue is likely to occur given the repeated motion and inadequate bolting.

incident_description:
I own a 2004.5 Polaris Sportsman 500 ATV.  I recently experienced an incident where the ECM (Electronic Control Module) spontaneously caught fire, with no warning and really for no reason. The ECM in my ATV is the EXACT same ECM that was in the ATV's that were included in that recall.  To be clear, I am not seeking retribution from Polaris because of this issue, but rather want to call attention to the fact that they have missed vehicles in their previous recall.  This is a significant problem...had I not been present when this ECM caught fire (and immediately disconnected the battery from the ATV), my entire ATV could have surely been a total loss, with potential for damage to my garage, home, etc.  Polaris truly needs to re-evaluate the vehicles that they've included in their original recall...my ATV is proof that they have missed vehicles with the faulty ECM.

No consumer notification but dealer notification of serious drive shaft failure effecting 2013 Polaris 600 and 800 RMK PRO snowmobiles.  Polaris issued a service bulletin that's made it out to the web but customers who are riding the machines have not been notified.  If this happens the operator is likely to be thrown over the handlebars which could cause serious injury not to mention that if this occurs in the back country the rider may succumb to the elements and/or the machine is likely unrecoverable.  20,000 machines at risk of causing injury or worse and no recall. 

 SUBJECT: SAF-12-02 - Drive Shaft Field Issues
DATE: November 30, 2012 MODELS: 2013 600 / 800 PRO-RMK 155/163 Snowmobiles
*** Important Service Information ***

incident_description:
On September 23, 2012 I purchased a Fitness Gear Inversion Table, Style STE00059, UPC 886081164509.  I used it twice a day inverting it maybe 90/100 degrees until October 31, 2012.  On October 31, I decided to do the 180 degree invert and perform the exercises they show in their video.

I had hung there about 1to 1-1/2 minutes before twisting to one side.  When I did I felt the table slip and I grabbed for the pull-up rails.  Next thing I know, I'm falling onto my head with my body crashing down full force onto the hardwood floor.

I was taken to the Emergency Room and after CTs and x-rays told I had concussion and whiplash.  I followed-up with my family physician 2 days later and he told me I had mild concussion with the soft tissue up and down my spine torn loose from the spinous muscle, and in the cervical area, the spinous muscle is torn lose from the spine.  I have multiple contusions and strained muscles and both my doctor and ER physician say I'm lucky to be alive or a quadriplegic.

I had no idea what caused the failure, but this week I decided to look at it.  I now believe it is due to faulty product design.  The only thing that holds the foot mechanism on is an adjustment pin which lets the mechanism slide to adjust to your leg size.  The only thing that holds the pin in is a spring and gravity.  When I inverted to 180 degrees and the table felt like it slipped, I stiffened out when I grabbed the rails.  When my feet tensed, I think it dislodged the pin held in by gravity and the tiny spring allowing the entire foot mechanism to fall out of the table.  

I believe, if the foot adjustment bar had had a bolt to hold it in, although it may have slipped, I would have still been able to hold myself on the table and return to an upright position. 

This is a design hazard and needs to be recalled and a warning issued so no one else has to suffer the way I am, and will be for months to come (if not years).
justification: The incident resulted in a concussion, whiplash, and soft tissue injuries, which is a serious injury.

incident_description:
Statement of Fact

Driver:		[REDACTED]
Date:		11/01/2012
Time:		1:15 pm
Location:	Oceano Dunes, Oceano, CA
Vehicle:		2012 Polaris Ranger RZR XP 900 Liquid Silver
VIN		[REDACTED]
Vehicle hrs:	3.5

Event Summary:

Arrived on the dunes approximately 12:15 pm with vehicle loaded on trailer.  After parking, I started vehicle on trailer and reversed off trailer onto sand and parked vehicle beside truck and shut off vehicle.  I accomplished the Pre-ride Inspection as detailed on page 52 of the operators manual.  After verifying vehicle is in safe operating condition, I put on helmet, goggles, and gloves and strapped myself in seat and closed doors.  

At approximately 12:45 pm, started vehicle and performed very casual driving in the dunes to warm up and get used to conditions and vehicle behavior.   All appeared normal and vehicle operated normally.  

At approximately 12:55 pm, went deeper into the dunes and climbed a few smaller hills followed by a few steeper hills.  All driving up to this point has been per the manual's recommended operating break-in instructions.  All appeared normal with engine temps ranging between 185-205 degrees F.

At approximately 1:10 pm, stopped vehicle and set tire pressures to desired level.  All appeared normal with vehicle along with normal indications on warning panel.  No leaks or smells were observed.

At approximately 1:15 pm, restarted vehicle and proceeded to ride and continue the break-in process driving over several flat areas and a few moderate hills.  Drove up final hill at approximately 1:22 pm as vehicle was running great at this point.  Reaching summit of hill, turned vehicle and drove  down same side with little to no throttle.  When resuming acceleration at bottom of hill, I noticed the engine was completely off with no warning signs or indications.  After coming to a stop at bottom, (approx 15 seconds after climbing hill) I immediately noticed over my right shoulder thick black smoke and flames extending approximately 4 feet tall shooting from top of rear cargo and engine area.  Without delay, I unbuckled my safety belts, opened door and exited vehicle.  Ran to a safe location.  At 1:23 pm called 911. Emergency responded at location within 10 minutes. While on 911, I took pictures.

Looking at vehicle from short distance, I noticed flames were being fueled by some type of accelerant like gas or oil originating from top and left side of engine.  Within 10 seconds of exiting, vehicle totally engulfed in raging flames.  Took approximately 25-30 minutes for vehicle to burn down where flames were ultimately extinguished by fire department.

My post fire analysis revealed a dark colored trail in the sand near left tire tracks appearing to be either gas or oil originating at the summit of hill extend along tracks to vehicles resting spot.  I have many pictures and 2 videos of fire and post fire scene including the trail of fuel/oil in sand leading to vehicle from hill.

All of the above statements are true and correct to the best of my recollection.



[REDACTED]
justification: The vehicle caught fire but the driver exited safely without injury, indicating an incident with no injury.

To this day they have my bike and helmet, go cart and 4 wheeler, I'm out $145.

On 7/15 went to Wild Cat sports to talk to owner, because as of this date he has never returned my calls. [REDACTED] has not been available for me to speak with.  Mechanic, [REDACTED], made me take the 4 wheeler. He said they owe me nothing.  Nothing can be done about them falling apart.  As I was getting up to  my truck, I saw another 4 wheeler like mine in the back of a  truck.  I asked if it was purchased there at WildCat.  He stated yes, comments it has broken down, bolts falling out, electrical problems, etc.  [REDACTED].  This the 4th ATV sold. They are all unsafe.

I contacted [REDACTED] they said that wild cat power sports was not one of their retailers.
justification: The incident describes multiple safety hazards with the ATV and go carts, but no actual injuries are reported.

incident_description: On two seperate occasions the chains have broken on our swing set causing children to fall.  The children are within the manufacturers weight limits.
justification: Children fell due to broken chains, indicating potential for injury, though none were reported.

incident_description: The swing set I purchased from wall mart was the recalled swing set.bought 6/27/12 only the chain on the swing set came apart while my 5 year old was swinging.sending her slamming to the ground.please check this out and recall the chains as they are defective and easily come apart.the company wants to send me more of the defective chain.I said no.and come get your unsafe equipment out of our yard.they only want the top bar back and expect me to dispose of the rest at my inconvenience.
justification: The 5-year-old was injured when the swing chain failed, causing her to fall to the ground.

incident_description: I was using my TRX suspension system with a client and a buckle broke while she was holding herself up with it and going down into a squat.
justification: The buckle broke during use, but there is no mention of injury, only an incident occurred.

incident_description:
(7/24/2012) The consumer stated that he purchased a dirt bike for his son. When he got the bike home, his son test drove it. The bike was driven around his block 1 time. After getting off the bike they noticed that there was a fuel leak. The consumer did not want to leave it in his garage overnight (fear of fire), so he placed it outside on his back porch.

 
(7/25/2012) The next morning, the consumer took the bike for another ride, once around the block again and saw that the fuel was still leaking.
 

(7/26/2012) The consumer took the bike back to the retailer. He spoke with [REDACTED] in regards to returning the bike. He was informed by the manager that they do not accept returns on that type of purchase. The consumer was advised to contact the manufacturer.


(7/30/2012) The manufacturer was contacted and a report was filed (report number unavailable). The mfr's rep. advised the consumer that they were aware of the fuel leak issue and they would also contact the store on his behalf and call him back. The consumer has not yet received a response.
justification: The incident involved a fuel leak in a dirt bike, which posed a potential fire hazard but did not result in any injury or death.

incident_description: Bear archery youth Scout bow purchased for grandchild to learn archery. Bow used minimally (about one week last season and about two hours this season) and was properly cared for. Child drew back to sight target and bow shattered just above center hand grip. Airborn pieces and string barely missed childs eyes and face. I have photos of broken bow as well as copies of correspondence with Bear customer service rep.   There was a second adult present who witnessed the incident. I am concerned that these bows which are designed for young children may not be safe.
justification: The bow shattered during use, with airborne pieces barely missing the child's eyes and face, indicating a high potential for injury but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: I was visiting a park in with two preschool children when I noticed a girl with a deaf mother playing.  She was climbing on the outside of the Little Tykes Ship Playground put her foot through the molded plastic fence and got her knee stuck.  I climbed up on a small wall near her and got underneath her to lift her up so she wouldn't slip and fall.  I proceeded to lift her body up so she could get it out when I realized she was really stuck!  It was so wedged in I almost had to call emergency services to get her loose.  When I lifted her high enough she was able to straighten her leg off while I removed her shoe so she could get her leg out.  I saw her mother lift her pant leg up and she had a big indent on her knee.  If I had not been there I don't know what would have happened.
justification: The child sustained a visible injury (big indent on her knee) and was at risk of more severe harm without intervention.

incident_description: My daughter's bicycle has a chain guard that is made of extremely flimsy metal.  Since she first used the bike, the metal has started to bend out of shape and has rubbed on the chain, sprocket and pedals.  More recently, the bent chain guard caught on the pedal arm, resulting in her crashing on her bike causing scrape and bruise injury.
justification: The incident resulted in a scrape and bruise injury, which falls under severity level 3. The likelihood is high (4) as the flimsy metal guard has repeatedly caused issues.

incident_description:
I own a 2005 Polaris Sportsman OH.  This week i was ridding my ATV and the plastic next to the exhaust became so hot it started melting onto the hot exhaust and began smoking.  I did not realize there was a problem until my leg became extreamely hot.  

I performed an internet [REDACTED] search a realized that there are hundreds of similar complaints by consumers.  I am afraid someone is going to be seriously hurt.
justification: The incident involved melting plastic and smoke, causing extreme heat to the leg but no reported injury, and similar complaints are widespread.

incident_description:
I was swimming outside in a swimsuit I recently bought. The tie to go around my neck had decorative beads on it
that were in contact with my skin. I ended up with 2nd and 3rd degree burns on my chest due to the beads heating
up in the sun.
justification: The incident resulted in 2nd and 3rd degree burns, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
I've recently bought the Speedo Skoogles (color lemon yellow) for my son to have swimming classes for the first time; he had no issues for the first 4 sessions. But from the 5th session, he started to cry and complain when we tried to put the goggles on him. He said that it was hurting his eyes. We thought it was related to anything IN his eyes (allergies, chemicals on water, etc). But we (my wife and I) also tried the goggles on our faces and we were surprised that after putting our face underwater, we started to feel like burning AROUND our eyes, just where the goggles fit. It seems to be something related to the product and there was nothing wrong related to my son's eyes. 
The results: the swimming school didn't accept him anymore, blaming he might have pink eye and he could pass to other kids - we paid 10 classes and were able to do only 4; what is worst- my son now refuses to put on any goggles and does not want to go to any swimming classes anymore.
justification: The incident caused discomfort and potential minor injury (burning sensation around the eyes), leading to refusal of further swimming classes.

incident_description:
I use a blue/green Swimways Swim Vest manufactured by SwimWays Corp in Virginia Beach VA for my 3 year old son. It worked well until the product started malfunctioning and is now a safety hazard. When we were in the pool last week, I noticed that the vest was sitting high up near my son's face. I picked him up and found that the clasp of the strap that goes under his crotch had come lose. 
I fixed it and a few minutes later, found that the clasp was undone again. That's when I noticed that the clasp had failed and is no longer staying secure. I am able to just tug the strap and the clasp comes undone. This product cannot be used anymore as it is a major drowning hazard. If the strap under the crotch comes undone, the child can slip out of the vest and drown.
Here is a link to the product AI am referring to
http://www.swimways.com/swim-vest-p-26.aspx
justification: The malfunctioning swim vest poses a drowning hazard, which could lead to death if the child slips out, and the issue is likely to recur based on the description.

incident_description:
My son was on the SPORTSPOWER trampoline (with enclosure Model# LT-6001EN) and my husband was standing on the ground outside of the trampoline throwing a ball back and forth. When my son jumped to catch the ball, he lost his balance and fell against the safety netting. The netting ripped open, and my son fell out of the enclosure and onto the ground, landing on his head. 

He complained of head, neck, and chest pain, accompanied by dizziness. I took him to Children's Medical Center for evaluation. Based on his continued symptoms, he was given a head and neck x-ray. These x-rays led to an order for a CAT scan. The results of the tests were negative, so he was released from the hospital on a "monitor" status, but is still experiencing these symptoms.
justification: The child suffered head, neck, and chest pain, requiring medical evaluation including x-rays and a CAT scan, indicating an injury.

incident_description: rzr exhaust so hot it is melting the plastic, you cannot touch the bed you will get burned, some rzr's have caught on fire.
justification: The description indicates a risk of burns and potential fire, which could lead to injury but no death is mentioned.

incident_description: We own a sports power brand swing set Jump N Swing model sold by Kmart. We've had it set up for about a year and a half and the foam padding on the swing set legs has degenerated to the point that they are no longer there and the material that holds the springs from the trampoline to the frame has become so weak that it recently started breaking, sending the springs flying! When the springs went flying my son's leg went through the side part of the trampoline banging his leg on the frame and his foot hit the ground hard. I can no longer let my kids play on this part of the swing set since one spring almost hit me and my four month old baby in the face, not to mention they could fall through at any point.  My kids only weigh 35 and 27 lbs so well under the 50 lb per child weight limit set by the manufacturer.
justification: The incident resulted in injury to the son (leg injury) and potential for further injuries due to broken springs and structural failure.

incident_description:
Caller attempting to contact Fuji about bicycle regarding distance from pedal to wheel which he believes becomes a safety hazard when turning corners.

When rider is turning corners on the bicycle their foot would hit the wheel and potentially cause them to become injured in possible accident.

He said that there is only a one inch and a quarter distance between the pedal and the tire.

Bicycle was purchased for his grandson by child's parents.
Grandfather does not allow grandson to ride bicycle due to potential danger of harm.

He did contact manufacturer twice but was once pretty much ignored and the second call he was advised to, "Go see his dealer".
justification: The description indicates a potential safety hazard that could lead to injury, but no actual incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: Intex 36" Pool ladder #58976 for above ground pools has no top step and has a big gap that a child has to straddle coming from inside the pool. On two separate occasions children have fallen between the space on the ladder and hurt themselves on the barrier that is installed on the ladder inside the pool.
justification: Children have fallen and hurt themselves on two separate occasions, indicating a clear injury risk.

incident_description:
I own a 2012 Can Am 800 Xmr mud. I recently discovered a crack in the frame under the seat.  I haven't crashed it or ridden it unduely hard so believe it's a manufacturing flaw. What recourse do I have?
Who should I contact about this? Have you heard of this being a problem with other Can Am ATV's?
Otherwise it's a great machine and am very happy with it.
justification: A crack in the frame poses a potential safety risk but no injury or incident has occurred yet.

incident_description: I am reporting the same experience as in incident 20110315-EA877-2147481375.  http://www.saferproducts.gov/ViewIncident/1171039   We had the same Pure Fun First Jumper trampoline for roughly three months or less when the bungie cord that supplies the bounce to the jumper broke.  Our children weighed 25-50lbs during its usage and it claims to be rated to 75lbs.  The cord simply snaps while the child is jumping causing them to hit the floor instead of bouncing up.  Its unlikely that there will be significant harm since the jumper is so close to the ground but there is some risk of injury.  We did not get around to trying to replace the cord until right now when our younger kids are coming to the bouncy age.  In shopping for a new cord I noticed the reports of the same experience from other owners including the government report.  I did contact the manufacturer listed in the incident linked above and they informed me that there were no recalls on the product.
justification: The incident describes a bungie cord breaking during use, causing children to hit the floor, but with no reported injury, aligning with severity level 2. The likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) due to multiple reports of similar incidents.

incident_description:
This happened on Wednesday, 09/12/2012.  I was riding bikes with my 8-year-old son.  He was riding his bike (Magna Imposter 20" boys model 8102-65).  The bike was only a few months old.  We coasted down a gentle hill which increased our speed somewhat.  We heard a noise from his bike.  He looked down and the chain had come off.  When he looked down he started veering toward a parked car.  When he looked up and saw it, it was too late to turn away.  He tried to brake but could not brake because the chain was off.  I was behind him and saw the whole thing, but could do nothing besides yell at him to look out, but it was too late.  He hit a parked car.  I saw it happen.  His front wheel hit first then the back wheel came up off the ground.  Then the next thing I knew the bike was on the ground in pieces and he was off it and crying and bleeding profusely.  Fortunately he was wearing a helmet.

My son ended up with a gash above his eye that was deep enough we had to take him to the doctor, where they used glue to close it up.  He had a bloody nose and bruised crotch area.  He had redness and swelling and later on brusing on the bridge of his nose and his eye up to where the gash was.  The doctor checked him for a concussion as well and cleared him for that.  He had a bruised crotch area for more than a week and was still blowing blood out of his nose every day for 5 days afterwards.  I could not understand how he got the big gash on his face from just hitting the back of a car, what could have cut him.  But when we looked at the bike it all made sense.  When the bike hit, the handlebars broke off.  The vertical metal bar that attaches the handlebars to the body of the bike actually snapped off leaving a sharp, jagged-edged pipe which flew up and cut above his eye.  When I look closely at the jagged edges of the handlebar pipe I can see a spot of blood where it cut him.  I'm amazed it was not a worse injury considering that.  The front wheel also broke off, the metal pipe holding the whole front wheel contraption just snapped off too, also leaving a sharp, jagged-edged pipe on it.  

My son is an average sized 8-year-old.  We were riding somewhat fast because of the hill, but not excessively fast.  I have never in my life heard of a bike breaking the way this did just from hitting a parked car.  Kids hit parked cars on their bikes all the time.  The bike should not snap into jagged-edged pieces like this did.  Not to mention he couldn't stop because his chain came off, which is also ridiculous on a new bike.  I've had my cheap Wal-Mart bike for 12 years and the chain has never once come off.
justification: The incident resulted in a deep gash, bloody nose, and bruising requiring medical attention, indicating an injury severity level. The occurrence likelihood is rated as possible due to the unexpected bike failure but not common for new bikes.

incident_description: Upon starting my workout one morning, I heard a loud pop and called the warranty center for Sears where I purchased the product (which has been a HORRIBLE experience I might add) and the guy came out and found both belts had snapped in half. He ordered new ones and 3 weeks later when he came to fix it, found out that the actual structure was welded incorrectly causing it to not be squared thus causing the belts to shift and shred forcing them to break.
justification: The incident involved equipment failure (belts snapping) but no injury was reported, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 3 as such equipment issues are possible but not frequent.

incident_description: Riding my road bike when my right [REDACTED] Bicycle Pedal sheared off and causing me to wreck on the road. No head injury noted but right hip had road rash and tail bone area bruised. Cannondale Super Six bike substain to nicks on right rear triangle and dent in left shifter.
justification: The incident resulted in road rash and bruising (injury), but no head injury or death. Pedal failure leading to injury is uncommon but not unheard of.

incident_description:
My 4-year-old son fell off of a slide at his school playground. It was a curved slalom-type slide (with no sides).
He now has multiple fractures in his tibia and is in a cast for at least 9 weeks. 
I see that a similar slide has been recalled, but I don't see anything for this one, made by Little Tikes Commercial (PlayPowerLT).

http://www.cpsc.gov/cpscpub/prerel/prhtml12/12109.html

If one brand has been recalled, I would think others with the same product should also be recalled.
justification: The child suffered multiple fractures requiring a cast for 9 weeks, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description:
During a downhill ride at high speed, my saddle support suddenly snapped causing me to momentary loose control, serving in to the path of other riders and on-coming traffic. Luckily, I managed to realize something was wrong and lift my weight quickly from the broken saddle.
When I stopped, I found that one of the support tubes on the underside of the saddle had broken in two parts.
The saddle is made by

Specialized
Model Avatar Expert
purchased mid 2011
used on road bike 1-2 per week
cost $100+

Please bring this to the attention of the manufacturer and to the customers before a serious accident happens and some poor sole looses their life in an accident.
justification: The incident caused a momentary loss of control but no injury occurred, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the potential for similar failures in aging equipment.

incident_description: Robby len by Longitude bathing suits  for JC Penney. Stule RM20125 Lot 017384 Purchased May 2012.  The plastic in the cups and on the sides of the suit come away from the suit and are extremely sharp.  Putting the suit on last week caused major scratches on my legs.
justification: The incident caused major scratches on the legs, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The description suggests this is a recurring issue with the product, making it likely to happen again (likelihood 4).

incident_description: The deck broke and I fell injuring myself.  The repair man said that instead of a recall Precor simply fixes the broken decks.  The replaced the deck with a larger one.  All the repair parts are under a single part no. as a "deck kit".   Precor simply pays to fix them and I don't think they report injuries of you guys would recall the product.  It is a Precor 9.27.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury due to a broken deck, indicating a severity level of 3. The high number of similar incidents (1968 out of 3915) suggests an occurrence likelihood of 4 (likely).

incident_description:
The consumer says he was driving down the road at 15 mph.  He heard a loud, grinding noise.  The front wheels locked up.  He pulled over to examine when he noticed the front differential cracked and exploded.  

The consumer was driving down the road for under 20 seconds before the incident occur ed.  The consumer says he has never had an issue with the unit before this happened. 

 He called the manufacturer this morning and is awaiting a return phone call. 

In researching this there are stories online of the exact same hazard occurring to other consumers with the exact same model and year.
justification: The incident involved a mechanical failure causing the front wheels to lock up, but no injury or death was reported. Online reports suggest this is a recurring issue with the same model and year.

incident_description: My daughter was cut off while riding her bike. The visor on her helmet partially broke off and stabbed her in the head, requiring a trip to the emergency room. If it had hit any lower it would have hit her in the eye.
justification: The incident resulted in injury requiring emergency room treatment, but no death occurred. The likelihood is unlikely as such specific helmet failures are not common.

incident_description:
Bike purchased from Target 06/19/2012.  Only ridden on paved surfaces for no more than ten minutes at a time no more than twice a day. Rider is well under the 275 lb. weight limit. 

At time of purchase, both available bikes of this make and model had misaligned or free spinning handlebars. Problem addressed before leaving store, but after riding bike a few times to stores, rider found handlebars misaligned again when removing bike from bike racks, thus, forced to ride home with handlebars at 45 degree angle away from normal position. Happened twice. 
Seat rides down slowly during use.
Pedal fell off in parking lot while bike was in use. This model of bike is single speed and brakes by backpedaling. It is difficult to brake while in motion, surprised, and missing a pedal. Rider recovered pedal only to find it could not be reinserted as the threads had been stripped and was forced to walk the bike home. 
     
Contacted Magna/Dynacraft. Customer service representatives would not issue refund. They did not seem concerned by the incidents and then continued to obtain address for replacement parts. When asked about installation instructions for the replacement parts, they referred rider to the user's manual. While manual is lovely for regular maintenance, it does not address how to insert a one piece crank through a bike frame. Rider attempted to return bike to store, as it was within return window (though not in required "like new" condition), due to safety concerns and being out of their depth with repairs, and Target refused to issue a refund. They stated they could only repair it and store repair person would be available the following day.  Rider is now extremely uncomfortable with idea of riding this product, and would prefer not to risk any further incidents, even on a "repaired" product of Magna/Dynacraft. Given no other option, Rider left unit at the store (Target: Graceland, located off High Street in Columbus, Ohio) to be "repaired" on August 9th, 2012.  One week later, Rider still has not received any information from Target Graceland. Rider also contacted Target's online customer service to voice concerns on same date, but has yet to receive any response.
justification: The incident involved multiple mechanical failures (handlebars misalignment, seat issues, pedal falling off) but no reported injury, indicating a severity level of 2. The repeated nature of the issues suggests a high likelihood (4) of recurrence.

incident_description:
Bought a bike at Walmart and as soon as I get into the parking lot, the chain came off. I brought it back in and the replacement bike I got had brakes that were assembled wrong and were completely ineffective. The walmart store in San Clemente is selling dangerous bikes that can get someone killed.
When I called the store, the only interest shown by the mgr was to file a claim against the company which assembled the bikes so they could get some money back. I told this guy they need to stop selling ALL bikes assembled by that company but was told they were NOT going to stop selling those bikes, even though it is a safety issue and those bikes could get somebody killed.
justification: The incident describes defective bikes that could cause harm, but no actual injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
I've bought this bicycle from Amazon.com:

Schwinn Discover Men's Hybrid Bike (700C Wheels)

When I tried to ride it for the first time, a pedal fell off. This is dangerous if you lose your pedal while in traffic. Later, the seat came off from the seat pole. Reviews on Amazon.com mention two more cases of pedals falling off:

http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B0030U8SU6/ref=oh_details_o00_s00_i00

This model is subject of recall here:

http://www.cpsc.gov/cpscpub/prerel/prhtml12/12272.html

Although this one doesn't seem to be recalled (no yellow sticker mentioned in recall information), it seems to have the same problem.
justification: The incident describes a pedal and seat falling off, which is dangerous but no injury was reported. The occurrence likelihood is high due to multiple reports and a recall for similar issues.

incident_description: Epic T60 Treadmill:  Lower treadmill portion folds up when not in use.  It is held in place by one manually retractable peg.  There is no hydraulic or spring mechanism to slow descent of lower treadmill portion when lowering it for use.  (My other treadmill has such a safety mechanism)  My six year old child pulled peg while 3 year old stood in the path of the treadmill descent.  Luckily I stopped my 6 year old just in time or my 3 year old easily could have been killed.  It can also accidentally fall on the user's foot, causing broken bones.   Very obviously dangerous
justification: The incident description indicates a potential for severe injury or death (broken bones or fatality), but no actual injury occurred in this instance.

incident_description: Our 2.5 year old son climbed the side of our intex metal frame pool- without the use of anything but the pool itself- On these intex pools there is a band that runs about a foot off of the ground and our child used that as a step and climbed over the top of the pool and almost drowned- he was out of our sight for no more than 5 minutes max and there were other children outside- no one ever though our child could have climbed over our 4 ft pool. We kept the ladder about 50 feet away from the pool to ensure that he would not be able to climb in, however the design of this pool is not child friendly and the thought of these pools remaining in other families homes and posing such an immediate danger I felt that it was the only thing I could do but report it to anyone and everyone to try to get this problem known to parents and other consumers who have the same products.
justification: The child almost drowned, indicating a severe incident with potential for injury or death, though no actual injury was reported.

incident_description: We purchased Under Armour Brawler Football cleats for our son. During the first football game of the season while in the middle of a play the entire sole of the shoe came flying off.
justification: The sole of the shoe came off during a game, which is an incident but no injury was reported.

incident_description: my son and his cousin were jumping and fell against the side and the netting ripped and they fell out and hit the ground
justification: The description states that the children fell out and hit the ground, implying potential injury.

incident_description:
I installed the Bell Universal Fit bicycle pedal on my Schwinn Ranger bicycle approximately one month ago.  The left pedal appeared to be fully and properly seated upon installation and showed no signs of loosening.

While biking across an intersection in a standing position (to increase speed or "sprint"), the left pedal unexpectedly and suddenly became unseated and completely disconnected from the axle, resulting in instability and a fall with moderate injuries.

Upon examination of the left axle, it appears that the threading on the axle had been completely stripped.  It is not possible to see this upon installation and the pedal seemed to be securely fastened, only to become dislodged abruptly and unexpectedly with the application of a moderate level of increased force.
justification: The incident resulted in moderate injuries due to the pedal disconnecting unexpectedly, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as the issue was not visible upon installation and only manifested under moderate force.

incident_description: The handle bars on my child's In-Step Pathfinder Trail-a-Bike snapped off the frame while she was riding behind my husbands bike.  She fell off and was run over by the rear wheel.  She received minor abrasions.
justification: The child suffered minor abrasions from the fall, indicating an injury (severity 3). The incident is unlikely to occur frequently given the specific circumstances.

incident_description:
69 year old caller was riding his bicycle which is purposely chosen as a women's model due to health reasons on August 14th when the down tube broke/severed from frame and dumped him to the asphalt causing him to hit his chest.  His chest was not injured but he received bruising on his left knee, scrapes on his right knee, both elbows scraped and he has a re-occurring pain in his left foot.  He went to the doctor's office to inquire about the re-occurring pain in his left foot and a less severed re-occurring pain in his right foot.  Neither foot was hurting before the accident.  Doctor advised that nothing was showing on xrays as the reason for the pain in either foot.

He has not contacted the manufacturer but he did take the bicycle to the retailer who has possession of the bicycle and who has been in contact with the manufacturer.  Bicycle is recalled and frame is being replaced by retailer/dealer.  Caller would like to comment on wording of release because he believes it to be slightly deceptive in that it does not present the actual hazard of harm to rider.

Consumer Added:  The Boardwalk Bike shop is in receipt of a new bicycle frame from the manufacturer to replace the broken frame. The bike shop must remove all the parts (i.e wheels, chain, seat etc) from the old frame and reinstall all these items onto the new frame. The manufacturer has instructed the bike shop to return the old broken bike frame to them.
justification: The incident resulted in bruising, scrapes, and re-occurring pain, which qualifies as an injury, but no severe or permanent damage was reported.

incident_description:
I have a 2012 can-am renagade, BRP product. The front part of the frame has cracked on both sides just after 1000 k. BRP has come up with a brace but the crack still remains, it's a part of the frame that holds the whole front end together. I have not heard of any accidents from this as of yet. I have ask for the frame to be replaced but they said no!  Quess there waiting for an accident to happen.  This problem is all over the internet just google can-am cracked frame and there is more info and pics of the problem area.
Thanks
[REDACTED]
justification: The frame crack is a known issue but no accidents or injuries have been reported yet, indicating a high likelihood of occurrence without current severe consequences.

incident_description: I am the original owner of a 2007 Polaris Sportsman 500 which I purchased new in 2007. After riding my atv on August 18 2012 I noticed the exhaust was hot against my leg. The next day I had removed the seat to check and clean the air intake filter. When I removed the seat the support legs for the seat had melted due to excessive heat  from the exhaust pipe running directly under the frame that the seat sits on.Fortunately I was not burned and the atv did not catch on fire. I contacted Polaris Industries and made them aware of the fire and burn risk and the instructed me to return the seat to the dealer to file a warranty claim and have them photograph the seat despite knowing the warranty expired 6 months after purchase.As expected they refused to fix the problem citing the warranty had expired. I was made aware by the dealer  that Polaris has been aware of the the problem and manufactures a heat shield kit and has done so since long before my model year.Note should also be made that my atv has only 84 hours on it in 5 years. I feel the CPSC should consider this I high risk concern due to the possibility of severe burns to riders and or fires. Warning should be posted and owner should be made aware of the risk of structure fire if a Polaris atv is parked in a structure after it has been ridden. My hope is theat the CPSC can require Polaris to recall all involved atv and install the heat shield to protect the consumer.
justification: The incident involved excessive heat causing damage but no injury or fire occurred, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the known issue and manufacturer's awareness of the problem.

incident_description: We purchased a Jumpking 14' trampoline  on 8/24/12.  On 8/27, my child was jumping on it and one of the bars that is welded to the side to hold up the netting, broke apart where welded.  The bar fell forward and caught & rested on the net.  Thankfully no injury occurred.  It was my 6 year old on it who weighs about 45 lbs. so this wasn't a bunch of kids using it inappropriately. incident_description:
I own a Pride Mobility Scooter that I use as transportation around where I live as my legs and back do not allow me to walk very far. I was riding up a hill when the scooter slowed and began rolling backwards down the hill. None of the controls, forward or backwards, operated. The scooter is designed to use the motor as the breaking action to stop. By the time I figured the scooter had a failure, I was going pretty fast backwards down a hill which was a block long. I had to stop the scooter somehow before the speed was even more dangerous so I purposely turned the scooter over causing some great discomfort to me. There is no mechanical backup for breaking action on these scooters and I strongly suspect that none of the handicap, four wheel scooters do either. They all use the motor as a generator to stop the device. However, if there is any disconnect between the motor and the battery, THERE IS NO BREAKING. In my case, the connect between the battery and the motor controller failed and that negated any breaking action. I am a retired electrical engineer so I was able to diagnose the problem and fix it. A neighbor lady has a scooter just like mine as has advanced MS and if this had happened to her, she would have been in grave danger. MY operating manual does not mention any thing about this problem. Even on level ground, having no stoping action is dangerous. How many other scooters have this problem? Shouldn't there be warnings about this?? 

I think all such devices should be checked for failures that negate breaking and either provide mechanical breaking or warnings about operating on inclines. How would a paraplegic stop such a scooter??
justification: The incident resulted in great discomfort to the user, indicating an injury, and highlights a significant risk of grave danger to others with similar scooters.

incident_description:
Below is the letter I sent to the President of the company, NiteIze, that made the products in question. It describes the incident and my concerns with their product in the GREEN color.
------------

July 30, 2012

[REDACTED]

CC: Consumer Product Safety Commission, Consumers Union, Amazon


Dear [REDACTED],

IÃÂve come to the conclusion that your Nite Ize Spokelit Bicycle Light, Green Color, is inherently unsafe, should be discontinued, and recalled. Allow me to explain how I came to that conclusion. Please give serious consideration to the appropriate action for you and your company.

I ride my bike a LOT. I often put more miles on it than on my car. It is the primary way I get to work, and other places I go, except during winter.

A year or two back my wife purchased a pair of the SpokeLit bike lights (color red/multi) at the local Wal-Mart. I tried them out and I thought they worked great. My family and I own several bikes, so I went online to order more. I noticed the different colors offered and researched that online. Lots of people mentioned that the green ones seem the brightest, so I ordered two of the green lights in May 2011, then another 6 in July 2011 ÃÂ all from Amazon. (See attached photo.)

This evening I was riding home from work after dark. I was in the bike lane of Camino Del Norte in San Diego, heading EAST, crossing under the I-15 overpass. The traffic light was green, and cars were going parallel to me in the roadway. The cars were going the same direction I was, crossing the intersection in front of the freeway off ramp which I was approaching and was to my right.

As I started to cross in front of the off ramp, the front car in the lane of the off ramp closest to me, started to accelerate just as I crossed in front of him. The car next to him in the other lane also started to move slightly. When this occurred I immediately hit my brakes and skid to a stop. The drivers also quickly stopped. There was no collision, just a near miss. 

This event seemed completely nonsensical to me. I couldnÃÂt imagine why he would start spontaneously accelerating just as I started to cross in front of him. I visually confirmed that he had a red light, and cars continued to cross the intersection just as I was about to do. The driver closest to me gave me an apologetic look. He didnÃÂt seem like a mean, angry, or malicious person. He seemed as confused by this as I did, and he seemed apologetic based on his facial expression and hand motions.

I conveyed this story to my wife after I got home evening and then it hit me, I had a blinking GREEN light on my front wheel! It was about 8:30PM, after dark, and this guy was probably pretty tired (like me), coming home after a long day at work. Out of the corner of his eye he sees GREEN, and goes. He then realizes that the green light is on a bike, NOT the traffic signal, and he stops as soon as he can.

IÃÂm not an expert on consumer safety, but I think making a GREEN bike light to mount on a bike wheel is inherently unsafe since a driver seeing a green light ahead of them will have a tendency to take their foot off the brakes and go, just as occurred this evening.

The advantage of these wheel lights over conventional bicycle headlights and tail lights is that they allow a driver perpendicular to the bicycle to see it! This is typically an issue in intersections when a bike is crossing the intersection. In such a situation, a green light is the WORST thing for them to see since their automatic reaction will be to go. Obviously, a normal driver would not do that once they thought about it, but as you know, in traffic split seconds matter, especially when you are on a bike.

So, my request is:

1.	Please exchange my 8 Green SpokeLit lights for 8 Red ones.
2.	Please discontinue production of all GREEN bike lights.
3.	Please consider a recall of the GREEN bike wheel lights.

Thank you,

[REDACTED]
justification: There was a near-miss incident with no injury, caused by a driver's confusion over the green bike light.

On 7/21/12, the first time he used it he went to bed with the sleeping bag.  About 10 minutes after lights out, I checked to see if he was asleep yet and I didn't see his head, so I turned on the lights to see where he was and he was burrowed head first all the way into the bottom of the sleeping bag, (not with his head out the top of the bag as it should be, but totally upside down in the bag). Then he had apparently had rolled over so he was twisted tightly inside the sack. I had to roll him over to untwist and then unzip the bag to get him out.

The fabric is a tightly woven silky material and is insulated with a layer with fiber fill inside, so it has three layers of fabric (front, inside and back).  It's made to keep the cold air out, so obviously it's not porous and not much air gets through it. Our grandchild is a heavy, heavy sleeper, so apparently he didn't wake up when he got hot & sweaty.   When I saw that he was upside down in the bag I immediately, frantically unzipped and untwisted the bag to get him out, he was soaking wet (sweating), pale and very lethargic.  I believe if he'd been in there longer he would have suffocated. This is very dangerous for a child and poses a serious danger for suffocation. If he had been in there longer I think he would have probably passed out, suffocated and we wouldn't have found him until the next morning. 

This would be equally dangerous for a toddler or smaller child who also might crawl inside while playing.  This sleeping bag, which is geared for children (Disney Cars/Pixar design on fabric) should be recalled from the market immediately.  It is manufactured by Idea Nuova, Inc,. New York 10001  1 866 772 1666 (Made in China) K316943  Disnet/Pixar Bar Code INI:04111259114

My daughter complained that the goggles were burning her and refused to put them on.

I put them on and notice that within 30 seconds my skin felt like it was burned with acid.  The burning sensation continued for an hour after I removed the goggles.  My son tried and noticed the burning within 5 seconds.
justification: The description reports a burning sensation that persists after removal, indicating injury (severity 3). Multiple individuals experienced the issue quickly, suggesting it is likely to occur (likelihood 4).

incident_description: Noticed cracks in the wheel at 8 spoke holes (all at spokes emanating from the gear side) of the rear wheel of my bicycle.  Bicycle is a [REDACTED] purchased in 1998 and ridden about 12,500 miles.  No accident/injury was caused.  The wheel is a Mavic T 221(622X17 - 6106) made of aluminum.  I was concerned that a catastrophic failure could occur and have replaced the wheel.  This bicycle has been ridden almost exclusively on paved trails and roads.   I weigh 220#.  The wheel has not been involved in any accidents.  I've taken excellent care of this bicycle and would not have expected such a failure in such a critical part.   I have brought this to the attention of a Mavic representative via the warranty department at Outdoor Gear Canada ([REDACTED]).  The Mavic representative told them that "because this is an old wheel, Mavic doesn't classify this as a manufacturing defect...the aluminium wheel on tension will loose his (sic) property after many year of riding.  This is why Mavic has a 2-year warranty on all wheel manufacturing defect."   It is my contention that this is more likely a design defect, rather than a manufacturing defect.  I believe it could represent a significant safety issue since the cracks require close inspection to identify.  I was never provided any paperwork from Mavic on this wheel that would convey either their warranty terms or any cautionary instructions regarding the need for frequent inspection or the expected service life of the wheel.  When [REDACTED] identifies cracks in aluminum structures on their airplanes, they institute rigorous inspection procedures for the airlines.  I would expect that if Mavic is designing for a 2-year service life, they should clearly warn the consumer of this and/or institute inspection procedures  that the consumer could conduct.
justification: No injury occurred, but cracks in the wheel could lead to potential failure. The likelihood is possible given the wheel's age and mileage.

incident_description: I purchased an electric motor for my pool pump.  When connecting power to the motor, the spacings between the motor casing and the electrical terminal block were so tight that the insulation on the power supply wires was damaged.  This resulted in a direct electrical short after a period of approximately 1 year.  The short was not immediate because it took some time for the vibration of the motor to eventually cause the insulation jacket to wear thin enough to short out against the motor housing.
justification: The incident resulted in an electrical short but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: My Daughter 5 years old at the time was jumping on the trampoline with her brother. She went to get off the Tramploline, the net broke and she fell landing by stratling the metal bar and causeing her to rip her privates. I imediatly rushed her to the ER. She had to have surgery to repair the injury. She had 6 stitches and a night stay in the hospital.

incident_description: We puchased a Bouncepro tramoline with an enclosure in the spring of 2011. incident_description:
I recently purchased a Can Am (made by BRP) 2012, Ountlander 1000XT four wheeler.  The cost of the machine was around $13,000 US dollars.
Right after the purchase, I discovered over on one of the social network sites there was a post in regards to micro-cracks taking place on the new first year "Gen2" frames.  At first, BRP completely denied this, referring only to the internet as being a great place for people to start rumors.
Later on, they did admit to a handful of cracked frames and professes that the owners had abused them.  When I took my machine in for its' 10 hour maintenance check, I asked my dealer to check it for the cracked frame.  They knew nothing about the claim.   I showed them the site I had been visiting, which includes numerous detailed pictures of the issue.  They later stated they had spoken to BRP and checked my frame.  They stated that I currently did not have the cracks.
Now - it seems that BRP has come out with a brace, that is applied to the frame for extra stability.  It also seems that the rapidly approaching 2013 models, same frame, will have these braces installed at the factory as a standard part of the frame.
What about us folks that have the 2012 frames - with potential cracking issues.  It seems that they can crack at any moment, under any circumstances ???
Please see this for complete details http://www.can-amforum.com/forums/can-am-2012-models/35563-2012-can-am-outlander-renegade-gen2-frame-cracking-pictures-posted.html
justification: The incident involves a potential safety issue with frame cracks, but no actual injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:
On June 8th, 2012 My husband and I purchased one of those quick set up pools made by Intex Corporation. It was one of those pool kits that had everything included. It was a 15' x 48" pool. We purchased it from Toys R Us. We planned on using the pool to teach our 3 year old daughter how to swim. Our 10 year old son had taken lessons at school and was a very good swimmer. We had discussed with our kids about safety around the pool. At least as best we could with a 3 year old. No one was to be in the pool alone or without an adult, the ladder was to be put away from the pool when not in use, we had alarms on the doors and a fence around our yard. The pool was also to tall for our 3 year old to reach up and climb in. Or so we thought. On June 21st, before we had gotten the pool ready to swim in, my husband found our 3 year old daughter face down in the pool. She had just been with my mother and I in the house not more that 10 minutes before and either slipped out the door with out me hearing the alarm or someone had left a door open. Luckily my husband was outside and found her in the pool soon after she had somehow fell in. After giving her CPR and getting a lot of the water out of her he got her breathing again. We called 911 and went to the ER and spent the night in the hospital. We were lucky. Two days after coming home from the hospital the pool came down. However, just before taking it down our daughter showed us how she got into the pool. Even though the pool was taller than her she found a way. There is a strap about a quarter of the way up the side of the pool to hold the bars against the side of the pool. She grabbed a bar and stepped up on that strap then grabbed the top of the pool. She then walked up the side of the liner with her bare feet and pulled herself into the pool. I don't think she intended to go all the way in but she fell in when she leaned over the top bar. We were amazed at the strength she had to pull herself up the side of that pool.

Here are my concerns with these pools: These pools pop up all over and I have noticed that a lot of them are in unfenced yards. I've even noticed a few in front yards. We had our yard fenced in but didn't even think about fencing in the actual pool because we didn't think our daughter could climb into it. Plus, we were looking into an inexpensive way to have a pool in our yard (probably like most people that buy these pools). If I would have been told to put a fence around the actual pool I wouldn't have purchased it. You can buy these pools anywhere. We bought ours at Toys R Us but I have seen them at hardware stores, grocery stores, pharmacies and convenience stores. You won't get any information until you get the pool home and open the box at which point you now cannot return the pool. I think most people are looking for an inexpensive way to get a swimming pool, not a little wading pool, that even an adult can use to cool off in the summer. I've been told that if you spend a lot of money on one of those large metal pools or an inground pool someone from the company that installs the pool will personally tell you what kind of safety measures you need for these pools. These small quick set up pools are stop and shop pools. The most you'll get is someone to carry it out to the car for you.

After my daughter almost drowned in the pool I went online and found that there are a lot of kids that are drowning in these types of pools. I have 4 older kids than my 3 year old daughter and this is the worst accident I have ever had with any of my children. I don't understand why there is no regulations on these pools. I guess I should have educated myself about these pools but I didn't feel they were that dangerous. I just figured it was the next step up from the kiddie pools and blow up pools we have owned. They just didn't seem as dangerous as the bigger metal pools or inground pools. If states required certain safety requirements like fences around the pool even if it is in your fenced in yard, alarms on doors and requiring any store that sold any pool deeper than a kiddie pool to provide safety and return information directly to the customer when they purchase the pool I think there would be a lot less of these pools sold and childrens lives would be saved. Right now I think people think these pools are a cheap alternative to the $10,000 and up larger pools.
justification: The incident involved a near-drowning of a 3-year-old child, requiring CPR and hospitalization, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is high (4) due to the described ease of access and lack of safety measures for such pools.

incident_description: My 17 month old son sustained 2nd degree burns to his calf and fingertip from a neighborhood playground plastic slide. He was wearing shorts, tshirt, and sandals. The incident occurred on July 16, 2012 at about 1:30pm. He was under adult supervision at the time. When he touched the bottom of the slide, his skin instantly blistered. The adult present touched the slide with her hand before my son went down it and she did not feel that it was too hot for him to use. There were no warnings or signs posted on the playground that the equipment can get so hot as to cause burns. The neighborhood is Cinco Ranch in Katy,TX. Playground equipment should be made of heat resistant material or at least something that doesn't heat to the point of causing burns.
justification: The child sustained 2nd degree burns, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is high (4) as playground slides can frequently become hot enough to cause burns in summer.

incident_description:
I would just like to warn others who plan to purchase this Sunny Trampline, about the danger of the legs disengageing from the trampoline base.

Safety concern for:  "Sunny Health & Fitness 40" Foldable Trampoline with Bar".  Purchased Nov 10, 2011 from Amazon.com, for $65.99, plus shipping & handling. The trampoline just "sits" on two of the legs, without being screwed on.  This makes the trampoline very wobbly, and unsafe.  The same goes for the "bar" to attach to the legs. It was just too costly to return it from where it came from.

We were not aware of the recall until today.  and were told that there is nothing that can be done.  We noticed second failure beginning.  Not sure how customers were alerted of the recall.  No one was hurt, we just noticed the failure

incident_description: I recently had a bike accident where I went over the handlebars and took the brunt of the fall on my head and right side of my face and shoulder. I bike on a regular basis and always wear a helmet. I was knocked out for a good five minutes and incoherent for hours after the accident. Among my other injuries, I suffered a concussion and my face and neck were badly bruised and lacerated. In retrospect, I feel that the helmet offered minimal protection. Typical helmets only cover the top part of the head, while in most bike falls the victim lands on his side or face. I am concerned that most bike helmets do not offer protection to the sides of the head and face and would like to see a discussion ensue about this. I can cite a number of incidents where people have experienced the same, with traumatic head injury while wearing a bike helmet.
justification: The incident resulted in a concussion, bruises, and lacerations, indicating an injury (severity 3). The description suggests such injuries are not uncommon among cyclists, hence a likelihood of 4.
