incident_description: Received a Next bike (model Surge) for Christmas 2011. One of the bars that the pedal attaches to has the threads going the wrong way so the pedal screws on wrong so that when my son pedals it eventually comes unscrewed, falls off, and causes him to fall. There was no nut included with the bike and the bolt on the actual pedal is barely long enough to go through the hole that even if we bought a nut, we couldn't attach it to the pedal. The last time this happened, he was cut by the pedal bar.
justification: The incident resulted in a cut, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The pedal repeatedly falls off during use, making recurrence likely (likelihood 4).

incident_description:
I was about 15 minutes into a 30 minute program on my elliptical exercise machine when the bar for the right foot pedal slipped off the flywheel crank and threw me off the machine, with no warning.

My opinion is that this could have caused injury since the machine went from 65 revolutions per minute to zero almost instantly, with the right pedal falling away from the machine.  I ended up completely clear of the machine and everything else in the room and no injury occurred.  The bar that hit the floor was heavy and made a loud noise, but did not cause any damage to the carpeted floor.

The bar under the foot pedal is held in place during normal action by a c-shaped piece of metal on the end of the bar and a metal latch that keeps it from lifting off the shaft of the crank.  It is also constrained laterally by a plastic sheath that covers the shaft, with a plastic flange on either side.  In this case the plastic flange on the outboard side of the sheath sheared off completely from the sheath and the c-shaped bar and latch slid off the shaft to the outside.
justification: The incident caused a sudden stop and disengagement of the pedal but resulted in no injury or damage, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as it requires specific component failure.

incident_description:
(2009)  The steering wheel was extremely loose from the time that the consumer purchased it.  It became worse overtime.  The consumer said that his daughters refuse to drive it because of the potential problem with the vehicle.

The consumer has had intermittent electrical problems, which may have been related to the accelerator recall.  On more than 3 occasions, the utility vehicle would quit working.  The consumer had to use a tractor to pull it back to his home and recharge the battery.  In several instances, the vehicle stopped working, while the consumer was driving it.  He had to turn it off and turn it back on to restart it.  However, there were some instances, where the vehicle would not restart and the consumer had to tow it back home.

The consumer was never notified about any of the recalls (CAP's #10-015, 11-079, 12-022).  

(2012)  The rear driver side axle snapped while the consumer was driving the vehicle.  The consumer was driving at top speed on a straightaway road at the time.  He said that rear tire detached from the vehicle and passed him, while he was driving it.  The consumer was able to stop the vehicle and there were no injuries.

(approx. 4/2012)  The consumer took the vehicle back to the dealer to have the axle repaired.  The dealer repaired it at a cost of nearly $1000.00.  At that same time, the consumer asked them to check his steering column, because the problems that he has had with it.  The dealer told him that there was a recall on the vehicle for the steering problem (CAP# 12-022), but their technician said that the consumer's vehicle fell outside of the recall dates by 2 months.  The dealer's tech. told the consumer that even if it was included in the recall, they did not have the parts to repair it at that time.  The dealer could not repair it, because they told him that it would be 2 -3 months before they could get the parts to repair it.  This may have been due to the high number of vehicles that they were repairing or had repaired so far. 


The consumer said that he could be driving the vehicle and when he hits a bump, the lights will go out.  Sometime, it is 1 of them and sometimes it is both of them.  The consumer has had the vehicle repaired twice for this problem, but it re-occurs every year.  At this time, one of the lights are not working on the vehicle.  Sometimes, the consumer would plug the lights back into their socket, behind the wheel and the plug would stay, but other times it would fall back out.  The consumer had had the dealer work on the lights and he indicated that they have even tried some type of glue to hold the plug in place, but over time, it always falls back out.

(6/25/2012)  The consumer called the firm's recall Hotline today (CAP# 12-022), (855) 738-3711, but he was not able to speak with anyone.

The consumer noted that his dealer has been great in terms of servicing his vehicle.  If they repair a part and the problem re-occurs, they have tried to re-address the problem at their own expense.

The consumer believes that the recall may need to be expanded or that a new recall needs to be created to address the variety of problems that he has experienced with his vehicle.

The consumer has never been injured, but he states that there have been some close calls.  However, when it has failed to work properly, he has towed it back home to avoid any injuries.
justification: The incident involved multiple mechanical failures (steering, electrical, axle) but no injuries occurred, though there were close calls. The issues were recurring and likely to happen again.

incident_description:
The consumer and two other passengers were riding down hill in the off road vehicle.  The automatic braking system failed and the vehicle flipped over. (See exhibit A, below.)

The consumer injured both his legs and believed he fractured one of his ribs. MRI shows he fractured his back.  The consumer did not receive emergency treatment at the time of the incident, but visited his doctor at a later time.  His doctor referred him to an orthopedic specialist in Baton Rouge, LA.  (See A)
 
There were 2 other passengers in the vehicle.  One of the two passengers received injuries to his back, but did not get medical treatment for the injury.  (See A)

incident_description:
I replaced the wheels on my road bike with newer fancy wheels, which came with their own quick release skewers. The rear was an exposed cam skewer, whereas the bike originally came with an internal cam skewer. This page is helpful to explain the differences:

http://sheldonbrown.com/skewers.html

The new exposed cam skewer apparently had a much weaker grip, and I had horizontal, rather than modern vertical dropouts. 

While climbing a steep hill, the force of the chain on the rear gears caused the rear axle to come loose from the right side. This caused the wheel to become misaligned in the frame, with the most forward part of the wheel now significantly aligned to the left, enough so that the tire began to rub on the rear left chainstay. 

Upon descending the hill, this slight rubbing which was not noticeable, generated enough friction and heat that the tire failed, and the tube exploded through the failure point. I had an instant flat tire during a high speed descent. 

Luckily, I was going straight at the time, and managed to come to a controlled stop, rather than crashing. 

Exposed cam skewers are too weak, and too easily used with horizontal dropout bikes. They should probably be taken off the market.
justification: The incident caused a flat tire during a high-speed descent but resulted in no injury, as the rider managed to stop safely.

incident_description:
I purchased the Motovox MVS 10 gasoline powered stand-up scooter on April 11, 2012 from Sears. On about May 15, 2012 the metal gas tank bracket failed and broke into causing the gas tank to fall off during operation of the scooter. I called the company and a warranty repair was initiated by a local repair shop approximately 10 miles from my home. The Motovox Company replaced the gas tank and paid the repair shop labor for the service. It took approximately two weeks for the repairs to be completed. 

One week later, (approximately June 1, 2012) after the first gas tank repair, while the scooter was in operation the bracket that is part of the scooter frame broke into causing the gas tank to swing out away from the scooter. The tank is bolted on with two bolts and the frame bracket broke in between the two bolts causing one to remain in place and the other to swing out with the gas tank. I called the company three times to date and left messages each time. I havenÃÂt received a call back from the company in reference to this problem. I feel this is a defect and is a direct result of the excessive vibration caused by the normal operation of the scooter engine (two cycle engine) and the lack of protection of the gas tank.

The first time this occurred the tank fell completely off and was being pulled along the sidewalk before the scooter could be stopped. It was still connected by the gas line to the carburetor. This problem has a great risk of the gasoline spilling from the tank and being ignited by the metal gas tank being dragged across the concrete and sparks from the friction. If the gasoline spills when the tank falls off and ignites the gasoline an explosion and resulting fire has the potential to be disastrous. 

The gasoline level measuring unit has fallen loose into the tank on both gas tanks causing the round plastic lens to just lay on top of the tank loose. This allows gasoline to splash out and spill from the tank. 

With the first instance of the bracket failing and now after the repair the frame mounting bracket failing, I feel this is a defect. I want the scooter repaired but I feel this will continue to be a problem with this design and would rather receive a refund from the manufacture and a return of the product to the manufacture. 

Something must be done to ensure the safety of our youth riders of this scooter. They are standing on a problem that when it fails can/will cause a fire/explosion to be literally at their feet. I'm a career firefighter of 20 years and a fire prevention specialist for a metro Atlanta fire department. I can see a huge problem brewing with this defect.
justification: The incident involves a gas tank falling off during operation, posing a significant fire hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
On April 21, 2012 I purchased a pool from Recreational Factory Warehouse in Anderson SC.  On May 25th 2012 I was injured and suffered other damages and losses as a result of an admitted defect with the Pump Sight Glass.   The sight glass, manufactured from glass, failed and was projected into my face as I moved the lever to the backwash position.  The glassÃÂs failure was [AN] event for which no instructions/warnings are given.

I immediately notified Hayward Industries of the failure on May 25th and on June 15th received the replacement sight glass, which is now made of some sort of composite/plastic material.

Hayward Industries knew, or should have known, that the failure of the sight glass could occur and cause injury.  In my specific installation, the pump (P/N 7-194330-02) is located underneath a deck (see attached photo.  For the record, during construction of the deck the entire pump assembly was protected by a cover) and as such, the operator must to crouch to perform backwash functions.  No Hayward instructions warn against such a practice.  When the sight glass failed it was not only at eye level, it was directly aimed at my eyes. Luckily I was wearing ANSI Z87.1 compliant glasses and averted serious eye injury.  I was however cut on the cheek (see attached photo) for which I am now sporting a scar.

Recreational Factory Warehouse should have ensured/inspected the sight glass for damage upon installation (and may have damaged the sight glass during installation).

Hayward changed the design from glass to plastic (as admitted in their bulletin ISSP0710): this new sight glass made of plastic is a retrofit to all prior models.

Is Hayward disclosing all incidents and properly conducting a 15b analysis? Projectile glass in an eye can severely injure and in some circumstances may lead to death.
justification: The incident resulted in a cut on the cheek and a scar, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the defect was known and led to a design change, but not all installations may be similarly affected.

I have had two close calls from the first unit before I realized the plate had a fracture in it.  I called Nautilus.  Unfortunately, I did not have a receipt and had to pay full price for a replacement unit.  The second time around, I again had a close call as the weight came within inches of my foot.  I will call Nautilus again to report this incident and attempt to get a replacement or a different product.

Again, the defect is in the thinness of the plate holding the biggest weight.  The metal material used is not strong enough to safely contain the large weight.  I have only had the dumbbells less than a year and use them an average of once a week.  I have always been careful not to drop them or handle them roughly.  I am very concerned about this development and hope Nautilus will address this other defect that I believe is truly a defect.

Sincerely,

incident_description:
I purchased this seat from Amazon and as usual, fulfillment was great! Then, I installed the seat and began riding. I do about 8 miles per day on flat to gentle hill bike trails for exercise. The seat was pretty comfortable UNTIL, I hit a SMALL bump in the trail on my suspension MTB in January and the seat blew up. I came down with full force onto the top tube of the bike and and crashed. When I say blew up, I mean there were seat parts all over the place. It felt like someone hit the bottom of my tailbone in an upward direction with a sledge hammer.

What appeared to happen during the catastrophic failure of this poorly and inadequately designed product was the attachment rails that fit into the seat post clamp bent down in front of the clamp when my weight came down on it going over the small bump (less than 2 inches). This bending, in turn, put undue pressure on two plastic attachment posts at the saeat's rear breaking them at the ends of the attaching screw. This detached the poly foam seat itself from it's metal attaching rails. The two posts connecting the rails to the seat are held by VERY SHORT screws going into the posts less than 1/2 of their length. The sheer point was a full inch below the bottom of the poly seat moulding.

Theese 2 posts appear to be molded directly into the seat and are only about a half inch diameter each and are hidden from view. They are essentially plastic cylinders 1 1/2" - 2" long that capture the screw with a wall thickness of only an eight to a quarter inch at most. CLEARLY NOT ENOUGH STRUCTURAL STRENGTH to maintain structural integrity when stressed. As I mentioned, the undersized posts are NOT VISIBLE because they are surrounded by two rubber bumpers presumably designed to absorb shock (clearly not functional). The rails also are not made of material strong enough to function as designed as they bent down so easily at the front. They appear to be cold steel rather than tougher stainless or magnesium allow that would resist bending.

The injury I sustained to my perineum and spine has not yet resolved and I am considering legal remedies for all the discomfort, pain and distress caused by this faulty product. This seat's inadequate design is NOT SAFE and certainly NOT DURABLE. IF YOU VALUE YOUR HEALTH, DO NOT BUY THIS SEAT.
justification: The incident resulted in injury to the perineum and spine, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) due to the product's design flaws and the described failure mechanism.

incident_description:
My family purchased the Wild Waves water park by Banzai pool / Toyquest at WalMart on
nicholasville road in lexington, kentucky.  We set up the
pool according to the directions. The slide is NOT functional
at all.  We tied it down and it still causes the children to fall off no
matter how they approach it. The bottom floats up since it is air filled
and we worry that over time it would tear the bottom of the pool or that a child could become trapped underneath. After removing the slide due to safety concerns.the problem comes at the bottom of the pool in that there are 4 little plastic anchors that have bruised and scraped my child numerous times. I contacted the company regarding this via email and they informed me they passed an inspection prior to releasing the pool. It is my belief this pool is NOT safe with or without the slide and that any injury no matter how small is far too many. The company refused to work with me on returning so I contacted walmart who immediately told me to return the pool to their store for a full refund. I have read many reviews online about children who have been harmed while using this pool and I believe strongly that it should be recalled. Thank you for your time!
justification: The description reports bruises and scrapes from the pool's plastic anchors, indicating an injury (severity 3). The issue is described as recurring and supported by online reviews, suggesting a likely occurrence (4).

incident_description: Banzai wild waves water park inflatable pool has an inflatable ladder/slide that ties to the bottom of the pool in four places.  It does not lie flat when tied as tightly as possible and floats above the floor of the pool.  Me grandson came down the slide and slipped from the side of the slide.  His head became trapped under the slide.  I pulled him free preventing him from drowning.  If he had not been holding his breath when he went down the slide he would have suffered a serious injury.
justification: The incident involved a near-drowning situation that was prevented, indicating potential for serious injury but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
Caller's husband purchased an AK47 Airsoft gun for himself and their ten year old son on May 19th, 2012.
Gun shoots plastic pellets.

On May20th, 2012 caller's husband and 10yr old son had been shooting targets for approximately ten minutes or less when the 10yr old son asked, "What's that smell" and he laid the gun down as he said it.
As he laid the gun down it began smoking and hissing, he ran to his father who decided to leave the gun alone until the hissing and smoking had stopped.

After the gun cooled off the father picked it up, looked inside to view the battery power pack and saw that it had exploded.
Parents state that if child had not laid the gun down the acid from the battery pack would have gotten on his face and possibly disfigured him.

Caller returned the gun to the retailer immediately but wanted to file an Incident Report for the protection of other consumers.

She would like the gun removed from retailers selling inventory until the battery pack explosion issue has been corrected and it is deemed safe to use by manufacturer.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning battery pack that could have caused injury but did not, and the likelihood of such an event is possible given the description.

incident_description: I was riding a Honda 2011 420 AT Rancher when it caught fire. leaves and other debris had accumulated between the skid plate and rear brake disc area and the heat from the disc caught the debris on fire. When I called Honda Corp to report this they told me to take it to a certified Honda dealer for inspection and they would pay for it. The person that directed me [redacted] to do this handed me off to another case manager [redacted]. I dropped the ATV at the Honda dealer in Ann Arbor MI. After several attempts to contact the new case manager i finally got a hold of him and he told me the company had determined there was no defect. I asked  how they had determined this without having any inspection and analysis and he said it was determined based on my previous conversations with the original case manager [redacted]. They refused to pay for the inspection. How in the world does a case manager sitting in an office determine the cause of a vehicle fire without an inspection?
justification: The ATV caught fire due to debris accumulation, but no injury or death was reported. The likelihood is unlikely as such incidents are not common.

incident_description: While riding on leval terrain, fork on Specialized bicycle snapped into, throwing me off the bicycle and over a bridge into a small creek.  Accident resulted in concussion and 158 stitches to face along with bruised knees.  Off work 10 days and accumulated over $9,000 in medical charges.
justification: The incident resulted in significant injuries (concussion, stitches, bruises) and medical expenses, warranting a severity level of 3. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such severe outcomes from a fork snap are not common.

incident_description:
04/16/2012 Kawasaki recalled on release# 07-561 four wheeler caught fire and burned completely.
Model# KFX450R

Caller had been riding ATV for approximately four minutes to travel from his house to his neighbors house to have coffee with him.  He sat and talked with his friend for approximately a half hour.
He was leaving his friends house but after opening the door and walking around the walkway he saw that his ATV was completely engulfed in flames.

He knocked on his neighbors window and asked for assistance, the neighbor ran out grabbed his hose and began extinguishing the fire.

Caller took pictures and contacted the manufacturer 04/16/2012, he left a message but has not received a return call to this date.

He would like his ATV replaced.
Purchase was made after recall date in 2007.

Product manufactured in 2008.
justification: The ATV caught fire but no injuries were reported, indicating an incident without injury.

incident_description: I was walking on my treadmill when it suddenly took off and almost threw me off the device.
justification: The treadmill malfunctioned but no injury occurred, only a near-miss incident.

incident_description: Our three children ages 11 and twins 9 were jumpimg on our Airzone trampoline when in two locations the frame broke.
justification: The frame broke but there is no mention of injury, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
My husband and I bought the float for our 13 month old daughter. We returned it the next day because it wouldn't stay upright while she was in it. If she moved, or you took one of your hands of it, she would tip forward. If she reached for something, it would tip forward. We were terrified she would drown. The way the seat is made is a flat piece of plastic with two leg holes in it. This caused her to sit on the float more than in it. I believe this is why it tips so bad. If someone had turned away to grab something would have very easily drowned. When I returned it today, the lady at the service desk at Wal-mart said that several other people had complained of the same problem when they returned theirs as well. I know it says on the box that it is not a life saving device, however a parent should not have to keep both hand on he float at all times for their child to be safe.

I tried to contact the manufacturer but I have been unable to find any kind of contact information for this manufacturer.
justification: The float's design flaw poses a significant risk of tipping, but no actual injury or death occurred. Multiple complaints indicate the issue is likely to recur.

incident_description: Two ATVs bumped tires and the decedent fell off.
justification: The incident resulted in a death (decedent fell off), and such severe outcomes are relatively uncommon.

incident_description:
This is to report to you an incident involving a Giant Halfway folding bicycle.  While riding this bike in traffic, the left hand crank arm broke. This caused me to fall and crash, putting myself in a perilous situation.

Luckily I avoided serious injury under difficult conditions but did suffer numerous bruises and abrasions.  Were it not for a pause in traffic, no doubt I would not have survived. 

I am concerned for other users of this bicycle and the potential that this could happen to someone else,  with a possible life threatening outcome.

I have attached pictures of the crank arm.
justification: The rider suffered bruises and abrasions from the fall, indicating an injury (severity 3). The concern for potential life-threatening outcomes suggests the likelihood of recurrence is high (likelihood 4).

incident_description: My daughter purchased this swim suit from Kohl's department store. She worn it for the first time yesterday which was Sunday May 27,2012 when she went to Ocean Grove located on the New Jersey Shore. She indicated she started to develop an itch on her chest. She believed it was caused from a birth mark. She was proactive in applying frequent reapplications of sunscreen when the itch started. When leaving for home she noticed a slight blue tint on her skin around the area where the beads rested. Upon her arrival home she told me how the beads of her swim suit melted in the sun. After looking at her chest where she said the beads were I noticed burn marks on her skin where each of the beads rested. I had her take a picture today and we plan to return the suit to Kohl's for a full refund. This is a very dangerous situation for any consumer and I hope it doesn't leave scars on her chest.
justification: The incident resulted in burn marks on the skin, indicating an injury caused by the melted beads of the swimsuit.

incident_description:
WE have had this trampoline for over two years now. The netting is terrible and doesn't do its job. If anyone leans on it the netting rips.  There have been at least 3 incidents with my children and their cousins have fallen through after the net ripped when they had fallen onto the netting. We have tried to sew the netting to repair it, but that doesn't work either.

Incident #1: 2 yr old child was jumping and fell back onto the netting and it ripped and she flipped over the bar and fell to the ground. She hurt her head.

Incident #2 : A 6 and 7 year old were jumping and there was a small hole that ripped open and they fell through it onto the ground together.. One child complained of elbow pain and the other complained of back and head pain.
justification: The description reports multiple injuries to children, including head, elbow, and back pain, indicating a severity level of 3. The repeated incidents with the netting failing suggest a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: Burley 2009 Solo ST wheel came loose from its axel.
justification: The wheel coming loose is an incident but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
My neighbor, an adult man of average height and weight (in other words, BELOW the maximum weight limit of 200 lbs. as indicated on the water slide), went down the water slide on his stomach.  Though as far as I can tell the slide did not deflate in any way, my neighbor hit the cement underneath the bottom of the slide.  He surfaced in severe pain and was later diagnosed with a cardiac contusion...his HEART was bruised!

We learned from Day 1 that the slide was not appropriate for adults, even adults well below the 200 lb. weight limit, and probably not for children such as pre-teens who are on the bigger side.   We found out when my husband, brother-in-law and I each decided to give it a go, only to find that we painfully bumped our behinds on the cement underneath the bottom of the slide. Unfortunately, my neighbor was not aware of the "no adults" rule and was halfway down the slide before I realized he was on it, and I was unable to stop him in time. 

The below date SHOULD be correct--I know it was in the summer of 2009 and most likely on July 4th--but I checked off "estimated" to be safe.
justification: The incident resulted in a cardiac contusion, which is a serious injury, hence severity level 3. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) as multiple adults experienced painful impacts from the slide.

incident_description:
The caller stated that while at the neighborhood playground in Park Scene lane in Cary, NC 27519. 

The caller was a volunteer in charge of the playground and was informed that around 7pm on Monday 4/16/2012 a volunteer was inspecting the playground and saw that the animal spring rider had been fractured and noticed sharp edges poking out. The volunteer in charge had someone go out to the park and had the item removed on 4/17/2012.  There were no injuries associated with the fractured part.

A report was filed with the manufacturer for a similar incident last year and the distributor was contacted but no response from them as of yet.

The inspector had came out and had contacted the manufacturer as well and had no response as well.

The consumer feels that the animal spring is unsafe and that there was no "warning" on the item that suggested a weight restriction or anything of that nature.  She feels that the spring should be redesigned to eliminate the possibility of sudden fracture caused by metal fatigue.  If this is feasible the spring should come with a warning that it must be replaces at intervals set by the manufacturer.  She was also informed that in order to have the part inspected it would cost her approximately $2000 each time.
justification: The incident involved a fractured playground equipment with no reported injuries, fitting severity level 2. The recurrence of similar incidents suggests a possible likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description: my wife and i bought a bonzai falls water slide at wal-mart in 2007, we used it one weekend with the grandkids 4th of july, it was very unstable and never held its air pressure, we were not the hit of the party like we thought we would be, after i bottomed out on my back.  we took it down, folded it up, stuck it up in the loft in the garage and thats where it has been ever since, we just chalked it up to a bad idea investment and cut our losses of about 300.00, we now learn there is a recall of this product, however, our model is the bigger one... " bonzai falls water slide"... the one the recall mentions states .. .".pool slide"... i do not see any difference as ours could also be set up next to a pool and we did have it set up on a hard surface that 4th of july weekend. i believe these products are dangerous, as we had adult supervision that day as children and adults were both using the slide for the short time until we made the decision to take it down.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous product that caused a minor injury (bottoming out on the back) and was unstable, leading to its removal.

incident_description:

incident_description: On May 6, 2012 while utilizing a Sportspower BouncePro 14' trampoline a 7 year old child fell through the netting resulting in multiple fractures.
justification: The child suffered multiple fractures, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is high (4) given the incident details and frequency data provided.

incident_description: 2008 BRP Cam-Am Outlander 400 ATV purchased on 3/1/2010. ATV was new with a 3 year warranty. While riding I heard a rattling noise from under the seat. I took to the dealer & the dealer advised that they could not find anything wrong. While cleaning the ATV in March of this year I noticed that the fuel tan shield is cracking & digging into the fuel tank. This is the part that was rattling. The fuel tank is plastic. The fuel tank shield will eventually put a hole in the fuel tank. This could possibly start a fire. I took back to the dealer. The dealer contacted BRP. BRP refused to take care of problem. The ATV is under warranty until 3/2013. This is not a damage or wear & tear issue. This is a faulty tank shield.
justification: The incident involves a faulty fuel tank shield that could potentially cause a fire, but no actual injury or damage has occurred yet.

incident_description: The lower a-frame mounts on my 2006 Polaris Hawkeye ATV separated from the frame while riding on a dirt road causing the other mounts to break. This created an unsafe riding situation as the right rear suspension collapsed while riding causing a loss of control. This also caused the axle shaft to separate. The lower a- arm twisted when the front mount ripped out of the thin frame rail. This caused the upper a-arm to twist and break the mount where it is attached to the transmission. This is un-repairable and the entire transmission must be replaced to re-mount the upper a-arm. The ATV had to be towed out of the trail system as it was unridable.
justification: The incident caused a loss of control and significant damage to the ATV, but no injury or death was mentioned.

incident_description:

incident_description:

incident_description: I bought a 14ft Super power Bouncepro wit model # TR1463A-FLEX the day after Thanksgiving 2010. The net is the same as the other recalled trampoline but the wire at the top of the trampoline is what the company says was "new and improved."  That is not the issue. I already forwarded picture s of the trampoline before and after pictures and they blew me off saying that was the improved enclosure.  Like I said before its the net not how its hung. Please hold the accountable or their products.

incident_description: My 4 year old son was playing with a new spiderman playhouse. He couldn't get the trapdoor bed to release, so he pushed hard and his finger got stuck in the gap that opened. After I got his finger released, it was indented in two places, purple and now bruised. I inspected this new toy house, and the trap door bed only releases as expected when the garage door is pulled down. If it is up, fingers easily get stuck using kid force.
justification: The child suffered bruising and indentations on his finger, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
The decedent, a 93 year old male, was driving a motorized scooter on a sidewalk and then drove it on the grass, where he hit an object causing the scooter to tip over and then land on top of him.  


Per the medical records from the hospital, this incident resulted in "an acute broken displaced arthroplasty of the right knee with right thigh hematoma, right hemarthrosis superimposed on history of long-term warfarin therapy".  Seven days after the incident, while the decedent was hospitalized, he suffered a "catastrophic neurological event", suspected to be a stroke and he expired the next day.  

However, autopsy revealed the arthroplasty was not broken, only severely worn down.  There was no hemarthrosis.  There was no evidence of a stroke or subdural hematoma.  There was a very large hematoma to the right upper thigh, which was thought to have contributed to significant blood loss resulting in decreased perfusion and death.  The cause of death was ruled: "blunt force leg injury", with the manner being "accidental".
justification: The incident resulted in the decedent's death due to a blunt force leg injury, as confirmed by autopsy.

incident_description:
On March 26, 2012 I ordered a trike from Monica LLC - Omegastores
                                                               P.O. Box 4572
                                                               Wallingford, CT 06492

Their e-mail address is      omegastores.com
their web site is      wwwcozy trikes.com

This trike came partially assembled. The handlebars baskets and front wheel needed to be assembled. This is an electric trike with a brush less motor mounted inside the front wheel. This trike was going to be used by my wife. She has MS and we believed this trike would give her exercise by being able to pedal and engage the motor when necessary. 

When I started to assemble the front wheel to the frame I noticed two spacers about 3/4 inch in diameter which butt up to the wheel bearings and then when attached to the front fork and the wheel nuts are tightened you have a tight fit. However, these spacers were machined on one side square with the body but the other side was obviously cut off with a saw. 

The saw cut end was cut diagonally so there is no way to have a tight fit against wheel bearings and the front fork. No matter how much torque is applied there would always be a misalignment due to the spacers being cut diagonally. Upon closer inspection I also observed that there were no front wheel locking mechanisms to hold the front wheel from coming off if it became loose. This in itself does not meet CPSC requirements. 

To complicate the matter this trike has reverse. It is my contention that when placed in reverse and then back into the forward position the the front wheel will shuck, the wheel could loosen and fall off.  

I notified the manufacturer and have told them I want to return the trike for safety reasons and I would not have anyone ride this product much less my wife who is handicapped. I sent them pictures of the spacers and advised them as well of non compliance to CPSC requirements. They will not accept a return of the trike without charging me freight and a restocking charge. I have told them that the trike cannot be fully assembled in a safe manner and refuse to accept the fact that they have shipped me an unsafe product. I have never fully assembled this trike and will not due to these safety issues. There is not a serial number, upc code, date of manufacture, a place of manufacturing, or any other form of identification on this trike.The manufacturer will not take the product back. Please help with this situation.

Sincerely,

[REDACTED]
justification: The trike has safety issues that could lead to an incident, but no injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description:
I was riding my bicycle to work (a Dahon Speed P8, bought in November 2011); I stood up on the pedals, while still pedaling, in order to speed up a bit. My right pedal was at the top of the downstroke and suddenly snapped off, sending me to the ground. I suffered a concussion (I was wearing a helmet), 5 broken ribs, and a broken collarbone.

I weight about 190lbs, and was carrying about 15lbs on my body (6lbs bag + 7 lbs chain + clothing). I was on a paved road with a slight decline.

Inspection of the right pedal shows that the plastic body broke, setting the metal cage loose. What's left of the body is still securely fastened to the crank arm.

The pedal in question is the Wellgo F147.

I feel that this pedal model should be recalled.
justification: The incident resulted in a concussion, broken ribs, and a broken collarbone, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) given the specific conditions described.

incident_description: My 9 year old and 3 year old daughters were jumping on our trampoline when my 9 year old fell into the net and as she did it ripped about 3 feet wide, she caught herself from falling out but not sure my 3 yr old would've been able to.
justification: The 9-year-old caught herself and no injury occurred, but the torn net poses a risk, especially for the younger child.

incident_description: The consumer said his grandson climbed up the cargo net and as he climbed up to the top,  the wood rung disintegrated.  His 8-year-old grandson fell approximately 7 feet.  He was not injured. He contacted the retailer who did not offer any assistance.  He contacted then the manufacturer who he sent pictures to and explained what happened.  They replied by stating that the ladder may have been built in a damp area.  The consumer says this is not the case.  The manufacturer offered to send him a new unit.  the consumer's issue is not with the swing set itself but the cargo net.
justification: The child fell but was not injured, indicating an incident without injury (severity 2). The likelihood is possible (3) as the failure of the cargo net could happen under similar conditions.

incident_description: We recently had a scary incident with a Banzai Falls Wall Park that was purchased at Toys R Us in August/Sept 2011.  We blew up the waterslide for the first time this summer but it was not as sturdy as last year.  It is under one year old and was stored properly during the offseason.  When one child got on the top of the slide, it started to sway and was not sturdy.  It almost fell over.  This happened multiple times with one child under 60 pounds on the top of the slide.  Later it got so bad that the slide imploded somewhat slowly on itself trapping a child inside.  Nobody was hurt but this could have been very dangerous as it is possible to get smothered under the plastic and water.
justification: The slide became unstable and imploded, trapping a child, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: TRAMPOLINE PURCHASED AT SAMS CLUB HAS NETTING THAT HAS PULLED (COMPLELETLY TORN LOSE) FROM TOP MANUF. SPORTSPOWER LIMITED MODEL # 1563A COMB.
justification: The netting has torn loose, which is an incident but there is no mention of injury.

incident_description:
Bouncepro SportsPower 14ft Trampoline with black mesh safety enclosure. 10 yr old daughter was jumping on trampoline and black safety net  ripped and she fell to the ground injuring her shoulder had to be taken to DR and arm imobilized for a week. This trampoline was purchased on 11/13/10 at Walmart #0105, Corinth, Ms 38834, for $277.00 dollars. I have my receipt.

Net is rotted and can be torn just by pushin against the mesh material.
justification: The incident resulted in a shoulder injury requiring medical attention and immobilization, indicating a severity level of 3. The net is described as rotted and easily torn, suggesting a high likelihood of recurrence.

justification: The child fell through a ripped trampoline net onto rocks, which likely resulted in injury.

incident_description: My husband and I bought our children a 4 wheeler from Budget ATVs in 2010. We ordered the ATA-110 Monster. About six months after we bought the 4 wheeler our son was riding it and the front left tire fell off. The whole inner part of the rim had broke. So we replaced it with a new one. Then about 3 months after that the something happened only to the right side, so once again we replaced that tire and rim. Then about 3 months after the second tire and rim had broke the left side once again broke. By this time I decided to e-mail the company that we ordered the 4 wheeler from and explained to them  what was happening and sent pictures along with it to give them a better understanding of what was going on. I stated that they need to recall these 4 wheelers before a child get really hurt. Luckly our children did not get hurt when the rims broke. I received an e-mail back from the company stating that this has happened to a handful of these 4 wheelers and they do not feel that they should be recalled. However, they did tell me that they would replace the tire and rim that had fallen off. When I said I would take the replacement tire and rim I was told I would need to pay for the shipping of them. I was also told that the reason the rims were braking is because of extreme riding. Well we live in Montana and the 4 wheeler is only rode maybe 5 months out of the year, and it is rode in our back yard and in a filed by our house. So therefore extreme riding is not what my children are doing on this 4 wheeler.
justification: The incident involved repeated mechanical failures (rim breakage) but no injuries occurred, fitting severity level 2. The issue has happened multiple times, indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description: This is a KidActive brand mini-trampoline. My daughter was simply stepping off of the trampoline in the living room on the carpet. She tripped on the padding of the trampoline which is only a few inches off the ground and broke both main bones in her forearm completely in half when breaking her fall with her arms. The problem with this trampoline is the padding around the base which was installed properly, is loose around the trampoline and causes tripping very easily. My daughter was not using the trampoline incorrectly, This trampoline can cause these kinds of falls and serious injury. This happened on Christmas eve 2011, she had to spend Christmas eve in the hospital and have surgery on her arm the next morning, Christmas day! She then had to wear a full arm non-waterproof cast for 8 weeks followed by a shorter cast for 3 more weeks. Because her bones broke completely in half, her bones are still quite crooked and she will have to go to the doctor for an entire year. The hope is that the bones will grow and eventually straighten themselves out. What kind of liability does the trampoline co m have? This trampoline padding is not safe!
justification: The incident resulted in a severe injury (broken forearm requiring surgery and long-term care), indicating a severity level of 3. The description suggests the padding issue is a recurring hazard, making occurrence likely.

incident_description:
The consumer says his children bought him a high performance bike at Dick Sporting goods.  In September of 2011 he was moving at a high rate of speed down a hill.  He felt something go wrong with the handle bar.  The handle broke, he fell near a bush and injured his groin.  The consumer says it developed into a hernia.  The consumer contacted an attorney who told him there was no severe injury so they would not pursue it.  The consumer called the retailer who said since he did not have an extended warranty there was nothing they can do.  The consumer says the bike has never received any repairs and hasn't been in any other accident. He was traveling at 30 miles per hour at the time of the incident.  The consumer fell on a dirt grass service.  The retailer has referred him to another company who says they have nothing to do with that bike.   
Consumer Added:  I have attempted to contact manufacterer.  South Bay is a jobber and provided no help.  Bad phone number/contact information given to me by Dick's for Realm.  The Realm owner I contacted with information provided by Dick's infor (phone # they provided) says he has told Dick's that they are giving out bad info, but they continue.
justification: The consumer suffered a groin injury that developed into a hernia, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the described circumstances of high-speed biking and handlebar failure.

incident_description: the rear A frame mount on my 2006 polaris hawkeye has failed three different times.  This could cause a wreck if traveling and made a quick turn.  Polaris has refused to fix it and I am afraid to drive it do to the amount of times it has failed.
justification: The A frame mount failure could cause a wreck, indicating potential for an incident without injury if it occurs during a quick turn.

incident_description: 2 Wellness Members reported that the treadmill which they were using (different Treadmills) accelerated radiply without the member advancing the speed
justification: Incident involved treadmill malfunction but no reported injuries.

incident_description: The consumer says the wires in the EMC box are all burned up.  He opened up and saw that the wires were blackened.  The consumer says he noticed it about a month ago when it was not running.  He contacted the manufacturer who told him it is not affected by the recall.  The ATV is the same one as in Release # 05-583.  His Serial number is not on the recall list but he is experiencing the same hazard.
justification: The wires are burned up but there is no report of injury or death, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
I have a 1994 Giant Cadex CFM-3 Mountain Bike that was purchased from Mikes's Bikes in San Rafael, CA.

Recently I discovered the fork crown had cracked because the stanchion tube poked up from the side of the crown while riding.   Upon inspection, I determined the fork crown on one side cracked all the way through on the outside radius where the stanchion goes through.  In the process of attempting to get more information on the fork, I found your release #95-032.  The bolts do go through the crown and the fork has serial number 57 31 93.  The fork is identified as a Marzocchi EGS.  My research indicates these were manufactured specially for Giant.

Since this bike has never been subject to only very mild off road use on rare occasions, and has never run into anything, it should not have failed, unless there was a latent defect.   However, upon closer examination and from a design point, I am not surprised that it failed, since the crack is at the thinnest part of the casting when the most tension is applied
justification: The incident describes a cracked fork crown during riding, but there is no mention of injury or death, so severity is 2. The occurrence likelihood is 2 (unlikely) as the failure appears to be due to a latent defect rather than common use.

incident_description:
Daugther fell from the side of the slide of the following :
Swing-N-Slide Cedar Brook Ready-to-Assemble Wood Playset Kit 

http://www.lowes.com/pd_336073-452-PB+8272_4294728506_4294937087_?productId=3344726&Ns=p_product_quantity_sold|1&pl=1&currentURL=%2Fpl_Wood%2BPlaysets_4294728506_4294937087_%3FNs%3Dp_product_quantity_sold%7C1&facetInfo=

onto the mulch and broke her wrist ( buckle fracture)

incident_description:
On Sept. 3, 2011, While peddeling on a new 20" Mongoose with "outer limits" graphics on the frame, (purchaced and assembled at Wal-Mart)The chain came off causing the riders foot to come down onto the speeding ground, which turned into a human cartwheel that ended up with a broken collar bone and several other minor injurys. The Bicycle was inspected and belived that the reflector in the rear wheel came loose and caused the chain to de-rail.
On May 2, 2012 Almost the exact same accident happened (fortunantly, no broken bones this time)with a different rider with no apperent cause as to how the chain came off of the sprokets. When chain is put back on- the chain is tight with very little free-play.
justification: The incident resulted in a broken collar bone and minor injuries, indicating a severity level of 3. The recurrence of a similar incident suggests a likelihood of 4 (likely).

incident_description:
The consumer purchased a porch swing chain set and he installed it by hanging it to the ceiling on his porch. The consumer stated that the package advertised that it holds 500 pounds (226kg safe work load). After the consumer installed the swing, the consumer's friend (225 pounds) sat to try the swing and the left chain loosened and broke. 

The consumer examined the chain and noticed that the loops of the chains are not completely bind together. The loops have space and thatÃÂs how the chain became unattached and broke.  The consumer had the swing approximately 2 foot of the ground while he was trying to adjust it.

The consumerÃÂs friend fell down, but did not become injured. 

The consumer is going to the retailer to request a refund for the product. He also plans to contact the manufacture. 

The consumer feels that this is a safety hazard that should be investigated.
justification: The chain broke causing a fall, but no injury occurred, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the product defect and potential for similar incidents.

incident_description: I have an Adventure wooden swing set that is not in the recall but the wood is breaking and rotting on this one as well, it is the Meridian set.  I was questioning the safety of it this spring while my daughter played on it.  The swings seem to be a little loose up top as well.  I can send pictures of the damage to this play set I bought and assembled in the summer of 2009.  The monkey bars area is especially bad where it is cracking and coming apart.  No injuries have occurred yet.
justification: The swing set is showing signs of significant wear and potential failure, but no injuries have occurred yet.

incident_description:
Caller purchased a DR70 dirt bike October 14, 2011 as well as helmet, gloves and other riding safety equipment. Sales reps name is [REDACTED].  Seven months after it was recalled.
Bike is recalled March 9, 2011 with release # 11-159 and then reannounced April 12, 2012 with release# 12-150.
The family had problems from the very beginning of purchase.
Within the first three days the bike was smoking, the brakes were not working properly which caused a tire to  burst.
October 17th, caller took bike to Quick Pawn & Loan, where an acquaintance [WES] advised her that the bike was not put together at any level.
 October 19th, 2011 caller took back to retailer to have repaired.  Retailer representative advised caller that bikes are not assembled in the store, they come already assembled and only gas needs to changed from dry gas.
[redacted] took bike in only because caller was frustrated and was leaving bike in parking lot, he put the bike in the back room.
She was given a replacement bike that had all of the same problems.
This bike appeared to be older that the first bike but she was getting a very large discount so she took it.
Bike is the same model, same vin of L98 and same issues.
It is recalled and had been recalled before caller ever purchased it.                                                  
Caller during this time was able to speak with someone at Baja who told her to take it to a repair shop they were instructing her to take it to.
She picked bike back up November 9th, 2011 and she took the  bike to Derita Small Engine Repair where [REDACTED] repaired the bike according to the problems they had been having since purchase.
She picked bike up from [REDACTED] 
She began allowing her son to ride the bike but it was still having multiple problems so she took it and parked it in the backyard.     
While we were talking the caller's son brought in two pairs of pants that had been burned but that he had hidden thinking he would be able to ride the bike if she didn't know about them.
Today, April 17th she received a letter advising her that the bike was recalled March 9, 2011 which was 7 months before her purchase of the bike.
She is livid, her son was able to ride the bike 3 days out of the 90 days, it was on recall the entire time, she feels very betrayed and she would like this bike replaced with a safe, non recalled bike at manufacturer expense.
justification: The bike had multiple safety issues and was recalled, but no injury was reported, only property damage and frustration.

incident_description: Infant was riding bicycle, bicycle fell to the ground on improperly installed plastic brake handles breaking the plastic handle and exposing sharp brake wire, which severely lacerated infant's upper thigh through her jeans.
justification: The infant suffered a severe laceration, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The incident involved a mechanical failure (improperly installed brake handles), which is possible but not highly frequent (likelihood 3).

incident_description:
Caller's husband purchased "Pool Shark" basketball with container base sometime between the end of 2007 and the end of 2008.

The base that holds water for weight is cracking which caller sees as a safety hazard thinking that the adjustable up to 44" pole may fall if cracking continues and possibly harm her 9yr old daughter and 10yr old son or one of their friends.

A neighbor informed her that their basketball assembly that is very similar to hers with the exception of color and manufacturer has lasted ten years and is still in fairly good shape.

She would request for the basketball assembly to be replaced at manufacturer expense stating that the base began cracking in 2009 but that she had not reported due to the unexpected necessity of nursing her husband during an extreme illness and losing him in 2011.
justification: The base is cracking, posing a potential safety hazard, but no actual incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: Myself and a friend were shooting a Crosman M4-177 pellet gun when my friend was pumping the rifle and the butt snapped from the stock hitting him in the eye and slicing his hand almost causing him to shoot himself in the eye.
justification: The incident resulted in injury to the eye and hand, but no death occurred.

incident_description:
Rainbow Systems Play set - While my 9 year old daughter was playing on her play set the plastic rigs which are part of the "10J Trapeze/Rings combo" accessory broke off.  My daughter fell down and was not seriously injured, but did get a bruise on her leg from the fall.   http://www.rainbowplay.com/index.php/swingsets/options/C140/#
Rainbow systems asked me to send them a picture of the broken part, which I did, and they have sent me a replacement pair of rings.  The original rings were a molded plastic set, and the new rings are cast aluminum.  This is a pretty significant redesign, most likely due to other rings failing in the same way.  When I looked for a recall on this, I was shocked to not see one.  I'm guessing that mine was not the first problem they had, and wonder how many other sets of defective rings are in consumers hands, only to be noticed after someone gets injured.  Hopefully you can look into this and get these replaced before someone gets killed or paralyzed.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury (bruise) to the child, and the redesign of the rings suggests a known issue with the product.

incident_description:
In January 2012, I purchased a Neptune AR Fluid Rower (First Degree Fitness product) from Creative Playthings in Acton, MA.    They did not have one on display.   I asked the sales representative about the seat and he said I would like it, very comfortable.

CPT delivered and assembled my rower about a week later.    I was uncomfortable on the seat from the beginning.    My insides would burn even after a brief rowing session.   I think it was late February when I had a problem with the rowing part of the unit.   Twice the cord came off the wheel causing the rower to stop and putting me on the floor.   This was when I contacted Creative Playthings and told them about this problem.    I did not mention the seat at this point.   They did agree to take the rower back even though I was beyond the 30-day return policy.   They charged me a 20% restocking fee, but I was happy to have them come for the rower.

I tried it a couple of more times but the seat hurt everything so much, I just didn't try again.    I did tell them about this problem and I also contacted First Degree Fitness.    I didn't hear from either one.

In early March I went for my annual physical and found out I had some blood in my urine (first time ever).   My doctor sent me to a Urogynecologist.    She said I was very irritated.    I showed her a picture of the rower seat and she said it wasn't designed for the female anatomy.   I had a number of tests and everything is fine now, but I have a feeling that this problem, while maybe not a direct result of the rower, certainly it was part of the problem.
justification: The incident resulted in physical injury (blood in urine and irritation) due to the rower's seat design, but no death occurred.

incident_description: While cycling downhill on a very steep section of Hicks Road in Almaden CA, my front tire spontaneously deflated, nearly causing a serious crash.  This caused the rider to become stranded, as it could not be repaired with equipment most riders will carry on this road.  When I replaced the inner tube, the second tube also spontaneously deflated.   I noticed that the plastic tire liner which sits between the wheel rim and the tire deformed, causing the puncture.   Due to brake friction on the steep descent, the wheel rim had heated up, and the tire liner could not withstand the heat.   Most road bikes use a cloth tire liner which is not subject to failing due to brake friction.   The Ridley Orion bike with Aksiom wheels must be recalled, and have the faulty tire liners replaced.
justification: The incident involved a near-crash due to tire deflation, but no injury was reported. The issue is likely to recur given the faulty tire liner design.

incident_description:
The consumer purchased the hammock that his only used 3 times since its purchased date.  The consumer stated that as he was sitting on the hammock, it collapsed.  The hammock was only a foot off the ground, when he fell and hit the ground. The consumer examined the hammock realized he felled because of defective knot contained in the hammock roping, which was hidden by the fabric.

The consumer contacted the manufacture and the representative that spoke to him recognized that they used the incorrect knot for that particular product. They offered to replace the product and the consumer declined. 

The consumer believes this is a serious and dangerous defect, which he suspected permeates the rest of the product line. He stated that while he was not injured, he fully expect that some customers will suffer serious if not life threatening injuries. He believes that this product needs to be fully investigated.
justification: The consumer was not injured, but the hammock collapsed due to a defective knot, indicating an incident without injury.

incident_description: I fell while skating with helmet on, was knocked out and taked to emergency room where I spend 5 days in ICU
justification: The incident resulted in a severe injury requiring ICU hospitalization, indicating a high severity level.

incident_description:
While sitting stationary on the stayball exercise ball it burst. I fell straight down hurting my tailbone, back & ribs. Nothing broken, but hurt.

I have photos but cannot get them to upload.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (hurt tailbone, back, and ribs) but no broken bones, warranting a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is set to 4 (likely) based on the provided frequency data.

incident_description:
I purchased 4 x 6 inch Miflex HP Hoses for my pressure gauges on my Apex diving regulators in a sidemount configuration on 7th March 2010 from Dive Gear Express in the US.

6th of September 2011 
Iwate Maru wreck near Rabaul PNG. 
Two 88 cubic foot scuba tanks in sidemount configuration. 
Time in 0834 time out 0925. Max depth 22m Average 16.2m
Approx. 45 minutes into the dive at 16m near the mid section of the wreck I heard a very loud bang followed by a "bubble bath" of air from my right tank HP hose. I shut down the right tank valve and the supply of air to the regulator in my mouth, swapped over to the left tank regulator and signalled to my Dive Guide [REDACTED] at Kabaira Dive I was terminating the dive. I completed a safety stop and exited the water. This hose had been used on approx. 25 dives.

8th September 2011.
Horseshoe Reef, Atlikklikum Bay PNG.
On entering the water at 0835 the hose on my left tank blew on the surface. Dive aborted and hoses removed from regulators for all future dives. This hose had been used on approx. 38 dives (hose taken off my nitrox dedicated regulator).

I rang Miflex in the UK on return to Australia in September 2011 to try to prevent any injury to other divers using these hoses. I was horrified with their response and lack of concern for the divers relying on these hoses to sustain life. I can quote him off by heart: "Now don't get me wrong but hoses do fail". They told I needed to take it up with Dive Gear Express who sold me the hoses.
The two blown hoses sent to DIve Gear Express and refunded promptly.
justification: The incident involved hose failures during dives, but no injuries or deaths occurred, only equipment malfunction.

incident_description: Purchased new 12-volt cooler at Walmart, cigarette lighter plug on cooler very hot. Started fire under dashboard of vehicle. Now need to replace wiring harness. Could have been worse if I did not have a fire extinguisher.
justification: The incident caused a fire under the dashboard but was controlled with a fire extinguisher, resulting in no injury or death, only property damage.

incident_description: we purchased the snug n secure swing expecting our daughter to be "snug and secure" which ended up in a trip to the emergency room due to the area between her lip and gum being completely split into thank God there were no brain bleeds or brain damages but my poor daughter had to suffer for weeks in pain while it healed because the strap slipped out of the back of the swing!! we purchase everything little tykes brand because of the good quality and safety I pray we never have to deal with something so terrifying over a little tykes item again

incident_description:
Caller purchased six leg swing set March 2010.  

Sometime around September 2010 caller's five year old daughter was swinging on one of the swings when the seat portion of the swing broke sending the child falling to the ground, luckily not causing any more harm than a scratch or bruise.

Caller contacted the manufacturer a couple of weeks later when she learned that there was a recall.
She was told that her model was not recalled and that there was nothing they could do for her.

Tuesday, March 13th, 2012 caller had friends over for a visit when while the friends daughter was swinging the swing broke, causing again no injury.
The child stated that she thought she felt the seat giving so she hung onto the chains very tightly.

Caller again contacted manufacturer March 19th, 2012 and was again informed that her model is not on recall and there is nothing they can do for her.

She is contacting the Consumer Protection Safety Commission asking for assistance in alerting the public and trying to encourage the manufacturer if they have a safer swing seat please replace her's with the safer one at manufacturer expense.
