incident_description: Our 10 year old Creative Playthings deluxe wooden playset unexpectedly broke while children were swinging. Top support beam from which swings are suspended basically disintegrated (apparent interior dry rot) and came crashing down on top of 7 year old girls who were swinging. All CP playsets come with warranties - the minimum being 10 years. But even if this were out of warranty, I would think that what happened was beyond the realm of "normal" wear and tear. The girls literally could've been killed, and were lucky to escape only with bumps and bruises.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries (bumps and bruises) to the children, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) given the specific failure mode (dry rot) and warranty context.

incident_description: The consumer says the bicycle crank pedal unexpectedly came off, causing his son to lose control of the bicycle and he fell.  His son was not injured but the consumer is concerned that the product could seriously injure someone.
justification: The incident caused a fall but no injury, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the consumer's concern about potential serious injury.

incident_description: We purchased the Cameron 4 leg 5 station swing set less than two years ago.  (Manufacturer: SportsPower, Ltd.  Model # MSC27695LDKM) The day before yesterday, my 5 1/2 year old son was swinging on the glide ride portion of the swing. One of the plastic brackets on the top of the glide ride cracked and the bolt at the top broke off. The pole came out of the swing set frame and my son fell off the glide ride on to the ground. He was not injured but possibly could have been. We understand certain things only have limited warranties attached to them, but when one is dealing with children's safety, better parts should be made. A swing set should not fall apart after less than two years when it has been used appropriately. My son has only used the swing set as a swing and nothing else. One of the metal ground anchors also broke a few months ago, which my husband has since replaced. Both plastic swings have broken as well, and luckily our son brought it to our attention before the swings totally broke where he could have been injured.
justification: The incident involved equipment failure leading to a fall, but no injury occurred. The description indicates recurring issues with the swing set, suggesting likelihood of similar incidents is high.

incident_description:
The consumer says he sat on the bicycle and started riding on it.  He says he kicked up a shift while spinning over 30 mph.  He heard an explosion.  there was a terrible pain in his groin and started bleeding immediately.  They called 911.  He got a large hole in the back of his leg.  The consumer had x-rays taken and a 4 inch piece of metal into the back of his leg.  [REDACTED]  The consumer is suing the manufacturer's.  He met with there attorney.  He says metal fragments embedded in the wall.  

[UPDATE]
I have included a summary of the events of my accident which occurred on November 22, 2011. This accident happened while I was spinning on my bicycle which was securely attached to a Computrainer, located at Lucky's Bicycle Works, Inc. in Ft Lauderdale.

I arrived at Lucky's around 11:00 AM that day; the bike looked great as always after [REDACTED] the owner of the shop works on
it. [REDACTED] effectively fixed the head set and put the cleats on my shoes. He pointed out how he used my sole imprints plus my measurements to ensure the cleats were on correctly. I told him I wanted to take a ride, he told me to just go out on
the street since he had ridden my bicycle and it felt great. Since I didnÃÂt bring my helmet I suggested we put it on the
trainer to ensure it fit properly; he agreed.

[REDACTED] attached my bicycle to the trainer, I mounted it and it felt great, I spun slowly then changed my front gear to the 50 chain ring and the back to the 11 sprocket then picked it up to what [REDACTED] guessed to be 35 plus mph. While accelerating there was loud explosion, [REDACTED] thought I was shot, I felt a terrible pain in my groin and blood was spurting everywhere, simultaneously my right foot was decleated off the pedal and my foot thrust upward. Trying not to panic, I carefully lifted my right leg over the seat and dismounted, took a few steps towards the door and fell to the ground. I told [REDACTED] this was it, I thought I was going to die, and to call 911. He called 911 while comforting me, he told me there was a large hole in the back of my right leg and that he could feel my heart beat every time blood spurted out of it. [REDACTED] ripped his shirt sleeve off to use it as a makeshift tourniquet to my leg but the 911 operator told him not to and asked him if he had clean paper towels, he said he did, he got them and applied them to my leg and the blood clotted. I had so much pain in my groin, it was unbearable!

The paramedics arrived in minutes, the 911 operator never got off the phone until they arrived. They asked me if I
wanted to be taken to Broward General or Broward West, I chose Broward General. I was in so much pain before they
drove away from LuckyÃÂs they gave me a morphine drip to minimize the pain. I was then driven to the hospital and
processed, due to the pain in my groin they x -rayed and cat scanned me and immediately decided to operate since I had
something inside me that wasnÃÂt supposed to be there.

The next morning the surgeon entered my room and told me they had to remove 6 inches of my lower intestine, he
then showed me a picture of a piece of metal removed from my groin, quite frankly I had no idea what it was! As we
determined later it was a piece of the flywheel from the Computrainer.

ItÃÂs important to note that the flywheel exploded with such velocity there were pieces imbedded in the wall which was a
few feet behind my bicycle. Since [REDACTED] was crouched behind my right leg when this occurred, it is only through the grace of God that he wasnÃÂt hit, this could have been a total disaster!

Since my attorney is currently in contact with both [REDACTED] and Computrainer over this matter I didnÃÂt want to file a
claim until I received permission from him.

I have included pictures which to help illustrate the potential danger that is out there for others who still have this
product.
justification: The incident resulted in severe injury requiring surgery and removal of part of the intestine, along with significant bleeding and pain, indicating a high severity level.

incident_description: We received a new Log Swing purchased from Big Lots on Saturday (4/14/12). It was properly assembled with all screws, bolts, and nuts tightened before use. The swing was on a flat, stable surface. This morning (4/16/12) we were sitting on it, swinging gently when it broke. One side apparently broke first where there was a knot in the wood, and the other side must've broken immediately after. We crashed to the porch, landing on our back and head. It is supposedly tested to be used at a weight of 440.5 pounds. Combined, we weigh about 330 pounds. We have not yet sought medical treatment, but are both likely injured. The swing was definitely properly assembled and was being used in the proper manner.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (landing on back and head) but no death, and the likelihood is unlikely as the swing was properly assembled and used within weight limits.

incident_description: Intex 13' steel frame pool , the steel frame rotted away after 2 years
justification: The steel frame rotting away is an incident that could lead to potential hazards, but no injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description: My son, age 4, was riding his brother's scooter in the driveway. He turned the steering wheel and fell. He hit his face on the bracket that adjusts the steering column height. The bracket is very sharp. It sliced into his face next to his nose. The gash required sutures or glue. We chose glue. His nose was also fractured. The hospital said we may want to consider plastic surgery later.
justification: The incident resulted in a facial injury requiring medical treatment (glue for the gash) and a fractured nose, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as such injuries can happen with children playing on scooters.

incident_description:
My wife and I were riding an ohv trail near Florence Arizona in our new 2012 Polaris Ranger RZR XP 900, along with friends and members of our ATV club.  We left our campsite at about 10:30 am on or about Friday March 16, 2012 and had been on the trail maybe 4 hours and heading back to camp.  We stopped a number of times for water and lunch break and to view the scenery.  I was leading the group of 6, in an area called box canyon when my wife said she smelled something sweet, which I didn't so we continued on.  Box Canyon is a rocky area and we were traveling about 5-10 mph when suddenly the second in our group raced up to us yelling fire, fire.  I immediately hit the brakes and we both exited and I immediately unstrapped the 2 gallon spare plastic gas can and raced it to a safe place then back to pull out my cargo chest that I also purchased (see pictures of before and after fire). Note that the gas can was on the driver's side and away from the fire.  Then we all worked (all 6 of us) throwing dirt at the fire on the rzr.  The fire was finally extinguished by someone finding some water.  The fire was very close to my wife's head which you will read in the witness report (see witness letter).  Please note; my wife and I also smelled gas fumes on occasions, inside the cab, on the return and other rides.

The fire was directly on the exhaust manifold/heat shield directly above the hole nearest the passenger seat of the cargo box.  It appears as though that the fire was started from extreme engine and exhaust heat, melting the cargo box in this location which dripped plastic onto the exhaust manifold/heat shield (see pictures).  As a flame developed it melted more plastic which made more fire which burned through my cargo chest which burned an ice chest and a tool carrying bag.

What is prompting my report is numerous and is all bout consumer safety. NOTE see letter to cpsc
justification: The incident involved a fire in the vehicle, but no injuries or deaths were reported, and the fire was extinguished by the group.

incident_description: The consumer says his mom was on the treadmill for 30 minutes.  She had it set at 2.8 miles per hour, but went to 12 miles an hour after pressing the cool down button.  They contacted the manufacturer who sent her a power cord as the prong to the old cord broke off when the incident occurred.  The company offered to send someone out to inspect the treadmill.   His mom suffered some minor bruises on her elbow and left knee.  She went to the nurse's office in her retirement development.  They gave her a few bandages and ointment.  The company sent out a technician 14 hours before the incident to change the upper control board to the unit.  This needed replacement due to the original error message stating to "lube belt".
justification: The consumer's mom suffered minor bruises, which constitutes an injury (severity 3). The incident seems unlikely to recur given the specific circumstances and recent technician intervention.

incident_description: We bought the Atlantis Cedar Playset in May 2011.  On 3-22-12, the beam mount that attached the swing to the clubhouse broke.  This caused the clubhouse to fall, leading to further damage to the clubhouse.  There was not a significant storm or any unusual force that should have caused the beam mount to break.  I have contacted the company (Backyard Discovery), and they are insisting the damage was caused my mother nature.  I feel like there is a real safety concern here that the company is not taking seriously.  There was some rain and wind the day that it happened, but no significant storm that should have caused this damage.  I have asked nothing from the company other than for them to investigate this safety concern, and have had no response to the safety issue.  If my kids had been playing on the playset at the time the beam mount broke, they could have been seriously injured.  I feel there is a defect in the quality of this playset, and I don't want anybody to get injured from the same thing happening to them.  I have pictures of the damage if needed.
justification: The beam mount broke causing damage to the playset, but no one was injured as the children were not playing on it at the time.

incident_description: An 11 yr old neighbor boy was injured when slam dunking a ball on a Spalding in ground basketball hoop.  The supporting vertical pole broke in two and the top half fell off , including the rim, backboard, and pole.  The boy was struck in the face by the heavy glass backboard and sustained many injuries including broken teeth and jaw.  We had it professionally installed in hopes of avoiding anything like this.
justification: The boy sustained serious injuries including broken teeth and jaw, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). Such incidents are rare but possible given the professional installation and unexpected failure.

incident_description:
This report was extracted from email sent to the information center.

 Woman, age 25, height 5'4, as passenger with very long braided hair down to her knee. She was not aware of open place next to seat. No warnings/no knowledge of risk. 

 Hair went down behind/to side of seat and got wrapped around drive shaft; result is she was scalped (literally). 
    She was belted, with helmet, etc.   The ATV was not in any way modified from way purchased new spring 2011 and was not being improperly operated.  The ATV was being operated time (unknown) on a mud/dirt surface (not paved).

The victim was taken first by car to Saint JosephÃÂs Hospital in Savannah, Ga and then ambulance to Medical University hospital (Medical College of South Carolina), Charleston SC for further specialized care.

incident_description: The consumer says that the chains started coming off on the bike.  He took the cover off and noticed residue on the chain.  He wiped off the chain and he felt a pinch on his finger.  He says that the bike amputated part of his thumb.  The consumer says that the chains started coming off on two or three bikes after 60 days.  The consumer feels that there should be a label stating of a possible amputation concern.  The consumer has had one surgery on his thumb and now the nail is bending over the side and into his skin.  First surgery date as 2/25/11, 2nd surgery date was 3/13/12.  The caller works for the gym where the incident occured and is now unable to service the bicycles.
justification: The incident resulted in amputation of part of the thumb and required multiple surgeries, indicating a severe injury. The occurrence likelihood is rated as unlikely (2) as it happened in a specific context with certain conditions.

incident_description: The deceased, a 35 year old white female, was driving a Suzuki 450 ATV with her 11 year old daughter on a trail when the ATV stalled. The decedent applied the brakes, causing the ATV to flip. The decedent fell 25 feet backwards, with the ATV possibly rolling on her.

incident_description: We bought a 110cc Tao Tao Atv on Dec.31, 2011. My 5 year old son is the only person that has rode it. Last week the chain came off and mu husband fixed it. Then a few days later my son said his foot brake felt weird, like loose. So I looked from ground level under the machine as he pressed the brake and I saw the frame is broken in 2 places. Had he continued riding he could have seriously been hurt. I called the place we bought it Behind Bars motorsports in Knox Indiana and they told me that Tao Tao would not do anything about it. They said if I brought it in they could maybe weld it back together for me. The item is less than 4 months old and always kept in a heated garage....the frame should not be broken!!!!
justification: The frame broke but no injury occurred, though the potential for serious harm was present if the issue had not been noticed.

incident_description:
I have a Gary Fisher Fast City bike. I purchased it about 6 years ago, it is one of the first 29'ers. The configuration of the bike is for road riding, even though it has front suspension.

I am filing this because the bike does not have adequate ground clearance between the padals and ground.

Shortly after I bought the bike I realized that the pedal on the inside of a turn needed to be in a up position, I own about 15 bikes and have been an avid rider since the early 1970's.

I called Trek when I realized this, and the customer service people recommended that I replace the crank arms with shorter ones if this was a concern, but otherwise they had no advice.

So, since I bought the bike I have always ridden it with this design flaw in mind. My first major lapse in attention was last fall, riding with my wife on a rail trail. I made a turn, a gently turn at a fairly slow speed, and the pedal was down, and basically jacked the bike up and the wheels went left and I fell to the right and bloodied my elbow and knee.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (bloodied elbow and knee), but the occurrence is unlikely as the rider is experienced and aware of the design flaw.

incident_description: Treadmill was set at speed of 3.6 and an incline of 10.  About 5 minutes into my work out the treadmill suddenly sped up .  I pushed the "stop" button and nothing happened. It continued to run at full speed.  I pulled the emergency safety key and still it continued to run.  I fell on the treadmill and received numerous road burns .  The machine only stopped when my husband came into the room and pushed to power button.

incident_description:
On July 6th 2011my son and his friend and me had been out riding for quite a while when I attempted to go up a hill on my LTZ 400. While climbing the hill the quad seemed to run out of power and stall. When this happened the quad flipped over landing on top of me and then preceded to roll the rest of the way down the hill causing significant damage to the quad and myself. My son and his friend came up the hill and helped me down to the bottom of the hill. I had significant contusions to my lower back and legs. After getting home my lower back had begun to swell making it very difficult to walk. At that time we decided that it would be best to go to the emergency room. By the time I got there I had numbness in my legs. I had a Cat scan and multiple ex rays and it was determined that I should stay over night. I was released the next day; however, I am a kidney transplant patient and in October I went into rejection. I have had several doctors tell me since then that there is a very good chance that the trauma of the accident caused the rejection. It was not until recently when I was looking online at ATV Connection that I saw that there was a recall on the LTZ 400 which is why I am now reporting this incident.

Thanks
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in significant injuries requiring emergency care and potential long-term health impacts, but no death occurred.

incident_description:
Consumer wanted to report that her Polaris ATV is a dangerous product. She stated that while she was riding the ATV it smoked from the ECM and resulted in her burning her hand as well as melting to all of the wiring of the ATV. The consumer stated that she was on the ATV for about 10 minutes then parked it to do some work, allowing the product to cool off for 20 minutes; then 3 minutes after she started the ATV again, it started to smoke. The smoke stopped when the consumer turned off the ATV and went to get a fire extinguisher and stated the smoke stopped when she got back to the product. The consumer didn't call the fire department. The consumer suffered a slight burn on her right hand and the extent of her injuries is mostly smoke inhalation. The consumer did not seek medical attention. 

The consumer's husband called the firm at 800-765-2747 on 5/23/2011 and was told they could not assist them since the firm concluded that her product was not under recall. The consumer and her husband consulted a repair dealership. However, the product was bought from a private seller. The product had a few minor modifications as it had a cup holder and winch installed prior to her purchasing the product. The repair dealership had told the consumer and her husband since the firm wonÃÂt offer to do anything to help her and will fix the ATV, they can only fix the ATV at the consumer's expense.

 The dealer concluded that the ATV's ECM cause the fire and was the same issue as cited in release in 08-193.  The consumer stated that there is no charring or discoloration on the product on the outside but there is on the inside of the unit and reported that between the cracks of the culling near the headlight and front fender there is melted plastic. The consumer felt it was imperative to report this issue to the CPSC.
justification: The consumer suffered a slight burn and smoke inhalation, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The incident involved a specific component failure (ECM), suggesting a possible but not certain recurrence (likelihood 3).

incident_description:
The consumer stated that her daughter was injured when she fell from a piece of playground equipment at school. The equipment is Game Time Sky Wheels Upper Body Equipment. The consumer's daughter was playing on the equipment which is designed as four posts placed deep into the wood chip surface. These posts have a horizontal cross beams and an overhead bar which supports three free-spinning metallic wheels set at angles to the overhead bar. By design, the child is intended to grasp from one free-spinning wheel to the other in an overhead traverse. The horizontal bar and wheels are set approximately 8 feet from the ground, with a wood chip surface material below.
On February 7, 2012, the consumer's 10 year old daughter was attempting to complete the overhead course. As she transferred from the first to the second wheel, the second wheel began to spin. The spinning action of the wheels overpowered her grip, pulling her free of the equipment, resulting in a heels-over-head fall. She landed on her left side and hit her head on the mulch surface.
The consumer's daughter fell approximately 8 feet to the mulch surface below and suffered a grade 4 or 5 spleen laceration, collapsed lung, internal bleeding and loss of consciousness/ concussion. The school nurse contacted the paramedics, who transported the child to Carroll Hospital Center, where the child was diagnosed by CT and promptly transported by helicopter to Johns Hopkins Children's Center in Baltimore, MD. The child was in pediatric ICU overnight, and was on strict, medicated bed rest for 48 hours. The child remained in the hospital for 5 nights, 6 days.
The consumer's daughter was prescribed narcotics and was given IV support and oxygen. The consumer stated that her daughter's body temperature exceeded 103 degrees F, and that ice packs and compresses were applied to the child. The child was
required to complete breathing exercises for her lungs several times per hour. The hospital released the child from their care and she has not yet returned to school.
The consumer mentioned that her child will see her primary care doctor on Monday, February 20,2012, and will meet with the trauma team at Johns Hopkins on Monday, February 27, 2012. The consumer attempted to contact the equipment manufacturer today, but has yet to receive a response.
The consumer stated that the school system has conducted an investigation and found that the surface material is appropriate; the product was installed and maintained properly. She was informed of the school's findings as of Monday of this week.
justification: The child suffered severe injuries including a grade 4 or 5 spleen laceration, collapsed lung, and internal bleeding, which are life-threatening conditions, warranting a severity level of 4. The occurrence likelihood is 2 (unlikely) as the investigation found the equipment was properly installed and maintained, suggesting such incidents are not common.

incident_description:
I am frequently swimming for recreation. To avoid fog in my swimming goggles, I bought a product from the swimoutlet - JAWS SPIT ANTIFOG. It has to be applied at the inside of the goggles, then has to be rinsed. I was using the product alreday several times. On February 26th 2012, I applied the product as usual and was swimming for half an hour in the pool. There was a little bit of water running into my swimming goggles and somehow dissolved some of the residuals of the ANTIFOG solution. My eye was burning terribly, even after rinsing the eye for half an hour. I finally went to the emergency eye clinic, since my eye turned red and was hurting a lot. The doctor's diagnosis was a chemical burn of my cornea. I was in pain for two days and had bad vision for about 2 weeks. Fortunately the chemical burn did not leave any permanent damage on my eye. In my opinion, such a product should be taken off the market, when already in the diluted form can cause potentially dangerous chemical burn of the eye. 

Product informtaion:
http://www.swimoutlet.com/product_p/5138.htm
justification: The incident resulted in a chemical burn of the cornea, causing pain and temporary vision impairment, which qualifies as an injury.

The Polaris dealer checked the serial # and told me that my atv was not a part of the carrier recall. A few months later , my son riding in a field at he estimates 15-20 mph. Upon fixing atv I noticed that the original carrier was much thiner the the new one. I took the atv directly back to the dealer, they are contacting polaris. Is there any thing else that I should do?

incident_description: I was riding my ski mobile on March 10th 2012.  It is a Yamaha 2009 FX Nytro with 4910 miles.  I did my pre-trip inspection before heading out for the day including checking all parts of the front end for loose, warn or damaged parts.  I was about 25 miles into my day and noticed my sled was not handling the way it should so I stopped to see what was wrong.   The bolt that holds the top right  a-arm  onto the spindle was missing.  The spindle was flopped to the side hanging in the breeze.  This spindle is the main component that holds the upper and lower a-arms together along with the sway bar and with out that it pretty much makes it impossible to steer.  This is the equivalent of a tie-rod in your car just falling off which should not happen.  Imagine going down the highway and having your tie-rod fall off, the loss of control at almost any speed never mind highway speed could be catastrophic.  Well the same could have happened to me on the trail.  Im just happy i didn't crash and hurt myself or my two friends who were riding behind me, or someone coming the other way on the trail.  Luckily I was traveling at a  low speed when this happened.  The bolt was gone so i don't know if it sheared off or came loose and fell off.  Yamaha does not want to cover this under warranty because they feel Loose bolts are the consumers job to check which i agree but not only did i check that before the ride i believe it may have broke.  There has been other people complaining about the Nytro front ends having bolts come loose on the totally yamaha website and I believe there is a design flaw and Yamaha  does not want to address the situation.  They certainly were not interested in my situation. It is funny they had a recall on a different LOOSE BOLT ON THE SAME A-ARM (Alert #10-719) in 2010 but I guess they changed there safety policy to who cares about the consumers safety.  At the very least they should issue a recall and replace the bolt with one that has a castle nut and cotter pin.
justification: The incident involved a mechanical failure that could have led to loss of control but no injury occurred, and the likelihood is possible given the reported issues with the model.

incident_description:
I was using the Tower 200 - Body by Jake when the equipment came free from the door and stuck me in the mouth. This cause extensive damaged to my teeth and gums. In total, there is  damage to 9 of my teeth... 3 of which will most like need to be removed and replaced. I've spent hours/days in the dentist chair and will need continued work until all the damage can be corrected. This was very dramatic event for me and want to file this incident/safety concern with you.

The events that occurred... that I can remember (due to a high force impact) are:

I was trying to adjust (per instructions) the piece of equipment by raising the two locking mechanisms at the top. It was at this point when the equipment came off the door and stuck me in the mouth. 

The Tower 200 was attached to a regular bedroom door. The top piece was placed over the top of the door and the bottom piece under the door. The door was shut when I was using the Tower 200 and closed when I went to adjust the tension on the equipment. 

My safety concern is that there is nothing permanently  attaching the Tower 200 to the door other than the tension of the bands. It was the tension of the bands that caused the great force of impact into my mouth. I strongly feel that if there was a permanment device securing the Tower 200 to the door this incident would have been avoided. 

I can only assume that the door had came open allowing the Tower 200 top piece to come off the top of the door and sticking me in the mouth. if the Tower 200 had a permanent device securing it to the door, it could not come off the door whether it was opened or closed.

Thank you,
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in significant injury to teeth and gums, requiring extensive dental work, but no death occurred. The likelihood is unlikely as it requires specific conditions for the equipment to fail.

incident_description:
On June 28, 2011, I crashed on my bicycle.  The last thing I remember is looking down at my bike computer (30 miles per hour) AND seeing a seam in the road.  Apparently I hit the seam and lost control of my bike.  A family that lives nearby found me lying on the pavement -- all crumpled up.  The woman was a former EMT, so she put a neck brace on me.  And her husband put their cars on both sides of me so nobody would come along and accidently run over me. 
 
They called the Bedford, PA ambulance.  When the ambulance got there, they called for a helicopter and I was then life-flighted to the Trauma Center at the Altoona Hospital (PA) in critical condition.  The hospital chaplain called my wife with the shocking news.  She immediately got a friend to take her to the Trauma Center, where she spent the next 30 hours with no sleep.  My injuries consisted of a shattered pelvic bone, 4 broken ribs, a broken collar bone, a concussion, a skull fracture, a closed hematoma on the left side of my head, a permanently damaged auditory nerve on the left side of my head, and two blood clots in my leg. 
 
After 5 days, I was transferred to the Health South Rehabilitation Hospital.  Everything healed quickly, except for the shattered pelvic bone.  The pain was extreme and hard to control.  I was there for 3 weeks, and then returned home in a wheelchair.  My brother hired a carpenter to construct a walkway and ramp into our mobile home.  I spent another two weeks in a wheelchair, and then used a walker for a while, then a cane, and now I am walking with no support at all.  ItÃÂs painful, and I limp, but full recovery is not too far away.  

My point, regarding this report, is that the CPSC-approved helmet (Bell Phi) did not adequately protect my head.  It appears to me that the high-density foam on the inside of the helmet is as hard as solid plastic and, consequently, all of the force of the blow was transmitted directly to my head.  The only protection the helmet provided was from abrasions.  A bicycle helmet needs a soft, compressible layer, as well as a hard shell and a hard foam layer.
justification: The incident resulted in multiple severe injuries including a shattered pelvic bone, broken ribs, and a skull fracture, but no death occurred.

When I folded the treadmill I noticed that the latch pin does not engage the frame of the treadmill. It is about an inch too short. The instructions state: "Raise the frame until the hole in the platform cushion is aligned with the latch pin. Then, slowly release the latch knob; make sure that the latch pin is fully inserted into the platform cushion."

Unfortunately, the latch pin is not long enough to fully engage the metal frame and is held primarily by the plastic skirting or trim. After several minutes the plastic was warped out of shape and the latch pin appeared to be on the verge of slipping out. I lowered the treadmill back to the floor and contacted the Sears Warranty division. I was informed that they could not review the problem because it takes 24 hours for the purchase to be registered in their system. I told them the latch system was a design flaw and would fail whether the purchase was registered in their system or not. Sears advised me to contact them at 0800 March 2.

incident_description:
In June 2009, I had an above ground Kayak Pools swimming pool installed in my back yard.  Unit was 12ft X 24ft with an 8ft deck extention.  The unit is advertised as an "aluminum pool" and the 30 year warranty also described it as an aluminum pool. 
On January 15, 2012,  found a corner of the pool deck split open at the top the with the affected wall starting to collapse from the pressure of the pool water on the liner.  The extended deck was also leaning toward the collapsing side.  I braced the leaning side and started to drain the contents of the pool.  I sent an email request for service help to the company that installed the pool.  
Backing up to the sale, we were offered two different types of chlorene systems.  One where the chemical was added directly to the pool or a chlorene generator system where salt is added to the pool and then chlorene is generated as the water is circulated through the system.  We elected the later, but little did we know the the connecting hardware that keeps the pool together was iron.  The corners of the pool structure were connected using a non aluminum L plate with two bolts and nuts on each side.  The bolts were installed in a verticle position with the head on top and the lock washer and nut on the bottom.  The bolts and nuts were made of non-marine usage material.  Over the period of two years the heads of the bolts corroded entirely letting the body of the bolt fall out of the support structure.  There is no question that if a person were at the position of the deck separation at the time it happened, he or she would have been injured.  (I am 80 and my wife is close behind.)
The installing company, SunTex, has blamed the salt water for the failure and offered no assistance.  They said it appears that the proper level of salt was not maintained.   In any event, I was never advised either in writing or verbally that the salt water would be a problem to the structure nor that the main structure hardware was not corrosion resistant.  
My investment in the pool is appx $25,000.  Neither the installing company, SunTex, or the manufacturer, Kayak Pools Corporation have offered to help.
justification: The incident involved structural failure of the pool deck, posing a potential injury risk, but no actual injury occurred.

The result of the pre-release was a fall that tore the labrum in his shoulder, resulting in surgery.  He suspected the bindings were releasing early so he went to a ski shop afterwards to see if his settings were correct and they were.  Fast forward one year after shoulder surgery, he was skiing on a groomed run, his binding released again resulting in a cracked Tibial Plateau.  I took the skis to have the bindings tested at a reputable ski shop. According to the ski shop the DIN and forward pressure were set correctly and the bindings passed a static test.

I called Marker USA and they referred me to K2.  K2 basically said they trusted what the ski shop found and that if I wanted to send the skis back for further testing by their engineers they would take a look at them. K2 showed no concern for the fact that the binding was clearly failing on snow and that the bindings could repeatedly release for no apparent reason, causing injuries.  K2 only cared that the bindings passed a static indoor test. 

I researched Marker bindings on the web and they clearly have a history of pre-releasing.  Marker and their associated ski manufacturing partners need to take responsibility for the pre-release defects resulting in injuries.

The shoulder injury was February 2011. The leg injury was January 2012
justification: The incident resulted in two injuries (torn labrum and cracked tibial plateau) requiring surgery, indicating a severity level of 3.

incident_description:
A friend and I were using a swing set with our two sons. The swing is part of a large commercial installation at [REDACTED] in Washington DC. I come to this park regularly. The swing set is of the standard design: a steel frame about 9 feet high, with two pairs of swings below it. In this particular installation there are two 'bucket' seats for toddlers, and two rigid black plastic seats for older children. His son was using the latter. They are all attached to the frame with the standard heavy duty steel chains. The installation looks like it's new and in good shape (< 5 years old). At this particular playground, there are two sets of swings, and this one was in the NE corner of the park.

I pushed my son for several minutes on the swing, as did he. Suddenly, without warning, his son's chain became disconnected from the frame, and fell to the ground. His son fell directly to the ground at the same time. He was not hurt because of a soft rubber surface the playground has installed (thank you CPSC!). He fell about 2-4 feet.

When I looked at it, it looked like no part had actually broken. However, what happened is that the nut & bolt that hold the chain to the top crossbar simply unscrewed, making the chain drop. My guess is that vibration, etc. from the swing had just eventually loosened this bolt. I think this is a particular poor design: a better design would mount the chain from the top of the crossbar (rather than the bottom), so that in case of a failure, the kid wouldn't be immediately dropped to the ground. 

The nut is actually contained within a black rounded plastic cover, perhaps to be either weatherproof or tamperproof. After the accident, I found it resting (in place) on top of the cross bar.

The bolt is about 3/8" by 5", standard heavy-duty steel bolt, with a rounded machine head. It's installed in a little bracket, which then holds the chain. The bracket, chain, and bolt were all connected when they fell.

It didn't look like there was any obvious break, tampering, etc: all of the hardware looked to have the normal weathering. The rest of the park is in general well maintained.

This swingset is stamped with the manufacturer name 'KOMPAN.'

In the photo, you can see that I hand-tightened the nut (black plastic, semicircle) back onto the bolt. They are all sitting on the ground connected to the chain.
justification: The child fell but was not injured due to the soft rubber surface, indicating a severity level of 2. The incident was caused by a design flaw leading to bolt loosening, suggesting a possible occurrence likelihood.

The consumer contacted the manufacturer who told him they had not heard of that before.   The consumer was on an ATV behind his son and girlfriend at time of the incident.
justification: The incident resulted in two people being pinned under the ATV and bruised badly, indicating injury but no death.

incident_description:
We purchased the Smooth Fitness Model 6.65 Treadmill in April 2011 from a family who had purchased it the previous December 2010.  The treadmill worked fine until early January 2012 when it began to have uncommanded acceleration of the belt resulting in the belt running very fast.  This occured several times and was also accompanied by an acid odor.  The belt would run at maximum speed for approximately 15 seconds and then slow down on its own without any input from me.

I called the Smooth Fitness Customer Service 1-888-800-1167 three times.  The first two times I was put on hold and then transfered to a voice mail for technical support.  I left a message each time detailing the problem.  No one ever returned by call.  The third time I explained the problem to a sales representative who said he would document and pass the problem to the approxpriate section.

I feel uncommanded and uncontrolled acceleration of the belt to a high speed is a dangereous safety condition.  The treadmill will automatically stop when you fall from the machine if you have the safety cord attached to you clothing.  This is too late because you can be injured when either falling off or trying to exit the treadmill because you can not keep up with the belt speed.

I think there should be a safety override in the software or firmware of the treadmill that monitors belt speed and will shut off the treadmill if belt speed accelerates without a command.
justification: The uncontrolled acceleration of the treadmill belt poses a significant risk of injury, as described, but no actual injury is reported.

incident_description:
Product in question are 2002 Atomic race 614 bindings.  The heel component is prone to breaking (same defective heel component as recalled Race 412 bindings - Release #09-077 - December 23, 2008).  

I was sking (not raceing) downhill at a controlled pace when the heel cup of my Atomic race 614 bindings spit down the middle causing me to fall suffering mild injuries & bruising.  I hate to consider what significant injuries could have been sustained had I been raceing at the time of failure.  

A photo of the defective heel cup can be viewed at:   https://docs.google.com/leaf?id=0B1R7uDEkSVRpODU4M2Y3OGUtMmVjZC00NDFjLTkxY2ItM2NmNWQxZTNmOTk5&hl=en_US 

Product in question are 2002 Atomic race 614 bindings.  The heel component is prone to breaking (same defective heel component as recalled Race 412 bindings - Release #09-077 - December 23, 2008).  

I was skiing (not racing) downhill at a controlled pace when the heel cup of my Atomic race 614 bindings spit down the middle causing me to fall suffering mild injuries & bruising.  I hate to consider what significant injuries could have been sustained had I been racing at the time of failure.  

A photo of the defective heel cup can be viewed at:   https://docs.google.com/leaf?id=0B1R7uDEkSVRpODU4M2Y3OGUtMmVjZC00NDFjLTkxY2ItM2NmNWQxZTNmOTk5&hl=en_US 

this is not an isolated incident, and an general search online for Atomic Race 614 bindings will show MANY consumers impacted by broken heel components to these bindings.  (Why the Race 614 bindings were not included in recall release #09-077 is beyond me since the same defective heel component is used on the race 614 as the included race 412 bindings.)  I have contacted Atomic asking about the inclusion of this binding model in the prior recall, and the affirmed it was not included, and neither product replacement/repair, nor a public notice of injury pertained to the Race 614 bindings.  Therefore I am compelled to report the issue to the USCPSC to get the information out to the public who may still be skiing on this model of ski binding that the product us unsafe, and should discontinue use immediately.
justification: The incident resulted in mild injuries and bruising, and there are reports of many consumers impacted by the same issue.

incident_description:
I have a 2009 Polaris Ranger Crew 700 EFI. After experceing several problems with one recall (fire in wiring harness) now the fuel pump is out and the Polaris dealers (several) have told me that they are seeing this on this particular model more frequently in the past months. Please advise.

Thank you

incident_description: 25 year old unhelmeted driver of all terrain vehicle, exceeding speed limit, lost control and ran off the right side of the roadway and overturned.  Driver was fatally injured and died at the scene.
justification: The driver was fatally injured and died at the scene, indicating the highest severity level. The occurrence likelihood is set to 2 (unlikely) based on the provided frequency of 76 out of 3915 incidents.

incident_description: A welded piece of the right roller arm of the elliptical(Nordic Track E7sv) snapped completely right off when it was in use, sending my wife flying off of the machine.  Luckily she did not get injured or need medical attention.  Obviously this is a manufacturing defect and a huge safety hazard!!!!!!!!!!  Someone could get seriously hurt.  Looking at the reviews on sears.com (where we purchased this), this appears to have happened to many others.  This product needs to be recalled so it doesn't happen to anyone else.
justification: The incident caused no injury but was a significant safety hazard, and reviews indicate it has happened to others, suggesting it is likely to occur again.

incident_description:
Kenda brand bicycle inner tubes failing next to valve.

I've had 10 tubes within the past month from Kenda (manufacturer) fail in the exact same manner.  I reached out to them as well as the distributer (QBP) and was issued replacements that also failed in the same exact way.

The puncture occurs on the inside of the tube about 1 inch away from the valve.  All of my failures have occurred at low speed but it could very easily happen at a much faster speed and cause a catastrophic accident and injury.

Upon further investigation, I found the exact same issue happening to other users via the internet. Here are some of those posts with photographs that match my exact issue.

http://www.cyclingforums.com/t/324561/strange-tube-failure

http://www.bikeforums.net/archive/index.php/t-87229.html

It appears that this dates back to at least 2005.
justification: The incident describes repeated failures of bicycle inner tubes that could lead to injury, especially at high speeds, and evidence shows this is a recurring issue.

incident_description:
Text of consumer's complaint

I have a safety concern over a product purchased several months ago. The safety issue concerns a Horton Visions Crossbow cocking mechanism. Photo one and two show the cocking mechanism I have concerns about. This cocking sled and crank are used to mechanically cock this crossbow. The draw weight this crank is suppose to cock is 175 pounds. The concerns I have with this crank are numerous. On two occasions while cocking this crossbow the cords used on the crank snapped, (Photo Three). This prematurely released pressure on the crossbow limbs which can cause serious injuries. On the first incident of this crank cord snapping also caused the crossbow string to snap. This string came back and I received a gash about three inches long slightly above my right eye. Higher could have caused blindness. The second incident this crank cord snapped resulted in my right tail light housing being smashed on my vehicle, (Photo Four). This snapped cord is also visible on pictures one and two. On another occasion the crank slide came off the aluminium track of the crossbow and the crossbow string again snapped prematurely releasing again the pressure on the crossbow limbs. This has also happened on several occasions. While cocking the slide assembly used to cock this crossbow comes separated from the track as previously mentioned. Another issue while cocking is this slide assembly continually twists and binds on the aluminum track. Photo five shows the grinding marks on the slide assembly. You must continually release the pressure on the crank to unbind the cocking assembly. This can also be highly dangerous. Another safety issue concerns the ratchet assembly on the crank, (Photo six) the spring toggle used on the gear of the cranking assembly disengages while cranking, again causing the pressure on the limbs to be pramaturely released. As shown in the photo the retaining spring does not keep pressure on the cocking tog. You must hold this in place with one hand while cocking with the other. If your finger slides off the tog again you have a dangerous release of the crossbow limbs. I have had dangerous issues with this crank assembly on every attempt to cock this crossbow. All these incidents occurred after using this crank approximately fifteen times. As the way this unit is currently manufactured I am afraid to cock this crossbow. I have been unable to use this crossbow since being purchased. I have also had to pay for replacement cranking cords and strings plus labor. This crank as designed cannot handle the 175 pound draw weight needed to cock this crossbow. I have heard from several retailers selling this crank all have major concerns over the safety of this unit. I have contacted the company directly on several occasion and all I seem to get is a list of excuses and no results. No modifications have been made to this crank assembly. Someone will become seriously injured with the cranking assembly as currently designed. The Manufacture is Horton Archery, 4430 Crystal parkway, Kent Ohio 44240. Phone 330-474-5710, fax 330-673-1476.
justification: The consumer reported a gash above the eye from a snapped string, indicating an injury, and multiple dangerous incidents with the product.

incident_description: I purchased my 2005 Arctic Cat snowmobile brand new so I have been the only owner or operator of the vehicle for its entire life. Shortly after purchasing it I receive a recall letter conserning a steering component and the fuel tank. I returned the machine to the dealer where both issue where corrected, I thought. they installed a sleeve in the filler neck to strengthen it and change a knuckle on the stering. Last weekend while snowmobiling in Michigan my gas tank started leaking. At first I thought it was the gas cap leaking so I purchased one at the Picklemans AC dealership in Newberry, MI. I found out later that day that my filler neck was cracked almost all of the way around it. I didn't recieve any serious injury just a red area on my leg form the fuel that went away quickly. I repaired the crack as best I could 500 miles from home and on vacation. The sled is not leaking anymore and is ridable but I feel Acrtic Cat should make it right with me since their "fix" for the recalled fuel tank didn't work. Kind of leaves me wondering about their "fix" for the steerin issue also.
justification: The incident involved a fuel tank leak due to a cracked filler neck, causing minor skin irritation but no serious injury.

incident_description: Bought a Carolina Cruiser 20" Magna bike for my 6 year old daughter for xmas.  She rode it on 12/26 and the pedal kept coming unscrewed.  We would screw it back in and she would pedal some more and the force of her pedaling caused it to unscrew.  This happened several times then we gave up.  I returned it to Target in Eagle Rock, CA and was appalled to see it back on the shelf for resale a few minutes later...the exact bike..despite the fact that I told the Manager, [REDACTED], it was defective and unsafe and that I was going to contact you. Even my 3 year old knew it was the broken one we just returned.

incident_description:
Caller purchased an electrically charged 8 battery operated Bad Boy Buggy Classic ATV Friday December 2nd, 2011 from the dealer who informed consumer that there had been a recall on these ATV's but all being sold had been repaired to be compliant.

Model# Not immediately accessible  with Serial# Not immediately accessible    DOM07/26/2010

ATV was loaded by dealer's employees.

He drove the two hours to his home, took the ATV off his trailer and took it riding on his gravel road noticing immediately that the steering was pulling from right to left.

He brought it back, put it in the garage but was talking with neighbors later that day who said they wanted to look at it, he took it out but when they began riding it they told him they didn't want to ride it until he got it fixed.

Friday, December 2nd 2011 (same day of purchase) Caller contacted dealer, Bad Boy and  spoke with [REDACTED]  who told him that she had no certification stating the the ATV he had purchased had been repaired.  He said that there is a brown piece of paper wired to the steeing wheel reading, "Steering Column Complete".

incident_description: I bought a gut buster and the spring snapped off at the handle.  it snapped back and injured my toe.  I would like a replacement

incident_description:
While riding a PETSROLL 3 wheel scooter, the scooter became overbalanced rearward to the wheelie protection wheel and lost control, resulting in broken leg and ankle.  The reason control was lot is that the unit is driven by the front wheel and all braking, drive and steering is on the front wheel. if the unit becomes overbalanced backward and the front wheel leaves the ground, there is no way to control or stop the device. When overbalanced backward, the unit is practically impossible to return to the proper attitude. These units are imported from China and named PERTSROLL, ZAPPY 3, etc www.petsroll.net, www.zapworld.com/zappy-3-standard, etc.

These units need to be banned until safety issues can be corrected by the manufacturer or importer.
justification: The incident resulted in a broken leg and ankle, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The description suggests a design flaw that makes such incidents likely when the scooter is overbalanced backward.

incident_description: My son receive this skateboard for Christmas. He rode the skateboard two times. Very beginner moves, just standing and gliding on board. The piece that holds the wheels to the skateboard, literally broke into half causing the wheels to fall off the skateboard. My concern is that when I went online to Toys R us (where it was purchased) there was another review that was the exact same thing. I feel that if a kids is riding the skateboard more agressive then mine, serious injury may occur. Obviously if there are two incidents documented with the same exact thing, there must be more.
justification: The skateboard broke during use, but no injury occurred. Similar incidents reported suggest a likely occurrence.

Inspecting the scooter then I found that the front fork was attached to a tube with 3 poor welds.  My concern is that other children could experience serious injury on this product if this poor design and shoddy workmanship is wide spread.

As it fell on top of my head, one of the bolts lodged in my skull, causing a dent and bleeding.  I suffered a concussion and went to the emergency room for treatment.  I was given a tetanus shot and was told it may take a while to fully recover.  To date, I still suffer from periodic head aches, lower back pain, ear aches, and slight apathy.  I lost two days of work because of this (December 8th and 9th) and the cost of emergency room treatment.  This product is dangerous and should (1) be removed from the market (recalled), (2) redesigned and tested for safety, (3) warning stickers placed on the product on proper securing and placement, (4) and safety devices or attachments provided for secure placement on door.  This product does not contain any such warnings now and is advertised on their website in the following way:  "Total upper body workout bar.  Attaches & Removes from Door Frame in Seconds!  No Drilling!  No Tools! No Fasteners!  Heavy Duty Steal Construction."  The website address is www.getirongym.com and the manufacturer identified on the website under customer service is Ontel Products Corporation, 21 Law Dr., 1st Floor, Fairfield, NJ, 07004.  The phone number listed is:  973-439-9035.
justification: The incident resulted in a concussion, bleeding, and ongoing health issues, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The description suggests this is a recurring issue with the product, making occurrence likely (4).

API Climbing Treestand Chain Failure Incident ÃÂ Nov 28, 2011

Victim:  [REDACTED]

API Outdoor

Weight Capacity 275 lbs (as per label).
Purchased from Cabelas approximately 2003 (from memory) ÃÂ credit card records could confirm.

Incident Summary 
On Monday November 28, 2011 at approximately 10:40 AM, [REDACTED] (I) was climbing down a tree in his API Outdoor climber, Model Mega Bucks GS2600MEG.  When the standing platform portion of the stand got approximately 15 feet from the ground there was a metallic crack/snap sound which was the result of the upper stand portion chain breaking.

The chain break caused the upper rail portion of the climber to become unattached to the tree causing the upper rail portion of the climber to fly back.  The victim was left suspended upside-down secured to the platform portion of the stand by only the foot straps that are used to position the standing platform when climbing and descending.    

From the hanging upside-down position, [REDACTED] initiated incident response and command actions for rescue.  These included:  
ÃÂ	Notification of co-hunter hunting nearby (brother ÃÂ [REDACTED]).
ÃÂ	Called wife to call 911 and report incident and address. Requested EMT and Fire Rescue.
ÃÂ	Instructed brother to bring his treestand so he could climb up to help save me. 
ÃÂ	Communicated with dispatcher regarding incident real-time status.
ÃÂ	Cut off upper portion of stand that was hanging by the tether line.
ÃÂ	Brother climbed up and cut foot straps to free legs. (He took a picture of me before climbing up).
ÃÂ	From the position of hanging from my hands, I dropped to the forest floor.
ÃÂ	Blowing whistle to notify of emergency location.
ÃÂ	First Responders arrived at address about the time I dropped to the ground, arrived to my scene approximately 5 minutes later.

I treated the ankle with rest and minimal use over the next few days. I was not wearing a fall restraint system since the climber had an upper rail that acted as protection from falling out of the stand and because I was descending the tree at the time.  

My body weight at the time of the incident was ~ 235 pounds.  Weight of equipment and clothing was approximately 10 pounds.  Treestand was approved, as per label, to 275 pounds. Temperature that day was approximately 65 degrees F.

incident_description: I sent an Daisy Powerline dual ammo air pistol from Walmart in Anchorage Alaska and sent it to the Philippines. The pistol had never been used and the pellet got stuck in the chamber and would not come out. This being the case the person did not know that the pistol has a fault and nearly shot themselves trying to remove pellet from the chamber. incident_description:
I found this vehicle advertised on the internet. I asked a local dealer to order one for me. It was shipped preassembled. All the dealer had to do was install the front wheels and the battery. The dealer mentioned that the steering was stiff, but he thought it would break in over time.

I have put about 100 miles on it, but cannot ride it over 30mph. It was advertised to go over 60. The problem is the steering. It never did "break in". When you hit a bump in the road it abruptly veers either left or right. The direction is not dependent on which side of the vehicle or which wheel hits the bump. It is not the size of the bump that causes the deflection, but the speed of the vehicle. I have not been over 45mph on it. At that speed I don't know if I am going to end up in a ditch or an on coming lane of traffic.

The dealer has tried to correct the problem, but reports that he is not getting reliable support from the distributor, importer or manufacturer. The vehicle is not safe to operate. Since the dealer did not stock this vehicle and I requested he order it for me, he says there is not much he can do for me other than be the middleman and try to rectify the malfunction. I would like to return the vehicle, but the dealer's distributor has not been responsive to the request.

The warranty will expire Feb. 2, 2012

The product can be viewed at http://www.icebearatv.com/PST250K.TRIKE.htm

The dealer I ordered it through is: ARTEMAN'S CYCLE REPAIR, 1310 State Route 54 E, Clinton, IL 61727
justification: The vehicle's steering issue poses a significant safety risk, potentially leading to loss of control, but no incident or injury has been reported yet.

incident_description:
The consumer indicated that the  seven pound bar that holds weights weighing 250 pounds  is too thin to hold the weigh  and while her 19 year old son was using it with the weight she noticed that the bar started to bend in the middle. 

The retailer and various different retailers with the same name in different cities were contacted weeks after the failure occurred (date is unknown) and she voiced her concerns about the bar.

She was also provided the number to the headquarters of the retailer but has contacted them on numerous occassions and no one has called her back.

The consumer son still currently using the bar but now uses it with less weights.

incident_description:
Purchased July 15, 2011 on sale from $375.00 to $301.00. Returned Dec 21, 2011. 

The safety enclosure net and padding around the top of our 15 foot BouncePro by Sports Power combo trampoline was deteriorating rapidly. We put it up in late July, used it for two weeks, went on a two week vacation and generally used the trampoline on weekends once daylight savings started. Within three months, the safety net had a major rip. This rendered the net more of a safety hazard than a safety feature. The kids were told to stay out until the net was fixed. They did not.

One of the neighborhood kids was on the trampoline and tripped forward as she was exiting the enclosure, then the seams where you enter and leave to shut the enclosure came undone and she fell right out! She went home crying to her mother but between us we were able to determine that there was no major injury. Luckily she fell onto our overgrown grass on the soft part of the lawn.

 We decided we'd try to replace the net and that the trampoline was OFF LIMITS until ALL safety features where intact. A week later, the safety pads began cracking, peeling, and curling or ripping.  

The trampoline was dangerous and it was too risky to leave up and chance an injury. So, we took it down. 

We are returning it to Sam's Club today per the manufacturer's suggestion. Sam's has a 100% customer satisfaction guarantee. The manufacturer was not in the least bit 'concerned' about the inferior quality of their product.
justification: The incident involved a child falling but no major injury occurred, and the trampoline was subsequently taken down to prevent further incidents.

incident_description:
I bought an Ontel ISO 7X Isometric Workout Bar and used it for exercise for three times, less than 10 minutes each. 

On this occasion while pressing it down, with less than 70Lb force, the handle broke and  spring and metal casing shot from the device flying across the room. The casing is metal but it is connected to the handle with plastic part, which for some reason just broke and there was nothing to prevent the big spring and metal casing to go flying. 

It could have hit me or hit anyone standing near by. Could hurt a person on damage things in your place of workout.

This product is unsafe and should be recalled till the plastic connector is replaced with a metal connector and some safety feature is added to prevent the spring and bar from going flying. 

I have provided the picture of broken device to seller but have not get any explanation on what they plan to do to protect others.
justification: The handle broke, causing parts to fly, posing a risk of injury but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description:
I am writing in regards to the 2011 Polaris Sportsman XP 850 All Terrain Vehicle. There is an extremely unsafe condition involving a defect in the valve cover, breather, and air box which allows the air box to fill with oil. This issue is well documented on various websites, yet Polaris has only offered to remedy the situation in rare circumstances. Upon contacting Polaris regarding this issue I was informed that they would not offer the updated 2012 replacement parts under my 6 month new ATV warranty. 

This defect exposes the consumer to a potential fire hazard, contact with used motor oil, and increased air filter replacement costs. 

While Polaris has updated the 2012 Sportsman XP 850 components to ensure there are no further issues, they have yet to offer a recall for the 2010 and 2011 models. Further, they have denied my request to cover the defects under my 6 month consumer warranty when contacted by e-mail. Polaris has made it apparent that they will not remedy this defect through good will or consumer warranty, and it is time for the CPSC to step in and help protect consumers from this hazardous defect.
justification: The defect poses a potential fire hazard and contact with motor oil, but no actual incidents or injuries are reported in the description.

incident_description: The consumer says the unit is designed with a chain that wraps around the back of the tree.  The chain broke in two.  The consumer says he has brusing on his left leg.  He was hanging upside down by one leg when the chain snapped.  He was able to raise himself up and get a hold of the stand and free his foot.  The consumer tried to contact the manufacturer who had been bought out.  The acquiring company would not give him any information about his product.  The consumer says this same product is being sold in stores.
justification: The consumer suffered bruising on his leg, indicating an injury, and the incident involved a broken chain that caused him to hang upside down.

incident_description: Consumer says that after changing the seal kit on the bicycle it starts leaking pressure/oil from the adjustment rebound knob within a few weeks. Consumer says the shaft leaking problem is a manufacturing defect because the o-ring was not aligned properly during installation.
justification: The incident involves a product defect causing a leak, but no injury or harm is reported.

incident_description:
I am a physical therapist and I was working with a patient who was using a Johnny G Krank Cycle by Matrix. Below is the incident report content outlining the incident which occurred at [REDACTED]
This patient was seen by this therapist for his usual physical therapy appointment starting at 11 am on Wed. 11/17/11. He participated in this session from 11 am until 11:50 pm without incident. The last activity was using the UBE ÃÂKrank CycleÃÂ, which this patient has used several times with therapist supervision. The cycle appeared stable and the seat position appeared normal during the first 2 minutes of use. Suddenly the seat came unattached and the patient fell backward onto his back. This therapist was standing next to the patient as this occurred. The patient did not appear to hit his head. He was questioned carefully while on the ground and was alert. He was assisted to a standing position [REDACTED] assist x2 by this therapist and [REDACTED] the front desk employee. He was seated in a chair at the site of the fall. He was alert and oriented, in good humor but obviously stunned. He remained seated for 5 minutes before being assisted by this therapist to a chair in the lobby. His wife was called and came with a neighbor to pick up the patient with the intention of driving him home. He was insisting on driving home but this therapist advised him against it. His wife was  informed of the incident on the phone and when she came to pick up the patient. He was wincing in pain with sit to stand, stand to sit transfers, but this was brief during transfers and he was ambulating normally. He was advised to contact [REDACTED] or go to the emergency room if pain became notable and changed from his usual status. He called and spoke to [REDACTED] the front desk employee informing her that he was seeing [REDACTED] for an x-ray. This therapist will call the patient this evening for a status update.

Status update by this patient's wife is that he has 2 fractured ribs as diagnosed by a visit to his primary care physician with (+) X-ray.

The Krank Cycle has a seat that rests on two short metal posts and a hook on the separate seat piece rests on top of the posts. There is no pin to secure the seat, and the seat can be easily removed by lifting up on the seat piece.
justification: The patient suffered 2 fractured ribs from the fall, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: The razor scooter has knobs/buttons on each side of the handle bar that when pushed in by accident the handle bar(s) comes off.  My 4 year old has accidentally pushed one of the buttons while riding the scooter and the handle bar came off and he fell off the scooter.  This happens twice now.  It is so easy for a kid to push these buttons because they are located right on the handle bars and it is what secures the handle bars.  When a kid has his hands on the handle bar naturally while riding, he can unconsciously push the buttons and then the handle bars they are holding on to come off.  This creates a very potentially dangerous situation.  My son luckily did not hit his face on the ground but he did suffer from scratches and his fingers got caught between the handle bar that came off.
justification: The child suffered scratches and caught fingers, indicating an injury, and the incident has occurred twice, suggesting it is likely to happen again.

incident_description:
My son owns an orange and white jeep bike, came with training wheels. The bikes pedals are the problem, they are consisted souly of a screwable/unscrewable nut on the inside with absolutely no washers or anything holding them in place. Thus as my son is pedaling his bike, they can unscrew on their own, many times is my son riding his bike and the pedal has come off and he has been left without full control of the bike. Furthermore the breaks on this child's bicycle is provided by reversing the pedals, so if a pedal falls off as you need to break, it forms further complications.also the unrealized sudden loss of a pedal can cause for a loss of balance, causing the rider to have a hard fall onto the ground, possibly trapping the foot that went down for the lost pedal. Now luckily my son is still using his training wheels, and im with him all the time, so he's had no accidents related to this except for the fact that his pedal comes off constantly. I do hope this gets reported before someone becomes more injured. as for the incident date, its happened more than once, so ill just give you the last time it happened.

the bike has a white body with orange and black tire tracks across several sections of it as well as the word "jeep" its seat is black with an orange and black tire mark and X12 on it, it has black tires with orange rims, and orange shocks all over the bike.
justification: The pedals frequently come off during use, posing a risk of loss of control, but no injuries have occurred due to supervision and training wheels.

incident_description: Fender on child bicycle cut the adult assembling the bicycle.   Edges of fender are extremely sharp and will cut children.
justification: The incident describes an injury to an adult from sharp edges on a child's bicycle fender, indicating a severity level of 3. The mention of the fender being extremely sharp suggests a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:

incident_description: The hinge on the handlebar post completely cracked off while I was riding my Dahon Speed D7.

He got in the shower, when his brother told him that the ATV was on fire.  He says the unit was on fire ten feet from his house.  He said only 10 minutes had passed from him turning it off and the fire occurring.  The flames where ten feet high.  The consumer says the fire melted some of his windows.  he says there was no indication that something was wrong with it.  He went online and noticed reports of similar incidences with this brand.  The consumer says he is experiencing the same issues as stated in Alert #08-580.  The consumer's model is not included in the recall.

incident_description:
The 180 lbs., consumer was riding the bicycle on a city street and going downhill when the brakes failed.  The consumer was able to stop the bike with his feet and he was not injured.

The brakes were made by Tektro (Model# Novella) and they were sold already assembled on the bike.

The brakes initially began to squeal while in use.  The consumer took the bike back to the retailer and they adjusted them.  When he took it back home and rode it again, the brakes were still squeaking.  The consumer took the bicycle back to the same retailer he purchased it from.  The dealer's technicians cleaned the brakes with alcohol.  

The 3rd time the consumer took the bike to Jerry and Sparky (an authorized bicycle service center).  The service center's technicians called the bicycle mfr. and they contacted the brake mfr., who sent out a set of replacement brakes and the service technician installed them.

The consumer rode the bicycle with the replacement brakes and the squeaking sound was gone, but the brakes did not perform as well as they should have.  The consumer said that he was riding between 35 and 30 mph, at the time and he believes that if he had hit a vehicle, the accident would have been fatal.

(10/10/11)  The consumer returned the bicycle back to the retailer where he purchased it from.  The consumer said that every time he takes the bicycle back to the dealer, they clean them with alcohol and claim that they are just dirty. 

The consumer believes that the bike is not safe to ride.
u went to www.ntbr.com and he said that out of the 31 reviews he read, 28 of them were negative. The consumer said that the mfr. also makes brakes with model # IOX and they present a similar problem, based on reviews that he read.
justification: The consumer was able to stop the bike without injury, but the repeated brake failures indicate a significant safety issue.

incident_description: Bought a Specialized P1 which had an incorrectly manufactured frame.  The rear wheel offset is wrong so that the bike turns slightly left all the time.  When my son who I bought it for jumped it (it is a bike made for that), it turned on take-off, rotated uncontrollably in the air, causing him to crash.  No serious injury but I've been told that Specialized made a whole production run like this.  I was told this by the dealer where I bought the bike.  I've tried to get Specialized to fix the bike - they gave us a new frame but we had to pay to have it changed ourselves.
justification: The incident resulted in a crash due to a manufacturing defect, causing injury but no serious harm. The likelihood is high as it affects a whole production run.

incident_description:
Polaris Sportsman XP 850 ATV suspension failure as described in Alert # 10-713.  

While riding the ATV on the Oregon Dunes, the left front upper A-Arm suddenly separated from the spindle knuckle causing loss of control and damage to the front suspension components.  Fortunately, the speed at the time was approximately 15 mph and no injury resulted.

The ATV had to be towed and transported to the local dealer, Florence Yamaha-Polaris.  The dealer advised that the repair should be covered as the failure was the direct subject of the safety alert #10-713.  The Polaris factory repeatedly declined to pay for any of the damage or for any of the repairs required, and thus did not stand behind the faulty parts.  

This ATV was previously inspected by a dealer in California during approximately February or March of 2010 due to the safety alert and no parts were changed at that time.  It is assumed that the Polaris factory noted this inspection was previously done per the recall by the VIN # and this may be the basis for the denial.
justification: The incident resulted in loss of control and damage to the ATV but no injury occurred, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) as the issue was known and previously inspected under a safety alert.

incident_description: We have a tornado slide on our playground that within one week we had two accidents 11/01 & 11/03, both of which required trips to the emergency room.  Neither child was seriously hurt but when contacting the agency regarding slide we were informed that it has one of the deepest beds in the industry and that maybe we needed to train students on how to use the slide.  We contacted the company because we wanted to either put a top on it and make it enclosed or find a solution to raise the sides of the slide at the top curve so students would be unable to stop and lean over the slide to look at the bottom to see if there was anyone still there.  Neither solution is an option with the company, our only option would be to take it down and replace it with another slide that would cost more money.

incident_description:
Caller's husband was rowing on exercise machine at Gym when it froze and threw all pressure from momentum to the top of his right foot rupturing his anterior tibialis tendon.
He hobbled to his car, drove himself home.
The following day (June 02, 2011) he and his wife went to an orthopedist who sent him to have MRI.
MRI showed the rupture.
Caller's husband was scheduled for surgery the following week,
Surgery was performed June 10th, caller's husband was placed in a cast and will remain in one for the next two months.
He will then need physical therapy.
Caller wanted this reported due to danger of rowing machine repeating
justification: The incident resulted in a ruptured tendon requiring surgery and physical therapy, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as possible (3) based on the caller's concern about the danger of the rowing machine repeating the incident.

incident_description:

In 2010 the vinyl again tore from the seams at new spots and the repaired vinyl also tore again (repaired under warranty by Rayner). A representative from the retailer (www.backyardcitypools.com) we used to ship the pool cover back to Rayner informed us that the vinyl they used in 2008 was defective and that they were receiving numerous complaints and returns for repairs. 

The vinyl tears so bad that a small child or animal can easily fall through the cover and become entrapped underneath.
