incident_description:
My 2009 Fuji Roubaix RC road bike came with Shimano WH-RS10 wheels. These wheels in fact are on many new bikes. After a recent ride and inspecting those wheels I noticed a crack in the rim perpendicular to the spoke. On removal of the wheel and careful inspection there were breaks at 9 of the 20 spokes in that rear wheel. The wheels have considerable use but should not fail in such an unsafe way.
I sent these wheels back to Shimano to impress them that this is a serious safety issue. I'm tired of products being designed to the point that failure occurs in the worst possible way. I have been told by the bike shop that returned them for me that the problem occurs frequently with these wheels. Also these wheels are still on bikes sold today.
It is said that a new generation wheel will have re-enforcement rings at the point the spoke enters the rim. But the public should be aware the RS10 is dangerous!

I think Shimano will send replacement wheels although that was not my intention.
justification: The incident describes a safety issue with the wheels but no actual injury occurred, and the problem is reported to occur frequently.

incident_description:
The Kolpin Power Sports Geartector Mitts are "L" shaped tubular gauntlets designed to fit over ATV handle bars.  I installed a set on my 2005 Kawasaki 750 Brute Force atv, and almost immediately recognized that the portion of the tube installed on the right handle bar was too narrow, and the inside of the bend in the tube was located where the throttle on the atv is located.  The result was that on several occasions, the mitt contacted and opened the throttle.  The first time this happened, my machine was in reverse and as I inserted my hand into the tube, the tube contacted the throttle opening it to near full, causing my machine to vigorously back up into a large tree.  There were several other instances where the tube contacted the throttle, and rather than discontinue use, I attempted to resolve the problem by insuring that my hand was over the throttle before putting my atv in gear.  This can only be accomplished by using the left hand to shift a shift mechanism located on the right side of the atv.  The last incident before I removed the mitts from my atv happened when I was attempting  to back out of a large snow drift on a road along a steep, deep slope.  As I backed up, I needed to use the right hand brake, and discovered that doing so caused the mitt to contact the throttle again, causing the atv to go vigorously backward.  I nearly went off the road over the edge of the steep slope before I regained control of the atv.  That is when I removed the mitt from the right handle bar, thinking it is better to have a cold hand that wreck my atv.

I have years of experience operating an atv in the Wind River Mountains of central Wyoming in all sorts of weather conditions.  I have never experienced the kind of loss of control the Geartector Mitt caused, and will not use the product again.  The actuation of the throttle can also be caused when the hand is inserted into the gauntlet if the user is not very careful.  

I strongly urge you to investigate this product because in the current design they can cause unintended actuation of the throttle and loss of control of the atv.  I am lucky my encounter with the tree did not result in injury to me, and I am lucky I did not go off the road and down a steep slope.
justification: The incident caused loss of control of the ATV multiple times but no injury was reported, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) as the issue happened several times under different conditions.

incident_description:
Around a year and a half ago, I purchased a Thomson Elite X2 road stem from TreeFort Bikes in Michigan. This stem is made from CNC'd aluminum. About a year later, while I was out of town and the bike was sitting in my empty apartment on the stand, both handlebar retaining collars on the aluminum faceplate, cracked and broke. When I returned from my trip, I removed the bike from the stand to go for a ride. The aero bars flopped straight down, so I placed the bike back on the stand to have a look. 

I can provide pictures of the broken faceplate. Those handlebar retaining collars are too weak, have a  and should be redesigned. Perhaps there was also a bad batch of aluminum, but this should never happen. Imagine the results of this if I had been descending a hill at 40+mph. 

I was disappointed in this stem, as I had believed in the reputation of Thomson to be very good in designing and building quality bike components that didn't break. 

I was further disappointed in the fact that despite three attempts via e-mail to call this to the attention of someone at Thomson, I did not even receive a reply to my e-mail, although their contact webpage reaction indicated that my message had been received.

I have since switched to a forged Origin8 stem with no problems. 

There are numerous other reports of the same thing happening to other people in various bike forums online. Some examples:

http://www.bikeforums.net/archive/index.php/t-458531.html

http://forums.roadbikereview.com/general-cycling-discussion/thomson-x2-stem-197085.html

What is incredible in my case, is the unwillingness of the company to even acknowledge my e-mails. It seems as though they are building a case for deniability.
justification: The incident involved a product failure without injury, and there are multiple reports of similar failures, indicating a possible design or material issue.

incident_description:
The consumer wanted to report that he purchased 2 bike tires from a retailer and stated that he has had the tires slide from under him on two occasions. The first incident happened two months ago. The consumer was riding on the sidewalk  to the street and the tire slid out from under him. The consumer was going at a very slow speed and did not come in contact with any unforeseen objects. The consumer fell on his left side landing on his ribs. The consumer did not go to the doctor but had to be in recovery for 4 weeks. 

The consumer purchased the tire in June of 2011 (exact date unknown). On the second incident Tuesday September 20, 2011, the consumer was riding at a park on dry asphalt, rounding a bend at slow speed when the front tire went out from under him. The consumer fell directly forward and landed on his wrists and rolled on the ground. This time the consumer chose to go to the hospital September 21, 2011. The consumer severely sprained his left hand with possible ligament damage and may be scheduled for MRI's. 

The consumer had a sprain on the right wrist but still painful. The consumer cannot open beverage container because of his injuries. The consumer is very active and is going through depression because of his injury limitations. The consumer stayed at the hospital for 2 hours. The consumer was unable to drive himself to the hospital and someone had to transport him to the hospital both ways.  The consumer had x-rays taken at the hospital and both his wrists. 

The consumer was also given a splint for his left hand and placed a sports wrap on his right hand. The consumer was also prescribed pain killers. The consumer went Saint Vincent's Hospital in Erie, PA. The consumer was told to follow up with a sports doctor and a visit has not yet been scheduled. His medical record number is [REDACTED]. The consumer spoke with the firm about the issue and was told that they would investigate the failure. The consumer called the retailer- the number was disconnected. The tires states that they are to be inflated at 40-60 pounds. The diameter of the tires are 26 inches. In both cases, the front tire failed and caused the fall.

The rear tire started to split down the middle- Bell sent a replacement in July, no questions asked.  

Consumer is still unable to do push-ups.  He's very depressed about that- he used to do 100 a day, lift weights and body bag/speed bag workouts.  He says this is killing him, he doesn't know how he's going to shovel snow this winter.
justification: The consumer suffered injuries in both incidents, including severe sprains and possible ligament damage, requiring medical attention and recovery time.

incident_description:
This report concerns the Weider X-Factor+, model no. WEBE2910.0 fitness equipment produced by ICON Heath & Fitness.
On two occassions the right side 45lbs resistance cord has broken away from the handle and struck me in the face or arm causing injury. The first time was on April 20, 2011 when I was during tricep presses facing the equipment. The right side 45lbs cord broke loose from the handle when I was pressing it downwards . The force of the recoil caused a small nick on my face and knocked my glasses from my face.I wsa quite fortunate that only the elastic portion had only come loose causing more shock than injury. The cord wsa eventually replaced directly by ICON after some argument concerning its warranty considering the equipment was only purchased on 12.27.2010 and it was less than four months old.
The second occurrance happened on 7.5.2011 when the replacement 45 lbs cord broke loose from the handle while during chest presses. This time I was facing away from the equipment, leaning slightly forward presing downwards when the cord broke loose. I felt a sharp pain in my left arm and noticed immediate swelling from the injury. I looked at the cord and noticed that this time there was some type of metal ring at the end of the cord which had caused the injury. I also found the metal retension pin which had apparently bent and come loose from the hole in the handle therefore causing the card to come loose. I went immediately to Solantic Heath Care where I was treated for a 15 inch welt/ on the upper portion on my arm. The injury was treated and I had limited use of my arm for over a week.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries on two separate occasions, including a 15-inch welt and limited arm use for over a week.

incident_description: We have an Eddie Bauer tent model EB30315.  When taking the tent down on 10/10/2011, a shard (or shards) from the fiberglass tent pole (part number 03-0054) came off while removing the tent clips and entered my right hand in the webbing between my thumb and pointer finger.  A small (3mm) shard near the point of entry was removable by me, however 2 larger shards (1cm each) required surgical removal.  In total this incident resulted in 1 trip to the ER, 4 Dr visits, and 1 surgical operation.

incident_description: 2005 polaris fusion 900 fuel tank neck cracked and gas would seep out and pour all over my clothes when i was riding
justification: Gas seeping from a cracked fuel tank neck poses a fire hazard and inconvenience, but no injury is reported.

incident_description:
I was driving my 2005 Suzuki LT-A700XK5 KING QUAD back to my house from the 100 acres of farm land I own. The machine died while I was driving at a very slow pace of about 15 ÃÂ 20 MPH. As I attempted to diagnose what the issue was smoke begin to emerge from under the seat by the battery casing. There is obviously a defect with this machine as I have never done any modifications, repairs, or anything else to this machine and always cared for it with great detail.

incident_description:
I purchased a used Landice Executive L7 Treadmill for $2,000 in 2007.  It was a year old when we purchased it.  This is a very robust and durable treadmill that we have installed in our 2nd home.  We rent our vacation house to guests and use it ourselves occasionally.  So the Treadmill gets usage, but not often.

About 2 months ago when I used the machine after a workout, I turned it OFF and after a few seconds it continued to run.  It would not stop.  It runs very slowly.  The only way to stop it is to unplug it from the wall.

I called Landice and they seemed to know immediately what the problem was.  They said that since I bought it used it would NOT be covered for Warranty.  It turned out from the repairman, they recommended, that the repair would cost close to a $1,000 to replace the main circuit board.

I have young children and would like to report this problem in that with the machine suddenly runs, when one expects the machine to Stop.  

One could slip and fall or a child could get severely hurt.
justification: The treadmill continues to run after being turned off, posing a risk of slip and fall or injury, especially to children, though no injury has been reported yet.

incident_description:
Two products are being reported: 1) Huffy Cranbrook Women's Bicycle 26" purchased from Walmart in New Orleans 2) Huffy Cranbrook Men's Bicycle 26" purchased from Walmart in New Orleans. 

Both bicycles have suffered, over 3 months since purchase multiple incidences of the bicycle chain falling off, preventing the rider from breaking or speeding up to avoid traffic. Fortunately, there were no injuries, but being unable to stop or accelerate can lead to potentially fatal accidents.
justification: The incident involves multiple occurrences of the bicycle chain falling off, which could lead to accidents, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I bought a weight lifting bar from powersystems and used this product for about 5 years. The bar snapped in two this past week. I used the bar with weight that was far below the recommended 500 lbs and specifically the way it is recommended by lifting experts etc. I contacted the company and sent pictures showing the clean break of the bar. I called the company and asked them to at least investigate. They offered to sell me another bar at a discounted price. I declined and again asked them to look at the photos and either consider testing there products to ensure that they can in fact hold weight and for longer than the 90 day warrenty or perhaps investigate to see if my bar was in fact defective. I have lifted for 35 years and never seen a bar snap in two. I was lucky that the person lifting when the bar snapped in half did not get injured. I am willing to send along the photos to show my point. I would have expected the product safety folks for this company to at least look into this before someone else has the same issue and is not as lucky.
justification: The bar snapped but no injury occurred, indicating an incident without harm. The likelihood is unlikely as the user notes this is the first such incident in 35 years of lifting.

incident_description: I was supervising my son playing in the trampoline one evening and I noticed some unsual squeaking, or should I say more squeaking than usual, so I walked around it to inspect it and I didnt see anything unusual so I didnt think anything of it, at the time. The very next morning when I woke up to get ready for work, I glanced outside to see the trampoline had collapsed.....so I went outside to get a closer look....and notice that the inter-locking poles that go around in a circle to hold up the jumping mat had completely snapped in half in four different places--causing very sharp metal to be exposed. I am shocked and dissapointed in this product(and the Manufacturer). I expected and am disgusted on the product being so poorly constructed and I firmly believe that something that is targeted for children(espeacially so expensive) shouldve have been made with more durable materials and better constructed!
justification: The incident involved a trampoline collapse with no injury, but potential for serious harm if someone had been using it.

incident_description: My husband and I purchased the Pure Fun 44" Mini Trampoline from ToysRUs.com ( UPC # 812461010821) back in June of this year for my 5 year old son who weighs less than 50 pounds. Within 2 months of use, the metal springs on the trampoline started to break in half. I called ToysRUs and they agreed to send me a replacement. This was in August. After getting the replacement and using it for less than 3 months, the same thing happened. One of the springs on the trampoline snapped in half and came off. I am returning the trampoline to ToysRUs for a refund, but I am afraid that if enough springs come off of this trampoline, it could collapse and be a danger to children or adults using it.

incident_description:
There is a current recall on Cannondale carbon Crankset (Release #07-206).  I have the same crankset, and the pedal insert has detached from the carbon crankset.  This causes a safety risk as identified by my bike shop.

I called Cannondale HQ and they were aware of the problem, but pointed to the manufacturer of the crank set, Full Speed Ahead (FSA) Bike Components.  Cannondale said I should call FSA to have the crankset replaced.  Cannondale acknowledged the recall on this product, but said it was for other defects.  They declined to replace the pedal for the defect that I identified.

I called Full Speed Ahead (FSA) Bike Components and they acknowledged the defect that was recalled under Release #07-206, but deferred any other defects/safety risks to Cannnondale since they were the assembler of the bike.

Obviously there are multiple defects with this product.  I ask that my crankset be replaced with one that does not have any defects.

Currently, the bike is not operational.  If I were to operate the bike with the current defect, I run the risk of the pedal falling off causing a wreck.

incident_description:
On or about August 13, 2011, at approximately 10:00am, my nine-year-old client was driving his Razor Ground Force electric powered go-kart in front of his family home.  At some point, the child's left hand came into contact with the go-kart's rear wheel.  As the result of the contact, the child suffered severe injuries to his left hand that have required three surgeries to date.  The first surgery was a debridement of the injuries.  Soon thereafter a skin flap was created using skin from the child's left middle finger.  The third surgery released the flap, and a skin graft from the child's hand was used to repair the middle finger.  Also, a vein from the child's hand was removed and used as a sheath over the damaged nerve, with the objective of restoring nerve function in the left ring finger.  The child is facing at least one more surgery to release scar tissue on the left pinky finger.  As the result of the injury, the child lost 40% of the tendon on his pinky finger, and all of the nerve conduction in his left ring finger.  The child's surgeon is uncertain at this time whether the hand can be restored to normal, pre-injury, functioning. Medical expenses, to date, exceed $60,000.

The Ground Force go-kart is equipped with rails along the side of the toy, but does not have any fender or other device to cover the spinning wheel.  Because of the their small diameter, the wheels spin at a high number of revolutions per minute notwithstanding the go-kart's modest speed.

I am one of the attorneys representing the child and his family with respect to this matter.
justification: The child suffered severe injuries requiring multiple surgeries, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) given the specific circumstances described.

incident_description:
To whom it may concern,

My Company was recently involved in a law suit where a chemical feed pump overfeed liquid chlorine in to a small commercial spa, severely burning (2) people. In researching the failure we became aware that the mechanism on the chemical feed pump responsible for controlling the intermittent pumping feature has a tendency to fail. When the intermittent pumping feature fails on the feed pump the chemical feed pump continues to uncontrollably feed chemical until the reservoir holding the chemical is empty.  We became aware that the failure has occurred more than 50 times in the last ten years.
justification: The incident resulted in severe burns to two people, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The failure has occurred more than 50 times in ten years, suggesting an occurrence likelihood of 4 (likely).

incident_description:
Record of Events Related to the Purchase and Use of 
2010 Bad Boy ÃÂClassicÃÂ ATV 

September 8, 2011


1.	Purchase of Bad Boy Buggy Vehicle:

The ÃÂBad Boy BuggyÃÂ ATV was purchased by mother-in-law, [REDACTED] in September of 2010.  [REDACTED] desired an all-terrain vehicle that had a low ecological impact and could be used to negotiate her 175 acre parcel of woods and fields on [REDACTED] in the town of Middlefield, New York.  The ÃÂBad Boy BuggyÃÂ was recommended to her by a neighborhood friend and by the dealer for the company, a Mr. [REDACTED] of Clay New York as a vehicle she could use to transport tools and supplies throughout her property.  Mr. [REDACTED] who owns the 4ward Sales Company dealership came to her property with a demonstration vehicle in early September of 2010. At that time he drove the vehicle on the land with [REDACTED] and I and we talked with him about its suitability for its intended purposes, including travel on rough logging roads with steep inclines.  He said that the vehicle was made for just this type of use and so should work well for us. He also gave me an introductory lesson on how to use the vehicle including the operation of its directional switching and the electrically activated braking system. 

[REDACTED] and Mr. [REDACTED] negotiated a deal on a 2010 demonstrator model that had been used by another family in the area as a service replacement.  Mr. [REDACTED] said that he would take the vehicle back to his shop and clean and service it so that it could be delivered in ÃÂas newÃÂ condition and would be fully warranted by the company.

The vehicle (Bad Boy Buggy Classic, VIN# [REDACTED]) was purchased by [REDACTED] for $11,775.52 from 4ward Sales on September 15th and delivered to her [REDACTED] of property.  The vehicle was kept in a shed specially purchased and wired for the vehicle on her property.  During the Fall and Winter of 2010 and 2011 the vehicle was used only 3-4 times due to inclement weather followed by the winter snows. In the Spring and Summer of 2011 the Buggy was used somewhat more frequently with a total of about a dozen usages all on [REDACTED]ÃÂs property and for short distances on [REDACTED] by members of her family (mostly myself) for recreation.  

During the entire ownership period the only service on the vehicle was that I removed the right rear tire to add sealant to fix a flat.  Other than that it was entirely as it was received from Mr. [REDACTED] in September of 2010.



2.	The ATV Accident of August 21st, 2011:

On the evening of August 21st my family consisting of my wife, [REDACTED] (53), my daughter [REDACTED] (17), son [REDACTED] (14) and myself [REDACTED] (53) were invited to [REDACTED]'s ÃÂUpper Lean-ToÃÂ on her property for a picnic with her, her friend Dr. [REDACTED] and my brother and sister-in-law [REDACTED] and [REDACTED].  We were scheduled to travel to South Korea the next day and this was a farewell picnic for the family. The ÃÂUpper Lean-ToÃÂ is situated on the southern side of [REDACTED] on a steep clearing with a view of the Village of Cooperstown and Otsego Lake in the distance.  That evening we were invited by [REDACTED] to use the ATV to get to the Lean-To and my son [REDACTED] drove the vehicle up to the site.  The trip was uneventful and we parked behind my brother-in-lawÃÂs SUV on a flat area and enjoyed our picnic.

At about 7:15pm that evening we decide that it was time to go, my daughter decided that she would like to try driving the ATV down to the parking area.  Others were seated as follows, [REDACTED] was in the right rear position, [REDACTED] in the left rear seat position and I sat in the passenger seat.  Although the vehicle was equipped  with seat belts (available only on special request) none of us were wearing them that night. I reviewed the vehicleÃÂs operations with [REDACTED], including putting the vehicle drive switch in the forward position and the use of the electric brakes. She put the ATV in forward and moved it around my brother-in-lawÃÂs SUV and began the descent down the hill. I immediately noticed that the ATV was picking up speed in an unsafe manner and told her to let her foot off of the accelerator and put the brake on.  She looked at me and said that she was already doing that and told me that her foot was on the brake, I looked over at her and confirmed that both of her feet were holding the brake pedal to the floor.  I could feel some resistance coming from the mechanical braking system, but at no time could I feel the electric braking system engage. We traveled very quickly down the upper part of the hill and struck a tree head on.  My wife, daughter and son were thrown from the vehicle by the force of the impact.  I hit the windshield, which was hitting the tree and then managed to stumble out of the ATV and then lay on the ground. The total distance travelled was approximately 325 feet from the place where we got into the ATV to where we struck the tree.  If we did not strike that tree we would have continued down the hill (approximately as steep as a downhill ski slope), with much more dire consequences. 

My in-laws called 911 for emergency help and I and my family, stayed in the positions we had fallen on the ground until the EMS crew from the Cooperstown Fire Department arrived and removed us to Bassett Hospital in Cooperstown, NY to be treated in the Emergency Room. Also responding to the incident, besides the Cooperstown Fire Department were the New York State Police and the Hartwick and Milford, New York Fire Department EMS squads.

I stayed in the hospital overnight for treatment and then received plastic surgery at Bassett Hospital to repair my broken cheekbone.  I have residual numbness over the right side of my face and continue to experience intermittent pain as a result of my injuries.  I also have some scarring from the injuries and from the surgery.

incident_description:
I was riding my mountain bike on a trail when the bike unexpectedly lurched sharply left throwing me off the bike onto rocks.  I experienced great chest (rib) and left knee pain.  I had to see my doctor who diagnosed broken ribs.

Not long before this I had replaced the front suspension fork on the bike with a fork from SRAM/Rockshox - the SID Team model.  While there had been reports in bicycling product reviews of this (and other) models from Rockshox of problems with the lower legs of the forks, I had spoken with two bicycle dealers who assured me 'those problems with the 2009 forks have been taken care of'.  Those problems as described by riders were: 'crooked forks,' 'unpredictable handling', an 'not knowing where the bike will go'.  The first mention of this does seem to occur in reviews of the 2009 products, but my fork is a 2010 model made in May of 2010, and if the dealers' statements were correct my fork would have been free of that defect.

Some time later, after careful examination of the fork, I saw that when a wheel trued in a truing stand was inserted in the fork the rim was offset to the left between the fork lowers.  This means the front wheel is not being held perpendicular to the ground, and so on heavy impact the wheel's spokes are unevenly loaded. This is exactly the same problem described by some of the reviewers who were critical of the 2009 fork.  More careful measurement showed that the right  fork leg was approximately 1.5 mm shorter than the left fork leg.  I called Rockshox customer service # and spoke with '[REDACTED]' who confirmed the 'problem with the lower casting'.

My concerns are: Why didn't Rockshox inspect for this defect before shipping?  And why did they allow this product to ship for two full years?  How many of these defective suspension forks are still in use, and how many have been injured by them?  This defect is not hard to find - once I saw how to check for it, it took only a few seconds.

Rockshox did agree to replace the defective lower for me, but as of this moment I still have the item available.  Replacement is not the solution here. Many, if not most users, will not discover their product is dangerous until it is too late.  I believe there are still thousands of these forks still in use.  Rockshox' position on this is  to replace the product only if the customer discovers the defect.

Link to MTBR (Mountain Bike Reviews) for 2009 Sid Team showing some of the complaints.
http://www.mtbr.com/cat/suspension/2009-forks/rockshox/sid-team/prd_425078_6513crx.aspx

Link to MTBR for 2009 Rockshox Reba showing some of the 'crooked lowers' complaints.
http://www.mtbr.com/cat/suspension/2009-forks/rockshox/reba-team/prd_425076_6513crx.aspx

Link to MTBR for 2010 Rockshox Sid Team 
http://www.mtbr.com/cat/suspension/2010-forks/rockshox/sid-team/prd_446894_6743crx.aspx
justification: The incident resulted in broken ribs, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is possible (3) given the reported defects and similar complaints.

The technician attempted to "lock" the bar in but said it would not lock. He said that the pin was "faulty" and would not lock a rod to keep it from rotating. The technician said that this is, "A DESIGN FLAW ON THE BIKE". The technician attempted to tighten the pin and we took the bike home. I was informed that consumers can no longer purchase the original model of handle bar or pin on the bicycle. 

I understand that the bike is no longer under warranty but as the bike is intended for use by children and if this mechanism is a design flaw and causes a danger of serious injury or harm to children then Trek should have repaired this flaw in their kids bikes.

incident_description:
I am writing to report a defect in a consumer product which has the potential to threaten the safety of consumers using the product.

On October 7th, 2011, I purchased a Pacific Cycle Mongoose XR-75, 26" men's 21 speed full-suspension mountain bike at Wal-Mart. The model number is R5116WMA, the date code is FS00315AA, and the serial number is SNFSD11C72297.  

When I got the bike to my home and attempted to ride it, the bike went less than 500' before the rear sprocket assembly began spinning freely on the rear wheel hub while pedaling in the forward direction, making it impossible to propel the bike by pedaling.

I removed the rear wheel from the bike, at which time the sprocket assembly fell off in my hand.

I examined the threads of the sprocket and the hub which join the two parts together. I am a marine mechanic, a mechanical design technician trained in geometric dimensioning and tolerancing, and a third-year mechanical engineering student - I am thoroughly competent to examine these threads. Online, I found a specification for these threads as 1.375" X 24TPI. The sprocket is made of steel, with a female thread, and the minor diameter (crest to crest, inside) measures 1.337". The hub is rolled steel tube, with male threads that measure 1.335" across the crests. The threads on the hub appear to be about 90% intact, the crests had been truncated by contact with the rotating sprocket and appear as 0.005" flats with a 0.035" wide "Vee" trough between.

I believe the threads on the hub were cut approximately 0.040" undersize, which allowed the bike to be assembled with insufficient thread engagement to withstand the stress of its intended load. 

The hub is stamped "DACHANG" - this is a Chinese hub made by the company that makes the one shown here: http://www.cndachang.com/ecp.asp?id=31 - I believe (but can not confirm) that the hub shown in the linked page is the same one I have. I believe the recall should extend to all DaChang hubs that are threaded on the same machine that threaded mine - my problem could have been caused by "improper machine setup - tool out of position" (producing a batch of defect parts persisting until the next tool change), or by "improper setup - loose tool" (producing a batch of parts with varying degrees of deviation), or by bad indexing of the machine (producing occasional defect parts for the life of the machine).

I have reported the defective hub to Pacific Cycle, they have offered to replace the entire rear wheel and sprocket set without charge. I will be satisfied, and my own claim with Pacific Cycle will end, when I receive a replacement wheel with the correct threads. At this time, I do not need CPSC assistance with my own claim.

I am reporting this defect in the interest of public safety. The severity of my hub's undercut, combined with the load imposed by my 200lb body, caused the defect to reveal itself immediately upon the first attempt to use it. But, a less severe deviation from specification, and/or a lighter rider, could allow a similarly defective hub to function for an unpredictable amount of time, with excessively high shear stresses on the hub threads for the entire service life of the bike. In this situation, the undersize threads would be most likely to fail at the exact time the rider needs them most - when he is pushing hardest - to climb a hill or cross a busy street or recover from a momentary loss of balance. A failure - loss of propulsion - at this time could have catastrophic consequences.

I recommend a service inspection recall of all Pacific Cycle bikes built with Dachang hubs, for their dealers (or a set of designated service locations) to disassemble the rear sprocket assembly from the rear wheel hub, and inspect the hub threads for compliance with specifications. I recommend that Pacific Cycle provide a "No-go" thread gauge to each inspection location, where such gauge has female threads cut to the minimum acceptable thread diameter, so that the gauge will thread by hand onto all undersize threads but will not thread by hand onto a hub with acceptable threads.

This recall is urgently needed for all bikes equipped with Dachang rear hubs. It will also promote bike safety overall, by permitting qualified service techs to examine these rear wheels for bent axles, loose, bent or broken spokes, deformed rims, sprocket wear etc.., and to repair any deficiencies they find.
justification: The incident describes a defective bike part that could lead to loss of propulsion, posing a safety risk, but no actual injury or death occurred in this case.

incident_description:
I am writing a letter of concern about your product. I am a 62 year old, retired teacher. I ride bike 4 times a week all year long; sometimes more often in the summer months. I belong to a bike club in my retirement community [REDACTED].  I spent a year researching bicycles before I settled on purchasing the 7.5 FX WSD Model 17 SATIN wtu143cl24e (7.524128245)- WTU143C2124E on August 17, 2010. I am 5'6" and weigh 125 lbs. My local bike shop is [REDACTED]. I chose TREK because I thought I was purchasing a safe product at high quality.

I rode the bike happily for 8 months, and then on April 20, 201 I, while on a club ride, the bolt that holds the seat component onto the seat stem shirred, the seat collapsed under me, and I fell into the roadway on [REDACTED] near my home. I sustained burns and bruises to my left knee, thigh, and elbow, and the bike brakes, handle bars, and of course seat housing were misaligned, but there was no major damage to the bike, and as far as I can tell, no major damage to me either. incident_description:
On Aug 6, 2011, I was hit by a car while cycling on my time trial bike with my Spiuk Kronos helmet.  I was ejected from the bike and landed hard on the asphalt road.  Immediately I was unconcious and later rushed to the ICU by an ambulance. I spent total 7 days in the emergency room.

Despite wearing Spiuk Kronos helmet (bought in May 2011), the helmet didn't manage to protect my head.  The back strap opened very easily and as a result only the front one going around my hears and chin was maintaining the helmet on my head. Due to the chock,  the helmet was then stripped off my head causing further damage to my right hear that required few stitches.

I then hit the pavement and suffered a frontal skull fracture extending through the roof of the right orbit and had at least 5mm stitches on the right forehead! 


The main problem I am reporting here is how easily the back strap could open, leaving the overall strapping system ineffective. 
Overall, my helmet only had very minor damage at the "tail".  Had the helmet didn't fly from my head, my head injury would have been spared!!
justification: The incident resulted in severe injuries including a skull fracture and required ICU care, indicating a high severity level. The occurrence likelihood is rated as unlikely (2) based on the specific and rare nature of the described helmet failure.

incident_description:
I received a Ruger Air Hawk Elite air rifle as a Christmas present about 3 years ago.  After about one year of intermittent (not heavy) use, I tried to use it and it discharged by itself.  I tried several times to load and use the air rifle and it discharged about 1/2 of the time without the trigger being pulled.  This is a break barrel air rifle, which means the barrel must be cocked open to load the pellet and engage the spring for firing.  One time the barrel swung up by itself and discharged, bending the barrel.  If my finger had been in the way while loading the pellet, I am sure it would have caused severe damage.  
I called the company (Umarex) to report the problem and they said it was my fault for pulling the trigger while it was open, which I did not do, and that the warranty was void because of that.  I have a hole in my wall and a hole in my rain gutter from it firing on its own.  For about $50 return shipping, another fee to straighten the barrel and the cost of me shipping the air rifle to the company, they said they would straighten the barrel, so I decided to locate a local repair person.  
The gun has remained untouched for about 1.5 years as it was unsafe to use due to both the bent barrel and the firing on its own.  I finally found a local repair person who fixed it.  He said the spring that pushes the air was broken (I have the broken spring), the barrel was obviously bent, and the firing holding mechanism was a lousy design.  According to what I was told, he said there is a small piece of metal that falls into place and it was worn and no longer holding the firing mechanism, which is why it fired on its own.  He flipped this piece over to the non-worn side and placed it back in the gun, and also told me it was soft metal which will wear out again.  This means at some time it will fire without the trigger being pulled, and I have no idea when.  
While researching the problem, I came across a review on Cabelas web site whereby another consumer reported the same problem.  I again notified Umarex that I considered this gun unsafe, I was not the only experiencing these problems, and was told they could not cover expenses for someone else to fix the gun and were aware of no other problems.  That is why I am contacting you in regards to this.  Note this is not a firearm, as no gunpowder is used, so ATF does not handle it.  
Here is the website for Cabelas, or you can go to their website, search for Ruger Air Hawk Elite and read the reviews.  http://www.cabelas.com/product/Ruger-Air-Hawk-Elite-Air-Rifle/742338.uts?Ntk=AllProducts&searchPath=%2Fcatalog%2Fsearch.cmd%3Fform_state%3DsearchForm%26N%3D0%26fsch%3Dtrue%26Ntk%3DAllProducts%26Ntt%3Druger%2Bair%26x%3D0%26y%3D0%26WTz_l%3DHeader%253BSearch-All%2BProducts&Ntt=ruger+air&WTz_l=Header%3BSearch-All+Products
Again, I consider this gun unsafe as it fires on its own, it is one of the most powerful air rifles available and think it should be recalled.  If their other guns have a similar design, they should also be recalled.
justification: The air rifle discharged multiple times without trigger pull, causing property damage and posing a severe injury risk, though no injury was reported.

incident_description:
I was driving my 2011 Polaris Ranger 800 XP UTV with my son and my wife as passengers.  This is a 3 seat UTV.  We were riding on the approved trails at approx. speeds of 20-30 MPH.  I purchased the unit new March 15, 2011,.  The factory warranty expired 09/15/11.  The UTV has about 30 hours and less than 200 miles on it after this day of riding.
While riding, I had to stop (3) three time because the seat was becoming hot on the passsenger side.  The seat is secured by two molded plastic tabs in the front on the bottom.  The heat caused the tabs to soften and bend.  The seat came loose while under operation which could have caused us to crash.  
Upon examination of the under side of the seat,  There is damage to the bottom molded plastic.  The securing plastic posts are canted because of heating up.  There is melted plastic on the bottom side of the molded plastic seat.  The seat will no longer properly and safely secure back in place.  
I took the UTV back to the dealer.  The machine was examined and found to be operating at normal temperature range.  The dealer/Owner [REDACTED]  at Motorsports Inc. in Hanover, PA indicated he had attended a Polaris seminar recently where Polaris made  changes to the 2012 Model year to include additional thicker heat shielding on the bottom of the molded plastic seat, replaced the plastic molded securing posts with metal posts, and installed a bracket under the center part of the seat for additional support.  He ordered the mentioned corrective upgrade parts feeling certain that Polaris would stand behind the upgrade parts.  Polaris refused to pay telling them it was out of warranty (by 10 days).  The dealeship suggested I contact POLARIS and express my safety concern directly.
I spoke with a [REDACTED] at Polaris Customer Service [REDACTED].  I conveyed her my assigned case # [REDACTED].  She put me on hold for about 15 minutes and returned to the phone and advised she reviewed the case and POLARIS would not cover the parts.  I conveyed my Safety Concern of a potential FIRE hazard but most imprtantly a LIFE SAFETY issue of the seat failing to stay secured while in motion due to the heat.  I conveyed to her the information the dealer had told me and showed me on the conversion/changes to correct the problem on the 2012 model.  She related that changes were nothing more than a model year change and had nothing to due with design or problem changes.  She further related the conversion parts WOULD NOT EVEN BE COVERED IF UNDER WARRANTY.
I am truly concern that this posses a potention Fire hazard as the plastic has melting.  More improtantly, this a a SEVERE Life Safety Hazard if and when the seat posts fail and come unsecured causing the seat to come loose.  
POLARIS should be held accountable to provide all owners with an upgrade kit to render their product safe.
justification: The seat became loose due to heat damage, posing a risk of crash but no actual injury occurred.

Once the breaks were applied the plastic seat post sheered off resulting in  the seat cushion to slide forward .  My wife was wearing a seat belt . incident_description: I have a New Balance 1800 treadmill that was purchased at Dick's Sporting Goods February 2006.  I am the original owner and the only operator of this treadmill.  In March 2011, I was on this treadmill at my residence.  The  treadmill suddenly sped up to full speed on its own.  I was thrown off the treadmill, hit my head and the tread burnt my legs and arm. I had pulled the emergency cord that is supposed to immediately stop the treadmill but the treadmill did not stop.  My husband got me off the treadmill and it faulted off.  I have contacted Fitness Quest, who is now "responsible" for New Balance treadmills, multiple times.  They claim that it is the motor control board, that they no longer manufacture, so the treadmill is non-repairable.  We had a past incident with this treadmill which will be described below, where we were told that the problem was the motor control board.  However, replacing the motor control board did not solve the problem and the technician left a new motor control board with us.  So, we replaced this supposedly broken motor control board with the one we had, and the treadmill still will not operate.  I told this to Fitness Quest but they continued to claim that there is nothing they can do for us.  The treadmill is 5 years old, purchased from Dick's Sporting goods and has been repaired at least 5 times in it's lifespan.  Prior incidents were just as dangerous (treadmill would suddenly stop when I changed the speed, would skip or just suddenly turn off) but I was fortunate to not experience injuries prior to this one.  The treadmill no longer runs.  The emergency switch not operating and these sudden large changes of speed and/or suddenly shutting off could cause very serious injuries.  I was fortunate that I had people to help me off the treadmill as the emergency shut-off failed.  The refusal of Fitness Quest to look further into this incident and/or fix the problem is suspicious.   I have the contact emails and the repair receipts for this treadmill. I do not want someone else to experience the same or worse injury due to this defective product.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries including head impact and burns, and the treadmill's recurring malfunctions indicate a high likelihood of recurrence.

I purchased new, a Schwinn 28" rimmed hybrid bicycle on June 17, 2011.  On  August 26th and 28th of 2011 Not having added any more air pressure to the tires. During a pull up sitting on the floor, the door opened and the ball catapulted and hit me square in the right eye.  I didn't even know it happened right away - it took me a minute to register something had even occurred.  It caused a broken  lower eye socket, a traumatic cataract, traumatic glaucoma, corneal damage and mydriasis.  I have undergone 2 surgeries, one an implant to correct the fracture, and one cataract removal and pupil cerclage.  I most likely will need to have glaucoma surgery and a corneal transplant. I am functioning well and can see decent since the surgery, but my eye is plagued by constant inflammation and general achiness.  It just isn't the same.  Partially user error and partially just a dangerous product.  I'm glad to hear this product was removed from shelves. I consider myself lucky to have vision in my eye still, but I definitely won't ever be the same.
justification: The incident resulted in severe eye injuries requiring multiple surgeries and potential future procedures, indicating a high severity level.

incident_description: My son [REDACTED], age 17, suffered a near fatal skull fracture and arterial bleed after getting struck on the left side of the head with a lacrosse ball. Although he was wearing a new Cascade Pro 7 helmet, the helmet failed to protect him.
justification: The incident involved a near fatal skull fracture and arterial bleed, indicating a life-threatening injury.

incident_description:
We were traveling 70 mph on Interstate 77 (in the mountains) and the bike rack (mounted in trailer hitch) pivoted towards the driver side of the vehicle.   The rack was loaded with four bikes and locked in with cable lock.  The bikes were drug approximately 500-1000 yards once we gained control of the vehicle and could pull over.  This was a serious and unsafe situation to be in.  The shoulder space on the side of a mountain is very limited.  We managed to pull the loaded rack into the upright position.   We then unlocked the bikes and removed one of the bikes hoping that less weight on the rack would alleviate the problem.  

We were traveling with another vehicle that had some space to transport the first bike we took of the rack.  Both vehicles were pulled over on the shoulder trying to get the situation resolved as quickly as possible.   As soon as we got back up to speed, the rack pivoted again and we were dragging three bikes until we could stop.

We pulled over for the second time and had no other option but to remove all remaining bikes off of the rack and strap them onto a fully packed truck bed.  In order to do this we had to remove the front wheels of the bikes and rearrange the cargo between the vehicles to accommodate the four bikes.  

I cannot stress enough how dangerous this entire situation was.  Semi Trailers and cars were passing us at 70 mph in the mountains as we had about 8 feet of shoulder space to work with.  We were on the side of the road twice strapping down bikes just to get to the nearest exit to assess the situation.  Not to mention we had to enter back onto the highway (twice) as quickly as possible for there was limited view points due to the winding interstate.  

We managed to strap down all four disassembled bikes in the back of a truck that was traveling with us.   The bikes where piled on top of cargo and was as tall as the cab.  Had we not had this additional vehicle and the additional straps to tie down the heap of bikes, we would have had to call for assistance and wait on the dangerous shoulder for an unknown amount of time to get our bikes into another vehicle.  We may have had to rent another vehicle to transport the bikes the 1,000 miles we needed to travel to get back home.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous situation with potential for injury due to the bike rack failure and limited shoulder space, but no actual injuries were reported.

incident_description: THE CONSUMER WAS SITTING ON A PIECE OF PLAYGROUND EQUIPMENT WHEN THE EQUIPMENT BROKE AND THE  CONSUMER FELL TO THE GROUND.
justification: The consumer fell from playground equipment, which typically results in injury.

justification: The incident resulted in injury (knocked out teeth), which corresponds to severity level 3. The likelihood is possible (3) given the nature of bumper car rides.

incident_description:
We have purchase an Adventure Playset a little more then a year ago. It was all installed correctly as per the instructions. However, we found that the "A" frame that extand from the fort and holds the swing set is starting to split and possibly will break which will cause and injury if a child is on it. I cannot find the manual so I cant give teh exact number.

incident_description:
Caller had purchased a thumb extender for use when riding his ATV.
Thumb Extender is meant to relieve fatigue on the thumb when giving gas to the ATV/Lessen pressure applied to throttle.
Caller had completed maintenance on his ATV, installed the thumb extender on 06/22/2011, completed check for proper positioning.
Took ATV for a test drive, when he pushed for fuel the ATV came up to a wheelie, the higher the wheelie the more pressure was applied to the throttle and the faster he ended up going.
He couldn't regain control of the ATV, crashed into trees, slammed face onto ATV, lost consciousness.
Caller estimates he was going about 25 - 30 miles when he hit the trees.
Thumb extender makes the throttle more sensitive, caller states that he has been riding ATV's for over twenty years and hasn't had an incident like this one until now.
Caller would like this product investigated and recalled before someone is injured very seriously or possibly suffers extreme loss.
justification: Caller lost consciousness and crashed into trees, indicating injury.

incident_description:
We bought an Artic Cat 366 in 2008 in West Virginia.   This Artic Cat has been nothing but problems.  First there were numerous problems with shifting into different gears.  We even bought an extended service plan, only to find out the place we bought the Artic Cat at by our home had a new owner and decided he was not going to service Artic Cat anymore.  We would then have to go up to at least Clarksburg, WV from Elkins, WV which was not an option at the time.

My sons drove this Artic Cat only for me to find out later it had flipped due to the fact they could not shift the gears going up a hill and God knows what else.

The Artic Cat seems to have more then numerous problems.  Leaking gas, now the starter is gone, solenoid, numerous problems not starting.  

I am just wondering if there are any other complaints on this particular model and if anything is being done about it.  Seems ridiculous to spend over $5,000.00 and can barely use the thing.
justification: The incident describes mechanical failures leading to a flip, but no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: I have Garden Treasures Hammock (Item #: 206254 |  Model #:SC-XHMK-NN) bought at Lowes in April 2010. On August 20, 2011 the stitching in the end seam of hammock bed came apart with my 7 year old son (weighs about 60 lbs) sitting on it and he fell. He was just sitting, not bouncing or jumping. It appears that the stitching is made from a thin cotton, non-durable tread. The tread was certainly not suitable for an outdoor product. It creates a very foreseeable safety/falling hazard. While my son only sustained minor bumps and bruises it could have been much worse had an adult been laying prone on the hammock. Customer reviews on Lowes website indicate this is a common problem. Your assistance in getting this hazardous product off the market is needed. Thank you [REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in minor injuries (bumps and bruises) to a child, and customer reviews indicate it is a common problem.

incident_description:
Caller purchased 26" bicycle in May 2011, weather has not permitted him to ride until recently.
On 07/27/2011 he and his wife decided to go bike riding, he got on the bike but before he rode 10 feet the bicycle fell apart broke into three pieces. 
The frame broke in half, front frame and forks and front wheel were second break and rear portion with frame & rear wheel were third piece.
Bicycle was assembled by Target Stores.
Callers left elbow and left lower leg hit pavement and he received abrasions, his wife administered first aid.
Caller states that the failure is somewhere in the front portion of the bicycle, that he hadn't gotten up to any speed in 10 feet but if someone were going faster due to the bicycle coming apart it would throw them forward with force and they could hit their head.

Caller contacted manufacturer on 07/27/2011, was referred to another office within their company, he called, left a message at that extension also on 07/27/2011, hasn't received return call yet.

Caller's wife has the same model bicycle, her bicycle did not fall apart but she only rode it for approximately 25 yards.
As quickly as his bike fell apart she got off of hers and they put them away for fear of injury.
Caller is reporting as a severe safety hazard with potential for great harm.
justification: The incident resulted in abrasions from the bicycle breaking apart, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is unlikely (2) as the wife's identical bicycle did not fail under similar use.

incident_description: My younger daughter was using an arm floating (wing water in both arms)  in the condo swimming pool, when suddenly for no reason it has torn itself (plastic material) and was no longer able to remain surrounding one of her arms. Fortunately we were very close to her and she was in a shallow part of the pool where she could stand up by herself. I can not imagine what would have happened if she was either away from us or in a location inside the pool that is not shallow. I still have the arm floating and have pictures from it as well on which I attached under this claim.
justification: The arm float tore but the child was unharmed due to proximity to parents and shallow water, indicating no injury occurred.

incident_description:
Wooden swing set was purchased 14 months prior to this 07-25-2011 report.
Set up around May 2010 but within 3 to 4 weeks after being set up callers noticed that the screws were loosening, boards were becoming warped.
Two children have played on this set; neither is at their grandparentÃÂs home all the time.
Granddaughter is 1 1/2yrs old and now weighs around 25 lbs, the grandson is 4 1/2 and weighs around 45 lbs.
Over the past year although screws have been tightened multiple times they continue to loosen and the boards keep warping.
Boards that are warping are the legs to the set and the worst is the main top beam which is supposed to be a 2 x 4 but is believed to be smaller.  (Has not been measured)
Caller is reporting that this swing set is a very dangerous swing set, his grandchildren are small but if purchasers had larger children they could become harmed very badly.
He doesn't believe that it is safe for his grandchildren as small as they are and would very much like to either be reimbursed or have this swingset replaced by a stronger, safer swingset at manufacturer expense.
justification: The swing set has structural issues like loosening screws and warped boards, but no injuries have been reported yet.

incident_description: my 18 month old son was riding his radio flyer scoot'n zoom scooter on our hardwood floors in our home. He went to turn he flipped over the front of the scooter and cut his frenulum(the piece of skin between the lip and gum).  He landed straight down on his mouth. It also looks as if one tooth got chipped but is very minor.
justification: The child suffered a cut to the frenulum and a minor chipped tooth, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: After aquiring an almost new Litespeed "Veneto", a high-end titanium road bike manufactered between 2003 and 2004 by the Litespeed bicycle company, a subsidiary of the American bicycle Group, I crested a climb during a ride and began a decent to find the bike  shaking uncontrollably in the front end. The wobble increased with speed causing me to hit a riderÃÂs rear wheel resulting in the other rider falling while I tried to regain control. After the incident, I tested the bike to find that whenever it exceeds  approximately 26 mph, the frontend begins to shake and vibrate due to a design flaw. To find out whether my bike was a peculiarity, I began a query of other Litespeed Vento owners and found that there bike's have responded in the same manner whenever accelerated beyond a specific point resulting, in some instances, in crashes and injury.  Incidents are reported on bicylce blog pages and through local bike shops.  As a result of the bike instability, I have fallen twice resulting in minor cuts and scratches and a sprained wrist.
justification: The incident resulted in minor injuries (cuts, scratches, and a sprained wrist) and other riders have also experienced crashes and injuries due to the bike's design flaw.

incident_description: I purchased my 2004 Polaris sportsman 700 twin EFI brand new in september 2004, one year later I had a fuel leak, the fuel line was rubbing on the frame and wore a hole in the gas line, I called the dealer and they said just to put a metal inline fuel filter where it was rubbing on the rubber hose, I did and that solved that problem. Next about two years after purchase I was out hunting and my fuel gauge started to flicker and then disappeared, my atv then started to spit and sputter then died on me. I sat on the hill for 20 minutes and then tried to start the atv and it started, that was the start of a long 5 years with this machine. it would run fine than it would act like it was starving for fuel then it would die on me, Id pull off the gas cap and the fuel acted like it was boiling. it done this for 5 years, i took it to the repair shop and they said that I needed a new fuel pump and fuel regulator assembly $500-$600 they replaced it and said that the ECM (Computer) was heating up extremely bad I have searched on the internet for fix solutions for my atv  and Ive seen hundreds of posts reading that they have experienced the same problems with their 2004 Polaris sportsman 700 twin EFI atv. and some of those experiencing these problems happened weeks to only a few months after purchase. My wife was riding our 2004 Polaris sportsman 700 twin EFI  up a hill and it started to spit and sputter and died on her while she was climbing the hill on a forest service approved trail. when the atv died on her she started rolling backwards and the atv turned sideways going down hill it didnt roll onto her, she was able to jump off but the atv tipped on its side. My wife could have been seriously injured or worse because of this fuel pump/ECM problem that not only me but hundreds maybe even thousands of people have experienced the same exact thing. Ive sent Polaris industries some messages and Ive never gotten a response back from them on this issue I love my machine its paid for and I cant even sell because if the issues it has because Id hate for someone else to get hurt because of it I paid almost $9500 for this 2004 Polaris sportsman 700 twin EFI  and the problems arrised after the warranty expired so now im stuck with a potential death trap that I want to go out and enjoy once again.
justification: The incident involved a near-miss with potential for serious injury or death due to a known mechanical failure, and similar issues are widely reported.

incident_description:
Caller purchased her Durango Swing Set about four years ago, she noticed that the set was not as stable as it should be just two years later.

In  2009 caller's granddaughter who was then four years old was swinging when the frame began falling and she fell off the swing.

Caller noticed frame was continuing to fall, ran to get her granddaughter and moved her.

The frame fell, caller examined and saw that the wood frame had rotted in more than one or two places.

The recalls on this swing would not cover the damage since they are replacing only the plastic pieces not the wood.

Caller would like for the manufacturer to reimburse her with some sort of compensation siting that she paid a very large price for this swing set, believed it would last longer than the metal one's and would also be cosmetically attractive.

Caller purchased the swing set for her child and her grandchild, they used it for a very short time compared to the price paid.
justification: The granddaughter fell off the swing when the frame began falling, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description: My 6 year old son was riding his A3 kick Razor Scooter outside my parents condo (with his grandmother watching) in Murrells Inlet, South Carolina.   While he was holding the handlebars he accidentally hit one of the spring loaded buttons on the handle bars.  The handle bar came off and he fell and hit his right elbow on the cement.  He was taken to his pediatrician and an xray found that there was a fracture in his elbow.  He ended up with a cast from his hand up to his armpit for 3 weeks.   My concern is that the handlebars should not be designed where a 6 year old can accidentally push the button while riding and make the handle bars fall off.   The buttons are VERY easy to push in and now that this happened it is very easy for me to see how it could.  I do not see how this is safe.  This scooter is designed for children over 5 and should be manufactured accordingly.
justification: The incident resulted in a fractured elbow requiring a cast, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The description indicates the buttons are very easy to push, suggesting a high likelihood of recurrence (likelihood 4).

incident_description:
Durango or Duarngo 2 playset already has recalls for weak support structure (monkey bars and vertical posts in main structure) but I am not sure this addresses another issue.  The shear strength of the main structure is dependent on the screws going though multiple horizontal 1"x4" uncoated wood pieces into the coated vertical 2x4's.  The 1x4's have holes pre-drilled in them very near their ends and the shear stresses on the set (from someone climbing the angled ladder, for instance) cause the end grain of the 1x4's to tear out (the holes turn from an "o" to a "c").  The 1x4's then can slide sideways under the screws and the entire structure can lean to the side.  

No injuries from this in this case, mainly because the swingset has been "off limits" for some time. 

This swingset also has a broken coated 2x4 support for the monkey bars (i.e. one of the vertical portions of the ladder).

I have ordered the monkey bar and vertical supports replacement kits.
justification: The swingset has structural issues causing potential failure, but no injuries occurred as it was off limits.

I am just grateful they were not on it when this happened.  It did not look right one day and the next it looked like this. I am very happy I did not allow them on it the day I noticed it looking a bit off.  My daughter tried to talk to someone at phone # 1-800-248-5327 but they are saying it is not the one that has been recalled. Look at the photos, they are the same.

incident_description: I have a 2011 Polaris Sportsman 850xp ATV.  It is 4 months old with 20 hours of riding time.  I have found that with normal riding, oil will be pushed out of the engine into the air box.  If not cleaned up it will fill the air box and could end up on the hot engine causing a fire.

justification: The steering failure is described as potentially deadly, indicating a high severity risk, but no actual incident or injury is reported.

incident_description: One of my grandsons, 7 years old, was playing on the Tacoma swing set model 1AP051-07 in our yard, while traversing the overhead ladder one of the rungs broke, causing him to fall and the broken sharp piece fell on him causing a minor laceration to his right cheek.  The overhead ladder part consists of several wooden rungs about 1" diameter set horizontally, and perpendicular to the plastic-covered horizontal 2X4 pieces.  I am further concerned because the ladder to the "fort" part of the set consists of similar 1" diameter wooden rungs, and if one breaks while one of our 11 grandchildren is climbing it, injuries are likely.  I examined the broken run and it clearly has rotted in the inside of it.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor laceration, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is high (4) due to visible rot in the wooden rungs and frequent use by multiple grandchildren.

incident_description:
While riding the bicycle on a sidewalk for approximately 25 minutes he noticed that the left pedal  wobbly and within a matter of seconds it detached itself from the bicycle and fell off.  

He took the bike back into the retailer on the same date and was given another bike (same model number and color) as an exchange.  

On 7/14/2011 while riding the bicycle  for approximately an hour the left pedal began to wobble. He hopped of the bicycle and the left pedal fell off. He tried to attach the pedal  to the bicycle but was not able to do so. 
He has not contacted the firm and or the retailer but plans to return the bicycle to the retailer.
justification: The incident involved a mechanical failure (pedal detachment) but no injury was reported, only inconvenience.

incident_description:
I purchased a new 2011 Polaris Ranger 800 XP on 7/30/2011. My wife and I rode the UTV around our neighborhood for about 30 minutes that day at slow speeds. The floorbed and inside of the passenger compartment got extremely hot. My wife was wearing flip flops and could not keep her feet on the floor because of the heat. I was wearing a pair of Crocs and it was extremely uncomfortable to try to operate the accelerator. I changed to close toed shoes and it was tolerable. There was an extreme amount of heat coming from the front of the vehicle where the radiator and fan are located. The fan was blowing hot air through holes in the front of the passenger compartment.

The vertical wall of the passenger compartment below the seat was so hot I could not hold my hand on the surface.

The sales personnel at the dealership did not advise of any heat related issues. The Operations Manual does not mention any issues related to high levels of heat inside of the passenger compartment. There are no warning signs / labels inside the passenger compartment indicating potential heat issues.

We checked the internet on Sunday, 7/31/2011, and found that there were quite a few reports of excessive heat inside of the passenger compartment of the Polaris Ranger 800. 

I registered a complaint with Polaris on 7/31/2011 and all they did was refer me back to the dealership. They indicated that the dealer was the most knowledgeable to address the issue which sounds absolutely unbelievable. Are you kidding me? I find it hard to believe that the manufacturer of a product with a manufacturing defect would say the dealer is more knowledgeable than the manufacturer of the product. Polaris did not even indicate that there was a potential heat issue or how to solve it.
justification: The incident describes discomfort and potential safety hazards due to excessive heat, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: I purchased an INTEX 18x52 ultra deluxe salt water  metal frame pool which came with pool, ladder, hoses, pump, etc. on 05-08-2010. The ladder provided with the pool was correctly assembled and put to use in the saltwater pool. One June 8th, 2011 my wife and I were in the pool. When my wife attempted to get out of the pool, the ladder  collapsed on one of the legs. Luckily, my wife only suffered a small cut and bruising on her leg. After much effort, I was finally able to get out of the pool myself by climbing over the wall of pool. I had to get a step ladder out of my shed in order to get my wife out of the pool. Upon inspection the pool ladder, it was determined the ladder had completely rusted through at one of the connection sleeves, causing the ladder to collapse. I contacted INTEX to advise of the incident in an attempt to prevent injuries and possible death to other consumers. If a child or adult were standing near the  top of ladder during collapse, it could be fatal. I advised INTEX the metal ladder did not appear to be salt water resistant. It appears this is the same ladder and the same metal constuction used on the ladders provided with non-salt water pools. INTEX simply advised they appreciated the call, but the ladder was not under warranty. It appeas they have no intention of recalling the ladder, or changing the design. I am not writing to complain about the warranty issue, but out of concern that the ladder they are selling is not designed for use in saltwater and could cause serious injury or death. I still have the ladder in my possesion and offered to have INTEX inspect the ladder. The offer was declined.
justification: The incident resulted in a small cut and bruising, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) due to the ladder's rusting issue in saltwater environments, which could affect many users.

incident_description:
a nine-year old boy was playing on the "Spring Across Bridge," manufactured by Landscape Structures Incorporated, when he fell. The Spring Across Bridge has thick metal coils that are connected to several relatively narrow metal beams, causing the Bridge to toggle back and forth in different areas when children walk or run along it. There is no housing unit or covering in place where the round coil meets the square beam, leaving the four metal corners of each beam exposed. This appears to be the intentional design of Landscape Structures, rather than an alteration by a user or consumer, although this is not certain.
When the nine year old boy fell, his shin hit the exposed upper corners of the metal beam, causing a large V-shaped
laceration. one of the arms of the "V" was approximately 4 centimeters long and the other arm was about 3
centimeters long. The laceration was so deep, a chunk of flesh and muscle tissue was torn off.
justification: The boy suffered a deep laceration with tissue damage, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description: 11 year old daughter suffered a laceration on her right ankle from the rear bolt on the housing cover for the chain.  Four stiches were required to suture the area.  The bolt is not covered in plastic or some other protective wrap.
justification: The incident resulted in a laceration requiring stitches, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: On August 19th, 2010, the second day of school, my 9-yr old daughter was playing right at the start of recess and ended up getting KILLED! She was playing on a new peice of equipment called the X-Wave and when she was at the highest point she fell off, almost right under it. As she tried to get up this heavy peice of equipment came down and hit her on the head with enough force to kill her almost. She didn't even have a chance to get out of the way of this very dangerous peice of equipment before it came down and hit her, killing her. School was her most favorite thing and she ended up being killed there. I just don't want this happening to another child and family.
justification: The incident resulted in the death of a child, which is the highest severity level.

incident_description: My 13 yr old son was riding his Ezip 400 electric scooter when the throttle stuck in the fast position. The only way to stop the scooter was to shut off the master power. The way the scooter is designed to work is if you let go of the throttle the motor will disengage and the scooter will slow to a stop. I contacted the company Currie Industries and their primary concern was had my son dropped or crashed his scooter previously. Once I told them that he had not they agreed to ship me the necessary parts to fix the scooter but were going to charge me shipping and handling on the parts. The scooter was still within the 90 day warranty. I refused the new parts and the shipping and handling and returned the scooter to Walmart where I purchased it.
justification: The throttle malfunction caused an incident but no injury occurred, and the scooter was safely stopped by turning off the power.

incident_description: [REDACTED] Caller stated that the play set was built with laminated 2X4's not 4X4's. The consumer stated that he has owned the product. The consumer emailed the firm this morning asking what he should do about reimbursement, or refund for his product but has not gotten a response. The consumer has yet to call the retailer. The consumer stated that the wood is cracking creating a fall and stability hazard. The consumer stated that his children have not been harmed by the product. The play set appears to show no fading in the wood.
justification: The play set has a stability hazard but no injuries have occurred yet.

incident_description:
This is regarding the ladder bars of the Durango swingset produced by Adventure Playsets, of Amarillo, Texas which you issued a recall Nov 2009.  My daughter has one of these, purchased around 2006.  While my daughter had several friends over for her 6th birthday, and while both swings and the glider were occupied, the wood for one of the ladder bars broke under the combined weight.  The swingset did not fail completely since the plastic coating held things together.  There were no injuries and we made sure nobody used the swingset.

I later noticed small mushrooms growing out of the holes in the plastic of the ladder bars. I determined the ladder bars were of a poor design, the plastic was as effective at keeping water in, rotting the wood as it was at keeping it out.

I did not know of any recall for the product, nor did I think of reporting this to the company or the CPSC.  I replaced the rotted ladder bars with weather resistant lumber which I cut and drilled to match the old ladder bars.

[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
justification: The ladder bar broke but the swingset did not fail completely and there were no injuries.

incident_description: The consumer says as he was riding the ATV, the voltage regulator keeps charging the battery.  The battery expands like it is going to explode.  The consumer says the battery leaks acid out on the roads.  After he turns the ATV off, the battery hums for about 15 minutes while it is off.  The consumer says he fears he may burn himself with the battery acid.  There is also a sulphur scent that the battery gives off.  The consumer fears someone will be hurt by this.  He says the same thing happened to his brother, almost a year prior to his incident.  The consumer contacted the manufacturer who gave him a case [REDACTED] and was told that there is no need for a recall, they put out a bulletin at the dealerships but did not notify the customers directly.  The consumer feels there is a chance that a battery could explode on somebody.  The consumer says he rides slow and does not go as fast as other people.  The consumer says it only has 1,408 miles on it and 88 hours.  The consumer says the rep with the dealer did mention that most ATV riders work on their own vehicles making it difficult for customers to be aware of the [Warranty and Service Bulletins] at the dealer.  The consumer says the voltage regulator is causing the problem but the safety concern is the battery.
justification: The incident involves a battery leaking acid and potential explosion risk, posing a clear safety hazard, though no injury is reported yet. The recurrence with the consumer's brother suggests the issue is not isolated, increasing likelihood.

incident_description: I purchased a Tailwind scooter from Menards at Christmastime and not long after the kids started using it, the foot brake at the end of the scooter broke off--leaving a sharp metal edge exposed at the back of the scooter--VERY dangerous. I exchanged the scooter and the new one did the same thing. I am SHOCKED that this scooter hasn't been recalled.
justification: The incident describes a dangerous defect (sharp metal edge) but no injury was reported, indicating a severity level of 2. The issue occurred twice, suggesting a likelihood of 4 (likely).

incident_description: On July 18. 2011, my 13 year old son fell completely through the safety net enclosure of our Sportspower 14 foot trampoline, and as a result hit his head on a cement wall. We have owned this trampoline for less than 1 year and live in California, so it has not even seen a full summer or any extreme weather. Since this happened, I researched online and have seen numerous reports of the netting ripping on this brand of trampoline. We owned a different brand of trampoline and enclosure and had it for over 3 years in Colorado without ever having a single rip or tear in the netting. This product is a safety hazard and should be recalled.
justification: The incident resulted in a head injury from falling through the safety net, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to multiple reports of netting rips with this brand.

incident_description:
On 06/26 ConsumerÃÂs grand children were jumping on the trampoline when the roof collapsed on them hitting up her younger grandchild.  Consumer stated that no medical attention was required for her one year old grandchild.
