incident_description: Honda Rancher AT [REDACTED] ATV will sometimes get caught in between gears and not shift up/down. Rocking ATV will not "jar" it into gear. Owners manual does not specifically address the situation. Only remedy is to turn the machine off/on and then try shifting into neutral for a restart. If ATV must be stopped on an incline this causes an unsafe condition having to maintain position on an incline while simultaneously turning machine off/on and attempting restart and then shifting. Honda Corporate states that unless the machine is stopped in first gear this situation may occur and there is nothing they can do about it. Stopping in first gear is not always possible/practical especially when traversing inclines. Honda Corporate refuses to provide any documentation to this effect or to our numerous conversations stating that all correspondence is for internal use only. Potential for loss of control and/or uncontrolled descent and rollover of vehicle and passengers on an incline is a distinct possiblity.
justification: The ATV's gear shifting issue creates an unsafe condition with potential for loss of control, especially on inclines, but no actual injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
I've tried contacting the company, but I'm not sure if I have a good e-mail address for them. I sent this to info@digginactive.com regarding a Skuut push bike:

We have a Skuut bike that we bought new about 4 yrs ago. Yesterday our 3 yo daughter was riding, and the entire front wheel+steering assembly separated from the rest of the bike, and she took a pretty good spill. Fortunately, she just has a couple of skinned knees.
This part of the bike is held in place essentially by a single screw at the very front of the bike. Years of use combined with the natural expansion, contraction, and flex of a wood product caused this screw to work loose. Of course nothing lasts forever, but I (and my 3yo) did not expect such a sudden and catastrophic failure as the bike breaking in two!

Repairing the bike would be relatively simple, but I would not put faith in the product again. I view this as a design flaw and hope you might consider a remedy. In retrospect, I should have purchased a metal framed push bike and I will make this recommendation to fellow parents.
justification: The incident resulted in a 3-year-old child sustaining skinned knees from a sudden bike failure, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is unlikely (2) as it involves a specific design flaw after years of use.

incident_description:
Brand of item:                           Allan Sports

Model:                                      103DB Trunk Mounted Bicycle Carrier 
                                                 "Deluxe Three Bike Trunk Mounted Carrier"

Car that rack was mounted on: 1994 Mercury Grand Marquis

Number of bikes carried: 3
Position and weight of bikes: Bike closest to car's trunk------------37.0 lbs
                                              Bike in rack's center position---------33.4 lbs
                                              Bike furthest from trunk lid/bumper---25.4 lbs
Place of purchase/Price: Walmart in Columbia, MD/ $50.0

Incident: The bike rack collapsed while transporting the three bikes. My speed was ~15mph. It collapsed when I hit a slight pot hole in the road. The pot hole was not excessive and was in line with what one occasionally finds while driving. The rack was installed on the car per the manufacturer's directions. The top straps were connected to the metal edge of the trunk (where it meets the rear window). The lower straps were connected to the metal frame support below the bumper. The "arms" which held the three bikes were horizontal. All straps were very taunt. The rack comes pre-assembled right out of the box. The only thing the consumer has to do is to snap the two chromed "tension bars" into holes in the bike frame. The two "tension bars" expand the frame and hold it open much like the horizontal bar in the letter "A". When I hit the bump in the road the two "tension bars" slid/pulled back out of the holes in the frame, causing the frame to collapse. I stopped the car, and after removing the bikes was able to snap the "tension bars" back into place. After snapping the "tension bars" back in place, I inspected the straps and found them to be very taunt. The max allowable weight for three bikes on this rack is 100 lbs. My bikes weigh 95.8 lbs (total). In a static situation this bike rack appears very sturdy, but it can collapse when subjected to an impact load due to a bump in the road. Had my situation happened on a highway, I might not have been able to stop prior to losing the bikes. Someone could have been killed. The impact may have been made more severe due to the Grand Marquis having such a long wheel base and the long distance from it's rear tires to the end of it's trunk. Please investigate this design and ensure that it is redesigned and then qualification tested for typical impact loading due to road conditions.
justification: The incident involved a bike rack collapse without injury, but with potential for severe consequences under different circumstances.

incident_description:

My 3-year old son was playing near the tee on our back patio when I went inside for a couple minutes to help my 5-year old son get his swimsuit off.  I came right back outside to hang his swimsuit and in that short time my 3-year had the tether cord wrapped tight around his neck.  He managed to get his leg caught too, further tightening the cord.  I couldn't remove the cord from his neck without freeing his leg first.  
He is fine now, because I came out of the house so fast.  I don't believe he could have freed himself from the cord.  
This product says it is for 3 years+ which should be fine considering the t-ball age is typically 3-5 years, but I believe it is very, very dangerous for younger kids.
justification: The child was unharmed but the incident could have been severe if not for quick intervention, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence without changes.

incident_description:
I have just experienced my second unexplained sidewall blowout with Continental's "Grand Prix 4000 S" road bicycle tires.  Obviously these are not just a "recreational product", as they are used at high speeds and in traffic, so this is a serious safety issue.  There are no signs of cutting where either tire has blown out; the sidewall casing appears to have simply pulled itself apart, leaving a ragged hole.

There is a little more to this than just 2 tire failures.  "Once upon a time", probably 3-4 years ago, these were great, reliable tires.  More recently, all of the stock I have bought in the USA and elsewhere has, after short periods of use, started having threads dangling out of the sidewall near the tire bead, shown signs of rubber cracking where one would expect it on maybe 10-year-old tires, etc.
justification: The description reports tire blowouts at high speeds, which could lead to accidents, but no actual injuries or deaths are mentioned.

He again insisted we couldn't have a copy of the report or even the name of the person who witnessed and wrote the report. My anger is with the fact that not knowing what unsafe condition caused my grandson's cut they continued to allow children into this activity. The general manager via phone was completely indifferent to the fact that a child was injured. He seemed to only care about his liability.

My grandson is visiting from Colorado and as grandparents we wanted to make sure we took care of this incident in the right way. His cut appears to be healing ok at this time but I don't want to see any other child hurt. I want to make them accountable for the safety of their visitors. I also don't believe they have procedures in place to address any accidents that happen on their property. I would appreciate knowing this facility is going to be inspected so that any unsafe condition will be corrected. The attitude of the staff was cavalier and does not give me confidence they will even try to determine the cause of my grandson's injury. The activity was a 3 story slide, webcrawl with bridges and foam balls. There were metal bolts exposed that may have accounted for my grandson's cut.
 
Please feel free to contact me by email or phone.

Fortunately, the child sustained only abrasions to the knee.  

I have pictures of the scooter, the sheared metal and the damage to his knee.
Please contact if necessary.

[REDACTED]
justification: The child sustained abrasions to the knee, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The incident involved a mechanical failure, which is possible but not highly frequent (occurrence likelihood 3).

incident_description: I was riding my Jamis Eclipse bike that came new with an Eason EC90 offset seat post , when I heard a pop and my bike seat fell off. After getting up injured, I looked at the seat to find that the bolt that holds on the seat had SNAPPED!  I realize the Easton EC90 Zero seat post has been recalled , but not for the bolt. ( The clamp fails).  I called Easton and they will send another / replacement bolt. I asked if they were made in China. They said , yes, either China or Thaiwan. I will find a grade 8 bolt made in the US to replace the broken one with. I don't like dragging my flesh on road cinders!. I also asked Easton who pays to have my rear wheel fixed, and they said they don't pay for damage done during a crash.
justification: The rider was injured when the bike seat fell off due to a snapped bolt, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as the issue is known but not widespread.

incident_description:
Regarding: Product #18595 - Banzai Spray 'N Splash Giraffe Pool, Manufactured in China for ToyQuest of Los Angeles, CA and purchased from Toys-R-Us on May 8, 2011.

1. This pool has an inflatable giraffe's head that when connected to a hose is supposed to remain erect and provide a gentle spray for the user(s). However, it cannot be hooked up to a hose as designed; too little water pressure and the head will not stand, enough pressure to maintain support creates too fine and painful (ultimately harmful) a spray for even an adult. 

2. The pool also has an inflatable slide that is supposed to be held down (inside of pool only) by two plastic anchors on the bottom of the pool via tying down with two provided pieces of rope (string). However, even with the pool filled with water, the inflated (I tried varying pressures) ladder pulls up the bottom and floats, causing it to bob and sway even while being climbed upon by my 30+lb boys making it far too unstable for even supervised use without the risk of injury.


It is my sincere belief that this product is unsafe as designed and will eventually result in a sever injury to someone's child.
justification: The product design flaws pose a risk of injury due to unstable ladder and painful water spray, but no actual injury is reported yet.

incident_description: We purchased an Intex Ultra Frame 16' x 48" above ground pool and set it up in our back yard.  We have 3 small children (ages 5, 4, and 2) and have been extremely cautious about pool safety.  However, today we noticed our 2 year old standing on the restraining belt that goes around the outside of the pool.  While standing on this belt he was high enough to fall into the pool.  We understand this belt is necessary for the stability of the pool, but many parents of small or older children may not be aware of the potentially dangerous situation of children accidentally falling in the pool if they climb on this belt.  We just wanted to make you aware of the situation.  We contacted Intex Corp. and informed them of this potential safety hazard and they informed us to keep children away from the pool unsupervised.  We told them we don't leave our children unsupervised, but other consumers may not be as vigilant as we are.  Thank you for your time.
justification: The incident describes a potential safety hazard where a child could fall into the pool, but no actual injury or incident occurred.

incident_description:
I bought a Coleman power chill iceless 12-volt cooler model #5644 on Jan. 21, 2011 at Wal-mart in Poway CA.  This model plugs into a cigarette lighter or to a 120V AC power supply.  I have use the unit for the past six months while camping.  I pluged in in using the cigarette liter in my 34' ft motor home.  With in a short time and not realizing it the plug started to melt and over heat.  Fortunately we found it before it started a fire in the motorhome.  The plug was too hot to touch and the plastic was melting.  The fuse is in the cigarette plug and it did not cut the power.  I tried it again using the AC power adapter and again the plug became red hot.  Needless to say we stopped using the unit right away.  I receive a burn to my fingers.

I look up simular complaints on the internet and found many people are having the same experence.  In some cases they sent the unit still under warranty back to Coleman and they repaired it only to have the same problem again.  Coleman wants me to send the parts back to them so they can send out new ones and I can repair it.  I told them with all the complaints I have seen on the internet that I am no longe confident the product is safe, not only from electrical shock but fire hazard.  It appears Coleman is doing nothing to correct the problem other then giving the consumer new replacement parts that are still defective.  

When I tried to return the cooler to the store it was past there 90 day return policy, but was told that they are receiving about one a week in returns.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury and a near fire hazard, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to multiple similar complaints and frequent returns.

incident_description: Two incidents recently with our Parkside trampoline.  (1)  My daughter broke her leg when she hit one of the metal safety poles (the netting had become too loose/stretched, which allowed her to fall into the metal pole).  (2)  The fabric (jumping part) of the trampoline split in two while my son (77 pounds) was jumping on it, but fortunately he was not hurt.  We have had the trampoline for three years, used it somewhat regularly and always in the manner for which it was intended.  The trampoline was never abused.
justification: The incident resulted in a broken leg (severity 3) and a non-injury incident (severity 2), with two occurrences in three years of regular use.

incident_description:
The product is:  Banzai Battle Blast Sting Ray.  It is a pool play toy.  Manufacturer is Toyquest Product number seems to be 01452.  Los Angeles Ca 90064.  Their website is www.toyquest.com.

It is a floating toy upon which the child can sit.  It has a central hole through which you pass a water tube to drawn water into a water pistol.  My 8 year old put his arm through the hole and could not remove it.  I had to help him extract his arm.  I can easily foresee that the float would flip over and the child would be stuck underneath unable to remove his arm and would drown.  

I believe that the toy WILL result in drowning of some children.  I urge to to act before such an incident occurs and recall the toy.  

[REDACTED], MD, FACP, FASN
justification: The description indicates a potential drowning hazard, which could lead to death, and the likelihood is considered high due to the toy's design flaw.

incident_description: Hello there, thank you for taking the time to read this. I bought a black rubber inner tube made for recreational use from Orschelns in Marysville, KS. That same day, I used the tube on a float trip and shortly into the float the backs of my legs started to burn. By the end of the day the backs of my legs, arms and back, anywhere that the tube had touched were bright red and felt like a really bad sunburn. I'm not allergic to rubber, it wasn't from the rubber getting hot, wasn't chafing, it was definitely some kind of reaction or chemical burn from something on or in the rubber. The sack the tube came sealed in has an obnoxious smelling florecent yellow powder on the inside of it. I have contacted the place I purchased the tube, as well as the distributer. Neither has had anyone else make this complaint. I'm waiting to hear back from the distributer who is going to contact the manufacturer in China and share the pictures with them that I sent. I just don't want this to happen to anyone else.
justification: The description indicates a chemical burn or reaction resulting in injury (bright red skin, severe burning sensation), but no death or life-threatening condition is mentioned.

incident_description: The consumer says he smelled gas the first time he used it.  It was so bad he took the passenger seat out and he could see gas leaking out of the tank.  the consumer says it looks like when they melded the mounting surface into the tank it was not melded good enough and that is where it leaks.  The consumer contacted the manufacturer and said they would look into it.  Consumer has product similar to Alert #08-521.
justification: Gas leak was reported but no injury occurred; the issue is likely to recur given the manufacturing defect described.

incident_description:
Product: CycleAware Reflex Mirror
ManufacturerÃÂs website: http://www.cycleaware.com/

The Reflex mirror attaches to the side of a bicycle helmet. In part, a bicycle helmet protects the wearer's head by distributing impact forces across as large an area as possible. The Reflex's attachment device is made of sturdy plastic and stands out from the helmet by about 3/4 inch.
If the attachment device hits the ground, it concentrates impact force onto an area about the size of quarter.

This is not merely theoretical. Examination of my helmet makes it completely obvious that the Reflex's attachment device serves to concentrate the impact force. I did have a concussion. Although it cannot be proven, I believe that I would not have had the concussion without the mirror.

Upon request, I can provide a photo of the helmet.
justification: The incident resulted in a concussion, which qualifies as an injury, and the description suggests the mirror's design contributed to the injury.

incident_description: My daughter was riding a Razor Pocket Mod Daisy electric scooter (item # 15130610) when the steering locked up causing her to lose control and be injured (bruised chest, shoulder, and sprained wrist).
justification: The incident resulted in injuries (bruised chest, shoulder, and sprained wrist), warranting a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is set to 3 (possible) based on the provided frequency data (58 of 127).

incident_description: I purchased a wicker hanging swing that attaches to a metal base from Pier 1 Imports.  I sat down on the swing and the base lifted up off my cement patio floor and flung me out into my yard injuring my fingers on my left hand, both wrists and my right ankle.  My husband thought maybe I had sat down on the edge and that is why the incident happened so we tested it again.  Even if I was sitting all the way on the seat, if I moved at all, the base lifted off the patio and again started to tip.  Fortunately, my husband was there to catch it before I once again was propelled out into my yard.  Then my husband tried and it and it started happening to him too.  We decided since we have a variety of poeple over to our house during the summer and could not always be standing by the swing to catch it from tipping over when someone would attempt to sit in it, we returned it to Pier 1 Imports for a full refund.  Even though the staff there told us that they have never had a report like this from a customer, we felt it should be reported to someone for inspection or recall.  My husband and I are both average size people and don't know why this particular product would not stay on the patio floor when someone is attempting to sit on it or moving it slightly while in it.  It could be the base was defective.  We just wanted someone to know.  Thanks.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries to fingers, wrists, and ankle, and the swing's instability was consistently reproducible, indicating a likely occurrence for others.

incident_description: On the morning of May 10,2011 I went for a bike ride ,while going down hill the front of the bike began to shake the front forks lost integrity and I crashed into the road sustaining a facial fracture.
justification: The incident resulted in a facial fracture, which is classified as an injury.

incident_description: I put my 13 month old daughter in the My sunshine Baby Buggy Float.If she moved in the anyway it woulld pitch her forward face down towards the water.I was even holding on to it.When she would try to touch the water or even adjust herself it started to flip over.The seat portion of the float it a flat area.It doesn't give a very good supoort for the child.It cause the whole float to be unstable.
justification: The float is unstable and could pitch the child face down into the water, posing a risk of drowning, but no injury or death occurred in this instance.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that while her 3 1/2 year old was in the swingin motion it broke apart which dispersed her son distance away into a fence he fell out onto his head and back which caused  injury to his spines, neck and the top of his head.  The child was seen was by a physician the following day where he was examined and treated for his injuries at the Urgent Care [REDACTED].


Consumer is concerned that this product could have caused fatality and feels that this should be investigated.
justification: The child suffered injuries to the spine, neck, and head, requiring medical treatment, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) based on the description of the incident and the concern raised about potential fatality.

incident_description: On approx Dec 23rd, 2010, I purchased a boys Next brand, Surge model bicycle for my 5-year old son. Since he has owned this bicycle, he has had numerous problems with it. Most of which, has caused him to have minor to serious bicycle accidents. The right pedal has come off & will not stay tightened & the thread has now been stripped. We had to use a pedal from a neighbor's old bike so that my son may ride his bike again. The handle bars will not stay straight & frequently come loose & cause my son to lose control & not be able to steer properly. This incident has happened more than 3 times & the last time was on June 2nd, 2011. The handle-bars came loose, twisted to the side & caused my son to wreck badly. He landed face first into the concrete, he had a bloody nose, cuts on the top of his nose, loosened a tooth, knocked a second tooth out, scraped both elbows & knees, busted his top lip, cuts on his chin, cuts on the inside of his nose, rubber burns on the back of his legs from the handlebars. The seat will not stay straight as my son is riding it, even when the seat is tightly fastened. This also has caused many minor accidents as well.
justification: The incident resulted in multiple injuries including a bloody nose, cuts, and a knocked-out tooth, indicating a severity level of 3. The repeated occurrences of handlebar and pedal failures suggest a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: Summer Escapes polly pool 5ft diameter Blue hard plastic with slide and steps. about 1ft deep. It has a drain plug that is near the steps made of hard plastic. We had bought one and exchanged due to drain popping out when you step on the stairs, We took the pool back and exchanged for a new one. The new pool(exact same pool) does the same thing when you step on the stairs the drain plug pops out. It is about 1" in diameter. My 3yr old was playing in the pool and was choking severly on the plastic drain plug...... I contacted the manufacturer they said yes it is a choking hazard to send and email if I was concerned I asked to speak to a superviser and they hung up on me. I will be returning this to walmart.
justification: The 3-year-old was severely choking on the drain plug, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description:
I have a Bliss large 15' metallic bronze steel hammock stand. while in the hammock with my toddler the weld on the base bracket gave way, and we fell to the ground. Thankfully no one was seriously injured, just shocked and buzzed. I saw that some other brands with identical design were recalled, but do not know if this one was. I purchased it at Bed Bath and beyond about 5 years ago.
Thanks
[redacted]
justification: The weld failure caused a fall, but no serious injuries were reported, only shock and minor effects.

incident_description:
This is the Grand Trunk Ultralight Hammock.

I owned two of these and both claim a 2 year warranty. Both state can be used for weights up to 250 pounds. I am 130 pounds. March 18, 2011, one of the hammocks split right down the middle as I was lounging in it, and dropped me to the ground. The company offered to replace it only if I paid to ship it back to them. The item was only $16 to begin with, so I didn't bother. They assured me that wasn't a common issue and apologized. 

However, yesterday, May 30, 2011, the second hammock I owned from them did the exact same thing. It split down the middle, dropping me to the ground. This could prove to be extremely dangerous if someone was hanging above rocky ground. Thankfully, I was only suspended above the dirt. If this happened in less than 10 months to both hammocks that I owned, I have to assume it's happened to others who maybe haven't reported it. This is a safety issue that needs to be looked into. Thank you.
justification: The hammock failed twice, causing falls but no reported injuries, indicating a severity level of 2. The recurrence in two out of two hammocks suggests a likely occurrence likelihood of 4.

incident_description:
I have an air walker / Pro form Sears product. model# 831290841 part# 138463. Exercise  product of Sears brand.
  I was exercising on it when the leg tilted.  I found the metal leg had separated from the welded circle.  This is dangerous to anyone that owns this, mine only cracked at the joined spot, it could have broken off and I would have been injured.  I am not an obese person, but this is a very heavy metal exerciser.  Sears stated that no one has recalled this equipment for metal fatigue and stated thru their CSR's that any thing they sell over 10 years is lifetime of the product so they will not replace or repair the defective dangerous part.   They will not even investigate this because they claim it is past 10 years old.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous equipment failure but no injury occurred, and the likelihood is possible given the description of metal fatigue.

incident_description:
the lower steering shaft spline failed/ striped out  , & steering control was lost .
 I was the only vehicle occupant & there were no injuries
justification: Steering control was lost, but there were no injuries.

incident_description: We have the Tacoma Playset that was mentioned in a previous safety recall, http://www.cpsc.gov/cpscpub/prerel/prhtml10/10029.html . We received the new monkey bar set to fix the playset. The problem is that the same defect that occurred in the previous recall (the rotting wood surrounded by the plastic coating) happened in the other part of the playset (the part with the ladders and slide). So, when the children swing, the entire playset becomes unstable, and the monkey bar and slide sections are becoming detached due to the weak supports on the slide side.
justification: The playset is unstable and parts are detaching, posing a risk of injury to children, but no injury is reported yet.

incident_description:
I own a 2004.5 polaris sportsman 500HO. my polaris allways killed the battery with in two days of sitting.

I was using my atv for some work around the place. I smelt somthing burning and went looking for the smell. when i saw my atv it was bellowing smoke from the front of the atv. my vin number on my atv is

incident_description:
My 2 year old son and his four year old brother were swinging on the teeter totter on the Playsafe Verona 2 swingset that we purchased 4 years ago.

The male and female bolts holding one of the bars on the swing to the bar of the set backed out.  The swing fell apart breaking my 2 yearolds leg (tibia) and had my 4 year old hanging by the crotch.  The 4 year old didn't sustain serious injury.

I am very upset about this faulty design in the product.  There was only about 4 or 5 threads that held this thing together.  We are very thankful however that our sons didn' t not sustain head injuries or even death because of this.
justification: The incident resulted in a broken leg (tibia) for the 2-year-old, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the description of the faulty design but without broader statistical context.

incident_description:
While pulling the handle straight down from the overhead position, the pin disengaged, causing the arm to fall quickly landing on the top of his head. There was an EMT in the facility in which contacted the paramedics and he was taken to St. Francis Hospital Poughkeepsie, NY. 

He received ten stitches on his head and was also provided with medication. Three days later he went back to the gym and noticed that the equipment was no longer on the floor. He asked a representative that worked at the facility where the equipment was and why was it removed. He also advised the representative that he noticed a recall online.  There is a recall for the same equipment (see Release #07-001) and the hazard was the selector pin for the weight plates can slip out of its slot if the edges of the pin are worn, allowing the weights to drop suddenly.  The attendant informed him that the equipment was a free motion dual cable cross machine.

Falling weight plates can hit consumers using the machines. He was advised there was nothing wrong with the equipment and it that it worked fine. He is not sure if the model number in which is listed on the release is the same model number on the equipment in the gym and the employees at the gym will not provide him with any further assistance. No further information was provided.
justification: The incident resulted in injury requiring stitches and medication, indicating a severity level of 3. The recall and hazard description suggest the occurrence likelihood is likely, given the equipment's known issue.

incident_description:
I had previously filed a complaint under IDI [REDACTED] for an elliptical manufactured by Icon Fitness.    In response to my complaint, and subsequent report completed by the CPSC, Bearson and Peck Attorneys at law (who represent ICON Fitness) wrote a  letter to the CPSC in response to the complaint that was filed under IDI [REDACTED].  I would like to provide comment sdirectly to the points made in this letter in hopes that additional investigation will be made into the elliptical.
 
In the letter, Bearnson & Peck indicated that the elliptical machine was approximately three years old; however, at the time the elliptical broke it was just over 2 years old. 

In the letter Bearnson & Peck  stated that the elliptical was stored in an unfinished basement with concrete floors and that it is not uncommon for concrete floors to be uneven that may weaken the ellipticalÃÂs weld.  I have taken photos in which I have placed a level in front of the broken elliptical, which is still in our basement.  The level indicates that the basement floor is NOT uneven as was suggested by the attorneys.

In the letter Bearnson & Peck  have said that no other external factors have been ruled out and that misuse or failure to appropriate follow any instruction sheets are potentially contributing factors.  Both my wife and I, the main users of the elliptical, both read and understood the directions of use. We have also been using similar equipment for many years without issue. 

Finally the letter stated that injury did not result from this occurrence.  However, I think a clarification needs to be made.  When I used the elliptical and it failed, I fell off of the elliptical tweaking my ankle and hitting my arm on the elliptical.  An injury did result from the product failure.  However, at the time, I did not deem the injury to be severe enough to warrant medical attention.  However, it should be noted that one of my main concerns is that should have someone older or less fit been on this elliptical or a similar product that a more serious injury could have occurred. From my understanding of the regulations, CPSC has the right to address products that have an ÃÂunreasonable risk of serious injuryÃÂ.  The issue related to this product could result in an ÃÂunreasonable risk of serious injuryÃÂ.  So, this product resulted in an injury to me, although not one that required me to seek medical attention, and could present an ÃÂunreasonable risk of seriousÃÂ injury to others.

Please contact me for further information

Kind regards,

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury (tweaked ankle and arm impact) that did not require medical attention, but poses a potential risk of more serious injury to others.

incident_description: In October or November of 2009 I received a replacement set of monkey bars for our Durango swingset that we purchased we kept the replacement in the box because we live in Maine and at that time of year it is cold and snowy. We figuired the longer we could keep it out of the elements the better. We put it up in the spring of 2010, we covered it for the winter in the fall of 2010 and took all necessary precautions to keep it out of the elements. We just got the swings out again this spring and the first time my boys who are not overly big swang on it the monkey bar replacement split down the middle of the wood and now the swing set is unusable again. We are so lucky that neither of them were seriously hurt when this happened. We have spent more time not using this swingset then we have using it. We feel that the company should have to not only replace the monkey bars but the whole swing set with a sturdy swing set that we do not have to fear using. This should have brought us many years of use and grown with our children. We are so disappointed in the quality of the set and that the whole swing set was not recalled.  We have taken every step we could to preserve it.
justification: The monkey bars split during use, but no injuries were reported, indicating an incident without injury.

incident_description: Purchased the Playsafe Dartmouth metal swingset from Toys R Us on April 16, 2011. The swingset is only 3 weeks old. The young child who weighs only about 45-50 lbs was swinging when the swing snapped in half in mid air. Thank goodness the little girl did not get hurt. The swing was not flawed but apparently it is made of too rigid of a material and just snapped in half under pressure. The swingset was made in China but the swings are marked Playsafe out of Wisconsin so not sure if that info will help or not. If you go to the Toys R Us website, it is listed being the first swingset under the metal swingset heading (Playsafe Dartmouth) I did call Toys R Us to report this incident and was told it would take 7 to 10 days to get back to me over this complaint. I am not happy as first of all, another little child could be getting injured in this 7 to 10 days waiting period and also I am afraid that it will not be seriously looked into. In the meantime, I am going out and buying different swings and replacing the remainder one that came with this unsafe swingset.
justification: The swing snapped but the child was not injured, indicating an incident without harm. The likelihood is rated as possible due to the reported material rigidity issue.

incident_description:
The 13 YOM, 5' 8ÃÂ tall,  113 lbs.,  was driving the off road vehicle, with his friend inside.  They were riding in a hayfield when the driver attempted to turn the steering wheel in one direction (exact direction unknown).   The steering wheel spun out of the driverÃÂs hands, which caused him to lose control of the vehicle. The driver (victim) fell out of the vehicle face down in the hay field and the vehicle rolled over on him.  The father said that the off road vehicleÃÂs cross bar fell onto his sonÃÂs neck.

The vehicle was purchased to be used around the consumerÃÂs farm. He also told the consumer that he didnÃÂt have to worry about the warning label for use of 16 years or older since the vehicle would be used on the farms.ÃÂ 
 
(2009) A CPSC Field investigator, [redacted], came out with a team of investigators, to examine the hay field where the off-road vehicle was driven.   There was no further follow-up with the consumer regarding the investigation.
justification: The incident resulted in the death of the victim due to a severed spinal cord, which is the highest severity level. The likelihood is rated as likely (4) given the circumstances of an inexperienced driver and potential vehicle defects.

incident_description: When consumer dials in the weights on the weight lifting set, they do not lock on to the dumbbell so when it is lifted up, the dumbbell plates often fall off. Consumer had one fall onto his foot as he lifted the dumbbell from the stand. The plates fall off sometimes when he is working out with them.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (plates falling on the foot) and occurs frequently during workouts.

incident_description: We purchased a baseball tee for use by several 4-year-olds. Within 5 minutes of use, the base of the tee broke and the tee went flying, with sharp edges where the plastic broke. This product should not be marketed to children as it is unsafe. By definition tee ball is for 4- to -6-year-olds. A plastic tee that snaps off exposing sharp edges so easily is not safe for children running and playing. It should be recalled.
justification: The incident involved a broken baseball tee with sharp edges, posing a potential hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I purchased the Bodylastics strength bands  product last July and I consistently use it 2 - 3 times per week.  You insert a strength band through a holder that then is inserted into a door that is held in place by a foam, circular ball.  The seam on the strap that goes through the circular, foam holder separated and the orange band snapped across my neck/back this morning.  Fortunately, I was doing the 2 handed chest exercise so I was facing away from the door.  If not, the band would have snapped into my neck/face.  Please see the attached photos.
justification: The band snapped across the user's neck/back, which could have caused injury if they were facing the door, indicating a potential for harm.

incident_description: The 2006 Polaris Sportsman ATV and other ATV's manufactured and sold by Polaris have an unchecked gas tank vent tube that results in a dangerous spill of gasoline in tip over and rollover accidents. Other manufacturers use a "tip over" valve or fluid discrimination device to prevent the spill of fuel through the vent tube in a rollover accident. Our client was seriously burned by a fuel fed fire when he tipped over and was trapped by a Polaris Sportsman ATV in the course of his job as a ranch hand. Both of his legs had to be amputed as a result of his burn injuries. The ATVs are marked and sold as utility work vehicles and are routinely used by agricultural workers and state and federal forestry and wildlife workers around controlled burn fires. Additional information is provided in the attached engineering reports. We have located other consumer reports of gas and gas vapors leaking from the vent tube of Polaris' ATVs, and one other accident where a Polaris Sportsman ATV was consumed by fire after tipping over. We would be happy to provide additional information and share test results and video with you.
justification: The incident resulted in serious injuries requiring amputation, and there are other reported cases of similar incidents, indicating a significant risk.

incident_description:
Sudden failure for critical bicycle component with high potential of grave bodily injury.

Luckily, no injury occured in this instance. 
The bolt (see photo accompanying this report) holding the bike saddle to the stem failed with no warning at the end of a ride (when entering a driveway) and left the saddle pole totally exposed where it could have inflicted serious injury on a most tender portion of the human anatomy.
This is original equipment, 1 1/4 year old. The bolt has not been adjusted since the bike was sold and the bike has only been ridden on roads and paths (both paved and gravel), bot trails or across open countryside.
The bike is a man's Trek "Pure" serial 1243U227.
A casual examination of the bolt appears to show failure due to inferior materials. If this is true of the production run, it will surely result in similar failures, perhaps with serious or fatal results.
justification: The incident involved a critical component failure with high potential for injury, but no injury occurred in this instance. The description suggests that similar failures could be likely due to inferior materials.

incident_description: My name is [REDACTED] and I have a 3 year old daughter who recently started playing Tball. We purchased the pink Rawlings Tball helmet a week ago and I noticed there was a small hole in the top, Im assuming for ventilation. However, after a game my daughter wanted to hold the helmet then proceded to put her index finger in this small hole. We tried every way possible to remove the helmet at home, but ended up going to the ER. My daughter was in severe pain due to swelling of the finger. From there we were transferred to another hospital for a Pediactric ICU. There was talk of orthopedic surgery and the possibility of her losing the finger. They eventually had to take a saw to the helmet to get it removed. My daughter ended up with 3 doses of Morphine (strong pain reliever) and 1 of Diprivan which put her to sleep. She has cuts on her finger and its still swollen. She can barely use it right now. Maybe the manufactuer will consider redesigning the helmets to ensure this doesn't happen to another child. Thank You.
justification: The child suffered severe pain, required medical intervention including strong pain relievers, and faced potential surgery, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description:
Received a Nordic Track Relfex 4500 Pro treadmill as a replacement for another defective treadmill from same manufacturer.  After about four months of light use the main support that holds the console and treadmill together fell apart causing a very serious hazard for use.  Upon inspection the main welds of the unit separated. I contacted the firm and they told me not to use the unit because of the serious injury that could occur.
Upon closer look of the welded area it appears that the weld was made from the main frame to a painted surface of the support bar. It think it needs to be welded directly to the metal, so not sure if this was a manufacturing error and could affect other units produced.
justification: The treadmill's structural failure posed a serious hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
little tikes garden play house #615894 . when put together correctly the stove top and peg board top are attached in front inside play house with screws. no screws or attachment for backside facing outside ofproduct. these flat parts have grooves anderneath to slide over window opening botton of window sill. one on each side of playhouse. the 2 parts can bend up by kids playing with stove top and peg board causing pieces to bend forward moving up and down and child on other side can get fingers and hands under plastic pieces getiing pinched or smashed if child playing with on other pushes down on stove top or peg board top. as i have seen done with my son and his friends playing with. so i discontinued use. bought at toys r us and they would not return. contacted little tikes about issue getting run around about return or exchange for safer playhouse. they seem to not care about child safty complaints
thanks [REDACTED]
justification: The description indicates that children can get fingers and hands pinched or smashed, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description:
My grandson just got injured at the Pump IT Up "Bounce House" as they are called in Huntington Beach, CA. He required surgery to address the seriousness of his fracture. He was sliding on an inflatable slide along with many other kids. While at CHOC, Children's Hospital in Orange, CA, the surgeon told us that in one week he performed surgery on three children from such places (there are two Bounce Houses in our city that I know of) and the nurses told us that other children had been seen at the hospital with injuries from such places.

We do not wish to file an lawsuits, but it is our intent to find a govermental agency that regulates Children's Safety to assess the safety of these places. Parents are unaware that children are getting hurt and the Bounce Houses are not accountable because they require parents to sign a release prior to using the facility. While there I noticed over 40 kids and only saw one person with a staff shirt watching the kids. Saw two other staff, young people, in another area who were not really watching, it was very hectic with so many children all bouncing on the various inflatable play equipment.

If you are not able to help, please direct me to the right agency, I am trying to prevent other children to go through the painful process my little four year old grandson is going through.
justification: The incident resulted in a serious injury requiring surgery, and there is evidence of multiple similar injuries occurring at the same facility.

incident_description: Repeated failure of hand brake/parking brake has caused the atv to roll off trailer and roll away unatended. The brake has been repaired three times but always fails soon after repair.
justification: The ATV rolling away is an incident with potential for injury, but the description does not mention any actual injury or death.

incident_description: My son's swing set became unwelded.  At the location that the main top bar to the side A-frame where it is welded popped apart.  It just came unwelded. I haven't even had this swing set a year, it's just unacceptable that this should happen. It's poor quality.  And when I called to report this safety issue they just said warranty only lasts 180 days and that I could order a replacement part, and it wasn't even about ordering a new part it was the safety involved.  If I did not notice this problem it could've broke and caused serious injury to my child. I can replace a swing set, not my child. The swing set I purchased was a SportsPower Jump N Swing.
justification: The swing set became unwelded, posing a potential safety hazard, but no injury occurred as the issue was noticed in time.

incident_description:
Bike rear wheel rim on right side weld is poorly made and actually damaging the brake pad.  
Bike has been ridden for about 50 miles when this problem was noted.
Bike is a 2011 Motobecane Le Champion CF Ltd road bike with a 54 CM frame.

http://www.bikesdirect.com/products/motobecane/lechamp_cf_ltd_xi.htm

Bike was purchased through bikesdirect.com.
Wheels are manufactured by Mavic and come with the bike.
Wheel rim model is Aksium Race.
Rear wheel serial number is L00890217.

I have purchased and assembled about a dozen bikes in my life and have not see this problem in the past.  I examined about a dozen other wheels and they all have a smooth machined surface in this area.  If the machining is not correct is the welding correct?

I am an engineer by profession but not a wheel expert.  These bikes are designed to go as fast as 40 MPH and I would be concerned about a catastrophic failure
justification: The poorly made weld is damaging the brake pad, posing a risk of incident but no injury has occurred yet.

incident_description:
My Five year old son was riding his Hyper Moto 16in Bicycle when the spring system for the rear shocks some how came apart causing the bike to fold in half while he was still on it. He fell and the bike folded around his leg. He is well under the weight limit and is not hard on the bike at all. He has had the bike for about 11 months and rides it in the spring and summer months for a few hours a couple of times a week. He was scraped up but luckily didn't break any bones. I fear that if this were to unexpectedly happen to an older child who is more apt to be jumping jumps with the bike, as it is modeled after a dirt bike, They could get seriously hurt or worse.

We bought the bike at Walmart in May 2010, WMA-91604 model number
justification: The child suffered scrapes but no broken bones, indicating an injury without severe consequences. The incident suggests a potential hazard that could cause more serious harm under different circumstances.

incident_description:
My wife called Custom Pools of DeQueen Arkansas to discuss having them build us an in ground swimming pool. The price of 18,791.78 was agreed to and a contract was signed. Before signing of the contract the owner of Custom Pools [REDACTED] was asked if she had a contractors License and she said yes. I found out later she did not. The job was estimated to take 2 or 3 weeks instead it took 4 and a half months. When the job was finally complete additional charges of over $3,000 was added to the final bill. 

When the pool was finished my children swam in the pool and complained that the water was shocking them. When I investigated sure enough the water was energized. When the deck is wet and you touch the water you will receive an electric shock. This is very dangerous and absolutely unacceptable. The new pool is basically rendered useless if not a death trap. They performed electrical work without a license that was not up to code especially for a swimming pool. The pool is not bonded and or grounded, there are no GFCI anywhere to be seen. The pool pumps manufacturer says a GFCI MUST BE INSTALLED. This was ignored by Custom pools.

Basically I want this pool brought to code at Custom Pools expense before someone is electrocuted. Custom Pools should be put out of business before some gets hurt. Thank You. 

The information contained here is true and accurate to the best of my knowledge. I understand that the Arkansas Attorney General's office does not represent individuals in matters involving private disputes. I am, however, filing this complaint to notify the Attorney General's office of the activities of this party and for any other assistance which may be rendered. I give my permission for this complaint to be referred to other agencies when appropriate.
justification: The pool's electrical issues pose a serious risk of electric shock, which could lead to injury or death, making the severity level high. The likelihood is also high given the described conditions and lack of safety measures.

incident_description:
Product: 2010 Kona Sutra touring-type bicycle with original fenders http://www.konaworld.com/bike.cfm?content=sutra a product that has been offered for several years with this fender and front rack combination. 

Location: C&O Canal trail http://www.nps.gov/choh an unpaved trail, approximately 13 miles east of Cumberland MD. The bicycle met the recommended tire size for the trail (32 mm or greater). 

What happened: Something (probably a stone from the path) caught in the front fender causing the plastic fender to contact the front tire which grabbed hold of the fender causing it to crumple and jam at the upper part of the fork. The steel fender stays, bolted to the lower part of the fork near the axle and solidly attached to the fender also moved upward jamming at the crown and causing the heavy, mountain bike type fork to bend severely, destroying it. The bike had been traveling about 13 mph and stopped almost immediately throwing me over the handlebars and slamming me to the ground. The rider behind me crashed due to my sudden stop. Neither of us required medical attention. Her bike, the same model, had been picking up mud and gravel in the front fender and we had stopped twice to scrape this material from her fender. I thought I was fortunate not to have this problem. Maybe my fenders were installed differently ... possibly closer to the tire or farther away. We had my bike repaired without the fender and had the other bike's fender removed and shipped home. Since then her fender has been reattached but with SKS breakaway mounts (Secu-Clips) at the fork which are designed to release in this situation. http://www.rivbike.com/products/show/sks-fender-secu-clips-pair/27-009

Anyway, I've previously had the impression that fenders are "dorky" and hardly a safety concern. I have learned, the hard way, that they can be quite dangerous. A week before this accident we went on a road tour to practice and this involved a few 35 mph downhill sections. I shudder to think what could have happened if the tire caught the fender at speed and on a paved surface.
justification: The incident resulted in the rider being thrown over the handlebars and another rider crashing, but no medical attention was required.

incident_description:
I purchased two Specialized Sequioa bicycles in 2004 from retail bicycle store in Bainbridge Island, Washington.

I traveled about 10,000 miles on one of the bicycles, commuted approximately 6,000 of those miles.

On April 21, 2011, I cleaned this bicycle and found a crack in the metal at the rear dropout where the rack mount bolt passes through.

It appears failure of this dropout would cause a crash and injury.
justification: The description indicates a potential for injury due to a crack in the bicycle's rear dropout, but no actual incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: On my 2009 polaris ranger xp 700 the seat post broke on passengers side ,Only had the machine 4 months,the passenger fell in the floor.
justification: The passenger fell but the description does not mention any injury, so the severity is level 2.

incident_description:
2011 Polaris ranger crew and other bench type Polaris seats have had there plastic flimsy seat post mounts break, crack,melt and sheer off. this makes the seat sitting on the frame with nothing holding it down when the plastic post breaks. a real safety issue. imagine riding 30-40 mph and the seat is not sitting freely with nothing holding it down securely!

I had this happen, dealer contacted, Polaris contacted, they always claim operator mis aligns this causing break. that is ABSOLUTELY NOT CORRECT. in fact it would be hard to mis align it without knowing it if you look at the design of this. I was the only one to ever take back seat off and it had not been off for 3 weeks prior to the post breaking! there is several people with the same issue, over Internet forums, through declined repair orders for warranty work, its all over. I have seen over 40 complaints online, legit ones with pictures.

my machine is 60 hours and 5 months old, it broke off, declined the warranty repair, for the same reply they give everyone, operator mis aligned it... no way... look at this design and tell me you can mis align it and not clearly know it. that is a lame excuse, it did not happen....

but even at there claim, it should not be able to be mis aligned, its a critical safety issue. the posts are flimsy plastic, near a engine heat source where it gets hot. in fact it gets so hot, that another issue we had, which was fixed under warranty was the air filter box melted from the engine hot and bad design from Polaris. they put a new cover and added heat tape, a band aid fix.

this complaint is about the plastic seat post that holds on the bench seats. there is a real safety issue there. seat could come free while driving, going down a hill, etc.. 2 simple flimsy plastic posts are all that hold this on. in a vibration riding are, near very hot temps, they break easy. I have also seen injuries from this failure on forums with pictures. Polaris is arrogant about it. even under factory warranty. please, before people die, check it out... please..

i found mine broke at home while doing a check of everything, so im lucky, before we went out to ride the trails, this could have turned out with injury had i not found it by luck.
justification: The incident describes a critical safety issue with potential for injury due to seat detachment, supported by multiple complaints and evidence of injuries from similar failures.

incident_description: The trampoline was being used as directed.  It has only been in use one year and was new in box prior to use.  Two of the legs on the trampoline broke during normal use causing son to fall sideways.
justification: The incident resulted in a fall, which implies an injury occurred, and the trampoline legs broke during normal use, suggesting a possible likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
first of I would like to say that i just now saw the recall about the bravo sports/ variflex trampolines which is quite bothersome to me since i bought it almost a year ago.
we purchased the 12' variflex trampoline with enclosure last year april/may.
my son then was 10 yrs old ,after jumping on it a few times the jumping mat became very stretched out and i received a replacement mat from the company.

Due to the lack of tension on the jumping mat from useless defective springs my son has fallen many times and hurt his head on stretched out springs. I have tried to contact the company numerous times the last few days with no luck.
I could understand if my son was maybe heavy set or he had a lot of friends jumping on it but neither applies. Another fact is we live in Alaska which means 3 months of summer so last summer he barely even used it due to the fact that the mat had a defect to begin with and now the springs are useless as well. some of them are just kind of hanging there. Safety issue !!

I dont understand how an estimated 50 of the springs can look the way they do unless they are defective. please see attached photos
justification: The description reports that the son has fallen many times and hurt his head due to defective springs, indicating an injury.

incident_description: Aluminum frame completely cracked and failed at the base just forward of the pedals, causing rider to lose contol. Minor injuries of abrasions from falling, incident occured just after mounting to ride.
justification: The incident resulted in minor injuries (abrasions) from falling, which corresponds to severity level 3. The occurrence likelihood is possible (3) as frame failure is not common but can happen.

incident_description: I bought a Mongoose bike last fall and did not use it much before storing it for the winter this spring I got the bike out and I noticed it was breaking the tires for no aparent reason well I figured maybe it would help if I rode it so I drove it up the street it stopped on me several times but then it started getting better so I was going to turn around and head home as I turned the front tire colapsed under the bike I took the bike back to walmart where I bought it and was told that this has happened to alot of the mongoose bikes they sold last fall including some where peoble have gotten hurt
justification: The incident involved a bike tire collapse, which is an incident but no injury was reported in this specific case.

incident_description: Item is a Parkside 14 foot trampoline. The Legs lack a set bolt where they attach to the frame. When moved to mow under, the Legs can come out of the frame socket especially when lifting up on the frame to move. Since one end of the U tube leg may still be in its socket the other end can spin (or rotate) leaving it directly under the trampoline mat pointing straight up. When a child jumps on the trampoline in this condition the child can be dangerously skewered and impaled by the end of the leg. Definite design flaw. Should be recalled before someone is killed or paralized. [REDACTED]
justification: The description indicates a design flaw that could lead to severe injury or death, but no actual incident has occurred yet.

incident_description: I was riding a Dahon Speed D7 bicycle slowly when the handlepost hinge spontaneously cracked off and I fell off the bike.  I was not seriously injured because I was riding very slowly but would have likely been very injured if it had happened moments earlier.  There appears to be very little metal holding the handlepost to the frame and it appears to be a soft aluminum alloy without enough strength for normal use.
justification: The incident resulted in a fall but no serious injury, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the apparent design flaw in the handlepost hinge.

incident_description:

Incident is currently being investigated by Nationwide fire inspectors and attorneys.  Vehicle is currently shrink wrapped and secured at incident site.

incident_description: I was riding my Trek cruiser bicycle when the right side crank arm broke in the middle. I was standing up on the pedals when it happened with no warning. It caused me to fall to the seat hard, and I nearly lost control of the bicycle. This really concerns me because it could have caused me to lose control and fall or go into traffic. Since the bicycle is a cruiser, it only has the coaster type of brake, which is activated when pushing backwards on the pedal. If I was braking when the crank arm broke, I could have been prevented from stopping, which could have been disastrous.
justification: The incident involved a mechanical failure that caused a fall but no injury, and the potential for more severe outcomes was noted.

incident_description: I bought a swing set from Flexible Flyer Newcastle Model # 46603T in December 2011 for my kids for Christmas. Since then I have had a few incidents with this product. First there is a two seater swing that the pole under one of the sewing bent and forced the end cap off which made that swing come all apart while my kids were on it. The company did contact me back on this incident and sent me replacement parts. Second incident my 5 yr old was swinging on a single seater swing and the link broke and he went flying. He thank God was not hurt but he did land really hard on the ground. I have tried contacting the company a few times by phone. They will not answer there phones. Then I have emailed them a few times and there has been no response that way either. There is a 6 month warranty so I think maybe they are trying to put me off until after that 6 month period.
justification: The incident involved a swing set failure causing a child to fall hard but without injury, and another incident with no injury but equipment damage.

incident_description: DECEDENT FELL OFF HIS ATV AND THE ATV FELL BACK ON TOP OF HIM, STRIKING HIM IN THE BACK.  DECEDENT WAS ABLE TO GET UP, FLIP THE ATV, AND DRIVE BACK HOME.  HE WAS RESPONSIVE AND CONSCIOUS UPON ARRIVAL AT THE HOSPITAL.  WHEN THE DOCOTORS BEGAN TO EXAMINE HIM, HE FELL INTO CARDIAC ARREST AND PASSED AWAY.  IT WAS REPORTED THAT THE DECEDENT WAS NOT WEARING A HELMET.

incident_description:
While her five year old approximately thirty pound son was laying in the plastic swing with his belly touching the seat.  The seat folded in half and cracked causing the child to fall onto the wood chips in which the play ground is planted. 

She removed the swings into the house and placed them in the basement. On 3/31/20100 she noticed there was a recall  (Release #11-120) but it was with a different company where the swing seats on the playsets can crack and break in half, causing the user to fall to the ground.

Manufacturer stated that the cracking may have occurred from leaving the swng outside during the winter season. She advised them that she put the swings up when the weather changed.

She still currently has the swings in her basement but is considering disposing of the swing set. Her concerns are that the children could be seriously injured.
justification: The child fell but was not injured, and the swing was removed to prevent future incidents.

incident_description: On right side of atv get very very hot like burn leg ang plastic hot.My Plastic has not melted yet but in Dec while riding my Grandson it got so hot we had to stop riding.I have been back to Polaris at least 6 times,called the 1800 number 2 times I have eaven asked them if they had a heat sheild I would buy it but no luck.The year after they fixed the problem.I use the atv working on the farm it get so hot I have to shut it down.I have heard that there have been fires plastic melted and people burn and Polaris want help The last time which was in April 2011 and went back to service manerger he called Polaris and he said they told him for me to make a fix.I hope you all can help all the poaple that got Polaris ATV"S
justification: The description mentions burns and overheating issues, indicating potential for injury but no confirmed injuries or deaths.

incident_description: None of the kids I had here were actually hurt, but easily could have been! I purchased a Skywalker Trampoline 3 years ago. It is a 14' trampoline with a netting enclosure. The trampoline itself is great and I have no complaints... However, the netting does not last very long at all and it is supposed to be a safety device. This will be the second spring we will have to replace the netting because it rips after almost exactly one year of use! My son and his friend were jumping on it and one of them fell against the netting. Suddenly a huge rip occurred. The netting is so fragile that when I tried to sew it up, it continued to rip, so I told them they could not jump on it anymore. We had severe storms just after that with high gusting winds which caused the ENTIRE netting to rip all the way around and is now literally blowing in the breeze... I feel this is a very dangerous thing since my son or his friend could easily have fallen out of the netting and off the trampoline! The netting should be safe at all times. I understand that sometimes there may be an accidental rip or what have you and I may need to replace parts at times. However, the exact same thing happen this time last year! I purchased a brand new netting and now this year it has happened again. I can take the netting and practically put my fingers right through it! It should weather better than this or have a warning that every year it will need to be replaced! I would never have allowed my child or his friends jump on it had I known it would rip so easily! The replacement netting is "ENCLOSURE #6003 - Key #10 Enclosure Netting" on their website. They are currently out of stock on it and I am the 44th customer waiting for a new netting. I have the feeling I am not the only one with this problem...
justification: No injury occurred, but the netting failure poses a clear risk of injury if not addressed.

incident_description: My 2005 Polaris ATV 500 started on fire and burned in its entirety.  A chain saw was on the ATV and that was completely burned.  Additionally, a trailor was attached to the ATV and sustained damage.
justification: The ATV and attached items were completely burned, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
I recently purchased a replacement pool ladder from INTEXCORP.  The replacement ladder does not come with a platform at the top of the ladder.  The new ladder forces the consumer to step over the pool top and onto the opposing side of the ladder.  This is not conducive for a safe transition into the pool for small people.  The small person is likely not to make the long step and fall behind the ladder, either to the groud or in the pool, or end up straddling the pool edge.
I contacted INTEXCORP and was told they no longer have platforms on their ladders.
This product, if has not injured an individual, will cause injury or death from fall or drowning from not being able to get out from behind the ladder (for small people).
justification: The description indicates a high risk of injury or death for small people due to falls or drowning, and the issue is likely to occur given the design flaw.

incident_description:
I was using a brand new Everlast Excersicse (three bands in the package) band as intended after reading the instructions, warnings, etc. I was doing an excersise on their brochure (seated, stretching the band with both legs out in front of me, when somehow it sprung back with force and hit me directly in the eye.  I didn't even see it coming.  I had major eye trauma and surgery the following day for a detached retina (right eye)  To date, I have had 4 hospital surgeries to try and save the vision in that eye.  I have a 5th surgery scheduled in Apr.  I will be partially blind and still may loose all vision in that eye. 

To be totally safe against this happening to someone else, there needs to be a safety warning, I believe, telling the user that "eye protection is recommended should the band break and or come out of position while using."
justification: The incident resulted in severe eye trauma requiring multiple surgeries and potential permanent vision loss, indicating a high severity level. The likelihood is considered possible given the detailed account of the incident.

incident_description:
Last January (2010) I was skiing at Copper around a little hill, stopped, took 2 steps, stopped & committed to a turn. The next thing I knew I was careening down the hill head first landing for the icy catwalk.  the skis had crossed in the back & the K2 signature metal pieces combined with the twin tip tails caught & would not release.  I feel that this is a very dangerous design.  It caused a very serious injury.  I dislocated my shoulder and had a fracture of the humerus (2 chips attached to the rotator cuff had to be reattached).
I am an expert woman skier and have never had this kind of fall.  This never would have happened with my old skis.  I was out for the rest of the ski season & had a long, painful rehabilitation.  The medical records of this accident are enclosed.
justification: The incident resulted in a dislocated shoulder and humerus fracture, indicating an injury (severity 3). The occurrence is unlikely (2) as the skier is an expert and this was a unique event with her new skis.

incident_description: I purchased the Cap Barbell Fitness FID bench from Amazon.com. When the product was delivered and I began to unpack it, I noticed a terrible chemical smell coming from what I thought was just the bench (the product was in pieces, requiring assembly). It was the strongest chemical smell I have ever encountered while unpacking packaging. I made the mistake of casually sniffing one of the foam grips, with the goal of putting the offending pieces outside to air out, and suddenly shooting pain ran down my neck and into my shoulder. My neck, shoulder and chest were instantly and partially paralysed for 48 hours after coming into contact with this bench. I do not know what they use to manufacture and package this product, but I was seriously considering a lawsuit -- I was terrified that I had experienced some nerve damage (and, a week later, since my neck is still a little stiff, I am not entirely convinced that some damage was not done). Thankfully, the paralysis did eventually fade away, but the entire situation was disturbing, to say the least. Whatever is used on this bench is dangerous and toxic, and this should not be legally allowed to be sent casually into people's homes. I want to specific in no uncertain terms that I am not a hypochondriac. I am a healthy person with no allergies who opened and began to assemble this product in a well ventilated room, near an open window with a fan blowing. This was not in my head.
justification: The user experienced partial paralysis and stiffness for an extended period, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description:
No injury occurred because I was testing the device when I discovered the malfuction.

The stem cover opened on it's own after i blew it up and securly closed it into the device. I tried it again- I blew it up closed the stem cover inserted it into the floatation device and once again the pressure from the air in the floatation toy pushed the cap opened.  This is extremely dangerous as it can cause a childs toy to deflate while in use in the pool and cause a possible drowning.

Product:  Intex Kddie Float  #59586 (airplane)  73cm x 58cm  28 5/8" x 23" 
              It says "The Wet Set" on the bottom left cornor of the packaging cardboard

On back:    2003 Intex Corp., Long Beach, CA  90801-1440 USA (Made in China)

I due need to add that I later noticed that this product is for 2 and under and so I would have not used the device anyway since my child is 25 months old, but my child was NOT in it when I tested it and it malfunctioned!

incident_description: I was riding down the street on my 1999 women's Magna Equator bicycle (model number 8546-84) when the pedal popped off without warning, causing me to nearly fly over the handlebars.
justification: The pedal popping off caused a near-accident but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: I was execising on the Weslo Momentum G 3.8.  My leg slipped and my knee hit the cupholder and the cupholder went into my knee.  It tore a big hole in my knee that required stitches.  The hole was very deep.
justification: The incident resulted in a deep knee injury requiring stitches, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description: My 2 year old was in a little tikes swing purchased at toys r us and properly attached to our swingset.  She is within the height and weight limits for the swing.  The shoulder strap securing her into the harness simply broke through the back of the swing causing her to fall out of the swing face first and awkwardly onto the ground. incident_description:
There is currently an alert (Alert #06-547) for Artic Cat snowmobile gas tanks with leaking fuel filler necks that includes 2003 Firecat carbureted models along with 2004 - 2006 Firecat and Sabrecat models.  Arctic Cat has issued a recall covering the models specified in the alert.

This problem is far more extensive than the models specified in the alert.  I have a 2003 ZL 550 carbureted snowmobile.  The filler neck cracked and begin leaking a few years after I purchased it new.  The dealer inserted the Arctic Cat recommended sleeve inside the filler neck but it continued to crack and leak fuel.  I replaced the fuel tank with one that I was told no longer had the problem that caused the crack.  

This weekend my son and I went on a trip and once again the filler neck cracked and my son was soaked in gasoline from the crotch area down.  

A quick Google search will show the CPSC that this is a widespread Artic Cat problem involving many years and models other than those specified in the alert.  Why isn't the CPSC forcing Artic Cat to resolve this issue?  It is clearly a product defect with the potential for life threatening injury.

If you had an automobile with a gas filler tube that cracked and leaked gas on the passengers, would you let it continue?  I think not.

Thank you.

***
justification: The incident involves a fuel leak that soaked a passenger in gasoline, indicating a clear hazard but no reported injury.

incident_description:
I purchased a weslo cadence 4.8 treadmill at kmart as a floor model.  The treadmill never worked.  After contacting Weslo during the manufacturers warranty period, and after the representative telling me they would charge for the part in spite of the warranty, I received a replacement digital panel at no charge and they assured me that this would be the problem.  After replacing the panel the machine worked, with the treadmill operating at a very fast speed, but did not shut off even when the safety key was removed.  

At the time of purchase I also purchased an extended warranty.  A repairman from that company came to my home and examined the machine.  He showed my fiancee who was home at the time that the motor was excessive sparking during operation and this what was causing all of the problems.  He stated that it was a hazardous situation and had I been able to get the machine to work the sparks could have started a fire.  He ordered several parts but told me I would have to obtain a replacement motor from Weslo.  Weslo refuses to provide this part at no charge although the unit suffers a manufacturer defect and the intital complaints were during the warranty period.

I would like the Commissiont to examine the product to determine the hazard.
justification: The treadmill malfunctioned with excessive sparking, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.
